title: [kernel] RUNG 2 (axon-01, blade): nested agenix-identity aspects reach collections.nix:205 with NO content.id_hash — and a.key COLLIDES across every user on a host, so the obvious repair merges distinct users
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 by the corpus-frontier scout, on axon-01 and blade, with the offending records dumped by
name from an instrumented site. RUNG 2 of the corpus blocker chain (see den-hoag-1kd).

FAILURE: Nix-level abort, not a den-hoag throw.
  error: attribute 'id_hash' missing
  at lib/attributes/collections.nix:205:32 — identity = a.content.id_hash;

THE RECORD, DUMPED: a keys = ["content","key","sharedFoldKey"]; a.content keys = ["home-manager",
"homeManagerModules","name","nixos"] — it carries `name` and NO `id_hash`. channel = homeManagerModules,
coordKinds = ["host","user"].
OFFENDERS BY NAME: axon-01 agenix-identity/{dvicory,pol,sini,theutz,vic}@axon-01;
blade agenix-identity/{shuo,sini,will}@blade. cortex never reaches this site (probe trace counts, same
predicate same instrument same run family: axon 20 / blade 12 / cortex 0).

★★ THE TRAP THE FIX MUST NOT FALL INTO, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS BEAD EXISTS RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE PATCH:
**a.key = "__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0" IS IDENTICAL FOR EVERY USER ON A HOST.** So the obvious
repair — deriving an identity via aspectIdHash over a.key — **COLLIDES ALL PRODUCERS ON THAT HOST**. Only
content.name distinguishes them. A collision here does not abort; it silently merges distinct users'
home-manager contributions, which is a wrong answer rather than a failure.

SHAPE: this is the nested-aspect "crosses the bridge as a BARE content set (no id_hash / no name)" case that
ci/tests/compat-nested-aspects.nix:9,20 already documents.

SCOPE CONTROL: content.id_hash is read at EXACTLY ONE site in lib/ (positive control on the same predicate:
content.name matches 4 files), so no second consumer is silently bypassed by a fix here.

★ NOTE FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS: the scout BYPASSED this rung with a synthetic identity rather than fixing it,
and left a.content unchanged. A correct fix stamps id_hash ONTO a.content — a different shape — so the rung-3
failures recorded downstream on den-hoag-1kd were measured under substitution and could differ under a real
fix. An ordering control (a second hash scheme verified to genuinely permute producer order) showed axon-01's
downstream error byte-identical under both orderings, which bounds but does not eliminate that risk.

title: [compat] RUNG 2 (cortex): den-hoag DROPS 'aspect' from the microvm-guest entity — corpus code den.lib.aspects.resolve reads it and aborts, while v1 builds exit 0
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 by the corpus-frontier scout on cortex. RUNG 2 of cortex's blocker chain (den-hoag-1kd).

FAILURE, raised from CORPUS CODE:
  error: attribute 'aspect' missing
  at nix-config/modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:43:77
  the corpus line is: den.lib.aspects.resolve "microvm" vm.aspect

CAUSE: den-hoag DROPS `aspect` from the microvm-guest entity. Reached via assertions → microvm.vms →
virtualization.microvm-host.nixos.

★ ATTRIBUTION IS CONTROLLED, NOT ASSUMED: cortex builds EXIT 0 on the corpus's own pinned den v1
(denful/den rev 99cc0c5a1cc846cb1be681344b10d2731d430e13) with a real .drv verified present on disk —
/nix/store/hvj9k6kdc2yj7bdpfvbx4waj3cddj6ni-nixos-system-cortex-26.11.20260723.e2587ca.drv. The corpus code
is unchanged between the arms. **THIS IS A den-hoag DIVERGENCE, NOT A CORPUS BUG.**

★ WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE HOST: this is a den-surface expressibility failure on PUBLIC corpus code — an
entity field that v1 delivers and den-hoag does not. The bar is den-surface expressibility, not
corpus-presence, so the missing field is the defect regardless of how many hosts happen to read it today.

cortex forks from axon-01/blade HERE — it never reaches the id_hash site at collections.nix:205 that blocks
the other two (probe trace counts: axon 20 / blade 12 / cortex 0).

title: [compat] e6c8edc MOVED THE CORPUS FAILURE EARLIER (not a regression — no toplevel at either point) and MASKS TWO distinct downstream defects; the guard fires on its own documented witness, broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares
description:
★★★ MEASURED 2026-07-29. `e6c8edc` IS A CORPUS REGRESSION AND NOTHING IN THE GRAPH RECORDED IT. It landed as
a clean three-state commit — 18 known-red, each attributed, parity 71/71 — and that accounting was TRUE ABOUT
THE SUITE AND SILENT ABOUT THE CORPUS.

THE ABORT, identical on blade / axon-01 / cortex, corpus arm (b), `.config.home-manager.users`:
    error: den-hoag: compose commitment: policy `__kindInclude__user__policy__8` produced a `pipeOp`
    declaration carrying a derived-channel DAG or a delivery route from its BODY.
Defined `lib/errors.nix:190`. `git merge-base --is-ancestor c42df53 e6c8edc` -> TRUE, so **THE GUARD LANDED
AFTER THE FROZEN MEASUREMENT BASE OF THE BEADS IT NOW BLOCKS.**
★ INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED by a second agent on the same day, measuring `axon-01` and `cortex` TOPLEVELS
rather than home-manager users, with the SAME message — and with the decisive control: **the same host builds
EXIT 0 on the corpus's own pinned den v1 (99cc0c5a), real drv
`/nix/store/wg8ihlp68m5cbsh47lijk3yxry8wi4mb-nixos-system-axon-01-….drv`.** The corpus is fine; den-hoag is
the difference.

★★ IT MASKS THREE P0s, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST BE FILED RATHER THAN NOTED. Three of the six corpus P0s can no
longer be reproduced at their own anchors — NOT because they were fixed, but because this guard blocks in
front of them:
· `9xo.61` — `attribute 'id_hash' missing` at collections.nix:205. MEASURED NOT TO REPRODUCE: `id_hash` token
  count **0** across three 231-line traces, with the POSITIVE CONTROL `compose commitment` = **1** in the same
  three files on the same grep. And `collections.nix:205 identity = a.content.id_hash` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to
  222af84. ⇒ **THE DEFECT IS NOT FIXED. IT IS UNREACHABLE.**
· `9xo.51` — every source anchor verified EXACT (`placeRemapped` output-modules.nix:547, `bind.crossEval`
  :561, dispatch :601, `ensureSeed` :611, `hmUserDetect` builtins.nix:121) and the file byte-untouched since
  222af84 — but its "6 of 7 hosts" is now **UNCHECKABLE**.
· `9xo.49` — items 1 (`aspect`) and 2 (`age`) masked.
⇒ ★ A MASKING REGRESSION IS WORSE THAN A PLAIN ONE: it converts three live, measured P0s into
unreproducible ones, and the natural reading of "it no longer reproduces" is "it was fixed."

CORPUS CANDIDATE, NOT PINNED: `den.schema.user.includes` is contributed by 9 files; the only pipeOp-bearing
feed is `modules/den/policies/pipes.nix:184-189` — expose-resolved-users, broadcast-syncthing-peers,
broadcast-syncthing-peers-to-hub, broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares. **NOT pinned to index 8**; that needs
instrumentation nobody has run. ★ AND NOTE THE NAME IS POSITIONALLY INDEXED — `__kindInclude__user__policy__8`
— the same brittleness already recorded for `…__policy__0`, so any diagnostic keyed on it re-targets silently
when the corpus reorders that list.

★★ THE RELATIONSHIP TO THE TWELVE KNOWN-RED, AND IT RAISES THEIR PRIORITY DECISIVELY: this is THE SAME ABORT
as the twelve `den-pipe` tests (den-hoag-66t), the same defect as `4kh.53.64`, and the subject of the ruling
at `den-hoag-i5m`. Those were carried all session as A TEST-SUITE CONCERN — twelve fixtures and an attribution
question. **THEY ARE THE THING STOPPING THE CORPUS FROM PRODUCING A SINGLE NixOS TOPLEVEL.**
⇒ AND IT RETROACTIVELY VINDICATES THE RULING NOT TO DECLARE THEM: declaring the twelve as expected errors
would have pinned as "correctly refused" the exact construct that blocks the corpus, and the gate would then
have FAILED when the real fix landed.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE THREE-STATE ACCOUNTING, and it is the generalisable part: `e6c8edc`'s commit message
enumerated every red BY CAUSE with zero unattributed, and that was honest and correct — **FOR THE SUITE**.
The corpus is not in the suite. `parity#tests` cannot witness corpus policy behaviour (already recorded on
den-hoag-9xo.75), and `ci#tests` uses fixtures. ⇒ **A COMMIT CAN BE FULLY ACCOUNTED AGAINST EVERY GATE IT RUNS
AND STILL BREAK THE ONLY THING THAT MATTERS.** The works-on-den arm exists precisely to catch this and was not
run on that commit.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ MY "REGRESSION" LABEL IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. VERDICT: **MOVED-THE-FAILURE — STRICTLY EARLIER.**
THE CORPUS PRODUCED NO TOPLEVEL UNDER den-hoag AT EITHER POINT. I expected the corpus got further before
`e6c8edc` and that was RIGHT ON THE FACT and WRONG ON THE LABEL: "regression" implies it previously built.
It did not. This is a FRONTIER regression, and the distinction matters because "regression" invites a revert
and a revert would restore nothing.

THE TWO TERMINAL THROWS, axon-01, corpus 4acf0a1d, arm (b), both exit 1:
  HEAD      : den-hoag: compose commitment: policy `__kindInclude__user__policy__8` produced a `pipeOp`
              declaration ... — stack tip `optionalValue.value`, COMPILE/DECLARE stage.
  c42df53   : attribute 'id_hash' missing at lib/attributes/collections.nix:205 — stack tip
              system.build.toplevel -> assertions -> core.impermanence.nixos -> home-manager.users,
              CONTENT-MATERIALIZATION depth, far past the guard.

★★ THE MASKING IS CONFIRMED **CAUSALLY, NOT BY STACK DEPTH** — which matters, because laziness makes a
depth argument unsound. Method: take the **HEAD tree**, disable **ONLY** the pipeOp arm in
`lib/concern-policies.nix` `conformingProduce` (`errors.opsInBody name` -> `a // { __policy = name; }`, one
occurrence, asserted), change nothing else. THE FRONTIER PER HOST THEN MATCHES `c42df53` EXACTLY:
    host      c42df53                     HEAD                  HEAD guard-off
    axon-01   id_hash missing             compose commitment    id_hash missing
    blade     id_hash missing             compose commitment    id_hash missing
    cortex    attribute 'aspect' missing  compose commitment    attribute 'aspect' missing
Nine evals, all exit 1 read from `$?` into `.exit` files.

★★★ AND IT MASKS **TWO DISTINCT DOWNSTREAM DEFECTS, NOT ONE.** `cortex` never reached `id_hash` even at
`c42df53` — it dies further downstream still, in THE CORPUS'S OWN CODE:
    error: attribute 'aspect' missing
    at nix-config modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:43:77
      microvmOpts = microvmSubmoduleOpts (den.lib.aspects.resolve "microvm" vm.aspect);
via `microvm.vms` <- `virtualization.microvm-host.nixos`. **A den-hoag ENTITY-FIELD divergence (`vm.aspect`
absent), unrelated to the compose seed, and INVISIBLE TODAY.** Filed separately — it would otherwise be
discovered only after the compose defect is fixed, by someone who assumes one blocker.

★★ `__kindInclude__user__policy__8` IS **`broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares`** — PINNED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT
GUESSED. `compile.nix` `perKind` builds `policyPolicies` as `imap0` over
`policyRefs = builtins.filter isPolicyRef refs`, so the index runs over the POLICY-FILTERED includes rather
than the raw list. Traced in a scratchpad copy:
    0=droidHm-user-detect  1=homeLinux-to-hm  2=homeDarwin-to-hm  3=homeAarch64-to-hm
    4=user-aspect-auto-include  5=expose-resolved-users  6=broadcast-syncthing-peers
    7=broadcast-syncthing-peers-to-hub  8=broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares  9=project-user-overlays
Source nix-config `modules/den/policies/pipes.nix:136-149`, `pipe.transform` closing over
`srcUser = user.name`.
★★★ **THAT IS THE EXACT POLICY `lib/errors.nix`'s OWN `opsInBody` COMMENT CITES AS THE MEASURED PROOF THAT
`ops` CANNOT BE A STATIC FIELD** — "its function closes over `user.name`, so the ops observed at two
different users DIFFER." ⇒ **THE GUARD FIRES ON ITS OWN DOCUMENTED WITNESS. THE ABORT IS BEHAVING EXACTLY AS
DESIGNED AND THE DESIGN'S PREMISE IS INTACT.** That is the strongest possible confirmation that `e6c8edc` is
correct-as-written and that the work is at `4kh.53.64` (the `ops` representation), not in the guard.

CONFOUNDS RULED OUT, each measured: `flake.lock` BYTE-IDENTICAL c42df53 <-> HEAD, so no gen-pin difference.
`lib/attributes/collections.nix` md5 `d40873fb34eaae71b0710755c3ac98f0` at ALL of 222af84, c42df53, e6c8edc
and HEAD — **the defect site is untouched; only REACHABILITY moved.** Predicate controls in the same run with
the real binary: `compose commitment` in lib/errors.nix is 0 at the c42df53 tree and 1 at HEAD; trace tokens
are c42df53 `id_hash` 2 / `compose commitment` 0, HEAD `id_hash` 0 / `compose commitment` 1 — **each arm is
the other's positive control.**
★ AND ON den-hoag-9xo.61'S BAD CITATION: `9ebf3316` confirmed ABSENT from nix-config (count 0; positive
control `4acf0a1d` = 1), so its measurement base stays unverifiable — **BUT ITS `id_hash` FINDING REPRODUCES
AT 4acf0a1d. THE FINDING SURVIVES ITS BAD CITATION.** A wrong rev citation is not a wrong finding, and I
should not have let the one cast doubt on the other.

STATED WOULD-OVERTURN, kept because it is honest: the guard-off patch replaces a throw with the site-mark
branch's own passthrough, so a non-site-mark `pipeOp` now carries `__policy` — if anything downstream branches
on that, the guard-off frontier is an artefact. The exact per-host match with `c42df53` argues strongly
against but does not exclude. Also unmeasured: the other four of `9xo.61`'s seven hosts, and whether `id_hash`
is itself terminal or masks something again.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ THE ENTIRE CORPUS BLOCKAGE IS **ONE DERIVING STAGE IN ONE POLICY** — and my note that index 8 "needs
instrumentation nobody has run" is REFUTED by elimination, no instrumentation required.
MEASURED over nix-config, with positive controls in the same run:
    pipe.as        -> **0**            (grep -rn 'pipe\.as\b')
    deriving stage -> **1**            (pipe.transform at modules/den/policies/pipes.nix:143)
    POSITIVE CONTROLS: pipe.from 17 · collect 9 · collectAll 4 · broadcast 4 · expose 2
The guard fires only on `derived.__derived || routes != [ ]`. With zero `as` and exactly one deriving stage,
**`broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares` IS THE ONLY CANDIDATE BY ELIMINATION — the positional index is irrelevant.**
⇒ ★★ **16 OF THE CORPUS'S 17 PIPE SITES ALREADY PASS.** The thing blocking every NixOS toplevel in the fleet
is a single `pipe.transform` whose function closes over `user.name`. That is a far smaller blast radius than
"the corpus cannot build" suggests, and it should change how the fix is scoped and how it is risked.

★ AND THE gen-pipe REUSE SCAN CAME BACK CLEAN, which removes a suspicion I had raised: **THE SEED DOES RUN
THROUGH gen-pipe's OWN PRIMITIVE.** `lib/concern-quirks.nix` is `pipe.compose (channelDecls ++ opDecls ++
policyOps)` — ONE call, no re-implementation. **NOT a fourth build-what-exists instance.** Surface scan: 17
gen-pipe exports, den-hoag uses `channel` `compose` `consume` `contribute` `deferred` `run` `map` `filter`
`fold` `over` `route`; unused are `scan` `join` `tee` `provenanceOf` `traceOf`. Hand-rolled duplication is
ALMOST NONE — `append`/`to`/`expose`/`broadcast`/`collect`/`collectAll`/`withProvenance` are **not gen-pipe
exports at all**, they are v1 verbs. Two genuine small gaps: `compose` computes an `idToName` internally and
does not export it (den-hoag rebuilds it), and a `closureOf` helper would remove `pipeChainOf` from every
consumer.
★ ALSO REFUTED: the standing "clones run ahead of the pin" caution is **FALSE FOR gen-pipe today** — clone
HEAD == `53509308` == both locks. True for gen-schema, not universal. Name the rev; do not assume the drift.

★★ AND den-hoag-4kh.36 IS **NOT** THE SAME CONSTRUCT AS THIS BEAD — they are TWO ENDS OF ONE SEAM, and I had
recorded them as possible duplicates. THIS bead is the DERIVING/ROUTE half, which can never reach the seed.
**4kh.36 is the SITE-MARK half: marks DO reach the per-node declaration via `gather.nix collectionDeclsAt`,
and are then NOT INTERPRETED.** Different failure, different fix. The ops spec closes this bead and
den-hoag-66t, and **LEAVES 4kh.36 OPEN.**

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ THE CORPUS BLOCKER CHAIN, MEASURED END TO END. **VERDICT ON den-hoag-4kh.53.64's PREMISE: UNSOUND AS
STATED.** Fixing the ops representation clears RUNG 1 ONLY and hands off to a NAMED SUCCESSOR. The corpus
still produces NO TOPLEVEL. ★ **THIS IS THE SAME "MOVED THE FAILURE EARLIER" SHAPE AS den-hoag-1kd, ONE LEVEL
UP** — if 53.64 lands as-is, the arc reads "critical path fixed" while corpus output stays at zero.

════ THE NO-GUARD TREE IS TRUSTWORTHY — ESTABLISHED THREE INDEPENDENT WAYS ════
1. /run/current-system/sw/bin/diff -r dh-head dh-head-noguard = EXACTLY ONE HUNK, lib/concern-policies.nix:209,
   `errors.opsInBody name` replaced by `a // { __policy = name; }`.
2. NOT STALE: diff -rq dh-head/lib <live repo>/lib exit 0 — BYTE-IDENTICAL to current HEAD.
3. The replacement text is byte-identical to (a) the `else` branch two lines below in the same
   conformingProduce, AND (b) c42df53's UNCONDITIONAL stamp at lib/concern-policies.nix:167.
★★ ⇒ **den-hoag-1kd's OWN STATED WOULD-OVERTURN IS CLOSED.** 1kd worried that a non-site-mark pipeOp now
carrying `__policy` would make the guard-off frontier an artefact if anything downstream branches on it.
c42df53 stamped `__policy` on EVERY kind unconditionally, and conformingProduce did not exist then. Guard-off
REPRODUCES PRE-GUARD BEHAVIOUR EXACTLY; it is not a novel state.

════ THE CHAIN ════
RUNG 1 — ALL THREE HOSTS. den-hoag throw, lib/errors.nix:190 opsInBody, raised at concern-policies.nix:209:
  "den-hoag: compose commitment: policy `__kindInclude__user__policy__8` produced a `pipeOp` declaration
   carrying a derived-channel DAG or a delivery route from its BODY..."
★ THEN THE CHAIN FORKS PER HOST.

──── axon-01 / blade ────
RUNG 2 — a NIX-LEVEL ABORT, not a den-hoag throw:
  "error: attribute 'id_hash' missing" at lib/attributes/collections.nix:205:32 — `identity = a.content.id_hash;`
★ NEW BEYOND 1kd/9xo.61 — THE OFFENDER IS PINNED BY NAME, NOT INFERRED. The site was instrumented to dump the
record: `a` keys = ["content","key","sharedFoldKey"]; `a.content` keys = ["home-manager",
"homeManagerModules","name","nixos"] — it carries `name` and NO `id_hash`. Channel homeManagerModules,
coordKinds ["host","user"]. Offenders: axon-01 agenix-identity/{dvicory,pol,sini,theutz,vic}@axon-01;
blade agenix-identity/{shuo,sini,will}@blade.
★★ **`a.key` = "__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0" — IDENTICAL FOR EVERY USER ON A HOST.** So the
obvious repair `aspectIdHash a.key` **COLLIDES ALL PRODUCERS**. Only content.name distinguishes them. This is
the nested-aspect "crosses the bridge as a BARE content set (no id_hash/name)" shape that
ci/tests/compat-nested-aspects.nix:9,20 documents. WHOEVER WRITES THE FIX NEEDS THIS — IT IS A LIVE TRAP.
content.id_hash is read at EXACTLY ONE site in lib/ (positive control: content.name = 4 files), so no second
consumer is being bypassed.

RUNG 3 — reached by substituting a synthetic identity. DIFFERENT PER HOST.
· axon-01: "error: The option `services' was accessed but has no value defined." — nixpkgs lib/modules.nix:1267.
  Localized to the HOME-MANAGER USER SUBMODULE: config.home-manager.users.sini.services reproduces it, while
  config.home-manager.users attrNames SUCCEEDS returning ["dvicory","pol","sini","theutz","vic"].
  builtins.attrNames on the user config also throws.
· blade: "error: attribute 'image' missing" at stylix mk-target.nix:224:28 (`inherit (cfg.${argument})
  override;`), via assertions → core.impermanence.nixos → stylix modules/gnome/hm.nix. stylix.image is
  undelivered into the HM user config.

──── cortex — FORKS EARLIER, AT RUNG 2 ────
RUNG 2: "error: attribute 'aspect' missing" at nix-config/modules/den/aspects/virtualization/
microvm-guests.nix:43:77 — CORPUS CODE calling `den.lib.aspects.resolve "microvm" vm.aspect`. den-hoag DROPS
`aspect` off the microvm-guest entity. Via assertions → microvm.vms → virtualization.microvm-host.nixos.
★ CORTEX NEVER REACHES THE id_hash SITE. Probe trace counts, same predicate, same instrument, same run
family: axon 20 / blade 12 / **cortex 0**.
RUNG 3: with `vm.aspect` stubbed to `vm.aspect or { }` in a scratchpad nix-config copy (whole-tree
`/run/current-system/sw/bin/diff -rq --exclude=.git` = ONE FILE, ONE LINE), the next failure is in
**den-hoag's own** lib/compat/resolve-verbs.nix:44:20 — `nodeOf = handle: handle.__denNode;`,
"attribute '__denNode' missing". A Nix-level abort.

════ DOES THE CHAIN TERMINATE IN A TOPLEVEL? **NO.** ════
Deepest reached: rung 3 on all three hosts, ALL EXIT 1, exit codes read from $? into .exit files and NEVER
through a pipe. ★ **EVERY den-hoag .out IS 0 BYTES ON EVERY HOST AT EVERY DEPTH — no drvPath was ever
produced, so there was nothing to force.**
★ ATTRIBUTION CONTROL: all three hosts build EXIT 0 on the corpus's OWN PINNED den v1 (denful/den rev
99cc0c5a1cc846cb1be681344b10d2731d430e13), with real .drv files VERIFIED TO EXIST ON DISK —
blade /nix/store/a5g05y5rawspvbg1pkabw6p0m8f4vgr6-nixos-system-blade-26.11.20260723.e2587ca.drv and
cortex /nix/store/hvj9k6kdc2yj7bdpfvbx4waj3cddj6ni-nixos-system-cortex-26.11.20260723.e2587ca.drv.
⇒ **EVERY RUNG ≥2 IS A den-hoag DIVERGENCE, NOT A CORPUS BUG.**

════ ★ FOUR HYPOTHESES REFUTED BY THE SCOUT, REPORTED AS RESULTS ════
1. "The no-guard tree is stale or mis-edited" — REFUTED (lib byte-identical to HEAD; one hunk).
2. "__policy on a non-site-mark pipeOp makes guard-off an artefact" — 1kd's OWN stated would-overturn —
   REFUTED by c42df53:167's unconditional stamp.
3. ★ "Rung 3 is an artefact of the synthetic A12 ordering" — REFUTED BY AN ORDERING CONTROL. A second scheme
   (ZZALT| vs PROBE| hash prefix) was VERIFIED TO GENUINELY PERMUTE producer order
   (theutz,vic,sini,dvicory,pol → vic,theutz,dvicory,sini,pol) and axon-01's terminal error is BYTE-IDENTICAL
   under both.
4. "A second lib/ reader of content.id_hash was silently bypassed" — REFUTED, one reader only.

════ COVERAGE — HONEST, AND THE LIMITS MATTER ════
· THREE hosts measured (axon-01, blade, cortex), nix-config ONLY. The 19 external configs in
  ~/Documents/repos/den-configs were NOT measured. 9xo.61's other four hosts NOT measured.
· ★ RUNG 1 WAS GENUINELY DISABLED. **RUNG 2 WAS NOT FIXED ON ANY HOST — IT WAS BYPASSED** (synthetic identity
  on axon/blade, a corpus stub on cortex). So rung 3 is measured UNDER SUBSTITUTION. Mitigated by the
  ordering control and the single-reader grep, but A REAL FIX COULD DIFFER — notably, a correct fix stamps
  id_hash ONTO a.content, whereas the probe left content unchanged.
· ★★ **RUNG 3 COULD NOT BE DISABLED ANYWHERE.** axon's `services` and blade's `stylix.image` live inside
  HM/stylix module eval; cortex's __denNode is a den-hoag compat defect needing a real fix, not a stub.
  ⇒ **CHAIN DEPTH ≥3 PER HOST IS A FLOOR, NOT A CEILING.**
· axon's rung-3 attribution to a den-hoag delivery gap rests on READING plus the den v1 control, NOT on
  isolating the missing module. What declares or reads that `services` was not identified.
· Everything else rests on execution.

title: [perf] CONFIRMED BY TWO INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATIONS: den-hoag is CUBIC IN CELL COUNT (exponent 2.98, constant offset 260 across all eight rungs) — the ~7000-cell target is ~1.5e12 function calls
description:
★★★ MEASURED 2026-07-29, NOT READ. THE NODE-ENUMERATION PATH IS CUBIC IN CELL COUNT. This is the first
scaling defect in this project established by EXECUTION rather than by reading asymptotics off source, and
it was found by the calibration runs of the witness den-hoag-4kh.53.74 says does not exist.

THE MEASUREMENT. Forcing `attrNames den.structural.eval.allNodes` over a synthetic H-host x 2-user fleet,
floor-subtracted, successive ratios per doubling:
    1.78 -> 2.36 -> 3.69 -> 5.67 -> 7.10 -> 7.69 -> 7.89
7.89 -> 2^3. Exponent estimates rise MONOTONICALLY toward the asymptote (2.50 -> 2.83 -> 2.94 -> 2.98), so
every early stop UNDERSTATES — which is why the witness spec makes an unconverged estimate a FAILURE rather
than a datapoint.
AT H=128 (256 cells): 72,042,060 function calls, 14.2 s.

title: [decision] RESOLVED: do NOT declare the 12 — the compliant form cannot be authored, so they are an unimplemented surface rather than a known-fail; declare the other 6 instead
description:
OWNER DECISION. Raised rather than resolved, because it is a question about what the gate MEANS, not about which mechanism implements it.

THE FACTS, measured at 4b61112. The 12 den-pipe failures are ThrownError from errors.opsInBody, reached from lib/concern-policies.nix at 'else if k == "pipeOp" && !(declare.isSiteMarkData a) then errors.opsInBody name'. They are 12 of the 18 known-red — the largest cluster — and the three-state gate design (den-hoag-9uv) assigns them twelve xfail declarations.

★★ BUT THE COMMENT IMMEDIATELY ABOVE opsInBody IN lib/errors.nix SAYS THE FLEET COMPOSE SEED'S CONSTRUCTION 'IS WRONG UPSTREAM OF THIS SHIM RATHER THAN MERELY UNWIRED HERE ... DO NOT WORK AROUND THIS IN THE SHIM.'
⇒ THESE TWELVE ARE AN ACKNOWLEDGED UNRESOLVED DEFECT, NOT INTENDED BEHAVIOUR. Declaring them as expected errors converts twelve RED PARITY GAPS into twelve GREEN TESTS THAT PIN THE DEFECT AS EXPECTED. The suite would then assert that den-hoag CORRECTLY REFUSES a construct it is supposed to eventually support.

THE TENSION IS REAL IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the project's own rules point opposite ways:
  FOR DECLARING — CI is three-state by owner ruling and an armed failing test is a LANDING, not a blocker. Eighteen anonymous reds mean the gate carries zero information (den-hoag-9uv); attribution has to live in the tree, not a commit message. And a declared xfail that STARTS PASSING fails the gate, so the day the upstream defect is fixed, the gate says so loudly. That is the argument that a declaration is a TRACKING device, not an endorsement.
  AGAINST — the errors.nix comment is an explicit instruction not to accommodate this in the test layer, and a green test is what a reader trusts INSTEAD of reading. Twelve green tests naming a compose-commitment law would read as the law being correct and enforced, when the law's own author recorded that its premise is wrong upstream. That is the vacuous-anchor failure (den-hoag-akj) arriving by a different route: not a test that cannot fail, but a test that passes for a reason nobody intends to keep.

THE MIDDLE OPTIONS, neither costless: (a) declare them but make the DECLARATION carry the upstream bead id and the word provisional, so the tree records that these pin a defect rather than a law — this is what the required 'bead'/'construct' fields in the 9uv design are for, and it may be exactly the case they were designed for; (b) leave them red, accept that the gate stays uninformative until the upstream construction is fixed, and fix that first.
★ NOTE WHAT (b) COSTS: the gate is currently ONE BOOLEAN PINNED AT 1 and CI has been red on main since e6c8edc. Leaving twelve of eighteen undeclared means the gate keeps carrying zero information for as long as the upstream fix takes.
★ AND NOTE WHAT MAY DECIDE IT ANYWAY: den-hoag-4kh.51 records that a suppression path's soundness rests on the staged pre-pass scheduled for retirement (register den-hoag-4kh.17 entry 3). IF THESE TWELVE ARE DOWNSTREAM OF THAT, THEY GO GREEN WHEN IT RETIRES — and under 'a known-fail that starts passing must fail the gate' that turns a successful retirement into a gate failure unless the declarations retire in the same change. Establishing whether they are downstream of entry 3 may make this decision for us, and that is a measurement, not a ruling.

REPORTED BY THE SCOPING AGENT AS A FLAG, EXPLICITLY NOT ARGUED: 'Migrating them to expectedError turns 12 red parity gaps into 12 green tests that PIN the defect as expected. That is a design decision, not a mechanical migration — I am reporting it, not arguing it.'

title: [kernel] CONFIRMED LIVE BY EXECUTION on a PUBLIC surface: one containment binding silently drops a root settings layer (workers 16 -> 1), two throw unknown-dim — coordDims is a negative enumeration over an open key set
description:
MEASURED BY READING 2026-07-29 at HEAD 6f30460, found while settling whether __coords can become a graph query (den-hoag-5ae). NO nix eval was run — this is source-derived, and the reachability preconditions are stated below precisely so it can be FALSIFIED by constructing the case.

THE SHAPE. lib/attributes/resolved-settings.nix computes a node's coordinate map by NEGATIVE ENUMERATION:
    coordDims = removeAttrs (node.decls or { }) [ "__entry" "__edges" "__containment" "__coords" "__root" ]
i.e. 'the coordinates are whatever is left after removing the machinery keys I know about'. ★ THAT IS ONLY SOUND IF THE KEY SET IS CLOSED. IT IS NOT.
lib/default.nix builds scopeRoots as
    decls = node.decls // (prePass.containmentBindings.${id} or { }) // systemView // prelude.optionalAttrs (prePass.suppressions ? ${id}) { suppressedPolicies = ...; }
and THAT DECORATED MAP IS WHAT gen-scope RECEIVES (roots = scopeRoots), so self.node id returns the polluted decls.
THREE POLLUTION SOURCES, NONE IN THE STRIP LIST:
  systemView — lib/compat/bridge.nix flakeViews = { inputs'; self'; }, folded onto EVERY root whose __entry.system matches. ★ THE WHOLE COMPAT PATH.
  containmentBindings.${id} — USER-NAMED binding keys (e.g. bindings.grant in ci/tests/topology-join.nix).
  suppressedPolicies — ★ lib/attributes/structural.nix STRIPS this key; resolved-settings.nix coordDims DOES NOT.

CONSEQUENCES at an affected root once an aspect is present there — TWO, and they are opposite:
  key count lands != |dimKinds| ⇒ isFullCell false ⇒ the flat arm ⇒ coordsEq compares ["host" "inputs'" "self'"] against a layer's ["host"] ⇒ ★ EVERY ROOT-SCOPED den.settings.layers ENTRY IS SILENTLY DROPPED.
  key count lands == |dimKinds| by coincidence (e.g. { host, grant } against dimKinds = [ "host" "user" ]) ⇒ isFullCell TRUE ⇒ containmentChain ⇒ gen-product HARD THROW 'unknown-dim grant'.
★ isFullCell IS A CARDINALITY TEST, NOT A KEY-IDENTITY TEST: isFullCell = builtins.length (builtins.attrNames coords) == builtins.length dimKinds. A wrong key set of the RIGHT SIZE passes it.

WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN — and this is the falsification recipe, not an excuse. LAZINESS: coords is only forced inside map ... present, so a root with present == [ ] never evaluates it. AND the compat path declares no settings layers: grep -rn 'den.settings.layers' lib/compat/ -> 0 hits, POSITIVE CONTROL SAME RUN grep -rn 'den\.aspects' lib/compat/ -> 99 hits, so the grep reaches that tree. Nine ci test files declare den.settings.layers and seven set systemViews/containTo; THE TWO IN BOTH SETS are ci/tests/settings-witness.nix and ci/tests/topology-join.nix — and in both, the aspect is included at the USER CELL and resolved-settings is read at the CELL id, so the polluted ROOTS are never forced.
⇒ TO FALSIFY OR CONFIRM: construct a root carrying a present aspect AND a folded decls key (a systemView is the easiest — it lands on every matching root automatically). Then read resolved-settings at the ROOT id, not the cell id.

★★ WHY THIS IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE MIGRATION RATHER THAN A BUG BESIDE IT: A NEGATIVE ENUMERATION CANNOT BE MADE TOTAL AGAINST AN OPEN KEY SET. systemView's keys are ARBITRARY BY DEFINITION — inputs' and self' today, whatever the compat bridge folds tomorrow — so NO STRIP LIST CAN EVER COVER THEM, and every future fold silently widens the hole. A per-dimension keyed contains-edge query is a POSITIVE ENUMERATION and closes this BY CONSTRUCTION. This is a repair that cannot be completed versus a construction in which the defect cannot arise.
⇒ RECOMMENDATION CARRIED INTO den-hoag-5ae: the migration spec must OWN THE ROOT-ARM REPLACEMENT rather than leaving coordDims in place beside the new query.

★ AND IT SETTLES THE STRIP-LIST QUESTION MORE PRECISELY THAN EITHER EARLIER READ. Both prior findings were partly right: the __entry split IS purposeful (the two coordDims sites are coordinate projections, __entry is not a coordinate) — so den-hoag-5ae's original 'four lists have drifted' framing stays withdrawn. BUT the suppressedPolicies omission in coordDims is a REAL DIVERGENCE WITH A REAL CONSEQUENCE, because coordDims' output is counted rather than checked. Two lists differing is not a defect; two lists differing where one of them is a negative enumeration feeding a cardinality test IS.

title: [ci] BLOCKING: den-compat-test.nix's hasExpectedError SILENTLY ERASES type and msg before nix-unit sees the leaf — it is why the three-state gate spec cannot reach 12 of its 18, and it exists because of the instrument that spec drops
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 at HEAD 6f30460 while specifying den-hoag-9uv. Returned to the orchestrator, not filed by the finder.

ci/tests/_lib/den-compat-test.nix binds hasExpectedError, which lowers to
    { expr = (builtins.tryEval (builtins.deepSeq expr expr)).success; expected = false; }
TWO INDEPENDENT WEAKNESSES, both measured against a probe run the same session:
 1. ★ tryEval CATCHES ONLY throw AND assert. Missing-attribute, type error and division-by-zero PROPAGATE STRAIGHT THROUGH IT — measured on a throwaway file with nix eval --impure. So a test asserting 'this aborts' via hasExpectedError DOES NOT PASS when the abort is an EvalError; IT KILLS THE EVALUATION. The failure mode is not a false green, it is a confusing red attributed to the wrong thing.
 2. ★ IT DISCARDS THE MESSAGE ENTIRELY. Any error at all satisfies it. A test named for one abort passes on a completely different one — the signature-is-not-a-cause failure, embedded in a helper.
★★ AND IT SHADOWS THE NAME OF THE STRONGER THING. nix-unit 2.35.1 ships a NATIVE expectedError = { type; msg; } which: catches EvalError (measured: { a = 1; }.b with type = "EvalError" PASSES); FAILS when the expression does not throw at all ('Expected error, but no error was caught'); FAILS on a type mismatch; and matches msg as an UNANCHORED SUBSTRING so no regex padding is needed. The native channel is strictly stronger on every axis, and the in-tree helper wearing nearly its name is the weaker one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR den-hoag-9uv: the spec adopts the NATIVE channel. This helper then becomes an actively misleading neighbour — a future author reaching for 'the expectedError thing' in ci/tests/_lib/ finds the weak one. Decide whether hasExpectedError is re-implemented on top of the native channel, deleted with its call sites migrated, or renamed to say what it actually does (something like 'throwsOrAsserts').
★ BEFORE ANY OF THAT: ENUMERATE ITS CALL SITES AND CHECK EACH FOR THE CLASS-2 WEAKNESS — a test currently passing on the wrong error is indistinguishable from one passing on the right error, so migration to the native channel may turn up reds that were always wrong. That is a feature, and it should be expected rather than treated as a regression.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ SCOPED. THE CRUX IS ANSWERED AND IT INVERTS THE TASK: **DELETION ALONE DOES NOT ENABLE THE NATIVE CHANNEL. denTest CONSTRUCTS ITS OUTPUT FROM A FIXED KEY SET.** This is a TWO-PART CHANGE, not a removal. Measured at 4b61112, tree clean.

THE CONSTRUCTOR, quoted. out is read at exactly three places — out.expr, out.expected, out ? expectedError — and is NEVER SPREAD (grep -n 'out //|// out' -> NOTHING; positive control grep -n 'out = ' -> the expected single site). Every branch builds a LITERAL 2-KEY ATTRSET:
    if hasExpectedError then { expr = (tryEval (deepSeq expr expr)).success; expected = false; }
    else let expected = out.expected; in
      if isAttrs expected && isAttrs expr then { expr = intersectAttrs expected expr; inherit expected; }
      else { inherit expr expected; }
CONSEQUENCES OF DELETING ONLY THE ARM:
  expectedError-only leaf -> falls to the else branch -> out.expected -> LOUD 'attribute expected missing'. Not silent, which is the good case.
  leaf carrying BOTH expected and expectedError -> ★ SILENT DROP: the else branch compares against expected and expectedError VANISHES.
  Either way expectedError NEVER REACHES NIX-UNIT.
⇒ THE FIX IS: delete hasExpectedError and its arm, AND ADD AN EXPLICIT FORWARDING ARM emitting { expr; expectedError; }.
★★ AND A HARD CONSTRAINT MEASURED ON THE INSTRUMENT: A LEAF CARRYING BOTH expected AND expectedError MAKES NIX-UNIT ☢️ — the throw escapes UNCAUGHT and expectedError does not win. SO THE FORWARDING ARM MUST EMIT THE LEAF WITHOUT expected.
★ AND THE removeAttrs ENTRY FOR "expectedError" MUST STAY — it is what keeps the key off the flake-parts module face. Deleting it too makes any future expectedError declaration an undeclared-option error.

THE ARM IS DEAD — VERIFIED EXACTLY. grep -rn expectedError over the whole repo (excluding .git/.worktrees/.beads) returns SIX hits TOTAL: four in _lib/den-compat-test.nix (two header comments, the removeAttrs string, the binding) and two COMMENTS in b1-supportedness.nix and compat-nested-class-named-aspect.nix. ZERO test files pass it through denTest; ZERO pass it directly to nix-unit.
POSITIVE CONTROLS, same runs: (a) same predicate with .worktrees INCLUDED -> 4 hits, so the token is matchable and the exclusion is what removes them; (b) grep -rln 'expected' over den-behavioral/ -> 56 of the 57 importers, so grep reaches these files with an assertion-key predicate and expectedError matches none.
IMPORTERS ARE 57, NOT 59 — my figure was wrong. Re-derived positively: grep -rln 'import \.\./_lib/den-compat-test\.nix' -> 57 (56 in den-behavioral/ plus flake-namespace.nix). The 59 count included the scaffold matching its own moduleLocation string and a PROSE COMMENT in ci/flake.nix.

SEPARABILITY CONFIRMED: denTest has EIGHT responsibilities (flake-parts wrapping with the removeAttrs face, evalFlakeModule through the real bridge, v1 denTest defaults, hm seed/gate modules, env seed with the derived-primitive shape, helper splicing, double invocation of testFn, and leaf shaping). hasExpectedError is bound in the same let as out/expr and READ AT EXACTLY ONE SITE. Nothing in the other seven reads it.

mkCi IS NOT A SECOND DROP SITE, verified on the LOCKED rev (ci/flake.lock pins gen 793f83f; ★ the local clone at cb10282 is AHEAD and NOT AUTHORITATIVE): options.flake.tests is lazyAttrsOf (lazyAttrsOf raw) — the leaf is raw, untouched. Nothing else in den-hoag reads config.flake.tests.
mkCi/assertTests CONFIRMED NOT RUN IN CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml has exactly two jobs and four run: steps — nix fmt -- --ci, and the two nix-unit invocations. No nix flake check, no checks.default reference anywhere, and den-hoag's root flake declares no checks. treefmt.flakeCheck = false and pre-commit.check.enable = false in the locked gen, so nothing is injected from that side either. ⇒ THE ARM'S STATED REASON HAS ALREADY EXPIRED.
★ NOTE FOR THE MIGRATION: testSingletons DOES NOT EXIST at the LOCKED gen rev (only at local cb10282), so #tests.<suite> is the finest granularity that runs until the ci lock is bumped.

MIGRATION UNIT: PER-TEST, and partial is coherent. Stage A is ONE edit to the scaffold, shared by all 57 importers but INERT for every leaf declaring no expectedError — i.e. all 57 today, so it is byte-neutral to the suite. Stage B is per-LEAF; suite membership is irrelevant to leaf shape, so den-pipe being declared across five files constrains nothing, and migrating some of the 12 leaves the rest coherently ☢️.

title: [kernel] the nine framework edge kinds get their projection tag from a DEFAULT, not a declaration — absence-is-a-decision; the seed is in lib/edges.nix, and the parity-hazard story I first gave for it is refuted
description:
MEASURED at HEAD 6f30460 while answering den-hoag-5bp. Found as a by-product, which is why it was never seen: it is INERT TODAY and becomes LIVE ONLY when the migration it blocks is attempted.

MECHANISM. lib/reserved-registry.nix's mkReservedRegistry seeds
    reserved = prelude.genAttrs reservedNames (n: { stratum = ...; })
with NO 'to' FIELD. Then allRaw = reserved // table passes through entryOf, whose default is
    to = raw.to or "materialize"
⇒ contains, include, kindOf, member, reach and reach-suppress ALL COMPILE WITH to = "materialize".

NOT AN INFERENCE — THE TREE STATES IT. ci/tests/projection-tag.nix:8 says verbatim that 'EVERY other kind (framework-pre-registered, user den.edges, demand/cascade) defaults to = "materialize"', and line 117 PINS expected = "materialize" for a framework kind. The behaviour is asserted by a test, so it is intended-as-built, not an accident of reading.

WHY IT IS INERT TODAY: the pools are PHYSICALLY SEPARATE. memberEdges and relationEdges never merge into edgesForRoot — lib/default.nix states memberEdges are 'NOT in output.edgesForRoot / the live trace', and output-modules.nix states relation edges 'live in a separate pool never merged into edgesForRoot'. Nothing structural currently reaches materializeFilter, so the wrong tag costs nothing.

★★ WHY IT IS A LANDMINE. den-hoag-5ae's migration produces a contains edge from fleet.nix's containmentPairs into the relation pool. THE MOMENT SUCH AN EDGE REACHES edgesForRoot, materializeFilter KEEPS IT — because its kind says materialize — AND IT LANDS ON THE FROZEN PARITY TRACE. The failure would appear as a parity divergence in the oracle, attributed to the migration, with the actual cause four files away in a registry seed. That is the most expensive possible way to discover this.

THE FIX BELONGS AT THE SEED, NOT PER-PRODUCER. The relations desugar ALREADY solved the same problem by stamping to = "query" explicitly on its rows — so there is an in-tree precedent and this is a BY-CONSTRUCTION fix, not a new design. But preRegisteredStrata carries ONLY strata today (contains/include/kindOf = structural, member/reach/reach-suppress = resolution, nest/defer = output, demand = demand): ★ THE ROW SHAPE HAS NO PLACE TO SAY 'to'. So the change is to the row shape plus the six seeds, and a per-producer stamp would be the repair rather than the construction — it would leave the wrong default in place for the seventh kind, whenever that arrives.

RELATED PRODUCER CENSUS, same run, correcting an earlier claim that only 'demand' had a producer. Command: for k in contains include kindOf member reach reach-suppress nest defer demand; do grep -rn "kind = \"$k\"" --include='*.nix' lib/; done — POSITIVE CONTROL: the predicate fired on 3 of 9 in the same run, so the six zeros are about the code.
  member -> lib/concern-collectors.nix:200 (Model-Q intent shape, does not reach the live trace)
  nest   -> lib/edges.nix:453 (receiver-gated; its own comment: 'the corpus producer set is EMPTY by construction')
  demand -> lib/demand.nix:159 and :173 (Model D, the one kind genuinely live)
  contains / include / kindOf / reach / reach-suppress / defer -> ZERO PRODUCERS.
★ AND NO USER SURFACE CAN EVER SUPPLY ONE: user kinds arrive through relationsToEdgeKinds / claimEdgesOf, but relationCollisionMessage REJECTS any label in reservedNames. These six are framework-reserved names awaiting a framework producer — the registry declares a topology the kernel does not build, and has reserved the names against anyone else building it.

BLOCKS den-hoag-5ae. Any spec for the payload-to-edge migration must state which projection tag its new edges carry and why, and must fix the seed rather than stamping at the producer.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THREE CORRECTIONS FROM THE MIGRATION SPEC, 2026-07-29, each measured.

1. ★ **NINE RESERVED KINDS DEFAULT TO `to = "materialize"`, NOT SIX.** Measured via `compileEdges`. My bead
   named six (contains/include/kindOf/member/reach/reach-suppress) and omitted nest/defer/demand. The seed
   fix must cover the row shape for all nine, and the spec's rule — MATERIALIZE IFF IT DELIVERS CONTENT —
   splits them: the six structural+resolution kinds become `query`, while nest/defer/demand correctly STAY
   `materialize`. The `or "materialize"` default survives for USER kinds only.
2. ★ **NO TEST PINS `contains`/`include`/`kindOf` — 0/0/0**, with same-run positive controls `member` = 2 and
   `materialize` = 23. So re-tagging those three is ASSERTION-FREE. `member` is different: re-tagging it
   breaks one test, which the spec re-points. My bead's claim that the projection tag is pinned was accurate
   for the tag in general and OVER-EXTENDED to these three specifically.
3. THE COST IS WORSE THAN THIS BEAD STATES, AND IT MAKES A PREREQUISITE OF SOMETHING I HAD DEPRIORITISED.
   Today's cost is O(N.K.E) = **O(N^2.K)**, because `denQuery` rebuilds `perLabelFromEdges` INSIDE ITS OWN
   LET and Nix has no CSE. ★ THE COORDINATE QUERY RUNS AT EVERY NODE, SO THE MIGRATION CONVERTS A LATENT
   O(N^2) INTO A LIVE ONE. ⇒ THE ADJACENCY HOIST (den-hoag-ag3) MUST LAND IN THIS CHANGE, not after it.
   I had just deprioritised ag3 on the grounds that the cell-path cubic dominates it (den-hoag-qxz). Both
   are true and they are not in tension: ag3 is not the leading term TODAY, and it becomes a prerequisite
   THE MOMENT the coordinate query goes live. Sequencing, not priority.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD, BOTH MINE, BOTH MEASURED BY THE MIGRATION SPEC'S REVIEWER.

1. **THE EDIT SITE IS MISATTRIBUTED.** I wrote that `mkReservedRegistry` in `lib/reserved-registry.nix` seeds
   the rows. It does not. `preRegisteredStrata` AND the row expression
   `reserved = prelude.genAttrs reservedNames (n: { stratum = preRegisteredStrata.${n}; })` are **BOTH IN
   `lib/edges.nix`**; `mkReservedRegistry` is the GENERIC COMBINATOR that receives them. The fix lands in
   edges.nix, not reserved-registry.nix — and an implementer following this bead would have opened the wrong
   file first.

2. ★★ **THE PARITY-DIVERGENCE STORY IS WRONG FOR THE MIGRATION AS DESIGNED, AND IT WAS THIS BEAD'S HEADLINE.**
   I wrote that the moment a `contains` edge reaches `edgesForRoot`, `materializeFilter` keeps it and it
   lands on the frozen parity trace. MEASURED: `to` is read at EXACTLY ONE SITE — `projectsMaterialize`'s
   `to = if k == null then "materialize" else (compiledKinds.${k}.to or "materialize")` — applied only inside
   `edgesForRoot`. And `edgesForRoot = materializeFilter (edge.edgesFor { graph = graphAccessor; ... } ++
   demandEdges)`, where `graphAccessor`'s ONLY edge field is `edgesAt = deliveryEdgesAt`.
   ⇒ **A Model-Q RELATION-POOL EDGE CANNOT REACH THE FILTER AT ALL.** The migration routes `contains` into
   the relation pool, so the landmine I described does not arm.
   ⇒ THE SEED FIX STILL STANDS — but on **ABSENCE IS A DECISION**, not on a parity hazard: a registry row
   whose `to` is decided by a DEFAULT rather than DECLARED is a field that should be total and is not.
   ★ AND NOTE THE COST OF THE WRONG STORY: nothing in the migration can DEMONSTRATE the fix worked, because
   the failure it was supposed to prevent cannot occur on that path. A fix justified by a hazard that cannot
   fire has no witness — which is precisely why the reviewer marked the corresponding witness as unable to
   fail.

3. Also corrected upstream and repeated here so this bead is self-consistent: **NINE reserved kinds default,
   not six** — nest/defer/demand default too, and correctly STAY `materialize` under the rule "materialize
   iff it delivers content". And **no test pins `contains`/`include`/`kindOf`** (0/0/0, same-run controls
   `member` 2 and `materialize` 23), so retagging those three is assertion-free while `member` breaks one
   test that must be re-pointed.

⇒ NET: the defect is real, the remedy is unchanged, and BOTH REASONS I GAVE FOR IT WERE WRONG. Recorded in
full rather than quietly edited, because "right fix, wrong reason" is the failure mode that makes a fix
unfalsifiable — the same shape as the `__entry` boundary I asserted as external and that turned out to be a
default we chose.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ A SECOND absence-implies-materialize SURVIVES AT THE **READ** SITE, and this bead only covers the seed. Measured 2026-07-29 by the containment gate reviewer.
lib/edges.nix : to = if k == null then "materialize" else (compiledKinds.${k}.to or "materialize")
⇒ EVEN WITH THE SEED MADE TOTAL, ANY EDGE WHOSE kind STRING IS ABSENT FROM THE COMPILED TABLE STILL LANDS ON THE TRACE. The absence-is-a-decision argument, unapplied one file over from where this bead applies it.
★ NOTE THE TWO ARE NOT REDUNDANT: making the seed total fixes what the table CONTAINS; this  fixes what happens when a lookup MISSES. A kind can be absent from the table for reasons the seed cannot prevent — a dynamically-registered user kind, a typo in a producer, a kind removed while a producer still emits it. Fix both or state why the read-site default is safe.
Related and also measured in the same review: the rename's reference set is wider than this bead names — preRegisteredStrata has FIVE in-file references (definition; reservedNames = attrNames preRegisteredStrata; entryOf's stratum fallback; the reserved seed; the module EXPORT) plus ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix. Any row-shape change touches all six.

title: [ci] THE THREE-STATE GATE IS PROSE ONLY — it is a single boolean already pinned at 1, so at HEAD the gate carries ZERO INFORMATION, and the 18 known-red are attributed nowhere but a commit message
description:
MEASURED at HEAD 6f30460 by a read-only suite sweep. Exit status read on the line AFTER each command, never through a pipe (zsh has no \$PIPESTATUS).
  nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests      1919/1937  EXIT 1
  nix-unit --flake ./parity#tests    71/71    EXIT 0
  cd ci && nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.default -L   EXIT 1

★★★ THE RULE 'a known-fail that starts PASSING must also fail the gate' EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE REPO.
grep -rniE 'xfail|expected[-_]?fail|knownred|known[-_]red|allow[-_]?fail|expectedRed|armed[-_]red' over ci/ parity/ .github/ -> 0 HITS.
POSITIVE CONTROL, same instrument same run: expectedError -> 5 hits (ci/tests/_lib/den-compat-test.nix:4,27,205,263 and compat-nested-class-named-aspect.nix:217); den-hoag-4kh in CLAUDE.md -> 1 hit. The instrument matches when the thing is there. The zero is about the repo.

.github/workflows/ci.yml runs a BARE nix run nixpkgs#nix-unit -- --flake ./ci#tests. No baseline, no allowlist, no diff. CONSEQUENCES, and the third is the one that matters:
  1. GITHUB CI IS RED ON EVERY PUSH TO main RIGHT NOW and has been since e6c8edc.
  2. checks.default is a DIFFERENT and STRICTLY LESS INFORMATIVE instrument — gen/ci/flakeModule.nix's homegrown assertTests THROWS ON THE FIRST MISMATCH. It exited 1 reporting only compat-feature-severed.test-probeSentinel-off-parks. It cannot enumerate the 18.
  3. ★★ THE GATE IS A SINGLE BOOLEAN ALREADY PINNED AT 1. A 19th unexpected failure, a known-red silently going green, and the intended status quo are ALL INDISTINGUISHABLE TO IT. At HEAD THE GATE CARRIES ZERO INFORMATION, and because it is red on main the signal is already habituated away. This is the instrument every other quality finding depends on, and it detects nothing.

★ nix-unit USES THREE MARKERS, NOT TWO: 1919 ✅, 6 ❌ (value mismatch), 12 ☢️ (eval error). 1919+6+12 = 1937, arithmetic closes. ★ THE 12 ☢️ PRODUCE NO ❌ LINE — ANY NAME-ONLY GREP FOR FAILURES UNDERCOUNTS BY TWELVE. That is a live counting trap for every future triage.

18 KNOWN-RED CROSS-CHECK: ALL 18 STILL RED, EVERY STATED CAUSE CONFIRMED, NONE HAS STARTED PASSING.
  12 ☢️ den-pipe.test-*, each trace ending 'compose commitment: policy ... produced a pipeOp declaration carrying a derived-channel DAG or a delivery route from its BODY'
  4 ❌ pipe-consume.{test-derived-channels-consumed 0!=3, test-for-single-derived 0!=2, test-for-honored-as-over false!=true, test-transform-stays-map false!=true} — all measured-empty
  1 ❌ compat-scope-local-firing.test-expansion-collapses-to-one-rule, subRuleCount 0 vs 1 (den-hoag-9xo.75)
  1 ❌ compat-feature-severed.test-probeSentinel-off-parks (deliberate expected-red)

★★ BUT ATTRIBUTION FAILS THE STATED BAR. grep -rn '9xo' over ci/ parity/ *.md -> ZERO HITS. Across the five red-bearing files (pipe-policy.nix, pipe-broadcast.nix, pipe-consume.nix, compat-scope-local-firing.nix, compat-feature-severed.nix) THERE IS NOT ONE BEAD ID. Positive control: the same regex matched den-hoag-4kh in CLAUDE.md and found near-miss strings den-hoag-abs / den-hoag-nat in ci/ (identifiers, not ids).
⇒ e6c8edc's message says 'zero unattributed'. THAT IS TRUE OF THE COMMIT MESSAGE ONLY. In the tree the 18 reds are ANONYMOUS, and the message is one git log away from being the sole record of why anything is red. ★ THIS IS EXACTLY THE OWNER'S REPORTED SYMPTOM — agents cannot reason about the state — with a mechanical cause and a cheap fix.

REMEDY SHAPE (unvalidated, goes to the gate den-hoag-4kh.6 before it becomes work): the gate must compare the observed result set against a CHECKED-IN BASELINE keyed by test id, where a red not in the baseline FAILS and a baseline entry that passes ALSO FAILS. Each baseline entry carries its bead id, which puts attribution in the tree rather than in a commit message. Note the ☢️/❌ split above: a baseline keyed on names alone must still parse both markers or it silently ignores 12 of 18.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ SPEC WRITTEN, AND THE INSTRUMENT ALREADY DOES MOST OF THE JOB — the design changed on a measured probe rather than on argument.
ARTEFACT: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-29-three-state-ci-gate.md, 340 lines, md5 01bfba783e31c57c245924f40a1c010e — RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE ORCHESTRATOR at the same value. Untracked in papers; needs git add before any nix eval or review.

★★ THE FINDING: nix-unit 2.35.1 ALREADY SHIPS A NATIVE EXPECTED-FAILURE CHANNEL, and it is STRICTLY STRONGER THAN ANYTHING EXPRESSIBLE IN NIX. Probed on a throwaway file, 4 leaves:
  { expr = throw "boom"; expectedError = { type = "ThrownError"; msg = "boom"; }; }  -> PASS
  same with non-matching msg  -> FAIL, 'Expected error msg pattern X does not match thrown error msg Y'
  ★ expr does NOT throw       -> FAIL, 'Expected error, but no error was caught'
  type mismatched             -> FAIL, 'Expected error type EvalError, while ThrownError was thrown'
  ★★ { a = 1; }.b with type = "EvalError"  -> PASS — NIX-UNIT CATCHES WHAT tryEval CANNOT.
PAIRED CONTROL, measured the same run: tryEval catches ONLY throw and assert. MISSING-ATTRIBUTE, TYPE ERROR AND DIVISION-BY-ZERO PROPAGATE STRAIGHT THROUGH IT. And msg matches as an UNANCHORED SUBSTRING, so 'compose commitment' matches den-hoag's full abort message with no regex padding.
⇒ VERDICTS (2) AND (3) OF THE THREE-STATE CONTRACT ARE ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN THE INSTRUMENT. NO BASELINE FILE IS NEEDED for the error class, and NO PURE-NIX HARNESS CAN EVER BE THE GATE FOR IT. This is by-construction rather than repair, and it was found by probing the tool instead of designing around an assumed limitation.

THE FIVE DECISIONS:
 1. NO BASELINE FILE — THE DECLARATION IS THE TEST, AND IT IS GREEN. New ci/tests/_lib/xfail.nix with two forms: 'error' (lowers to nix-unit's native channel) and 'value' (expected = actual, asserting the wrong value produced TODAY, with 'correct' named beside it and 'assert actual != correct' MAKING A DEGENERATE XFAIL UNWRITABLE). ★ bead and construct are REQUIRED AND TOTAL — absence is an eval error, not a tolerated default (den-hoag's standing absence-is-a-decision rule). A side file diffed against scraped stdout was REJECTED as a repair: second artefact, unpromised output format, and structurally blind to the empty-suite hole (see refutation 1).
 2. THREE VERDICTS. Red-undeclared -> FAIL. Declared-and-now-passing -> FAIL. ★ FAILING DIFFERENTLY -> ALSO FAIL (msg/type mismatch) — which catches marker-class change WITH NO MARKER ARITHMETIC AND NO STDOUT PARSING. All-as-declared -> 1937/1937 exit 0, and the one bit carries information again.
 3. THE 0/0 HOLE — STRUCTURAL, NEVER A COUNT. Non-emptiness over attrNames tests closes it alone; no file list, no maintenance tax. TOTAL-COUNT ASSERTION REJECTED: it turns adding a test into a gate failure AND it cannot see the failure already live. Plus leaf-test-prefix and no-third-level checks. ★ THE UNTRACKED-FILE TRAP IS EXPLICITLY MARKED NOT COVERED — the CI flake sources the GIT tree, so readDir and attrNames see the SAME filtered source and agree with each other; the honest instrument is git ls-files at the dev boundary. Stating the hole rather than papering it.
 4. nix-unit SOLE GATE; checks.default DROPPED. Not preference: gen's assertTests evaluates t.expr == t.expected, so an error-form leaf (no 'expected') raises a MISSING-ATTRIBUTE error which by the probe above NOTHING CATCHES. It cannot host the mechanism. It is also not run in CI today, so dropping it changes no observed behaviour.
 5. RETIREMENT (§7). Self-explaining failure; grep -rn '<construct>' ci/tests/ enumerates every claim a retirement invalidates BEFORE the change is written; retiring an xfail is three hunks in the same branch.

REGISTER ANSWER (den-hoag-4kh.17 entry 3, verified live at HEAD), IN THREE PARTS AS REQUIRED:
  THEORY — SURVIVES. A claim about the gate's state space; references no kernel representation, no bucket, no state carrier, no staging.
  MECHANISM — SURVIVES. Parameterised by 'construct' rather than knowing any construct's name, so retiring the pre-pass is data-level churn: twelve declarations deleted, mechanism identical.
  ★ ARGUMENT — ONE PART DOES NOT SURVIVE, AND WAS REPLACED. The natural argument for in-test over side-file is FILE ADJACENCY ('the retirement edits the test file anyway'). THAT IS FALSE FOR EXACTLY THE RETIREMENTS IN THIS REGISTER: entry 3 is a change to lib/default.nix, and an author retiring prePassScopeRoots HAS NO REASON TO OPEN ci/tests/den-behavioral/pipe-policy.nix. Adjacency buys nothing. The durable argument is GREP-REACHABILITY, which comes from 'construct' being a REQUIRED FIELD, not from where the file lives. §1 and §7 were rewritten on the durable form. ⇒ This is the three-part question earning its keep for the second time in this arc.

★ FIVE FACTS REFUTED, one of them load-bearing:
 1. ★★ '172 SUITES' AND '168' ARE BOTH RIGHT AND THE RECONCILIATION DECIDES DESIGN DECISION 3. nix eval ... builtins.length (attrNames ts) -> 172; suites appearing in nix-unit STDOUT -> 168. THE FOUR EMPTY SUITES ARE PRESENT IN THE EVALUATED TREE AS { } BUT EMIT NO STDOUT LINE AT ALL. ⇒ A STDOUT-PARSING GATE IS STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF SEEING THE 0/0 HOLE, while attrNames sees it for free. Second-strongest argument in the spec after the probe.
 2. ★ THERE IS NO FILENAME-TO-SUITE-NAME CORRESPONDENCE. ci/tests/den-behavioral/pipe-policy.nix declares flake.tests.den-pipe. Suite names are declared INSIDE modules. A first draft of §5 asserted a readDir-file-list vs attrNames-tests mapping guard; THAT CORRESPONDENCE DOES NOT EXIST and the section was rewritten. Flagging for any future brief reaching for 'compare files to suites'.
 3. expectedError positive control is 6 hits in 3 files, not 5 in 2 — the third is ci/tests/b1-supportedness.nix. Directionally harmless; the control still fires.
 4. zero-machinery is 1/1, NOT empty (nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests.zero-machinery -> 1/1 successful). It belongs in the one-test-from-silent eight, not the empty four.
 5. .github/workflows/ci.yml is NOT one bare command — it is a format job (nix fmt -- --ci) plus TWO nix-unit steps (ci#tests and parity#tests). The substantive claim holds: no baseline, no allowlist, no diff. And checks.default is NOT RUN IN CI AT ALL, which is what makes decision 4 free.

FOUR ITEMS LEFT OPEN FOR THE OWNER, each with its reason:
 1. BEAD IDS FOR 16 OF THE 18. Only compat-scope-local-firing.test-expansion-collapses-to-one-rule has one on record (den-hoag-9xo.75). ★ Inventing ids would put FABRICATED ATTRIBUTION in the tree — the exact failure this spec exists to fix. Whether the 12 den-pipe aborts share one bead or take twelve is a tracker-graph shape decision.
 2. Whether to make gen's assertTests honour expectedError — a gen-lib change on a requirement den-hoag has not confirmed it needs, since it does not run checks.default. (Gen-lib push gate applies.)
 3. compat-feature-severed.test-probeSentinel-off-parks: §6 argues it should be rewritten GREEN on its own terms rather than parked, because there is no defect behind it — but that changes what the test asserts about the feature-severance probe. Behavioural call.
 4. Whether the xfail census should assert the bead is OPEN. Impossible in a pure eval; possible as a CI step shelling to bd. Trades gate purity for a real check.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ ADVERSARIAL GATE REVIEW — VERDICT: **REDESIGN**. Independent reviewer, artefact-and-rubric only, never the author's reasoning.
INTEGRITY: md5 01bfba783e31c57c245924f40a1c010e, 340 lines, re-derived from BOTH the working tree and 'git show 492a533:'. Artefact did not move. Repo HEAD 04648d5, porcelain empty. Worktree exclusion POSITIVE CONTROL: .worktrees/ holds 296 files matching flake.tests., so the filter was live and necessary.

★ THE PROBE HOLDS — ALL FOUR SUB-CLAIMS CONFIRMED on nix-unit 2.35.1 (store path 4qi8nh197sfq6lyym97wxc9ccpqaqvm6), reviewer's own throwaway file, exit read on the next line, positive control green in the same run. EvalError caught; not-throwing gives ☢️; type mismatch ❌; unanchored msg matched.
★★ BUT TWO PROPERTIES THE SPEC DID NOT PROBE, BOTH MEASURED:
  msg IS A REGEX, NOT A SUBSTRING — 'c.mpose c[a-z]+tment' MATCHED. §6 says 'substring'. Wrong in the direction that misleads an author writing literal text.
  ★★ msg = "" MATCHES ANY ERROR — expr = throw 'totally unrelated catastrophe' with msg = "" -> PASS.
STRUCTURAL CLAIM CONFIRMED EXACTLY: attrNames 172, stdout 168, comm -23 gap = exactly the four empty suites, ★ REVERSE DIFFERENCE EMPTY — a positive control that the join is sound rather than a coincidental count match. 1919+6+12=1937 CI_EXIT=1; parity 71/71 PARITY_EXIT=0. Decision 3 is the spec's strongest section and survives untouched.

★★★ THE KILL — THE MECHANISM DOES NOT REACH 12 OF THE 18. ci/tests/den-behavioral/pipe-policy.nix, the file §6 assigns twelve xfail.error declarations, IS HOSTED BY THE COMPAT SCAFFOLD: every leaf in its flake.tests.den-pipe is denTest ( ... ), including test-pipe-filter, the leaf §7.1 narrates BY NAME. 59 files import _lib/den-compat-test.nix and all five den-pipe contributors are among them.
THE SCAFFOLD INTERCEPTS ON THE KEY ITSELF: hasExpectedError = out ? expectedError; then lowers to { expr = (tryEval (deepSeq expr expr)).success; expected = false; }. ★ type AND msg ARE DISCARDED BEFORE NIX-UNIT EVER SEES THE LEAF.
MEASURED, NOT READ — the reviewer applied that lowering VERBATIM beside the native channel:
  native, declared msg = 'compose commitment', actual error 'infinite recursion encountered in some other subsystem'  -> ❌ 'does not match'
  scaffold-lowered, SAME declared intent, SAME wrong error                                                            -> ✅ GREEN
⇒ §2's VERDICT ROW 4 ('failing differently -> FAIL') DOES NOT HOLD FOR 12 OF THE 18. Row 3 (now-passing -> FAIL) does survive the lowering. §4's central justification — that nix-unit reports errors tryEval cannot — is EXACTLY WHAT THE SCAFFOLD UNDOES for two-thirds of the population.
★ THE SPEC HAS BOTH HALVES AND NEVER JOINS THEM: its own F17 identifies hasExpectedError as 'a weaker homonym' that 'shadows the name of the stronger native channel', and §6 then routes twelve scaffold-hosted tests through that name. F17 appears in NO decision section and in NONE of §10's four open items.

★★ AND IT IS A C9 HIT OF THE REGISTER'S OWN KNOWN-POSITIVE SHAPE — THE THIRD IN THIS ARC, AND THE THIRD FOUND ONLY BY READING. den-compat-test.nix's deviation comment reads VERBATIM: 'expectedError -> tryEval (mkCi has no error channel)'. THE WEAK HOMONYM EXISTS BECAUSE OF mkCi — THE INSTRUMENT DECISION 4 DROPS. The design retires the cause and leaves the workaround load-bearing. Invisible to word-sweep: the spec does name expectedError; it never notices that F17's construct and §6's twelve tests are THE SAME FILES. Corroborated by comments in compat-nested-class-named-aspect.nix and b1-supportedness.nix, both reading 'the homegrown CI asserter has no message-text channel'. The scaffold's expectedError arm is currently DEAD (4 hits in _lib/ + 2 comments) — §6 WOULD BE ITS FIRST CONSUMER.

★★ SIX FAIL-OPEN STATES, each found by enumerating the edit that defeats a guard:
 1. ★★ A MULTI-FILE SUITE SILENTLY EMPTIED. 202 files declare exactly one suite each (control: 202/202 single, and grep 'flake.tests *=' -> 0, so the dotted predicate is complete for this tree) but only 172 DISTINCT NAMES — 30 files share a name; den-include x6, ★ den-pipe x5. DELETE pipe-policy.nix's flake.tests.den-pipe BODY AND den-pipe STAYS NON-EMPTY VIA FOUR OTHER FILES: §5(1) non-emptiness green, (2) prefix green, (3) depth green, (4) file census green (file still on disk), G2 green (no xfail removed). ARBITRARILY MANY TESTS DELETED, EVERY GUARD GREEN — IN THE EXACT SUITE THE SPEC IS BUILT AROUND. §5's 'emptying a suite always does break them' is true of SUITES and false of the EDIT UNIT. The spec reasoned about file->zero-suites and never about many-files->one-suite. The one instrument that would catch it is a count, which §5 rejects.
 2. ★★ VACUOUS msg. msg = "" passes on any error. bead/construct required-and-total stops ABSENCE, NOT VACUITY. ★ This is the spec's own diagnosed failure mode REBUILT INSIDE THE NEW MECHANISM: it identifies vacuous greens in the tree, then ships a vacuity hole of the same shape.
 3. ★★ STALE OR EMPTY construct — THERE IS NO GUARD ON IT AT ALL; G1 constrains bead only. Yet §9's DURABLE ARGUMENT RESTS ENTIRELY ON THAT FIELD.
 4. correct IS UNVERIFIABLE — used only inside assert actual != correct, never evaluated against truth. actual=0, correct=3 passes when the true answer is 5. Accurate as stated (it claims only degeneracy), but correct is PROSE OCCUPYING AN EXECUTABLE SLOT.
 5. UNPINNED INSTRUMENT — ci.yml runs 'nix run nixpkgs#nix-unit'. The spec's foundation floats with the runner's nixpkgs, with no stated violation behaviour.
 6. Error-form leaves catch an error ANYWHERE in the deep-forced expr, and all 12 share one errors.nix opsInBody message, so they cannot distinguish 'this policy still trips' from 'some policy trips'.
SEARCHED AND FOUND NOT FAIL-OPEN: bogus type (fail-closed ❌); a leaf renamed off the test prefix (§5(2) catches it); a value-form leaf that starts throwing (☢️, measured).

CRITERIA: C1 FAIL (preconditions not enumerated; the unstated one — leaves reach nix-unit unmodified — is violated for 12/18). C2 violation TOTAL for the twelve (msg/type discrimination is ERASED, not degraded). C3 minor ('substring' licenses literal text into a regex field). C4 FAIL (approximation direction never named, and it is the COARSE one). ★ C5 PASS — every coordinate re-derivable was exact. C6 FAIL MULTIPLY (no defined behaviour on stale construct, empty msg, one contributor emptied, or version drift; §7's remedy is explicitly 'a register discipline, not a gate feature' — 'by convention' is the named C6 failure). C7 SPLIT (assert actual != correct is genuine construction and correctly narrow, but THE ERROR FORM HAS NO DEGENERACY GUARD — construction on the form covering 6, discipline on the form covering 12; and §1 rejects a baseline as 'a second artifact that must be kept in step' then ships TWO hand-maintained lists). C7-a PARTIAL — probing expectedError was the right primitive scan and correctly changed the design, but the substrate's OTHER surface (_lib/den-compat-test.nix's own expectedError arm) was found and never evaluated as alternative or conflict: ★ RIGHT LIB, WRONG SURFACE. C7-b PASS, best-executed criterion. C8 PASS. C9 FAIL.
★★ C9 IN DETAIL, BECAUSE THE CONCESSION WAS INCOMPLETE EXACTLY AS THE BRIEF PREDICTED: THEORY survives. MECHANISM survives in principle but not as specified (see the kill). ARGUMENT — §9 concedes ADJACENCY dies and substitutes GREP-REACHABILITY, and ★ THE SUBSTITUTE DIES BY THE SAME MECHANISM, MEASURED: an author retiring register entry 3 holds the register's own anchors — the binding prePassScopeRoots and the header 'THE STAGING THAT BREAKS THE CYCLE (design note §3b)'. grep -rn prePassScopeRoots ci/ -> 0, POSITIVE CONTROL SAME RUN 6 hits in lib/default.nix. §6 prescribes construct = 'staged pre-pass / compose-commitment law', A PROSE PHRASE MATCHING NEITHER ANCHOR. The grep the author actually runs returns nothing; the one §7.2 describes requires already knowing a token that exists only in this spec. So the durable argument is durable BY REGISTER BOOKKEEPING — a repair — and the spec's own §7 close says exactly that while §9 does not concede it.
OWNER RULINGS: Performance PASS (exemplary; nothing scales with fleet size, the forcing guard rejected on the right grounds). Prose-vs-executable FAIL (§7's retirement mechanism, correct, and §9's replacement argument all live in prose). ★ ABSENCE-IS-A-DECISION: PASS on bead/construct, FAIL ON type ? "ThrownError" — THE SIGNATURE DEFAULTS THE VERY AXIS THE PROBE'S ROW 5 EXISTS TO EXPLOIT, IN THE SAME LINE THAT MAKES TWO NEIGHBOURS TOTAL.

REDESIGN NEEDS FOUR ITEMS, NONE TOUCHING DECISION 3: (1) resolve F17 — either bypass the scaffold for error-class xfails or DELETE hasExpectedError (its stated reason retires with decision 4) and re-host the twelve; until then §6's assignment is unsound. (2) construct = the register's OWN ANCHOR FORM (binding name / verbatim header), not a prose phrase — which also satisfies the register's 'CITE BY EXPRESSION OR BINDING NAME' rule. (3) close the multi-file-suite hole, or state it as explicitly not covered the way §5 already does for the untracked-file trap. (4) constrain msg (non-empty, and say REGEX not substring); drop the type default.

★ RESOLVED — **compat-feature-severed.test-probeSentinel-off-parks IS ATTRIBUTED TO den-hoag-9xo.75.** Orchestrator ruling; I raised it as an owner question and it was not one.
The test's own comment at HEAD names 'the empty-recovery hazard' as a KNOWN OPEN DEFECT. den-hoag-9xo.75 IS that hazard — value-conditional policies vanishing because recovery fires the body at a fabricated ctx and the false branch returns [ ] — and it is OPEN at P0.
★ THE WORRY WAS THAT MATCHING TWO TEXTS IS 'INVENTING ATTRIBUTION'. IT IS NOT. Inventing attribution is writing a bead id that names nothing, or naming a plausible-sounding bead without opening it. Reading a test's stated cause and matching it to the open bead describing that exact cause IS what attribution means — and the alternative, leaving it unattributed, is the defect this spec exists to fix.
OVERTURN CONDITION, so this is falsifiable rather than merely decided: if the empty-recovery hazard is fixed and this test still parks for a different reason, the attribution is wrong and must be re-pointed at whatever that reason turns out to be.

comments.text:
★★ THE DEFECT THIS BEAD TRACKS BIT LOCALLY TODAY, ON A COMMENTS-ONLY COMMIT. Worth recording because it is a THIRD instrument carrying the same two-state assumption, and nobody had counted it.
The pre-commit `ci` hook runs the FULL nix-unit suite and fails on exit 1. The suite is 1919/1937 with EIGHTEEN KNOWN-RED BY DESIGN. ⇒ **THE HOOK CANNOT PASS WHILE CI IS THREE-STATE**, so every commit touching a .nix file must be forced past it.
MEASURED: a comments-only change (eight citation corrections, git diff -U0 showing ZERO changed lines without a comment marker, suite verified unmoved at 1919 ✅ / 12 ☢️ / 6 ❌, exit 1 read on the line after redirection) was BLOCKED. Landed with SKIP=ci at c9172dc, with the reason in the commit message.
★ WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE INCONVENIENCE: a hook that must be routinely bypassed TEACHES BYPASSING. The next person skips it on a change that is not comments-only, and the habit is already established — so the local gate degrades to nothing by exactly the mechanism §4.5 of the scaling-witness spec names for the CI gate (a permanently-red required job gets disabled). ⇒ THE THREE-STATE MECHANISM MUST COVER THE PRE-COMMIT HOOK, NOT ONLY THE GITHUB WORKFLOW. Add it to the spec's scope: the hook should consume the same baseline and apply the same three verdicts, or it should not run the suite at all.
NOTE THE INSTRUMENT COUNT IS NOW THREE, each with the same flaw: the GitHub workflow (bare nix-unit, one boolean pinned at 1), gen's checks.default assertTests (throws on the FIRST mismatch, cannot enumerate), and this pre-commit hook. The spec currently addresses one of the three.

  CONDITION den-hoag-9uv EXISTS TO FIX. The PASS state of a three-state gate ships unreachable, contingent on
  den-hoag-4kh.53.64. The spec notices "the error form ships with no declared instance" and does not notice
  the dual.

  `grep -rn '66t' ci/ parity/` -> **0** (positive control same run: a bead-shaped regex on CLAUDE.md -> 1).

  everyone today, and by the fail-open above STAYS RED AFTER THIS LANDS.

§6b — THE SCAFFOLD FIX — SURVIVES ON MECHANISM, with two prose errors. Necessity CONFIRMED (`out` read at
exactly three places, never spread; three literal-attrset branches). F14c CONFIRMED on the real instrument
(both-keys -> ☢️ uncaught; only-expectedError -> ✅ same run). ★ AND THE ATTACK THAT WOULD HAVE KILLED IT
DIDN'T: the deleted arm used `deepSeq expr expr` and the replacement forwards `expr` raw — but **nix-unit
DEEP-FORCES `expr`** (nested-throw-in-attrset ✅, nested-in-list ✅, both with controls). Dropping deepSeq is
safe.
★ BUT §6b's "the removeAttrs list and the forwarded leaf's key set are the same set viewed twice — one
definition, two uses" IS **FALSE**: removeAttrs is {expr, expected, expectedError, bead, construct}, the
forwarded leaf is {expr, expectedError, bead, construct} — `expected` MUST be absent by the spec's own F14c.
**AN IMPLEMENTER FOLLOWING THAT SENTENCE LITERALLY EMITS BOTH KEYS AND GETS ☢️ ON EVERY SCAFFOLD-HOSTED ERROR
TEST.** And `attributionOf` is used twice and defined nowhere.
★ AN UNNOTICED C7 REPEAT: §6b DELETES AN ARM WITH ZERO CONSUMERS AND INSTALLS AN ARM WITH ZERO CONSUMERS —
the spec's own rule about untested arms, applied to everything except the arm it is installing.
★★ AND A SECOND LIVE INSTANCE OF §9's OWN NEWEST HIT SHAPE, MISSED BY ITS SELF-SWEEP: §6's in-run negative
self-test is written with **tryEval** — the exact idiom den-hoag-30a files at 235 lines across 95 files —
INSIDE THE FILE INSTALLING ITS REPLACEMENT. The native channel demonstrably expresses it: measured
`expectedError = { type = "AssertionError"; msg = "actual != correct"; }` -> ✅ in a 4/4 run.
★ AND THE DISCRIMINATING HALF OF THE ERROR FORM (F14 rows 2-4, F14c) IS PINNED BY `ci/tests/_lib/xfail-probe.nix`
— **A FILE CI NEVER RUNS, "with its expected marker in a comment"** — living under `_lib/`, which
suite-completeness (4) EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES. **No guard in this spec covers the file this spec adds.**

WHAT HELD, AND STRONGLY: the multi-file-suite numbers exactly (202/202/172, den-include 6, den-pipe 5) and
the lexical-scan rejection is SOUND — 8 commented-out `test-… = denTest (` against 12 live in the same file,
so a fully commented file would pass a `test-` scan. Suite-completeness (1) measured cheap and correct
(0.21 s / 45 MB). ★ THE INTRA-LEAF VACUITY CLAIM IS **TRUE** and verbatim-verified, and the proposed narrowing
— declare `subRuleCount` only, split the two `all`s into a `w6SubRules != [ ] && …` sibling — **is correct and
is the right construction**, the same paired-control shape no-fleet-flags.nix already uses. Called the
strongest passage in the spec.
EXECUTABLE CORE: 42 fenced lines of 720; **prescriptive core 30 lines = 4.2%**. ★ BUT UNLIKE ITS SIBLING,
**`leafKeys`/`error`/`value` ACTUALLY EVALUATES** — the reviewer wrapped it, built both forms, ran them
through real nix-unit, and both degenerate-refusal asserts fired with a same-run positive control. Genuinely
better than the sibling's 51 non-evaluating lines. ★ THE PROBLEM IS THE SPLIT: **SEVEN OF THE EIGHT MECHANISMS
— G1, G2, G3 and suite-completeness (1)-(4) — HAVE NO EXECUTABLE FORM ANYWHERE**, and BOTH KILLS LIVE IN THE
PROSE-ONLY HALF, each one command from visible. A spec that measures its EVIDENCE to seven decimals and
leaves its GUARDS in prose has put the rigour on the wrong side.
★ INCIDENTAL CONFIRMATION: the reviewer's first probe used `builtins.match ".*needle.*"` over whole files and
**OVERFLOWED THE C STACK**, independently reproducing the hazard ci.yml records — so §3's
genPrelude.hasInfix-not-nixpkgs reasoning is right.
CRITERIA: C1/C1-a PASS · C2/C2-a PASS · C3 PASS with note · **C4 FAIL** (G3 is the COARSER approximation and
is not named as such) · **C5 PASS, ZERO coordinate defects** · **C6 FAIL** (three violating inputs, three
undefined behaviours) · **C7 FAIL on three counts** · **C7-a FAIL** (hasInfix bound for `construct`, not
considered for `msg`, the other fail-open axis) · **C7-b FAIL, measured** (§8's marginal-cost story is false:
boundary.nix EXCLUDES lib/compat/ by construction — 49 files / 580 KB / 53% of the bytes read by no existing
guard, and `recoverEmits` LIVES THERE; absolute cost is fine at 0.10 s, the STATED price is wrong in the
flattering direction) · C8 PASS · **C9 PASS on the register, FAIL on the self-sweep.**
