DEEP-FORCES `expr`** (nested-throw-in-attrset ✅, nested-in-list ✅, both with controls). Dropping deepSeq is
safe.
★ BUT §6b's "the removeAttrs list and the forwarded leaf's key set are the same set viewed twice — one
definition, two uses" IS **FALSE**: removeAttrs is {expr, expected, expectedError, bead, construct}, the
forwarded leaf is {expr, expectedError, bead, construct} — `expected` MUST be absent by the spec's own F14c.
**AN IMPLEMENTER FOLLOWING THAT SENTENCE LITERALLY EMITS BOTH KEYS AND GETS ☢️ ON EVERY SCAFFOLD-HOSTED ERROR
TEST.** And `attributionOf` is used twice and defined nowhere.
★ AN UNNOTICED C7 REPEAT: §6b DELETES AN ARM WITH ZERO CONSUMERS AND INSTALLS AN ARM WITH ZERO CONSUMERS —
the spec's own rule about untested arms, applied to everything except the arm it is installing.
★★ AND A SECOND LIVE INSTANCE OF §9's OWN NEWEST HIT SHAPE, MISSED BY ITS SELF-SWEEP: §6's in-run negative
self-test is written with **tryEval** — the exact idiom den-hoag-30a files at 235 lines across 95 files —
INSIDE THE FILE INSTALLING ITS REPLACEMENT. The native channel demonstrably expresses it: measured
`expectedError = { type = "AssertionError"; msg = "actual != correct"; }` -> ✅ in a 4/4 run.
★ AND THE DISCRIMINATING HALF OF THE ERROR FORM (F14 rows 2-4, F14c) IS PINNED BY `ci/tests/_lib/xfail-probe.nix`
— **A FILE CI NEVER RUNS, "with its expected marker in a comment"** — living under `_lib/`, which
suite-completeness (4) EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES. **No guard in this spec covers the file this spec adds.**

WHAT HELD, AND STRONGLY: the multi-file-suite numbers exactly (202/202/172, den-include 6, den-pipe 5) and
the lexical-scan rejection is SOUND — 8 commented-out `test-… = denTest (` against 12 live in the same file,
so a fully commented file would pass a `test-` scan. Suite-completeness (1) measured cheap and correct
(0.21 s / 45 MB). ★ THE INTRA-LEAF VACUITY CLAIM IS **TRUE** and verbatim-verified, and the proposed narrowing
— declare `subRuleCount` only, split the two `all`s into a `w6SubRules != [ ] && …` sibling — **is correct and
is the right construction**, the same paired-control shape no-fleet-flags.nix already uses. Called the
strongest passage in the spec.
EXECUTABLE CORE: 42 fenced lines of 720; **prescriptive core 30 lines = 4.2%**. ★ BUT UNLIKE ITS SIBLING,
**`leafKeys`/`error`/`value` ACTUALLY EVALUATES** — the reviewer wrapped it, built both forms, ran them
through real nix-unit, and both degenerate-refusal asserts fired with a same-run positive control. Genuinely
better than the sibling's 51 non-evaluating lines. ★ THE PROBLEM IS THE SPLIT: **SEVEN OF THE EIGHT MECHANISMS
— G1, G2, G3 and suite-completeness (1)-(4) — HAVE NO EXECUTABLE FORM ANYWHERE**, and BOTH KILLS LIVE IN THE
PROSE-ONLY HALF, each one command from visible. A spec that measures its EVIDENCE to seven decimals and
leaves its GUARDS in prose has put the rigour on the wrong side.
★ INCIDENTAL CONFIRMATION: the reviewer's first probe used `builtins.match ".*needle.*"` over whole files and
**OVERFLOWED THE C STACK**, independently reproducing the hazard ci.yml records — so §3's
genPrelude.hasInfix-not-nixpkgs reasoning is right.
CRITERIA: C1/C1-a PASS · C2/C2-a PASS · C3 PASS with note · **C4 FAIL** (G3 is the COARSER approximation and
is not named as such) · **C5 PASS, ZERO coordinate defects** · **C6 FAIL** (three violating inputs, three
undefined behaviours) · **C7 FAIL on three counts** · **C7-a FAIL** (hasInfix bound for `construct`, not
considered for `msg`, the other fail-open axis) · **C7-b FAIL, measured** (§8's marginal-cost story is false:
boundary.nix EXCLUDES lib/compat/ by construction — 49 files / 580 KB / 53% of the bytes read by no existing
guard, and `recoverEmits` LIVES THERE; absolute cost is fine at 0.10 s, the STATED price is wrong in the
flattering direction) · C8 PASS · **C9 PASS on the register, FAIL on the self-sweep.**

comments.text:
★★ THREE-STATE CI GATE — REVISION 3 AUTHORED. Both r2 kills discharged, all four fail-opens addressed (two
CLOSED, two recorded UNCOVERED WITH EXECUTING WITNESSES). Spec now 1133 lines, md5
cfe4b20b9e7611509a67b4abb2becc3a. ★ AND FOR THE FIRST TIME THE CORE IS A SEPARATE, SEPARATELY-HASHED,
SEPARATELY-RUNNING FILE: 429 lines, md5 9baa3bfac7bbd288c9033eb8754422f9, **32/32 EXIT 0 READ DIRECTLY (no
pipe), 0.55 s**, exercising BOTH ARMS of the two leaf forms, G1, G2, G3 plus the anchor index,
suite-completeness (1)-(4), and the scaffold's forwarding arm. Prescribed home ci/tests/_lib/xfail-core-probe
.nix; the spec states explicitly it is NOT in the tree.
The author re-derived the target's 720 lines / md5 2d259017359b57a8430d8e7deff49e5a before starting, found
papers HEAD had moved off the cited commit, and verified `git diff <cited> HEAD -- <spec>` was EMPTY so the
reviewed state was byte-identical. That is the anchor discipline working.

════ KILL 1 DISCHARGED — G3 NO LONGER ADMITS PROSE ════
G3 rebuilt from OCCURRENCE-IN-TEXT to **MEMBERSHIP IN A SET OF IDENTIFIERS DERIVED FROM SOURCE** (per-line
builtins.match for a binding LHS). Measured: "empty codomain" gives the empty set, "the" gives the empty set,
pipeOps gives exactly ["lib/concern-policies.nix"]. ★ A PROSE PHRASE HAS A SPACE AND IS THEREFORE
UNREPRESENTABLE — not merely unlikely. That is the construction-over-repair form of the fix.

════ KILL 2 DISCHARGED — G3 NO LONGER RED-LINES ITS OWN SELF-TEST ════
ci/tests/_lib is a THIRD GOVERNED ROOT, following from `construct`'s own definition ("the binding whose
deletion falsifies the claim"); the self-test's construct = "xfailError" resolves there. ★ The widening was
NOT silently taken — it is recorded as UNCOVERED-3, and the author checked its own `harness` root for being a
CARVE-OUT WEARING A GENERAL NAME.
RETIREMENT TEST: deleting the binding drops the name EVEN WHEN THE COMMENT STAYS —
testRetirementDropsAnchor asserts before AND after AND asserts that hasInfix WOULD HAVE SURVIVED, in one run.
Also stated honestly: NEITHER shipped construct is scheduled for deletion (den-hoag-gb9 FIXES pipeOps,
den-hoag-9xo.75 EDITS recoverEmits), so G3's value for the six is AUTHORING, not retirement detection.
VACUOUS CONTROL REPLACED with ONE POSITIVE CONTROL PER ROOT (buildRoots / compilePolicy / denTest), each a
structural binding deliberately NOT a register-retirement target. ★ prePassScopeRoots would have been the
obvious core control AND IS EXACTLY WRONG.
C7 DIRECTION TAKEN, NOT DEFLECTED: the token is DERIVED FROM SOURCE — the actualCore shape rev-2 cited for G2
and never carried to G3.

════ THE FOUR FAIL-OPENS ════
1. OPT-IN — NOT CLOSABLE, recorded UNCOVERED-1 ★ WITH AN EXECUTING WITNESS:
   testG2BlindToInPlaceWeakening runs the census over a red fixture AND the same fixture weakened in place
   and asserts the outputs EQUAL, with testG2SeesADeclaration as a same-run positive control. §2's "exit 0
   means exactly as declared" DELETED and replaced with what the mechanism actually changes. Rejected
   closure: an expectation-set census is the baseline-file shape §1 rejects.
2. PASS UNREACHABLE — the verdict table's fifth row DELETED. Post-landing is 0 ❌ / 12 ☢️ / exit 1; exit 0
   becomes reachable when den-hoag-4kh.53.64 closes. ★ NO TOTAL QUOTED, because the change ADDS LEAVES so
   1937 is not the denominator — the kind of arithmetic honesty that usually goes missing.
3. ATTRIBUTION — the den-hoag-66t claim DELETED, recorded UNCOVERED-2. grep -rn '66t\|4kh' ci/ parity/ lib/
   gives 0, POSITIVE CONTROL returns 4 hits all English (den-hoag-absent, den-hoag-native). Rejected closure:
   a non-suppressing register has a STALE-ROW FAIL-OPEN no pure eval can check.
4. PRE-COMMIT HOOK — now F23 plus a §4 subsection plus owner item 6. .pre-commit-config.yaml's ci hook is
   `exec nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests`, files "\.nix$", pass_filenames false — RED TODAY, RED AFTER LANDING.

════ SMALLER, ALL DISCHARGED ════
"One definition, two uses" replaced with one definition and two DERIVED uses (assertionKeys is a superset of
attributionKeys; the error leaf is {expr, expectedError} union (out intersect attributionKeys), and `expected`
is not in its construction). attributionOf defined as errorLeafOf. The installed arm ships WITH A CONSUMER,
exercised on three inputs. The tryEval self-test moved to the native channel. xfail-probe.nix gets a fourth
ci.yml step. §8's numbers corrected. ★ The msg floor upgraded from `msg != ""` to `builtins.match msg "" !=
null` — AN EXACT CHARACTERISATION OF "matches every message", which rejects ".*" and "x?" where the old form
did not. G1 specified as FULL-MATCH.

════ UNCOVERED, NOT FIXED — EACH WITH ITS REJECTED CLOSURE ════
1 opt-in mechanism · 2 the twelve unattributed · 3 root/collision indistinguishability (rejected:
file-qualified anchors break on a file move) · 4 msg = "." (not in the always-matching set) · 5 extractor
false negatives (FAIL-CLOSED) · 6 G2's WHNF cost is data-dependent (today's measurement, not a property).

════ C9, THREE PARTS ════
THEORY survives and references no kernel representation. ★ MECHANISM survives AND THE COUPLING NOW ACTUALLY
WORKS — rev-2 asserted that a retirement goes red while ITS OWN G3 WOULD HAVE STAYED GREEN through entries
3/4/5, all of which retire named bindings that carry comments. ARGUMENT: there is no third argument —
adjacency died to entry 3, grep-reachability died in rev-1's own document, and G3-as-hasInfix died the same
death A THIRD TIME in rev-2's; all three were checks an author could satisfy WRONGLY, and the fourth position
is a membership test IN WHICH EACH PREDECESSOR'S FAILURE MODE IS UNREPRESENTABLE.

════ ★★ THE SELF-SWEEP — THE AUTHOR SWEPT ITS OWN DIFF, WHICH rev-2 DID NOT ════
rev-2 swept only the target. This author found THREE INSTANCES IN ITS OWN ADDITIONS: the tryEval self-test
sitting inside the file that installs its replacement; deleting a zero-consumer arm and installing a
zero-consumer arm; and G3 inheriting boundary.nix's primitive WHOSE SEMANTICS IS INVERTED FOR THIS USE.
★ AND IT CAUGHT ITS OWN `|| true; rc=$?` BUG in the ci.yml step it wrote — that reads the exit of `true`,
the same class as ${PIPESTATUS[0]} under zsh.

════ ★★ FOUR FACTS REFUTED, INCLUDING TWO OF THE AUTHOR'S OWN ════
1. ★ "lib/compat/ = 49 files / 580 KB READ BY NO EXISTING GUARD" — **FALSE.** boundary.nix reads EVERY .nix
   under lib/compat/ via compatFiles = filesUnder "" then readCompat, consumed by test-shim-consumes-only-
   seam, test-shim-internal-seam and test-legacy-sibling-isolation. nix eval of that walk gives 49. §8's
   MARGINAL-COST CLAIM THEREFORE STANDS; only its numbers were wrong. But the precedent is cited FOR INVERTED
   SEMANTICS — boundary.nix WANTS comments to count, G3 must not.
2. The size figures: measured APPARENT bytes are core 770,134 and compat 684,645, not 472 KB / 580 KB.
   ★ du -sh REPORTS ALLOCATED BLOCKS. Correct instrument: find -printf '%s\n' piped to awk.
3. The author's OWN hypothesis that G2's `? bead` walk forces the fleet through denTest's isAttrs expr —
   **REFUTED**: 0.235 s over all 1937 leaves with --no-eval-cache vs 0.217 s names-only, WITH A SAME-RUN
   POSITIVE CONTROL (forcing ts.test-pipe-as-basic.expr THROWS). Kept as UNCOVERED-6 because it is TODAY'S
   TREE, not a property.
4. The reviewer's ci.yml sketch numbers — the author built the six-row probe and measured rc=1 with
   2 ✅ / 2 ❌ / 2 ☢️, NOT the 4 ❌ / 2 ☢️ it had drafted.

════ ★ TWO FINDINGS THE CORE PRODUCED THAT READING DID NOT ════
ci/tests/_fixtures/fleet.nix — 203 files on disk against F19's 202, so §5(4)'s "excluding _lib/" WAS OFF BY
ONE ON LANDING DAY (fixed to the repo's own /_-infix rule); and the rc=$? bug above. The author also
INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED the deep-forcing result (nested throw in attrset ✅ and in list ✅, both with
same-run controls, 4/4 exit 0) rather than inheriting it.
⇒ THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS ARC THAT WRITING THE RUNNER FOUND DEFECTS THE PROSE HID.

Baseline re-derived independently: 1919 ✅ / 6 ❌ / 12 ☢️ = 1937, exit 1. ★ THE TWELVE ARE `throw`s FROM
lib/errors.nix opsInBody, NOT ABORTS — which matters for how xfail can catch them.
No beads created or modified; nothing written under lib/, ci/, parity/ or .github/.

comments.text:
★★ GATE REVIEW r3 — three-state CI gate. VERDICT: **REDESIGN.** Hashes re-derived by reviewer AND
orchestrator: cfe4b20b9e7611509a67b4abb2becc3a (1133) / 9baa3bfac7bbd288c9033eb8754422f9 (429), papers
bda66d6. den-hoag moved since the spec but `git diff --stat 8cf8745..HEAD -- lib/ ci/ .github/ parity/
.pre-commit-config.yaml` is EMPTY — measured surface unchanged, all measurements valid.

★ THE FACTS ARE EXCELLENT AND THAT IS NOT THE KILL. Seventeen numbered facts independently verified and
every one reproduces. **THE KILL IS THAT THE TWO GUARDS THE DESIGN TURNS ON ARE DEFINED, UNIT-TESTED, AND
NEVER INVOKED.**

════ K1 ★★ G1 AND G3 ARE UNWIRED. THE SPEC'S OWN KILLED VALUE BUILDS, AND CENSUSES, SILENTLY ════
Authored through the spec's own wrapper:
  xfail.value { bead = "TODO"; construct = "empty codomain"; expr = 0; actual = 0; correct = 3; } SUCCEEDS.
  beadShapeOk "TODO" false. anchorResolves "empty codomain" false. censusOf yields a row with sites = [ ].
  Positive control same run: a good leaf yields sites = [ "lib/concern-policies.nix" ].
The predicates say false. NOTHING CONSULTS THEM. xfailError checks only msg; xfailValue only actual ==
correct; neither validates bead or construct. censusOf calls sitesOf, never anchorResolves — a non-resolving
construct yields sites = [ ] with no abort.
CALL-SITE CENSUS OF THE WHOLE ARTEFACT: anchorResolves and beadShapeOk appear at core lines 91 and 159
(definitions) and 277, 286, 290, 328 (four unit tests over STRING LITERALS). **ZERO other call sites. NEITHER
IDENTIFIER APPEARS ANYWHERE IN THE 1133-LINE PROSE SPEC.**
⇒ §9's ARGUMENT — "the fourth position ... a membership test in which the failure modes of the previous three
are unrepresentable" — IS REFUTED. A prose phrase is not unrepresentable; it is representable, constructible
and censusable. ★★ **THE FAILURE MODE DID NOT BECOME UNREPRESENTABLE. IT MOVED FROM "A CHECK AN AUTHOR COULD
SATISFY WRONGLY" TO "A CHECK NOTHING RUNS." FOURTH POSITION, FOURTH DEATH, SAME DOCUMENT.**
§11 UNCOVERED-5's "naming it as a construct is an eval error rather than a silent pass" is MEASURED FALSE —
there is no eval error. §3's O(#xfails) on G1 shows the intent that it run over the census; the leaf that
would do so is written NOWHERE, not in core and not as prose code.

════ K2 ★ THE PER-ROOT CONTROLS DO NOT DETECT A SHRUNK HAYSTACK — THE FAILURE THEY ARE NAMED TO DETECT ════
§3 says verbatim: "The mode that can occur is a SILENTLY SHRUNK HAYSTACK, and the three controls above are
what sees it, one per subtree."
  M6 — filesOfRoot walk made NON-RECURSIVE: core 32/32 EXIT 0, UNCHANGED. Positive control on the same
       instrument: index falls 99 files / 4963 pairs to 77 / 3936. **22 files, 1027 name-pairs, 20.7 % OF THE
       HAYSTACK GONE, SILENTLY.**
  M7 — skipDirs = [ "legacy" "parity" ] on the compat root: 32/32 EXIT 0, index 89 files / 4586 pairs.
  M8 — harness root deleted entirely: CAUGHT.
CAUSE: every asserted site in the core is at the TOP LEVEL of its root. lib/ has 37 top-level of 49;
lib/compat/ 39 of 49. **22 of 101 governed files sit below top level and NO ASSERTION TOUCHES ANY OF THEM.**
⇒ The controls see a root FULLY unreached, never a root PARTLY unreached.
★★ AND THIS IS r2's OWN DIAGNOSED DEFECT REPRODUCED VERBATIM — "a control sound for a DIFFERENT PROPOSITION
than the one it is said to prove" — **OCCURRING IN THE PARAGRAPH THAT DIAGNOSES IT.**
Consequence: the sites property (a) "a partial retirement changes sites" and (b) "a collision shows both
files" FAIL SILENTLY for any binding under an unreached subtree.

════ K3 ★ THE CORE AT ITS PRESCRIBED HOME POISONS THE INDEX IT ASSERTS ON ════
§12 prescribes ci/tests/_lib/xfail-core-probe.nix; §3 makes ci/tests/_lib a GOVERNED ROOT; core lines 308-309
are BINDING-SHAPED (pipeOps = [...]; recoverEmits = [...]). Simulated at that path against the real tree:
sitesOf "pipeOps" returns [ "ci/tests/_lib/xfail-core-probe.nix", "lib/concern-policies.nix" ] and
testG3SitesAreDefinitionsNotOccurrences goes FALSE. Control: sitesOf "buildRoots" unchanged (the core does
not bind it). testG2CensusRow breaks the same way, and the four gb9 xfails' shipped census rows carry sites
for pipeOps — so the checked-in census must list the probe file.
★ **THIS IS WHAT THE UNCOVERED-3 WIDENING BOUGHT.** Admitting _lib is defensible from `construct`'s own
definition, but it ALSO admits THE HARNESS'S OWN EXPECTATION LINES AS BINDING SITES FOR KERNEL CONSTRUCTS.
Same applies to the prescribed xfail-probe.nix and xfail.nix (which add error, value, type, msg, expr,
expected to the index).

════ K4 ★ G3 PROPERTY 2 IS FALSE — COMMENTS CAN SATISFY IT, AND DOC STRINGS DO SO LIVE TODAY ════
The claim is that a comment line begins # which is not in the identifier class. But bindingPat is LINE-LOCAL
WITH NO LEXER STATE, and Nix comments are # **AND** /* */.
  retirement leaving a /* */ block comment: "recoverEmits" STILL BOUND (true)
  retirement leaving a '' doc string:       "recoverEmits" STILL BOUND (true)
  positive control, the # form the spec tested: NOT bound (false)
Block-comment vector is LATENT (the 12 /* hits in governed roots are glob text inside # comments). ★★ THE
DOC-STRING VECTOR IS LIVE: 41 binding-shaped lines sit inside '' strings in the governed roots, and **20
NAMES ARE IN THE ANCHOR INDEX ONLY BECAUSE THEY APPEAR INSIDE A DOCUMENTATION STRING** — denApps,
denPackages, denShell, hostApps, homeApps, buildInputs, action, den.default.includes and more. An author
writes construct = "denApps" and G3 resolves against AN EXAMPLE IN PROSE.
★ A further 13 names are bound BOTH really AND in a string (nixosConfigurations, includes, imports, type,
value, name, default, hosts, homes, os, hm, nixos, darwin) — so for these, **DELETING THE REAL BINDING LEAVES
THE NAME IN THE INDEX, REFUTING CLAIMED PROPERTY 3 LIVE IN THE TREE.**

════ K5 ★ COORDINATE FAILURE — AND IT IS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S, NOT THE AUTHOR'S ════
F16 ★ says den-hoag-gg8 "names only pipe-consume, so this instance is outside its stated scope ... reported
to the orchestrator, not filed", and §10 item 2 ships "whether that is gg8 widened or a second bead is a
tracker-graph decision" to the owner.
VERIFIED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR DIRECTLY: gg8's title already reads "sibling AND intra-leaf"; its comments are
2026-07-29T02:59:04Z (the scope question) and **2026-07-29T03:05:53Z "RESOLVED — WIDEN THIS BEAD TO COVER
INTRA-LEAF VACUITY. Orchestrator ruling; I raised it as an owner question and it was not one."** The spec
commit bda66d6 is 2026-07-28T21:45:25-07:00 = 04:45:25Z. **THE RULING PREDATES THE COMMIT BY 1 h 40 m.**
⇒ ★★ THE PROCESS DEFECT IS MINE: I RECORDED A RULING IN THE GRAPH AND DID NOT RELAY IT TO THE AGENT ALREADY
RUNNING. Agents do not poll the tracker; a ruling made after dispatch is invisible to exactly the work it was
made for. Recorded as a standing rule — relay by message, do not merely record.

════ K6 "ABOUT NOTHING" IS STILL AUTHORABLE ════
26 of 36 common English words resolve — name, value, type, text, result, file, path, self, config, enable,
message, source, target, key, kind, group, content, entry, root, node, id, data, set, all, head, tail.
Control zzznotabindingzzz returns [ ]. 346 of 2533 index names match [a-z]{2,6}. Disclosed at UNCOVERED-3, so
a severity-raiser rather than an independent kill — ★ BUT WITH K1 IT IS NOT MITIGATED AT ALL, because `sites`
only reaches a reviewed diff if something enforces the census.

════ K7 COST, TWO MISSES (MINOR) ════
★ The core's denHoagSrc is a PATH LITERAL and "${denHoagSrc}/lib" COERCES — copying the whole repo to the
store: 176,635,191 B / 872 files, .git INCLUDED. §8's 0.55 s / 0.58 s are WARM-STORE numbers only. (A probe
artifact — at the prescribed home the source is already a store path — but §8 presents them as the
instrument's cost.) And §8's "three .md files under lib/ — 228,900 B" measures 234,425 (ledger 214,308 +
runbook 14,062 + edge-schema 6,055), off by 5,525 in a section whose thesis is "the number must be right,
not just small".

════ FAIL-OPENS, ENUMERATED ════
FO1 bead malformed ("TODO") — NO named abort, G1 unwired — UNDISCLOSED
FO2 construct not in index — NO named abort, G3 unwired; §11 claims an eval error, measured false —
    UNDISCLOSED AND CONTRADICTED
FO3 anchor haystack silently shrinks — NO abort; the spec names controls that do not fire (M6/M7) —
    UNDISCLOSED AND CONTRADICTED
FO4 binding inside /* */ or '' — none; 20 live phantom names — UNDISCLOSED
FO5 in-place weakening of expected — disclosed UNCOVERED-1
FO6 twelve den-pipe unattributed — disclosed UNCOVERED-2
FO7 generic-name anchor — disclosed UNCOVERED-3, sites mitigates
FO8 msg = "." — disclosed UNCOVERED-4
★ FO5 and FO6's REJECTED CLOSURES ARE SOUND, NOT LOAD-BEARING PROSE — an expectation-set census at 1937
entries genuinely IS §1's rejected baseline shape, and a non-suppressing register genuinely CANNOT be checked
against a result in pure eval. Both rejections survive. FO2's "sites=[ ] shows up in a reviewed diff"
mitigation, however, is prose only.

════ THE RUBRIC ════
C1 HYPOTHESIS FAIL — G3 properties 2 and 3 carry an UNSTATED precondition: the extractor is line-local with
  no lexer state. Property 2 holds only for # comments; property 3 only when the name is lexically bound
  nowhere else. K4 refutes both.
C1-a ARITY FAIL — the declared domain of `construct` is "an identifier BOUND in the governed source"; the
  ACTUAL domain is any string, because membership is never checked at any call site.
C2 SINGLE-VIOLATION-IS-TOTAL FAIL — property 2 fails and §9's unrepresentability conclusion is NOT
  re-sourced; it stands verbatim.
C2-a PASS — F25's equivalence (matches-every iff match msg "" != null) is used AS A THEOREM and is correct:
  M2 confirms removing the clause loses 3 tests; ".*", "x?", "", "^$" refused, "." accepted. boundary.nix's
  actualCore is used as a PATTERN and §3 correctly flags the semantic inversion.
C3 LICENSING FAIL, two sentences — "Three guards ... All three are executable at §12" licenses shipping
  PREDICATES as GUARDS, which is exactly what §12 contains; and UNCOVERED-5's "is an eval error rather than a
  silent pass" licenses belief in an abort that does not exist.
C4 DIRECTION OF APPROXIMATION MIXED — the msg floor errs FINER and loud (M2 verified), the degenerate-value
  clause FINER (M3); the shrunk haystack errs COARSER and SILENT for sites/G2 and the named repairing
  discipline does not repair (K2); G3-unwired errs coarser with no discipline named.
C5 COORDINATES FAIL ON ONE, otherwise clean — gg8 (K5). Everything else verified against primary text
  including F4, F5, F6, F17, F18 (57), F19 (172 distinct / 202 files), F23 (hook entry literally
  `exec nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests "$@"`), F24 (203 vs 202), F26 (49/49). ★ den-hoag-30a's "235 lines across
  95 files" is CORRECT; the bead title's 201 counts a narrower idiom.
C6 TOTALITY OF THE DISCHARGE **FAIL — DECISIVE.** Three violation classes with no named abort (FO1, FO2,
  FO3), and TWO OF THEM ARE THE DESIGN'S OWN GUARDS. The question "what does the system do on the input that
  violates the invariant?" answers, for the central invariant, **"it builds it and censuses it."** Measured.
C7 CONSTRUCTION-VS-REPAIR PARTIAL — the leaf forms ARE genuinely by-construction (M3 and M4 both caught;
  `expected` is STRUCTURALLY ABSENT from errorLeafOf). G3 is back to REPAIR SHAPE: a predicate that must be
  invoked — an invariant someone must maintain, and nobody currently does.
C7-a PRIMITIVE GRANULARITY FAIL — the scan stopped at PATTERN granularity. It took boundary.nix's actualCore
  shape and correctly noted the comment-semantics inversion, but the chosen primitive (a line-local regex)
  CANNOT REPRESENT NIX LEXICAL STATE, which is precisely what "identifier bound in source" requires. Right
  idea, wrong surface, invisible to review. No scan for a Nix-aware extractor is recorded.
C7-b COST MOSTLY PASS — complexity stated as a property throughout, O(#lines)/O(#files)/O(#suites) correct,
  hasInfix avoidance correct, lib/**.nix = 1,454,779 B / 98 files exactly as claimed. Two misses at K7.
C8 PARITY TARGET PASS — the population of six is selected from measurement plus the den-hoag-i5m ruling, not
  calibrated to what passes. ★ **PASS-UNREACHABILITY IS DISCLOSED HONESTLY AND CONSISTENTLY** — §2(i), §4,
  §10 item 6 and §13 all state 0 ❌ / 12 ☢️ / exit 1 post-landing, and an exhaustive sweep of all 12 "exit 0"
  and 30 "green" occurrences found every one scoped to the core, to parity#tests, or explicitly the thing
  being refuted. THE BEST PART OF THIS REVISION.

expectedError` branch and leaves the value branch "unchanged". Run VERBATIM on a value-form declaration:

description:
MEASURED BY READING at HEAD 6f30460 (read-only census; derived structurally, NOT benchmarked — stated as such). Performance is a DEFECT here by standing rule, and den-hoag-4kh.53.74 requires pricing at THOUSANDS of hosts, never at corpus scale.

THE DEFECT. lib/attributes/resolution-relations.nix binds rel-accessor = resolve.attr { readsAttrs = [ ]; compute = _self: id: relations.mkRelAccessor { denQuery = query.denQuery; inherit relationEdges strataOrder; ... } id; }. mkRelAccessor (lib/concern-relations.nix) returns id: builtins.mapAttrs (kind: kindRow: { targets = denQuery (base // {follow=kind;...}); inverse = ...; closure = ...; paths = ...; }) where base = { edges = scopedEdges; from = id; }.
EACH denQuery CALL INDEPENDENTLY EXECUTES lib/query.nix's kindGraph = graph.labeledFrom (perLabelFromEdges edges), and perLabelFromEdges is the TWO-groupBy FULL-POOL ADJACENCY BUILD. ★ NIX HAS NO COMMON-SUBEXPRESSION ELIMINATION, so it is rebuilt on every call. Across the accessor that is |N| x |K| x 4 x O(E). With E ~ O(|H|), the growth is O(|H|^2 x |K|). Laziness limits it to fields actually forced, but ANY consumer reading 'targets' fleet-wide pays |N| x O(E).

★★ AND THE COMMENT DENIES IT. lib/query.nix:30-38 claims 'PREBUILT ADJACENCY (O(E) once, O(1) per lookup) ... the avoidable O(E^2) the gather expose arm inherited through this facade'. THE HOIST IS ONLY INSIDE ONE denQuery CALL. The comment is true of the function and false of the system, and it is exactly the kind of claim a reader takes on faith and does not re-derive. This is the second such comment found in one census (den-hoag-5ae records the other: a strip-list comment asserting an equality between two lists that differ).

★ THE CONSTRUCTION TO COPY IS IN THE SIBLING FILE. lib/attributes/claim-accessor.nix hoists correctly — scopedReverse = reverseByKind scopedPool; sits OUTSIDE the compute, with a comment explicitly noting why. Two sibling accessors, same shape, one hoisted and one not. That makes this a BY-CONSTRUCTION fix with an in-tree precedent rather than a new design.

NINE MORE PER-NODE COST SITES, none reported negligible, each with its growth variable:
  declaredEdges = _id: relationEndpoints — EVERY node is handed the FULL endpoint list. The comment calls it a deliberate 'SAFE over-declaration ... a tighter per-node reachable set is the tracked perf refinement, §13'. Growth |N| x |E| in declared read-set size.
  contentIdsOf = name: prelude.filter (id: memberClassName id == name && terminalModulesAt id name != [ ]) allNodeIds — called per class inside the systems build, so |classes| x |allNodeIds| uncached memberClassName calls. && short-circuits the projection force, so the scan and the classOf recomputation are the cost.
  producerConfigs — concatMap over allNodeIds, O(|N|) with a classOfNode + locator call each.
  inverseRelationEdges — filters the whole forward pool per relation kind, O(|K| x |E|) plus a prelude.unique.
  reverseByKind / projectedByKind — each filters the whole pool per kind, O(|K| x |E|) twice.
  edgesBelowStratum — filters the whole relation pool per call; INERT TODAY because ceiling = null short-circuits it, and becomes O(E) per accessor construction the moment per-relation strata land (§11 L2).
  ancestorResolvedKeys — keysAt aid folds every ancestor's ENTIRE resolved-aspect key set, per node. A cell under host under env re-folds the env's full aspect key set: for |H| x |U| cells sharing one env that is |H| x |U| x |A_env| attrset unions.
  enrichments supportedness — two full context copies plus a deep == per node.
  provenance — re-runs the whole fixpoint capped at a MAGIC 100 iterations; error path only, but the comment's 'same complexity as the fixpoint itself' is accurate.

prelude.unique CONFIRMED AT SOURCE — gen-prelude/lib/default.nix:233, unique = foldl' (acc: x: if elem x acc then acc else acc ++ [ x ]) [ ]: O(n^2) COMPARISONS AND O(n^2) ALLOCATION, since acc ++ [x] copies the accumulator every element. SIXTEEN kernel call sites. The expensive ones: relationEndpoints (O(|E|^2)), the per-relation-kind nodes build (O(|K| x |E|^2) worst), claim-accessor's nodes build (same), resolved-aspects ancestorIds (PER NODE), class-modules relocation endpoints (PER NODE with relocations). ★ NOTE den-hoag-4kh.53.47 ALREADY MEASURED THAT THE OBVIOUS REMEDY (delegate to dedupByKey) IS 272x WORSE AT den-hoag's ACTUAL INPUT SHAPE — do not reach for it. The fix is per-site and must be measured per-site.

CAVEAT STATED BY THE CENSUS: unique was read from the LOCAL gen-prelude working clone, not from the rev pinned in flake.lock. The definition is almost certainly stable but the rev was not verified.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NARROWED BY MEASUREMENT, 2026-07-29 — THIS IS REAL BUT IT IS NOT THE LEADING TERM, AND MY PRIORITY ORDERING WAS WRONG.
Measured with a clean reporter and a LIVE relation pool (the first attempt used a fixture declaring NO relations and reported the accessor as CHEAPER than the plain node arm — logged as a flattering trap on den-hoag-4kh.20). Marginal cost of the accessor ABOVE node enumeration, across H=4..32: 7,565 -> 16,921 -> 43,121 -> 125,473, log2 ratios 1.16 / 1.35 / 1.54 AND STILL RISING.
⇒ BY THE WITNESS'S OWN CONVERGENCE RULE THAT IS INCONCLUSIVE, NOT QUADRATIC. The estimates have not converged, and estimates rise monotonically toward the asymptote, so this is a lower bound rather than a measurement.
★★ AND AT EVERY RUNG THE DOMINANT COST IS SOMETHING ELSE: a RELATION-INDEPENDENT CUBIC in cell count (den-hoag-qxz, exponent 2.98). rel=true versus rel=false differ by THIRTY-TWO function calls at H=32. I queued this bead as the leading performance item on a reading of the source; execution says the cell-multiplication path dominates it at every size measured.
WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED: the defect is real and the by-construction fix has an in-tree precedent, re-confirmed at HEAD — lib/attributes/claim-accessor.nix binds scopedReverse = reverseByKind scopedPool in the let ABOVE resolve.attr, while lib/attributes/resolution-relations.nix calls relations.mkRelAccessor { ... } id INSIDE compute. Two sibling accessors, same shape, one hoisted and one not.
WHAT DOES NOT STAND: its priority. Fixing this while the cell path is cubic is optimising a term that is not the leading one — and per the standing rule that performance is a DEFECT, the honest ordering is by measured contribution, not by how legible the defect is in source.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ RE-SEQUENCED, 2026-07-29 — NOT A PRIORITY CHANGE BUT A DEPENDENCY ONE, and it partly reverses what I said an hour ago.
I deprioritised this on measured grounds: den-hoag-qxz's relation-independent cubic dominates it at every rung, and this bead's own marginal cost is INCONCLUSIVE rather than quadratic. That stands.
★★ BUT THE CONTAINMENT-AS-EDGES SPEC MAKES IT A PREREQUISITE. Today's query cost is O(N.K.E) = O(N^2.K) because denQuery rebuilds perLabelFromEdges INSIDE ITS OWN LET and Nix has no CSE. ★ THE NEW COORDINATE QUERY RUNS AT EVERY NODE, so the migration CONVERTS THIS LATENT O(N^2) INTO A LIVE ONE. The spec therefore lands the adjacency hoist IN THE SAME CHANGE, giving O(E + N.D).
⇒ BOTH FACTS HOLD AND THEY ARE NOT IN TENSION: not the leading term today; unavoidable the moment the coordinate query ships. Sequencing, not priority — and worth stating plainly because 'deprioritised' and 'prerequisite' read as contradictory in a task list.
den-hoag-5ae now depends on this bead.

title: [arch] [kernel] THE TOPOLOGY AS IT IS: TWO EDGE MODELS (delivery vs adjacency) and seven disjoint pools — the live query substrate is Model-Q and six framework structural kinds have NO producer
description:
READ-ONLY KERNEL CENSUS, fresh context, at HEAD 6f30460 (clean). Dispatched against the owner directive den-hoag-2rh: get the correct TOPOLOGY represented, and everything reduces to a native graph query. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT IS REPRESENTED TODAY'.

★★★ THERE IS NO ONE GRAPH. There are SEVEN DISJOINT POOLS, and only ONE of them materializes configuration.
  A. THE EDGE-KIND REGISTRY (lib/edges.nix, preRegisteredStrata): contains/include/kindOf = structural, member/reach/reach-suppress = resolution, nest/defer = output, demand = demand. Compiled at lib/default.nix:1273; its to-tag {query,materialize,both} is read live by materializeEdges. ★ BUT NOTHING IN THE KERNEL STAMPS RECORDS WITH THESE KINDS. Of the nine, ONLY 'demand' has a live producer (lib/demand.nix toEdges).
  B. THE P-EDGE is A FIELD, not an edge: node.parent, walked by scope.inheritAll / scope.ancestors / parseParent (a REGEX OVER THE ID STRING, build-roots.nix). There is no parent-edge record anywhere.
  C. THE I-EDGE (imports) is built by concatMap over declarations.importEdgesOf, resolved via linkTarget, consumed only by neron-order.
  D. THE RELATION POOL: relationEdgesRaw = forwardRelationEdges ++ inverseRelationEdges ++ productionClaimEdges, a flat [{id;kind;from;to}]. output-modules.nix states it 'lives in a separate pool NEVER MERGED into edgesForRoot'.
  E. THE CONTENT POOL (gen-edge) — the ONLY pool that materializes config: edgesForRoot = root: materializeFilter (edge.edgesFor { graph = graphAccessor; inherit root; } ++ demandEdges), behind a 7-field accessor record.
  F. A SECOND, MULTI-VALUED PARENT RELATION, disjoint from B: byTarget = prelude.groupBy (e: e.tid) containmentEmissions, giving containmentAncestors/containmentAttachments, then RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY in resolved-settings.nix as containEdges. That file says so itself: 'a separate map from the single-parent self-graph P-edge (node.parent) ... untraversable by a single-parent inherit walk'.
  G. A PER-NODE CHANNEL-RELOCATION GRAPH (class-modules.nix relOf), node domain Ch union endpoints(P(n)).
⇒ A reader asking 'what graph is this' has seven answers, and the registry that LOOKS like the answer (A) is the one with almost no live producers.

SEVEN NODE KINDS ACROSS THREE ID NAMESPACES: scope ROOT (kind:name, or bareId@parent when multi-attached), scope CELL (leafDim:name@hostNodeId), entity REGISTRY ENTRY (id_hash), fleet PRODUCT CELL (coordinate tuple), RELATION-GRAPH node (bare string), CHANNEL node, ASPECT node ({key;content;sharedFoldKey}). ★ Root-vs-cell is discriminated by a PAYLOAD TAG, not a graph fact: build-roots.nix sets __root = true and isCellNode = node: !(node.decls.__root or false) — the file argues this at length because the id-SHAPE test broke once mintedRootId put @ into root ids. The registry-to-product factor is an EDGELESS graph: edges = _: [ ]; parent = _: null.

★★ POSITION IS CACHED AS PAYLOAD — CONFIRMED LIVE. lib/fleet.nix:117 __coords = c // { ${parentDim} = hostEntry; } and :125 __containment = map (d: "${d}:${c.${d}.name}") (...). Both land on decls. __containment IS AN EDGE SET WRITTEN INTO PAYLOAD. Read at resolved-settings.nix coordsOfNode = node: node.decls.__coords or (coordDims node) and resolved-aspects.nix containment = node.decls.__containment or [ ]. ★ THE 'or' FALLBACK IS THE TELL: TWO DIFFERENT DERIVATIONS OF ONE FACT, selected by whether the cache happens to be present.

★★★ AND THE STRIP LISTS HAVE ALREADY DRIFTED INTO THREE DIFFERENT KEY SETS ACROSS FOUR SITES — the invariant-someone-must-maintain failure, caught in the act. Cited BY EXPRESSION per den-hoag-4kh.17's own standing rule:
  staged-resolution.nix  baseCtxOf = id: removeAttrs scopeRoots.${id}.decls [ ... ]      -> __edges __containment __coords __root
  structural.nix         inherited-context's extract = node: removeAttrs (node.decls or { }) [ ... ] -> those four PLUS suppressedPolicies (not even a __ key)
  resolved-settings.nix  removeAttrs (node.decls or { }) [ ... ]                          -> __entry PLUS those four
  collections.nix        removeAttrs (node.decls or { }) [ ... ]                          -> __entry PLUS those four
★ __entry is stripped in TWO and kept in TWO. suppressedPolicies is stripped in exactly ONE. AND staged-resolution.nix's own comment ASSERTS it is 'the same __-key strip as attr 1' — IT IS NOT. A comment a reader takes on faith, asserting an equality that does not hold, over a hand-maintained list four sites must agree on.

THE KERNEL WRITES EIGHT __ KEYS OF ITS OWN (26 distinct names, 155 occurrence lines total; the rest are gen-library-owned and legitimate — __isWrappedFn/__functionArgs/__fn from gen-aspects, __sel from gen-select, __configThunk/__sourceScope from gen-bind, __edges from gen-scope, __derive/__derived from gen-pipe):
  __entry (build-roots, fleet) — the node's kindOf EDGE TARGET stored on the node. Externally constrained: scope-adapter says gen-select's adapter reads exactly this shape, so the SHAPE is forced; the NAME is a v1 echo.
  __root — constructor tag standing in for 'which minter made this node' = a kindOf edge.
  __coords, __containment — position and an ancestor edge-set as payload.
  __policy (concern-policies a // { __policy = name; }) — PROVENANCE STAMPED INTO THE VALUE; a source-attribution edge written as a field. Read at 9 sites.
  __action — ★ THIS IS THE TYPE TAG OF A SUM TYPE, and ELEVEN consumer sites across five files re-implement dispatch as builtins.filter (a: a.__action == "..."). Each filter is a LINEAR SCAN OF THE NODE'S WHOLE ACT LIST — a per-node per-question rescan where a partitioned or labelled edge set would be an index. The naming is a holdover; the PATTERN is the deeper defect. ★ AND THE COMPLETE TAG SET IS ENUMERATED NOWHERE — a reader cannot consult a declaration site.
  __den-demands — a reserved channel identified by PREFIX MATCHING ON ITS NAME (isReserved = ch: prelude.hasPrefix "__" ch), filtered out of the fold.
  __terminal, plus a __spawn NAME-MANGLED SUFFIX ("${name}__spawn") used as a namespace for a synthesized second equation.
⇒ ★ FOUR OF THE EIGHT ARE GRAPH FACTS WRITTEN INTO NODE PAYLOAD (__entry, __root, __coords, __containment) AND THOSE FOUR ARE EXACTLY THE FOUR THE STRIP LISTS EXIST TO HIDE AGAIN. That is the whole thesis in one sentence: a graph edge needs no strip list.

WHERE CONTENT ALREADY LANDED CORRECTLY, and it is the model for the rest: class/channel content. class-seeds = resolve.attr { compute = self: id: ... prelude.genAttrs classNames (classSeedsAt frame resolvedAspects exempt injects) }, with srcOrder derived from preimageOf over the TRANSPOSED relocation relation. Header verbatim: 'THE QUERY. Per (node, channel). Total. Order-free in the act list.' Genuinely demand-driven and order-free. EVERYTHING ELSE is a per-node fixpoint or an up-front fold: aspects (scope.circular least fixpoint per node), settings (per-node expandPreorder), declarations (per-node dispatch), enrichments (per-node circular re-dispatch), collections.

FIVE WHOLE-STRUCTURE MAPS BUILT UP FRONT, with the verdict on each:
  producerConfigs — listToAttrs (concatMap ... allNodeIds), handed to EVERY member build. Its own comment calls it 'THE FIXPOINT KNOT' and relies on Nix laziness for the spine. That is a REPAIR, not a construction: a producer->consumer EDGE answers the same question without a fleet-wide index.
  entryNodeIndex (default.nix) — nested foldl' over all root kinds x all instances -> id_hash -> {kind;nodeIds}, read ONLY by linkTarget. This is entity->node resolution, i.e. exactly a kindOf/contains edge query materialized as a map. HOLDOVER.
  rootNodeIndex (staged-resolution) — A SECOND WHOLE-REGISTRY FOLD of the same id_hash -> kind:name shape, built independently. HOLDOVER AND A DUPLICATION.
  containmentBindings — foldl' (acc: m: acc // m) { } over byTarget. Its header argues at length that this is not an accumulator BECAUSE IT IS ORDER-INDEPENDENT. That argument is sound about ORDERING and SILENT ABOUT REPRESENTATION: byTarget IS the adjacency, one hop from an edge set.
  sliceById (resolved-settings) — listToAttrs over every containmentRelations entry, rebuilding the inverse of a map staged-resolution just built. ★ A THIRD RE-DERIVATION OF THE SAME CONTAINMENT FACT.

THE STAGED PRE-PASS IS CONFIRMED AND IT IS MORE THAN A SCHEDULE. lib/default.nix:1016 header verbatim 'THE STAGING THAT BREAKS THE CYCLE (design note §3b). Naive "cellKinds <- tuples <- pre-pass <- roots <- cellKinds" is circular.' prePassScopeRoots built :1025, consumed :1040 — 15 lines apart, as recorded. ★ THE CENSUS'S JUDGEMENT, AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT THAT MATTERS: THIS IS A CYCLE IN A REPRESENTATION, NOT IN THE DOMAIN. It exists because node MINTING must precede dispatch, and dispatch produces the MEMBERSHIP that decides what should have been minted. IN A GRAPH WHERE MEMBERSHIP IS AN EDGE RATHER THAN AN INPUT TO NODE CONSTRUCTION, THERE IS NO ORDERING TO STAGE. Note also staged-resolution advertises 'TWO COLLECT/DELIVER FIRINGS (order-independent, no phase schedule)' — the FIRINGS are order-independent, but the PASS is a stage, and both fireAt calls dispatch every root twice under a header naming it the DOUBLE-FIRE DISCIPLINE.

CORRECTIONS TO FACTS THE ORCHESTRATOR SUPPLIED, all measured:
  TWO worktrees on disk, not four (.worktrees/projection, .worktrees/sweep-main). Independently confirmed by a second agent the same session.
  The gen-graph transpose citation was ~50 lines off and pointed at an UNRELATED comment. Actual banner lib/default.nix:2013-2021, call at :2045 (reversed = genGraphLib.transpose { edges = id: adjacency.${id} or [ ]; inherit nodes; }), comment verbatim at :2014 'a per-kind genGraphLib.transpose (Mokhov 2017 §4.3), NOT a hand-rolled from/to swap'. :2067 is a different comment about claimKinds. AND IT IS NOT THE ONLY TRANSPOSE — two more at class-modules.nix (rev = graph.transpose rel) and claim-accessor.nix (threaded from attributes/default.nix).
  prelude.unique in staged-resolution is per-TARGET, not per-attachment.

INSTRUMENT CONTROLS AS REPORTED: removeAttrs grep returned hits under lib/ AND 79 under .worktrees/ (exclusion meaningful, predicate live). __provider = 0 in kernel, 18 in lib/compat/ (the predicate CAN match; the kernel really is clean of it). codebase-memory was NOT used for any reachability claim, per its attrset-mediated-call gap.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD, SAME DAY, BY AN INDEPENDENT READ. TWO OF ITS CLAIMS ARE REFUTED AND THE ORCHESTRATOR HAD ALREADY RELAYED BOTH TO THE OWNER AS FINDINGS.

REFUTED 1 — THE STRIP-LIST 'DRIFT' IS A PURPOSE SPLIT, NOT DRIFT. The two lists that KEEP __entry are binding-CONTEXT projections (baseCtxOf, inherited-context) where __entry is a legitimate binding. The two that STRIP it are BOTH NAMED coordDims — product-COORDINATE projections — and their own comment states the reason: 'The reserved decls keys are graph machinery, never producing-scope coordinates.' __entry is not a coordinate. Three key sets, two purposes, internally consistent.
REFUTED 2 — staged-resolution.nix's comment 'the same __-key strip as attr 1' IS TRUE. Attr 1 is inherited-context (confirmed by grep -n '^  # [0-9]' over structural.nix). RESTRICTED TO __-KEYS THE TWO SETS ARE IDENTICAL: {__edges, __containment, __coords, __root}. The only difference is suppressedPolicies, which is NOT a __-key. The qualifier is load-bearing and correct.
⇒ ★ THE METHOD LESSON: A SET DIFFERENCE IS NOT A DEFECT UNTIL YOU HAVE READ WHAT EACH SITE IS FOR. 'These four lists disagree' is a shape observation. 'These four lists were MEANT to agree' is the claim that turns it into a defect, and it was never checked. The original reading was produced by comparing key sets without reading purposes — a predicate that was SOUND (the sets do differ) while proving a DIFFERENT PROPOSITION than the one reported.
WHAT SURVIVES: the lists still encode graph facts as payload, and after the migration they shrink to TWO keys — __edges (gen-scope's own) and suppressedPolicies (a typed control fact on its own inheritSet carrier). THEY DO NOT DISAPPEAR. Any spec claiming the strip lists go away is wrong.

★★ AND __entry MUST NOT MIGRATE — ITS SHAPE IS CONTRACTUALLY PINNED BY AN EXTERNAL LIBRARY. lib/scope-adapter.nix states gen-select's default scope adapter reads entryFor = decls.__entry and kind = node.type. Confirmed at the adapter contract, not inferred. And its ~14 read sites are attribute reads off the entry (.name / .id_hash / .system), NOT traversals — it is the node's IDENTITY ACCESSOR, not an edge stored as payload. Of the four payload facts this bead names, only __containment is cleanly an edge; __coords is a product-coordinate TUPLE (recoverable as a per-dim keyed inbound query, but see the MEDIUM-confidence caveat below); __root is a ONE-BIT NODE-KIND PARTITION that should move to a node field rather than become an edge, and is the lowest-value of the four.

★★★ NEW DEFECT FOUND WHILE ANSWERING, AND IT IS A LANDMINE DIRECTLY UNDER THE MIGRATION THIS BEAD PROPOSES: THE SIX FRAMEWORK-RESERVED STRUCTURAL EDGE KINDS ARE PRE-REGISTERED WITH THE WRONG PROJECTION TARGET. reserved-registry.nix's mkReservedRegistry seeds reserved = prelude.genAttrs reservedNames (n: { stratum = ...; }) with NO 'to' field; allRaw = reserved // table then passes through entryOf, whose to = raw.to or 'materialize'. So contains / include / kindOf / member / reach / reach-suppress ALL COMPILE WITH to = 'materialize' — ON THE FROZEN PARITY TRACE. NOT AN INFERENCE: ci/tests/projection-tag.nix states it verbatim ('EVERY other kind ... defaults to = "materialize"') and pins expected = 'materialize' for a framework kind.
INERT TODAY ONLY BECAUSE THE POOLS ARE PHYSICALLY SEPARATE (memberEdges/relationEdges never merge into edgesForRoot). ★ THE MOMENT A contains EDGE REACHES edgesForRoot, materializeFilter KEEPS IT AND IT LANDS ON THE PARITY TRACE. The relations desugar already solved this by stamping to = 'query' explicitly; the pre-registered structural rows need the same, AND THE FIX BELONGS AT THE SEED — preRegisteredStrata's row shape carries only strata today and HAS NO PLACE TO SAY 'to'.

PRODUCER CENSUS, correcting this bead's 'only demand has a live producer'. Command: for k in contains include kindOf member reach reach-suppress nest defer demand; do grep -rn "kind = \"$k\"" --include='*.nix' lib/; done — POSITIVE CONTROL: fired on 3 of 9 in the same run.
  member -> concern-collectors.nix:200 (Model-Q intent shape)   nest -> edges.nix:453 (gated, corpus-empty)   demand -> demand.nix:159,:173
  contains / include / kindOf / reach / reach-suppress / defer -> ZERO.
So THREE kinds have producers, not one — though neither member nor nest reaches the live trace. Dynamic-kind escape is closed: relationCollisionMessage rejects any user label in reservedNames, so NO USER SURFACE CAN EVER PRODUCE A contains EDGE. These six are framework-reserved names awaiting a framework producer.

MEDIUM-CONFIDENCE ITEM THE AGENT FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSERTING: whether __coords is CLEANLY replaceable by a query. It did not trace what resolved-settings' coords is consumed FOR downstream, so an ordering or TOTALITY requirement that a coordinate tuple satisfies and a sparse query result would not cannot be ruled out. Named instrument to settle it: read policyLayersAt and gen-settings' batch contract, and check whether coordsEq (attrNames a == attrNames b) imposes a dim-completeness invariant.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ CORRECTION — **`__entry` IS NOT EXTERNALLY PINNED. I ASSERTED THAT AS A BOUNDARY AND IT IS FALSE.**
Measured 2026-07-29 by the topology spec's author, who checked the claim rather than inheriting it.

WHAT I WROTE, in this bead and in two dispatch briefs: "lib/scope-adapter.nix states gen-select's default
scope adapter reads entryFor = decls.__entry, so the SHAPE is contractually pinned by an external library."
WHAT IS TRUE: gen-select's `entryFor` and `project` are **DEFAULTED, OVERRIDABLE PARAMETERS**. den-hoag
never overrides either (two `mkContext` sites). A default is not a contract. There is no external pin.

★ THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES; THE ARGUMENT DOES NOT. `__entry` should still stay, for reasons that are
den-hoag's own rather than borrowed: its reads are ATTRIBUTE READS off the entry (`.name`, `.id_hash`,
`.system`), not traversals; it is an IDENTITY PROJECTION rather than a graph fact; and the
containment-as-edges design DEPENDS on it as the coordinate VALUE — `coordsOf n` maps each ancestor's
`node.type` to its `decls.__entry`, so removing it would remove the thing the new query returns.
⇒ RIGHT ANSWER, WRONG REASON, AND THE WRONG REASON WAS LOAD-BEARING IN TWO BRIEFS. This is the
THEORY/MECHANISM/ARGUMENT split applying to a boundary rather than to a design: I stated a constraint as
externally imposed when it is internally chosen, which would have made it un-revisitable for the wrong
reason. A constraint we choose can be re-chosen; a contract cannot.
★ AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY I HAVE PASSED ON A CLAIM WITHOUT RUNNING THE ONE COMMAND THAT CHECKS IT —
after the c42df53 commit ordering and the entry-3 CI inference. All three were inherited from a prior
agent's report and repeated in a brief. The standing rule "state every brief's fact as REFUTABLE" caught all
three, which is the system working; but the cheaper fix is that an orchestrator relaying a fact into a brief
owns verifying it.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ GATE VERDICT ON THE FIRST MIGRATION SPEC: **REDESIGN.** Independent adversarial review, artefact and
rubric only. Artefact intact (md5 a80f1e18a321f71928bdc4c00d467799, 379 lines, on disk AND at papers
080c130). Every count below from `/run/current-system/sw/bin/grep`; exits read on the next line.

★★★ THE CENTRAL ERROR — **THE DESIGN RE-CREATES THE DEFECT IT REMOVES.** Measured on the corpus shape
(env <- host <- user, env via containTo), exit 0:
    dimKinds            = [ host, user ]      <- env is NOT a dim
    host:axon.parent    = "env:prod"          <- containTo made env a P-PARENT
    host:axon declKeys  = [ __entry, __root, grant, host ]   <- 5kt pollution, live
`coordsOf n = { type(a) -> __entry(a) | a in {n} u inboundClosure(n) }` over a pool that the spec's own
obligation fills with ROOT->ROOT containment reaches `env:prod`, giving key set {env, host, user} against
dimKinds [host, user].
  C1 AS SPECIFIED (attrNames coords == sort dimKinds, throws NAMED otherwise) -> **HARD THROW ON THE NORMAL
    CORPUS TOPOLOGY.**
  RELAXED to the cardinality test it replaces -> 3 != 2 -> flat arm -> **THE SILENT SETTINGS DROP RETURNS.**
⇒ EITHER WAY BLOCKER 2 IS NOT FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION. IT IS RE-CREATED WITH A DIFFERENT POLLUTION SOURCE.
★ AND THE SPEC REFUTES ITSELF: its own §7 states that a containment ancestor **is NOT a product dimension**,
which is exactly why `containmentRelations` is prepended separately today. `coordsOf` COLLAPSES TWO
DIFFERENT RELATIONS INTO ONE. Same failure reproduced verbatim: `error: gen-product: unknown-dim
'authToken' — declared (free) dims: blade, rack, zone`.
REPAIRABLE by filtering the closure to `type ∈ dimKinds` — but that is not what is specified, and it costs
the "one closure over one edge set" collapse the design is sold on.

★★ TWO OF FOUR WITNESSES CANNOT FAIL — A THIRD VACUOUS ANCHOR, THIS TIME ON THE MIGRATION ITSELF.
  A — DISCRIMINATES. Independently re-derived in one eval, three arms, one variable, exit 0:
      0 bindings (CONTROL) -> workers 16 | 1 -> workers 1 SILENT DROP | 2 -> THREW.
      Red today, green required after, control reaches the right answer in the same run. KEEP THIS.
  B — DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE OLD FROM NEW. On the spec's own >=3-dim fixture, today's
      `unique (parentChain ++ containment)` ALREADY equals the required-after answer and `__coords` keys are

declared (free) dims: host, user". coordOf reproduces the DEPOLLUTED coordDims at every root; cellCoordsOf
reproduces __coords at the cell; and rev-2's kill is confirmed real — cellCoordsOf is EMPTY at the two
non-dim roots whose live layers are 22 and 11. §6.5/R25 also confirmed: isFullCell host:axon true while
isCellNode false, a root down the cell arm on a count match.

KILL 2 — THE STRUCTURAL CANCELLATION. ★ VERIFIED ON BOTH ARMS AND **STRONGER THAN THE SPEC ARGUES**.
The reviewer REFUSED the spec's instrument: rev3/pA.nix reconstructs cellKinds as candidateKinds intersect
dimKinds, which makes cellKinds-subset-dimKinds — one of the two side conditions — TRUE BY THE INSTRUMENT'S
OWN DEFINITION. Conclusion right, instrument weaker than presented.
Live oracle used instead: a settings layer at a bogus dim aborts with den-hoag printing its own binding —
"den-hoag: settings layer (§2.6): 'at' names dimension 'zzz_bogus' not in the product (product dims: host,
user, cluster, env)". THAT LIST IS settingsDims, and it EQUALS allKinds. Not a reconstruction.
★★ AND THE SIDE CONDITIONS ARE IDENTITIES, NOT MEASUREMENTS. lib/entity.nix:174 — registries = prelude.
mapAttrs (kindName: _: tree.config.den.${kindName}) denMeta — mapAttrs PRESERVES THE KEY SET, so attrNames
registries equals attrNames meta BY CONSTRUCTION. Confirmed empirically on a schema where a kind has ZERO
entities: pod registry size 0 but still a registries key, candidatesMissingRegistry empty. A third shape
where a membership tuple names pod: pod enters dimKinds, the subset holds, settingsDims still equals allKinds.
⇒ cellKinds ⊆ candidateKinds ⊆ allKinds = registryKinds, and cellKinds ⊆ tupleDimKinds, so cellKinds ⊆
dimKinds; dimKinds ⊆ registryKinds = allKinds. THE CANCELLATION IS STRUCTURAL. C9's hardest problem — moving
the codomain off the retiring construct — IS SOLVED STRUCTURALLY, and THE SPEC UNDERSTATES ITS OWN RESULT by
presenting the side conditions as measured.

KILL 3 — THE attachments-EMPTY TRAP. Built A / A' / B and recorded WHICH ENDPOINT is missing per pair:
  A  (suite multiDen verbatim)          2 pairs, both blade   rootKindChildPairCount 0   allResolve true
  A' (attachments = { })                1 pair,  blade        count 0   allResolve FALSE
     red: parentExists=false AND childExists=false; child kind blade, NOT a root kind
  B  (membership names zone, rack:r2 one attachment)  2 pairs  count 1   allResolve FALSE
     red: parentExists=true, childExists=false, childIsRootKind=true — the isolated child-id fault
★ THE TRAP IS REAL AND THE SPEC'S ROOT CAUSE IS RIGHT: A''s red is the wrong PARENT id (rack:r1 is not a
node; the minted ones are rack:r1@zone:z1 and @zone:z2), and the child id goes wrong only DOWNSTREAM of it
since childId is built from parentId. §5(a)'s root-kind rule is untouched — count 0. ★ BUT THE SPEC DOES NOT
MENTION THE CHILD ALSO REDDENING, WHICH MAKES THE TRAP MORE DANGEROUS THAN WRITTEN. Witness C assertion 3
DOES discharge the vacuity obligation for assertion 1: 0/0/1 on one instrument in one run, and 0 on precisely
the fixture rev 2 offered as the control.

════ THE DEFECTS ════
⚠ WITNESS F'S ASSERTION IS LITERALLY FALSE. settingsDims = prelude.unique (dimKinds ++ rootScopeKinds) is
FIRST-OCCURRENCE-ORDERED giving [host, user, cluster, env]; sort allKinds gives [cluster, env, host, user].
The equality fails. Needs sort on both sides. ★ A GUARD WRITTEN RED IS WORSE THAN A VACUOUS ONE — someone
weakens it.
⚠ ARM 2 DOES NOT EVALUATE ONCE AN ASPECT IS PRESENT, so no behavioural instrument can confirm the
cancellation there: "gen-scope: node 'cluster:k3s' not reachable from roots". ★ CAUSE — __containment CARRIES
THE SAME DANGLING-ID DEFECT AS containmentPairs: under a plain member the cell's __containment spells
cluster:k3s BARE while the minted node is cluster:k3s@env:prod, and ancestorResolvedKeys reads it. A SECOND
SITE of §5(a)'s one-id-rule obligation, LIVE ON PUBLIC SURFACE (den.membership + den.include), and the spec
names only containmentPairs. It SUPPORTS the design (§6.3 deletes the payload, obligation 1 fixes it) but
belongs in §5 and the ledger. FILED SEPARATELY as a live wrong-answer.
⚠ WITNESS C ASSERTION 2 IS VACUOUS ON ITS OWN FIXTURE — the same law, unapplied to the sibling assertion.
§5(b) is REAL and was measured with a same-run control (gr6: zone:z1 containTo rack:r9 with no blade cell
gives NO pair naming r9; rack:r2 with a cell gives a pair). But fixture B has NO cell-less child, and
assertion 2 names rack:r1 which IS NOT AN INSTANCE OF FIXTURE B AT ALL. On fixture B the zone-rack pair IS
emitted, so assertion 2 is green before and after. §5(b) has no discriminating input anywhere in the spec.
⚠ R27's STATED PRECONDITION IS THE WRONG MECHANISM. gen-product/lib/chain.nix header: "containmentChain
returns all 2^|D| subsets ... as a LINEAR EXTENSION of the inclusion order" (subs = subsets D, mkEntry over
every subset). The ancestor's singleton is in baseChain by POWERSET-COMPLETENESS FOR EVERY LINEARIZATION;
den.linearization.dims changes only the ORDER, not membership. So "the reduction holds when the linearization
respects ancestry" names a precondition that is NOT THE OPERATIVE ONE — and no named abort attaches to it.
RIGHT DECISION (spec the slice test), WRONG REASON. C6 gap, and C7-a: the one gen-product export the argument
turns on was not enumerated.
⚠ projectsMaterialize's RESIDUAL SET IS MISDESCRIBED AND THE ARM IS LIVE. Measured: an unregistered label
gives inTable=false, projectsMaterialize=true, KEPT. The spec says "the only labels that can reach it are
user-registered ones" — but a user-REGISTERED kind HAS a row, so .to exists and the or never fires for it.
The reachable set is labels registered NOWHERE, and the spec gives no reachability analysis for them. The
framework half IS by construction (reservedNames = attrNames preRegisteredKinds is an identity); the residual
half is UNDISCHARGED. ★ And defending the arm because "it sits on the frozen-parity path" is C8(b) IN FORM —
weakened further because §3.1 already argues nothing in this design can reach that path.
⚠ NEW — §6.3 UNDERSTATES THE CHANGE SURFACE. resolved-settings.nix compute binds coords = coordsOfNode node
and uses it THREE times: isFullCell, baseChain, and policyLayersAt resolutionActs coords aspectEntry. THE
SPEC HAS ZERO OCCURRENCES OF policyLayers OR nodeCoords. policyLayersAt writes scope = nodeCoords into the
layer record and gen-settings lib/resolve.nix SURFACES it (layerLabel keeps scope/rendered/via) — the
reviewer printed scope in provenance in its own run. Deleting coordsOfNode/coordDims leaves that argument
undefined; the substitution is derivable but unstated, ★ AND AT A POLLUTED ROOT IT CHANGES EMITTED PROVENANCE
scope FROM [grant,host] TO [host] — an OBSERVABLE OUTPUT CHANGE with no equivalence-vs-identity ruling. C8(d).
⚠ WITNESS E ROW 4 IS A HOLE, and unlike rows 1-3 it is CHEAP. The spec says it "needs the same fixture work";
it does not — the discriminating input (dim-kind root with a dim-kind containment ancestor) is ONE COORDINATE
added to a membership tuple, and fixture B already is one. IT IS THE ROW THAT CATCHES THE DEFECT THE AUTHOR
CAUGHT IN ITSELF.

════ CONFIRMED ════
R27 CONFIRMED BEHAVIOURALLY WITH CONTROL: root rack:r2 (type rack, a dim) whose containment ancestor zone:z1
is ALSO a dim gives workers 44, provenance rendered "zone=z1", scope [zone]; the control (same fleet, no
containTo) gives workers 1 and provenance default only. Rev-2's "type a not in dimKinds" DROPS THAT SLICE
SILENTLY. The unsoundness is real.
R26 CONFIRMED: __containment is ABSENT on every root and empty on the cell, both arms. Mechanism read at
lib/fleet.nix cellChildrenFor — product.slice drops parentDim from c before filtering the leaf dim. THE
BRIEF'S CLAIM IS REFUTED; containmentRelations is the second source (measured).
§6.1 CITATION OBLIGATION SHIPPED and is the cleanest part of the spec. Primary text re-derived independently:
lines 623/624 give 4.3 Undirected Graphs, 923/924 give 5.2 Graph Transpose. The 8 comment sites are
comments-only; ★ the archive seed was corrected IN PLACE WITH A WARNING rather than deleted.
§6.2 SEED VERIFIED: preRegisteredStrata is exactly 5 in-file sites plus 1 test; nine compiled kinds, ALL NINE
to = "materialize". Witness D's instrument pre-verified: contains 1, demand 1, unlabeled 1 today, must become
0/1/1 — two same-predicate same-instrument controls, fails today and passes after.
§6.8 HONOURS qxz: the linear claim is WITHDRAWN, 2.98 and the two implementations are cited, relations are
named as not-the-leading-term, only the marginal claim is kept, and the ag3 hoist is IN-CHANGE. ag3 confirmed
OPEN P0. containmentPairs has NO lib/ caller — verified (definition, export, one comment, an inherit
re-export, 2 test sites). C7-b satisfied.

════ THE RUBRIC ════
C1 / C1-a / C2 / C2-a PASS — Mokhov transpose used as a primitive with adjacency-only stated; multi-valued
containment legal under the edge model; cycle guard named.
C3 LICENSING PARTIAL — the three-projection vocabulary invites the type reduction; the spec correctly demotes
it to an optimisation but attaches the WRONG precondition, which re-licenses it for the wrong reason.
C4 PASS — MISSING as a STATED VALUE, not an absent key. Finer direction.
C5 COORDINATES PASS, independently re-derived; replicator and seed both fixed.
C6 TOTALITY **FAIL ON TWO** — the linearization precondition names the wrong mechanism and has no violation
behaviour; projectsMaterialize's unregistered-label arm has its residual set misidentified, behaviour
measured live (kept on-trace), no guard and no reachability argument.
C7 CONSTRUCTION-VS-REPAIR PASS, STRONGLY — the edge identity contains/from->to turns the two-representation
duplicate into IDEMPOTENCE rather than a dedup step; coordOf is total with no or-fallback; strip lists are
DELETED not extended.
C7-a PRIMITIVE GRANULARITY PARTIAL — expandPreorder vs the reverse-reachability family is a re-used ruling
with both disqualifiers cited, and foldPreorder's emit-cannot-prune was CHECKED not assumed; but
gen-product's containmentChain powerset semantics — the export the cascade-filter argument turns on — was not
enumerated, and that is exactly where the precondition went wrong.
C7-b COST PASS.
C8 PARITY **FAIL ON (d)** (policyLayersAt scope, unstated parity notion); (b) RISK on the projectsMaterialize
frozen-path defence. Otherwise strong: §6.1 states byte EQUIVALENCE with its scope and its gap, and §3.1
WITHDRAWS the parity story rather than defending on oracle grounds.
C9 / C9-a **PASS — THE STRONGEST C9 ANSWER IN THIS ARC.** Entry 3 named and cited; THEORY/MECHANISM/ARGUMENT
answered SEPARATELY with one part measured FALSE and KILLED rather than argued; the register's own §8 claim
ratified as false FOR THIS DESIGN; and the codomain moved off the retiring construct to allKinds —
STRUCTURALLY, as verified. Vocabulary is the successor's, not the retiring construct's. Caveat: the guard on
it (Witness F) is mis-stated.

════ THE SIX CONDITIONS ════
1. Name policyLayersAt's coords consumer in §6.3; state which projection feeds it and RULE equivalence-vs-
   identity on the emitted scope provenance. C8(d).
2. Fix Witness F to sort both sides. FALSE as written.
3. Give Witness C assertion 2 a fixture reaching §5(b) — a contained child with NO SURVIVING CELL — or delete
   it. The gr6 fixture is that input, measured with a same-run control.
4. Replace §6.1's linearization precondition with the correct mechanism (containmentChain emits all 2^|D|
   subsets, so membership is LINEARIZATION-INDEPENDENT), or, if a precondition survives, give it a NAMED
   ABORT. C6.
5. Correct §6.2's residual-set sentence (unregistered labels, NOT user-registered ones); give the arm a
   reachability argument or a guard. Re-ground the keep-decision on resolved-configuration, NOT on the frozen
   path. C6 + C8(b).
6. Build Witness E ROW 4. One coordinate on an existing fixture; not the branching/diamond cost.
DO NOT BLOCK ON: Witness E rows 1-3 — that is HONEST LEDGERING (§11 item 4 flags it, the scope is stated as
single-source-linear-measured, the claim is not generalised, and resolved-settings.nix independently records
both deltas as latent).

════ COVERAGE — WHAT RESTS ON PROSE THE REVIEWER DID NOT EXECUTE ════
§8 entirely (runPrePass's five-to-three-value narrowing, the mint-ordering entanglement) — read-only.
§2.3's rack:r2 keeping parent=null under a static membership tuple — not re-measured.
§6.4's gen-select entryFor/project defaults and the two mkContext call sites — R2 taken on the spec's word.
§6.6's four strip-list dispositions — staged-resolution.nix baseCtxOf and structural.nix inherited-context
not audited.
§6.8's cubic — qxz read from the bead, series not re-run; prelude.unique's quadratic and scope.ancestors's
O(D^2) taken from the spec's source quotes.
Witness E rows 1-3 — unbuilt by the author AND by the reviewer. Branching/diamond cascade order remains
UNMEASURED BY ANYONE.
★ THE LINEARIZATION USER-BREAK — reasoned from chain.nix's header and subs = subsets D, NOT executed with a
redeclared den.linearization.dims. THAT IS THE ONE PROBE LEFT TO RUN if condition 4 must be airtight.
The suite ran 1919/1937 but the 18 red were not diffed.

════ ★★ THE MUTATION SWEEP IS THE STRONGEST CORE DISCIPLINE IN THIS ARC ════
**ALL 28 TARGETS SWEPT, NOT A SAMPLE: 28 iterated, 28 flipped to EXIT 1 with a named "✗ <name> [MUTATED]"
row, 0 anomalies.** ★ And the sweep DERIVES ITS TARGET LIST FROM THE TOOL'S OWN UNKNOWN-TARGET ABORT rather

Groups: F 6 (codomain + the guard-on-guard), P 5 (three projections, P1 strengthened to assert id_hash which

★ §12 prints the recipe AND the hash IN THE SPEC, including the `--apply` form (`nix eval --file` returns the
lambda, so `--argstr` is wrong) and the exit-status-on-its-own-line discipline.

════ THE SIX CONDITIONS ════
1 C8(d) DISCHARGED. Third consumer named: resolved-settings.nix:273 `policyLayersAt resolutionActs coords
  aspectEntry`. Substitution stated. ★ RULING = **VALUE IDENTITY, PROVENANCE EQUIVALENCE**. Value identity is
  UNCONDITIONAL — gen-settings/lib/resolve.nix:50 says verbatim the label is "fully opaque to

  against the clean arm's 3 — the host=axon 33 layer SILENTLY DROPPED, making §4.1(b) visible as a MISSING
  ENTRY rather than an argument.
2 WITNESS F DISCHARGED. Confirmed r3's assertion FALSE: relation arm settingsDims = [host,user,cluster,env]
  vs sort allKinds = [cluster,env,host,user]. Corrected to sort-both-sides (true on both arms). ★★ AND A
  **GUARD ON THE GUARD** ADDED: the unsorted equality is false on the relation arm and true on the tuple arm
  — **IT FLIPS WITH THE VERY VARIABLE THE WITNESS HOLDS FIXED.** Pinned as core check F1a. ★ The CONSEQUENCE
  was chased too — §9 line 828 restated the false form in different words and was fixed.
3 WITNESS C ASSERTION 2 DISCHARGED, FIXTURE BUILT. One fleet, three racks, one variable (how zone:z1 contains
  rack:_ is declared): tuple-declared r2 → 1 pair; containTo-declared r9 (relation, no surviving cell) → 0
  pairs; r0 uncontained control. ★ ABSENCE CONTROL IN THE SAME RUN: workers r9 = 44 (the relation IS live),
  r0 = 1. Added as numbered assertion 4 — **an absence claim about the pair needs a positive claim about the
  relation.** ★ BONUS MEASURED: r2 (tuple) resolves 1 while r9 (relation) resolves 44 — §2.3's
  two-representations defect now measured ON RESOLVED SETTINGS, not just on `parent`. Added to §5.
4 LINEARIZATION PRECONDITION (C6) DISCHARGED — ★ **DELETED, NOT RENAMED.** chain.nix emits all 2^|D| subsets
  as a linear extension, so membership is linearization-INDEPENDENT and den.linearization.dims moves order
  only. No precondition survives ⇒ no named abort needed. What the reduction actually turns on is (2)'s
  uniqueness, whose violation is ALREADY the named errors.coordCollision. The slice test stays the contract —
  now because the reduction is cell-arm-only (R27), not because of a lurking precondition. Consequences fixed
  at R27 and the §11 closing paragraph.
5 projectsMaterialize RESIDUAL SET (C6 + C8(b)) DISCHARGED, KEEP RE-GROUNDED. Corrected: the reachable set is
  labels registered NOWHERE (a registered kind goes through entryOf which SETS `to`, so the `or` never fires).
  Reachability argued AT THE PRODUCERS: exactly 3 constructors feed edgesForRoot; gen-edge/lib/edge.nix:29
  defaults kind ? null; edgesFor's defaultEdges and deliveryEdgesAt's renderDelivery pass no kind;
  demandLib.toEdges passes the literal reserved "demand". Measured non-vacuously: content fleet 1 edge labels
  [null], demand fleet 3 edges labels ["demand"]. ★ THE SOUNDNESS OF TESTING A POST-FILTER FOR A PRE-FILTER
  QUESTION IS STATED EXPLICITLY (the arm KEEPS, so an unregistered label would survive and show). Arm
  confirmed live-as-a-function in the same run. ★ **THE FROZEN-PATH DEFENCE IS WITHDRAWN AND NAMED AS
  C8(b)-IN-FORM**, with an expiry condition and the in-file disagreement recorded (assembleEdges already
  aborts NAMED on the identical condition).
6 WITNESS E ROW 4 BUILT. rack:r9 is a root with type rack in dimKinds whose ancestor zone:z1 is also a dim.
  **Slice rule keeps [{zone}], type rule keeps [] — rulesAgree = false.** Behaviourally workers = 44 with
  provenance rendered "zone=z1", scope [zone]; under the type rule it silently falls to 1. Same-run control
  rack:r0: empty closure, rules AGREE, workers 1. ★ Rows 1-3 left EXPLICITLY unbuilt and §11 item 4 rescoped
  to rows 1-3 only — not quietly widened.

════ den-hoag-3t8 FOLDED IN AS §5.2 ════
§5's title and intro rewritten: the one-id-rule obligation has TWO SITES. lib/fleet.nix:125 spells a bare
"${d}:${c.${d}.name}" while fleet.nix:167 routes the parent side through the shared mintedRootId. Measured
with one variable (containTo vs plain member): the plain-member arm has 4 payload entries of which **2
DANGLE** (user:alice@host:axon → cluster:k3s, and cluster:k3s@env:prod → user:alice), both naming

then on 'cluster:k3s'. ★★ NON-VACUITY INSIDE THE SAME ARM: 2 of 4 entries RESOLVE and 2 DANGLE — both values,
one instrument. ★ AND THE CONTROL ARM'S ZERO-ENTRY "ALL RESOLVE" IS FLAGGED AS VACUOUS AND EXPLICITLY NOT
OFFERED AS THE CONTROL. Reachable from den.membership + den.include alone. Added as R28 and §11 item 5.
New §10 rows: R29 (linearization), R30 (residual set), R31 (Witness F false), R32 (policyLayersAt).

Witness E rows 1-3 (branching/diamond): no fixture, UNMEASURED BY ANYONE. §8 entirely (runPrePass narrowing,
mint-ordering): read-only. §6.4's gen-select entryFor/project and the two mkContext sites: read, not

★★ GATE REVIEW r4 — containment-as-edges. **VERDICT: VALIDATED-WITH-CONDITIONS.** FIVE conditions, ALL
coverage-statement / instrument repairs — **none touches the construction, and none touches a condition-1..6
discharge. ALL SIX r3 CONDITIONS ARE DISCHARGED.** Hashes re-derived and matching (1959c450… / 992;

ci/ parity/` is EMPTY, as is 8453edc..3e31da5, with a same-run positive control (the all-paths range returns
1 file) proving the instrument reads changes. **Both cited paths confirmed to EXIST at 3e31da5 via
`git cat-file -e` — the path-exists-first trap, applied.**

════ ★★ THE MUTATION SWEEP — VERIFIED, AND STRONGER THAN THE AUTHOR CLAIMED ════
EXECUTED with the target list derived from the tool's own abort: **28 targets / 28 EXIT 1 / 28 carrying their
own named [MUTATED] row / 28 with EXACTLY ONE RED ROW.** ★ That last column is the author's understatement:
**NO MUTATION COLLATERALLY REDDENS ANOTHER CHECK**, so each check is independently load-bearing on the
harness.
· Does it enumerate every check? EXECUTED INDEPENDENTLY: `grep -c '^      name = "'` gives 28, and the
  file-derived name set diffed against the tool-derived set is BYTE-IDENTICAL. The green banner's count is
  `count applied`, so the printed 28/28 cannot drift from the list either.
· Can a check escape? EXECUTED: appended a 29th — auto-counted 29/29, auto-listed by the abort, auto-swept.
  **NO CHECK CAN ESCAPE THE SWEEP.**
· Is every check boolean? EXECUTED, YES — a non-boolean `ok` would make `!c.ok` throw with NO named row; all
  28 produced one. Mutation is a real logical inversion.

════ ★★★ F-5 — AND IT CORRECTS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN CAPTION ════
**THE SWEEP PROVES HARNESS REACHABILITY, NOT CHECK STRENGTH.** EXECUTED: the reviewer's 29th check was
`{ name = "Z9-vacuous-asserts-nothing"; ok = true; }` — **it asserts NOTHING and it sweeps PERFECTLY**:
counted, listed, EXIT 1, own [MUTATED] row.
§12.2's own sentence is exactly right ("an all-green run is worth nothing unless a red one is reachable").
★ **THE ORCHESTRATOR'S r4 CAPTION — "28 flipped ⇒ the strongest core discipline in this arc" — READS AS
VALIDATING THE CHECKS, WHICH `mutate` CANNOT DO.** Recorded as an over-read of mine, not an author defect.
COUNTER-EVIDENCE THAT THE CHECKS ARE MOSTLY LOAD-BEARING, executed on targets the author did not choose:
pointing `coordOf` at a nonexistent decls key reddens P1 AND ONLY P1 (P2/P4 compare attrNames only, so P1 is
the single point pinning the VALUE); dropping F1's sort reddens F1.

════ ★★ F-1 (C6, DECISIVE) — THE CORE EXECUTES NONE OF §6.1's THREE NAMED ABORTS ════
· **`MISSING`** — §6.1 states it TWICE ("a MISSING axis is a *stated* value, not an absent key"; "Absence is a
  decision, twice"). The core's cellCoordsOf (line 259) **OMITS THE KEY**. ★ EXECUTED: patching it to the
  SPECIFIED form turns **P2 RED**. So the core does not merely skip the specified behaviour — **P2 REQUIRES
  THE REJECTED ONE. A C4 COMMITMENT IS PINNED INVERTED.**
· **`errors.coordCollision`** — implemented by nothing, reached by nothing. EXECUTED: `head ms` → `last ms`
  leaves 28/28 green EXIT 0. ★ AND THE NULL RESULT CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROL, because a no-op patch proves
  nothing: multiplicity instrumented directly, **max |ms| = 1 at every node of every dim**, with the same
  table showing 0 AND 1 so the instrument reads multiplicity. ⇒ The collision arm is UNREACHABLE on these
  fixtures. **This matters because §6.1's R29 rests condition 4's WHOLE REPLACEMENT ARGUMENT on it — "the
  guard the reduction needs therefore already exists, is named." IT HAS ZERO EXECUTABLE PRESENCE.**
· **`errors.unknownAxis`** — F3 asserts only that its precondition is unreachable at HEAD; the spec is honest
  that this is the point.
F-2 (C6/C9-a): **ONE BINDING PLAYS TWO INCOMPATIBLE ROLES.** Core line 271 `rev2CoordsOf = cellCoordsOf`. P2
reads it as REVISION 2's construction (correctly {} at non-dim roots); P4 reads it as THE DESIGN'S PROJECTION
