  that as a rule: when a defect's remedy would satisfy the assertion that detects it,
  the assertion is measuring the wrong thing.

⇒ COMMIT AUTHORISED. Every remaining red is either individually verified as
ops-blocked against a rejected design, or a recorded witness for a tracked open
defect. That is the three-state posture honoured rather than approximated.
⇒ NOT A GATE CONDITION, TRACKED SEPARATELY: the coarse-assertion sweep
(den-hoag-9xo.79). It bounds what the SUITE CAN NO LONGER SEE rather than what this
migration broke, and holding a verified bounded migration for a tree-wide audit
would be scope creep. The migration's own script-caused instances are already bounded
by condition 2's sweep.
close_reason: GATE MET AND LANDED. Commit e6c8edc pushed to origin/main (c42df53..e6c8edc), 67 files +2628/-2085. parity 71/71 exit 0; ci 1919/1937 exit 1 with 18 known-red each verified INDIVIDUALLY and zero unattributed - 16 ops-blocked against the rejected 9xo.62 design (12 by direct opsInBody, 4 by measured-empty seed), 1 9xo.75 witness, 1 deliberate expected-red. All three conditions discharged: A bucket re-derived per-test at current state with the tux check (0 hits - den-pipe went 21 to 12 when 9xo.76 landed, so the hm family was already cleared); sibling sweep with a 2/2 positive control by re-introducing both known corruptions; C bucket triaged 4 to 1. Coarse-assertion sweep split to 9xo.79 as suite-quality work. Commit message enumerates every red by cause and explains the 1946 to 1937 total.

title: [compat] arm (b) cannot materialize user-bearing NixOS config: attribute id_hash missing at collections.nix:205 on all 7 hosts — and it is a LADDER, the next rung is already known
description:
★★ THIS IS THE CRITICAL PATH TO THE MILESTONE. Everything else measured today is
graph-level; THIS is what stands between den-hoag and a materialized den v1
configuration. Measured 2026-07-28, den-hoag frozen at c42df53 via git archive
(concurrent writer edits explicitly NOT in the measurement), corpus nix-config
MAIN tree HEAD 9ebf3316. ARM (a) EVALUATED GREEN, so this is a real blocker under
the works-on-den gate and not an arm-(a) failure wearing an arm-(b) label.

THE FAILURE. Arm (b) cannot materialize USER-BEARING NixOS config:
    .config.users.users         -> error: attribute 'id_hash' missing
    .config.home-manager.users  -> error: attribute 'id_hash' missing
at den-hoag lib/attributes/collections.nix:205. ALL SEVEN HOSTS.

★ THE GRAPH RESOLVES; ONLY ASPECT CONTENT DIES. In the same arm:
    .config.networking.hostName   -> "blade"
    nixosConfigurations attrNames -> all 7
So this is not a topology failure. The nodes are there and the edges are there;
what fails is materializing the content hanging off them.

★★ IT IS A LADDER, NOT A GAP -- and that is the finding that should shape the
work. Making :205 total IN A SCRATCH COPY did not produce a materialized config;
it moved the failure to a FURTHER rung:
    den-compat: the hjem battery requires den.hosts.<system>.<name>.hjem.module
    set explicitly            (lib/compat/builtins.nix:230)
ON A CORPUS WITH ZERO hjem REFERENCES. Whatever fixes :205 will surface the next
rung immediately, so this must be scoped as a LADDER CLIMB with a rung census,
not as one defect to patch. Budgeting it as a single fix will be wrong.

WHAT IT SURVIVES -- the obvious escapes are already closed:
· The runbook's belt-severed override set (lib/compat/parity/runbook.md:188-192,
  gen-schema + gen-merge, four nested overrides) does NOT clear it.
· den/gen-aspects rollback makes it WORSE, not better, and den-hoag turns its own
  gate on itself: bf9325f -> `undeclared aspect key 'hardware' (closed-key gate
  on)`; ded8e76 -> `expected a set but found a list: [ ]`
  (lib/compat/gated-aspects-type.nix:57-58).

★ AND THE CORPUS HEAD IS FURTHER ALONG THAN THE FROZEN PARITY CORPUS. At parity
pin b0b20769 arm (b) fails EARLIER -- `gen-aspects: includes element is a bare
module ({ imports = [ ... ]; }) with no aspect identity` -- failing even for
attrNames, which HEAD passes. So the parity pin is NOT a conservative proxy for
the live corpus, and a rung cleared against the pin is not evidence about HEAD.
This should change which artefact the ladder is climbed against.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the first thing the next agent needs:
WHICH ASPECT LACKS id_hash. The error names the attribute, not the producer.

RELATED-BUT-DISTINCT, do not conflate: the arm-(b) darwin path is an UNCROSSED
STUB -- darwinConfigurations.patch has keys ["__terminal","bindings","modules",
"name"] against arm (a)'s real darwin config. Its bindings.resolved-users =
["sini"] agrees with arm (a), but NO darwin crossing was exercised, so darwin is
unmeasured rather than passing. cortex-cuda and slab declare hosts and
materialize no configuration -- likewise unmeasured.

HOW MEMBERSHIP WAS OBTAINED DESPITE THIS BLOCKER (method note for reuse, and a
caveat on today's membership result): a SCRATCH-ONLY probe appended
`// { __probeBindings = bindings; }` to crossVia's return (lib/output/terminal.
nix:62) and read `resolved-users` -- the CORPUS's OWN quirk collection
(modules/den/aspects/core/users/resolved-user-emitter.nix). It is ROUTE-AGNOSTIC:
any user entity resolved under a host emits, whatever placed it, so it covers
den-hoag's structural host.users -> member route and not only the ACL. But it is a
GRAPH-LEVEL read, and it could NOT be cross-checked against arm (b)'s own
materialized users.users -- that is precisely the blocked path. Today's
empty-membership-diff rests on agreement with arm (a) across all 8 hosts plus a
shared perturbation response, NOT on a materialized arm-(b) read.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ CENSUS COMPLETE, 2026-07-28. RUNG 1 IS ROOT-CAUSED TO ONE ASPECT AND ONE
MINT SITE, AND ONE EDIT CARRIES ARM B TO FULL MATERIALIZED MEMBERSHIP ON ALL 7
HOSTS, BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ARM A. Frozen at den-hoag c42df53 (git archive; the
concurrent writer's edits are NOT in it), corpus nix-config main HEAD 9ebf3316.

Q1 — WHICH ASPECT. Exactly ONE distinct aspect fleet-wide: 124 firings, 1 distinct
key. NOT a class of aspects.
  name    "agenix-identity/shuo@blade"  (per-user-per-host)
  key     "__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0"   sharedFoldKey null
  channel homeManagerModules
  content keys: home-manager, homeManagerModules, name, nixos -- NO id_hash

★ THE MECHANISM, END TO END:
· CORPUS: modules/den/batteries/agenix.nix:91 `agenixUserAspect` is a BARE
  FUNCTION -- { user, host, secretsConfig, ... }: { name = ...; homeManagerModules
  = ...; ${host.class} = ...; } -- registered at :196 as
  `den.schema.user.includes = [ agenixUserAspect ];`.
· DEN-HOAG MINT: lib/compat/compile.nix:1758 synthName =
  "__kindInclude__${kind}__aspect__${toString i}"; the FUNCTION branch at :1764
  wraps it as { includes = normalizeListForKind kind "${synthName}:include" [ ref ]; }.
· ★ THE DEFECT: the content the function returns is a PLAIN ATTRSET. IT NEVER
  PASSES THROUGH gen-aspects' ASPECT TYPE, which is what mints id_hash
  (gen-aspects lib/types.nix:462, "Convenience content-address on plain
  submodules"). The consumer then reads it UNCONDITIONALLY at
  lib/attributes/collections.nix:205.
HOW ATTRIBUTED (four one-line variants of the same fallback, same corpus, same
command): (A) constant throw -> fires, proving the site is forced; (B) attrNames a
-> content,key,sharedFoldKey + chan; (C) a.key + attrNames a.content; (D)
a.content.name -> the name. Then grep to the corpus site.

★ DIRECTION FOR THE FIX -- AND THE PROBE IS NOT THE FIX. The measured edit
(`a.content.id_hash or <synthetic identity from a.key>`) FABRICATES AN IDENTITY at
the consumer. That is a repair at the read, on the wrong side of the defect. The
cause is a compat MINT that produces content gen-aspects never typed. Route the
function-branch content THROUGH gen-aspects' aspect type so id_hash is minted the
way every other aspect's is (feedback_route_through_gen_native: route gen-capability
duplications through native gen, never re-implement in compat; and
feedback_by_construction_over_repair: a fabricated identity is an invariant someone
must maintain at every future consumer). ★ VERIFY THE TYPE IS APPLICABLE AT THAT
MINT SITE BEFORE COMMITTING TO THIS -- if the function branch cannot reach the
aspect type for a structural reason, that reason is the real finding and the
direction changes.

RUNG-1 RESULT, MEASURED: with only that edit, arm B materializes
home-manager.users on ALL SEVEN HOSTS --
  axon-01 axon-02 axon-03 bitstream uplink -> dvicory pol sini theutz vic
  blade cortex                             -> shuo sini will
BYTE-IDENTICAL TO ARM A, and users.users evaluates on all 7.
★ THIS CLOSES THE COVERAGE GAP FROM THE MEMBERSHIP RUN: that verdict rested on a
graph-level `resolved-users` read that could not be cross-checked against a
materialized surface, because this rung was the blocked path. It is now confirmed
on the materialized surface.
ABLATION CONTROL: two different synthetic identities -- per-aspect, and
per-aspect-per-channel-per-emission (which defeats dedup collapse entirely) --
give IDENTICAL downstream behaviour. Nothing below depends on the identity value
chosen.

★★ Q3 — THE hjem RUNG WAS THE PROBE'S OWN ARTIFACT, NOT den-hoag's. Established by
POSITIVE REPRODUCTION, not by elimination. Same site, same corpus, three fallbacks:
  throw "CONST"                       -> PROBE_NO_ID_HASH_CONST
  throw (a.key + attrNames a.content) -> PROBE_KEY=...
  throw (builtins.toJSON coords)      -> REPRODUCES THE hjem ERROR EXACTLY
⇒ `builtins.toJSON coords` forcing the scope-coordinate record is what reached the
hjem stub (lib/compat/builtins.nix:230). The earlier report's "rung 2" was the
instrument's, and it is retracted.
RESIDUAL, STATED BY THE AGENT AND KEPT: this proves hjem is not reached VIA the
id_hash path. It does NOT prove den-hoag never reaches hjem on this corpus -- the
stub is genuinely reachable by forcing scope coords, on a corpus with ZERO hjem
references, which is its own oddity.

Q2 — ★ RUNG 2 IS A FAN, NOT A CHAIN. Pristine corpus, only the rung-1 edit, target
config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath. EACH HOST FAILS DIFFERENTLY:
· axon-01/02/03, bitstream, uplink (5 servers) -> "The option 'services' was
  accessed but has no value defined." Trace is ENTIRELY nixpkgs option-merge frames
  (modules.nix:1267 via emptyValue/getSubOptions), reached from
  system.build.toplevel -> assertions. NO den-hoag FRAME IN THE TRACE.
· blade -> `attribute 'image' missing`, stylix mk-target.nix:224
  `inherit (cfg.${argument}) override;`. Arm A's HM stylix carries 21 keys
  INCLUDING image; under arm B ANY read of HM stylix.* throws.
· cortex -> `attribute 'aspect' missing` -- a THIRD distinct rung, matching the
  missing host.aspect field already tracked at den-hoag-9xo.49.
ALL THREE ARM-A CONTROLLED: arm A yields real drvPaths (blade 73z2xmpx...,
axon-01 wg8ihlp6..., cortex yvg0fccl...).

RUNG 3 — OBSERVED, NOT ATTRIBUTABLE, AND NO CLAIM IS MADE. Passing blade's stylix
rung required removing stylix from the corpus, WHICH BREAKS ARM A TOO ("The option
'home-manager.users.sini.stylix' does not exist" -- other aspects still feed the
stylix-hm quirk, firefox.nix:222). Two edits tried, both broke arm A. NO ARM-A-
NEUTRAL WAY PAST RUNG 2 WAS FOUND ON ANY HOST.
★★ ⇒ TRUE LADDER DEPTH BEYOND RUNG 2 IS UNKNOWN. DO NOT READ "2 RUNGS TO
MEMBERSHIP" AS "2 RUNGS TO A BUILD".

★ RUNG 0 exists at the PARITY PIN ONLY and is ABSENT at HEAD: "gen-aspects:
includes element is a bare module ({ imports = [ ... ]; }) with no aspect
identity", blocking even nixosConfigurations attrNames.

COVERAGE NOT REACHED, kept verbatim: blade's stylix rung not isolated to
module-absent vs option-undeclared; the `services` rung not located to ANY den-hoag
expression (the trace carries no den-hoag frame); cortex's `aspect` rung named but
not diagnosed; only nix-config and only nixos hosts -- darwin `patch` remains an
uncrossed stub under den-hoag; den-hoag's own CI was NOT run against the rung-1
edit; and the rung-1 edit is a PROBE, not a remedy.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE FIX DIRECTION IS CORRECTED, 2026-07-28. BOTH EARLIER CANDIDATES WERE
WRONG, INCLUDING MINE. The right fix is SMALLER than either: apply an accessor
that is ALREADY THREADED INTO THIS EXACT FILE and simply not applied at one arm.

WHAT WAS WRONG:
· The probe's `a.content.id_hash or <synthetic>` fabricates an identity at the
  CONSUMER -- a repair on the wrong side.
· ★ MY OWN DIRECTION -- "route the function-branch content through gen-aspects'
  aspect type so id_hash is minted" -- IS ALSO WRONG, and wrong at the premise.

WHY: THE ASPECT TYPE IS NOT REACHABLE AT THE MINT SITE, AND IT IS NOT SUPPOSED TO
BE.
1. STRUCTURAL -- AT MINT TIME THERE IS NO CONTENT. compile.nix:1746-1748: a bare
   fn becomes `{ includes = normalizeList ... [ fn ] }`, and the wrapped fn is
   "invoked with the real node ctx at forwardExpand -> callGated -> grounded
   ATTRSET content". The :1764 branch wraps the FUNCTION; content exists only
   PER-NODE after ctx application. A content-address computed at mint time would
   have NOTHING TO ADDRESS. The value observed (agenix-identity/shuo@blade) is the
   POST-invocation grounded attrset.
2. ★ gen-aspects SAYS SO AND SHIPS THE ALTERNATIVE. lib/types.nix:459-461, on
   id_hash: "Convenience content-address on plain submodules... Wrapped-fn / guard
   aspects are bare records (no submodule, no option); consumers id them uniformly
   via `aspects.aspectId`." And :228-234 on aspectId: "THE canonical
   content-address for an aspect of ANY kind -- plain, wrapped-fn (__isWrappedFn),
   or guard (__guard)... a wrapped-fn / guard record -- NOT a submodule instance,
   carries no `id_hash` option -- gets the SAME id as a plain aspect via the SAME
   formula. Consumers ... call THIS, never re-derive the preimage."
   ⇒ CARRYING NO id_hash IS THE DOCUMENTED CORRECT STATE FOR THIS CLASS. The defect
   is a CONSUMER READING THE CONVENIENCE MIRROR INSTEAD OF THE CANONICAL ACCESSOR
   -- not a missing stamp at the mint.
3. ★★ AND den-hoag ALREADY THREADS THAT ACCESSOR INTO THIS FILE. compile.nix:28-30
   takes `aspectIdHash`, commented "routed onto gen-native's `aspects.aspectId`".
   It is ALREADY APPLIED at :426 and :436, and the comment at :422-424 states this
   very obligation: "ensure a content-stable `id_hash` (derive from `.key` when the
   node did not carry one -- a manually-emitted value)." THE SYNTHETIC-ASPECT ARM
   AT :1758-1764 SIMPLY DOES NOT DO IT.
   INPUT AVAILABILITY, MEASURED: the failing record carries
   key = "__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0", and `aspectIdHash`'s required
   input is present at BOTH the mint and the consumer.

⇒ THE FIX IS TO APPLY THE EXISTING ROUTED ACCESSOR AT THE ARM THAT OMITS IT, in
the same shape as :426/:436 -- NOT to introduce a new routing, NOT to fabricate an
identity, and NOT to reach for the aspect type.
This is feedback_route_through_gen_native satisfied by USING what is already
routed, and it is a smaller change than either rejected candidate.

★ THE ONE THING NOT VERIFIED, AND IT DECIDES BETWEEN THE TWO SANCTIONED
PLACEMENTS: whether `aspectId`/`identity.key` computed on the GROUNDED CONTENT
yields the SAME id as computed on the wrapped-fn record's `key` -- i.e. whether
stamping at the mint and computing at the consumer AGREE. No eval was run for it.
FLAGGED, NOT ASSUMED. If they disagree, the placement is forced and the
disagreement itself is a finding.

★ AND RE-READ THIS BEAD'S EARLIER "SURVIVES THE BELT-SEVERED OVERRIDE SET" CLAIM
IN LIGHT OF den-hoag-9xo.66: the belt was NEVER SEVERED by that recipe (passThrough
is a function argument with no CLI path), and the pin-alignment half is observably
inert on this corpus. The rung-1 and rung-2 diagnoses stand on their own evidence;
the override citation adds nothing and must not be read as ruling out a gen-pin
cause.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE ACCESSOR-AGREEMENT QUESTION IS ANSWERED: DISAGREE. THE PLACEMENT IS
FORCED TO THE CONTENT/CONSUMER SIDE, AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS A SECOND DEFECT.
Measured 2026-07-28 IN SITU -- both routes computed inside the real eval at
collections.nix:205, no record reconstruction. den-hoag c42df53, nix-config
9ebf3316, gen-aspects 1689e41.

★ POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, and it is what makes the verdict safe: of 45 trace rows
(28 distinct) on blade's home-manager.users, 25 DISTINCT ROWS CARRY A REAL STORED
id_hash, AND BOTH ROUTES REPRODUCE IT 25/25 EXACTLY --
    core/network/manager  stored = routeA = routeB = a6651b7129c1fb3f...
    core/systemd          stored = routeA = routeB = d79a72f32c435706...
    core/security         stored = routeA = routeB = 9907ab2dc8770d13...
So the instrument is sound and NEITHER ROUTE IS WRONG IN GENERAL. An agreement
result could not have been "two computations wrong the same way", and the
disagreement below is therefore specific to the stamp-less class.

THE THREE STAMP-LESS ROWS ARE THE THREE BLADE USERS:
    agenix-identity/shuo@blade   routeA = 6b7f13a647a4b4f5   routeB = 5b07e98feb9578ed
    agenix-identity/sini@blade   routeA = 6b7f13a647a4b4f5   routeB = 8750fe57552aa18e
    agenix-identity/will@blade   routeA = 6b7f13a647a4b4f5   routeB = d2192163dabdc601
★★ routeA IS IDENTICAL ACROSS ALL THREE. routeB is distinct for each.

WHY. routeA = `aspectId [ ] { name = a.key; meta.aspect-chain = [ ]; }`, exactly
den-hoag's own `aspectIdHashFor` (lib/identity-preimage.nix:20-28). But `a.key` is
the SYNTHETIC POSITIONAL KEY `__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0`
(compile.nix:1758 `__kindInclude__${kind}__aspect__${toString i}` plus the
`:include:<j>` suffix) -- AN INDEX INTO THE KIND'S INCLUDE LIST. It carries NO
per-node coordinate, so every user under every host shares it.
routeB = `aspectId [ ] a.content`, whose identity.key else-branch (gen-aspects
lib/identity.nix:105-112) is `pathKey (aspectPath content)` over the grounded
content's OWN name -- `agenix-identity/<user>@<host>` -- which IS per-node.

⇒ PLACEMENT FORCED. `identity` at collections.nix:205 is the A12 PRODUCER KEY,
consumed by scopeAdapter.sortByProducer and the per-channel grouping. At mint time
THE CONTENT DOES NOT EXIST (compile.nix:1746-1748), so a mint-side stamp can only
use the positional key -- which would install A THREE-WAY IDENTITY COLLISION AMONG
THREE GENUINELY DISTINCT PRODUCERS on channel homeManagerModules. That is exactly
what compile.nix:422-424's own comment exists to prevent ("ensure a content-stable
id_hash").
⇒ STAMPING AT THE MINT IN THE SHAPE OF :426/:436 IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE, IT IS
WRONG. The identity must be computed where the grounded content exists.

★★ AND THE COLLAPSE GENERALISES BEYOND THIS FIX: `aspectIdHash <key>` IS NOT A
VALID IDENTITY FOR ANY kindInclude SYNTHETIC ASPECT WHOSE fn PRODUCES PER-NODE
CONTENT. Whether the two EXISTING uses at compile.nix:426 and :436 are exposed to
the same hazard was NOT CHECKED -- tracked separately as its own bead, because it
is shipped code and a live collision there would be silent.

NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S OWN HISTORY: three fix directions have now been proposed and
two rejected -- the probe's fabricated identity at the consumer (repair on the
wrong side), and the orchestrator's "route the mint through gen-aspects' aspect
type" (no content exists at mint time). The surviving direction is to compute the
canonical `aspectId` over the GROUNDED CONTENT at the consumer. Each rejection is
recorded so none is re-proposed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE FIX SITE IS CORRECTED, 2026-07-28. THE COLLISION DOES NOT COME FROM
`aspectIdHash` AT ALL.

MEASURED: `__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0` NEVER PASSES THROUGH
`stampIdentity` -- 0 STAMP rows fleet-wide, all 7 hosts. So neither
compile.nix:426 nor :436 produces it (both audited and closed at den-hoag-9xo.69).

THE ACTUAL ROUTE: a bare FN takes `normalize`'s FUNCTION arm, compile.nix:501-508:
    aspects.wrapGatedFn { ... name = name; onResult = grndDispatch name; } ref
where `name` is the POSITIONAL `fallbackName`. THE COLLISION IS IN THE BARE-FN WRAP
NAMING.

⇒ CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN EARLIER ENTRY: "aspectIdHash <key> is not a valid
identity for a kindInclude synthetic aspect" was RIGHT ABOUT THE KEY AND WRONG
ABOUT THE ROUTE. The key IS invalid as an identity -- that stands, and the 31-way
collision below proves it -- but it never reaches an aspectIdHash site, so a fix
aimed at those sites would have changed nothing and looked correct while doing so.

THE COLLISION, measured fleet-wide at collections.nix:205 where `identity` IS the
A12 producer key: 54 distinct keys, 84 distinct (key, content-name, stored-id)
triples. EXACTLY ONE key covers more than one grounded content --
    __kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0  ->  31 DISTINCT CONTENTS
the full agenix-identity/<user>@<host> cross-product, carrying no stored id_hash.
(31 independently matches env-users' firing count from the membership run.) The
other 53 keys are 1:1 with their content, all carry a stored id_hash, and all are
definition paths. ★ THE PREDICATE FOUND THE 31-WAY COLLISION IN THE SAME RUN IT
REPORTED 53 CLEAN KEYS.

⇒ THE FIX MUST ADDRESS THE NAME GIVEN AT THE WRAP, or compute the identity from the
GROUNDED CONTENT at the consumer -- the two remaining candidates. It must NOT be
aimed at :426/:436. Four directions have now been proposed on this bead and three
rejected with reasons: the probe's fabricated identity at the consumer (repair on
the wrong side); "route the mint through gen-aspects' aspect type" (no content
exists at mint time); and "stamp at the mint in the shape of :426/:436" (would
install the collision, and in any case those sites are not on this path).

★ AND A CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE WRAP-NAMING ROUTE: `fallbackName` is a
SYNTACTIC include-list position. compile.nix:436 uses the same construction and is
SAFE ONLY INCIDENTALLY -- because the refs reaching it carry no content (tracked
separately). So the wrap naming is not uniquely broken; POSITIONAL NAMING IS
UNSOUND WHEREVER PER-NODE CONTENT FOLLOWS IT, and a fix that repairs one call site
leaves the construction in place. Prefer the construction that cannot produce a
node-invariant name for per-node content over a repair at the one site where it
currently bites.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ THE FINDING SURVIVES ITS BAD CITATION — and I nearly let the one discredit the other.
This bead cites corpus HEAD 9ebf3316, which DOES NOT EXIST in nix-config (count 0; positive control 4acf0a1d = 1). I recorded that as casting doubt on the measurement.
★★ MEASURED 2026-07-29: THE id_hash FINDING REPRODUCES AT 4acf0a1d. On a guard-off differential over the HEAD tree — one edit, the pipeOp arm disabled — axon-01 and blade both die at 'attribute id_hash missing' at lib/attributes/collections.nix:205, EXACTLY as this bead records. And collections.nix is md5 d40873fb34eaae71b0710755c3ac98f0 at ALL of 222af84, c42df53, e6c8edc and HEAD — the defect site is BYTE-UNTOUCHED; only reachability moved.
⇒ **A WRONG REV CITATION IS NOT A WRONG FINDING.** The citation is unverifiable and the finding is reproducible, and those are independent facts. I should not have let the first cast doubt on the second — that is the same error as treating a bead title as a claim about the code, arriving from the other direction.
★ AND THE LADDER HAS AT LEAST ONE MORE RUNG THAN THIS BEAD RECORDS: cortex does NOT stop at id_hash even with the guard off — it gets further and dies at 'attribute aspect missing' in the corpus's own microvm-guests.nix. Filed as den-hoag-8ge. So 'all 7 hosts' is wrong in shape as well as unverified in count: the hosts sit at DIFFERENT frontiers, and only three of seven were measured.
CURRENT STATUS: this defect is UNREACHABLE at HEAD, masked by den-hoag-1kd's compose-commitment guard. Not fixed — masked. The distinction is recorded there with its causal proof.

title: [kernel] wrong users on wrong hosts: inert excludes + policies applied outside includes means the kind schema does not govern policy application — one defect, two directions
description:
★★ OWNER SYNTHESIS, 2026-07-28 — THREE MEASURED DEFECTS ARE ONE CHAIN, AND THE SYMPTOM IS WRONG USERS ON
WRONG HOSTS. Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS TO VERIFY, not as established: the owner offered it from a partial
read, and the chain must be measured end to end before anything is built on it.

OWNER, verbatim: "sini/nix-config's ACL user system is complex and DISABLES/DOESN'T USE THE DEFAULT
HOST-USERS MAPPING… it seems that USERS ARE APPEARING ON HOSTS THAT THEY SHOULD NOT (dvicory should only be
on a few select server hosts, NEVER DESKTOPS)."

THE CHAIN, each link already measured independently:
 1. nix-config DISABLES the default mapping — `modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:91`
    `den.schema.host.excludes = [ den.policies.host-to-users ];`
    with the author's comment: "Exclude den's built-in host-to-users (fleet user policies replace it)."
 2. ★ `den.schema.<kind>.excludes` IS INERT under den-hoag — den-hoag-9xo.28, measured with a four-arm eval
    and a positive control; den v1 CONSUMES it at nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix:22,:72.
 3. ★ den-hoag APPLIES POLICIES THAT ARE IN NO `includes` LIST — den-hoag-9xo.53, measured on fleet-demo:
    `env-users` fires 6× and `host-users` 1× under den-hoag while v1 fires them ZERO times.
⇒ PREDICTED CONSEQUENCE: `host-to-users` RUNS ANYWAY, delivering den's built-in host→user mapping ALONGSIDE
the ACL system that was meant to replace it — so users land on hosts the ACL never granted. THAT IS EXACTLY
THE REPORTED SYMPTOM.

title: [compat] den-hoag produces ZERO nixosConfigurations on all 13 den templates — six distinct causes, breaking at the entry point; the flakeModule path has never worked
description:
★★ den-hoag PRODUCES ZERO `nixosConfigurations` ON ALL 13 den TEMPLATES. Not one node set, let alone a
drvPath. Measured 2026-07-28 at den-hoag 222af84 against den v1 cdc95ce, both arms `--override-input den`
(templates' own pins are unmaintained and are NOT an oracle).
POSITIVE CONTROL, same predicate same runs: arm-(b) non-empty logs = 0 FILES; arm-(a) non-empty = 28 FILES.
The predicate is live; the zero is real.

★ IT BREAKS AT THE FLOOR, NOT AT THE CEILING. `minimal` — ONE host, no flake-parts — dies at the ENTRY POINT:
den v1's flakeModule declares `options.flake` (den-v1/nix/flakeOutputs.nix:122); den-hoag's does not. The
template's own comment — "we can import this flakeModule even if we dont have flake-parts as input!" — IS NOW
FALSE. Same root kills `noflake`.

SIX DISTINCT CAUSES, NO SHARED ROOT (Nix aborts at the first throw, so counts behind each are UNKNOWN):
 1. `flakeModule` does not declare `options.flake` — requires flake-parts.
 2. `inputs.den.lib` is a plain set; v1's is `__functor`-CALLABLE (den-v1/nix/default.nix:32).
 3. `flakeModules` = [default dendritic strict]; v1 = [default denTest dendritic strict] — `denTest` MISSING.
 4. ★ `den.policies` GAPS: v1 declares THIRTEEN, den-hoag provides NINE (lib/compat/builtins.nix:417-427),
    three of those `outputStub`. ABSENT: `packages-to-flake-parts`, `packages-to-flake`, `flake-to-systems`.
 5. `den.systems` REJECTED by C1 (lib/compat/errors.nix:188) though v1 DECLARES it
    (den-v1/modules/outputs/systems.nix:20).
 6. 19 `gen-*` flake inputs make den-hoag unusable from the npins/non-flake path v1 ships as a template.

THE LADDER, shallow → deep by how far each reaches into den-hoag: entry-point/interface (minimal, noflake,
scoped-import-tree) → policy-surface (flake-parts-modules, microvm, diagram-demo) → compat content (example)
→ ★ KERNEL DISPATCH (default, fleet-demo). `default` is the SIMPLEST template that reaches real graph work,
and it lands on `fleet-context-enrich` B1/B2 at `reach` on host:igloo.

★ WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* CONTRADICT, and the distinction matters: `parity/ship-gate.nix` still yields
`allEqual: true` with a BYTE-IDENTICAL nixos-system derivation. So den-hoag WORKS THROUGH THE `mkDen`/compat
SHIM PATH the parity suite drives, and FAILS THROUGH THE flakeModule/TEMPLATE PATH. Those are two different
entry surfaces and only one has ever been exercised. THE SUITE'S GREEN AND THE TEMPLATES' ZERO ARE BOTH TRUE.

EDGE-LINKING ORACLE ESTABLISHED ON ARM (a) — discriminating, because a missing edge yields EMPTY and a
mis-scoped edge LEAKS: containment nodes [lb-prod web-prod-1 web-prod-2 web-staging] reachable only via
flake→fleet→environment→host + `instantiate`; cross-host env-scoped `pipe.collect` giving lb-prod exactly its
two prod backends and NOT staging's 10.0.2.10; sibling collect where each prod host sees all 3 prod peers and
web-staging sees only itself; policy-driven user delivery placing `alice` on all four and `bob` ONLY on
web-staging. ★ den-hoag REACHES NONE OF THESE — it aborts before any node set exists. So the edge-linking
question the owner posed is currently UNANSWERABLE ON TEMPLATES, and that is itself the finding.

CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF: `fleet-demo` and `terranix-demo` do NOT build a system even on arm (a) — toplevel
throws on `fileSystems`/`boot.loader.grub.devices`; their measurable ceiling is the node set plus resolved

all (npins + default.nix). ★ AND `a-lock` vs `a-HEAD` drvPaths are IDENTICAL for all six lock-passing
templates — the templates are NOT stale against den v1 HEAD, so every arm-(b) delta is den-hoag's alone.

title: [kernel] den-hoag applies policies present in NO includes list — v1 applies zero, den-hoag fires env-users x6 and host-users x1, and one of them aborted the fleet
description:
★★ den-hoag APPLIES POLICIES THAT ARE IN NO `includes` LIST. den v1 NEVER APPLIES THEM. Measured on the
`fleet-demo` template, 2026-07-28, both arms `--override-input den`, arm (a) as the control.

TRACED INERT BODIES, probe counts:
  `PROBEFIRED:env-users`   — arm A (v1) **0**, arm B (den-hoag) **6**
  `PROBEFIRED:host-users`  — arm A **0**, arm B **1**
  CONTROL `PROBEFIRED:collect-backends`, a policy that genuinely IS included — arm A **4**, arm B 1
  (B aborted early so the counts are not comparable; PRESENCE is, and it establishes the probe fires in both).
⇒ THE ZEROES ON ARM A ARE NOT A DEAD PROBE. v1 does not run these policies; den-hoag runs them.

★ AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC: at peel-3 of the fleet-demo ladder, THE UN-INCLUDED `env-users` BODY THREW AND
ABORTED THE WHOLE EVALUATION. A policy that should never have been applied took the fleet down.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: that v1 never applies them and den-hoag does. WHAT IS NOT: whether their results
contribute edges to the resolved graph — the investigator was explicit that this is unestablished, and it
should not be assumed either way.

WHY THIS IS SEVERE INDEPENDENT OF THE ABORT: `includes` is the surface by which a schema says WHICH policies
run at a kind. If den-hoag applies policies outside it, then the include list is not the authority it is
documented to be — and every reasoning step that assumes "only included policies fire" is unsound, including
the exclusion semantics ruled at den-hoag-9xo.28 (where `excludes` is the dual and is inert). ★ AN INERT
`excludes` AND AN OVER-BROAD `includes` ARE THE SAME DEFECT SEEN FROM TWO SIDES: the kind schema is not
governing which policies apply.

FIRST THING TO ESTABLISH: WHERE do `env-users` and `host-users` enter den-hoag's dispatch, given they are in
no include list? Candidates worth testing rather than assuming — the compat builtins policy set
(lib/compat/builtins.nix:417-427) being applied unconditionally rather than on demand; a default-fold or
walking policy applied at kind level; or the kind-include compilation adding to a set it should be selecting
from. Whichever it is, the fix must make the include list AUTHORITATIVE, not merely add a filter downstream.

title: [kernel] placeRemapped nested-evals a routed class slice and places RESOLVED config — v1 defers a module; mkIf false becomes a throwing key, osConfig and hm config vanish; 6 of 7 corpus hosts
description:
★★ ROOT CAUSE, MEASURED — den-hoag RESOLVES A ROUTED CLASS SLICE WHERE den v1 DEFERS IT. Six of seven corpus
hosts fail from this ONE mechanism. It is unfiled, it is not any existing bead, and it is the mechanism
UNDER den-hoag-9xo.49 items 2 and 3.

THE DIVERGENCE, measured on `options.home-manager.users.definitionsWithLocations`, host `uplink`:
  v1        — 5 definitions, one per user, each a MODULE FUNCTION (`<fn args=>`)
  den-hoag  — 45 definitions, NINE per user, each a PRE-RESOLVED ATTRSET
             ({home,xdg} {age,services} {home,programs} {home} {home} {home} {nixpkgs} {age} {home})
⇒ v1 HANDS HOME-MANAGER A DEFERRED MODULE. den-hoag HANDS IT ALREADY-EVALUATED CONFIG.

THE SITE: `lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:547-574` `placeRemapped` →
  `nested = bind.crossEval { module = sliceMod; specialArgs = special; }` then
  `{ config = setAttrByPath route.at (removeAttrs nested.config [ "_module" "warnings" "assertions" ]); }`
dispatched at `:601` when `route.at != [ ]`, with NO eval-time guard. Route is `hmUserDetect`
(`lib/compat/builtins.nix:121-146`), `intoPath = [ "home-manager" "users" <user> ]`, `fromClass = "homeManager"`,
NO `adaptArgs`. `crossEval` (`gen-bind/lib/arg-env.nix:37-51`) runs `lib.evalModules` with `prefix = [ ]`, a
freeform `lazyAttrsOf raw`, and ★ NEITHER HOME-MANAGER'S OPTION UNIVERSE NOR ITS MODULE ARGS.

★ THREE MEASURED CONSEQUENCES, ALL FROM THAT ONE CHOICE:
 1. `mkIf false` BECOMES A PRESENT-BUT-THROWING KEY INSTEAD OF AN ABSENT ONE. Traced through nixpkgs:
    `modules.nix:302` `recursiveUpdate freeformConfig declaredConfig` · `pushDownProperties` pushes the mkIf
    into each top-level key · `dischargeProperties (mkIf false …)` → `[ ]` → `isDefined = false` →
    `types.nix:1028` falls through `optionalValue`/`emptyValue` to `mergedValue` → `modules.nix:1265` THROW.
    MINIMAL REPRO with three controls in one run: keys SURVIVE a `mkIf false`; reading one throws verbatim
    "The option `age' was accessed but has no value defined"; ★ a `lazyAttrsOf anything` throws too, SO THE
    ELEMENT TYPE IS NOT THE LEVER; and `mkIf true` does not throw (sanity).
 2. `osConfig` ABSENT — `agenixUserAspect.homeManager` is `{ osConfig, ... }:`, and osConfig is supplied BY
    home-manager, outside the nested eval. Measured: `attribute 'osConfig' missing`.
 3. `config.<hm-option>` ABSENT — `apps/shell/zsh.nix:28` reads `config.xdg.configHome`; in the nested eval
    `config` is the freeform eval's own. Measured: `attribute 'configHome' missing`.

★★ FALSIFIER RUN AND CONFIRMED, ONE TOKEN: in a scratch corpus copy, `member.nix`'s
`lib.mkIf (dirs != [ ])` → `lib.optionalAttrs (dirs != [ ])`, nothing else changed. THE `age` ERROR IS GONE —
`home-manager.users` resolves to all five users. NOT by defining `age`; BY REMOVING THE mkIf.

★ THE 5/2 SPLIT IS THE mkIf CONDITION AND NOTHING ELSE. v1 `services.syncthing.enable` is TRUE for blade and
cortex, FALSE for all users on axon-01/02/03, bitstream, uplink — exactly the five that throw on `age`.
★ AND blade IS THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, NOT A SEPARATE BLOCKER: its abort passes through
`output-modules.nix:569` — the same `removeAttrs nested.config` frame — where `mkRenamedOptionModule`'s
`getAttrFromPath [ "programs" "neovim-flake" ]` aborts because the nested eval has no HM options.
⇒ SIX OF SEVEN HOSTS, ONE CAUSE. Only cortex is separate (`attribute 'aspect' missing`, 9xo.49 item 1).

BLAST RADIUS: EVERY homeManager ASPECT THAT IS NOT A LITERAL ATTRSET — anything using `mkIf`, reading a
home-manager `config` option, reading `osConfig`, or carrying a rename module. Three distinct surfaces
demonstrated; TOTAL UNBOUNDED.

★ THE ORIGIN DECISION IS IN den-hoag'S OWN COMMENT, `lib/compat/legacy/batteries/home-manager.nix:15-19`:
  "`parentPath`/`parentArg = \"osConfig\"` are v1 pipe-layer fields whose den-hoag rendering is the
   config-thunk resolve-at-producing-scope machinery (PR #623 / decision #27 — deferred thunks get
   config+osConfig at the producing class+scope) — NOT re-ported as class fields."
MEASUREMENT SAYS THAT RENDERING DOES NOT HAPPEN ON THE `hmUserDetect` ROUTE.
★ AND `output-modules.nix:541-546` ALREADY LEDGERS THE SIBLING COLLAPSE — "mkDefault/mkForce/mkMerge …
COLLAPSED to its resolved value at the nested boundary". `mkIf false` IS THE UNLEDGERED CASE OF THAT SAME
COLLAPSE, and it collapses TO A THROW rather than to absence. The ledger knew about the class and missed the
member that fails loudly.

NOT ADOPTED — WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT: v1's exact placement path is NOT fully pinned. v1's
`nix/lib/aspects/fx/edges/route.nix:103` `nestPlain` ALSO nested-evals, yet v1 measures ONE def and it is a
FUNCTION, which `nestPlain` cannot produce at `.sini` — so v1 reaches this some other way (the
`den.batteries.forward` complex/synthesize arm, or the `parentPath`/`parentArg` registration at
`modules/aspects/batteries/home-manager.nix:34-36`). ★ IF v1 TURNS OUT TO NESTED-EVAL IDENTICALLY, THE
DIAGNOSIS MOVES TO WHY v1's NESTED EVAL CARRIES THE HM OPTION AND ARG UNIVERSE AND den-hoag's DOES NOT — the
defect stays, its description changes. Also refuted if a routed homeManager slice with `mkIf false` were shown
to throw under v1.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ P4 SPEC WRITTEN — specs/2026-07-28-route-contribution-design.md, 514 lines, md5
f0e47045d902a09a9bf3fcc99fb46164. Core 209 lines contiguous, md5 0d8f5889204a1beccdf4b27678d3d388, fenced by
its own markers; CONTROL1 perturb inside → 1b310f01…, MOVED; CONTROL2 append outside → HELD. Hash table lives
OUTSIDE the core. No evaluation was run — every claim is source-read at c42df53 except this bead's own
measurements, which remain this bead's.

★★ THE ONE-LINE THEORY, AND IT COLLAPSES TWO SEPARATELY-LEDGERED DEFECTS INTO ONE:
**`evalModules` MAPS DEFINITION SPACE TO VALUE SPACE. Priorities (`mkDefault`/`mkForce`/`mkMerge`) and ABSENCE
(`mkIf false`) ARE OBJECTS OF DEFINITION SPACE WITH NO IMAGE IN VALUE SPACE.** An early map must therefore
either FORGET the priorities or INVENT a value for absence — and the only inhabitant of "no value" is ⊥.
⇒ THE mkIf-FALSE THROW AND THE PRIORITY COLLAPSE ARE THE SAME DEFECT. The ledger recorded them as two
(output-modules.nix:535-546); they are one, and the design does not fix them separately.

★ THE FIX IS ONE STEP: **BIND FIRST, PLACE SECOND.** And the historical reason the site left the law is
recorded in the tree at output-modules.nix:529-531 — the DIAGNOSIS THERE IS CORRECT (placeSlice placed
`{ <at> = fn; }`, `wrapCore` passes plain attrsets through, so the inner fn was never bound and peer-dev/pkgs
were lost) — ★ BUT THE CONCLUSION DRAWN FROM IT ("own an evalModules") WAS THE WRONG STEP. Options and args
come from the terminal provably: `bind.wrapAll` binds a formal IFF the module declares it AND the env carries
it, and returns the module STILL ADVERTISING its remaining formals; den's binding set contains no
config/options/osConfig/pkgs, so those stay FREE and the target's own `evalModules` supplies them.

WHAT LANDS: a content-mode contribution carrying the raw module face — `nest.executeNest`'s content arm
(nest.nix:139-152), product `ModulesInfo` (products.nix:53), row = `routeRow route`. The payload gather is
UNCHANGED. ★ PRIORITY ANNOTATIONS SURVIVE TO THE MOUNT and are resolved by the target's merge, so the parked
`mkDefault`/`mkForce` pair at :544-546 becomes correct BY CONSTRUCTION — that ledger row is DISCHARGED, not
inherited. Per-module-vs-combined (:535-539) DISSOLVES: no eval ⇒ no per-module boundary ⇒ N definitions
resolved ONCE by the target merge, which is v1's combined semantics.
`placeRemapped` IS DELETED, its arg derivation surviving as `adaptedEnv` carrying :554-557 verbatim. The
`removeAttrs nested.config [ "_module" "warnings" "assertions" ]` strip list goes — ★ it is a REPAIR, and
under the law there is nothing to strip. The local `placeSlice` (:439), token-identical to nest.nix:29, is
deleted. ★ AND THE ANSWER ON THE DISPATCH IS STRONGER THAN I ASKED: :601 is one arm of a THREE-way and ALL
THREE GO — `at` STOPS BEING A DISCRIMINATOR entirely; the new discriminator is whether the arg env is known
at projection, derived at crossing, or gated on the target's options. ONE nested eval survives, on the
eval-time-guard arm, and it is the only one whose SEMANTICS require it (imports←guard(options)←options←imports
is a real cycle); zero corpus routes carry a guard.

★ THE AUTHOR CAUGHT A LIVE BREAK IN ITS OWN FIRST SHAPE: the adaptArgs arm returns a crossing module
INDEPENDENT of payload, so `placed == [ ]` would never be true and `ensureSeed` (:611-617, v1's
ensureTargetPath) WOULD HAVE BEEN SILENTLY DELETED. Guarded with an explicit empty arm plus fixture W7.

COMPLEXITY, defect-grade: current is ONE `lib.evalModules` PER (reached node × slice × route) — measured 45
on `uplink` for a single route, each a full module-system fixpoint over a freeform absorber — and
★ `removeAttrs nested.config` FORCES THE NESTED CONFIG SPINE AT PROJECTION, WHICH IS THE FORCE THAT TURNS
`mkIf false` INTO AN OBSERVED ⊥. After: ZERO additional evalModules on non-guarded arms; per slice one
`functionArgs`, one intersectAttrs-scale attrset and one `setAttrByPath`, ALL LAZY. Removes a
Θ(N_routedSlices) factor of module-system evaluations and converts an eager projection-time force into a lazy
one.

★★ AND IT CLOSED THIS BEAD'S OWN OPEN QUESTION FROM A SOURCE I DID NOT NAME. The bead recorded that v1's exact
placement path was NOT fully pinned. den-hoag's OWN reconstruction settles it: `lib/compat/legacy/forwards.nix:163-169`
rebuilds v1's forward composition value-identically as
`if adaptArgs == null then { imports = mods; } else args: { imports = mods; _module.args = adaptArgs args; }`
— ★ **v1 HANDS THE TARGET A MODULE AND NEVER NESTED-EVALS ON THIS PATH.** In the direction the bead predicted,
established from the repo rather than from the pin (11866c16 is not resolvable locally).

LIMITS LEDGERED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the guard arm still collapses priorities (intrinsic to a config-gate,
corpus-inert); `at == [ ]` now pre-binds source bindings, ★ FLAGGED AS A MEASURED QUESTION NOT A CLAIM (theory
says source is right per decision #27 and the Q2 ruling; same-scope ⇒ byte-inert; the corpus's only such route
is home-platform same-node); definition granularity stays 9/user against v1's 1 — ★ AND THE ONE-LINER THAT
WOULD MATCH THE COUNT IS NAMED AND RULED AGAINST, because identity of count is not free and gen-native
expression is priority 1; collision validators drop on the routed path, which removes a check and never a
value.
WITNESS: seven legs, ★ INCLUDING W1c AS A NAMED POSITIVE CONTROL — `mkIf true` must be green under BOTH
designs, without which a green W1 cannot separate "definition correctly dropped" from "harness sees no
definitions at all". W4 and W5 are the two ledgered divergences this bead does not carry. W6 asserts the
placed value `isFunction` — v1's measured module-FUNCTION shape asserted on the placement itself.
CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF: `hmUserDetect` is compat/builtins.nix:121-**144**; the nest.nix law is TWO ranges,
:8-9 and :17-22, not :17-23; and :601 has a peer at :589 I did not name.

title: [kernel] the unset 'age' option on 5 of 7 corpus hosts is a SYMPTOM — the agenix-rekey battery's policies are not resolving under den-hoag
description:
★ OWNER DIAGNOSIS, 2026-07-28: "The age option error is a symptom of our agenix-rekey battery and policies
not being resolved properly and needs a deeper investigation to root cause."
⇒ THIS IS NOT A CORPUS DEFECT AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT PROBLEM. I had it filed as one of three assorted
blockers behind the includes guard; it is a den-hoag RESOLUTION failure surfacing downstream as a missing
option value.

THE SYMPTOM, measured 2026-07-28 with the includes guard neutralised in a scratch gen-aspects copy only:
  axon-01, axon-02, axon-03, bitstream, uplink — 5 of 7 hosts —
  "The option 'age' was accessed but has no value defined. Try setting the option."
  at `config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`.
★ v1 CONTROL AT THE IDENTICAL DEPTH, arm (a), no override: axon-01 and uplink each RETURN A drvPath, exit 0.
So v1 resolves whatever den-hoag does not.

WHY THE SYMPTOM IS MISLEADING AND MUST NOT BE FIXED WHERE IT APPEARS: "option accessed but has no value" is
what the NixOS module system says when a definition never arrived. THE DEFECT IS UPSTREAM OF THE READ — the
agenix-rekey battery's policies are not resolving, so the definitions that would set `age` are never produced.
Setting a default, stubbing the option, or adding a definition at the read site would make the eval green
WHILE LEAVING THE POLICIES UNRESOLVED — a shortcut of exactly the kind the owner ruled out, and one that would
silently disarm secret rekeying rather than fix it.

WHAT ROOT-CAUSE MEANS HERE: establish WHICH policies in the agenix-rekey battery fail to resolve under
den-hoag and WHY — not which option is unset. The `age` read is the first place the absence becomes visible,
not the place it originates. Expect the cause to be shared across all five hosts, since the same battery
serves them; a per-host cause would itself be a finding.
RELATED CONTEXT: den-hoag-9xo.49 (this blocker's siblings), and the standing rule that nix-config is the
reference implementation for agenix-rekey generators — manual `age -r` is only for externally-issued values.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS REFUTED. THE agenix-rekey BATTERY RESOLVES CORRECTLY UNDER den-hoag. Measured, not inferred. Superseded by den-hoag-9xo.51.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, arm (b), den-hoag 222af84:
  `nixosConfigurations.axon-01.config.age.rekey.hostPubkey` → the real host key, EXIT 0.
  `…config.age.secrets` → 14 SECRETS, including user-identity-{sini,vic,pol,theutz,dvicory}, nix_store_signing_key, kubernetes-cluster-token, tailscale-auth-key — each with `rekeyFile` AND `generator.script`.
  All three schema includes FIRE: `den.schema.{host,user,cluster}.includes`. `secretsConfig` binds from modules/den/secrets-config.nix via policies/fleet.nix:27.
⇒ REKEYING IS ARMED, NOT DISARMED. Nothing in the battery fails to resolve.

★ THE THROW IS NOT THE SYSTEM `age` — IT IS THE HOME-MANAGER `age`, inside `config.home-manager.users.<u>`, and `home-manager.sharedModules` is IDENTICAL in both arms (same 8 elements including age-home.nix and agenix-rekey.nix), so the HM `age` OPTION IS DECLARED IN BOTH. Nothing is missing.
★ AND THE FALSIFIER SETTLES IT BEYOND ARGUMENT: changing ONE TOKEN in `modules/den/aspects/core/network/syncthing/member.nix` — `lib.mkIf` → `lib.optionalAttrs` — MAKES THE `age` ERROR DISAPPEAR. The fix touched a SYNCTHING aspect, not agenix. A defect whose falsifier lives in an unrelated aspect is not a defect in the battery.

★ THE REAL CAUSE IS A MATERIALIZATION DEFECT, WHICH IS WHY THE OWNER'S INSTINCT WAS RIGHT EVEN THOUGH THE ATTRIBUTION WAS NOT: den-hoag RESOLVES a routed class slice through a private `evalModules` and places the RESULT, where v1 defers a MODULE. `mkIf false` then collapses to a PRESENT-BUT-THROWING key instead of an absent one, and `age` is simply where that first becomes visible on the five hosts whose syncthing guard is false. Full mechanism, falsifier and blast radius at den-hoag-9xo.51.
THE OWNER'S FRAMING ON THE SAME DAY — 'the microvm is a MATERIALIZATION problem, we need to first verify we're LINKING THE EDGES TOGETHER PROPERLY' — names exactly this class. The route/placement layer is where both live.

MY OWN ERRORS IN THIS BEAD, corrected: (1) 'the battery's policies are not resolving' — false, they all resolve; (2) 'expect the cause shared across all five hosts' — UNDERSTATED, it is shared across SIX (blade too, same output-modules.nix:569 frame); (3) '5 of 7 hosts fail' — SEVEN of seven fail under den-hoag; the `age` error is 5 of 7, blade and cortex simply throw something else first, and their HM user configs are broken too.
METHOD NOTES WORTH KEEPING: `~/Documents/repos/sini/nix-config` local HEAD is 9584dd2, THREE COMMITS AHEAD of the pinned b0b2076 with a dirty file — so my brief's 'locally ~/…/nix-config' WOULD NOT HAVE MEASURED THE PIN; the investigator archived the pin to scratch instead. And `--override-input den path:…` ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT to get past the includes guard: the gen-aspects override must be NESTED, `--override-input den/gen-aspects path:<probe>`.

title: [corpus] three further blockers behind the includes guard — missing host.aspect field, unset 'age' option, missing programs.neovim-flake; count is >=4 and unbounded
description:
★ THE COUNT WAS NEVER ONE. WITH THE INCLUDES GUARD NEUTRALISED IN A SCRATCH gen-aspects COPY ONLY, THREE
FURTHER DISTINCT BLOCKERS APPEAR — AND EACH STILL ABORTS AT ITS OWN FIRST THROW, SO THE TOTAL IS ≥ 4 WITH NO
UPPER BOUND ESTABLISHED.

`#nixosConfigurations` attrNames succeeds past the guard (7 hosts, exit 0). Pushing to
`config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` on all seven:
 1. cortex — `attribute 'aspect' missing` at modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:43:77,
    from `den.lib.aspects.resolve "microvm" vm.aspect`. ★ v1 DECLARES IT: nix/lib/entities/host.nix:68
    `aspect = lib.mkOption { description = "Aspect that configures this host."; default = lookupAspect den config; }`
    (and :163 for users). DEN-HOAG'S HOST ENTITY LACKS IT.
 2. axon-01, axon-02, axon-03, bitstream, uplink — "The option 'age' was accessed but has no value defined."
 3. blade — "cannot find attribute 'programs.neovim-flake'".

★ v1 CONTROL AT THE IDENTICAL DEPTH, arm (a), no override: axon-01, blade, cortex and uplink EACH RETURN A
drvPath, exit 0 — e.g. /nix/store/74rs2nz5vsmm8qa2mqzzkb6iyp3cfllh-nixos-system-cortex-26.11.20260625.5e7c3e8.drv
⇒ ALL THREE ARE den-hoag GAPS, not corpus defects and not environment.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE COUNT: I recorded "ONE named throw" and the owner reasonably read it as one
remaining problem. Nix aborts at the first throw, so every blocker behind the first is INVISIBLE. The honest
statement is ≥ 4 AND UNBOUNDED, and it should stay that way in the record until each is cleared and the eval
is re-run. Each of the three above needs its own bead once triaged; the missing `aspect` entity field is the
best-specified and has v1's own declaration as its spec.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORRECTION — ITEM 3 (blade, 'cannot find attribute programs.neovim-flake') IS NOT A SEPARATE BLOCKER. It is the SAME root cause as item 2, now filed as den-hoag-9xo.51.
MEASURED: blade's abort trace passes through `lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:569` — the `builtins.removeAttrs nested.config` frame inside `placeRemapped`'s nested `crossEval`. `mkRenamedOptionModule`'s `getAttrFromPath [ "programs" "neovim-flake" ]` aborts because THE NESTED EVAL HAS NO HOME-MANAGER OPTIONS. Same mechanism as the `age` throw, different surface: one is a missing option READ, the other a missing option DECLARATION.
⇒ THE SEVEN-HOST PICTURE IS 6 + 1, NOT 5 + 1 + 1: six hosts fail from the placeRemapped materialization defect, and only cortex (`attribute 'aspect' missing`, item 1) is independent. Item 1 stands — den-hoag's host entity lacks the `aspect` field v1 declares at nix/lib/entities/host.nix:68.
★ AND ONE ARM OF THIS BEAD'S OWN CONTROL WAS NOT RE-RUN: I recorded v1 returning drvPaths for axon-01, blade, cortex and uplink. The investigator re-established axon-01, uplink and blade with drvPaths at exit 0 — CORTEX WAS NOT RE-RUN. Do not treat cortex's v1 control as re-verified.
NOTE ALSO: `tryEval` catches the `age` case (it is a `throw`) but NOT blade's (it is an `abort`). A containment claim must name which.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ SECOND AND THIRD WITNESSES FOR ITEM 1 (the missing `host.aspect` field), from a different corpus entirely — the den TEMPLATES, measured 2026-07-28.
  `fleet-demo` → `attribute 'environment' missing` at modules/policies/fleet.nix:76:29 (`accessByEnv.${host.environment}`). The template DECLARES `environment = "prod"` on each host and EXTENDS THE HOST SCHEMA at modules/environments.nix:43. ⇒ den-hoag's RESOLVED HOST ctx CARRIES `name` BUT NOT THE CUSTOM SCHEMA FIELD.
  `microvm` template → `attribute 'microvm' missing` at modules/microvm-integration.nix:59:20.
⇒ THREE FIELDS NOW: `aspect` (corpus, v1 declares it at nix/lib/entities/host.nix:68), `environment` (template, user-declared via schema extension), `microvm` (template). ★ THE CLASS IS BROADER THAN 'one field den-hoag forgot': THE RESOLVED HOST RECORD DOES NOT CARRY SCHEMA-DECLARED FIELDS. A user-extended schema field and a den-declared one both fail, which means it is the record's CONSTRUCTION, not a missing declaration.

★★ AND THIS BEARS DIRECTLY ON THE OWNER'S microvm REORDERING. The corpus blocker at den-hoag-9xo.48 was framed as an advanced MATERIALIZATION case — a host within a host. The template hits `host.microvm` MISSING FROM THE HOST RECORD, which is the SAME SHAPE as `host.environment` and `host.aspect`. ⇒ THE microvm CASE IS AT LEAST PARTLY A *LINKING* DEFECT — the host record not carrying its declared fields — RATHER THAN ONLY A MATERIALIZATION ONE. That is evidence FOR the reordering (fix the record construction first, on the simple cases, where it is cheap to witness) and it means the microvm work may substantially dissolve once this class is fixed.
NOTE ALSO: no template reproduced the `age` blocker or `programs.neovim-flake` — consistent with den-hoag-9xo.51's finding that both are the placeRemapped nested-eval defect, which needs a home-manager route the templates do not exercise.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ MECHANISM ATTRIBUTION REFUTED — `excludedType` IS NOT WHAT DROPS THESE FIELDS, AND THE CAUSE IS NOW OPEN AGAIN.
The structural audit proposed, and I relayed to the owner, that `excludedType` drops `raw`/`deferredModule` fields and is therefore this bead's mechanism — v1 declares `aspect` as `lib.types.raw`, so the inference was clean. MEASURED FALSE at HEAD (den-hoag-4kh.49): `excludedType` STOPPED dropping fields at commit 77cb3c8; it now PARTITIONS them across two transports, and ★ `stampFieldNamesByKind` (lib/compat/ingest.nix:449-456) UNIONS BOTH TREES' NAMES, so THE DECLARED FIELD SET IS IDENTICAL EITHER WAY. Widening the predicate in a scratch tree changed nothing but six tests that assert the exclusion itself.
⇒ **ALL DECLARED REGISTRY FIELDS ALREADY REACH THE RECORD.** So `host.aspect`, `host.environment` and `host.microvm` are missing for some OTHER reason, and this bead's mechanism is UNKNOWN rather than identified.

★ WHAT THE SAME INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT MAY BE THE REAL LEAD, though it did not chase it: running the corpus under den-hoag, BOTH arms (baseline and widened) reach `system.build.toplevel` → `assertions` → `home-manager.users` and fail at the SAME frontier — **`error: attribute 'id_hash' missing` at lib/attributes/collections.nix:205:32**, `identity = a.content.id_hash`. That is a MISSING FIELD ON A CONTENT RECORD, one layer in from the entity record, and it is where the corpus actually stops today.
★ AND A SECOND LEAD FROM THE SAME REPORT: the kernel RE-DECLARES every stamped name at lib/compat/ingest.nix:465-472 as `schema.types.raw` WITH `default = null` — UNIFORMLY, for safe and raw names alike. A field that is declared-with-null-default IS PRESENT IN THE RECORD BUT CARRIES NO VALUE. ⇒ THE SYMPTOM 'attribute missing' AND THE SYMPTOM 'declared but null' ARE DIFFERENT FAILURES, and this bead has only ever observed the first at the READ site. Establish which one each of the three fields actually is before designing anything.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the three witnesses themselves — `host.aspect` (corpus, v1 declares it at nix/lib/entities/host.nix:68), `host.environment` (fleet-demo, user-declared via schema extension at modules/environments.nix:43), `host.microvm` (microvm template). And the class observation survives too: a user-extended field and a den-declared one fail IDENTICALLY, so whatever the mechanism is, it is in the record's CONSTRUCTION and not in any single declaration.
⇒ P3 IS NOT BLOCKED ON den-hoag-4kh.49 ANY MORE — that question is answered NO. It is blocked on identifying THIS mechanism, which is now the open item.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ VERDICT: **TWO DEFECTS, NOT ONE. THIS BEAD'S CLASS CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE RECORD'S CONSTRUCTION IS FINE.**
`entityFields.host.<name>` carries EVERY schema-declared field — user-extended and den-declared alike — with
CORRECT VALUES. Measured on both templates and the corpus. **PRESENT-BUT-NULL OCCURS FOR NONE OF THEM**;
`default = null` is not implicated, because the `instanceConfig` stamp overwrites the raw+null re-declaration
on every measured path.

★ DEFECT A — `environment` AND `microvm` FAIL ON A SYNTHETIC PROBE ENTITY, NEVER ON A REAL HOST.
`lib/concern-policies.nix:139-144`: `probeEntry = { id_hash = "«probe»"; name = "«probe»"; } // sentinelFields`,
where `sentinelFields` is `den.probeSentinelFields` — ★ A HAND-MAINTAINED THREE-NAME LITERAL
(`{ class; system; hostName; }` + optional `settings`) at `lib/compat/flake-module.nix:528-537`. **IT IS NOT
DERIVED FROM THE SCHEMA, THE REGISTRY, OR THE STAMP.** And `tryEval` DOES NOT CATCH `attribute 'X' missing`,
so any policy body reading an unlisted field aborts the whole evaluation.
MEASURED IN ONE RUN: the probe record's attrNames are `[class hostName id_hash name system]` with
`has_environment = false`; the four REAL hosts in the SAME RUN carry eighteen names including
`environment_val = "prod"`. And the `«probe»` fire is FIRST in emission order, which is why the template
aborts before any real host is reached.
★ CAUSAL TEST, ADOPTED EVIDENCE NOT INFERENCE: adding ONE line `environment = "«probe»";` to
`probeSentinelModule` makes that error DISAPPEAR ENTIRELY and evaluation advances. Same with
`microvm = { guests = [ ]; }`. ⇒ FIELDS SELF-ANNOUNCE ONE AT A TIME.
★★ AND THE CEILING IS DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE — `flake-module.nix:518` and `concern-policies.nix:138`:
"a corpus policy reading an un-enriched field still hard-fails LOUDLY (self-announcing → add it)".
**THIS BEAD HAS BEEN RE-DERIVING A KNOWN, WRITTEN-DOWN CEILING.**

★ DEFECT B — `aspect` IS NOT DECLARED AT ALL, DELIBERATELY, AND IT SAYS SO. `lib/compat/registry.nix:34-38`:
"Everything else v1 declares there (**aspect**, description, mainModule, `__resolveResult`,
`__pathSetByScope`) reads den v1 RUNTIME machinery the shim replaces wholesale — none is grain- or
stamp-relevant, so none is declared." Not in `baseEntityModule` ⇒ not an option ⇒ invisible to BOTH stamp
trees ⇒ absent from the registry entry. MEASURED AT REAL DISPATCH on host `cortex` and guest `cortex-cuda` —
NOT on `«probe»`.
★ ABSENCE CLAIM WITH POSITIVE CONTROL, same predicate, same runs: `grep -c probeOf` over the three traces
gives 3 / 3 / **0**, and the `«probe»` token count 1 / 1 / **0**. The predicate is live, and THE CORPUS
FAILURE HAS NO PROBE FRAME — which is what separates B from A.

⇒ SO THE THREE FIELDS ARE NOT ONE CLASS. My inference from "a user-extended field and a den-declared one fail
identically" was wrong: they fail identically BECAUSE THE PROBE SENTINEL IS A LITERAL THAT KNOWS ABOUT
NEITHER, not because construction drops both.
`id_hash` at collections.nix:205 IS A THIRD, DIFFERENT DEFECT: `a.content` there is a gen-aspects ASPECT NODE,
not an entity record (`a.content.${chName}` at :179, `aspect = a.content` at :200), and `id_hash` is a
gen-aspects native structural key — a missing one means an UNTYPED ATTRSET REACHED THE ASPECT-EMISSION
POSITION. ★ NOT REPRODUCED — all seven corpus configs abort earlier; reported as structurally-determined-by-
reading, with `id_hash` token count 0 in all six logs.

★★ WHAT DISSOLVES DEFECT A: **P1 DELETES THE PROBE FROM THE KERNEL** (den-hoag-9xo.54,
specs/2026-07-28-policy-record-primitive-design.md). A policy that declares `emits` is never probed, so no
synthetic entity is ever built for it and no unlisted field can be read. The compat probe that survives is
NON-AUTHORITATIVE and ★ TOTAL ON FAILURE — a caught throw becomes a NAMED abort naming the escape, never a
bare missing-attribute crash. ⇒ DEFECT A IS DOWNSTREAM OF P1 AND SHOULD NOT BE FIXED SEPARATELY.
★ AND A REAL CAVEAT ON THE OBVIOUS ALTERNATIVE, with partial evidence: "just derive the sentinel from the
schema" IS NOT FREE. A five-key `microvm` sentinel including the deferredModule slots did NOT clear the
blocker — it produced "The option 'flake' does not exist" — while the one-key `{ guests = [ ]; }` variant
behaved correctly. **SENTINEL VALUES PERTURB STRATUM DETECTION.** That cascade was not chased. It is an
argument for removing the probe rather than enriching it.
DEFECT B NEEDS A DECISION, NOT A SENTINEL: either declare `aspect` in `baseEntityModule` with a den-hoag-native
resolution for v1's `lookupAspect den config`, or route the corpus read through a native surface.

title: [corpus] nix-config fails under den-hoag on ONE guard: gen-aspects rejects a bare module in includes — is the corpus wrong or the guard too strict?
description:
★ FIRST CORPUS EVAL OF THE ARC — MEASURED 2026-07-28 at den-hoag `222af84`. THE REAL nix-config FAILS UNDER
den-hoag ON EXACTLY ONE NAMED GUARD, AND THAT GUARD IS THE CLASS-CONTENT/ASPECT AMBIGUITY THIS ARC IS ABOUT.

WORKS-ON-DEN GATE, BOTH ARMS RUN:
  (a) `github:sini/nix-config/b0b2076` on its OWN pinned den — RESOLVES. 7 hosts:
      axon-01, axon-02, axon-03, bitstream, blade, cortex, uplink.
  (b) same rev, `--override-input den path:<den-hoag>` — FAILS. EXIT 1.
⇒ Gate satisfied: this IS a real den-hoag gap, not a broken config.

THE FAILURE, and it is ONE named throw rather than a cascade — 2 `error:` lines in the whole trace, the throw
plus its module-system wrapper. From `gen-aspects/lib/types.nix:324-327`, verbatim:
  "gen-aspects: includes element is a bare module ({ imports = [ … ]; }) with no aspect identity —
   a class-content node included AS an aspect? An include must be an aspect (by value or fixpoint ref), a
   keyRef, or a deferred fn/policy; `imports` is the module merge slot, never an aspect content key."
Corpus site: `modules/den/flake-parts.nix`, reached through `flake.nixosConfigurations`.

★★ THE FINDING IS *WHICH* GUARD IT IS. The error's own diagnostic question — "a class-content node included
AS an aspect?" — is the ASPECT/CLASS-CONTENT DISAMBIGUATION, the collision class this arc has been working
all session (den-hoag-4kh.16's history, the key-semantics/keyCategory landing). den v1 ACCEPTED a bare module
in `includes`; gen-aspects REJECTS it by declaration.
⇒ SO THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOT "wire another consumer". IT IS WHETHER THE CORPUS IS WRONG OR den-hoag IS TOO
STRICT — a semantics question about the den surface, exactly the class [[feedback_den_surface_not_config]]
says to decide on EXPRESSIBILITY rather than on corpus presence. Both readings are live:
  (i) the corpus is passing class content where an aspect belongs, v1 tolerated it, and the guard is right —
      in which case the corpus needs a change and this is a MIGRATION note, not a den-hoag defect;
  (ii) a bare module in `includes` is legitimate den surface that gen-aspects must accept — in which case the
      guard is over-strict and the fix is upstream in gen-aspects.
DO NOT ASSUME (i) BECAUSE THE GUARD IS NEW. The guard is newer than the corpus, which is an argument about
chronology, not about correctness.

★ WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN, and it is more than I expected: THE MECHANISM PRODUCES A BYTE-IDENTICAL SYSTEM.
`parity/ship-gate.nix` run at 222af84 returns `allEqual: true`, with v1 and den-hoag yielding THE SAME
toplevel derivation for a real bootable NixOS system through the shim —
`/nix/store/q7vk7qda3687g06p2kaaql00raqmpb3x-nixos-system-igloo-26.11.20260705.d407951.drv` on BOTH arms, and
a second channel-fixture host likewise. Not a hash of a fixture: a full nixos module fixpoint.
So "can den-hoag evaluate a v1 config to the same system?" is ANSWERED YES at n=1 on a synthetic bootable
fixture. What is unproven is the real corpus, and it is unproven for ONE reason, named above.

NEXT STEP IS A DECISION, NOT A BUILD: read `modules/den/flake-parts.nix`'s `includes` at the corpus rev,
establish what it actually passes, and rule (i) vs (ii). If (ii), the fix is a gen-aspects change and belongs
upstream. If (i), the corpus migration note belongs with the v2 release arc.
★ AND WHATEVER THE RULING, THIS IS THE FIRST CORPUS-BLOCKING ITEM THE ARC HAS MEASURED RATHER THAN INFERRED.
den-hoag-9xo.27 records that the gates cannot fail on a corpus-breaking change; this eval is the manual
substitute and should become the gate.

title: [kernel] the shipped supportedness guard aborts on ANY enrich value containing a lambda — Nix == is false for distinct closures; ec6ba23 HELD UNPUSHED
description:
★★ MEASURED REGRESSION IN `ec6ba23` — THE SUPPORTEDNESS GUARD REJECTS WELL-FORMED FLEETS. COMMIT IS HELD
UNPUSHED. DO NOT PUSH UNTIL RESOLVED.

MECHANISM: `supported = published == converged`. Nix's `==` is FALSE FOR ANY TWO DISTINCT CLOSURES.
`converged.k` and `published.k` come from two DIFFERENT `enrichAt` calls, so any enrich value that IS a
lambda, or CONTAINS one anywhere in its tree, compares unequal and the guard aborts.

MEASURED, single policy, NO cycle, NO negation:
  fnPol = _: [ (d.enrich { key = "fn"; value = (x: x + 1); }) ];
  at a40cc96 → exit 0, keys ["__entry","fn","node"], forcing `.fn 41` gives 42
  at ec6ba23 → ABORT
BLAST RADIUS at ec6ba23: a nested attrset `{ mod = { pkgs, ... }: {...}; n = 5; }` → ABORT. A list
`[ 1 (x: x) ]` → ABORT. A plain `{ a = 1; b = "two"; }` → exit 0. So: ANY VALUE CONTAINING A LAMBDA ANYWHERE.
★ AND THE MESSAGE MISDIAGNOSES IT — it names the key and its writer, then asserts a negative-edge cycle THAT
DOES NOT EXIST. A user hits an abort blaming a construct they did not write.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: every b1-supportedness fixture uses scalars or strings, and nothing in-tree enriches a
function today, so 1922/1922 and parity 71/71 are both green and both blind. But `d.enrich`'s `value` has NO
TYPE CONSTRAINT — proved by the a40cc96 arm above, where a function value evaluates and applies fine — and
`den.policies` is the user surface. A deferred module is the obvious thing to enrich with.
POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE COVERAGE CLAIM: `enrich` is den-hoag-native and absent from den v1 — 0 hits across
the den-configs corpus, with 1150 files matching `den.` in the same run. So corpus silence is expected and is
NOT evidence the surface is unused.

★ THIS NEEDS AN OWNER-LEVEL DECISION, NOT A PATCH. Two shapes:
  (a) CONSTRAIN enrich values to a comparison-total domain, and say so in `lib/errors.nix` — rejecting a
      function value FOR ITS OWN REASON, with its own named error, rather than as a false supportedness
      failure. This narrows a public surface.
  (b) MAKE `supported` COMPARE ON A COMPARISON-TOTAL PROJECTION, so incomparable values are excluded from the
      equality rather than failing it. This keeps the surface and weakens the guard on exactly the values it
      cannot judge — and the weakening must then be stated as a limit of the law, not hidden.
Under construction-over-repair, (a) makes the defect unrepresentable and (b) leaves a documented hole. Under
"improve the API rather than preserve it", (a) is defensible only if a function-valued enrich is genuinely
not meant to be expressible — which is an owner question about the surface, not an implementation detail.

SECOND, SMALLER GAP — A THIRD DISAGREEMENT ARM IS UNREPORTED (errs SAFE, under-names). `dropped ∪ drifted`
does not cover "key in `published`, NEVER in `converged`". The bare `ctx:` lambda form always fires and can
branch on VALUES, so `enrichAt converged` can fire a rule `enrichAt prev` did not. Measured with a `lateZ`
rule alongside a drift pair: it aborts, but names only `x`, and `z` appears in NEITHER clause.
And with both lists empty the message names NOTHING — no dangling punctuation, but no key either.

★ THE REMEDY SENTENCE IS A SPEC-LEVEL DEFECT, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION ONE. The unconditional trailing clause
asserts "a policy whose guard reads the ABSENCE of a context key another policy writes forms a cycle through
a negative edge" — FALSE for the drift case and FALSE for the function-value false positive. It is inherited
VERBATIM from the gate-attested spec (`specs/2026-07-28-ctx-supportedness-design.md`, error builder :329-338),
so the spec must change with the code.

WHAT THE REVIEW CONFIRMED SOUND: spec fidelity is EXACT (token-diff of the extracted core against the impl
shows only nixfmt lambda breaking); the witness is real, with red 1918/1922 exit 1, exactly the four claimed
reds, ★ all four failing `got false, expected true` — i.e. NO ABORT OCCURRED, which is itself the proof they
fail for THIS guard's reason, since an earlier guard aborting first would have produced a false PASS; green
1922/1922 exit 0; parity 71/71; `checks.default` exit 0; kernel hygiene clean with positive controls.

PROVENANCE: independent implementation review of ec6ba23, 2026-07-28, before push.
