comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ OWNER RULING, 2026-07-28: COMPARE ON A COMPARISON-TOTAL PROJECTION. Option (b).

The guard keeps the surface and excludes incomparable values from the equality rather than failing on them; THE RESULTING HOLE IS A STATED LIMIT OF THE LAW, not a hidden one. `enrich` may still carry a function, a deferred module, or anything containing one.
THE REASONING, recorded because it decides similar cases later: A FUNCTION RE-DERIVED IDENTICALLY IS NOT AN UNSUPPORTED FACT. The law is about whether the fixpoint and the published delta AGREE; Nix's `==` is simply unable to answer that for closures, and answering 'they disagree' when the instrument cannot tell is a FALSE POSITIVE, not a conservative one. ⇒ THE EQUALITY WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT — THE VALUE WAS NEVER THE WRONG SHAPE. And narrowing a public surface to fix a guard is backwards: the guard exists to serve the surface.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION OWES:
  1. A projection under which comparison is TOTAL, with the incomparable part named — say what is compared and what is not, in the source, citing theory rather than a bead key.
  2. ★ THE LIMIT STATED IN THE SPEC AS WELL AS THE CODE. specs/2026-07-28-ctx-supportedness-design.md is gate-VALIDATED and its error builder (:329-338) is attested — THE SPEC CHANGES WITH THE CODE. A guard that silently judges less than it claims is the documented-but-unenforced pattern this arc exists to remove.
  3. ★ THE ERROR MESSAGE'S TRAILING REMEDY SENTENCE MUST GO OR BE CONDITIONALISED. It asserts unconditionally that 'a policy whose guard reads the ABSENCE of a context key another policy writes forms a cycle through a negative edge' — FALSE for the drift case and FALSE for this false positive. It is inherited verbatim from the attested spec, so this is a spec-level fix.
  4. THE THIRD DISAGREEMENT ARM, while the message is being touched: `dropped ∪ drifted` does not cover 'key in published, NEVER in converged'. Errs SAFE (still aborts) but names nothing — measured with a `lateZ` rule, where the abort named only `x` and `z` appeared in neither clause.
  5. A WITNESS THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS: a fleet enriching a function value, and one enriching a nested attrset containing one, both required to evaluate CLEAN. Red before the fix — measured to abort at ec6ba23 — and green after. ★ Every existing b1-supportedness fixture uses scalars or strings, which is exactly why 1922/1922 and parity 71/71 were both green and both blind.
⇒ ec6ba23 STAYS UNPUSHED until this lands. The law is right and the witness is real; it simply rejects fleets it has no business rejecting.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ FIXED AND PUSHED — 6f472d3, alongside ec6ba23 which is now also pushed. Verified independently by the orchestrator with exit status captured directly: ci 1933/1933 EXIT=0, parity 71/71 EXIT=0.

THE PROJECTION, per the owner's ruling: a TAGGED UNION with a single-key wrapper, so no value can forge another's projection — a user's `{ fn = …; }` projects to `{ attrs = { fn = …; }; }`.
  COMPARES: int/float/string/path/bool/null; lists and attrsets ELEMENTWISE TO ANY DEPTH; derivations by `outPath` — ★ which is `==`'s OWN rule, INHERITED rather than invented. So a value that merely CONTAINS a lambda is still compared FIELD BY FIELD; only the lambda itself is exempt.
  DOES NOT COMPARE: a function's BODY. Two functions agree unless their FORMALS differ.
  ★ AND THE HOLE IS WITNESSED, NOT MERELY DESCRIBED — `test-limit-of-the-law-a-lambda-body-is-not-compared` publishes a closure answering 3 while the fixpoint state carried one answering 2, and asserts CLEAN. The limit is a test, so it cannot rot into a claim.
`agree = a: b: a == b || project a == project b` — a fully comparable value costs exactly what the `==`-only law cost it; the projection is paid only where equality already returned false.

★ RESTRUCTURING THE LAW TO EXPOSE THE LIMIT SURFACED A FOURTH ARM I NEVER NAMED. I flagged the third (a key derived only at the converged context, never in state). The agent found a FOURTH: AN INHERITED KEY OVERWRITTEN DURING ITERATION AND INERT AT CONVERGENCE. `dropped` was blind (the published set still has the key — the base's own value) and the drifted scan was blind (it scanned `attrNames added`, and the key is not in `added`). MEASURED AT ec6ba23: IT ABORTS NAMING NOTHING AT ALL and asserts the negative-edge remedy anyway. The law is now three named arms — `dropped` / `unclosed` / `drifted` — each naming its key AND its writer AND carrying its own remedy. `unclosed` keys are exactly what `provenance` cannot attribute (it re-runs the ITERATION), so it falls back to `owners`, already forced for B1 precedence.

★★ ANTI-VACUITY — THE REAL RISK, AND IT IS DISCHARGED PROPERLY. With `supported` stubbed TRUE and the arms still forced: NINE REDS. The four originals plus five new abort guards. ★ ALL NINE ARE ASSERTION FAILURES, ZERO EVALUATION ERRORS — 'got false, expected true', i.e. NO ABORT OCCURRED. An earlier guard firing first would have SATISFIED the assertion and produced a false PASS, so the direction of failure proves each fails for THIS law's reason. THREE of the nine carry a function value in the same context as the disagreement, and ONE puts the disagreement INSIDE the function-carrying value, with a differential control where the same value SHAPE without drift evaluates clean. The projection is not loose enough to admit a genuine disagreement.

COMPLEXITY — ★ STRICTLY LESS FORCING THAN ec6ba23, not merely neutral. Agreement is decided per TOUCHED key (`added ∪ (converged \ base)` — precisely the keys whose two sides are distinct values, which ec6ba23's `==` was descending into anyway), and untouched keys settle under ONE `removeAttrs`-restricted `==` at pointer-check price. `project` runs only where `==` already answered false, one traversal per side, O(size of forced value), each value visited once.
MESSAGE TEXT IS UNWITNESSABLE IN-SUITE (no `expectedError` through checks.default — den-hoag-9mo) so the three arms were verified BY HAND: dropped → `a`/`negA`, unclosed → `z`/`lateN`, drifted → `x`/`driftX`. The unconditional trailing remedy sentence is GONE from code AND spec; an empty clause now renders no remedy.
SPEC UPDATED AND PUSHED (752b2a9): new core hash 7c978b18cdb82243e713a92355153b51, error builder db944941e9bd66a4aa1e371825b5faf8. ★ The recipe was reproduced against the PREVIOUS revision's own recorded values BEFORE recomputing — so the new numbers are anchored to a verified method, not to a fresh guess. Every fenced fragment verified byte-present in the shipped source: the spec blocks are now the SHIPPED TEXT, not a proposal. §8 and §9.2 figures NOT re-measured and stated as such.

title: [kernel] P0 LIVE: declare.inject/declare.reroute DO NOT REACH THE BUILT SYSTEM — anchor by expression 'terminalModulesAt = id: class: projectClass id class', NOT by applyInjectReroute which no longer exists
description:
★★ MEASURED KERNEL DEFECT — TWO CONTENT PATHS DISAGREE AT HEAD. `declare.inject` AND `declare.reroute` ARE
PUBLIC VERBS THAT DO NOT REACH THE BUILT SYSTEM.

MECHANISM: there are TWO consumers of class content and only ONE of them applies the inject/reroute acts.
  `terminalModulesAt = projectClass` (lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:776) reads `classSliceOf` over reach
  DIRECTLY. It never touches the per-node class-content map, so IT NEVER SEES `applyInjectReroute`.
⇒ `declare.inject` / `declare.reroute` DO reach `outputFor`, `den.graph.trace`, the compat resolve-verbs and
the PARITY ORACLE — and DO NOT reach the built system. A user declares a relocation, every introspection
surface agrees it happened, and the actual NixOS configuration does not contain it.

POSITIVE CONTROL, same run — this is a fact about the CODE, not about the instrument:
  grep `inject|reroute` over `lib/` finds the acts CONSUMED at exactly TWO sites —
  `lib/attributes/class-modules.nix:133` and `:152`, BOTH inside `applyInjectReroute`.
  The same run matches `lib/declarations.nix:39-40`, which REGISTERS the kind and NAMES class-modules as its
  consumer, and `:54-55`. So the instrument finds declaration sites and consumer sites; the absence of a
  THIRD consumer is measured, not an artefact of the predicate.
  `lib/compat/legacy/forwards.nix:85` desugars to `deliver`, not a relocation — not a third path.

★ WHY NO GUARD CAUGHT IT: `ci/tests/edge-completeness.nix:214` asserts the ATTRIBUTE, not the TERMINAL. The
attribute is correct. Every test that checks class content checks the path that works. The divergence is
invisible to a suite that never compares the two consumers against each other — which is the general lesson:
WHEN A VALUE HAS TWO CONSUMERS, A TEST OF EITHER ONE PROVES NOTHING ABOUT THEIR AGREEMENT.

CORPUS COST TODAY IS ZERO: Ρ=∅ and Ι=∅ fleet-wide — no corpus config declares a relocation, which is exactly
why this has never been observed. The defect is latent, and the first user to use a documented public verb
finds it.

★ THE FIX IS ALREADY DESIGNED, AS A SIDE EFFECT. The bucket-to-seed-query design
(specs/2026-07-28-bucket-to-edge-design.md, den-hoag-4kh.16) unifies BOTH consumers onto one query, which
closes this BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by adding a second application of the acts. That is the preferable
remedy under the standing construction-over-repair rule: applying the acts in a second place would be a
repair that must be re-applied at every future consumer.
★ BUT IT REQUIRES AN OWNER RULING, because it CHANGES WHAT A PUBLIC EXPORT DOES (`declare`, at
lib/default.nix:2730). The change makes the export behave as documented; it is still an observable change.
The fallback if the ruling is "no" is to keep two disagreeing sources — explicitly NOT recommended by the
design.

PROVENANCE: found by the bucket-to-seed-query design agent, 2026-07-28, while establishing the blast radius
of a different change. It was in NO input — not in the scope doc, not in any bead, not in any papers tracker.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ OWNER RULING, 2026-07-28: "the change is acceptable."

The design's §13 Q1 is ANSWERED YES. Unifying both class-content consumers onto the single channel-coordinate seed query is APPROVED, including the observable change to what the public `declare` export does (lib/default.nix:2730).

⇒ THIS DEFECT IS FIXED BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY REPAIR. The rejected alternative was to apply the inject/reroute acts a SECOND time on the terminal path — which would have been a repair in the precise sense C7 objects to: an invariant that must be re-applied at every future consumer of class content, regressing silently the moment a third consumer appears. Under the approved decision there is ONE query and therefore no second place for the acts to be missing from. The defect cannot recur because the shape that permits it is gone.

THE FALLBACK IS NOW MOOT and should not be revived: 'keep two disagreeing sources' was explicitly not recommended by the design and is not recommended here. Two sources of truth for the same value, with no test comparing them, is what produced this defect.

SEQUENCING: this bead closes when den-hoag-4kh.16's design is IMPLEMENTED, not when it is gated. Until then the defect is LIVE — `declare.inject`/`declare.reroute` remain public verbs that do not reach the built system, and the corpus does not exercise them (Ρ=∅, Ι=∅ fleet-wide), so nothing will surface it in the meantime.
★ A WITNESS IS OWED AND MUST LAND RED FIRST: a fixture that declares a relocation and asserts it is present in the TERMINAL output — not in the attribute. The existing suite cannot catch this because ci/tests/edge-completeness.nix:214 asserts the attribute, which is correct. The new fixture must compare the two consumers against each other, since that is the only thing their agreement is visible in.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CAVEAT ON THE OWNER RULING — THE RULING STANDS, BUT THE DESIGN CANNOT YET EXPRESS THE CHANGE IT AUTHORISES.

The 2026-07-28 ruling ('the change is acceptable') approved unifying both class-content consumers, which closes this defect by construction. The bucket-to-seed-query gate has since found that THE UNIFYING HALF HAS NO EXECUTABLE FORM:
  E10(b) does `concatMap (n: … classSeedsAt n class) reach`, but `reach` (lib/attributes/resolved-aspects.nix:313, emit :126-133) yields records `{ key; content; sharedFoldKey; }` WITH NO SCOPE COORDINATE, while `classSeedsAt` requires a NODE ID. It is internally inconsistent within four lines — the same `let` calls `forwardSourceClassesOf reach` (treating elements as ASPECT records) and then feeds those same elements to `classSeedsAt` (needing IDS).
★ AND THE REPAIR IS NOT MECHANICAL. A reach element carries no coordinate, so there is NO WAY TO SAY WHOSE `Acts` GOVERN A REACH-SOURCED ASPECT. That is an owner-level SEMANTIC question the design never poses: do the PROJECTING SCOPE's acts govern, or the aspect's OWNING SCOPE's? The two give different answers whenever an aspect reaches a node that did not declare it — which is the only case that matters here.

⇒ THE RULING IS NOT INVALIDATED; it authorised the intent and the intent is right. But it was given on a change whose semantics are underdetermined, so a SECOND, NARROWER question is owed before implementation: WHICH SCOPE'S ACTS GOVERN A REACH-SOURCED ASPECT.

★ AND A SECOND BEHAVIOUR DELTA WAS NOT COVERED BY THE RULING AT ALL — it was not in the design when the question was asked. Today `projectClass` (output-modules.nix:741-745) computes `exempt = forwardSourceClassesOf reach`, REACH-sourced deliberately (class-modules.nix:56: 'an unregistered fromClass a meta.__forward spec on a REACHED node names'). The design's E6 computes it OWN-NODE only, and in E10(b) the reach-sourced set is used only by routeRemapFor/forwardModulesFor — the content leg loses it. CONSEQUENCE: a `meta.__forward` spec on a reached-but-not-own aspect stops exempting, so `classifyKey` ABORTS on a typo where content materializes today. That is a compat-fleet-visible regression, unstated in the design and outside what was approved.

THIS DEFECT REMAINS LIVE AND UNCHANGED: `declare.inject`/`declare.reroute` still do not reach the built system. Nothing here alters that; it alters only what the fix must settle first. The witness owed (a fixture asserting a declared relocation reaches the TERMINAL, not the attribute) is unaffected and can be written now — it is red today and should be.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND EXPLAINED — THIS BEAD AND E10(b) ARE THE SAME DEFECT SEEN FROM TWO SIDES. Independent verification at 4b61112 (222af84 is an ancestor; the three relevant files are unchanged since it).

THIS BEAD SAYS declare.inject / declare.reroute do not reach the built system. THE PRECISE REASON:
    projectClass = id: class: ... prelude.concatMap (n: ... classSliceOf exempt n class) reach ++ routeRemapFor exempt id class ++ forwardModulesFor reach exempt class;
classSliceOf is the RAW per-aspect extraction, reading content.${class} DIRECTLY. ★ frameAt, srcOrder, preimageOf, relocationsOf and rawSeedsAt APPEAR NOWHERE IN projectClass's CALL GRAPH — positive control: grepping reroute|relocat|injects over the whole of output-modules.nix returns ONLY PROSE, while the same grep over class-modules.nix hits the live filters. reroute and inject have EXACTLY ONE consumer each in all of lib/, both inside class-seeds.compute, which is strictly node-local.
So relocation is computed correctly by the shipped query and then NOT CONSULTED by the terminal projection. All three terminal reads — contentIdsOf, deltaOf (modules = terminalModulesAt id name), hostModules — route through projectClass. (NOT exhaustively traced: whether the gen-edge fold output re-enters deltaOf by another route.)

★ AND THE SIBLING ASYMMETRY IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS AN OMISSION RATHER THAN A DESIGN: routeRemapFor exempt id class DOES read declarations at the projecting scope (routesAt id -> deliveriesAt id -> declarations.actions.resolution). ROUTE declarations are honoured at the projecting scope; reroute/inject are honoured NOWHERE ON THIS PATH. Two sibling relocation mechanisms, two treatments, no comment reconciling them — in a file that ledgers SIX other known gaps loudly and by name. The absence of a seventh ledger reads as non-awareness.

★★ WHY NO INSTRUMENT CAUGHT IT, AND THIS IS THE PART TO ACT ON: ci/tests/projection.nix pins the anchor projectClass id C == classSubtreeAt id C ++ <route remap delta>. classSubtreeAt reads class-seeds — RELOCATION APPLIED. projectClass does not. ★ WITH ZERO REROUTES ANYWHERE IN THE CORPUS OR FIXTURES, BOTH SIDES AGREE TRIVIALLY. comm -12 over 'grep -rl reroute ci/' and 'grep -rl reachEdge ci/' is EMPTY — no test file contains both, and no fixture declares a reroute at all. The anchor that exists precisely to pin this equivalence is GREEN ON AN INPUT CLASS THAT CANNOT DISTINGUISH ITS TWO SIDES.
⇒ THE FIX HAS A PREREQUISITE: a fixture that declares a reroute AND builds a reach. Without it, any repair to projectClass is unfalsifiable and the anchor will stay green through both the defect and the fix. Same vacuity family as den-hoag-gg8 (a green sibling over an empty list) and den-hoag-6jo — but on the projection ANCHOR, which is worse, because an anchor is what a reader trusts INSTEAD of reading.
⇒ AND THE E10(b) CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY REPAIR: the projecting-scope reading is EXPRESSIBLE (id is bound in projectClass, exactly as routeRemapFor already uses it) and the owning-scope reading is NOT — reach elements are { key; content; sharedFoldKey } with no scope coordinate, and at both construction sites the scope id is in lexical scope and DISCARDED. A repair therefore either takes the projecting-scope reading, or first adds a coordinate to the reach element. See den-hoag-4kh.16.

title: [kernel] a negative-edge cycle in den.policies yields an UNSUPPORTED FACT; nothing guards ctx-key negation
description:
MEASURED DEFECT IN SHIPPED CODE, REACHABLE FROM PLAIN USER CONFIG, PRODUCING A WRONG ANSWER.
Constructed with `den.policies` only — no internal APIs. Fixture: scratchpad/q6-usersurface.nix.

THE SHAPE — ABW Lemma 1's forbidden configuration, a cycle through a negative edge:

    negA = ctx: if ctx ? b then [ ] else [ (declare.enrich { key = "a"; value = 1; }) ];   # a --NEGATIVE--> b
    posB = { a, ... }:        [ (declare.enrich { key = "b"; value = 2; }) ];              # b --POSITIVE--> a

MEASURED, enriched-context keys:
    no policies        ["__entry","node"]
    negA alone         ["__entry","a","node"]        <- control: negA fires, produces a
    posB alone         [ ]                            <- control: never fires, requires a
    BOTH (the cycle)   ["__entry","b","node"]         <- ★ b IS PRESENT, a IS NOT

★ `b` IS IN THE MODEL AND `a` — b's SOLE JUSTIFICATION — IS NOT. AN UNSUPPORTED FACT.
No abort. No warning. Deterministic under reversed declaration order (so it is not a race).
This is exactly what ABW's stratification exists to prevent, and it violates THEOREM 7 (p. 111,
supportedness): every atom in M_P is the head of a ground clause whose body holds. Here nothing justifies b.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT:
· The only ctx-key guard is projectCtx (lib/concern-policies.nix:129). It is an INDEX COMPARISON —
  structurally incapable of observing a CYCLE — and it is NOT USER-REACHABLE (see below), so it is not even
  running.
· L4 (`negates`) ranges only over DECLARED negations on RELATION kinds. A policy body negating a CTX KEY is
  outside its domain entirely.
· `ctx ? key` is the negation, and it is invisible: policy condition edges are derived from
  `builtins.functionArgs`, which yields POSITIVE dependencies only. THE SIGN IS NOT DERIVABLE — negatives
  live inside opaque `ctx: [decls]` bodies and pure Nix cannot introspect them.

★★ IT LANDS ON A STATED-BUT-UNENFORCED PREMISE. lib/attributes/structural.nix:96-99, verbatim:
  "single-writer + KEYSET-MONOTONE GUARDS make a key's value fixed once it appears, so a refire at a grown
   context is idempotent."
That is ABW's no-negative-edge condition stated informally in a comment. A NON-MONOTONE GUARD WAS SUPPLIED
AND ACCEPTED. Kernel-purity criterion 6 — an invariant documented but unenforced.

NOT MEASURED, and it is the one fact separating "latent soundness hole" from "observable corpus bug":
whether the unsupported `b` PROPAGATES INTO MATERIALIZED OUTPUT. Not guessed at. Also unmeasured: whether
any external config in ~/Documents/repos/den-configs currently takes this route.

ACCEPTANCE: a fixture pinning the cycle case. Against the current tree it produces the unsupported fact;
that is the point. Under the three-state CI ruling it lands as a known-fail with a tracked id.

RELATED: den-hoag-4kh.11 (the ABW guard arc that surfaced it). The remedy space overlaps but is NOT the
same — 4kh.11 is about a guard being over-strict on the wrong rule; this is about a guard that does not
exist for a domain that needs one. Do not fold them.
close_reason: EXPIRED — fixed by ec6ba23 + 6f472d3, verified two ways this session. (1) Symbol/site: the bead's own fixtures are bound under their own names in ci/tests/b1-supportedness.nix — negA (emits=["enrich"]; fn = ctx: if ctx ? b then [ ] else [d.enrich{key="a";...}]) and posB (fn = { a, ... }: [d.enrich{key="b";...}]) — and test-negative-cycle-aborts asserts aborts(...) == true. Its quoted premise comment is gone: grep -n KEYSET-MONOTONE lib/attributes/structural.nix -> 0, positive control same run single-writer -> 3 hits. (2) EXECUTION: nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests.b1-supportedness -> EXIT 0 SEEN DIRECTLY (redirected to file, $? read on the adjacent line, not through a pipe), 22/22, with test-negative-cycle-aborts, test-negative-cycle-aborts-at-the-crossing and test-self-negative-aborts all green. The guard the bead asks for exists, fires, and is tested.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ Q1 ANSWERED: THE UNSUPPORTED FACT REACHES MATERIALIZED OUTPUT. This is not a latent hole.
Measured by an independent agent, read-only. Probes: scratchpad/{qA-propagate.nix,qA-ctx.nix,qB-shape.nix}.

PATH: enriched-context -> lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:1006-1007 `bindingsAt`
(`bindings = (result.get id "enriched-context") // channels // settings`) -> gen-bind wrapAll ->
class-content module arg -> crossNixos -> a real NixOS option. Fleet shape from
ci/tests/binding-totality.nix; den.nixpkgs = root-lock nixpkgs d407951447dc.
Consumer: den.aspects.consumer.nixos = { b, ... }: { networking.domain = "SAW-b-${toString b}"; }

FORCED THROUGH THE REAL CROSSING (nixosConfigurations.bare.config.networking.domain):
    CYCLE (negA+posB)   "SAW-b-2"                       <- MATERIALIZED
    negA alone          error: attribute 'b' missing    <- control
    no policies         error: attribute 'b' missing    <- control
    SENTINEL            error: attribute 'zzz_never_written' missing   <- proves the force reaches the
                                                                          module fn; positive arm not vacuous
builtins.tryEval did NOT catch these — a missing-attribute error escapes it, as expected.
ctx at this fleet (node id host:bare@env:prod): CYCLE -> ["__entry","b","env","host"], ctx.b = 2,
ctx.a = missing-attribute error. Controls: negA alone -> a present; posB alone -> never fires.

════ ★ Q2 — THE SHAPE, and it is worse than "a value that should not exist" ════
The agent sharpened the fixture so b's value DERIVES from a:
    posB = { a, ... }: [ (d.enrich { key = "b"; value = "from-a=${builtins.toJSON a}"; }) ]
    materialized      networking.domain = "SAW-b-from-a=1"
⇒ a = 1 WAS REALLY SUPPLIED to posB during the fixpoint, AND THEN DROPPED.
NOT a missing value, NOT a silent default, NOT a malformed value — A WELL-FORMED, FULLY-TYPED NixOS OPTION
VALUE WHOSE DERIVATION READS A PREMISE THE FINAL GRAPH DOES NOT HOLD. Exactly ABW Theorem 7 (p. 111,
supportedness) violated, and it is observable in a built configuration.
Supporting reads on the same arm: enrichments.added = {"b":"from-a=1"} (a is NOT in the delta);
enrichments.owners = {"b":"posB"} (ONE writer; negA leaves NO trace). Control (negA alone): added = {"a":1}.

════ ★★ MECHANISM LOCATED — lib/attributes/structural.nix:136-149 ════
`converged` (the scope.circular fixpoint value) DOES contain a = 1 — that is why posB fired at all. But
:148-149 RE-DERIVES THE PUBLISHED DELTA FROM SCRATCH at the converged context:
    finalActs = enrichAt converged;  added = delta finalActs
At the converged context `ctx ? b` is TRUE, so negA is INERT in that final dispatch and `a` is never
re-produced. :172 then publishes `enriched-context = inherited-context // enrichments.added` = b WITHOUT a.
⇒ THE FIXPOINT AND THE PUBLISHED DELTA DISAGREE. The value is justified during iteration and unjustified in
the result. That is the precise fix target, and it is one site.

════ Q3 — WHAT DID NOT STOP IT ════
The only guard on this path is the single-writer check, structural.nix:150-158 (`owners`,
errors.singleWriter). It is a per-KEY COLLISION check — it fires when two policies write one key. A key with
exactly ONE writer whose premise has vanished is invisible to it: owners = {"b":"posB"} is a CLEAN PASS.
NOTHING ON THE PATH OBSERVES JUSTIFICATION.

════ ★★★ Q4 — THE ROUTE IS TRAVELLED IN SHIPPED USER CONFIG ════
Trees searched as SEPARATE runs (never one grep across both), no --include filter, .worktrees AND .git
excluded from every grep.
NEGATIVE EDGES IN REAL CONFIG — absence of a ctx key changes the declaration set:
  den-configs/nixfos/modules/den/policies/route-factories.nix:46  `args@{ host, ... }: lib.optional
      (host.class == "nixos" && !(args ? user))`  — and :68, :95 with `!(args ? home)`
  den-configs/nixfos/.../hardware/persist/class/classes.nix:55    same shape
  ★ den-configs/nixfos/modules/den/policies/users.nix:94-98
      den.policies.env-users = { accessGroups ? [ ], ... }: map (...) (matchRegistryUsers accessGroups);
    A DEFAULTED FORMAL — fires regardless; absent ⇒ [ ] ⇒ zero declarations. A NEGATIVE EDGE.
★ AND THE KEY IS ENRICHMENT-CARRIED, IN THE SAME CONFIG:
  den-configs/nixfos/modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:60,69
      den.policies.env-to-hosts = { environment, ... }: (resolve.to "host" { host = bridgedHost;
                                                                            inherit accessGroups; })
  A MIXED resolve — schema key `host` = transition, NON-SCHEMA key `accessGroups` = ENRICHMENT. That
  semantics is pinned by den's own template (denful/den/templates/ci/modules/public-api/
  policy-context-enrichment.nix:104, "the non-schema key should enrich the current context") and den-hoag's
  parity ledger independently records accessGroups as a ctx key (lib/compat/parity/ledger.md).
⇒ A REAL ENRICH-WRITTEN KEY IS READ BY A REAL ABSENCE-BRANCHING POLICY, IN ONE SHIPPED USER CONFIG.
TEMPLATES: 8 further negated-membership sites (route.nix:227, features/entity-isolation.nix:113,
internal-api/fx-edge-parity.nix:137, fx-materialize-unified.nix:232, edge-trace.nix:360 and :977,
fx-edge-unification-gate.nix:318), plus public-api/dynamic-forward.nix:16 and the or-default-on-ctx-read
shape at internal-api/policy-combinators.nix:228 (`den.lib.policy.when (ctx: ctx.flag or false)`).

════ NOT MEASURED — the one thing that would make this a confirmed live corpus bug ════
WHETHER THE nixfos accessGroups PRODUCER/CONSUMER PAIR ACTUALLY CLOSES INTO A FIXPOINT CYCLE AT RUNTIME.
That needs a full corpus build through den-hoag compat, which the parity ledger records as currently blocked
at the exclude-of-policy stub. So: NEGATIVE EDGE ON AN ENRICHMENT-CARRIED KEY = MEASURED PRESENT in shipped
config; CLOSED CYCLE IN THE CORPUS = NEITHER CONFIRMED NOR REFUTED. Do not upgrade the claim past that.
Also: Q1/Q2 measured on the synthetic two-policy fixture, not a corpus fleet. nix-config not searched.

════ INSTRUMENT NOTE — a false clean the agent caught in its own work ════
Its first enrichment-writer sweep used the token `enrich` and returned 0 files across den-configs. WRONG
PREDICATE: v1 spells enrichment `resolve { <non-schema-key> = … }`, so that sweep could not have matched.
Corrected predicate: bare `resolve { … }` = 0 in den-configs with POSITIVE CONTROL `resolve.to ` = 5; = 4 in
templates. It also closed the unparenthesized `!x ? y` form (valid Nix; its first regex required parens) —
0 hits in both trees.

════ CONSEQUENCE ════
This bead is no longer "a latent soundness hole reachable from the user surface". It is a defect that
MATERIALIZES A WRONG NixOS OPTION VALUE, with a located single-site mechanism, and with BOTH INGREDIENTS
(an enrichment-written key, an absence-branching read of it) PRESENT IN ONE SHIPPED CONFIG. Only the closure
is unproven.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ REMEDY DESIGN WRITTEN — papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-28-ctx-supportedness-design.md
619 lines · md5 710fecbceb0b5876588ce4bd55deaf6d · core delimited :234-290, error builder :297-306.
den-hoag and gen-* untouched; no beads, no commits; all patched trees are scratchpad copies. Going to the gate.

════ ★ REPAIR IS IMPOSSIBLE. MEASURED, NOT ARGUED. ════
"Publish the fixpoint instead of re-deriving" was the obvious remedy. IT IS UNSOUND, and the author settled it
by enumerating T_P over the fixture's ENTIRE 2-atom Herbrand base, using THE SHIPPED FIRING PREDICATE
transcribed from gen-derive/lib/core/rule.nix:29-48 (scratchpad/tp.nix):
      {}  → {a}        {a} → {a,b}        {b} → {}        {a,b} → {b}
NO FIXED POINT EXISTS. Both {b} (what den-hoag publishes) and {a,b} (the fixpoint) are MODELS but NEITHER IS
SUPPORTED. Publishing `converged` trades one unsupported fact for another.
⇒ REJECTION IS THE ONLY SOUND REMEDY. This is exactly what ABW predicts for a program that is not stratified,
and it converts the orchestrator's instinct into a measurement.

════ THE HYPOTHESIS HELD — IN A STRONGER FORM THAN POSED ════

title: [compat] den.schema.<kind>.excludes — the INERT headline is EXPIRED (kindExcludesOf landed after the bead was measured); what survives is the subtree-vs-same-kind REPRESENTATION question
description:
den.schema.<kind>.excludes is INERT in den-hoag. The corpus writes it; nothing
consumes it. A consumer's exclusion of a policy therefore does nothing at all,
silently.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY (2026-07-27) -- design-reviewer first, then
reproduced by denhoag-writer with the same four-arm eval at ab1112a rather than
taken on report:

  a_noSchema     ["marker"]
  b_includeOnly  ["__kindInclude__host__policy__0"]   instrument responds
  c_includeExcl  ["__kindInclude__host__policy__0"]   BYTE-IDENTICAL to b
  d_exclOnly     ["marker"]                            no-op

Arm b is the positive control: the instrument does respond to the kind-schema
surface, so c's identity to b is a real negative, not a dead probe.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, and it is instructive: the design cited
lib/compat/compile.nix:714-723 as the displacement consumer. That is
translateAspect reading ASPECT-level aspect.excludes. The corpus writes
KIND-level den.schema.<kind>.excludes -- a different surface. The cited
comment's own next clause says "corpus excludes are policy excludes on kinds",
and the quotation stopped one clause short of the sentence that said so.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this is P1 not a note: any design that relies on a
consumer displacing a den-hoag-provisioned default is unimplementable today.
That is what killed route 1 / A-prime in the .13 default-attachment design
(papers plans/2026-07-27-default-attachment-design.md rev 3, review rev 2 at
papers 64aaed1). Route 1 would have DOUBLE-ATTACHED every corpus host.

NOT SCHEDULED. The decision this bead needs: should kind-level excludes be
implemented (v1 parity -- the corpus already writes it and expects it to work),
or should the corpus's usage be recognised as unsupported and the surface
rejected LOUDLY rather than ignored silently? Silently ignoring a declared
exclusion is the arc's recurring shape: a declared fact the framework does not
read.
notes:
★ RULING AMENDED 2026-07-28 BY MEASUREMENT -- THE ANSWER STANDS, THE REASON DOES
NOT. Full measurement and read-site trace at den-hoag-9xo.58 (closed).

CONFIRMED: den.schema.<K>.excludes IS SUBTREE-SCOPED. It reaches K and all its
descendants. Measured on den v1 at 99cc0c5a with two positive controls, including
the non-ancestor arm that rules out a merely GLOBAL reading.

AMENDED: the ruling's stated reason -- "excludes is includes' DUAL, scoped to the
subtree" -- is WRONG, and it is the kind of wrong that licenses a bad
implementation. A dual invites modelling excludes as includes-with-a-minus-sign,
i.e. as a flat per-kind list. MEASURED, from two ADJACENT LINES of one record
(nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix:72-73), same instrument same run:
    includes at host, observed AT THE HOST -> FIRES    (positive control)
    includes at host, observed at the USER -> ABSENT
    excludes at host, observed at the USER -> SUPPRESSED
INCLUDES FIRES ONLY AT K-NODES; EXCLUDES REACHES K AND ALL DESCENDANTS.
A DUAL HAS ONE EXTENT. THESE DO NOT.

THE ACTUAL REASON: the schema-excludes producer writes a constraint carrying a
LITERAL `scope = "subtree"` (children.nix registerConstraints), registered into
scopedConstraintRegistry keyed by the K INSTANCE's scope, and EVERY reader
resolves it through foldScopeAncestors. The reach comes from the registry and the
ancestor fold, not from any duality with includes.

AND (1) AND (2) ARE ONE MECHANISM WITH TWO PRODUCERS, not two mechanisms. The
static schema field and the dynamic policy.exclude effect emit the same
{ type = "exclude"; scope = "subtree"; identity = ...; } record into the same
registry, read by the same four readers, differing only in `owner` and identity
grain. So the exclude-family work already shipped (#72) and this defect are
closer kin than the bead graph currently shows.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX, and it is why this amendment matters more than a
citation correction: P1's `selects :: null | [ Kind ]` CANNOT REPRESENT
EXCLUDES. The policy-record spec's :828 fold would drop the descendant reach.
Instruction dispatched to p1-impl: honour the SAME-KIND case (which is every one
of the eight declarations that exist anywhere -- full census in 9xo.58 -- so the
live parity break IS fixed), and ABORT BY NAME on a descendant-kind exclusion
rather than under-suppress silently. The full subtree representation is its own
design task with its own gate.

★ NOTE FOR THAT DESIGN: the descendant reach is a reachability query over the
containment relation and gen-graph already provides one -- but reachableFrom is
IRREFLEXIVE while excludes reaches K ITSELF, so the reflexive closure is required
and a mechanical swap silently drops the K-node case.

★ AND NOTE WHY NO CONFIG WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: all eight schema-tier exclude
declarations in nix-config, the den templates and den-configs are SAME-KIND, so
kind-flat and subtree-scoped agree on every one of them. The corpus cannot
discriminate. A fixture must be CONSTRUCTED: policy attached at
den.schema.user.includes, excluded at den.schema.host.excludes, observed at the
user.

STILL OPEN, INFERENCE NOT MEASUREMENT: whether den.schema.<K>.isolated
(scopeIsolated, push-scope.nix) cuts the ancestor walk. foldScopeAncestors never
consults it, so no effect is expected -- untested. If it does cut, the extent is
subtree-modulo-isolation and the eventual design must carry that.


★ THE TWO OPEN CAVEATS ON THE SUBTREE-SCOPING RESULT ARE CLOSED, BOTH MEASURED,
den v1 at 99cc0c5a (clean tree). The extent result stands WITHOUT qualification.

(1) ISOLATION DOES NOT CUT THE CONSTRAINT WALK. The extent is the PLAIN
CONTAINMENT CLOSURE over scopeParent -- NOT "subtree modulo isolation". A
representation built on plain containment is CORRECT.
Five arms, one eval run. Policy at den.schema.host.includes emitting nixos
content; excluded at den.schema.flake-system.excludes (an ANCESTOR of host);
observed at igloo.environment.variables.NMARK:
  s0 CONTROL  exclude at flake-system, no isolation      -> ABSENT (exclusion reaches the host)
  s1 MEASURE  same + den.schema.host.isolated = true     -> ABSENT  (WALK NOT CUT)
  s2 CONTROL  isolation on, no exclusion                 -> PRESENT (observable alive under isolation)
  v1 TOOK-EFFECT  host package -> flake.packages, no isolation -> ["one"]
  v2 TOOK-EFFECT  same, host isolated                    -> [ ]  (ISOLATION DEMONSTRABLY FIRED)
v1/v2 is what makes s1 meaningful: route.nix sends flake-targeted routes through
collectFromSubtree, which IS isolation-aware via scope-walk.nix, so host content
drops out of the flake's collected subtree the moment the host is isolated. s1
matching s0 therefore means isolation genuinely does not touch constraints -- not
that `isolated` did nothing.

★ AND THE EXEMPTION IS PRINCIPLED, QUOTED FROM v1's OWN COMMENT rather than
inferred. nix/lib/aspects/fx/edges/default.nix:
    collected(subtree minus isolated, class) -> (root, class), P=[], M=merge.
    `isolated` is consumed HERE, at edge construction (the subtree boundary via
    subtreeScopes), NOT inside the materializer -- corollary 2: ISOLATION IS
    EDGE-ABSENCE, NEVER A MID-WALK FILTER. An isolated descendant is its OWN
    entity-root, so it is ABSENT from its parent's collected subtree and emits
    its own fold edge instead.
and nix/lib/aspects/fx/scope-walk.nix, note the DIRECTION:
    Scope IDs in `root`'s subtree. `root` is ALWAYS included: isolation gates
    crossing INTO a descendant, not collecting AT the root.
⇒ Isolation governs DOWNWARD content collection at edge construction. The
constraint registry is an UPWARD ancestor fold. Different relation, different
direction, different phase. "Isolation is edge-absence, never a mid-walk filter"
is precisely the sentence that puts the constraint walk out of its scope -- the
constraint walk is not an edge.
STRUCTURAL ABSENCE WITH POSITIVE CONTROL, same predicate same run: grep -c
scopeIsolated over the four constraint readers = 0,0,0,0 (constraint.nix,
dispatch-policies.nix, compile-conditional.nix, policy/schema.nix); the SAME
predicate in the SAME run = 22 in resolve.nix, 8 in edges/route.nix, 2 in
push-scope.nix. The predicate matches abundantly where isolation lives and never
where constraints are read.

(2) foldScopeAncestors IS TOTAL ON A CYCLE. It returns the COMPLETE reachable-
ancestor set; the `seen` guard prevents NON-TERMINATION, never OMISSION.
  c0 ACYCLIC CONTROL {c=b; b=a}          from c -> ["a","b","c"] full chain
  c1 RHO tail->loop  {d=c; c=b; b=a; a=b} from d -> ["a","b","c","d"] ALL FOUR
  c2 self-loop       {a=a}                from a -> ["a"]
  c3 same rho, entered mid-loop           from b -> ["a","b"] (d,c are DESCENDANTS, correctly absent)
  c4 no parent       { }                  from solo -> ["solo"]
★ AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT LUCKY: scopeParent is an ATTRSET, hence a
FUNCTION -- every sid has AT MOST ONE parent. The reachable set from any start is
therefore a simple path optionally ending in a rho-loop, and `go` visits each
reachable node exactly once before `seen` fires. THERE IS NO BRANCHING, hence no
traversal-order freedom. The worry that prompted this -- "an exclusion applies to
some descendants and not others depending on traversal order" -- CANNOT ARISE.
ONE REAL ORDER EFFECT, NOT A DEFECT: merge is zipAttrsWith concatLists, so entries
accumulate in walk order (own scope first, then ancestors), and check-constraint
takes `builtins.head scopedEntries`. For pure excludes this is order-INDEPENDENT
(dispatch-policies uses builtins.any; entryToResume maps every exclude to the same
action). It bites only when an exclude and a SUBSTITUTE collide on one identity,
where the NEAREST scope wins -- deterministic, and arguably correct precedence.

★ SEPARATE FINDING, worth its own attention: AN ISOLATED USER HAS NO REACHABLE
OUTPUT AT ALL. Discovery arms: `igloo ? home-manager` is TRUE without isolation
and FALSE with den.schema.user.isolated = true; flake outputs under user isolation
collapse to ["denful" "nixosConfigurations"] with homeConfigurations = [ ]. This
follows from edge-absence (an isolated user becomes its own entity-root), but
whether a user with no reachable output is INTENDED or a usability defect is
undecided and is not this bead's question.

COVERAGE, named: the isolation measurement used den.schema.host.isolated; an
intervening NON-ROOT kind (tier) was not tested. The MECHANISM argument (the fold
never reads scopeIsolated) covers all kinds; the MEASUREMENT is host-specific.
Took-effect was established for host (v1/v2) and user (home-manager
disappearance), not for other kinds. No LIVE cycle was constructed in a real
spawn/forward merged sub-pipeline -- the fold was measured as a pure function on
synthetic rho maps, which settles what it RETURNS but not that a real spawn
produces those shapes; bounded by spawn-node.nix merging two scopeParent ATTRSETS,
and an attrset cannot encode multi-parent, so the rho family is exhaustive.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ PRIORITY RAISED TO P0 AND UNBLOCKED FROM THE POSTURE DECISION NODE — this is a PARITY DEFECT with live consumers, not a posture question.
DEN V1 CONSUMES IT: nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix:22 `schemaExcludes = schemaEntry.excludes or [ ]`, :72 `excludes = schemaExcludes`.
THE CORPUS DEPENDS ON IT, with the author's stated intent attached: nix-config/modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:85-88 excludes `system-to-os-outputs` and `system-to-hm-outputs` ('Fleet handles host instantiation'), :91 excludes `host-to-users` ('fleet user policies replace it'); den-configs/slashfiles/modules/schemas/flake-system.nix:5 excludes `packages-to-flake`.
⇒ UNDER den-hoag THOSE POLICIES RUN ANYWAY. The fleet is silently getting default walking policies and a built-in user policy that the configuration explicitly turns off. Owner-facing consequence: den-hoag cannot correctly build nix-config until this is honoured, and the failure is SILENT — no error, just extra policies firing.
NO POSTURE RULING NEEDED. Named-rejecting would reject a construct v1 honours and real configs use. The answer is to honour it; the only open question is where the consumer belongs.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ OWNER RULING, 2026-07-28: `excludes` IS `includes`' DUAL, BUT IT ONLY APPLIES TO ITS SUBTREE.

So the semantics are settled and are NOT any of the three readings the spec brief offered as candidates. Not a global edge removal, not a subtraction from a fully-resolved set. It is the DUAL OF `includes`, SCOPED: whatever region `den.schema.<kind>.includes` adds into, `den.schema.<kind>.excludes` subtracts from — and that region is THE KIND'S SUBTREE, not the whole graph.

★ THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MUST DRIVE THE WITNESS: A POLICY REACHABLE BY MORE THAN ONE ROUTE IS EXCLUDED ONLY ON ROUTES INSIDE THE DECLARING KIND'S SUBTREE, AND SURVIVES ELSEWHERE. That is precisely the case that distinguishes this reading from the two rejected ones, so a fixture must exercise it — the same policy reachable both inside and outside the subtree, with only the inside occurrence suppressed. ★ A WITNESS THAT ONLY TESTS A SINGLE-ROUTE POLICY CANNOT TELL THE THREE READINGS APART AND WOULD PASS UNDER ALL OF THEM — the predicate-blindness failure this arc keeps paying for, applied to an acceptance criterion.
AND THE SCOPING IS WHAT MAKES IT COMPOSABLE: an exclusion at one kind cannot silently disarm a policy some unrelated part of the fleet depends on.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION: THE CONSUMER BELONGS WHEREVER `includes` IS ALREADY CONSUMED, as its dual. den-hoag already honours the sibling surface, so the pair was split and only one landed — which is a more interesting defect than 'a consumer is missing', and the design should say why. If the two cannot sit together, that asymmetry is itself a finding.

★ ONE THING DELIBERATELY NOT RULED, AND IT MUST BE ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: WHAT THE SUBTREE IS, EXACTLY. Descendants in the kind/parent DAG? The reachable set from that kind? Whatever `includes`' existing consumer already computes? The owner ruled the SHAPE, not the REGION. It must be derived from `includes`' implementation AND from den v1's `nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix` behaviour, and stated as an EQUATION in the executable core. ⇒ IF `includes` AND v1 DISAGREE ON THE REGION, THAT DISAGREEMENT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING AVAILABLE HERE — it would mean den-hoag's shipped half of the pair is already off-parity, and this bead would grow a second defect.

★ AND THE aspect-level-vs-kind-level TRAP IS NOW MORE DANGEROUS, NOT LESS. `translateAspect` reading ASPECT-level `aspect.excludes` (lib/compat/compile.nix:714-723) is a DIFFERENT SURFACE from the KIND-level `den.schema.<kind>.excludes` the corpus writes. A dual-of-includes design is exactly the shape that could be mis-wired to it, because both plausibly 'subtract'. A previous design was already caught by this.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ MY CENTRAL CLAIM WAS FALSE, AND THE REAL ARGUMENT IS BETTER. Measured at 6f472d3 by the spec author.

I ASSERTED — to the owner, and in this bead's ruling comment — that 'under den-hoag those policies RUN ANYWAY' and that 'den-hoag cannot correctly build nix-config until this is honoured'. ★ FALSE. ALL FOUR CORPUS EXCLUSION TARGETS ARE ALREADY INERT AT HEAD, EACH FOR ITS OWN UNRELATED REASON:
  · `host-to-users` — lib/compat/builtins.nix:417 is literally `host-to-users = _ctx: [ ];`. INERT BY DEFINITION, and :17-20 says so verbatim: den-hoag resolves host→user STRUCTURALLY, and 'this inert never-emitting definition only satisfies the exclude reference (a genuine no-op)'. PINNED by ci/tests/compat-builtins.nix:83-88.
  · `system-to-os-outputs` / `system-to-hm-outputs` — builtins.nix:425-426, throwing stubs carrying v1's own `{ system, ... }` formals, so they fire ONLY where a `system` coordinate is bound, i.e. flake-system nodes, WHICH THE CORPUS NEVER SPAWNS (builtins.nix:36-40).
  · `packages-to-flake` (den-configs slashfiles) — NOT PROVISIONED AT ALL, absent from the policies set at builtins.nix:416-427. POSITIVE CONTROL, same grep same run: the predicate DID match `system-to-flake-parts` at :427 and `host-to-users` at :417. So this is a missing-attribute read in the consumer's own module eval — A SEPARATE C1 GAP, not this defect.
⇒ THE FLEET IS NOT SILENTLY GETTING POLICIES IT EXCLUDED. I inferred that from the surface being inert and did not check whether the TARGETS were live. A surface that does nothing and a target that does nothing produce the same observable, and I reported the wrong cause.

★ THE DEFECT REMAINS P0 ON A STRONGER ARGUMENT, WHICH IS §1.2 OF THE SPEC: the surface is inert, and each corpus exclusion is SEPARATELY COMPENSATED BY A PER-NAME PROVISIONING DECISION. THAT IS A REPAIR, NOT A CONSTRUCTION. `host-to-users` is inert BECAUSE THE CORPUS EXCLUDES IT — the compensation was chosen to match today's exclusions. The day a fleet that does NOT exclude it needs v1's default host→user policy, provisioning must go live, AND EVERY EXISTING EXCLUSION SILENTLY STOPS WORKING. Same bug, re-armed, at the moment someone is changing something else. Honouring the declaration removes the coupling entirely.
That argument is better than mine because it does not depend on the corpus's current shape — which is exactly the property the north-star ruling asks for.

★ AND ON THE OWNER'S RULING — CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, REFINED IN NAME. The owner ruled 'excludes IS includes' dual, but it only applies to its subtree'. The SUBTREE SCOPING IS CONFIRMED against v1. But the qualifier IS the asymmetry: `includes` fires AT K-NODES ONLY — compile.nix:1701-1706's `__firesAtKinds = [kind]` exists PRECISELY so a descendant inheriting K's coordinate does NOT fire it — while schema-tier `excludes` applies at K AND ALL DESCENDANTS (v1 constraint.nix:63-67: they 'register at the resolved KIND scope and reach descendants via the ancestor walk'). A dual has ONE extent.
SECOND ASYMMETRY, not in the ruling and not in my brief: IDENTITY GRAIN. `includes` refs are dereferenced to FULL ASPECT RECORDS via `resolveAspectRef`; `excludes` refs are REDUCED TO A NAME and never dereferenced — ci/tests/compat-builtins.nix:205-206 observes exactly that. Generative versus suppressive.
⇒ ONLY `includes` LANDED BECAUSE ONLY `includes` MINTS SOMETHING, and the arm-builder machinery is shaped around the mint. That is the answer to 'why was the pair split' and it is a better answer than 'someone forgot'.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
DESIGN WRITTEN — /home/sini/Documents/papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-28-kind-schema-excludes-design.md, 598 lines, md5 8f22b9eee8efe1cb80d1c933a4f63457. Core 5eb5375d6f6f44211d86b2762e1c2fb2, 84 lines, contiguous, with a marker-derived recipe printed in the document and BOTH controls verified — perturb inside → 73a5e080…, MOVES; append outside → unchanged, HOLDS (and held again across two later prose edits).

THE RULING: exclusion is a NAME-KEYED GATE ON POLICY DISPATCH, CLOSED OVER THE DECLARING KIND'S SCOPE SUBTREE, evaluated BEFORE the policy body runs — so effects are NEVER PRODUCED rather than produced-then-removed. Not edge removal, not set subtraction. Traced through v1 at pin cdc95ce: resolve-entity.nix:22 → children.nix:157-179 (`excludeIdentity`: `__isPolicy` ⇒ `ref.name`) → constraint.nix:112-161 registry → TWO readers, dispatch-policies.nix:30-31 filtering the policy attrset BY NAME and constraint.nix:163-202 checking by aspect IDENTITY, prefix-closed.
★ AND ROUTE-INDEPENDENCE IS DECIDABLE ON THE CORPUS RATHER THAN HYPOTHETICAL: v1 wires `host-to-users` BOTH as `den.schema.host.includes` (core.nix:33) AND as `den.policies.host-to-users` (core.nix:17), and nix-config excludes it ONCE. Subtraction kills one route; edge-removal kills one edge; a name-keyed dispatch gate kills BOTH inside the subtree and NEITHER outside. v1 behaves as the third. The corpus already distinguishes the readings.

★★ THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS — THIS IS A FEED, NOT A MECHANISM. The suppression chain is shipped end to end: `declare.suppress` (declarations.nix:49,263) → pre-pass `suppressions` (staged-resolution.nix:430-436) → root decls `suppressedPolicies` (default.nix:1221-1222) → the `suppressed-policies` inherited attribute, gen-scope inheritSet self∪ancestors (structural.nix:131-141) → ctx-injected at dispatch (:338-340) → `gateSuppression` fires the rule as `[ ]` (compile.nix:107-115).
AND `gateSuppression` IS ALREADY APPLIED AT BOTH ROUTES KEYED ON THE SAME v1 NAME — compile.nix:1141 (top-level `den.policies.<n>`) and :1720 (`__kindInclude__<K>__policy__<i>`). ⇒ ROUTE-INDEPENDENCE ALREADY HOLDS BY CONSTRUCTION. ONLY THE SET IS EMPTY.
TWO BREAKS, BOTH BRIDGE-SIDE: (1) bridge.nix:609-612 `rawForShim = { parent; includes; }` — `excludes` IS DROPPED BEFORE THE SHIM EVER SEES IT (positive control on the same record, same expression: `includes` IS carried at :611 and IS honoured). (2) bridge.nix:490 declares `collections.includes.default = [ ]` and nothing for excludes, so a multi-module `.excludes` would hit the list-conflict :461-469 explains — note :543-553 ALREADY lists `excludes` in `schemaCollectionKeys`, so the stripping half is present and the merging half absent.

★ THE CONSUMER SITE, chosen by construction rather than convenience: `structural.nix:139`'s `extract`. It is the ONE function mapping node → suppression contribution, `inheritSet` ALREADY calls it at every node it already visits, and `node.type` IS the kind:
  `extract = node: (kindSuppressions.${node.type} or [ ]) ++ (node.decls.suppressedPolicies or [ ]);`
Total over every node of the kind BY CONSTRUCTION — INCLUDING MINTING PATHS THAT DO NOT EXIST YET. No site can forget. Rejected alternatives with reasons: NOT the pre-pass (roots-only; `den.schema.user.excludes` names a CELL kind, so root injection silently does nothing — indistinguishable from today's bug); NOT per-node decls injection (≥3 minting sites — baseScopeRoots, attachment multiplication default.nix:1178-1184, fleetChildren :1229 — an invariant someone must maintain).
Crosses on the ESTABLISHED seam: a kernel option `den.kindSuppressions` (kind→[name], default `{ }`) written by the compat flake-module — the exact pattern of `den.excludeFamilyNames` (default.nix:968-974 / flake-module.nix:552). The kernel learns no v1 vocabulary; it gains the TYPE-keyed sibling of the ID-keyed `suppressions` it already folds.

ASPECT-VALUED kind excludes → NAMED ABORT, ruled not deferred. Corpus census ZERO across 19 configs + nix-config + templates; POSITIVE CONTROL same run — the same predicate DID find aspect-LEVEL `den.aspects.iceberg.excludes = [den.aspects.test]` in v1 templates. v1 supports them via a node-identity prefix-closed predicate; den-hoag has NO node-scoped aspect-drop carrier (`meta.drop` is a property of an ASPECT, not of a scope), and building one is THE SAME QUESTION AS THE CLASS-CONTENT REPRESENTATION QUESTION and must be answered with it. Bare-fn targets also abort — strictly better than v1, which reaches `identity.key` on a lambda and throws untyped.
★ AND A SHIPPED TEST PINS THE DEFECT AS INTENDED BEHAVIOUR: ci/tests/compat-builtins.nix:204-222 `test-schema-policy-valued-exclude-noop` asserts `excludes = [ (_ctx: [ ]) ]` compiles, commented 'so a policy-valued exclude is a no-op; the fleet compiles'. A bare fn is nameless and must now ABORT, so THAT TEST MUST BE RE-EXPRESSED — the implementer needs this or the change reads as a regression.

C9 SELF-CHECK, reasoned per item. ★ ITEM 3 IS A HIT AND IS THE ONE THE DESIGN IS MOST EXPOSED TO: the EXISTING suppression feed IS produced by the retiring pre-pass, and the obvious implementation extends it. THEORY survives (a name-keyed subtree gate says nothing about scheduling). MECHANISM survives AND MOVES OFF — §4.1 rules the pre-pass out on its own merits and §4.3 lands in a demand-driven attribute, the successor idiom the register itself names. ARGUMENT survives: the precedents are v1's dispatch-policies.nix:30-31 and den-hoag's own `gateSuppression`, none of them the staged schedule. ★ AND IT EXPLICITLY DOES NOT EXTEND lib/errors.nix:61-63 `excludeFamilyUntagged`, WHOSE ERROR TEXT READS 'the STAGED PRE-PASS's exclude-family feed' — THAT IS EXACTLY HOW REGISTER HIT 2 HID. Item 4 is a hit BY ADJACENCY and moves TOWARD the goal: no decls key added, no strip list grows, and suppression becomes derived from graph position (`node.type`) rather than cached as decls payload.
COMPLEXITY: build O(|kinds|), identical to `kindIncludesOf`; read ONE attrset lookup and ONE list concat added to an extract the walk already calls at every node it already visits — no new traversal, no new memo, walk shape unchanged; consult `builtins.elem` growing by ≤2. With the option unset, `[ ] ++ xs == xs` gives an IDENTICAL VALUE AT EVERY NODE — byte-identical BY EXPRESSION, not by measurement. No superlinear term.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THE WRITTEN DESIGN DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH den-hoag-9xo.53 — and the failure is in its ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, not its prose. Measured by the policy-domain investigation, 2026-07-28.

specs/2026-07-28-kind-schema-excludes-design.md ROUTES THE NEGATIVE ARM INTO `gateSuppression` (compile.nix:107-115), which rewrites a compiled rule's `fn` to return `[ ]`. ★ THE RULE IS STILL MINTED AND STILL DISPATCHED — so 9xo.53 (policies applied outside every `includes`) IS UNTOUCHED BY CONSTRUCTION. The design would make an excluded policy emit nothing while leaving 241 firings of a policy nothing ever selected.
★ AND ITS §7.2 ARM `d_exclOnly` ASSERTS THE DEFECT AS A PASSING PROPERTY: it declares `den.policies.mark` with NO kind-include and requires the marker 'PRESENT at a non-host root'. Under the policy-domain equation `I(π) = ∅ ⇒ dom(π) = ∅`, that leg GOES RED. The two designs cannot both be right about that fixture; §7.2/d must be re-expressed.

⇒ THIS BEAD'S SEMANTICS ARE UNCHANGED — the owner's ruling stands: `excludes` is `includes`' dual, scoped to the declaring kind's subtree. WHAT CHANGES IS THE MECHANISM. The successor design derives both arms from ONE equation, `dom(π) = closure₀(I(π)) \ closure*(E(π))`, where the positive and negative arms differ in exactly one parameter — the propagation exponent — and BOTH VALUES ARE READ OFF v1 RATHER THAN CHOSEN. Recorded at den-hoag-9xo.54.
WHAT OF THE EXCLUDES DESIGN SURVIVES AND IS CREDITED: the corpus census (kind-level exclusions all policy-valued, aspect-valued ZERO, with the aspect-level positive control), the name-keyed identity grain, the aspect-arm named abort, and its §1.2 correction that all four corpus exclusion targets are ALREADY INERT for their own reasons — ★ which the 241-firings measurement independently confirms and sharpens: `host-to-users` fires 241 times and emits nothing, so its inertness is a property of its BODY, not of any exclusion being honoured.

comments.text:
★★★ THE HEADLINE OF THIS BEAD IS FALSE AT HEAD. Retitled. Measured 2026-07-29, and INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR rather than accepted from the finder.

THE CLAIM: 'den.schema.<kind>.excludes is INERT — the corpus declares exclusions nothing consumes.' Measured when this bead was filed, at ab1112a.
THE MEASUREMENT NOW, same predicate at two revs — one matches, the other does not, which is the control:
    git grep -n 'kindExcludesOf' c42df53 -- lib  ->  0

      lib/compat/ingest.nix:789  kindExcludes = kindExcludesOf v1Schema;
