  1. "does the corpus first-run green or abort?" -> NEITHER. den-hoag does not
     abort on multi-attachment, it MULTIPLIES THE NODE (build-roots.nix:13-28,
     wired default.nix:1136-1143). Two claimants fail SILENTLY.
  2. the abort MECHANISM is unreachable: grep -rn buildNodes lib/ = 0 hits,
     against controls buildRoots 19 / attachmentsOf 3. den-hoag never calls
     gen-scope's partial-function check, so nothing enforces P-as-a-partial-
     function at all.
  3. the bijection objection UNDER-states the code: entity->node is already 1:N
     and entryNodeIndex already yields a list (default.nix:1210-1214, verbatim).

DELIVERED INSTEAD: the default-attachment design, 9 revisions through 6
independent review rounds to SHIP-WITH-NITS, and ROUTE 2 SHIPPED at 0d6174c --
`den.attach.<kind> = { ref; unless ? null; }`, native attachment from declared
kind parentage, opt-in and inert on the corpus.
  design papers plans/2026-07-27-default-attachment-design.md (rev 9)
  reviews papers 64aaed1 / b9d2d6b / 375c0e5 / 81fbfe5 / bc7981c

Superseded/relocated:
  - the A/B branch fork -> DEAD. The default chain is HEAD-LESS: flake-to-systems
    fires at flake nodes, there are none, so system-to-os-outputs never fires.
    Both branches argued about an edge to a node nobody constructs.
  - route 1 / A-prime -> DEAD. den.schema.<kind>.excludes is INERT (measured
    twice independently, no consumer under any policy name) -> den-hoag-9xo.28.
  - half (1) activation -> blocked, tracked on den-hoag-9xo.9 and .30.

★ AND THE TOPOLOGY MAP CORRECTS THE PREMISE UNDER ALL OF IT (papers 9eb5439):
`flake` having ZERO instances is v1's OWN BEHAVIOUR in 12/12 configs -- the
flake entity is the root of resolution and is excluded from the topology by
construction (capture.nix:105 + fleet-ir.nix:91). den-hoag MATCHES v1 there.
The head-less finding was factually right and was read as a den-hoag divergence
when it is not one. The real divergence is flake-system -> den-hoag-9xo.31.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ MEASURED 2026-07-27 — THE ROOT KIND IS DECLARED AND HAS ZERO INSTANCES.
This is the precise statement of why nothing downstream can be gated on
reaching it, and it is sharper than "there is no root".

  declaredKinds  [cluster environment flake flake-parts flake-system fleet
                  group hm-host host user]
  registryKinds  [same -- all ten resolve]
  registrySizes  flake 0   fleet 0   flake-parts 0   flake-system 0   hm-host 0
                 environment 2   cluster 1   host 10   group 34   user 1

flake and fleet are DECLARED, are KNOWN to the registry, and have NO INSTANCES.
So the head of the corpus's flake -> fleet -> env -> host chain never becomes a
scope node. Root enumeration on the corpus shows only environment:dev,
environment:prod and 36 parentless group:*. There is no flake: node and no
fleet: node. Structural -- v1's flake/fleet are SINGLETONS that never became
registry instances -- not an oversight.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY "MATERIALISE IFF REACHABLE" RULE: it has no starting node.
Under the only available reading (parentless => root), cortex-cuda is ITSELF a
root, is trivially reachable, and materialises -- so the rule excludes NOTHING.
Not merely unimplementable: VACUOUS. (Orchestrator ruled reachability and
withdrew it on this measurement.)

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SCHEMA-PARENT ALTERNATIVE (a kind whose schema declares a
parent materialises iff it actually attached; a kind with no declared parent is
a root): EXACT on the corpus -- environments and groups are roots, 9 hosts +
cluster:axon declare environment and have it, cortex-cuda declares environment
and has none so it is excluded FOR THE RIGHT REASON. But measured kernel-side
with no policy (schema.env.parent = null, schema.host.parent = "env", one env
instance, two hosts):

  roots:   env:e1 -> null,  host:attached -> null,  host:orphan -> null
  emitted: ["attached","orphan"]

NEITHER HOST ATTACHES. Declaring kind parentage attaches nothing -- attachment
comes ONLY from policy-emitted containTo/resolve.to members. So the rule
empties a kernel-native fleet.

★ BOTH FORMULATIONS FAIL FOR ONE REASON, AND IT IS WHAT .13 MUST SETTLE:
den-hoag HAS NO POLICY-FREE ATTACHMENT. Every "materialise iff
reachable/attached" rule needs an attachment den-hoag cannot produce without a
corpus-style policy. Until .13 supplies EITHER a root instance for flake/fleet
OR native attachment for declared-parent kinds, no intrinsic predicate
separates "activated" from "merely declared".

⇒ .13 BLOCKS den-hoag-9xo.9 half (1). The orchestrator earlier stated .13 was
not a blocker for activation; that was wrong, twice asserted and twice
measured against.

INTERIM (ruled): .9 half (1) stays blocked. The intoAttr placement gate
(ab1112a) STAYS -- subsumption cannot be proven because no replacement rule is
statable, and it is NOT activation and must not be labelled as one.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — THIS BEAD'S BIJECTION OBJECTION IS STALE.

The bead says: "default.nix:1140 entryNodeIndex (KEYED ONE-PER-id_hash => a
multi-attached host is N nodes the index can hold only one of -- structural,
not cosmetic)".

That no longer describes the code. The node-multiplication arc
(84fc117..fc29920) fixed it, and the bead's line numbers predate that arc.

At ab1112a, lib/default.nix:1210-1214 reads VERBATIM:

  # linked-context. Entity -> node is one-to-MANY: a multi-attached root mints
  # one node per attachment, so this yields a LIST and the id rule is the same
  # `mintedRootId` `buildRoots` mints with -- one owner, so the index cannot
  # name a node that was never built. The index is over the entity registries
  # (not scope nodes), so this stays demand-safe.

So entity->node is ALREADY 1:N and the index ALREADY yields a list. "The index
can hold only one of N" is not a live objection.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS (per the design, papers 16f09d9): seven sites still
CONSTRUCT the bare "${kind}:${name}" form. Those need CLASSIFICATION -- which
of them legitimately name a single-attachment entity and which assume 1:1 --
NOT suffix generation. The design lists them with line numbers.

Verification status: the comment above is quoted from the tree at ab1112a and
is direct evidence. Whether every consumer of entryNodeIndex handles the list
shape is being checked independently (design-reviewer, challenge 3). If the
reviewer finds a consumer that still assumes a single node, this correction
narrows to "the index is 1:N but a consumer is not" -- which would be a
different and smaller objection than the bead's.

Recorded so the design is not reviewed against an objection the code already
answered, and so nobody re-derives the 1:1 concern from this bead's text.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ SECOND STALE WARNING IN THIS BEAD, opposite direction to the bijection one.

This bead says (c) "=> both emit host:axon-01 with different to =
build-nodes.nix:61's exact ABORT condition" and its VERDICT records "the corpus
ABORTS at first run -- same id, two parents".

That is stale. den-hoag does not abort on multi-attachment -- it MULTIPLIES THE
NODE (build-roots.nix:13-28, wired at default.nix:1136-1143), which is exactly
what the node-multiplication arc shipped.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is worse than the abort would have been: two claimants do
not fail loudly. Every host id changes and the DOUBLE-CONTRIBUTION shape
returns for nine hosts at once -- den-hoag-ljr, deliberately, fleet-wide. A
loud abort would have been a better outcome than a silent fleet-wide
remultiplication.

So this bead now carries TWO stale warnings pointing opposite ways:
  - the bijection objection UNDER-states the code (entity->node is already 1:N;
    entryNodeIndex already yields a list -- see the earlier correction)
  - the abort warning OVER-states the failure (no abort; silent multiplication)

Both predate the node-multiplication arc (84fc117..fc29920). Anyone planning
from this bead's original text is planning against a tree that no longer
exists. The design at papers plans/2026-07-27-default-attachment-design.md
rev 3 supersedes both; its independent review is at papers 64aaed1.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ THIRD CORRECTION, and it is the strongest: THE ABORT CHECK IS NEVER CALLED.

This bead's settling test and verdict both turn on gen-scope
build-nodes.nix:61 -- the partial-function check that "throws on >1 parent
edge". The earlier correction on this bead said the abort warning was STALE
because den-hoag multiplies the node instead of aborting. That was right but
understated.

MEASURED (orchestrator, 2026-07-27, with a positive control in the same run):

  grep -rn buildNodes     lib/ --include='*.nix'   ->  0 hits
  grep -rn buildRoots     lib/ --include='*.nix'   -> 19 hits
  grep -rn attachmentsOf  lib/ --include='*.nix'   ->  3 hits

The control matters: the same predicate over the same tree finds buildRoots 19
times and attachmentsOf 3 times, so the zero is a REAL NEGATIVE and not a dead
probe. (My first control attempt was weak -- it matched comments -- and I
retried with terms known to be called. Recording that because a weak control is
how a false clean gets certified.)

⇒ den-hoag NEVER CALLS gen-scope's buildNodes. The check is dead code from this
repo's side, so NOTHING ENFORCES P-AS-A-PARTIAL-FUNCTION here.

CONSEQUENCE, and it changes what any .13 design must guard: a derivation bug in
the attachment map is a SILENTLY WRONG GRAPH, not an abort. There is no loud
failure waiting to catch it. That is why the rev-4 design promotes the
containmentAttachments diff to the FIRST instrument -- every other probe
observes OUTPUTS, and dedup can render an attachment-map error output-invisible.

So this bead now carries THREE stale claims, all predating the
node-multiplication arc (84fc117..fc29920), pointing in three directions:
  1. the bijection objection UNDER-states the code (entity->node is already
     1:N; entryNodeIndex already yields a list)
  2. the abort warning OVER-states the failure (no abort -- silent node
     multiplication)
  3. the abort MECHANISM is not reachable at all (buildNodes never called)

Anyone planning from this bead's original text is planning against a tree that
does not exist. Authority: papers plans/2026-07-27-default-attachment-design.md
rev 4 (papers 0c927d7) and its reviews at papers 64aaed1 / b9d2d6b.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ MUST LAND IN THE DESIGN BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION (rev 9, one paragraph in §2.1).
Found by denhoag-writer while locating the seam, 2026-07-27. NOT yet in rev 8.

ROUTE 2'S TWO NEW FIELDS DO NOT SURVIVE KIND-VALUE PROCESSING.

Declared and read back:

  den.schema.host = { parent = "env"; parentRef = "environment";
                      attachIf = "intoAttr"; }

  processed kind value keys:
    [__functor keySemantics kind methods mixins options parent refinements
     refs strict validators]

parentRef and attachIf are SILENTLY DROPPED -- accepted without abort, absent
from the processed value. An implementation reading them off den.schema.<kind>
gets null for every kind, attaches nothing, AND LOOKS LIKE THE CODE IS WRONG.

FIX, and it needs no gen-schema change: read them from the RAW declarations,
which den-hoag holds. registryKindsOf already does exactly this for exactly
this reason -- lib/compat/ingest.nix, "reads the RAW v1 declarations only".

WHY IT IS DESIGN-LEVEL, NOT IMPLEMENTATION-LEVEL: rev 8 §2.1 reads as though
the two fields are ordinary kind declarations. They are not. This is precisely
the class of unstated assumption that rounds 4, 5 and 6 of review were spent
removing -- a test that could not run, a safety property never named, a
default never specified. Discovering it in an implementation review is the
expensive path.

--- SEAM, located precisely (also for rev 9) ---

Route 2's emissions go into containmentEmissions
(lib/staged-resolution.nix:247-250), UPSTREAM of byTarget (:255) -- so they
reach all five products, which is what §2.3's coverage disqualifier requires.

Record shape fixed by containmentOf (:200-230):
  { tid; bindings; sourceSlice }
  sourceSlice = { <parentKind> = <parentEntry>; }
  tid = index.${entry.id_hash}

runPrePass already takes registries and kindParent, so the new input is narrow
-- a per-kind { parentRef; attachIf; } map. And containmentOf's existing slice
check already validates that the source kind equals kindParent, so A SYNTHETIC
EMISSION IS VALIDATED BY THE SAME RULE AS A POLICY ONE.

--- BASELINE, re-measured on the worktree rather than carried over ---

Fleet: schema.env.parent = null, schema.host.parent = "env", a real env:e1,
two hosts.

  scopeRoots  env:e1 -> null,  host:a -> null,  host:b -> null
  nixos       ["a","b"]

Neither host attaches though the parent KIND is declared and its INSTANCE
exists. That is the gap route 2 fills.

--- STATE ---

.worktrees/route2 on branch route2 from ab1112a. NO commits. Main untouched at
ab1112a. Nothing to clean up beyond removing the worktree if a fresh writer
prefers its own.

title: PLAN: derive the topology-wiring implementation plan from the final design
description:
writing-plans cycle over the FINAL design (papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-26-topology-wiring-design.md), then an INDEPENDENT plan review before any code (feedback_review_plan_before_execution).

Plan must carry, per owner ruling: PRUNE-not-paper-over (every prune verifiable as gone BY NAME, per the tightened §8.5 — reductions are exempt from byte-green, NOT from named-absence); kernel wiring capability vs compat policy definition kept on their own sides; (c) as the topology shape.

GATE per rung: nix build ./ci#checks.x86_64-linux.default AND ./parity#checks.x86_64-linux.default AND ship-gate allEqual — SEEN exit=0 empirically, never masked by a pipe (PIPESTATUS is clobbered by an intervening echo; capture $? directly). Behavior-changing rungs shift the structural graph => re-derive goldens per the parity-structural.nix convergence-bump contract; guardrail = ONLY the intended edge changes. Two §8.2 ledger rows need NAMED EXPECTED DELTAS: accessGroups (which users newly materialize per host) and collectedMembersOf (intermediate-ancestor buckets v1 does not read).
notes:
★★ DISCOVERY (owner-directed: relationship must NOT be coupled to rendering/materialization). The attachment mechanism IS ALREADY BUILT and merely wired to the wrong consumer. Orchestrator re-verified the two decisive claims.

(1) THE P EDGE ALREADY EXISTS: the `containTo` containment member.
- Surface: declare.member { coords; bindings ? {}; containTo ? null } (lib/declarations.nix:198-200).
- v1 mapping: `resolve.to <registry-backed root kind>` -> containment member (lib/compat/compile.nix:963-984).
- Producer: runPrePass containmentOf (staged-resolution.nix:178-192) -> byTarget groupBy (:204) -> **containmentAncestors (:220-222) = targetNodeId -> [ sourceSlice ]** — keyed by the CHILD (contained root), valued by the PARENT coordinate. VERIFIED verbatim; its own comment even handles the parentless case ("A parentless-root target's emission has an empty source slice, contributing no ancestor").
- Target id ALREADY uses buildRoots' convention ("${kind}:${name}", rootNodeIndex :70-81 == build-roots.nix:21); parent node id derivable via ancNodeId (resolved-settings.nix:115-120).
- TODAY it is threaded ONLY to the settings fold (default.nix:1295 containmentRelations -> containEdges/expandPreorder). The design's §0.4 item 3 called it "a parent POINTER reified as side data" — correct, and it is the shipped attachment primitive thrown at settings instead of at buildRoots.
- CI witnesses exist: ci/tests/topology-join.nix (env<-host<-user + sibling env<-cluster), staged-resolution.nix, settings-witness.nix.

(2) gen-scope buildNodes is NOT REQUIRED for this. VERIFIED gen-scope/lib/eval.nix:53-56 resolveNode: `if roots ? ${id} then roots.${id}` — the root descriptor is returned VERBATIM, so its `parent` field is honored by every ancestor walk / inheritAll / inheritSet. Setting `parent` in build-roots.nix:27 is sufficient. => the design's §1 buildNodes/parentGraph apparatus is OPTIONAL for rung 1 (may still be right long-term; it is not needed to make the corpus chain real). This SHRINKS the rung enormously.

(3) ★ THE DECOUPLING THE OWNER ASKED FOR ALREADY HOLDS. The terminal content path is BYTE-UNCHANGED by root parentage: reach (resolved-aspects.nix:380), classSubtreeAt (output-modules.nix:192-200) and parentTargetedRoutesAt (:387-399) all read `scope.descendants` = the `children` NTA, and fleetChildren (default.nix:1105-1123) spawns CELLS ONLY, so root parentage never enters childrenOf/descendants. Relationship and rendering are already separate graphs — which is exactly why the topology rung is safe to land alone.
CAVEAT on gen-edge: it is the shipped gen L2 library (Class B, Law E13 "reads a finished graph through accessors and never demands resolution") and den-hoag supplies its accessor at output-modules.nix:781-823 — BUT (a) gen-edge NEVER CALLS parentOf (exhaustive grep: only isolatedAt/childrenOf/nodes are used; parentOf is dead contract surface), and (b) the HOST BUILD does not go through gen-edge at all (systems.<class>.<member> :1146-1185 -> projectClass over reach). gen-edge's outputFor/traceFor feed only den.graph.edges/trace, the v1 resolve-verb shim, and the parity oracle. So the seam is clean but NOT on the host path.

(4) DEFERRAL CONFIRMED, BOTH HALVES. (a) corpus declares its own attachers (fleet.nix to-fleet/fleet-to-envs/env-to-hosts, schema-wired :80-82) — no default needed. CAVEAT: only env->host is live today (flake:0 / flake-system:0 means to-fleet never fires and fleet-to-envs has no fleet root), but environment IS registry-backed so env-to-hosts produces a genuine containment member. (b) ship-gate fixture (parity/ship-gate.nix:35-39, single host + one aspect, NO policies) => policiesRules.resolveFamily = [] => pre-pass INERT (staged-resolution.nix:108) => containmentAncestors = {} => host stays parentless => today's behavior, GREEN. Named CI case already exists: ci/tests/topology-join.nix:198 "(D) NO containment tuples ... the native identity path".
=> THE DEFAULT-ATTACHMENT FORK (Branch A/B) IS DEFERRABLE TO A LATER RUNG. Not decided now.

MINIMAL RUNG (scout-proposed, orchestrator-endorsed):
 1. staged-resolution.nix — no behavior change; optionally surface containmentParents (targetNodeId -> parent node id) beside containmentAncestors so the ancNodeId convention is not duplicated.
 2. build-roots.nix:12-37 — buildRoots takes `parents ? { }`; :27 becomes `parent = parents.${id} or null`.
 3. default.nix:1057-1060 — baseScopeRoots = buildRoots { ...; parents = <from prePass>; }. NO NEW CYCLE: baseScopeRoots (:1057) is already downstream of prePass (:984); prePassScopeRoots (:970) stays parent-null so the §0.5 staging constraint is untouched. Multi-parent: containmentAncestors.<nid> is a LIST and gen-scope requires <=1 parent — take head + ABORT LOUD on >1.
 4. ★ THE ONE COUPLING THAT BLOCKS THE RUNG — structural.nix:279 isMembershipDerived = parent != null -> :298 errors.memberAtCell. A parented environment root firing env-to-hosts ABORTS. Must be replaced IN THE SAME RUNG. The honest predicate is ALREADY SHIPPED: cell ids carry `@` (user:<n>@host:<h>) and root ids do not, so `parseParent id != null` (build-roots.nix:39-46) is exact; `!(scopeRoots ? id)` equivalently.
 5. Same rung — resolved-settings.nix:248 ancSlices branch: with real parentage a host takes the else branch and reads its ENVIRONMENT's ancestors instead of its own, dropping the env slice.

DELIBERATELY OUT (each inert, with reason): scope.descendants consumers (children NTA, untouched); deliveryTargetRootOf (:279-287, fires only for appendToParent; corpus's only one is the hm-user-detect route at CELLS whose parent stays the host); default.nix:165 hostId (home-manager-PRODUCING nodes are user cells in compat, never roots).
MUST DECIDE EXPLICITLY IN THE RUNG: graphAccessor.isolatedAt (output-modules.nix:785) INVERTS the moment roots gain parents. It does not touch the host build but DOES change den.graph.trace, compat/resolve-verbs.nix:54,74 and parity/oracle.nix:442,498,581. Settling test: run the parity oracle + den.graph.trace goldens with parentage on.

UNVERIFIED (flagged by scout): corpus registrySizes not re-measured this pass (taken from design §0.3 — but orchestrator DID measure it earlier: environment:0/cluster:0/fleet:0/flake:0/flake-system:0/host:10/group:34, consistent); gather.nix:370,373-376 not opened (compat-only, off the native materialization path); whether any home-manager-producing ROOT exists (inferred from ingest, not measured).
close_reason: Plan delivered and executed. Rung 1 T1.0-T1.5 shipped (f18f7c9, 8bc5202, 91b2d74, 273f916); T1.6's pivot failed as specified, producing the node-multiplication arc that superseded it (.19, 8 commits to fc29920). Frozen at md5 1b486033 as the design record; Phase-0 tasks refreshed in the rung-2 plan. NOTE: .13 (default-attachment fork) was wired as a blocker early and never actually gated this — the corpus declares its own attachers, so rung 1 needed no default. Edge removed; .13 remains open and deferred on its own merits.

title: DESIGN: kernel wiring capability + compat policy definition; default topology host->flake
description:
OWNER-RATIFIED DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (2026-07-26) for the topology fix (den-hoag-9xo.10). These are requirements, not options.

1. PRUNE, DO NOT PAPER OVER. This is a v0 launch — incorrect code gets DELETED, not wrapped. The design MUST name exactly what DIES, not merely what is added. Candidates: build-roots.nix registry-enumeration + the `parent = null` hardcode (:27); the structural pre-classification (default.nix:943-1018 candidateKinds/cellKinds/rootScopeKinds) IF subsumed by declared strata; runPrePass fire-to-observe (:984-996) IF deriveGroup discharges the stratum statically. A design that leaves these in place alongside a new path is REJECTED.

2. DEFAULT TOPOLOGY FOR UNCONFIGURED den v1: **host -> flake direct inclusion is the DEFAULT.** With no fleet policies declared, hosts attach DIRECTLY under the flake root. The corpuss flake->fleet->environment->host chain is then just what its own declared policies (to-fleet / fleet-to-envs / env-to-hosts) build ON TOP of that default — not a special case.

3. ★ KERNEL ⟂ COMPAT SEPARATION (the load-bearing rule):
   - **KERNEL owns the WIRING CAPABILITY** — consuming P edges into scope parentage (gen-scope buildNodes { parentGraph }), the stratum schedule (gen-resolve strataOrder / attr with declared readsAttrs+stratum), mid-fold spawning (children/derived-children NTA). NO v1 policy semantics in the kernel.
   - **COMPAT owns the POLICY DEFINITION** — the default host->flake rule AND the translation of v1 policy declarations into P-edge emissions. Value-shape/v1-dialect concerns stay at the compat boundary, never in the kernel (project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface).

4. NO NEW GEN PRIMITIVE (verdict on den-hoag-9xo.10, independently verified). The composition is gen-scope buildNodes + children/derived-children NTA + gen-resolve strataOrder/attr + gen-dispatch deriveGroup. gen-scopes P-edge parentage is BUILT AND UNUSED by den-hoag today (zero hits for buildNodes/parentGraph/edgeGraphs).

5. THE CYCLE must be answered, not routed around: kill fire-to-observe at its source via deriveGroups definition-time stratum discharge; order strata with strataOrder. Document the trackedAttrs / non-base-stratum-children unknown (gen-resolve override.nix:26 assumes children is base-stratum; untested) and how the design avoids or settles it.

6. CARRY FORWARD the verified isolation consequence: den-hoag output-modules.nix:785 isolatedAt = parent != null, so parenting fleet/env/host makes each its own edge-root and content-fold semantics are PRESERVED. The design must state this explicitly so no reviewer re-litigates it.

GATE for the eventual implementation: ci + parity + ship-gate allEqual, SEEN exit=0 empirically. Behavior-changing => structural graph shifts => re-derive goldens per the parity-structural.nix convergence-bump contract, guardrail ONLY-intended-edge-changes.

Deliverable: a written design in papers/den-architecture/, INDEPENDENTLY REVIEWED before any code is written (feedback_review_plan_before_execution, feedback_no_half_measures).
notes:
§3.2 CLOSED by orchestrator (scout idled twice without doing it; read was bounded so I did it directly). Design doc updated in place at papers/specs/2026-07-26-topology-wiring-design.md §3.2 + §7.3.

★ THE OWNER'S STATED DEFAULT IS CORRECTED. den v1's unconfigured attachment is NOT 'host -> flake direct'. VERIFIED via git show 11866c16:modules/policies/{flake,core}.nix at /home/sini/Documents/repos/denful/den (the checkout DOES exist; the scout probed ~/Documents/repos/den, which does not, and wrongly reported the source absent).

DEN V1 DEFAULT = FOUR LEVELS: flake -> flake-system -> host -> user
- den.policies.flake-to-systems (schema.flake.includes): _: map (system: resolve.to "flake-system" { inherit system; }) den.systems
- den.policies.system-to-os-outputs (schema.flake-system.includes): walks den.hosts.${system}, per host with intoAttr != [] emits BOTH resolve.to "host" AND den.lib.policy.instantiate host
- den.policies.system-to-hm-outputs: same shape for den.homes.${system} -> home
- den.policies.host-to-users (schema.host.includes, core.nix:17,33): the fourth level

CONSEQUENCES:
1. §3's producer must model flake-system as a REAL node level, not collapse to host->flake. Default P edges are flake-system:<system> -> flake:<name> and host:<name> -> flake-system:<system>. Hosts are keyed PER-SYSTEM in v1 (den.hosts.${system}.${hostName}) — the system coordinate is load-bearing.
2. 'WHOEVER ATTACHES, INSTANTIATES' is an INVARIANT of both topologies — instantiate is co-located with the attaching policy in the v1 default (system-to-os-outputs) and in the corpus (env-to-hosts, fleet.nix:74). Independent evidence for den-hoag-9xo.9: instantiation rides the attachment edge, it is not a separable concern that could be left ungated.
3. The corpus DISPLACES the default exactly as the design read it: fleet.nix:85-91 excludes system-to-os-outputs + system-to-hm-outputs from flake-system AND host-to-users from host, then substitutes flake->fleet->environment->host. Displacement, never absence. CONFIRMED.

AND den-hoag PROVISIONS NONE OF IT: builtins.nix:38 verbatim 'the flake -> flake-system fan-out flake-to-systems is NOT provisioned; hosts arrive via the nixos class terminal', corroborated by the measured registrySizes flake:0 / flake-system:0. There is not even a flake root node today — nothing for a host to attach TO. The entire default chain is absent, not subtly mis-wired.
★ OWNER COUNTER-EXAMPLE — option (b) (collapse flake-system, host->flake direct) is REFUTED as a permanent shape. VERIFIED at /home/sini/Documents/repos/denful/den/templates/flake-parts-modules/:
- modules/den.nix:107-108 — 'Enter flake-parts scope from flake-system.' then den.schema.flake-system.includes = [ den.policies.system-to-flake-parts ];
- modules/den.nix:110-111 — 'Exclude vanilla packages route' then den.schema.flake-system.excludes = [ den.policies.packages-to-flake ];
- modules/classes/packages.nix:3 — den.schema.flake-parts.includes = [ den.policies.packages-to-flake-parts ]; an entire flake-parts scope anchored BELOW flake-system.

A SHIPPED v1 TEMPLATE targets flake-system as a DISPATCH SITE BY NAME, and anchors a sub-scope under it. Collapse the level and den.schema.flake-system.includes/excludes has no node to fire at and flake-parts has no anchor.

WHY THE DESIGN GOT IT WRONG — it evaluated flake-system purely as an INHERITANCE CARRIER ('sole ctx binding is { inherit system; }, nothing a host inherits, systemViews already delivers system') and concluded collapsible. But its real role is a SCOPE LEVEL USER CODE EXTENDS AND DISPATCHES AT. Empty inheritable binding != dispositional irrelevance. The two roles were conflated.

AND §7.6's justification leans on 'the corpus NEVER spawns flake-system' (builtins.nix:38) — which violates the standing rule feedback_den_surface_not_config: the compat target is den-SURFACE expressibility, NOT corpus-presence. Corpus-absence is explicitly not the bar. This is the same class of error as gating on corpus-eval rather than framework correctness.

LIKELY THIRD OPTION (not in the design; sent to the reviewer to assess): flake-system exists as a real TOPOLOGY level (dispatch site + scope anchor) while flake-OUTPUT routing stays gated behind den.features.flakeOutputClasses (ALREADY EXISTS, default OFF — builtins.nix:55,545). The three stubs (builtins.nix:425-427) currently gate on { system, ... } i.e. ANY node binding a system coord, which CONFLATES 'topology level exists' with 'output routing requested'. Re-gating the stubs may be the real fix rather than collapsing the topology.

STATUS: independent design-reviewer dispatched and fed this evidence; asked to assess whether (b) survives any reading, whether the third option is sound, and what a real flake-system does to the rest of the design (author asserts everything but §7.6 is stable under either choice — to be verified).
INDEPENDENT REVIEW: **REWORK**. Core insight (parentage = edge-delivered fact) correct; execution has 4 blocking defects. Orchestrator independently re-verified D1, G3, and the one flagged gap.

★ (a)/(b) ANSWER: NEITHER — take (c). systemViews claim REFUTED (the load-bearing half of the collapse argument): default.nix:1083-1089 delivers inputs'/self', NOT system, and is INDEXED BY node.decls.__entry.system — it READS the coordinate the root already carries, so it cannot be how that coordinate arrives. Circular, not imprecise.

★ MY (c) NEEDED A CORRECTION: do NOT reuse den.features.flakeOutputClasses — builtins.nix:545-560 gates only class REGISTRATION for aspect-key classification, not policy firing; reusing it repeats the very conflation §7.6 is trying to undo. THE REAL FIX is v1's OWN gate, the schema include list: v1 gates via den.schema.flake-system.includes (flake.nix:84-90); den-hoag registers flake-system = { } with NO includes (builtins.nix:429-440) and compiles every policy into a fleet-wide standalone rule, so the { system, ... } formal does the work v1 assigns to the include list. den-hoag ALREADY has the machinery — fleet-context.nix:14-16 (__kindInclude__<kind>__policy arm + includeReferencedNames strips the global + __firesAtKinds confines it). No new flag. AND: system-to-flake-parts must be PROVIDED not stubbed — it is not an output route, it is an 8-line resolve.to "flake-parts" scope spawn (v1 flake-parts.nix:11-19); builtins.nix:157 lumps all three stubs under one 'populates flake outputs' message, and that mis-grouping is the error under §7.6. Keep system-to-os-outputs/system-to-hm-outputs stubbed (they genuinely conflict with den-hoag's nixos class terminal).

★ G3 — VERIFIED BY ORCHESTRATOR, neither of us had found it: templates/flake-parts-modules/modules/perSystem-from-hosts.nix parents HOSTS under flake-parts (flake-parts-to-host maps resolve.to "host" over ALL hosts, included on den.schema.flake-parts.includes). So a shipped den template runs flake -> flake-system -> flake-parts -> host -> user, hosts at DEPTH 4. Option (b)'s host:* -> flake:<name> star cannot express it at all. G4: that host has TWO parents (system-to-os-outputs stays included; only packages-to-flake is excluded) — multi-attachment is a SHIPPED IDIOM.

BLOCKING DEFECTS:
- D1 (VERIFIED by orchestrator at lib/attributes/structural.nix:279,298-299): isMembershipDerived = (self.node id).parent != null => any resolve-family emission at a parented node hits errors.memberAtCell = LOUD ABORT. Parenting environments/hosts makes the design's OWN target policies abort (env-to-hosts fires at an environment; env-users at a host). §0.1's 'three places' census is incomplete — 7 parent-reader sites exist; 4 uncensused (structural.nix:279; output-modules.nix:283 deliveryTargetRootOf/appendToParent retargets a host delivery to its ENVIRONMENT; resolved-settings.nix:248 ancSlices branch flips; default.nix:165 hostId).
- D2: §3's host:* -> flake:<name> vs §7.1's entity-gate are contradictory ON THE SHIP-GATE FIXTURE. flake is NOT an entity kind (empty schema body => isEntity = false; v1 flake-schema.nix: flake/flake-system/flake-parts/default are ROUTING kinds, non-entity), registrySizes flake:0, so flake:x synthesizes as a type=null decl-less PHANTOM — exactly what §7.1 calls 'strictly worse'. Gate must become KIND-AWARE: entity kinds gate on registry presence; declared ROUTING kinds gate on schema registration.
- D3: the cycle is RELOCATED, not broken. env-to-hosts is { environment, ... } and reads environment.name/system-access-groups — it needs a ctx coord that exists only because fleet-to-envs fired. Stratum 0 must fire policies at nodes it is itself creating (a seeded chase over the containment DAG). §4.3's stated obligation ('pure function of registries + declared containment, no attribute reads') FORBIDS exactly that. staged-resolution.nix:30-32 already names this shape as the current ceiling and calls it corpus-zero; this design makes it the corpus's MAIN PATH.
- D7: multi-attachment is legal den surface, not mis-declaration — G4 above + nix-config clusters.nix:39-45 TODO verbatim ('cluster-to-hosts causes duplicate instantiate specs because resolve.to "host" re-resolves the host entity'). v1 re-resolves into a NEW scope (push-scope.nix:52, one parent per SCOPE ID). The design converts a legal idiom into a hard abort — a second deliberate divergence that must be NAMED.

HIGH: D4 (gen-graph.roots is INVERTED for P edges — child->parent means roots returns the CHILDLESS set; 'no parent' is leaves, or just parent == null off buildNodes; deeper, §5.4's victims answer a KIND-level question and cells are NTA-spawned, absent from the buildNodes vertex set); D5 (prune list misses live dependents of tupleDimKinds/cellKinds/rootScopeKinds — dimKinds->theFleet->fleetChildren, cellFamilies, entryNodeIndex->linkTarget, baseScopeRoots; violates §8.5's own 'a prune that requires a compensating edit was not a prune'); D6 (policy census incomplete — 5 resolve.to sites in the corpus, incl. env-to-clusters and env-users' resolve.to "user" which COLLIDES with the NTA cell population: two id conventions, user:alice vs user:alice@host:axon-01).
MEDIUM: D8 (accessGroups is a FOURTH inherited key and a VALUE change — un-gates env-users, changing WHICH USERS MATERIALIZE; §8.2's ledger names only environment/secretsConfig/fleet); D9 (§1.4 right conclusion, wrong mechanism — gen-edge childrenOf reads the children NTA = CELLS ONLY, so the P-edge graph and gen-edge's descent relation are DIFFERENT graphs; the unasked load-bearing question is whether childrenOf should now follow P edges).

FOUND SOUND (spot-checked): §4.2's refutation (best-supported section), §1.1 buildNodes all three properties, §1.1 parseParent, §1.3 children auto-wrap, §4.3 schedule, §4.4 trackedAttrs (shape A genuinely moots it), §1.4's four v1 isolation facts, §5.6's conclusion ENDORSED, §0.2/§0.3/§3.1/§3.2/§7.6-stub-gating/§8.3.

★ CORRECTION TO THE REVIEW (orchestrator-verified): its lone 'NOT VERIFIED' — §4.1's deriveGroup citation, reported as 'gen-dispatch/lib/core/declared.nix does not exist' — is a WRONG-PATH artifact. The local dir is gen-derive/, and deriveGroup IS at gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:34. §4.1's citation is SOUND. (Same failure mode as the earlier ~/Documents/repos/den miss — absence claims from agents need the same verification as positive ones.)
REV 3 FINAL (1022 lines), author-declared. Narrow pass as scoped: N1 + N2 fixed, 3 nits tightened, D9 re-judged.

N1 — site 10 (output-modules.nix:310-314 collectedMembersOf) added and labelled CEILING LAPSE, with a §8.2 ledger row (NAMED EXPECTED DELTA, same bar as accessGroups). ★ The deeper fix is the METHOD: parentage is consumed TWO ways — by SPELLING .parent, and by CALLING a query that walks it (scope.ancestors/inheritAll/inheritSet). A .parent grep is structurally blind to the second. §0.1 now shows BOTH sweeps so the next reader can re-run rather than trust the count. Query sweep surfaced no eleventh; two checked EXCLUSIONS recorded so the absence is falsifiable (resolved-settings.nix:160 ancestorsOf walks containEdges via expandPreorder NOT node.parent — its :248 consumer is site 3, already counted; every scope.descendants caller reads the children NTA = D9's population, not this census).

N2 — the one-sentence fix ADOPTED as a normative block in §5.4: classification reads ent.config.den.membership ONLY, never prePass.tuples, never chase output. Closes D3: §2.2's carve-out needs classification BEFORE the chase and resolve.to "user" FEEDS tuples, so reading the static half is exactly what fixes the input before the chase begins. §2.2's table justification corrected — the clusters.nix:30 verdict stands but is now reached from 'cluster carries no static membership' instead of the tuple-derived 'untargeted'.

NITS: §8.5 exemption narrowed to byte-green only + a named-absence table (buildRoots enumeration, the :961-968 staging block, tupleDimKinds must each be verifiable GONE BY NAME — otherwise 'reduction' is unfalsifiable). §7.1 third branch added (kind in NEITHER schema nor registry => abort NAMED) + explicit note that the gate fixes  not decl-lessness (correct for a routing kind: no entity record to supply decls; the diagnostic property is ). §7.4 I-edge half DOWNGRADED to UNVERIFIED with a settling test (linkTarget drops cell targets per structural.nix:327-330; resolution-vs-membership semantics gap; missing resolve.to->link translation).

D9 RE-JUDGED HONESTLY: site 10 is a genuine counter-instance — collectedMembersOf mixes BOTH relations in one expression (ancestors walk P edges, descendants walk the NTA), weakening the 'two graphs are principled' argument. Recommendation STANDS but at LOWER CONFIDENCE; settling test moves into planning, run against collectedMembersOf specifically since that is where the graphs already meet.

title: TOPOLOGY: parent-chain kinds are membership-INDEPENDENT flat roots; the flake->fleet->env->host chain is not scope parentage
description:
THE architectural divergence from the corpus. Deeper than the empty registry (den-hoag-9xo.8) and the missing gate (den-hoag-9xo.9) — both are symptoms of this.

CORPUS INTENT (modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:1-3, 80-82): the scope tree is flake -> fleet -> environment -> host, WIRED BY POLICY EDGES. to-fleet fires at flake and resolve.to "fleet"; fleet-to-envs fires at fleet, fans out per registered environment; env-to-hosts fires at environment, walks den.hosts whose .environment matches, and calls resolve.to "host" + den.lib.policy.instantiate hostCfg (:69-75). Instantiation is INSIDE the environment arm => a host exists BECAUSE its environment activated it. flake-system.excludes drops system-to-os-outputs/system-to-hm-outputs (:85-88) so fleet OWNS instantiation. secretsConfig is set once at the fleet node (:27) and is documented to reach hosts "through scope inheritance to all descendants" (:19).

DEN-HOAG ACTUAL (lib/default.nix:943-959, 1018, 1057; lib/build-roots.nix:12-37) — VERIFIED by reading:
- candidateKinds = childless kinds that HAVE a parent (:952). A kind with children is in parentKinds => NOT a candidate.
- nonCandidateKinds are ROOTS *regardless of the membership-derived verdict* — the code comment says so verbatim (:955-958): "their root set is membership-INDEPENDENT."
- flake / fleet / environment / host are all parent-chain kinds => all non-candidates => ALL are flat roots.
- buildRoots (build-roots.nix:12-37) enumerates EVERY registry instance of every root kind into { id; type; parent = null; decls }. parent is hardcoded null (:27).
- Only CELLS (childless-with-parent, i.e. `user`) ever nest, via the children NTA + parseParent on "kind:name@parent" ids.

=> The 4-level chain exists in den-hoag ONLY as ent.meta.<kind>.parent containment METADATA, never as scope parentage. Every root is a sibling of every other root.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCES (all VERIFIED at lib==4044ed5 x corpus 6c4f0977):
- 10 host roots materialize unconditionally; axon-01 evaluates to a NixOS toplevel with ZERO environment nodes in the graph. It is not that a gate is missing — hosts are roots BY CONSTRUCTION, so no gate is even consultable (den-hoag-9xo.9).
- Fixing den-hoag-9xo.8 alone does NOT fix this: environment:dev/environment:prod would appear as SIBLING roots of host:axon-01, not as its ancestors. The chain still would not exist.
- AGENIX / secrets: secretsConfig at the fleet node cannot reach hosts, because fleet is a sibling root and not an ancestor — there is no inheritance chain to ride. Owner: "most agenix secrets require environment to materialize." This is STRUCTURAL, and is exactly why chasing secret materialization as a bug would be chasing a symptom.

THE DESIGN QUESTION (owner-framed, do NOT start implementing before it is answered): which PURE GEN PRIMITIVES are meant to build the graph + edges that materialize the system? Node existence must follow from a RESOLVED EDGE, not from registry enumeration. Reuse-scan the built set FIRST (feedback_reuse_scan_before_build): gen-edge (edge algebra S,T,P,M + materializeUnified toposorted fold — the delivery/existence primitive), gen-scope (scope tree + inheritSet — the ancestor->descendant propagation secretsConfig needs), gen-resolve (schedule conductor — flake->fleet->env->host IS a schedule), gen-dispatch (deriveGroup declared-stratum firing), gen-graph (foldReach/expandPreorder closure), gen-product (cells). Design at the KERNEL surface, never as a compat-boundary value hack (project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface).

NOTE the staging constraint that produced this shape: default.nix:961-968 breaks a real cycle (cellKinds <- tuples <- pre-pass <- roots <- cellKinds) by fixing a STRUCTURAL root set before classification. Any redesign must answer that cycle rather than ignore it — the current answer is structural pre-classification; an edge-derived answer needs its own well-founded ordering (gen-resolve schedule is the obvious candidate).
notes:
Design scout DISPATCHED (read-only, opus) on the primitive-identification question: which gen primitive makes node existence follow from a DELIVERED EDGE, and how to order strata without reintroducing the cellKinds<-tuples<-pre-pass<-roots cycle (default.nix:961-968).

Scan set: gen-edge / gen-scope / gen-resolve / gen-dispatch / gen-graph / gen-product primary; gen-algebra / gen-demand / gen-select / gen-aspects / gen-schema / gen-bind for relevance. Contracts: papers gen-specs/<lib>/REFERENCE.md + each repo README.
Mandate: full reuse-scan BEFORE any 'needs new primitive' claim — that bar is explicitly high (a prior audit produced 4 such claims, ALL FALSE; each was expressible via expandPreorder / wrapGatedFn / inheritSet). Non-goals: no patch design, no code, no compat-boundary hack — any design lands at the KERNEL surface.
Scout was warned OFF codebase-memory: the index has ZERO Nix symbols (my earlier redirect to it was wrong and cost the previous scout turns).
VERDICT: **NO NEW PRIMITIVE NEEDED.** Scout scan complete; orchestrator INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED every load-bearing claim below.

★ THE HEADLINE: gen-scope ALREADY OWNS edge-derived node existence, and den-hoag DOES NOT USE IT.
- gen-scope/lib/build-nodes.nix:57-66,81 — buildNodes { parentGraph; decls; types; } derives parent FROM a P-edge algebraic graph: parentIndex = groupBy (e: e.from) allEdgeGraphs.P.edges, then parent = parentIndex.${id} or null. Enforces P-as-partial-function (throws on >1 parent edge, Neron 2.2) — and its own throw message suggests the '@parent' distinct-id convention for genuine multi-parent, which is exactly what den-hoag already uses for CELLS.
- VERIFIED: grep buildNodes|parentGraph|edgeGraphs over den-hoag lib/ = ZERO HITS. den-hoag hand-rolls build-roots.nix:12-37 with parent = null hardcoded (:27) and supplies a regex parseParent. The flat-sibling topology is a den-hoag AUTHORING CHOICE, not a gen limitation. The primitive is BUILT AND UNUSED.

TWO owners, one per direction (neither is gen-edge):
(a) STATIC/definitional — gen-scope.buildNodes with a non-empty parentGraph (above).
(b) MID-FOLD — the children / derived-children NTA: gen-scope/lib/eval.nix:30-46 auto-wraps BOTH names, giving each spawned child a co-located _eval cache; recursive to grandchildren. Live witness in gen-resolve/ci/tests/conformance.nix:174-192,224-227 (derived-children spawns p-child with parent = id; allNodes ? p-child asserted, 'grammar grew mid-fold, Vogt 1989 2').

PARENTAGE IS EDGE-DERIVED, NOT ID-ENCODED. Every reader takes the STRUCTURAL field: queries.nix:7,16,33,61 all read (self.node id).parent; resolve.nix:211/236/284 inherit'/inheritAll/inheritSet walk that chain. parseParent does NOT define parentage — eval.nix:55-74 checks roots ? ${id} FIRST and returns the root descriptor directly; parseParent fires only for NON-root ids as a lookup shortcut, and need not even be a string parse (conformance:210-218 uses an attrset lookup). => den-hoag's 'kind:name@parent' convention is a perf choice, not a gen requirement.

gen-edge REFUTED as owner: materialize returns config keyed by root names that must ALREADY exist (REFERENCE.md:150-151); edgesFor is 'a pure function of the STRUCTURAL stratum' (derive.nix:2-3); sources.collected.members is 'the RESOLVED, isolation-bounded membership' — an INPUT. gen-edge delivers CONTENT into existing positions, strictly downstream of existence.

THE CYCLE — den-hoag's cycle root is FIRE-TO-OBSERVE (default.nix:984-996: runPrePass FIRES policy rules at a root set to observe which coordinates they emit; that is what forces the root set to be fixed before classification). gen-resolve admits the well-founded alternative TODAY: schedule.nix:65-91 collects violations ONLY where pb > pa, so a later stratum reading an EARLIER one is legal (Apt-Blair-Walker 1988); strataOrder is a public N-way knob (resolve.nix:55); derived-children is the shipped second node-generating stratum. And gen-dispatch deriveGroup (gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:34) discharges a rule's stratum at DEFINITION time from declared 'produces' WITHOUT firing — killing fire-to-observe at its source; its group names are deliberately shared with gen-resolve strataOrder.

PROPOSED ORDERING (scout, not yet owner-ratified): stratum 0 'topology' = buildNodes over P edges (pure function of registries + declared containment, closes with no fire-to-observe); stratum 1+ = children/derived-children NTAs authored via attr { kind = "nta"; readsAttrs; stratum; }; runtime order stays Nix demand inside eval's lib.fix.

RISK CHECKED — parenting does NOT break content folding. VERIFIED den-hoag lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:785 isolatedAt = id: (result.node id).parent != null. Giving fleet/environment/host non-null parents makes each ISOLATED in gen-edge's sense, so subtreeIds "aware" stops at each and every one stays its own edge-root. A flake-root default fold does NOT start swallowing the fleet.

REJECTED as owners (checked, with reasons): gen-graph.expandPreorder (demand-generates frames but emits a FLAT WITNESS LIST, not {id,type,parent,decls} descriptors with _eval caches — wrong output type; the scout checked this one FIRST since it falsified a prior audit claim); foldPreorder/foldReach (same shape objection); gen-demand (grows DEMANDS not nodes — 'never constructs edges, modules, or configuration'); gen-product (REFERENCE: 'products define no intrinsic parent edges' — supplies coordinates a children NTA turns into nodes, which is what den-hoag fleetChildren already does); gen-link ('never unions raw graphs (gen-scope does)'); gen-scope.inheritSet (correct for the secretsConfig-reaches-hosts half ONCE parents are non-null, but creates no nodes).

UNSETTLED (read alone can't close): trackedAttrs / non-base-stratum children interaction (gen-resolve resolve.nix:15-20, override.nix:26-40 comment ASSUMES children is base-stratum; believed inert since eval.nix:32 short-circuits before the warm branch, but NO test in gen-resolve/ci/tests exercises it). Would settle it: a warm-resolve/override case with strataOrder = [topology structural resolution] and children declared at structural.
close_reason: RESOLVED by the node-multiplication arc, 84fc117..fc29920. Root parentage is live: buildRoots takes an edge-delivered parent map fed by containmentAncestors — already computed, previously wired only to the settings fold. Verified: host:axon.parent = env:prod, cluster:k3s.parent = env:prod, env:prod.parent = null. Cells classify by constructor tag (decls.__root), not id shape. title: Hosts instantiate WITHOUT environment activation (axon-01 must be gated by prod)
description: OWNER-RATIFIED: a host must NOT be initialized without activation. TWO declared facts den-hoag ignores: (1) environment activation (env-to-hosts filters hostCfg.environment == environment.name); (2) intoAttr = [ ] — the standalone-output opt-out for EMBEDDED/GUEST hosts (cortex-cuda is a microvm guest of cortex, cortex.nix:14). Both ignored because hosts materialize by REGISTRY ENUMERATION -> scope root -> native nixos class terminal, not by activation. Per 9xo.14 the gate must target THAT path, not instantiate. Half (2) is independently fixable and testable NOW (assert cortex-cuda absent from nixosConfigurations); half (1) waits on 9xo.10/9xo.12.
notes:
★ OWNER REFINEMENT + LIVE WITNESS (2026-07-26): cortex-cuda is an EMBEDDED MICROVM HOST. VERIFIED: nix-config modules/den/hosts/cortex.nix:14 `microvm.guests = [ den.hosts.x86_64-linux.cortex-cuda ];` (option declared at modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm.nix:43 "Guest MicroVMs to run on this host. List of den hosts").

So `intoAttr = [ ]` at hosts/cortex-cuda.nix:5 ("do not emit a standalone nixosConfiguration output") is not a preference — it is the DECLARED OPT-OUT for a host that exists ONLY as a guest delivered INTO cortex. den-hoag emits it standalone anyway.
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: nix eval .#nixosConfigurations --apply builtins.attrNames over the corpus returns ["axon-01","axon-02","axon-03","bitstream","blade","cortex","cortex-cuda","uplink"] — cortex-cuda IS there.
=> the guest config materializes via TWO paths: embedded into cortex (the microvm guest delivery) AND standalone at the flake top level. The standalone one is built off the registry-enumerated root, i.e. WITHOUT the guest-delivery context.

★ THIS WIDENS 9xo.9: there are (at least) TWO corpus-declared activation/opt-out facts den-hoag's registry-enumeration -> root -> native-class-terminal path ignores:
1. ENVIRONMENT ACTIVATION — env-to-hosts filters on hostCfg.environment == environment.name (fleet.nix:69); no environment nodes exist, so nothing filters.
2. intoAttr = [ ] — the standalone-output opt-out for embedded/guest hosts. Per 9xo.14's settled trace, den-hoag's ONLY intoAttr consumers are the option declaration (registry.nix:165-192), a CLI attr-path builder (nh.nix:26), and the parked-spec placement path (default.nix:2313). NOTHING in the native terminal path reads it as a gate.

Both are the same defect shape: a host materializes because it is IN A REGISTRY, not because anything ACTIVATED it. Per 9xo.14 Q4 the gate must target the registry-enumeration -> root -> terminal path (NOT instantiate — gating instantiate would not touch host materialization at all).

RELATED PRIOR ART (check before designing the fix): den v1 keeps a delivered-child route mechanism — route reinstantiate + id_hash re-key for guests (den #111 / the delivered-child route fix). The guest path is a KNOWN v1 mechanism, so den-hoag's gap is likely that it never implemented the delivered-child route rather than that the semantics are undecided.

★ IMPLICATION FOR SEQUENCING: 9xo.9 now has a LIVE, REPRODUCIBLE symptom that needs NO part of the topology arc. `intoAttr = [ ]` gating is independently fixable and independently testable (assert cortex-cuda absent from nixosConfigurations). The environment-activation half still depends on 9xo.10/9xo.12.

comments.text:
CORTEX-CUDA MEASURED, 2026-07-27, with den-hoag-9xo.8's fix applied (environments now register).

Every other host root acquires an environment parent; cortex-cuda does NOT:
  host:axon-01/02/03, uplink                 -> environment:prod
  host:bitstream, blade, cortex, patch, slab -> environment:dev
  host:cortex-cuda                           -> null

And this is NOT a missing-field case -- cortex-cuda's registry entry carries environment = "prod",
same as axon-01/02/03/uplink which all parented correctly. So the source field is present and the
containment edge still did not form for this one host. That is the .9 shape stated precisely: it
materializes without being gated by its environment, and now there is a measurable structural
witness for it rather than only a behavioural complaint.

Also measured, independent of the above and present on BOTH sides of the .8 fix (so not caused by it):
cortex-cuda is the one host whose drvPath eval fails with
  "The option `microvm' does not exist. Definition values: - In <gen-merge>, via option cortex-cuda.nixos"
distinct from the cortex microvm failure tracked on den-hoag-9xo.20 / den-hoag-5pv.

Separately: `slab` is in the host registry (registrySizes.host = 10) but emits NEITHER a nixos NOR a
darwin configuration -- 9 configurations exist for 10 registry hosts. Absent on both sides of both the
.8 fix and T1.1, so it is long-standing. It does parent correctly (-> environment:dev).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CAVEAT ON THE CORTEX-CUDA CONTROL (2026-07-27) — it is a control BY ACCIDENT and it EXPIRES.

In den-hoag-ljr, cortex-cuda is the single nixos host that is NOT contributed twice to
nixosConfigurations, and that correlation is what identified the containment attachment as the source of
the second contribution:

  duplicated (7): axon-01 axon-02 axon-03 bitstream blade cortex uplink   -- all have an environment parent
  NOT duplicated: cortex-cuda                                            -- parent = null

cortex-cuda stays single ONLY because its parent edge failed to form, which is THIS issue. It is not
evidence that some hosts are legitimately single-contributed, and nothing about it is by design.

WHEN .9 IS FIXED, THE CONTROL EXPIRES: cortex-cuda will acquire environment:prod as a parent (its
registry field already says environment = "prod") and will then duplicate exactly like the other seven.
Do not later read "cortex-cuda was single" as a counter-example to the duplicate-member analysis, and do
not treat a fix that leaves it single as correct.

comments.text:
CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER COMMENT ON THIS BEAD (2026-07-27). A fact I recorded here was WRONG.

I previously wrote that slab "emits NEITHER a nixos NOR a darwin configuration" and summarised it as
"9 configurations for 10 registry hosts". The count is right; the CONCLUSION drawn from it was not.

slab DOES emit a configuration: nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab. My check enumerated only
nixosConfigurations and darwinConfigurations -- it was FAMILY-BLIND, so a host in a third family read as
producing nothing. That is the same predicate-blindness failure this arc keeps hitting: the predicate did
not cover the space it claimed to.

Why it mattered rather than being a harmless slip: on the strength of "slab emits nothing", suppressing
the parked-spawn arm at spawn-creation time looked safe. It is not. slab's ONLY producer is that spawn
(the droid family has no receiver row, so no class terminal contributes it), and site-1 suppression would
have DELETED slab's configuration outright. The wrong fact nearly justified the wrong fix; the measurement
that caught it was the placement breakdown in den-hoag-ljr.

Corrected statement: 10 registry hosts -> 10 configurations, across THREE families --
  nixosConfigurations   8  (all hosts except patch and slab)
  darwinConfigurations  1  (patch)
  nixOnDroidConfigurations 1 (slab)
The .9 defect for slab is NOT "emits nothing". Separately measured and filed on den-hoag-ljr: slab's
emission is INCOHERENT (parked at environment:dev, targeting slab) and its slice is nModules=0, so slab's
configuration is built from the environment's empty droid subtree rather than slab's own content -- a
silent wrong-content defect, not an absent-output one.

cortex-cuda remains correctly described: it has parent = null despite environment = "prod", and it is
contributed by the class terminal only.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-07-27): cortex-cuda's parent = null is NOT a defect, and this
bead's framing of it as one is WRONG. Also corrected: the orchestrator relayed
"the containment edge failing to form is a separate, still-live defect" as
fact. It is not.

The corpus gate is a CONJUNCTION, nix-config modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:69:

  lib.optionals ((hostCfg.environment or "prod") == environment.name
                 && hostCfg.intoAttr != [ ]) [
    (resolve.to "host" { host = hostCfg; inherit accessGroups; })
    (den.lib.policy.instantiate hostCfg)
  ]

cortex-cuda SATISFIES the environment conjunct ("prod") and FAILS the
intoAttr != [ ] conjunct, so the policy deliberately emits no attachment for
it. Working as declared.

MEASURED, exact correlation: it is the ONLY corpus host declaring
intoAttr = [ ] (grep over modules/den/hosts/ -> one hit) and the ONLY host with
parent = null. Mechanism from source: build-roots.nix:8-11 "a root is
parentless unless the caller names its attachments", fed by containmentAncestors
from containTo members (staged-resolution.nix:111).

So it is not a third defect and not half (1)'s inverse -- it is half (2)'s SAME
declared fact seen on the attachment side.

★ THE TRAP THIS CREATES, and it is why the shape was reported before coding:
implement half (1) as "filter enumeration by environment match" and cortex-cuda
is excluded FOR THE WRONG REASON -- its environment matches; it is the intoAttr
conjunct that excludes it. The exclusion would look correct while reasoning
from a mechanism that is not the one operating.

--- HALF (1) RULING (orchestrator, 2026-07-27) ---

MATERIALISATION FOLLOWS REACHABILITY, NOT ATTACHMENT:
    a node materialises iff it is REACHABLE FROM A DECLARED ROOT.

Rejected: attachment-driven ("a policy attached it"). The KERNEL CANNOT DEPEND
ON A CORPUS POLICY EXISTING -- a kernel-native fleet has no env-to-hosts, and
under a strict attachment rule its hosts would all vanish. Reachability is a
property of the graph, so it needs no policy.

Reachability also states the corpus's own intent structurally (flake -> fleet ->
env -> host: the host materialises BECAUSE it is reachable through the chain;
the policy is merely how v1 spells the edge), and excludes cortex-cuda for the
RIGHT reason -- unreachable because nothing attached it, not by reading
intoAttr.

It survives .14's counter-example: corpus batteries/colmena.nix:93-104 emits
instantiate UNGATED with no resolve.to beside it, so "whoever attaches,
instantiates" is a corpus authoring convention, NOT a framework guarantee.
Under reachability that spawn is parked at a host node and fires if the host is
reachable -- the rule never has to claim attachment implies instantiate.

WHAT DIES (per .12's prune-do-not-paper-over): build-roots.nix's unconditional
"every registry instance is a root". A registry instance becoming a root MERELY
BY EXISTING is the structural reason BOTH halves of .9 were ignored -- hosts
materialise by registry enumeration, so the policy that computes attachment
never governs materialisation.

Half (2)'s emitsNamedResult placement gate (ab1112a) MAY BE SUBSUMED and should
then be deleted -- two mechanisms for one fact. PROVE subsumption before
deleting; if reachability alone leaves cortex-cuda absent it is redundant, if
not they are two facts and both stay.

SEAMS ARE DIFFERENT AND MUST NOT BE MERGED: half (2) gates the family
PLACEMENT (late, artifact deliberately survives -- intoAttr says where a result
LANDS, not whether it is produced). Half (1) gates ROOT CONSTRUCTION, where
parentage now lives; activation is the stronger claim, "not initialised" rather
than "not published". A placement gate for half (1) would leave a
non-activated host fully built and merely unpublished -- papering over.

ACCEPTANCE: the seven currently-materialising hosts must ALL be reachable, and
the enumeration must change by EXACTLY cortex-cuda.
FALSIFIER: if any of the seven is not reachable, the formulation is WRONG --
stop and report, do not add an exception. An exception list is the name-list
lie one level up.

title: [compat] SHRUNK: _registryKinds IS populated and the chain collapsed (cells 2->33) — body wrong on three counts; live residue is the KERNEL-SIDE registryKindsOf twin still returning { }
description:
THE live blocker upstream of both #52 and F3. Framework-correctness defect in the compat ingest boundary, NOT a corpus problem: the corpus surface is FINE (fleetEnvironmentNames = [dev prod], fleetClusterNames = [axon], envIsInstanceRegistry = true, entries carry id_hash).

MEASURED MECHANISM (VERIFIED by scout, decisive numbers independently reproduced by orchestrator):
- _registryKinds = {} while _entityStamps keys = [clusters environments groups hosts] => consumerRegistryKeys non-empty => registryKindOf IS CALLED, and returns null for all three.
- Why null: envSubOptionKeys / clusterSubOptionKeys / groupSubOptionKeys are ALL []. bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf yields {} => identityKeysOf {} = [] => hash mismatch.
- Fallback: ingest drops to the VALUE-marker path, which catches groups (34) but MISSES environments and clusters (0/0).
- Consequence chain: no environment/cluster nodes => zero environment:*/cluster:* scope roots => env-to-hosts cannot fire => prePass.containmentBindings = {} => no accessGroups on any root => no human user cells (only 2 cells exist, both sini@patch/slab) => #52 empty edge set + F3 nothing to deliver.

The option-reflecting registry-kind fix (registryKindOf/_registryKinds, bridge.nix:292/340, registry.nix:355, ingest.nix:481) IS in-tree but INERT over this corpus. git log c82b729..HEAD over bridge.nix/registry.nix/ingest.nix is EMPTY - no den-hoag change since the diagnosis rev, so this is not a regression introduced after it.

=> F3 blocker-table row #1 ("Empty env/cluster registries - SHIPPED") must be RE-OPENED: the fix exists but does not work over this corpus.

OPEN QUESTION (UNVERIFIED, blocks the fix design): when did options.den.<registry>.type.getSubOptions stop yielding sub-options? Ruled OUT: the corpus gen-schema bump e6dbe8e7->c6331f30 (one commit, feat(refined): re-export checkRefinements). Would settle it: bisect corpus history for when getSubOptions went empty. Determines whether the fix belongs in den-hoag subOptionsOf, in gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry, or in how the corpus declares these registries.

NORTH-STAR FRAMING: this is NOT a corpus-eval chase. Kind-discovery that cannot reflect an option-declared registry is a compat-boundary correctness defect - the value-marker fallback is precisely the kind of v1 holdover the arc exists to dissolve.
notes:
★ OWNER-RATIFIED (2026-07-26): the registry sizes are WRONG — environment MUST populate (corpus declares dev + prod). den-hoag's current behavior is BROKEN, not merely incomplete. Raised to P0.

Owner also states a SEPARATE semantic requirement this exposes: **axon-01 must NOT be initialized in the config without being activated by its environment (prod).** Today it is: 10 host scope roots materialize and axon-01 evaluates all the way to a NixOS toplevel with ZERO environment nodes in the graph, so no activation gate exists to hold it back. Split to a sibling bead — same root, distinct correctness requirement (populating the registry alone does not create the gate).
RE-SCOPED by den-hoag-9xo.10: fixing the empty environment registry is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. environment:dev/prod would appear as flat SIBLING roots of host:axon-01 (buildRoots hardcodes parent = null), so the flake->fleet->env->host chain still would not exist and hosts would still materialize unconditionally.
★ OWNER RULING (2026-07-26): NO BISECT. den-hoag is a GREENFIELD implementation — _registryKinds was most likely NEVER populated correctly, per how the gen module system was built. This is not a regression with a last-good commit; it is a path that never worked. Drop the 'when did getSubOptions stop yielding sub-options' line of inquiry entirely.

RE-SCOPED: investigate bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf against how gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry ACTUALLY exposes sub-options — i.e. was the option-reflecting kind-discovery ever correct against the real gen-schema surface, or was it written against an assumed one? Fix belongs wherever that mismatch actually lives. Per the prune mandate: if the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover this never-working path, it is DEAD CODE to delete, not a fallback to preserve.
★ ROOT CAUSE FOUND — confirms the owner's greenfield call exactly: this path NEVER worked. No bisect could have found a last-good commit. All VERIFIED by orchestrator.

THE CHAIN:
1. registry.nix:369 `ikeys = identityKeysOf opts`; :373-375 gates on `hashIdentity k ikeys (...) == carried id_hash`. With ikeys empty the hash never matches => hits empty => registryKindOf null.
2. identityKeysOf (registry.nix:330-345) reflects the DECLARED OPTION SURFACE — needs opts.<n>.type.name / .internal / .identity.
3. It gets opts from bridge.nix:248 `subOptionsOf k = t.getSubOptions ["den" k]`, guarded by `if t == null || !(t ? getSubOptions) then <empty>`.
4. ★ gen-merge NEVER IMPLEMENTS getSubOptions ON ANY TYPE. attrsOfWith (gen-merge lib/types.nix:198-225) builds via mkOptionType { name; elemType; nestedTypes; merge; } — no getSubOptions. submodule (:142-168) sets getSubModules + substSubModules — no getSubOptions. mkOptionType's normalization (:122) then DEFAULTS it: `getSubOptions = t.getSubOptions or (_prefix: <empty>)`.
   => the field EXISTS (so den-hoag's `t ? getSubOptions` guard PASSES) but returns an EMPTY ATTRSET UNCONDITIONALLY. den-hoag takes the else-branch and gets nothing.
   => opts empty => ikeys empty => null for EVERY kind. Systemic, not env/cluster-specific.

WHY IT LOOKS ENV/CLUSTER-SPECIFIC: registryKindOf returns null for ALL kinds; the VALUE-marker fallback then silently covers hosts+groups (34) and misses environments/clusters. The fallback masks a TOTAL failure of the option-reflecting path.

THE TELL — the accommodation was made ONE LEVEL TOO SHALLOW. registry.nix:327-329 verbatim: "nixpkgs names primitives str/int/bool, gen-merge string/int/bool — both accepted". The author KNEW gen-merge types were in play and handled the type-NAME difference, but not that gen-merge implements no getSubOptions at all. Written against nixpkgs lib.types introspection semantics (attrsOf.getSubOptions delegates to elemType; submodule.getSubOptions returns evaluated sub-options) over a merge-plane library that never had them.
Per that same comment the hash gate makes a wrong key set "a LOUD miss (null), never a misclassification" — true, but the value-marker fallback converts that loud miss into a SILENT one end-to-end.

FIX CANDIDATES (choose before implementing; A is the route-through-gen-native shape):
(A) den-hoag reads the identity surface from gen-schema's KIND RECORD instead of reflecting the merge-plane option type. gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry's guard requires `kindValue ? options` (instance.nix:274-277) and entry-type.nix:166 says the kind result carries them "so mkInstanceRegistry can consume them automatically". gen-schema DECLARES the identity surface; re-deriving it by type reflection is the duplication. NO gen change. NEEDS ONE VERIFICATION: does den.schema.<kind>.options carry .type.name/.internal/.identity as identityKeysOf requires?
(B) gen-merge implements getSubOptions faithfully on attrsOf/submodule (nixpkgs parity). A real parity gap — BUT gen-merge deliberately exposes `nestedTypes` as its walker accessor instead (listOf:174-176 verbatim: "nixpkgs-parity introspection alias — lets a consumer's type-tree walker recurse unchanged"), so adding getSubOptions may be out of character. ALSO a gen-lib change => owner-confirmed requirement only, never pre-authorized.

PRUNE NOTE: if (A) lands, the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover a path that never worked => DEAD CODE per the owner's prune ruling, not a fallback to preserve.
FIX (A) IS AVAILABLE AND NEEDS NO GEN CHANGE — the declared option surface is ALREADY COLLECTED in-tree, one scope away from the consumer that needs it.

VERIFIED: lib/compat/bridge.nix:496-498
  rawOptionsOf = kindName: lib.foldl' (acc: d: lib.recursiveUpdate acc ((d.${kindName} or { }).options or { })) { } schemaDefs;
That is the merged DECLARED option surface per kind, taken from the schema DEFS — exactly what identityKeysOf (registry.nix:330-345) reads (.type.name / .internal / .identity). Corroborating: gen-schema entry-type.nix:230 `options = userOptions` — the kind record carries them; ingest.nix:249 passes tree.config.den.schema.<kindName> into mkInstanceRegistry.

=> THE FIX: registryKindOf's `opts` should come from the kind's DECLARED options (rawOptionsOf-shaped), not from bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf's `t.getSubOptions` type-reflection, which is dead on arrival because gen-merge implements getSubOptions on NO type (it defaults to `_prefix: {}` at gen-merge/lib/types.nix:122).
Threading note: rawOptionsOf lives in a `let` around bridge.nix:488 (the belt section); subOptionsOf is at :248. Different scopes — the rung must thread the value or hoist the helper. Small, but not literally one line.

RESIDUAL RISK (settle during implementation, degrades SAFELY): rawOptionsOf reads each def's inline `.options` only. If a kind's identity fields arrive via kind IMPORTS (rawImportsOf, :494-495) rather than inline options, the key set is incomplete. Per registry.nix:327-329 the hash-equality gate makes a wrong key set a LOUD MISS (null), never a misclassification — so an incomplete set fails closed, it does not mis-attribute. Settling test: compare identityKeysOf(rawOptionsOf k) against the keys gen-schema's mkIdentityModule actually hashed, for environment/cluster/group/host.

PRUNE CONSEQUENCE (owner ruling): once (A) lands and registryKindOf resolves for every kind, the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover a path that never worked => DELETE it, do not keep it as a fallback. Its presence is what converted registryKindOf's loud null into a silent end-to-end miss.

SEQUENCING: independent of the topology rung (different plane — ingest/identity, not scope parentage). Can land before, after, or in parallel. Note it is UPSTREAM of the corpus chain in effect: with environment/cluster registries empty, env-to-hosts has no environment root to fire at, so containmentAncestors stays empty for env->host and the topology rung has nothing to thread for those links. **Rung 1 will be exercised by whatever containment members DO fire; the corpus's flake->fleet->environment links need .8 fixed to appear at all.**

comments.text:
R2.0 STOPPED, correctly, past where the plan predicted. Plan's R2.2 remedy
source (rawOptionsOf) is EMPTY for all ten kinds -- corpus declares kind options
under den.schema.<kind>.imports, never .options, 5/5 kind files. R2.2 as written
would have shipped a silent no-op and passed.

Absence is trustworthy: known-positive on the SAME fold (rawImportsOf returns
1/1/1/1/7, host 7) proves the fold is live, so the empty result is real and not
a blind predicate.

Correct surface MEASURED: merged instance option surface (den-hoag's existing
hostInstanceOptions pattern, registry.nix:384) + withInjectedName reproduces the
carried id_hash for all three kinds:
  clusters     ikeys ['environment','name']
  environments ikeys ['domain','id','name','timezone']
  groups       ikeys ['description','name']
Without name: no match anywhere.

RULING: route (a) -- implement getSubOptions on gen-merge, completing the
nixpkgs mkOptionType protocol. bridge.nix:509-514 already names that completion
as this seam's RETIREMENT CONDITION (verified verbatim by orchestrator). Route
(b) would re-implement a gen-merge capability inside compat and deepen the seam
we plan to delete. (a) dissolves, (b) mimics.

OWNER AUTHORIZED THE GEN-MERGE PUSH (2026-07-27). Direct to main, no PR.
Authorization covers the change, NOT a shortcut past proof. Push gated on, in
order: C2 consumer census, C1 ikeys reproduction, gen-merge's own suite (its
checks.default is a homegrown asserter not nix-unit -- expectedError CRASHES
the gate), docs in the same commit (README + gen-specs/gen-merge/REFERENCE.md,
THEORY citations), format. Then den-hoag pin via
  nix flake lock ./ci --update-input den-hoag/gen-merge
NEVER nix flake update on the parent.

C1 falsifier: any ikeys deviation -- including a different membership that
still matches id_hash -- is a STOP, not an expectation to adjust. The claim
that withInjectedName becomes unnecessary is DERIVED, not measured.

DO NOT retire the bridge seam in this rung. Record whether the retirement
condition is now met and what still blocks severance; separate decision, own
blast radius.

Also settled at R2.0: R2.4 measured EARLY and PASSES (host parent ==
environment, cluster -> environment, user -> host; both silent `or null`
defaults benign) -- retires E2's misleading-abort risk. R2.1 premise VERIFIED:
the existing marker test builds zoneOpts from nixpkgs submoduleWith, which
DOES implement getSubOptions; the real path is gen-merge, which does not.
That is exactly why .8 survived a green suite -- the test could not fail for
