comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED UPSTREAM (2026-07-27). Not a den-hoag defect.

gen-merge lib/types.nix:122 completed the nixpkgs mkOptionType protocol with
  getSubOptions = t.getSubOptions or (_prefix: { });
a stub on EVERY type. Only field PRESENCE was pinned (ci/tests/nixpkgs-protocol.nix
test-protocol-complete), never behaviour. Correct for a leaf; on a STRUCTURAL type it reports
"declares nothing" indistinguishably from a type that genuinely declares nothing. The hash gate then
fails CLOSED (null = "not this kind"), which is why this was silent.

FIX: implement getSubOptions on gen-merge submodule / attrsOf / listOf. gen-merge commit 8daa25d
(local; push pending owner-authorized go-ahead). ZERO den-hoag edits required.

MEASURED, corpus, with the fix:
  registryKinds  {} -> {clusters=cluster, environments=environment, groups=group}
  registrySizes  environment 0->2, cluster 0->1, host 10->10, group 34->34
  scopeRoots     44 -> 47, gaining exactly cluster:axon, environment:dev, environment:prod
  identity keys  cluster ['environment','name']; environment ['domain','id','name','timezone'];
                 group ['description','name']  -- each reproduces the carried id_hash
  den-hoag gates ci=0, parity=0, ship-gate=0/true

*** DEPLOYMENT CHAIN -- THE FIX DOES NOT FLOW THROUGH den-hoag's GRAPH ***

The corpus builds its registries with its OWN inputs.gen-schema (nix-config
modules/den/schema/cluster.nix:97, environment.nix:140), so the option types the bridge reflects are
NIX-CONFIG's, not den-hoag's. Verified by overriding ONLY gen-schema/gen-merge -- den/gen-merge left
at its pin -- and that alone fixed it.

  Shipping end-to-end = gen-merge -> gen-schema -> NIX-CONFIG lock.
  den-hoag's own bump serves only its fixtures (the R2.1 witness).

This confirms the bridge seam comment's claim that the type half is the corpus's, at its pin.

VERSION NOTE. nix-config's gen-schema/gen-merge is pinned at f7e3afb -- exactly the base of the fix --
so the override introduces ONE commit and nothing else (no confound). den-hoag's gen-merge is
2701d8bb, FIVE commits behind, so a den-hoag bump pulls those five in as well; classify that delta
separately, it is not part of this fix.

*** DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE -- NEW, ATTRIBUTED, NOT YET DIAGNOSED ***

With environments materializing, host scope roots acquire parents for the first time:
  host:axon-01/02/03, uplink -> environment:prod
  host:bitstream, blade, cortex, patch, slab -> environment:dev
  host:cortex-cuda -> null   (ANOMALY: its environment field IS "prod" -- see den-hoag-9xo.9)
axon-01's root decls also gain accessGroups, so containment bindings are now delivering.

But all nixos hosts then fail EARLIER than before:
  before: "Failed assertions:" (initrd SSH key / wheel password)
  after:  "Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set"
ATTRIBUTION CONTROL RUN: the same path-override pointed at f7e3afb WITHOUT the getSubOptions change
reproduces "Failed assertions:", so the override mechanism is not the cause -- the change is.
Localized to lib/compat/flake-module.nix:288-290:
  hostEntry = bindings.host or null;
  sys       = if hostEntry == null then null else systemFor hostEntry;
  sysModule = if sys == null then [ ] else [ { nixpkgs.hostPlatform.system = sys; } ];
The host registry's own system field is INTACT and identical before/after (axon-01 = x86_64-linux), so
the field did not vanish. Which of the two is null -- bindings.host or systemFor's read -- is NOT yet
distinguished; downstream reads all cascade from the single hostPlatform error, so a probe of
networking.hostName is inconclusive and was not treated as evidence.

This is a den-hoag defect newly EXPOSED by parented hosts, not a gen-merge defect. It does not affect
any corpus build until nix-config's lock moves, so it does not gate the gen-merge push -- it gates the
nix-config bump.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
THE SEAM'S RETIREMENT CONDITION WAS NEVER A REAL GATE (2026-07-27).

lib/compat/bridge.nix:509-514 names the pass-through seam's severance condition as "once the consumer's
gen-schema is PROTOCOL-COMPLETE -- pins a gen-merge at/past the mkOptionType nixpkgs-protocol
completion". That condition was ALREADY SATISFIED before any of this work: gen-merge
ci/tests/nixpkgs-protocol.nix test-protocol-complete asserts field PRESENCE over the 14-field surface
and was green, because completeType stamped getSubOptions -- as a stub.

So a condition written to gate severance was met by a type surface on which one of its methods answered
"declares nothing" for every type. A completeness gate that tests PRESENCE and not BEHAVIOUR does not
gate anything. This is the same failure mode that kept .8 silent for den-hoag's whole life:
presence-checked, behaviour-unchecked.

MEASURED, so severance can be decided on data rather than argument: under the fix, belt
(passThrough = true) vs severed (passThrough = false) produce IDENTICAL corpus output -- registrySizes,
registryKinds, metaParents, rawSchemaParents all equal; scopeRoots 47 vs 47.

STILL BLOCKING SEVERANCE -- do not retire the seam on the strength of that:
 1. The seam's own bar is corpus-RESULT equivalence and there is NO OBSERVABLE: zero of nine
    configurations produce a toplevel drvPath. The comparison above is structural only.
 2. The in-code severability witness's second half ("activated with the types work") is not activated;
    no CI witness pins belt == severed.
 3. passThrough is a bare bridge ARGUMENT, not a den.features gate -- severance today is a code edit,
    not a flag flip. The comment's "passThrough makes the severance one flag" is aspirational until it
    actually is one; per the feature-flag/removability convention this wants a real den.features.<name>.
 4. Structural equality measured on THIS corpus (three consumer registries) -- not a general proof.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
R2.1 PREREQUISITE ANSWERED (2026-07-27): the targeted bump moves the WRONG NODE. R2.1 would be a false
witness.

den-hoag ci/flake.lock carries TEN gen-merge nodes across THREE revs:
    2701d8bb  x4   (gen-merge, _4, _6, _9)
    fa5d5cc2  x4   (gen-merge_2, _5, _7, _10)
    fdbf140b  x2   (gen-merge_3, _8)

R2.1's fixture builds its registry through mkInstanceRegistry, which comes from den-hoag's gen-schema.
Resolution path, measured:
    root.den-hoag              -> den-hoag
    den-hoag.gen-schema        -> gen-schema_3
    den-hoag/gen-schema.gen-merge -> gen-merge_5  = fa5d5cc2f56d

But the instructed bump, `nix flake lock ./ci --update-input den-hoag/gen-merge`, moves the node
`den-hoag.gen-merge` = gen-merge_4 = 2701d8bb -- a DIFFERENT node that the fixture never resolves
through. Bumping it would leave the fixture evaluating against fa5d5cc2, which has the stubbed
getSubOptions, so a reshaped R2.1 would report the defect as still present (or pass for an unrelated
reason) while the pin it was supposed to exercise had not moved at all.

That is the same class as the ORIGINAL .8 defect surviving a green suite: the witness exercising a
surface other than the one under test. Here it would have been the marker fixture reading a gen-merge
that never changed, instead of a nixpkgs submoduleWith.

CORRECT TARGET for R2.1 to be trustworthy:

title: NORTH STAR: graph-native framework correctness
description:
The bar for den-hoag WS-B is GRAPH-NATIVE FRAMEWORK CORRECTNESS (DL-HS-29): dissolve the v1 effect-runtime holdovers into native gen primitives. den-hoag is v0 alpha; tech debt is P1.

CORPUS-EVAL IS A VALIDATION SYMPTOM, NOT THE BAR. "works on the real corpus" is a no-regression check, never the driver. Reject sunk-cost, YAGNI, shortcuts, interim tech-debt, and band-aids that preserve a v1 ceiling. Route every gen-capability duplication through native gen rather than re-implementing in compat.

DONE (three arcs, all two-stage-reviewed):
1. Route-through arc, 17 rungs - every confirmed effect-runtime holdover dissolved (A1 flagship runPrePass state-accumulator -> prelude.groupBy per-target carrier + demand-read; A3/B9 -> gen-graph foldReach/expandPreorder; A5 -> gen-scope inheritSet; B7 -> gen-dispatch deriveGroup; compat-1 -> gen-graph foldPreorder; B6->G4 gen-bind; B8->G5 gen-pipe).
2. IDENTITY re-point - den no longer owns aspect/class identity (gen-aspects aspectId, gen-schema hashIdentity, gen-link origin).
3. raw/typed-dual + validation-authority dissolution (the audit ROOT) - gen-aspects recursiveClosed is the SINGLE validator; Model C closed vocabulary.

No effect-runtime duplication remains. Children of this epic are the REMAINING frontiers.

Pins: den-hoag main @4044ed5 (before the bd-init commit 0abf541); gen-aspects main @1689e41; corpus nix-config @6c4f0977.

GATE for every rung (SEE exit=0 empirically before any commit; never `runner | tail && commit`):
  nix build ./ci#checks.x86_64-linux.default
  nix build ./parity#checks.x86_64-linux.default
  nix eval --impure --json --expr (import ./parity/ship-gate.nix { flakePath = toString ./parity; }).allEqual  == true

Authoritative sources: papers/den-architecture/STATUS/route-through-board.md; specs/2026-07-22-wsb-autonomous-decision-log.md (DL-HS-54..68 latest); specs/2026-07-24-den-hoag-effects-runtime-audit.md (roadmap).

title: [gen-lib][gen-resolve] readsAttrs is a DECLARATION the evaluator NEVER consults — the circularity gate is loud on a declared edge, SILENT on an undeclared one, and blind to instance-arg edges entirely
description:
MEASURED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL, 2026-07-29, by a spike on den-hoag-4kh.53.64's condition 5. Not read —
executed, with the control in the same run.

★★ THE CLAIM: `readsAttrs` LOOKS LIKE A DEPENDENCY DECLARATION THAT BOUNDS WHAT AN ATTRIBUTE MAY READ. IT IS
NOT ONE. It is an input to a STATIC ANALYSIS THAT SEES ONLY WHAT THE AUTHOR DECLARES, and the evaluator never
consults it at read time.

SOURCE EVIDENCE. In the pinned gen-resolve (/nix/store/1gqihxag0ycpqf8crwi89x7ycaxcfr0c-source) `readsAttrs`
occurs ONLY in:
  lib/schedule.nix  — Knuth circularity test + stratum analysis
  lib/contract.nix  — the `why` trace
  lib/equation.nix  — the record constructor
★ ZERO occurrences in lib/resolve.nix or lib/materialize.nix. **IT IS NEVER CONSULTED AT `self.get`.**

THE EXECUTABLE CONTROL PAIR — same instrument, same family, same run:
  UNDECLARED edge: `declarations` compute reads self.get id "enrichments", readsAttrs left unchanged
      ⇒ **rc 0, SILENT.**
  DECLARED edge: the same class of edge with readsAttrs += "local-collection-data"
      ⇒ **rc 1**, "gen-resolve: attribute grammar is circular but not convergent (Knuth 1968 circularity
        test). SCC(s) contain non-'circular' attrs: [["declarations","local-collection-data",
        "resolved-aspects"]]"
⇒ **THE CIRCULARITY GATE IS LIVE AND LOUD ON A DECLARED EDGE AND COMPLETELY BLIND TO AN UNDECLARED ONE.**
An author who forgets to declare a read does not get a weaker check — they get NO check, and the analysis
still reports success.

★★ AND THERE IS A WHOLE DEPENDENCY CHANNEL `readsAttrs` CANNOT NAME AT ALL: **INSTANCE ARGS.**
den-hoag's `declarations` (lib/attributes/structural.nix:325-435) depends on `policiesIndex` (called
UNCONDITIONALLY at line 347), `linkTarget` (conditional) and `isCellNode` — all bound in lib/default.nix's
`let`. readsAttrs is a list of ATTRIBUTE NAMES; an instance arg is not an attribute, so it is unnameable
there and the schedule never analyses it.
MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (one-line edit making policiesIndex.policy seq `attrNames quirkDag.channels`, under the
proposed quirkDag/result knot):
  HEAD quirkDag → **rc 0, clean** ← POSITIVE CONTROL, the edit is harmless without the knot
  KNOT quirkDag → **rc 1, "error: infinite recursion encountered"**
  same, wrapped in builtins.tryEval (builtins.deepSeq v true) → **rc 1 — tryEval DOES NOT CATCH IT**
  ★ NO SCHEDULE GATE FIRED. The identical cycle spelled as a DECLARED ATTRIBUTE edge aborts with a NAMED SCC.

⇒ WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM THE DESIGN THAT FOUND IT. The finding is not "the knot is unsafe" — it is
that **a construct the whole codebase reads as a safety declaration provides no safety for the majority of
the real dependency surface, and fails in the worst available mode**: a raw infinite recursion, unattributed,
uncatchable, instead of the named SCC the same cycle produces one spelling over.

CONSEQUENCES TO CARRY:
1. ★ ANY den-hoag invariant of the form "no attribute in X's transitive readsAttrs closure may read X" is
   NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. It must also quantify over the instance args bound in lib/default.nix's
   `let`, or state plainly that it is enforced by nothing.
2. This is the mechanism behind the standing den-hoag note that a lib.fix black-hole is not tryEval-catchable
   (den-hoag-4kh.20) — now with the SPECIFIC channel identified rather than the symptom.
3. ★ ABSENCE-IS-A-DECISION APPLIES: an UNDECLARED read currently means "unanalysed", silently. Whether that
   should instead be an error, or whether reads should be derived rather than declared, is a gen-resolve
   design question — filed here per the convention that den-hoag's tracker covers all gen-* libs.
4. The gate's soundness direction is inverted from what a reader expects: it over-trusts the declaration. A
   declaration-based analysis is only as total as the declarations, and NOTHING checks the declarations
   against the code.

COVERAGE / LIMITS, STATED. Only the UNCONDITIONAL `policiesIndex` channel is demonstrated. ★ THE `linkTarget`
BRANCH IS UNCOVERED: a link fixture fires (positive control — 7 link declarations, 7 import edges) yet the
linkTarget-patched arm stayed clean, because `combine` appears unreached when no later-stratum rules exist.
One fixture (dense env/host/user crossing, one quirk channel, one aspect, one enrich policy) — NOT the
corpus. The suite was NOT run, so there is no claim about the 1919/1937 baseline here.

title: [kernel] __containment carries the SAME dangling-id defect as containmentPairs — a SECOND site of the one-id rule, live on den.membership + den.include
description:
MEASURED, LIVE ON PUBLIC SURFACE (den.membership + den.include), found by the containment-as-edges r3 gate
while building its own fixtures — not by reading.

SYMPTOM. With an aspect present, evaluation ABORTS: "gen-scope: node 'cluster:k3s' not reachable from roots".

MECHANISM. Under a plain member the cell's __containment spells the ancestor id BARE — cluster:k3s — while
the minted node is cluster:k3s@env:prod. ancestorResolvedKeys reads that bare id, and it names nothing.

★ WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE ABORT: this is a SECOND SITE of the same "one id rule, shared" obligation
that den-hoag-5ae's §5(a) raises against containmentPairs. The spec names only containmentPairs. Two
independent constructions of the same id, disagreeing — which is exactly the defect class the
containment-as-edges design exists to remove BY CONSTRUCTION (a single edge identity contains/from->to makes
the two spellings idempotent rather than divergent).

⇒ IT SUPPORTS THE DESIGN RATHER THAN BLOCKING IT: §6.3 deletes the payload and obligation 1 fixes the id
rule. But it must be named in §5 and in the ledger, because today it is a live wrong-answer with a public
trigger, and a reader of the spec would not learn that the second site exists.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE ITSELF, WHICH IS WHY IT WAS FOUND: it means ARM 2 OF THE CANCELLATION FIXTURE CANNOT
BE EVALUATED once an aspect is present, so no BEHAVIOURAL instrument can confirm the structural cancellation
on that arm. The reviewer confirmed the cancellation STRUCTURALLY instead (mapAttrs preserves the key set, so
attrNames registries == attrNames meta by construction) — a stronger result, reached because the behavioural
route was blocked by this defect.

REPRO: a membership tuple naming a kind whose ancestor is reached by a plain member rather than a containment
attachment, with an aspect included at the ancestor. Probes at scratchpad/rev/gr{1..8}.nix (session-local).

    compat bridge:  registryKinds = { clusters = "cluster"; environments = "environment"; groups = "group"; }
    kernel twin:    compat.ingest.registryKindsOf (head fleet).den = { }

title: [gen-lib] STANDING: gen changes are AUTHORIZED for real defects and gaps, at a HIGH validation bar — plus the six gen-side candidates measured this session
description:
★★★ OWNER DIRECTIVE, 2026-07-29, VERBATIM: "when appropriate, we are clear to make changes to gen when we
identify real defects or gaps — but the validation bar should be high."

WHAT THIS AUTHORIZES. A gen-side defect is no longer a reason to work around it in den-hoag. Where den-hoag
today compensates for a gen limitation, the compensation is a candidate for deletion and the fix belongs
upstream. This composes with the standing rule that den-hoag must ROUTE GEN-CAPABILITY DUPLICATIONS THROUGH
NATIVE GEN rather than re-implementing them in compat.
WHAT IT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE: a push on an unconfirmed requirement. The gen-lib push gate stands — never
pre-authorize pushing a gen-lib change on a requirement den-hoag has not confirmed it needs.

════ THE BAR, AND WHY IT IS SET HERE ════

★ TWO OF THREE "OBVIOUS" ONE-LINE GEN-LIBRARY FIXES WERE WRONG WHEN MEASURED, AND ONE WAS A 272x REGRESSION.
That is not a cautionary abstraction, it is den-hoag-4kh.53.47: `gen-prelude`'s `unique` is quadratic with
accumulator copying, the same file contains a linear `dedupByKey` seventy-five lines above, and delegating
one to the other is the obvious fix. MEASURED AT DEN-HOAG'S ACTUAL INPUT SHAPE IT IS 272x WORSE.
⇒ THE ASYMPTOTICS BEING UNAMBIGUOUS FROM SOURCE IS NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT THE REMEDY. Reading a complexity class
tells you the defect is real; it does not tell you the fix is an improvement at the shapes actually passed.

SO, FOR ANY GEN CHANGE:
1. THE DEFECT IS MEASURED, NOT READ. A source-derived complexity class is a hypothesis about cost.
2. ★ THE REMEDY IS MEASURED TOO, AT DEN-HOAG'S REAL INPUT SHAPES. This is the step that was skipped.
3. SPEC BEFORE DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING ONE-LINE CHANGES. "Small and measured green" is not an exemption —
   skipping it cost a public revert on gen-schema.
4. THE INSTRUMENT IS STATED WITH ITS OWN COMPLEXITY, and a positive control runs in the same session. A
   genuinely linear control measuring exactly 2x per doubling is what makes a flat result trustworthy.
5. WALL-CLOCK IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THESE SIZES — cpuTime measured FLAT at ~0.007s across every N, and a flake
   eval has a ~345ms floor. Use NIX_SHOW_STATS=1 counters on a PLAIN FILE: `list.elements` for ++/tail
   copying, `nrOpUpdateValuesCopied` for // copying, `nrPrimOpCalls`.
6. FROZEN ORACLE PINS STAY FROZEN. Rotating a `-orig` oracle pin vacates the oracle.
7. ★ READ THE PINNED REV, NOT THE LOCAL CLONE. `ci/flake.lock` pins the gen libraries and the clones run
   AHEAD — measured today: `testSingletons` exists in the local gen clone and NOT at the locked rev. A
   capability found in a clone is not a capability available to the build. Every gen claim names its rev.
8. FILE IT HERE. den-hoag's tracker is THE tracker for all gen-* repos; prefix the title `[gen-lib]`.

════ CANDIDATES IDENTIFIED TODAY — measured, unspecified, NOT yet authorized work ════

Each was found while measuring something else. None has had step 2 applied. Listed so the authorization has
a concrete surface rather than being an abstract permission.

· `gen-prelude` `unique = foldl' (acc: x: if elem x acc then acc else acc ++ [ x ]) [ ]` — linear scan inside
  a fold AND accumulator copying. 16 den-hoag kernel call sites, several per-node. ★ REMEDY REFUTED at 272x;
  a real fix must be measured per-site. den-hoag-4kh.53.47.
· `gen-prelude` `groupBy` — a quadratic shadow of `builtins.groupBy`, which den-hoag also uses directly at
  `lib/query.nix`. 26 `prelude.groupBy` sites in lib/, several on per-node paths. Both coexist.
  den-hoag-4kh.53.48.
· `gen-dispatch` `dispatch` — NO INDEX. `foldl' stepGroup` over `groupOrder`, every step re-scanning the full
  flat `rules` list; `|R| x |G|` candidate-predicate evaluations per call, paid unconditionally. Exhaustive:
  `rules` appears in exactly TWO executable positions library-wide. ★ The no-memo is DELIBERATE and
  documented ("dispatch keeps no cross-pass already-fired bookkeeping") — CONFLUENCE BOUGHT WITH
  RECOMPUTATION. That is a defensible theory choice AND a cost; any change must engage the confluence
  argument, not just the counter. den-hoag-yl3.
· `gen-algebra` `record.foldLayersTraced` — fleet-independent (good), but `allKeySet` is an EAGER `//`-fold
  rebuilding the accumulator each step, O(L x K) PAID WHOLE EVEN TO READ ONE FIELD; and the `semilattice-set`
  strategy runs `builtins.elem` inside a loop, O(m^2). den-hoag-yl3.
· `gen-scope` `paramAttr` — `eval` memoises the ATTRIBUTE, but the memoised value is a FUNCTION, and applying
  it to the param is plain application which Nix never memoises. ⇒ per-(host,user) questions recompute on
  every read: the |H| x |U| factor, UNMEMOISED. den-hoag-yl3.
· `gen-pipe` — UNDER SCAN NOW (owner-directed, den-hoag-4kh.36). The live question is whether the
  composition den-hoag records as "built and never applied" is already provided by gen-pipe, which would make
  den-hoag's gap WIRING rather than a missing capability.

★ AND THE ONE THAT IS NOT A GEN DEFECT, recorded so it is not mistaken for one: `gen-edge`'s delivery record
carrying no `from` field is CORRECT AND DELIBERATE for a delivery model whose identity is (S,T,P,M,K). It is
disqualifying for a TOPOLOGY edge, which is why den-hoag's containment migration routes through the Model-Q
adjacency pool instead. Wrong-model, not broken. den-hoag-5bp.

title: [ci] THE PROJECTION ANCHOR IS VACUOUS ON THE ONE PREDICATE IT EXISTS FOR — projection.nix pins projectClass == classSubtreeAt + route delta, but the two sides differ ONLY under a reroute, and NO fixture or corpus config declares one
description:
MEASURED at 4b61112 by an independent verifier while establishing which E10(b) reading shipped. Filed separately from den-hoag-4kh.41 because it is an INSTRUMENT defect, and it will outlive that bead's fix.

THE ANCHOR: ci/tests/projection.nix pins
    projectClass id C == classSubtreeAt id C ++ <route remap delta>
THE TWO SIDES ARE NOT THE SAME FUNCTION. classSubtreeAt reads class-seeds, which APPLIES the relocation relation P(n) — relocationsOf, preimageOf, srcOrder, frameAt. projectClass reads classSliceOf, the RAW per-aspect extraction that goes straight to content.${class}. POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE PREDICATE: grepping reroute|relocat|injects over the WHOLE of lib/attributes/output-modules.nix returns ONLY PROSE, while the same grep over lib/attributes/class-modules.nix hits the live filters.
★★ SO THE TWO SIDES DIVERGE EXACTLY WHEN A RELOCATION EXISTS — AND NO RELOCATION EXISTS ANYWHERE THE ANCHOR CAN SEE. comm -12 over 'grep -rl reroute ci/' and 'grep -rl reachEdge ci/' is EMPTY: NO TEST FILE CONTAINS BOTH. No fixture under ci/tests/_fixtures/ or ci/tests/_lib/ declares a reroute AT ALL. ci/tests/class-relocation.nix — the only relocation suite — drives class-seeds.compute DIRECTLY against a synthetic self, never building a reach and never calling projectClass.
⇒ THE ANCHOR IS GREEN ON AN INPUT CLASS THAT CANNOT DISTINGUISH ITS TWO SIDES. It certifies an equivalence it has never tested.

★ WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY VACUOUS TEST, and why it gets its own bead: AN ANCHOR IS WHAT A READER TRUSTS *INSTEAD OF* READING. den-hoag-gg8 is a vacuous leaf beside a known-red; den-hoag-6jo enumerates 0/0 suites and spine-only assertions. THIS one states a STRUCTURAL EQUIVALENCE between two code paths, which is precisely the kind of claim someone cites to avoid re-deriving. It certified that projectClass and classSubtreeAt agree, while den-hoag-4kh.41's P0 defect is that THEY DO NOT.

★★ AND IT IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A FOLLOW-UP. Any repair to projectClass (den-hoag-4kh.41) is UNFALSIFIABLE while this holds: the anchor will stay green through the defect AND through the fix, so nothing can demonstrate the repair worked. THE FIXTURE MUST LAND FIRST — one that declares a reroute AND builds a reach, so the two sides are forced apart before either is trusted to agree.
REQUIRED SHAPE, from the same measurement: the divergence needs an aspect arriving at a node BY REACH (structural subtree or reach-edge target) whose content carries a channel key subject to a reroute declared at the projecting node. class-relocation.nix's synthetic-self harness cannot produce this — it bypasses reach by construction.

GENERAL FORM WORTH SWEEPING FOR, and den-hoag-6jo's ~140 unadjudicated candidates are where to look: AN EQUIVALENCE ASSERTION BETWEEN TWO PATHS IS VACUOUS UNLESS THE CORPUS CONTAINS AN INPUT ON WHICH THEY WOULD DIFFER. Equality-shaped tests read as strong and are the easiest to satisfy trivially — both sides computing nothing agree perfectly.

title: [ci] ATTRIBUTION: the 12 den-pipe compose-commitment aborts — the largest known-red cluster, tracked nowhere in the tree and named only in a commit message
description:
MEASURED at HEAD by a read-only suite sweep, cross-checked against e6c8edc's commit message which enumerates the 18 known-red by cause.

THE CLUSTER: 12 tests reporting ☢️ (nix-unit's EVAL-ERROR marker, distinct from ❌ value-mismatch), all in flake.tests.den-pipe, each trace ending in the same errors.nix abort:
  'compose commitment: policy ... produced a pipeOp declaration carrying a derived-channel DAG or a delivery route from its BODY'
They are the single largest known-red cluster — 12 of 18 — and ★ grep -rn '9xo' over ci/ parity/ *.md returns ZERO HITS, so NO BEAD ID APPEARS ANYWHERE NEAR THEM. POSITIVE CONTROL SAME RUN: the identical regex matched den-hoag-4kh in CLAUDE.md, so the instrument fires. e6c8edc's message says 'zero unattributed' — TRUE OF THE COMMIT MESSAGE, FALSE OF THE TREE. A git log is one rebase away from being the sole record of why a third of the suite is red.
This bead exists to BE that attribution. Filed as one bead for one cause rather than twelve, because the twelve share a single abort message and a single mechanism — and ★ THAT SHARING IS ITSELF A LIMIT WORTH RECORDING: a msg-regex xfail declaration CANNOT DISTINGUISH THESE TWELVE FROM ONE ANOTHER, so any gate keyed on the message text will accept any one of them standing in for any other.

RELATED, and the relationship needs settling rather than assuming: den-hoag-4kh.36 (pipe run-wiring gap: pipe.append/filter/to not applied, 15 wrong-value divergences all commented out) and den-hoag-4kh.53.64 (O1, the ops DAG built-never-applied) look like THE SAME CONSTRUCT TRACKED TWICE. If these twelve aborts are that construct's third face, three beads describe one defect. Establish before scoping.
★ AND THE SOUNDNESS CAVEAT THAT MATTERS FOR THE GATE: den-hoag-4kh.51 records that a suppression path's soundness rests on the staged pre-pass scheduled for retirement (register den-hoag-4kh.17 entry 3). If these twelve are downstream of that, THEY WILL GO GREEN WHEN THE PRE-PASS RETIRES — and under a 'known-fail that starts passing must fail the gate' rule that turns a successful retirement into a gate failure unless the declarations retire in the same change. See den-hoag-9uv.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ TWO CORRECTIONS, MEASURED — one to my own framing, one that matters for any msg-based declaration.

1. THE TYPE IS ThrownError, NOT AN ABORT. lib/errors.nix binds fail as a plain builtins.throw of "den-hoag: CTX: MSG". The codebase's prose says "aborts"; the primitive is throw. Verified both raised directly from errors.opsInBody AND forced through lib.evalModules to reproduce the real optionalValue.value frames: BOTH ThrownError. The module system changes neither type nor text.
★ CONSEQUENCE THAT CUTS AGAINST AN EARLIER CLAIM: tryEval CAN catch these, so the dead scaffold arm would have gone GREEN on all 12. The scaffold's weakness on this cluster is NOT that it fails to catch them — it is that it DISCARDS type AND msg, so it cannot tell one from another, nor from any unrelated throw.

2. ★★ MY BRIEF SAID THE 12 SHARE ONE MESSAGE SO NO msg REGEX COULD DISTINGUISH THEM. THAT IS WRONG. It is ONE TEMPLATE, but THE INTERPOLATED POLICY NAME DIFFERENTIATES. The message, verbatim as nix-unit sees it — read out by deliberately supplying a NON-MATCHING msg so nix-unit prints what it caught:

  den-hoag: compose commitment: policy `NAME` produced a `pipeOp` declaration carrying a derived-channel
  DAG or a delivery route from its BODY. Those seed the ONE fleet gen-pipe compose before the eval and are
  ctx-independent by contract, so they are declared as data in `ops`; only per-node SITE MARKS are emitted
  from the body

ELEVEN DISTINCT NAMES OVER TWELVE TESTS:
  pipe-broadcast.nix  test-broadcast-source-transform      __kindInclude__user__policy__0
  pipe-policy.nix     test-pipe-filter                     __aspectInclude__filter-tcp
                      test-pipe-transform                  __aspectInclude__transform-items
                      test-pipe-fold                       __aspectInclude__fold-nums
                      test-pipe-for                        __aspectInclude__for-items
                      test-pipe-combined-stages            __aspectInclude__combined
                      test-pipe-multi-policy-merge         __aspectInclude__policy-a
                      test-pipe-multi-policy-multi-stage   __aspectInclude__policy-a
                      test-pipe-as-basic                   __aspectInclude__rename-pipe
                      test-pipe-as-with-transform          __aspectInclude__derive-rules
                      test-pipe-as-with-to                 __aspectInclude__as-and-to
                      test-pipe-as-no-emitter-quirk        __aspectInclude__backends-to-monitoring

⇒ A msg REGEX DISTINGUISHES ELEVEN. THE ONE INDISTINGUISHABLE PAIR IS test-pipe-multi-policy-merge versus
test-pipe-multi-policy-multi-stage, both __aspectInclude__policy-a. State that limit wherever these are declared.
★ AND A SEPARATE BRITTLENESS: __kindInclude__user__policy__0 IS POSITIONALLY INDEXED. A msg pinning it breaks
when the policy list in that file is reordered — a declaration that silently re-targets as the world changes,
which is the standing hazard about description-scoped rather than identity-scoped instructions.

SUITE RUN, exit read on the line after the command with no pipe: nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests.den-pipe gave
EXIT=1, 19/31 successful, exactly 12 eval-error markers.

★★ TECHNIQUE WORTH ADOPTING, and it is how the message above was obtained: DELIBERATELY SUPPLY A NON-MATCHING
msg SO NIX-UNIT PRINTS THE TEXT IT ACTUALLY CAUGHT. Reading the expected text out of the instrument beats
transcribing it from source, because the source is a template and what reaches nix-unit is the interpolation.

title: [ci] VACUOUS-OVER-EMPTY assertions, sibling AND intra-leaf: 'all p [ ]' is true over the very list a neighbour measures as 0 — and the intra-leaf form is invisible inside a red test until declaring it freezes the vacuity
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 at HEAD 6f30460, found while specifying the three-state gate (den-hoag-9uv). Not filed by the finder; returned to the orchestrator per the review gate.

ci/tests/pipe-consume.nix. test-derived-channels-consumed asserts length derivedAdded == 3 AND MEASURES 0 — it is one of the four known-red measured-empty seed failures enumerated in e6c8edc.
★ ITS SIBLING test-derived-channel-names asserts builtins.all (c: ...) derivedAdded OVER THE SAME EMPTY LIST. 'all p [ ]' IS TRUE BY DEFINITION. So it is GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON, it is NOT in the failing set, and it carries ZERO INFORMATION about the property it names.

★★ WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: the three-state gate design (den-hoag-9uv) will park test-derived-channels-consumed as a declared xfail. THE MOMENT IT DOES, THE FILE READS AS 'one known-red, one green' — and the green is vacuous. A reader, and a gate, would both conclude the derived-channel NAMES property is verified. It is not, and it cannot be until the list is non-empty. PARKING THE SIBLING WITHOUT ADDING A NON-EMPTINESS CONTROL CONVERTS A VISIBLE FAILURE INTO AN INVISIBLE ONE.
⇒ This is precisely why 9uv's decision 3 REJECTS COUNT-BASED SUITE ASSERTIONS: a count sees a NON-EMPTY SUITE CARRYING ZERO INFORMATION and reports it as covered.

FIX SHAPE (not applied; the finder was read-only): assert non-emptiness of derivedAdded in the same expression, so the 'all' cannot pass vacuously — the paired-positive-control-at-the-same-forcing-depth idiom the tree already uses in ci/tests/family-member-uniqueness.nix. Then the names property fails loudly alongside its sibling instead of certifying it.
GENERAL FORM, worth sweeping for: any builtins.all / builtins.any-negated assertion over a list produced by the SAME expression a known-red test measures as empty. den-hoag-6jo enumerates 87 count-only and 72 absence-shaped assertions of which ~140 remain unadjudicated; this is a WORKED INSTANCE of that class, found by accident rather than by the sweep.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ SCOPE QUESTION RAISED BY THE GATE-SPEC REVISION, 2026-07-29: THE SAME VACUITY EXISTS INSIDE A SINGLE LEAF, AND THIS BEAD NAMES pipe-consume ONLY.
compat-scope-local-firing.test-expansion-collapses-to-one-rule has a 3-field expr over w6SubRules. subRuleCount = 0 is the known failure — and its TWO SIBLINGS IN THE SAME ATTRSET, allFiresAtHost and noStratumSuffix, are builtins.all ... w6SubRules, TRUE BECAUSE THE LIST IS EMPTY.
⇒ SAME MECHANISM AS THIS BEAD (all p [ ] is true over the very list a sibling measures as 0), DIFFERENT GRANULARITY: there the vacuous assertion is a separate test, here it is a FIELD OF THE FAILING TEST'S OWN expr. Declaring the leaf as a whole-attrset xfail would FREEZE TWO VACUOUS TRUTHS AS EXPECTATIONS, and they would keep reading as verified after the seed is fixed.
THE REVISION'S REMEDY: narrow the declaration to builtins.length w6SubRules and split the two alls into a non-vacuous sibling, red on landing.
⇒ DECIDE: widen this bead to 'vacuous-over-empty assertions wherever they sit, including intra-leaf', or file a second bead for the intra-leaf class. ★ THE INTRA-LEAF FORM IS THE MORE DANGEROUS ONE — a separate vacuous test is at least visible as a green line, while a vacuous FIELD is invisible inside a red test and becomes an expectation the moment that test is declared.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ RESOLVED — **WIDEN THIS BEAD TO COVER INTRA-LEAF VACUITY.** Orchestrator ruling; I raised it as an owner question and it was not one.
The mechanism is identical: an assertion that is TRUE BECAUSE A LIST IS EMPTY, over the very list a sibling measures as 0. Only the granularity differs — pipe-consume's is a separate test, compat-scope-local-firing's are FIELDS of the failing test's own expr (allFiresAtHost / noStratumSuffix, both builtins.all over w6SubRules).
★ AND I ALREADY ARGUED THE INTRA-LEAF FORM IS THE MORE DANGEROUS ONE, which settles which bead should own it: a vacuous SIBLING is at least visible as a green line someone could question; a vacuous FIELD is INVISIBLE INSIDE A RED TEST and silently becomes an expectation the moment that test is declared. A bead that covers only the visible form would leave the invisible one to be rediscovered.
SCOPE NOW: vacuous-over-empty assertions wherever they sit — separate test, sibling field, or any assertion whose truth depends on the emptiness of a list another assertion measures as empty.
REMEDY UNCHANGED IN SHAPE: a non-emptiness control at the SAME forcing depth, per den-hoag-6jo's named model (ci/tests/family-member-uniqueness.nix). For the intra-leaf case the declaration narrows to the count and the two alls split into a sibling that is red on landing.

title: [ci] FOUR SUITES ARE SILENTLY EMPTY (0/0 = exit 0), EIGHT MORE ARE ONE PARKED TEST AWAY, and the kernel-purity tripwire scans 32 of 49 core files with no drift guard
description:
MEASURED at HEAD 6f30460, read-only. Test graph derived from the EVALUATED tree, not from text: nix eval ./ci#tests --apply 'ts: mapAttrs (n: v: attrNames v) ts' -> 172 suites, 1937 leaves, all test-prefixed, no suite name starts with 'test', no third nesting level. Classes A and E below are EXHAUSTIVE over 100 percent of ci/ and parity/; the judgement classes are NOT — see the honesty split at the end.

★ CLASS A — FOUR 0/0 TARGETS. Each 'nix-unit --flake ./ci#tests.<x>' prints '0/0 successful' and EXITS 0:
  delivery-chain (ci/tests/delivery-chain.nix, flake.tests.delivery-chain = { })
  den-delivery (den-behavioral/hm-host-forward-hm-class.nix, 2 tests commented out in place)
  den-forward-each-mutual (den-behavioral/forward-each-mutual.nix, 1 commented)
  den-nixpkgs-forward-positional (den-behavioral/nixpkgs-forward-positional.nix, 1 commented)
All four are '= { }' with tests commented out IN PLACE, so they contribute 0 to the 1937 total and #tests is unaffected. ★ THE FALSE PASS IS REACHABLE ONLY BY TARGETING THE SUITE — WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT A BISECTING AGENT DOES. den-hoag-9xo.78 records ONE of these; the pattern had recurred three more times unnoticed, which says it reproduces faster than it is caught. FIX: delete the flake.tests.<name> ATTRIBUTE, not its contents.

CLASS A-ADJACENT — EIGHT ONE TEST FROM SILENT. Parking the single named test makes the target green-and-empty:
  den-coscoped-provides-selfblock, den-flakeoutput-namespace-nav, den-nested-aspects, den-provides-fn-facet, den-provides-nixos-lift, den-provides-nav-registry, namespace-origin-identity, and ★ zero-machinery.

★★ zero-machinery IS THE ALARMING ONE: it is simultaneously one-test-from-silent AND the A1 KERNEL-PURITY TRIPWIRE named in CLAUDE.md. And it has a second, independent hole: ci/tests/zero-machinery.nix scans a HARDCODED libFiles list of 32 — MEASURED 32 OF 49 core lib/**.nix FILES. SEVENTEEN ARE NEVER SCANNED, and they are the kernel-arc files: staged-resolution.nix, concern-productions.nix, identity.nix, edges.nix, products.nix, receivers.nix, renders.nix among them. A forbidden token in any of them is INVISIBLE. No readDir drift guard, and no positive control that hasInfix can return true at all. NOT AN ACTIVE MISS TODAY — all three forbidden tokens were checked across all 17 and they are clean, positive control grep -Fc let lib/staged-resolution.nix = 12 proving the instrument reaches those files — IT BECOMES AN ACTIVE MISS SILENTLY, ON THE NEXT CORE FILE ADDED. ★ THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS IN-TREE: ci/tests/boundary.nix:374's test-core-file-list-complete compares its list against a readDir-derived set. Copy it. A third hardcoded list with the same hole sits in compat-identity-boundary.nix (5 entries).

OTHER CONFIRMED VACUITIES:
  golden-index.nix — present = hasInfix "${e.name} =" (readFile e.file). The predicate is a SOURCE-TEXT SUBSTRING, so a COMMENTED-OUT '# test-golden-... =' MATCHES. Parking by commenting is THIS REPO'S ESTABLISHED PRACTICE — it produced all four 0/0 suites above — so the guard is defeated by the repo's own normal method. Currently correct BY LUCK (all 7 goldens verified live against the evaluated tree). FIX: assert against config.flake.tests.<suite> ? <name>, not readFile.
  b2-two-stratum.nix:219 and :225 — expr = (tryEval (...).schedule).success; expected = true. MEASURED: structural.schedule = { attrGraph; condensation; edges; equations }. tryEval FORCES WHNF ONLY, so all four members — including condensation, the actual topo result — stay UNFORCED. It passes for any 4-key attrset whose every value is a throw. The .schedule select is decorative: the file's own header says the throw is at runResolve CONSTRUCTION, so the sibling abort test fires before .schedule is reached. Both green, NEITHER OBSERVES THE SCHEDULE. FIX: (tryEval (deepSeq (...).schedule.condensation true)).success, or assert the condensation's stratum ORDER.
  linearization.nix:141-152 — length defaultOrder == 8 and length reversedOrder == 8, under a comment claiming 'fewer-fixed-dims slices PRECEDE the more-fixed ones (count-major key)'. Only positions 0 and 7 are pinned. ANY PERMUTATION OF POSITIONS 1-6 PASSES.
  compat-provides-desugar.nix:247-250 — seq is WHNF, so the sentinel assertion passes on ANY throw reachable at WHNF, not specifically the un-desugared-provides sentinel. Fail-SAFE direction, so not fail-open, but it does not pin the identity it names.

★ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DISPATCH PREMISE, both refuting facts the orchestrator supplied:
  test-x86-route-gated-empty IS ALREADY FIXED at HEAD — compat-entity-fields.nix:210-219 now carries its positive control INSIDE the same expression (firesAtAarch64 alongside gatedOffAtX86) with a comment stating the vacuity and the reason for the pairing. The class-B exemplar named in the brief is not live.
  den-delivery is NOT the only 0/0 target; there are four.

★★ THE MODELS TO COPY, recorded because a fix should imitate them rather than invent: family-member-uniqueness.nix:71-88 (a paired positive control AT THE SAME FORCING DEPTH, with the reasoning written down); boundary.nix:374 (the readDir drift guard); boundary.nix:358,395 (NON-EMPTY expected lists that serve as in-run proof the scanner is live, which is what makes the sibling '== [ ]' at :390 meaningful); no-fleet-flags.nix:170,224 (perClassRead asserted true).

★★★ EXHAUSTIVE vs SAMPLED — THE AGENT MADE ONLY ONE OF THESE CLAIMS AND THE DISTINCTION IS LOAD-BEARING:
  EXHAUSTIVE, machine-enumerated over 100 percent of both trees: the 4 empty targets and 8 one-away (derived from the EVALUATED tree); the untracked-file check (git ls-files ci/ = 209 tracked, positive control large-not-zero, comm -13 -> ZERO untracked, clean); the three-state absence. Site censuses: 182 non-comment tryEval sites (91 with on-line deepSeq), 72 standalone absence-shaped expected values, 87 count-only length/attrNames assertions of which 32 carry an order or content word in the test name or comment.
  NOT EXHAUSTIVE: which of those 159 candidates are ACTUALLY vacuous. Roughly 15 were adjudicated by reading fixtures and siblings, chosen by ranking source-scan and architecture-invariant guards first. ~140 REMAIN ENUMERATED BUT UNADJUDICATED.
  ★ AND THE AGENT MEASURED ITS OWN FALSE-POSITIVE RATE: its automated tryEval direction pass produced 5 candidates and 2 WERE FALSE POSITIVES (compat-surface.nix:187, whose accept helper does deepSeq OFF-LINE so the window missed it; and compat-provides-desugar.nix:248) — 40 percent. That bounds how much the remainder would shrink under reading. It does NOT bound false negatives, which are unestimated.
  COVERAGE: ~3.5k of 53.8k lines read, about 6 percent. NEVER OPENED includes the largest files — materialization.nix (126K), edge-substrate.nix (53K, 27 tryEval sites), compat-feature-severed.nix (44K, 17 sites). ★ The agent names edge-substrate.nix + compat-feature-severed.nix (44 tryEval sites between them, both unopened) as where it expects the next findings.

title: [kernel] RESOLVED-DEAD: lib/edges.nix's assembleEdges/nestProducer are a DELIVERY-model construct that erases the tail and hashes the head — cannot carry the topology migration; 3 salvage items named
description:
MEASURED at HEAD 6f30460 by a read-only kernel census. Command: grep -rn 'assembleEdges|nestProducer' --include='*.nix' lib ci parity.

FINDING: 27 hits, and NOT ONE is a live kernel consumer. lib/edges.nix defines assembleEdges (:262) and nestProducer (:411); lib/default.nix:2789 merely RE-EXPORTS them; the only callers are ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix and ci/tests/nest-producers.nix. Only materializeEdges is live (lib/default.nix:1818). lib/edges.nix SAYS SO ITSELF at :238, verbatim: 'SYNTHETIC-ONLY in this step: no live producer routes through here yet'.

★ WHY THIS IS A P1 AND NOT A TIDY-UP. The census's own judgement, and it is about the owner's stated problem (agents cannot reason about this system): 'A reader who opens lib/edges.nix first — THE OBVIOUS ENTRY POINT for "what graph is this?" — reads 524 lines of edge-kind registry, override tier, identity assembly and nest production, and IT IS ALL UNREACHED FROM THE LIVE PATH. The single sentence that says so is at line 238, BURIED MID-FILE. This is, in my judgement, the largest single legibility trap in the kernel.'
Compounding it (den-hoag-5ae): the edge-kind REGISTRY those 524 lines serve registers nine kinds — contains, include, kindOf, member, reach, reach-suppress, nest, defer, demand — and ONLY 'demand' HAS A LIVE PRODUCER. So the file that looks like the answer to the topology question describes a graph the kernel does not build.

★★ THIS NEEDS AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A PATCH, AND THE TWO READINGS DIFFER IN KIND:
  (a) DEAD CODE. Delete edges.nix's unreached half and its two test files. Simplification, immediate legibility win, and it stops the next reader modelling the kernel on a graph that is not built.
  (b) SCAFFOLDING FOR THE EDGE MODEL THAT IS SUPPOSED TO LAND. den-hoag-4kh.35 records that the 'to' per-aspect consumer-addressed delivery seam — THE ONE NAMED NET-NEW KERNEL BINDING SEAM in the WS-B design — exists in no tree, no bead and no tracker. If assembleEdges is that seam's substrate, deleting it discards the construction and the tests that pin it.
Reading (b) is NOT speculative: den-hoag-5ae shows position and membership are currently carried as node PAYLOAD (__coords, __containment, __root, __entry) behind four drifting strip lists, and the fix for that is EXACTLY to make them edges. An edge substrate is what that fix needs. So this may be the right substrate arriving before its consumers rather than dead weight.
⇒ THE DECIDING QUESTION, and it is answerable by reading rather than by ruling: DOES assembleEdges's SHAPE MATCH WHAT THE PAYLOAD-TO-EDGE MIGRATION WOULD NEED? If yes it is scaffolding and should be documented as such AT THE TOP OF THE FILE, not at :238. If no it is dead and should go. Filed as a question because answering it wrong in either direction is expensive: deleting a needed construction, or keeping 524 lines of misleading entry point.

DO NOT ACT ON THIS WITHOUT THE ANSWER. Recorded per the standing rule that an unshipped finding is a review candidate, not a task.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ ANSWERED — VERDICT: **DEAD** for the topology migration. Independent read-only analysis, HIGH confidence, at HEAD 6f30460. This bead asked whether the unreached half is dead code or scaffolding the payload-to-edge migration needs. It is neither exactly: it is COMPLETE SCAFFOLDING FOR A DIFFERENT CONCERN.

★★ THE FINDING THAT DECIDES IT — THERE ARE TWO EDGE MODELS AND THIS BEAD WAS ASKING ABOUT THE WRONG ONE. The tree names them itself; lib/default.nix's relationEdges re-export comment reads 'the FLAT plain-string relation edge set ... the live SOURCE den.query consumes'.
  MODEL D (delivery) — gen-edge's record: { source; target; path; mode; adapt; annotations; kind }. ★ THERE IS NO 'from' FIELD. source is a CONTENT descriptor (sources.collected / synthesize / value / keyedValue / rewalk); target is a PLACE (targets.root / targets.output). This is (S,T,P,M,K), 'this content goes to this place'. Live via deliveryEdgesAt, demand.nix toEdges, edgesFor, materializeEdges, the frozen parity trace.
  MODEL Q (adjacency) — a flat triple { id; kind; from; to; data?; stratum? } where from/to are PLAIN NODE-ID STRINGS. The typing is proved by lib/query.nix's perLabelFromEdges doing builtins.groupBy (e: e.from) kindEdges — an attrset key, so from MUST be a string. Live via relationEdges, denQuery, mkRelAccessor, mkRelQuery, edgesBelowStratum, claimEdgesOf.
⇒ ★ MODEL Q IS THE SUBSTRATE THAT TURNS A PAYLOAD READ INTO A QUERY. IT ALREADY EXISTS, IT IS LIVE, AND IT CARRIES gen-graph's FULL REGEX-OVER-LABELS ENGINE (five modes: all/paths/visible/layers/fixpoint). lib/edges.nix's unreached half speaks MODEL D.

WHY assembleEdges CANNOT CARRY THE MIGRATION, from its own body: its INTENT is Model-Q-shaped (from and to both present, both entity ids), but in building the record it computes from = sideIdentity i.from AND THEN DISCARDS IT — 'from' survives only as a SUBSTRING OF THE PRODUCER-SUPPLIED id STRING, by convention. And 'to' is HASHED: to.instanceId = identity.instanceId {...} = hashString "sha256", a CONTENT ADDRESS, not a node id — while denQuery's 'where' is a node-id predicate (concern-relations mkRelQuery: 'relation endpoints ARE scope node-ids'). ⇒ AN assembleEdges OUTPUT CANNOT ANSWER parentOf, contains OR kindOf. HEAD IS A HASH, TAIL IS GONE. It is the opposite direction from the migration.
CORROBORATION: identity.edgeId { kind; fromInstanceId; toInstanceId; dataFingerprint } — the ONE function naming an edge by BOTH endpoints — is NEVER CALLED by assembleEdges and has ZERO lib/ consumers. POSITIVE CONTROL same predicate same run: instanceId (minus identity.nix) DOES find a real lib/ consumer at edges.nix:290.
AND THE TESTS AGREE: every pin in ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix is about the DELIVERY record and its TRACE identity (kind label, the frozen (T,P,S,M,K) sort key, unknown-kind throw, source keyed by readable id). ★ THE ONE ENDPOINT READ ACROSS BOTH SUITES is ci/tests/nest-producers.nix:293 fromEntity = p.intent.from.entityId — IT READS THE INTENT, NEVER THE RECORD. The from-endpoint is an intent-stage fact that does not survive assembly.
nestProducer is not a topology producer either: its gate is compiledKinds ? p.parentKind && resolveReceiver {...} != null — a DELIVERY gate (does content flow into this slot), not a topology gate (does A contain B). Its own comment says 'the corpus producer set is EMPTY by construction'. Containment is TOTAL; nestProducer's output is a content-flow SUBSET, so it can never be the contains producer.

WHAT THEY WERE FOR, recorded by the tree at lib/edges.nix:238-239 verbatim: 'SYNTHETIC-ONLY in this step: no live producer routes through here yet (a live producer arrives with later spec steps)'. The §2.1 spec pipeline built ahead of its producers — and the producer that did arrive (nestProducer, §4.2/§4.6) is a CONTENT-MOUNT producer. Not abandoned scaffolding for topology; complete scaffolding for nest/defer content delivery, still awaiting its live fold.
★ ROUTING THE MIGRATION THROUGH IT WOULD REPRODUCE EXACTLY THE FAILURE THE REGISTER EXISTS TO PREVENT: __containment would become a nest-kind DELIVERY record whose ancestors you still cannot query, because the record has no tail — a fold dissolved while the data structure it folded over survives.

★ PARTIAL SALVAGE — THREE ITEMS, PRECISELY, AND TWO ARE NOT IN edges.nix:
  1. applyOverrides — KEEP. Model-Q NATIVE: matchesEdge does match.${coord} == (edge.${coord} or null) over [ "kind" "from" "to" "data" ] and runs on INTENTS, pre-record. Works unchanged on a flat { id; kind; from; to; data } triple. The one genuinely model-agnostic piece in the unreached half.
  2. preRegisteredStrata + compile + reservedNames — KEEP. This IS the registry the migration registers against, already live via edgeKindTable, and it is where the to = 'query' fix goes.
  3. ★ fleet.nix containmentPairs — KEEP, AND IT IS THE ACTUAL contains PRODUCER: ungated and TOTAL, emitting { parentId; parentKind; childId; childKind; childName } for every parent-child coordinate pair, already unit-tested. ONE map from a Model-Q contains triple. It lives in fleet.nix, NOT edges.nix.

WHAT THE MIGRATION ACTUALLY BUILDS (the gap between live Model-Q and the need):
  a contains producer: containmentPairs -> { id; kind = "contains"; from = parentId; to = childId } into the relationEdges pool. __containment then becomes denQuery { follow = "contains+"; } or relAt's closure. ★ AND THE UNION IS ALREADY HALF A QUERY TODAY: ancestorIds = prelude.unique (parentChain ++ containment) where parentChain = scope.ancestors self id — with contains edges that is ONE closure over the union graph, which also removes a per-node prelude.unique.
  preRegisteredStrata's structural rows need to = 'query' — see den-hoag-5ae's comment; the row shape currently cannot express it.
  a per-dim contains label (or a data.dim field) so __coords is recoverable as a KEYED inbound query rather than an unordered parent set.
  __entry STAYS (externally pinned by gen-select's adapter contract). __root moves to a NODE FIELD, not an edge.

The edge-set availability question is answered favourably: relationEdges is a STATIC registry-derived pool (resolution-relations.nix header: readsAttrs = [ ]), so it is available at the point the payload reads happen.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ THE SALVAGE ITEM I PROMOTED FROM THIS BEAD IS BROKEN. **`containmentPairs` IS NOT "ungated and total,
one map away from a contains triple".** I relayed that as a finding and put it in a spec brief. Measured and
refuted 2026-07-29 by a purpose-built probe.

MEASURED: `containmentPairs` emits `zone:z1 --rack--> rack:r2@zone:z1` — ★ **A NODE THAT DOES NOT EXIST**,
because the minted id is `rack:r2` while the pair's child-id uses the CELL rule UNCONDITIONALLY. And it
emits **NOTHING** for `zone:z1 contains rack:r1`, because no cell survives there.
⇒ ADOPTING IT WOULD DROP THE ZONE COORDINATE, giving cardinality 2 != 3, which takes the flat arm, which
SILENTLY DROPS THE LAYER — **the exact failure the migration exists to remove.** Building the new topology
on this producer would have reproduced the defect in the new representation, and the witness that would
catch it (`__containment` on the corpus) is itself blind — see below.
⇒ THE SPEC THEREFORE SPECIFIES A PRODUCER RATHER THAN ADOPTING THIS ONE. Correct call.

★ AND A SECOND, INDEPENDENT TRAP ON THE SAME SEAM: **`__containment` EXCLUDES BOTH THE P-PARENT DIM AND THE
LEAF DIM, SO IT IS EMPTY ON ANY 2-DIMENSIONAL FLEET — WHICH IS THE CORPUS SHAPE.** A `__containment` witness
run only against corpus fixtures CANNOT DISTINGUISH THE NEW QUERY FROM A STUB RETURNING `[ ]`. That is
precisely den-hoag-akj's shape arriving on the migration itself: an equality that both sides satisfy
trivially because no input in the corpus discriminates. The witness must use >= 3 DIMENSIONS.
★ THAT IS TWICE IN ONE DAY THAT A MIGRATION'S OWN CHECK WOULD HAVE BEEN VACUOUS ON THE CORPUS. The general
rule is now earned rather than asserted: BEFORE TRUSTING ANY WITNESS, NAME THE INPUT ON WHICH THE OLD AND
NEW PATHS DIFFER, AND PROVE THE CORPUS CONTAINS ONE.

★ SCOPE CORRECTION TO A FINDING I CARRIED FORWARD: "NO ORDERING CONSTRAINT" was established for `__coords`
ONLY. It does NOT generalise — `ancestorsOf` REVERSES a pre-order specifically for least-specific-first, and
its comment says the order is load-bearing. Carrying the no-ordering result across to containment would have
introduced a PRECEDENCE defect. A result proven for one binding is not a result about the concept.

WHAT THIS BEAD'S OTHER TWO SALVAGE ITEMS STILL BUY, unchanged: `applyOverrides` remains Model-Q-native and
usable; `preRegisteredStrata` + `compile` + `reservedNames` remain the registry the migration registers
against, and are where the projection-tag fix lands (den-hoag-1xl).

title: [compat] 8 of 8 comparable den templates are GREEN on v1 and FAIL on den-hoag at e6c8edc — six named blockers, so the template suite is not a live gate and nix-config is the only witness
description:
★★ MEASURED AT e6c8edc, BOTH ARMS, 2026-07-29. THE SINGLE CONCRETE WORK LIST BETWEEN
den-hoag AND ANY TEMPLATE-BASED GATE.

METHOD: each template evaluated on den v1 (clone at 99cc0c5a) AND on den-hoag e6c8edc,
with `--override-input den` applied to BOTH ARMS -- never a template's own pin, which is
unmaintained and is not an oracle. Templates copied to scratch; the den repo was not
touched.

★ 8 OF 8 COMPARABLE TEMPLATES: GREEN ON v1, FAIL ON den-hoag. Arm A passes and arm B
fails on every one, SO EVERY ONE IS A REAL den-hoag BLOCKER RATHER THAN TEMPLATE ROT.

  template              v1 arm                        den-hoag e6c8edc
  default               ["igloo"]                     fleet-context enrichment: environment `prod`
                                                      not in registry, available: []
  example               ["igloo"]                     attribute 'name' missing
  fleet-demo            [4 hosts]                     surface totality (C1): unknown `den.systems`
  minimal               ["igloo"]                     The option `flake' does not exist
  microvm               ["server"]                    attribute 'microvm' missing
  diagram-demo          [3 hosts]                     `lib.capture.captureFleet` retired-fx fleet diagnostic
  flake-parts-modules   ["igloo"]                     attribute 'packages-to-flake-parts' missing
  scoped-import-tree    ["igloo"]                     attempt to call something which is not a function
                                                      but a set { __findFile ... }
  (noflake FAILS ON BOTH ARMS with the same path error -- HARNESS, NOT A den-hoag BLOCKER.
   EXCLUDED AND NOT COUNTED.)

★ THE POLICY-RECORD MIGRATION FIXED NONE OF THEM. All FOUR blockers named by the
2026-07-28 design audit reproduce VERBATIM at e6c8edc -- the environments registry, the
`name` attribute, `den.systems`, and `packages-to-flake-parts` -- PLUS TWO THE AUDIT DID
NOT NAME: `captureFleet` and the `__findFile` call error.

⇒ ★★ THE TEMPLATE SUITE IS NOT A LIVE GATE ON THE COMPAT LAYER, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF
THIS BEAD. nix-config is the ONLY fleet in the corpus that evaluates, which means:
· every compat finding is currently witnessed by ONE fleet;
· nix-config is immune to den-hoag-4kh.53.2's A1 SOLELY by an accident of its own topology
  file, so the corpus cannot show that defect at all;
· any claim of the form "the corpus is green" covers a single witness, not a suite.
Several children of den-hoag-4kh.53 are written assuming templates are not a gate. THEY
REMAIN CORRECT TO ASSUME SO until this bead closes.

★ AND A METHOD NOTE WORTH MORE THAN THE LIST: THE CONTROL CORRECTED THE MEASURER
MID-RUN. `minimal` and `microvm` fail with `The option 'flake' does not exist` and
`attribute 'microvm' missing` -- both of which READ LIKE TEMPLATE ROT and would have been
discounted as such. The v1 arm shows BOTH GREEN. ⇒ WITHOUT THE TWO-ARM CONTROL, TWO REAL
den-hoag BLOCKERS WOULD HAVE BEEN DISMISSED AS SOMEONE ELSE'S PROBLEM. A one-arm template
run is not evidence about den-hoag.

SCOPE: this bead is the CENSUS, not the fixes. Each blocker is its own diagnosis -- some
may share a cause and the list must not be treated as six independent items until one
instance is chased to a mechanism. That method (one instance, chased, then ask whether the
class shares it) is what worked across the whole policy-record migration and what failed
every time it was skipped.

title: [DECISION 7] contentClass two arities — no gen mechanism carries a kind-level edge except gen-schema parent, and M2 dissolution may change the choice
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 7 -- `contentClass`'s TWO ARITIES. DOES A KIND-LEVEL `contentClass` LOWER
TO PER-INSTANCE EDGES, OR SURVIVE AS A KIND-LEVEL FACT?
★★ THE CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THIS HARD: NEITHER GEN MECHANISM (refs, relations) CARRIES A
KIND-LEVEL EDGE. THE ONLY ONE IS GEN-SCHEMA'S `parent`, WHICH IS FIXED AND FRAMEWORK-OWNED.
⇒ Choosing "survive as a kind-level fact" means either extending a gen mechanism to carry
kind-level edges, or keeping a den-hoag-only representation for it.
★ PREREQUISITES IF LOWERING, all three stated by the audit:
1. FIX A8 (relation edge targets are unvalidated and the failure is UNCATCHABLE by tryEval)
2. THREAD THE REFS BINDINGS
3. DECIDE THE COMPAT STORY
★ AND M2 IS ENTANGLED: `metaWithClass` exists precisely because `contentClass` is a field
whose value is not knowable when the record is built. Its dissolution (pass the resolver as
an argument) may change what this decision is choosing between -- take M2's shape into
account rather than deciding around the current one.

title: [DECISION 4] what may a kind-include string name? One answer makes a load-bearing den-hoag fixture wrong, and it blocks A4 guard
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 4 -- WHAT MAY A KIND-INCLUDE STRING NAME?
A4's union guard (`aspects union policies`) MAKES THE SUITE PASS WITHOUT MAKING THE POLICY
WORK -- a policy named in a kind-include string STILL RESOLVES TO AN EMPTY STUB and
contributes nothing. It only APPEARS to work because the policy ALSO fires fleet-wide.
★★ AND `ci/tests/compat-expose-gather.nix` IS EXACTLY THIS SHAPE AND IS LOAD-BEARING IN
DEN-HOAG'S OWN FIXTURES. So the decision is not hypothetical -- one answer makes a shipped
fixture wrong.
⇒ EITHER such a string MAY name a policy AND IS ROUTED AS ONE, OR IT MAY NOT AND DEN-HOAG'S
OWN FIXTURES ARE WRONG. There is no third option that leaves both standing.
★ The pattern for the guard already exists: `compile.nix` guards a SIBLING ARM with
`registry ? ${ref.key}`.
BLOCKS A4 -- do not add the guard before this is answered, or it silences the error without
fixing the behaviour.

title: [DECISION 5] do the concern-name collisions fold into the redesign or stand alone? 39 by enumeration now, or 40 by construction later
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 5 -- DO THE CONCERN-NAME COLLISIONS FOLD INTO THE REDESIGN OR STAND ALONE?
The measured defect is at den-hoag-4kh.53.27 (24 of 40 framework concern names build
silently; a kind named `policies` corrupts the scope graph WITH NO INSTANCE AUTHORED).
★ THE ARGUMENT FOR STANDING ALONE: the resolution -- derive the reserved set from den-hoag's
own declared concern-option names -- is MECHANICALLY ENUMERABLE, CLOSES 39 NAMES, and NEEDS
NO GEN CHANGE. It is cheap and it is a live corruption.
★ THE ARGUMENT FOR FOLDING: the audit locates the ROOT CAUSE in the §0 thesis -- THE
REGISTRATION PATH CANNOT DISTINGUISH A NAMESPACE HOLDING ENTITIES FROM ONE HOLDING FRAMEWORK
DECLARATIONS, because kinds mount at `options.den.<kindName>` WITH NO RESERVATION. A
redesign that separates those namespaces closes all 40 BY CONSTRUCTION rather than 39 by
enumeration.
⇒ THE DECISION IS WHETHER TO PAY FOR THE ENUMERATED FIX NOW KNOWING THE CONSTRUCTION MAY
RETIRE IT. Note decision 6 leans the same way and may subsume the reserved-names half
entirely.

title: [DECISION 6] framework kinds as ordinary declarations vs framework-ness as declared data — establish the effectiveClassEntries threading cost first
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 6 -- FRAMEWORK KINDS: ORDINARY DECLARATIONS (v1's SHAPE) VERSUS
FRAMEWORK-NESS AS DECLARED DATA. ★ OWNER LEANING: DECLARED DATA.
Making framework kinds ORDINARY DECLARATIONS deletes `metaAugment`, the `collector`
reserved-name branch AND the S9 keyset divergence TOGETHER -- v1's shape, which privileges
nothing.
★★ THE COST THAT COULD TURN A DELETION INTO A REDESIGN, and it must be established BEFORE
the ruling: the collector's per-instance `contentClass` function needs
`effectiveClassEntries`/`effectiveClassNames`, WHICH ARE CURRENTLY COMPUTED OUTSIDE THE
MODULE TREE. THAT THREADING IS THE RISK. The reserved-name guard must also be removed or
inverted.
★ NOTE: the reserved-names half MAY NOT NEED A HOME AT ALL if decision 5's derivation lands
-- so decisions 5 and 6 should be taken together, not separately.
★ AND E5 IS THE SAME DISEASE AT A SECOND SITE: den-hoag privileges `host` and `user` as
MERGE LITERALS while v1 declares all five of ITS builtins through the ordinary consumer
surface. A ruling for "framework-ness is declared data" should say whether it also governs
those two.

title: [DECISION 1] merge or distinct — is a host seen as cluster member and environment member one resolved view or two? Merge is only viable once G6 is fixed
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 1 -- MERGE OR DISTINCT. The audit calls this the one that changes the most
downstream.
WHEN `axon-01` IS SEEN AS A CLUSTER MEMBER AND AS AN ENVIRONMENT MEMBER, IS THAT ONE
RESOLVED VIEW OR TWO?
· MERGE -> the RBAC pattern applies (containment in P, cluster as a LABELLED EDGE, ONE
  node, ONE memo entry), AVAILABLE TODAY WITH NO GEN EXTENSION, and it DROPS 11 HOST SCOPES
  TO 8.
· DISTINCT -> two nodes, and ★ v1's CONTEXT-KEYED SCOPES ARE CORRECT AND STAY.
nix-config's data HINTS at merge; ★ NOT VERIFIED.
★★ PREREQUISITE THE DECISION DEPENDS ON: the audit's own corrections ledger refuted "one
node, several inherited views beats v1's context-keyed scopes" -- single-valued-per-node is
what makes gen-scope's `_eval` SOUND, and ★ `paramAttr` WITH A PER-PARAMETER MEMO *IS* v1's
DESIGN, CURRENTLY WORSE (G6). ⇒ MERGE IS ONLY VIABLE ONCE G6 IS FIXED. Decide G6 first or
decide this knowing it.

title: [DECISION 2] the excludes posture — partially overtaken: 4kh.21 already removed excludes from that node and 9xo.28 measured it subtree-scoped
description:
★ OWNER DECISION 2 -- THE `excludes` POSTURE, AND PER den-hoag-4kh.21 IT MUST COVER `deps`
AND `provision` IN ONE POSTURE: IMPLEMENT / REFUSE LOUDLY / DELETE THE SURFACE.
★ PARTIALLY OVERTAKEN -- read before deciding: 4kh.21's owner ruling of 2026-07-28 already
set the posture for `deps` and `provision` as NAMED-REJECT AT DEFINITION TIME, and
explicitly REMOVED `excludes` FROM THAT NODE on the grounds that it is a PARITY DEFECT WITH
LIVE CONSUMERS -- den v1 CONSUMES it and the corpus USES it with stated intent, so
named-rejecting it would reject a construct v1 honours.
★ AND THE SEMANTICS ARE NOW MEASURED (den-hoag-9xo.28, amended 2026-07-28):
`den.schema.<K>.excludes` IS SUBTREE-SCOPED in v1 -- `includes` fires ONLY at K-nodes,
`excludes` reaches K AND ALL DESCENDANTS -- so ★ A FLAT PER-KIND LIST CANNOT REPRESENT IT,
and the "excludes is includes' DUAL" justification was WITHDRAWN as the wrong reason for a
right answer.
⇒ WHAT REMAINS FOR THE OWNER: whether the SUBTREE representation gets built now or the
same-kind case (which is EVERY declaration that exists anywhere -- full census in 9xo.58)
stays with a NAMED ABORT on the descendant case. See also A3.
notes:
★★ THE QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN THE AUDIT'S, AND MUST BE RESTATED. Measured at e6c8edc
(den-hoag-4kh.53.1, closed): the landed code ALREADY IMPLEMENTS the settled semantics.
· SAME-KIND exclude: HONOURED. Measured -- `selects` [ "host" ] -> [ ], marker gone from
  materialized resolved-aspects.
· DESCENDANT-KIND exclude: ABORTS BY NAME. Measured, and the message states the extent
  mismatch and says refusing beats silently over-applying.
· ★ ingest.nix:238-242 ALREADY ENCODES THE 9xo.28 AMENDMENT IN SOURCE: an `includes`
  entry fires at K-NODES ONLY, an `excludes` entry reaches K AND ITS WHOLE SUBTREE, and
  "excludes is includes with a minus sign" is named as the wrong model. The withdrawn DUAL
  justification is already retired where it lived.
⇒ SO DO NOT ASK "what should excludes mean" -- THAT IS SETTLED AND SHIPPED. ASK:
★ DOES DEN-HOAG'S PER-KIND SELECTION REPRESENTATION NEED TO BECOME PER-INSTANCE (SUBTREE)
SELECTION, OR IS REFUSING THE DESCENDANT CASE THE ACCEPTED PERMANENT POSTURE?
Inputs to that: every schema-tier exclude declaration in existence is SAME-KIND (full
census at den-hoag-9xo.58), so the descendant case has NO corpus witness -- which by
feedback_den_surface_not_config does NOT discharge it, since the bar is den-surface
expressibility. And the refusal is currently LOUD, which is the standing posture for a
declared surface the engine does not honour (den-hoag-4kh.21).

title: [G17] [gen-graph] phaseOrder promises only A valid order while den-hoag stratum POSITIONS are load-bearing — strataLt can flip, so ABW condition 2 is not well-defined
description:
[G17] ARGUED. gen-graph's `phaseOrder` PROMISES LESS THAN DEN-HOAG NEEDS.
`order.nix` promises only *A* VALID TOPOLOGICAL ORDER, with an EXPLICIT CAVEAT that
consumers threading a phase's effect only AFTER the phase are output-invariant.
★★ DEN-HOAG IS NOT. Its STRATUM POSITIONS ARE LOAD-BEARING -- `stratum-scope.nix`
`strataLt` drives `edgesBelowStratum`, `ceilingGate`, and STRATIFIED NEGATION.
⇒ TWO INDEPENDENT STRATA CAN SWAP BETWEEN VALID ORDERS, FLIPPING `strataLt`, TURNING A
LEGAL READ ILLEGAL. Silently, and only on some evaluations.
RESOLUTION: A `tieBreak` PARAMETER (default lexicographic) PLUS A DOCUMENTED
STABLE-ORDERING GUARANTEE for independent phases. NO NEW ALGORITHM. den-hoag then DROPS
`compileStrata`'s placement code and keeps only its seed set and reserved-name guards.
★ CONNECTS TO THE NEGATION WORK ALREADY TRACKED AT den-hoag-4kh.51/4kh.52: ABW condition 2
requires a negated read's definition to sit STRICTLY BELOW. If `strataLt` can flip between
runs, that requirement is not merely unenforced -- IT IS NOT WELL-DEFINED.

title: [G6] [gen-scope] paramAttr has no per-parameter cache and the file header claims exactly-once for all attributes — fixing it is what makes the merge option viable
description:
[G6] ARGUED. `paramAttr` CITES A GUARANTEE IT DOES NOT PROVIDE -- AND SO DOES THE FILE
HEADER, WHICH IS THE WORSE HALF.
`gen-scope/lib/resolve.nix` `paramAttr` is BARE ETA-EXPANSION WITH NO PER-PARAMETER CACHE
-- `_eval` memoises the CLOSURE, never its APPLICATIONS, so EVERY VIEW RECOMPUTES FOREVER.
Cited to Sloane 2010 / JastAdd, ★ WHERE PARAMETERIZED ATTRIBUTES ARE CACHED PER PARAMETER.
★★ THE OVERCLAIM IS NOT ONLY ON THE FUNCTION. `gen-scope/lib/eval.nix` header: "Every
attribute evaluates EXACTLY ONCE PER NODE -- including on dynamically synthesized nodes
(Vogt et al., 1989)." The memo is per (node, attrName), so FOR A PARAMETERIZED ATTRIBUTE
THE THUNK IS MEMOISED AND EVERY APPLICATION RECOMPUTES. ⇒ THE BLANKET HEADER CLAIM IS FALSE
FOR THAT ATTRIBUTE CLASS -- AND THE HEADER IS WHAT A READER TRUSTS BEFORE EVER REACHING
`paramAttr`. FIX BOTH.
★ CONNECTS TO THE §0 THESIS via the audit's own corrections ledger: "one node, several
inherited views, beats v1's context-keyed scopes" was REFUTED -- single-valued-per-node is
what makes `_eval` sound, and ★ `paramAttr` WITH A PER-PARAMETER MEMO *IS* v1's DESIGN,
CURRENTLY WORSE. So fixing G6 is not hygiene; it is what makes the merge option in §12.1
viable.

title: [G12] den-hoag runs a SECOND content-delivery engine in parallel with gen-edge, and edges.nix makes it permanent — the highest-value single item in the inventory
description:
★★★ THE HIGHEST-VALUE SINGLE ITEM IN THE INVENTORY, and it is NOT a line-count argument.
ARGUED.
`edge.materialize` IS CALLED ONCE, in `outputFor` (`output-modules.nix`), whose only
consumers are A COMPAT VERB AND THE PARITY ORACLE. ★ WHAT BUILDS THE ARTIFACT IS
`terminalModulesAt = projectClass`, A HAND-ROLLED `concatMap`.
★ THE FILE CONTRADICTS ITSELF THREE TIMES: its header calls the materialize fold "the only
content path (A15)"; a later comment says projection "supersedes the emission model
entirely"; a third says the built content is "not this fold".
★★ SO DEN-HOAG RUNS A SECOND CONTENT-DELIVERY ENGINE (`projectClass` + `lib/nest.nix`,
~300 code lines) IN PARALLEL WITH GEN-EDGE'S -- and `edges.nix` MAKES IT PERMANENT by
declaring the two NOT EQUAL for module-list payloads.
⇒ THAT IS WORSE THAN DUPLICATION, BECAUSE IT IS AN INVARIANT SOMEONE MUST MAINTAIN BY HAND
FOREVER.
RELATED EXTEND -- NEST PLACEMENT: gen-edge's materialize WRAPS THE WHOLE VALUE ONCE;
den-hoag needs PER-CONTRIBUTION-ITEM placement, stated as an invariant at `edges.nix`.
★ THAT IS WHY `lib/nest.nix` (19.9K) EXISTS AS A SECOND MATERIALIZATION ENGINE.
RESOLUTION: `materialize`'s nest arm places PER ITEM (or `adapt` applies per item); then
ONE engine. Line accounting: ~60-80 of nest.nix's 162 code lines recoverable that way; the
rest is den mode semantics.
★★ AND THE DEEPER STATEMENT, which is A8's theory question: den-hoag runs A SECOND EDGE
VOCABULARY WITH NO SHARED IDENTITY DISCIPLINE. gen-edge renders "<kind>:<idHash>";
den-hoag's query records are "<kind>:<name>", and `output-modules.nix` `nameOf = id: id;`
OPTS OUT OF nameSpec RENDERING ENTIRELY. A8's `or` is a patch; UNIFYING THE VOCABULARIES IS
THE THEORY QUESTION.

title: [G20] [gen-prelude] the dedupByKey remedy is REFUTED (quadratic in a different variable) — but "negligible at den-hoag scale" rests on a ci census that does not bound the real fleet
description:
★ ARGUED, HIGHEST MULTIPLIER IN THE ECOSYSTEM, and PERFORMANCE IS A DEFECT here by
standing rule.
`gen-prelude/lib/default.nix`: `unique = foldl' (acc: x: if elem x acc then acc else acc ++
[ x ]) [ ];`
TWO COMPOUNDED SUPERLINEAR FACTORS: `elem x acc` is a LINEAR SCAN PER ELEMENT, and
`acc ++ [ x ]` COPIES THE ACCUMULATOR ON EVERY APPEND.
★★ THE SAME FILE ALREADY CONTAINS THE LINEAR ALGORITHM 75 LINES ABOVE -- `dedupByKey`,
which uses an ATTRSET for membership (`seen ? ${k}`, O(1)). For string inputs `unique` IS
EXACTLY `dedupByKey (x: x)`.
★ ALL 14 DEN-HOAG `prelude.unique` CALL SITES PASS STRINGS -- kind names, stratum names,
node ids, id_hashes -- INCLUDING PER-NODE CODE: `resolved-aspects.nix` (`ancestorIds`, PER
NODE), `staged-resolution.nix` (per attachment), plus default.nix x3, edges.nix x2,
concern-policies x2, declarations, projects x2, class-modules, claim-accessor.
RESOLUTION: `unique` delegates to `dedupByKey (x: x)` for the string case, or the library
DOCUMENTS it as the general-value fallback and STEERS callers.
★ TODAY THE NAME EVERYONE REACHES FOR IS THE SLOW ONE -- the D3 shape in a different dress.
CAVEAT: no complexity claim in the audit's §9 was measured on a fleet; the asymptotics are
unambiguous from source but the cost at den-hoag's scale is unquantified.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ MEASURED 2026-07-29, AND THE BEAD'S RESOLUTION IS REFUTED. THE NAMED FIX IS 272x
WORSE AT DEN-HOAG'S ACTUAL INPUT SHAPE.

INSTRUMENT: `NIX_SHOW_STATS=1 nix-instantiate --eval --strict` on a PLAIN FILE (no flake).
`list.elements` counts the `++`/`tail` copying, `nrOpUpdateValuesCopied` the `//` copying,
`nrPrimOpCalls` the toJSON. Deterministic, and it SIDESTEPS THE 345 ms FLAKE FLOOR that
defeated the earlier attempt -- a plain-file eval is ~7 ms and ★ `cpuTime` STAYED FLAT AT
~0.007 s ACROSS EVERY N, so wall-clock proves nothing here and the counters are the signal.
POSITIVE CONTROL: a genuinely linear dedup measures 303 -> 603 -> 1203 -> 2403 across
N=100..800, EXACTLY 2x PER DOUBLING. The instrument can show linear, so a 4x is a real
quadratic and not an artefact.

THE ASYMPTOTIC IS REAL: `unique` on ALL-DISTINCT input goes 5,252 -> 322,002 list-elems
across N=100..800. Confirmed.

★ BUT DEN-HOAG NEVER PASSES THAT SHAPE. `gen-prelude.unique` instrumented over the WHOLE
ci suite:
    11,418 calls   min N=0   median N=1   p99=10   MAX N=24
    sum(N)=12,104  sum(N^2)=48,478   ONLY 7.8% OF CALLS HAVE N>1
Total quadratic work across 1,937 tests is 48K element-comparisons against 12K for a
linear implementation. REAL, AND NEGLIGIBLE.

★★ AND THE PROPOSED FIX IS DIRECTIONALLY WRONG. `dedupByKey`'s membership is O(1), BUT ITS
RECURSION CALLS `builtins.tail`, WHICH COPIES -- so it is quadratic IN LIST LENGTH
REGARDLESS OF DISTINCT COUNT, where `unique` is quadratic only IN DISTINCT COUNT. At
den-hoag's actual shape (few distinct; K=26, N=800):
    unique       1,179 list-elems
    dedupByKey   320,779 list-elems   ★ 272x WORSE
and `dedupByKey` additionally adds quadratic `//` copying (73 vs 0) that `unique` does not
have.
⇒ THE TWO ARE QUADRATIC IN DIFFERENT VARIABLES, AND THE BEAD ASSUMED ONE DOMINATES BECAUSE
IT READ "O(1) MEMBERSHIP" AND STOPPED. The audit called this "the highest multiplier in the
ecosystem"; measured, it is the smallest of the three and its remedy is a regression.

VERDICT: CLOSE AS MEASURED-NOT-WORTH-FIXING, and record that the named fix must not be
applied for string inputs. If anything is ever done here it is the `listToAttrs` shape, NOT
`dedupByKey`.
★ THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is why spec-before-development covers one-line gen-lib changes:
"the linear algorithm sits 75 lines above" was TRUE AS A STATEMENT ABOUT ASYMPTOTIC CLASS
AND FALSE AS A STATEMENT ABOUT THIS CONSUMER. An asymptotic argument names a growth rate; it
does not name the VARIABLE, and swapping primitives on an unmeasured input shape can invert
the answer.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ REOPENED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR. THE CLOSURE ABOVE WAS RECORDED WITH LESS SCRUTINY THAN
THIS ARC APPLIES TO ITS GATES, AND ONE OF ITS TWO CLAIMS DOES NOT SURVIVE THE DIFFERENCE.
The closure is NOT retracted wholesale -- it is SPLIT, because its two claims have very
different strength.

★ CLAIM 1 -- "THE NAMED FIX IS DIRECTIONALLY WRONG" -- STANDS. The mechanism is
STRUCTURAL and shape-independent: `dedupByKey`'s recursion calls `builtins.tail`, WHICH
COPIES, so it is quadratic IN LIST LENGTH while `unique` is quadratic IN DISTINCT COUNT.
Two implementations quadratic in DIFFERENT VARIABLES. That is checkable by reading and does
not depend on any input distribution. ⇒ DO NOT APPLY `dedupByKey` HERE ON THE STRENGTH OF
"O(1) MEMBERSHIP". That conclusion is safe.
★ BUT THE 272x FIGURE IS MEASURED AT K=26, N=800 -- A SHAPE THE SAME REPORT SAYS DOES NOT
OCCUR (median N=1, max N=24). It DRAMATISES a real mechanism at an operating point that is
not den-hoag's. At N=24 the gap would be far smaller. THE NUMBER SHOULD NOT BE CITED AS
DEN-HOAG'S EXPOSURE.

★★ CLAIM 2 -- "NEGLIGIBLE AT DEN-HOAG'S SCALE" -- IS UNESTABLISHED, AND THE REPORT ITSELF
CONTAINS THE REASON.
The distribution (11,418 calls, median N=1, max N=24, 7.8% with N>1) WAS MEASURED OVER THE
ci SUITE. ★ THE SAME REPORT STATES, FOR G22, THAT ci HAS NO LARGE FLEETS AND DOES NOT BOUND
THE REAL FLEET -- and does not carry that limitation here, THOUGH BOTH DISTRIBUTIONS COME
FROM THE SAME SUITE.
And `unique`'s call sites are not shape-neutral: `resolved-aspects.nix` `ancestorIds` runs
PER NODE and `staged-resolution.nix` PER ATTACHMENT. Those scale with fleet size, which is
exactly what ci does not exercise.

★★★ AND THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT, FROM THE SAME AGENT HOURS EARLIER: the "10 empty-recoveries,
ALL LEGITIMATELY INERT" claim was WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN AUTHOR because THE INSTRUMENT COULD
NOT HAVE SEEN THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IT WAS BEING USED TO RULE OUT -- a ci-suite census standing
in for a real-world population. CLAIM 2 IS THE IDENTICAL SHAPE. Recorded at den-hoag-9xo.72
and den-hoag-4kh.20.

★ AND THE EVIDENTIARY STANDARD DIFFERED, WHICH IS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ERROR TO OWN. Every
gate that earned trust tonight was INDEPENDENT, FRESH-CONTEXT, ADVERSARIALLY FRAMED, and run
by someone WHO DID NOT OWN THE CONCLUSION -- and two of them killed orchestrator designs. This
measurement was SELF-DIRECTED BY THE IMPLEMENTER, non-adversarial, and its conclusion REMOVES
WORK FROM ITS OWN QUEUE. That is not disqualifying and the work was careful; it is a DIFFERENT
STANDARD, and it was recorded as settled anyway.

WHAT IS OWED TO CLOSE THIS PROPERLY:
1. The real fleet's `unique` input distribution, measured where fleet scale is actually
   reached. ★ ci and `parity#tests` ARE BOTH KNOWN INSUFFICIENT -- the full-fleet content gate
   is `ship-gate.nix`, a RUNBOOK step, which is the third time tonight that path has been the
   only one able to witness a corpus-scale fact.
2. Specifically the per-node call sites (`ancestorIds`, the staged-resolution per-attachment
   site), not the aggregate -- an aggregate median over 11,418 calls hides a tail that lives
   entirely in the per-node ones.
3. An INDEPENDENT measurer. Not the agent whose queue the answer clears.
If claim 2 survives that, close again on the same reasoning. If it does not, `unique` is a
live performance defect on the per-node path and the standing rule applies: performance
issues are defects, filed and tracked like wrong answers.
