title: [ci] den-delivery reports 0/0 successful — a GREEN EMPTY SUITE, because parking its last test left the target with no bindings and nix-unit calls that success
description:
OBSERVED 2026-07-28 while classifying unrelated failures. Filed because it is the
false-pass shape this project has already been bitten by, now realised in the runner
rather than in a predicate.

`ci#tests.den-delivery` reports:
    🎉 0/0 successful
A GREEN EMPTY SUITE. Its only test lives in hm-host-forward-hm-class.nix and is
PARKED (commented out under the parking rule), so the suite has no bindings left --
and nix-unit reports that as SUCCESS.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the documented nix-unit trap -- tests are detected by a
`test` NAME-PREFIX, and a target with no matching bindings reports 0/0 and EXITS 0.
Any gate, script, or human reading suite results as coverage counts this as passing.
A suite whose entire subject has been parked is indistinguishable, from the outside,
from a suite that passed.

⇒ THE GENERAL HAZARD, and it is the sharper form of every parking decision: PARKING
THE LAST TEST IN A SUITE SILENTLY CONVERTS THAT SUITE FROM COVERAGE INTO A GREEN
NO-OP. The parking rule is sound -- leave the fixture in place, commented, with its
reason -- but it has no step that notices when a suite's population reaches zero.

WHAT TO DECIDE (not designed here):
· whether the runner should FAIL or WARN on a 0-binding target, which is the
  by-construction fix and would catch every future instance;
· or whether parked-empty suites should be removed from the target list with a
  recorded reason, which is the bookkeeping fix and must be re-applied forever.
· ★ EITHER WAY, AUDIT FOR OTHER 0/0 TARGETS FIRST -- this one was found by accident
  while running an unrelated control, and nothing in the gate looks for it. An
  absence claim here needs a positive control: confirm the audit predicate reports a
  known-populated suite as populated in the same run.

RELATED: den-hoag-4kh.20 records the corrupted-but-GREEN test found the same session
by a sibling sweep. Same family of hazard -- an instrument that reads failures cannot
see a subject that stopped being tested.

title: [compat] hm-user-detect is provisioned TWICE and the selects fix landed on the path mkDen does not use — the battery desugar re-registers it unwrapped and clobbers any wrapped copy
description:
★★ MEASURED 2026-07-28. A POLICY IS PROVISIONED TWICE, THE `selects` FIX LANDED ON
ONE PATH, AND `denCompat.mkDen` USES THE OTHER. Every arm below is a REAL FLEET
through `denCompat.mkDen` -- no fabricated ctx anywhere in this diagnosis.

THE TWO REGISTRATIONS, and the tree documents the pattern itself at
lib/compat/legacy/batteries/home-manager.nix:83-84: "Exported for builtins.nix
(THE DUAL-REGISTRATION PATTERN: ONE DEFINITION, BOTH PATHS)."
 1. lib/compat/builtins.nix:440  `hm-user-detect = ambient hmUserDetect;`
    ← THE `selects = null` FIX LANDED HERE.
 2. lib/compat/legacy/batteries/home-manager.nix:109-116, the battery's own desugar:
        desugar = v1: v1 // { policies = (v1.policies or { }) // { hm-user-detect = hmUserDetect; }; };
    ← UNWRAPPED. NO `selects`. Folded in by legacy/defaults.nix composeDesugars.

`denCompat.mkDen` REACHES IT THROUGH PATH 2, NEVER PATH 1.
mkDen -> mkDenWith -> compileFull rawDen, where rawDen = evalV1Raw userModules and
evalV1Raw evaluates flakeModuleCore ++ [ bindLegacyEnv ] ++ userModules, with
flakeModuleCore = [ v1OptionsModule ] and flakeModule = flakeModuleCore. NEITHER
INCLUDES builtinsModule -- that is a separate export a consumer must wire. The
batteries arrive later, at compile time, via desugarLegacy.
⇒ The record reaching the mint has no `selects` ⇒ mintFleetWide falls to
selectsFromSchema "hm-user-detect" ⇒ the name is in no includes list ⇒ [ ] ⇒ absent
from every node's rule list ⇒ NEVER FIRES. No hm forward, no home-manager->nixos
edge, both compat-hm-battery tests fail.

★ HOW IT WAS ESTABLISHED -- THE VARIABLE IS THE ATTRIBUTE NAME. All arms real
fleets; only the named field varies:
    { __denCanTake = "user-host"; selects = null; fn = <hmUserDetect body verbatim> }
      named `probe`           -> `probe:delivery` PRESENT
      renamed `hm-user-detect` -> ABSENT
Identical shape, identical body, ONE VARIABLE. A user-supplied `hm-user-detect`
loses because the desugar's `//` puts the battery's UNWRAPPED record LAST and
clobbers it. That is simultaneously the POSITIVE CONTROL for the mechanism -- the
record fires under any other name, so neither the shape nor the body is at fault.

★ TWO HYPOTHESES RAISED AND REFUTED BY THE SAME REPORTER, both worth keeping:
· the value-gated body does NOT break codomain recovery -- an arm with `emits`
  RECOVERED by firing at the sentinel, with the value-gated intoClass body, FIRES.
  The empty/failed-recovery story does not apply here.
· a className-mismatch hypothesis died on READING the body: hmUserDetect gates on
  `builtins.elem "homeManager" (user.classes or [ ])`, the v1 camelCase spelling,
  which matches the fixture's `classes = [ "homeManager" ]`.

★★ THE GENERAL SHAPE, AND IT IS THE ACTIONABLE PART: WHY `user-to-host` FIRES AND
`hm-user-detect` DOES NOT. legacy/batteries/os-user.nix and os-class export a
`routeInclude`, which legacy/defaults.nix coerces into the `defaults` aspect's
includes -- so they arrive as `__aspectInclude__*`, WITH AN INCLUDE PATH, and need
no `selects` declaration at all. The home-manager battery exports NO routeInclude
(full export list read: registersClasses, hmUserDetect, desugar), so it has NEITHER
an include path NOR a declared selection.
⇒ A BATTERY WITH A routeInclude GETS ITS SELECTION FOR FREE; A BATTERY WITHOUT ONE
MUST DECLARE `selects`. That is the rule, and it should be stated wherever batteries
are defined rather than rediscovered per battery.
⇒ maid/hjem/wsl batteries SHARE THE SHAPE and are worth the same look -- NOT TESTED.

NOT REACHED, stated by the reporter:
· The merged POST-DESUGAR policy record was never observed directly -- no accessor
  was found. The clobber rests on (a) reading the desugar's `//` ordering and (b) the
  name-variable experiment. Both point the same way; that is inference plus
  behaviour, not a direct read of the merged value.
· It was NOT verified that adding the wrapper at path 2 turns the two tests green --
  a remedy, deliberately out of scope.
· ★ AN UNEXPLAINED ABORT, FLAGGED RATHER THAN BURIED: one earlier probe aborted with
  `policyCodomainUnrecoverable` naming `probe`; three same-named arms shared that run
  so it could not be attributed, and the isolated re-run passed. It may be a real
  edge in recovery or an artefact of the three-arm construction. UNRESOLVED.
· compat-hm-battery.nix has changed TWICE and produces-by-name.nix THREE TIMES
  mid-session. Re-derive before acting.
close_reason: FIXED AND VERIFIED. legacy/batteries/home-manager.nix desugar now registers hmUserDetect // { selects = null; }; compat-hm-battery 3/5 -> 5/5, so wrapping at path 2 does turn them green. Cleared 4 not 2 - den-hasAspect and den-provides-fn-facet went green with it, confirming the cluster size claimed by measurement. General rule stated at the battery definitions: no routeInclude ⇒ declare selects. maid/hjem/wsl checked - registered once in builtins.nix, no second path, premise does not apply.

title: [kernel] should an honest-inert policy declare emits = [ ] explicitly? without it, "recovered empty" and "genuinely empty" are the same state and the silent drop cannot be made loud
description:
DESIGN QUESTION, surfaced 2026-07-28 by the implementer, who correctly declined to
patch it. It is the last thing standing between a silent-drop path and a loud one.

THE SILENT DROP, already measured. A compat-minted policy's codomain is RECOVERED
BY FIRING (lib/compat/policy-recover.nix). If recovery yields [ ], `compileOne`
compiles an empty codomain to NO RULE -- silently. `policyCodomainUnrecoverable`
fires only on a caught THROW, so a body that RETURNS [ ] for any reason is
indistinguishable from a body that has nothing to say. den-hoag-9xo.64 fixed ONE
route into that state (recovery firing through the suppression gate); the state
itself remains reachable and silent.

THE OBVIOUS FIX AND WHY IT IS NOT ONE. "Make an empty recovery abort" would make
the drop loud -- and would immediately reject a LEGITIMATE construct:
    host-to-users = _ctx: [ ]
is an HONEST INERT EMITTER. It is not broken, it is not suppressed, it genuinely
emits nothing, and den-hoag's own compat surface ships it
(lib/compat/builtins.nix). Aborting on an empty recovery would refuse it.

⇒ THE ACTUAL QUESTION: should an honest-inert policy be REQUIRED to declare
`emits = [ ]` explicitly, so that "declared empty" and "recovered empty" become
DIFFERENT STATES?
If yes, the abort becomes safe: a recovery yielding [ ] from a policy that did NOT
declare `emits = [ ]` is unambiguously a failure, and the honest case opts out by
saying so. This is the same shape as the `emits` opt-out that already works, and
the same principle that resolved the shim-ambient regression -- DECLARATION BEATS
DERIVATION, and an explicit value is not a missing key
(feedback_absence_is_a_decision).

WHY IT IS NOT A PATCH, and why it was right to stop: it has CORPUS BLAST RADIUS.
Every honest-inert emitter anywhere -- den-hoag's compat built-ins, the corpus, the
templates, den-configs -- would have to declare `emits = [ ]` or start aborting.
That is a surface change, not a guard change, and it needs:
· a CENSUS of honest-inert emitters across all four trees, with a positive control
  (the predicate must be shown able to find one it is known to contain);
· a decision on whether the requirement is retroactive (abort) or staged (warn,
  then abort), noting that this project's standing posture is to fail loud rather
  than warn;
· confirmation that `emits = [ ]` is even REPRESENTABLE end to end -- den-hoag-9xo.
  62's rejection turned on `ops = [ ]` being the correct declaration for a class
  that then got punished for making it, and the same trap must not be repeated here.
  ★ CHECK SPECIFICALLY: does anything currently treat `emits = [ ]` as "no rule" in
  a way that would make an honest declaration indistinguishable from the failure it
  is meant to disambiguate? If so, this design is circular and must be solved
  elsewhere.

UNTIL THEN: the retirement of `excludeFamilyUntagged` is NOT total for recovered
codomains, and that limitation is recorded in the code at the retargeted witness
(ci/tests/compat-exclude-family.nix) as well as here.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE CIRCULARITY CHECK IS ANSWERED: YES, CIRCULAR AS FEARED -- AND IT DISSOLVES
IN EXACTLY ONE DIRECTION. Measured 2026-07-28.

CONFIRMED: lib/concern-policies.nix:226, `if emits == [ ] then [ ]`, compiles an
empty codomain to NO RULE. So an honest `emits = [ ]` and a failed recovery
yielding [ ] are INDISTINGUISHABLE DOWNSTREAM. Exactly the ops = [ ] trap this bead
was filed to avoid repeating.

★ THE DISSOLUTION, and it is the whole design: THE CHECK BELONGS IN THE RECOVERY,
NEVER ON THE COMPILED VALUE. The circularity exists only if the failure is detected
by inspecting `emits == [ ]` downstream. If RECOVERY NEVER YIELDS [ ] -- it returns
kinds or it ABORTS -- then `emits = [ ]` can only ever be AUTHOR-WRITTEN, and the
two states stop sharing a value. Detection moves upstream of the collision instead
of trying to resolve it after the fact.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED OVER THE CI SUITE, NOT ESTIMATED. `recoverEmits`
instrumented across the full suite: 54 distinct names recover a codomain; EXACTLY
TEN recover EMPTY --
    hjem-host-module  host-to-users  hostToUsers  host-to-wsl-host  local-noise
    mark-aarch64  nix-maid-host-module  probe-enrich  user-aspect-auto-include  vc-host
Cross-checked against HEAD's own probe and real-context emissions: NINE emit
nothing at HEAD either, so [ ] is genuinely their codomain. The tenth,
`probe-enrich`, is the FLAG-OFF ARM of a fixture whose body is literally
`if host ? class` -- with probeSentinel off the sentinel lacks `class`, so empty is
correct there too. A BOUNDED, NAMEABLE SET OF TEN, ALL LEGITIMATELY INERT.
Requiring them to declare is cheap.

★★ AND THERE IS ALREADY A LIVE WITNESS OF THE HAZARD IN A TEST TODAY:
compat-feature-severed.test-probeSentinel-off-parks pinned `errors.expansionEnrich`
FIRING when the sentinel is off. That error is retired, and the flag-off arm now
recovers [ ] -> NO RULE, SILENTLY. That is precisely the LOUD-BECOMES-SILENT
conversion this bead exists to prevent, already realised, sitting in the suite.

★★ THE SCOPE GAP THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE RULE IS SAFE -- NOT YET MEASURED, AND IT
IS THE BLOCKER. The ten were measured over THE CI SUITE ONLY. The rule "a recovery
yielding [ ] aborts" is safe only if no LEGITIMATE policy outside the suite also
recovers empty. THERE IS A NAMED REASON TO EXPECT SOME DO:
recovery fires at a SENTINEL ctx (probe-sentinel.nix), whose field values are
deliberately TYPE-CORRECT AND NON-MATCHING. A VALUE-CONDITIONAL policy therefore
takes its FALSE branch at the sentinel and emits nothing -- legitimately. The corpus
contains exactly such a policy: nix-config's `drop-user-to-host-on-droid` is
`lib.optional (host.class == "droid") ...`, which at a non-droid sentinel returns
[ ]. Under a flat abort rule THAT WOULD ABORT THE CORPUS.
⇒ IF value-conditional policies recover empty, the rule cannot be flat, and the
design must distinguish "empty because the sentinel did not satisfy a value
condition" from "empty because the policy is inert" -- which is precisely what the
RETIRED probe machinery did. That would be a retiring construct discharging an
obligation nobody wrote down, for the second time in this arc (see den-hoag-4kh.18).
⇒ REQUIRED BEFORE ANY RULING: run the same `recoverEmits` instrumentation over the
CORPUS ARM and the TEMPLATES, not just ci. If the empty-recovering set is still the
ten, the rule is safe and cheap. If it includes value-conditional bodies, the design
changes shape entirely.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE BLOCKER ON THIS BEAD IS RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT, AND IN THE DIRECTION THAT
ARGUES FOR BUILDING IT. 2026-07-28.

I held this design pending one question: would a flat "recovery yields [ ] ⇒
abort" rule break a VALUE-CONDITIONAL policy that legitimately returns [ ] at the
non-matching sentinel -- naming nix-config's `drop-user-to-host-on-droid` as the
corpus instance at risk.

ANSWER: THE HAZARD IS ALREADY REALISED. den-hoag-9xo.75 measures a value-
conditional compat policy VANISHING TODAY, with no error, on a concrete failing
test -- the recovered codomain is [ ] because the body's gate is false under the
fabricated recovery context, and an empty codomain compiles to no rule.
⇒ THE PROPOSED RULE DOES NOT CREATE THE HAZARD. IT MAKES THE EXISTING ONE LOUD.
That inverts the argument against it: the objection was "this would break value-
conditional policies", and the measurement says they are ALREADY BROKEN, silently.

⇒ REVISED SHAPE OF THE ANSWER, and it is now two separable pieces:
 1. A value-conditional body must NOT have its codomain decided by a fabricated
    context. That is recovery-by-execution deciding a DECLARATION question. Fixing
    this is 9xo.75's business and it is a correctness fix, not a policy choice.
 2. Once (1) holds, "recovery yields [ ] ⇒ abort" becomes safe, because the only
    remaining empty recoveries are genuinely inert bodies -- the bounded, named set
    of ten measured over ci. AT THAT POINT requiring `emits = [ ]` from those ten
    costs ten declarations and converts the last silent drop into a named abort.
⇒ SEQUENCE THEM. Building (2) before (1) would abort every value-conditional policy
in the corpus. Building (1) alone leaves the silent drop for honest-inert bodies.

STILL OWED BEFORE (2): the corpus-scope measurement of `recoverEmits` (ci-scoped
set of ten is not a corpus claim), AND the urgent question raised at 9xo.75 --
whether the corpus's own `drop-user-to-host-on-droid` is vanishing on the real
fleet right now. The exclude-family fixtures pass 6/6, so something carries them;
if it is their declarations rather than the mechanism, the corpus excluder is
already silently dropped and the parity green is hiding it.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE "BOUNDED SET OF TEN, ALL LEGITIMATELY INERT" CLAIM IS WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN
AUTHOR, 2026-07-28. THIS UNDERCUTS THE SEQUENCING ARGUMENT RECORDED ABOVE AND MUST
BE RE-ESTABLISHED BEFORE STEP (2) IS BUILT.

WHAT WAS CLAIMED: `recoverEmits` instrumented across the suite found 54 names
recovering a codomain and EXACTLY TEN recovering EMPTY, all cross-checked as
"legitimately inert" -- so requiring those ten to declare `emits = [ ]` was cheap
and safe.

WHAT IS TRUE: at least ONE of the ten -- `mark-aarch64` -- is a LIVE VALUE-
CONDITIONAL EMITTER BEING SILENTLY DROPPED. Measured on the real path:
    emits     = [ ]         recovered empty (value-conditional on host.system)
    realKinds = [ "edge" ]  it DOES emit at real ctx
The other nine have NOT been re-verified on the real path.

★ WHY THE ORIGINAL MEASUREMENT COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT, in the author's own words:
it was taken from `mkSlice` firings INSIDE THE SUITE, which never reached this
fixture's REAL CONTEXT -- "THE INSTRUMENT COULD NOT HAVE SEEN THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IT
WAS BEING USED TO RULE OUT." A recovery-time census cannot distinguish "recovered
empty because inert" from "recovered empty because the fabricated ctx failed the
body's value condition", because BOTH produce the same [ ] at the same place. The
distinguishing evidence -- what the body emits at REAL ctx -- is not available at
the point the census ran. Same shape as the stamp-time collision predicate archived
at den-hoag-4kh.20: RIGHT QUESTION, WRONG STAGE.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S PLAN. Step (2) -- "recovery yields [ ] ⇒ abort" -- was
justified by the ten being inert. THAT JUSTIFICATION IS GONE. The step is still
plausibly right, but its cost is now UNKNOWN rather than bounded, and the honest
position is that the empty-recovering population has not been characterised at all.
⇒ RE-CHARACTERISE IT WITH AN INSTRUMENT THAT CAN SEE THE DIFFERENCE: for every name
that recovers empty, compare the recovered codomain against WHAT THE BODY EMITS AT
REAL CTX. A name where those differ is a value-conditional emitter being dropped
(a 9xo.75 instance, a DEFECT); a name where both are empty is genuinely inert (a
declaration candidate). Do this over ci AND the corpus AND the templates.
★ NOTE THE SILVER LINING, WHICH STRENGTHENS STEP (1): every such difference found is
a live silent drop. The re-characterisation is not overhead before the design -- it
IS the defect census for den-hoag-9xo.75.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★★ THE CENSUS I SPECIFIED REFUTES ITSELF, AND THE REFUTATION IS STRUCTURAL RATHER
THAN A FLAW IN THE ATTEMPT. 2026-07-28. THIS CHANGES WHAT STEP (2) CAN EVER BE.

WHAT I ASKED FOR: for each empty-recovering name, re-fire the body against alternate
sentinels; if the results differ the body is value-conditional and its drop is a live
defect; if they agree it is genuinely inert and a declaration candidate.

WHAT IT RETURNED over ci: 8 "agrees", 1 value-conditional (`probe-enrich`).

★ THAT RESULT IS WRONG, AND THE RUN CONTAINS ITS OWN COUNTEREXAMPLE. `vc-host`
reported "AGREES" -- a policy already proven value-conditional by direct measurement
minutes earlier. The three sentinel variants carried class/system/hostName but NO
`settings`, so `host.settings.on or false` was false in all three. THE CENSUS
REPORTED "INERT" ABOUT A POLICY ALREADY WATCHED VANISHING FOR BEING CONDITIONAL.

★★ THE STRUCTURAL REASON, AND IT IS THE FINDING: A FABRICATED-CONTEXT PROBE CANNOT
DECIDE WHETHER A FABRICATED-CONTEXT PROBE WAS WRONG. The census is THE SAME
INSTRUMENT AS THE RECOVERY, one level up, and it inherits the identical defect -- it
can only ever report "empty at the contexts I happened to fabricate."
POSITIVES ARE CONCLUSIVE; NEGATIVES ARE WORTHLESS. And the variant set can never be
shown complete, because the condition space is UNBOUNDED: `host.settings.<anything>`,
any field, any predicate.
⇒ THIS IS NOT "I NEED BETTER VARIANTS." NO FINITE VARIANT SET CLOSES IT.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR STEP (2): IT CANNOT BE COSTED BY ANY PROBE-BASED CENSUS, EVER.
The only sound discriminator is THE BODY'S SOURCE -- does it branch on a value? --
which is decidable by READING, and is what the corpus census used.
SOURCE-LEVEL RESULT SO FAR, reported as partial rather than papered over (several ci
names are helper-defined and the definition-grep missed them): `host-to-users` and
`hostToUsers` are `_ctx: [ ]`, genuinely inert; `probe-enrich` and `vc-host` are
value-conditional. So AT LEAST 2 OF THE 9 ci EMPTY-RECOVERIES ARE LIVE DROPS -- not
the 1 the census reported, and not the 0 the earlier "all inert" claim implied.

★ THE HONEST TOTAL FOR STEP (2): UNKNOWN, LOWER-BOUNDED AT 6 (2 ci + 4 corpus), AND
NOT OBTAINABLE BY PROBING. The withdrawal of the bounded-cost justification stands
and CANNOT BE RESTORED by more measurement of that kind.

★★ AND THE DEEPER READING, WHICH BEARS ON THE ARCHITECTURE AND NOT ONLY ON THIS
BEAD: RECOVERY-BY-EXECUTION IS NOT MERELY DEFECTIVE, IT IS UNDECIDABLE BY THE MEANS
AVAILABLE. You cannot census it, cannot bound its cost, and cannot certify any
individual policy safe -- only unsafe. Every instrument for auditing it is the
instrument itself, one level up. ⇒ THE ONLY SOUND REMEDIES ARE THE ONES THAT REMOVE
THE NEED: declare the codomain, or make it knowable BY CONSTRUCTION. That is
feedback_by_construction_over_repair arriving as a proof rather than a preference.

ALSO ATTRIBUTED THIS ROUND: ci/tests/compat-scope-local-firing.
test-expansion-collapses-to-one-rule is a LIVE 9xo.75 WITNESS. Measured
`subRuleCount = 0`, not 1 -- the rule DID NOT FAIL TO COLLAPSE, IT VANISHED
(`vcHostRec` is value-conditional on `host.settings.on or false`; `emits = [ ]`,
`keys = [ ]`). ★ THE STRONG LEG IS WHAT CAUGHT IT: a `>= 1` assertion would have gone
GREEN ON ZERO RULES. The re-expression was right and the mechanism beneath it is
broken. Unattributed count 11 -> 10.

title: [ci] five probe-sentinel properties were RELOCATED not retired — requiredCoordsOf and probe-sentinel.nix are now unpinned, directly upstream of a known silent-drop path
description:
OWED WORK, filed so it does not depend on a file comment surviving. Raised
2026-07-28 by the implementer, who declined to let it read as discharged.

Under the ruling on den-hoag-9xo.63, 11 tests in ci/tests/compat-policy-expansion.
nix were removed with an in-file RETIREMENT RECORD naming, for each, the property it
pinned and why that property is gone. The split was honest and the second half is
this bead:

· GROUP A (6) -- the 3-way expansion fan and its sub-rule routing. A TRUE
  RETIREMENT. The stratum is declared now, so there is nothing to fan over and the
  `#<stratum>` identities those tests addressed do not exist. Nothing is owed.
· ★ GROUP B (5) -- THE KERNEL PROBE SENTINEL. A RELOCATION, NOT A RETIREMENT.

THE PROPERTY IS STILL LIVE. It moved to lib/compat/policy-recover.nix
`requiredCoordsOf` and lib/compat/probe-sentinel.nix -- the sentinel ctx a codomain
recovery is fired at, and the derivation of which coordinates that ctx must carry.
NOTHING CURRENTLY PINS IT. The tests that did were removed because they addressed
the OLD construct's surface, not because the behaviour stopped mattering.

WHY THIS IS NOT BOOKKEEPING. The recovery sentinel is load-bearing for two things
already measured this arc: it is what makes den-hoag-9xo.64's fix correct (the
sentinel carries no `suppressedPolicies`, which is why the ungated recovery returns
the true codomain), and its coordinate derivation decides whether a compat body is
fired with the coords it destructures -- a body fired with the wrong ctx returns the
wrong codomain SILENTLY, and compileOne turns an empty codomain into NO RULE with no
abort. So the unpinned property sits directly upstream of a known silent-drop path.

WHAT IS OWED: re-express the five properties against the CURRENT surface --
`requiredCoordsOf`'s derivation and `probe-sentinel.nix`'s field set -- rather than
against the retired probe. Read the retirement record at the top of
ci/tests/compat-policy-expansion.nix for the five properties as they were stated; it
is the only place they are written down.

★ AND THE REASON THIS IS A BEAD RATHER THAN A COMMENT: the record lives in a file
that the next migration may itself rewrite, and a retirement record deleted with its
file leaves no trace at all. The graph survives compaction; markdown and comments do
not. Do not close this by pointing at the file.

title: [compat] are compile.nix:426 and :436 exposed to the same identity collapse? aspectIdHash over a positional key gives ONE id for N distinct per-node producers, and a collision there is silent
description:
★ OPEN QUESTION ON SHIPPED CODE, raised 2026-07-28 by the measurement at
den-hoag-9xo.61. NOT a claim -- the exposure was explicitly NOT checked, and it is
filed because a live instance would be SILENT.

THE ESTABLISHED FACT. `aspectIdHash <key>` is NOT a valid identity for a
kindInclude synthetic aspect whose fn produces PER-NODE content. Measured: the
synthetic key `__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0` is an INDEX INTO THE
KIND'S INCLUDE LIST with no per-node coordinate, so hashing it gives ONE identity
for THREE genuinely distinct producers --
    agenix-identity/{shuo,sini,will}@blade  ->  all three  6b7f13a647a4b4f5
while hashing the grounded content gives three distinct ids. Positive control in
the same run: 25 rows carrying a real stored id_hash reproduce it 25/25 by BOTH
routes, so the instrument is sound and the collapse is specific to the stamp-less
class.

THE QUESTION. den-hoag ALREADY APPLIES `aspectIdHash` at lib/compat/compile.nix:426
and :436. ARE EITHER OF THOSE CALL SITES PASSING A KEY THAT IS POSITIONAL OR
OTHERWISE NON-PER-NODE, for content that IS per-node? If so, the same collapse is
live in shipped code today.

WHY IT WOULD BE SILENT. `identity` at collections.nix:205 is the A12 PRODUCER KEY,
consumed by scopeAdapter.sortByProducer and the per-channel grouping. A collision
does not throw -- it merges or mis-orders producers that should have been distinct.
The symptom would be content from one node appearing under another, or content
silently lost to a grouping collapse, with a green eval. That is the same class as
the delivery defects this arc has already paid for, and no existing guard would
name it.

HOW TO SETTLE IT. For each of :426 and :436, establish (a) what key is passed, (b)
whether that key varies per node, and (c) whether the content it identifies varies
per node. The hazard is exactly (b) constant AND (c) varying. If either site is
safe, say WHY it is safe -- "it happens to be per-node" and "it is structurally
per-node" have different durability, and only the second is a property.
★ A POSITIVE CONTROL IS ESSENTIAL HERE: a predicate that finds no collision must be
shown capable of finding one -- construct or point to a case where two distinct
producers DO share a key and confirm the check fires.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH den-hoag-9xo.61: there, the missing stamp made the defect
LOUD (`attribute 'id_hash' missing`) and it was found immediately. Here a wrong
stamp would be QUIET. The loud one has been fixed-in-direction within a day; a
quiet one could have been in the tree since :426 was written.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ ANSWERED 2026-07-28. BOTH SITES SAFE — AND NEITHER IS THE SOURCE OF THE
COLLISION. Frozen at den-hoag c42df53, corpus nix-config 9ebf3316.

:426 -- SAFE-STRUCTURALLY, and NEVER EXERCISED. Both stated, neither hidden.
(a) key = `ref.key`, the node's OWN native key, which for refs reaching this branch
    IS its definition path in the typed tree. Measured: defaults/includes/
    define-user, .../hostname, .../inputs', .../self', sini/includes/host-aspects.
(b) varies per node? NO -- a definition path is per-definition.
(c) content varies per node? NO -- it is the authored content AT that path.
⇒ Not (b)-constant-AND-(c)-varying. STRUCTURALLY safe: the branch is entered only
when `hasRealContent ref` AND `ref ? key`, and for such refs key and content are
both functions of the SAME definition path, so key->content is single-valued BY
CONSTRUCTION OF THE TYPED TREE. That is a property, not a coincidence.
★ WHAT WOULD BREAK IT, named rather than assumed: nothing in the guard requires
`.key` to BE a definition path -- the branch's own comment says it exists for "a
manually-emitted value". An emitter stamping a node-INVARIANT key onto per-node
content collides here exactly like the kindInclude case. THE SAFETY RESTS ON THE
EMITTERS, NOT ON THIS SITE.
★ EMPIRICAL STATUS, not overstated: the fallback FIRED ZERO TIMES FLEET-WIDE (0 of
69 stamps, all 7 hosts) -- every ref reaching the branch already carried an
id_hash. POSITIVE CONTROL that this is a real never-fires and not a dead probe:
relaxing ONLY the `!(ref ? id_hash)` guard made the SAME emit fire 5x with the five
keys above. The wiring is live; the guard is what stops it.

:436 -- SAFE-INCIDENTALLY. ★ THE DANGEROUS HALF (b) IS ALREADY TRUE HERE.
(a) key = `nm` = `fallbackName` when positional or nameless, else ref.name. Only
    THREE distinct keys fleet-wide: __aspectInclude__bareFn__4__aspect:include:0:
    include:0 (33x), __aspectInclude__bareFn__6__... (33x), <emitted>@dev.slab.sini:
    content:0 (3x).
(b) varies per node? ★ NO. `fallbackName` is built from the include-list POSITION
    -- a SYNTACTIC coordinate, not a resolution one. Fleet run and blade-only run
    give the SAME 69 stamps: one stamp set shared across all 7 hosts. THIS IS
    PRECISELY THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE kindInclude KEY WRONG.
(c) content varies per node? NO -- because THERE IS NO CONTENT. At stamp time these
    refs are genuinely empty attrsets or includes-only; `hasRealContent` is false,
    which is WHY they fell to this branch.
⇒ SAFE, but only because the refs reaching it happen to be IDENTITY-ONLY -- NOT
because the key discriminates nodes. IT DOES NOT. Tracked separately so the
incidental safety cannot silently become unsafe.
· Also measured: none of :436's three keys reach the consumption point at all --
  0 rows each in the fleet-wide key->content map -- so they never act as A12
  producer identities there.

★★ THE COLLISION'S ACTUAL ORIGIN IS NEITHER SITE, AND THE EARLIER GENERALISATION
IS CORRECTED. `__kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0` NEVER PASSES THROUGH
`stampIdentity` -- 0 STAMP rows fleet-wide. A bare FN takes `normalize`'s FUNCTION
arm, compile.nix:501-508:
    aspects.wrapGatedFn { ... name = name; onResult = grndDispatch name; } ref
where `name` is the positional `fallbackName`. ⇒ den-hoag-9xo.61's collision comes
from THE BARE-FN WRAP NAMING, not from either aspectIdHash call.
The prior claim "aspectIdHash <key> is not valid for a kindInclude synthetic" was
RIGHT ABOUT THE KEY AND WRONG ABOUT THE ROUTE -- the key never reaches an
aspectIdHash site at all. Corrected on den-hoag-9xo.61.

★ THE POSITIVE CONTROL THAT MAKES EVERY NEGATIVE ABOVE SOUND. Fleet-wide census at
collections.nix:205, where `identity` IS the A12 producer key: 54 distinct keys, 84
distinct (key, content-name, stored-id) triples. EXACTLY ONE key covers more than
one grounded content -- __kindInclude__user__aspect__2:include:0 -> 31 DISTINCT
CONTENTS (agenix-identity/<user>@<host>, the full user x host cross-product; and 31
is the same number as env-users' firing count measured independently in the
membership run). No stored id_hash. The other 53 keys are 1:1 with their content,
ALL carry a stored id_hash, and ALL are definition paths.
⇒ THE PREDICATE FOUND A 31-WAY COLLISION IN THE SAME RUN IN WHICH IT REPORTED 53
CLEAN KEYS. That is what makes "safe" mean something here.

COVERAGE NOT REACHED: one surface only (home-manager.users), 7 nixos hosts, one
corpus -- other outputs could route different refs into either site. ★ Consumers of
id_hash OTHER than collections.nix:205 were NOT checked; :436's keys are absent from
that ONE consumer, which does not show they are unused everywhere. :426's structural
argument is a READING of the typed-tree invariant, not a measurement, since the site
never executes. The __aspectInclude__bareFn__* family's own definition site and what
`<emitted>@dev.slab.sini` is were not examined.
close_reason: ANSWERED: :426 SAFE-STRUCTURALLY (key is a definition path, so key->content is single-valued by construction of the typed tree) and never exercised on this corpus (0 of 69 stamps; positive control - relaxing only the id_hash guard made it fire 5x). :436 SAFE-INCIDENTALLY - the dangerous half is already true there, fallbackName is a SYNTACTIC position shared across all 7 hosts, and it is safe only because the refs reaching it carry no content; tracked onward as its own bead. ★ AND NEITHER SITE IS THE SOURCE: the kindInclude key has 0 stamp rows fleet-wide; the collision comes from the bare-fn wrap naming at compile.nix:501-508. Positive control: a fleet census found the 31-way collision in the same run it reported 53 clean keys.

title: [compat] pipe.nix:288 asserts "nix-config declares no deriving pipe" and that is FALSE at main — and all six pipe fixtures are _ctx: by selection, so no fixture could ever have caught it
description:
TWO FINDINGS FROM THE SAME MEASUREMENT (den-hoag-9xo.62's gate). One is a false
claim IN THE CODE; the other is why nobody could have noticed.

★ (1) A STATED CEILING IN den-hoag IS FACTUALLY FALSE.
lib/compat/pipe.nix:288 asserts, as a load-bearing ceiling:
    CEILING (corpus-zero, LOUD not silent): nix-config declares no deriving pipe
THAT FLAT CLAUSE IS FALSE at nix-config main 9ebf3316.
modules/den/policies/pipes.nix:143 IS a deriving pipe -- `pipe.transform` inside
`broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares`, role = "derive", added 2026-06-26 by 1b8c2f963
and wired at den.schema.user.includes:188.
SWEEP WITH POSITIVE CONTROL: grepping pipe.filter|pipe.transform|pipe.fold|pipe.for
|pipe.as over main (both .worktrees/ AND .claude/worktrees/ excluded) returns
EXACTLY ONE hit -- pipes.nix:143. The same predicate family returned 16 site-verb
hits in that file and 1 in quirks/nixpkgs-overlays.nix, so the instrument was live.
⇒ The ceiling is stated as a CORPUS FACT and the corpus contradicts it. A comment
asserting corpus-zero is exactly the kind of claim that silently expires: the corpus
moved on 2026-06-26 and nothing re-checked it. Note this is the SECOND corpus-zero
claim in this arc found false after the fact (see the capability-map case in
feedback_reuse_scan_before_build).
NOT ESTABLISHED, and it decides the severity: whether the NARROWER E6 sub-hazard the
sentence actually guards -- a config-thunk feeding a value-demanding derive -- is
REALIZED. `replicateHome` is a plain marker quirk (quirks/replicate-home.nix) and
one checked emission (aspects/apps/dev/ai/claude.nix:330) is a plain value, but not
every emission site was audited. So: the CLAUSE is false; whether the HAZARD is live
is open. Fix the claim either way -- a false premise guarding a real hazard is worse
than no comment, because the next reader trusts it.

★ (2) THE PIPE FIXTURE SET CANNOT WITNESS CTX-DEPENDENCE -- BY SELECTION.
All SIX pipe policies in parity/fixtures/pipe-stages.nix are `_ctx:` --
shapeMetric, shapeStream, routePorts, renameRaw, gatherPeers, shapeMarks. They
ignore ctx BY CONSTRUCTION. And the golden test SAYS SO OUT LOUD before relying on
it, compat-compile-golden.nix:157: "Each pipe fixture's pipe.from policy body is
UNCONDITIONAL, so ANY ctx yields the pipeOp declaration" -- then fires each with
`.fn { }`.
⇒ ANY QUESTION OF THE FORM "does pipe behaviour depend on ctx?" IS A DEAD PREDICATE
AGAINST THIS FIXTURE SET. It answers "no" for every input because the inputs were
chosen to make it so. The corpus policy above CANNOT EVEN BE FIRED with `{ }` -- it
reads user.name -- so it is not merely absent from the fixtures, it is
UNREPRESENTABLE in them.
★ THE GENERAL FORM, worth carrying: a fixture set assembled for SIMPLICITY encodes
an assumption, and every later question about that assumption reads as confirmed.
The comment at :157 is the tell -- it states the property as a convenience, and the
property is precisely what needed testing. Convenience assumptions in fixtures are
load-bearing claims wearing a helpful voice.
REMEDY SHAPE, not designed here: the fixture set needs at least one ctx-DEPENDENT
pipe policy, including one with a deriving stage that closes over ctx, so that
`.fn { }` is not a valid way to exercise it. Until then no pipe result measured
against these fixtures may be cited as evidence about ctx.

RELATED: den-configs (19 configs) and the den templates were NOT audited for further
deriving pipes -- one counterexample settled the gate and the sweep stopped. A full
census would size the problem and is worth doing before anyone re-states a
corpus-zero claim about pipes.

title: [ci] the parity corpus pin is not a conservative proxy — it fails on a construct HEAD does not present, so its failure surface has diverged from the north-star target
description:
★ INSTRUMENT FINDING, not a bug finding. Measured 2026-07-28 while censusing the
materialization ladder (den-hoag-9xo.61).

THE PARITY LEDGER'S CORPUS ARM IS PINNED TO b0b20769 (parity/flake.nix:12), a
2026-07-07 owner decision. It is now roughly 36 commits / three weeks behind
nix-config HEAD, AND THE DRIFT IS IN den-RELEVANT MODULES -- aspect renames off a
class-name collision, the nixpkgs-overlays quirk, useGlobalPkgs.

★★ THE PIN IS NOT A CONSERVATIVE PROXY IN EITHER DIRECTION. Measured, same
snapshot, same recipes, including the belt-severed override set:
  HEAD 9ebf3316  arm B resolves the fleet graph; ONE edit -> full materialized
                 membership on 7/7 hosts.
  Pin b0b20769   arm B fails EARLIER AND DIFFERENTLY -- "gen-aspects: includes
                 element is a bare module ({ imports = [ ... ]; }) with no aspect
                 identity" -- before it can even NAME the hosts.
⇒ THE PIN FAILS ON A CONSTRUCT HEAD DOES NOT PRESENT. This is the important part:
the relationship is "DIFFERENT", not "further back". A ladder climbed against the
pin would enumerate rungs HEAD DOES NOT HAVE and would NEVER REACH the rungs HEAD
does. So the pin is not conservative in either direction -- it does not
under-report progress and it does not over-report it; it reports a different
failure surface.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LEDGER: its corpus arm measures an artefact whose FAILURE
SURFACE HAS DIVERGED FROM THE NORTH-STAR TARGET. Ledger rows asserting corpus
behaviour are statements about b0b20769, not about the fleet we are trying to
support, and nothing in a row's text says so. Rows are not thereby wrong -- they
are SCOPED more narrowly than they read.

NOT A CALL FOR AN IMMEDIATE REPIN. The runbook already names the intended fix
(migrate to a synthetic self-contained corpus), and a moving external corpus is the
exact thing a pin exists to prevent. The finding is that the CURRENT pin's drift is
no longer inert, so the choice must be made deliberately rather than by default:
either repin, or migrate to the synthetic corpus, or keep the pin AND state in the
ledger that its arm does not track HEAD's failure surface. Silence is the one
option that is wrong, because a reader takes "the corpus arm" to mean the corpus.

RELATED, SAME MEASUREMENT: RUNG 0 -- the bare-module include failure -- exists at
the PIN ONLY and is ABSENT at HEAD. It should not be worked as a live blocker
without first establishing that it survives a repin.

title: [ci] the belt-severed override set has never been observed to change any outcome — every "survives the overrides" attribution in this arc may be vacuous
description:
★ SUSPECTED DEAD INSTRUMENT. Raised 2026-07-28 by an agent that flagged its OWN
negative as weak rather than banking it. Not established -- this bead is the
request to establish it either way.

THE OBSERVATION. The runbook's belt-severed override set (lib/compat/parity/
runbook.md:188-192 -- gen-schema + gen-merge, four nested overrides) was applied
repeatedly across this session's corpus work and WAS NEVER OBSERVED TO CHANGE ANY
OUTCOME. Every claim of the form "the failure SURVIVES the belt-severed overrides"
was therefore made WITHOUT A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT THE OVERRIDE SET IS LIVE.

★ WHY THIS MATTERS OUT OF PROPORTION TO ITS SIZE. "X survives the belt-severed
overrides" is used in this arc as evidence that X is NOT a gen-library artefact --
i.e. to attribute a failure to den-hoag rather than to a stale gen pin. IF THE
OVERRIDE SET IS NOT ACTUALLY TAKING EFFECT, EVERY SUCH ATTRIBUTION IS VACUOUS: the
predicate returns "survives" for a live override that genuinely does not help AND
for an override that never applied, and those are indistinguishable without a
took-effect arm. This is the dead-control shape archived at den-hoag-4kh.20, on a
recipe we reach for routinely.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT -- a took-effect arm, not another survival arm:
· Establish that the overrides RESOLVE: verify the flake.lock / eval actually
  resolves gen-schema and gen-merge to the override targets rather than the pinned
  revs. A lock-level or `nix eval` check on the resolved rev is the cheapest form.
· Then a BEHAVIOURAL arm: find any observable that DIFFERS between override-on and
  override-off. If none can be found, that is itself the answer -- the overrides
  target revs that are already what the tree resolves to, in which case the recipe
  is a no-op TODAY and should be documented as such rather than cited as evidence.
· Note the two outcomes have opposite remedies: a MIS-SPECIFIED override set needs
  fixing; a NO-OP-BECAUSE-ALREADY-CURRENT override set needs the runbook to say so,
  and every citation of it as evidence needs re-reading.

SCOPE NOTE: the agent that raised this stated plainly it had no positive control
and refused to offer its negative as evidence. That is the correct handling and is
why this is a bead rather than a silent assumption. Do not close it by finding one
case where the overrides "look applied" -- the claim under test is that they CHANGE
SOMETHING, and only a differing observable settles that.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ ANSWERED 2026-07-28: MIS-SPECIFIED, AND WORSE THAN VACUOUS. Not
"no-op-because-already-current". The bead asked whether the recipe is live; it is
not, for a reason nobody would have guessed.

★ THE RECIPE CANNOT PERFORM THE ACTION ITS OWN PROSE NAMES.
runbook.md:182 defines belt-severed as TWO actions: "sever the seam
(passThrough = false) AND align the consumer's gen-schema/gen-merge". THE COMMAND
AT :188-192 PERFORMS ONLY THE SECOND.
`passThrough` is a FUNCTION ARGUMENT -- lib/compat/bridge.nix:53
`passThrough ? true`, consumed at :602 `emittedKinds = if passThrough then
passThroughSeam else withStructure`. There is NO flake option, NO env var, NO
override that reaches it.
POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE ABSENCE: the predicate `passThrough =` DOES match in-tree
-- ci/tests/compat-schema-processing.nix:43 and :117 set it false. It matches
NOTHING in lib/ and nothing CLI-reachable. The absence is real, not a dead grep.
⇒ ★★ EVERY "BELT-SEVERED" RUN IN THIS ARC RAN WITH THE BELT ON.

THE PIN-ALIGNMENT HALF APPLIES BUT MOVES NOTHING HERE.
Took-effect at RESOLUTION: all four arms resolve to type=path local sources rather
than the pinned github revs, so the overrides DO apply. Content:
· den/gen-schema af3dbe98 -> local 6732239: ★ AN EXACT NO-OP. IDENTICAL TREE HASH
  9e268fc6f07bf0e7fd31a0dd1768d8bbefd827f0 -- the two intervening commits are a
  feat and its own Revert. THIS ARM CAN NEVER DO ANYTHING.
· gen-schema (corpus root) 103ea889 -> 6732239: real, 3 commits, lib/identity.nix
  +60/-33 plus a new ci test.
· both gen-merge arms 8daa25de -> f17f2f2: real, 7 commits, 1044 insertions incl.
