title: [compat] recoverEmits fires the codomain probe THROUGH the suppression gate — a suppressed policy would recover emits = [ ] and compileOne deletes the rule silently, falsifying policy-recover.nix own header property
description:
★ LATENT DEFECT IN CODE WRITTEN THIS SESSION. Measured 2026-07-28 by an
independent reader auditing the negation path; found because the file was NEW and
its bearing on suppression was checked rather than assumed.

THE COUPLING, traced by call order. `lib/compat/policy-recover.nix` exports
`recoverEmits`, which fires a v1 bare closure ONCE at a sentinel to recover its
`emits` codomain. `mintFleetWide name compiled` computes
`emits = emitsFor ... compiled.gate compiled.fn`, and ITS call sites are
`mintFleetWide name (gateSuppression name (compilePolicy ...))` and the canTake
twin.
⇒ `compiled.fn` IS THE GATE-WRAPPED fn. So every recovery evaluates
    if builtins.elem v1Name (ctx.suppressedPolicies or [ ]) then [ ] else ...
THE CODOMAIN RECOVERY FIRES THROUGH THE NEGATED SUPPRESSION GATE.

HARMLESS TODAY, AND ONLY BY ACCIDENT. The recovery sentinel ctx is
`genAttrs (requiredCoordsOf gate) (_: probeEntry)`, which carries no
`suppressedPolicies`, so the `or [ ]` fail-open default makes the policy
not-suppressed, the real body runs, and the codomain comes back correct. THE
FAIL-OPEN DEFAULT THAT MAKES den-hoag-4kh.51 UNSOUND IS THE SAME THING KEEPING
THIS ARM CORRECT.

★ THE LATENT DEFECT. If `suppressedPolicies` were ever present at recovery time,
`recoverEmits` returns [ ] -- and `compileOne` compiles an empty codomain to NO
RULE, SILENTLY (`if emits == [ ] then [ ]`). NOT an abort:
`policyCodomainUnrecoverable` fires only on a caught THROW, and a gated body does
not throw, it returns [ ]. A suppressed policy would therefore be silently deleted
from the fleet at COMPILE time, on a path whose whole purpose is to discover what
the policy does.

★ AND IT FALSIFIES THE FILE'S OWN HEADER PROPERTY. policy-recover.nix claims
property (2): "the three-meaning collapse ... cannot recur, because those states
reach different branches." That holds FOR THE THROW ARM ONLY. "EMITTED NOTHING"
and "WAS SUPPRESSED" still reach the SAME branch, and that branch DELETES THE
RULE. The collapse the file was written to eliminate survives in the arm it does
not discuss.

CLASS: this is a fresher, smaller instance of den-hoag-4kh.52 -- a declaration
recovered by FIRING, where an ABSENCE is silently read as a DECISION
(feedback_absence_is_a_decision). Third instance in this arc.

DIRECTION, and it is a layering argument rather than a patch: A POLICY'S CODOMAIN
IS A STATIC PROPERTY OF ITS BODY. Suppression is a PER-NODE DISPATCH concern.
Recovering the codomain through the dispatch gate is a layer inversion, and it is
what makes the two states collapse. Recover from the UNGATED body -- i.e. from
`compilePolicy`'s output before `gateSuppression` wraps it -- and the question
cannot arise: there is no gate in the path to return [ ] for the wrong reason. That
also removes the accidental dependence on the fail-open default, so fixing 4kh.51's
`or [ ]` later cannot silently break codomain recovery. VERIFY the ordering is
actually available at those call sites before committing to it.

ABSENCE CONTROL FOR THE SURROUNDING CLAIM: `grep -rn "suppress\|suppressedPolicies"`
over `lib/compat/policy-recover.nix` and `lib/compat/probe-sentinel.nix` returns
NO MATCH (exit 1); the same predicate on `lib/compat/compile.nix` returns 14. The
predicate is live. Neither new file contains suppression vocabulary -- the coupling
is by CALL ORDER, not by reference, which is exactly why a vocabulary search would
have missed it. `probe-sentinel.nix` (22 lines) is a constant attrset of
type-correct non-matching sentinel field values and is inert here.

title: [kernel] how does compat obtain a record ops without firing? pipeOps is universally empty and the compose seed is dead — candidate: the opt-out is on the COMPLETE record (gate candidate)
description:
GATE CANDIDATE -- NOT VALIDATED. Raised by p1-impl, which correctly refused to
decide it. The last open design question in the policy-record migration.

THE SITUATION, measured. `ops` is specified as ctx-INDEPENDENT data on the policy
record, and compilePipe already partitions on it. The spec does NOT say how COMPAT
OBTAINS it: a v1 body's pipe stages come from its effect list, which needs ctx, so
today they are recovered BY FIRING.
Consequence, source predicate plus positive control (its three consumers exist and
read it): NOTHING sets a record `ops`, so pipeOps = concatMap (r: r.ops) rules is
universally [ ] and the fleet compose seed is EMPTY. The 12 `compose commitment`
aborts are the law working CORRECTLY against a half-built other end.
Cost today: den-pipe 21, pipe-consume 4, compat-collect-gather 4.

THE FORK. One fire can yield BOTH codomain and ops. But section 4.7's opt-out says
a policy that DECLARES its codomain is NEVER FIRED -- and `broadcast-hub-peer`
declares emits = [ "pipeOp" ], so under the current rule it is never fired and
SILENTLY LOSES ITS OPS. Every candidate must answer that case.

CANDIDATE A -- FIRE WHEN emits CONTAINS pipeOp. Rejected on sight, recorded so it
is not re-proposed: it is an EXEMPTION to the opt-out, a second rule, and it
re-instates recovery-by-execution for one field. That is the unifying defect shape
this whole migration exists to remove -- "missing information recovered by
EXECUTION where it should have been carried by DECLARATION."

CANDIDATE B -- ★ THE OPT-OUT IS ON THE COMPLETE RECORD, NOT ON emits ALONE.
A record is COMPLETE when every ctx-independent field is declared. Incomplete
records are fired ONCE to fill whatever is missing; complete ones are never fired.
    recoverableFields = [ "emits" "ops" ];
    needsRecovery = r: builtins.any (f: !(r ? ${f})) recoverableFields;
No pipeOp special case, no exemption, no second rule. `broadcast-hub-peer` is fired
once because it is incomplete, and stops being fired the moment it declares `ops`.
This is A generalised correctly rather than A with better manners: same firing
behaviour on the one corpus case, stated as a total rule.

CANDIDATE C -- ops REQUIRED whenever emits contains pipeOp. Most by-construction,
and it FAILS: compat cannot determine the stages statically, so the shim would have
to fire anyway or abort, and aborting rejects a real corpus policy.

WHAT THE GATE MUST ATTACK -- and the first item is the one that decides it:
· ★ IS `ops` GENUINELY CTX-INDEPENDENT? The spec asserts it. If any real pipe's
  stage list varies with ctx, then ops is not declarable, B is unimplementable, and
  the answer is elsewhere entirely. MEASURE THIS FIRST against the corpus and the
  pipe fixtures; everything below is moot if it fails.
· p1-impl framed the deeper question as "what a MARKS-ONLY view of a derived pipe
  means for EMISSION ORDER." Ops carry order. Establish whether a declared ops list
  preserves the order a fired recovery produces, and whether anything downstream
  depends on order the marks cannot express.
· Does firing an INCOMPLETE record at compile time reintroduce anything the opt-out
  existed to prevent? Establish WHY the opt-out exists -- cost, throw-safety, or
  ctx-availability -- because B widens who gets fired and the reason decides whether
  that is safe. NOTE the compiled-body trap already measured: a v1 body is a `ctx:`
  wrapper with EMPTY formals, so a recovery firing must use the DECLARED gate, never
  functionArgs (p1-impl hit this as a real bug and fixed it).
· Is `ops` observable at the funnel the way `emits` is? emits could become a CHECKED
  contract because emissions pass one place (conformingProduce). If ops has no such
  funnel, a declared ops is an UNCHECKED ASSERTION -- den-hoag-4kh.52's exact hazard,
  and B would be adding a third instance of it.
· Complexity: state the cost of B against today. How many records become fired that
  are not fired now, and what does that cost on the corpus?

CONTEXT THE GATE SHOULD HAVE: the orchestrator's previous design at this gate
(den-hoag-9xo.57) was REJECTED for getting the cited theory backwards and for
proposing a check that could not fire. Candidate B above is also the orchestrator's.
Attack it accordingly.
notes:
★★ REJECTED AT THE GATE, 2026-07-28, AT ITEM 1. Recorded with reasons. AND THE
REJECTION GOES WIDER THAN THE CANDIDATE: it kills any design that makes `ops` a
STATIC FIELD ON THE POLICY RECORD, which is what the policy-record spec assumes.

★ `ops` IS NOT CTX-INDEPENDENT. The spec asserts it; the corpus refutes it.

COUNTEREXAMPLE, live at nix-config main 9ebf3316, modules/den/policies/pipes.nix
:136-149, `broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares`, wired at den.schema.user.includes:188,
added 2026-06-26 by 1b8c2f963:
    { user, ... }: let srcUser = user.name; in
    [ (pipe.from "replicateHome" [
        (pipe.transform (entry: { user = srcUser; directories = entry.directories or [ ]; }))
        (pipe.broadcast ({ host, ... }: host.settings.core.network.syncthing.isHub or false))
      ]) ]
`transform` is role = "derive" (lib/compat/pipe.nix), so compilePipe builds a real
DAG and derived.__derived = true, so isSiteMarkData is FALSE -- OPS-ELIGIBLE, a
compose commitment. AND ITS `f` CLOSES OVER ctx.

MEASURED, one eval against a clean git archive of den-hoag HEAD c42df533:
    control_siteOnly_isSiteMarkData  true   ← POSITIVE CONTROL (predicate can return true)
    hubShares_isSiteMarkData         false  ← ops-eligible
    opsAtAlice   { user = "alice"; directories = ["d1"]; }
    opsAtBob     { user = "bob";   directories = ["d1"]; }
    opsDependsOnCtx                  TRUE
Same policy, two ctx values, different ops. The corpus has 8 user files, so this
ONE RECORD WOULD NEED UP TO 8 DISTINCT `ops`.

★ WHY THE FIXTURES COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT -- the arc's recurring shape, and this
instance is self-documenting. ALL SIX parity/fixtures/pipe-stages.nix pipe policies
are `_ctx:` -- shapeMetric, shapeStream, routePorts, renameRaw, gatherPeers,
shapeMarks. They ignore ctx BY CONSTRUCTION, and compat-compile-golden.nix:157 says
so out loud -- "Each pipe fixture's pipe.from policy body is unconditional, so any
ctx yields the pipeOp declaration" -- then fires each with `.fn { }`. The corpus
policy CANNOT be fired with { }; it reads user.name. VALIDATING OPS-DECLARABILITY
AGAINST THOSE FIXTURES IS A DEAD PREDICATE: they were SELECTED to be unconditional.

★★ MY MOTIVATING CASE WAS MISDIAGNOSED, AND THE MISDIAGNOSIS WAS MINE.
The bead argued `broadcast-hub-peer` declares emits = [ "pipeOp" ] and so "would
SILENTLY LOSE ITS OPS". IT HAS NO OPS AND CANNOT HAVE ANY. Measured
isSiteMarkData = true; den-hoag's own census agrees verbatim
(compat/produces-by-name.nix: "broadcast-hub-peer -- pipe (site-mark) -> pipeOp
(collection)"); and policyMessage BANS site-marks from `ops`. What it loses by
never being fired is its SITE MARK -- per-node body data, a real problem, but a
DIFFERENT FIELD that `recoverableFields = [ "emits" "ops" ]` does not even name.
⇒ I took the motivating example from the implementer's framing and put it in a gate
brief without checking it. The gate then had to spend its budget correcting the
premise before it could reach the design.

★ SECOND, INDEPENDENT KILL -- B PUNISHES A CORRECT DECLARATION. (Derivation from
B's own predicate, not measurement; labelled as such by the reviewer.)
`ops = [ ]` is the CORRECT and ONLY legal declaration for a site-mark-only policy:
policyMessage rejects a site-mark in `ops`, and conformingProduce permits site-marks
only from the BODY, so the body is the sole route for a mark. Under B,
`needsRecovery = r: any (f: !(r ? ${f})) [ "emits" "ops" ]`, a site-mark policy that
TRUTHFULLY declares `emits = [ "pipeOp" ]; ops = [ ];` is COMPLETE ⇒ never fired ⇒
ITS SITE MARK IS SILENTLY DROPPED. The bead sold this as the design's virtue --
"stops being fired the moment it declares ops" -- and for broadcast-hub-peer that
sentence describes the bug. B is correct on the corpus today ONLY BECAUSE NOBODY HAS
YET WRITTEN THE TRUE `ops = [ ]`. IT REWARDS OMISSION AND PUNISHES DECLARATION --
the exact inverse of the migration's thesis.

THE FUNNEL QUESTION, answered independently and standing regardless of B:
`ops` HAS NO FUNNEL. `emits` is checkable because every emission passes
conformingProduce and is tested against the declaration at EVERY firing.
`pipeOps = concatMap (r: r.ops) rules` feeds the compose seed, and THE SEED IS
DEFINED AS THE UNION OF DECLARED OPS -- there is no independently-produced value to
compare against. ★ The one guard that LOOKS like a funnel is not one:
conformingProduce's `opsInBody` abort is a PARTITION guard preventing double-
counting; it says nothing about whether a declared `ops` matches the pipe the author
wrote. For compat the declared ops must MIRROR a v1 body's stage list and NO ORACLE
FOR THAT CORRESPONDENCE EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. That is worse than
`negates`/`from` (den-hoag-4kh.52) -- those at least describe something the engine
could in principle observe. And it traps any shim: it can neither keep the body
emitting (⇒ opsInBody aborts) nor validate what it substitutes.

★★ WHAT THIS LEAVES OPEN, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE ORIGINAL QUESTION. The question
was framed as "how does COMPAT obtain ops without firing". The measured answer is
that OPS IS PER-FIRING DATA, so the premise that it can be a declared record field
fails for NATIVE policies too. The compose seed is currently specified as the union
of DECLARED ops; if ops cannot be declared, THE SEED'S CONSTRUCTION IS WRONG
UPSTREAM OF COMPAT. This is a spec-premise failure, not a wiring gap, and it needs a
design spike rather than another candidate. NO REPLACEMENT IS PROPOSED HERE.
CONSTRAINTS ANY ANSWER MUST SATISFY, all measured: (i) ops content may depend on
ctx; (ii) site-marks are a THIRD thing -- banned from ops, recoverable only from the
body -- and must not be conflated with ops as I conflated them; (iii) there is no
oracle for declared-ops correspondence, so any declaration is unchecked unless one is
built.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MIGRATION: the ~29 pipe-cluster ci failures stay RED with a
tracked id pointing here. They are the compose-commitment law working correctly
against an end that is not merely half-built but wrongly specified.

COVERAGE, kept: emission ORDER under a marks-only view, why the opt-out exists, and
B's complexity cost were NOT investigated -- moot once item 1 failed. den-configs
and the templates were NOT audited for further deriving pipes; one counterexample
settles the gate but a census would size the problem. ctx-dependence was measured for
`transform`; `filter`, `fold`, `for`, `as` are equally ops-eligible and equally able
to close over ctx, but the corpus contains none, so that is structural inference.
close_reason: REJECTED at item 1. ops is NOT ctx-independent: broadcast-syncthing-hub-shares (nix-config main pipes.nix:136-149) has a deriving transform stage closing over ctx.user.name; measured opsAtAlice != opsAtBob with a positive control. That kills any design making ops a static record field, not just this candidate. Second independent kill: B punishes a correct declaration - a site-mark policy truthfully declaring ops = [ ] is COMPLETE, never fired, and silently loses its site mark. My motivating case was also misdiagnosed: broadcast-hub-peer has no ops and cannot have any; what it loses is its SITE MARK, a different field. And ops has no funnel, so any declaration is unchecked. The real question is now a spec-premise failure upstream of compat, needing a design spike. Full reasons in notes.

title: [kernel] a cycle through a negative edge is admitted silently on the suppression path — measured live, while b1 aborts the identical shape; soundness rests on the pre-pass staging that is scheduled for retirement
description:
★★ MEASURED, LIVE, 2026-07-28. A cycle through a negative edge is ADMITTED
SILENTLY on the suppression path, while THE IDENTICAL SHAPE ABORTS on the
enrichment path. Same paper, same condition, two subsystems, opposite behaviour.

THE NEGATED READ. lib/compat/compile.nix gateSuppression:
    fn = ctx: if builtins.elem v1Name (ctx.suppressedPolicies or [ ])
              then [ ] else compiled.fn ctx;
Fires iff its own name is ABSENT from the set. A negative body literal. And the
`or [ ]` FAILS OPEN.

THE WITNESSES, built and run in scratch against the working-tree flake, native
surface, no repo writes:
    mutual  (A |-> not B, B |-> not A)  ->  suppressed-policies = ["B","A"]  NO ABORT
      positive control, same run: single non-cyclic suppressor -> ["B"]
    selfNeg (A |-> not A)               ->  suppressed-policies = ["A"]      NO ABORT
      negative control, same run: no suppressor -> []
Both are ABW Lemma 1's forbidden shape. Neither has a supported model: each
derived atom's sole justification is the other's absence, or its own.

★ AND WE ALREADY REJECT EXACTLY THIS, ONE SUBSYSTEM OVER.
ci/tests/b1-supportedness.nix carries test-self-negative-aborts AND
test-negative-cycle-aborts, both GREEN (suite 22/22 at this tree). The identical
shape on the suppression path is admitted in silence. The difference is not a
judgement about the two paths -- it is that the law was written for one of them.

★★ WHAT KEEPS IT SOUND TODAY IS STAGING, NOT STRATIFICATION -- AND THE STAGING IS
SCHEDULED FOR RETIREMENT. `suppress` facts are produced by the staged pre-pass
(fireExcludeAt, lib/staged-resolution.nix), injected onto root decls, delivered as
an inherited EDB fact. The pre-pass's own ctx (baseCtxOf / deliverCtxOf) is built
from prePassScopeRoots, FIXED BEFORE THE SUPPRESSIONS EXIST -- so during the
pre-pass the negative literal is evaluated against an EMPTY extension of the very
relation being computed. That is what makes the requirement hold.
⇒ RETIRING THE STAGED PRE-PASS CONVERTS AN ACCIDENTALLY-SOUND READ INTO AN
UNGUARDED SAME-STRATUM NEGATED READ. See den-hoag-4kh.18. Nothing in the tree
records that the pre-pass is load-bearing for ABW condition 2, and this is a
SECOND, INDEPENDENT reason its retirement needs a condition-2 story -- unrelated
to the rejected den-hoag-9xo.57.

IS `suppress` NEGATION IN THE ABW SENSE? YES, AND OUR OWN REPRESENTATION DECIDES
IT. Two readings were available. META: suppression selects a subprogram P' subset
P before the semantics is defined -- a program transformation, outside the model,
condition 2 does not apply. OBJECT: fires(P,node) <- gate(P,node) AND NOT
suppressed(P,node) is literally a clause with a negated body literal.
★ v1's mechanism was a DISPATCH FILTER (fx/handlers/dispatch-policies.nix) --
meta-level, defensibly outside the model. DEN-HOAG MOVED IT TO THE OBJECT LEVEL.
`suppress` is a first-class DECLARATION in the same vocabulary as member/edge/link
(declarations.nix groups.structural), produced by a policy BODY, carrying a
STRATUM, collected per-root, delivered by a scheduled INHERITED ATTRIBUTE
(suppressed-policies, stratum = structural), and consumed by a gate on another
rule's body. A meta-level program transformation does not get a stratum, does not
ride an attribute, and is not produced by a rule. Every one of those is an
object-level move. CONDITION 2 APPLIES.

★ THE ASYMMETRY THAT EXPLAINS WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and it is the useful part:
`suppress` names a POLICY. It quantifies over RULES, where ABW's negated literals
range over DOMAIN INDIVIDUALS. So it is object-level in REPRESENTATION while
remaining rule-quantified in CONTENT. The machinery that would enforce condition 2
(den.derived's `negates`, den.productions' `from`) ranges over RELATIONS and has
NO VOCABULARY for a predicate whose argument is a policy name. THE GAP IS NOT AN
OVERSIGHT IN EITHER COMPONENT; IT IS THE SEAM BETWEEN THEM. A fix that only
extends the existing guards will not reach it.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY, stated honestly. `suppressedPolicies` has NO NATIVE READER --
gateSuppression (compat) is its only consumer in lib/. So on the native surface
`suppress` produces and delivers a fact nothing negates against, and the
unsoundness bites only through compat. ★ BUT THE REPRESENTATION THAT ADMITS IT IS
NATIVE. Corpus exposure is believed nil: nix-config has ONE excluder
(drop-user-to-host-on-droid) and one excluder cannot cycle -- ★ that count is from
the parity ledger and was NOT re-verified in this run, so treat it as unconfirmed.

VERIFICATION NOTE ON THE WITNESS ITSELF: the derivation of the unsupported
suppressed set is MEASURED; the downstream bite through gateSuppression is
REASONED from reading it, not run. A compat-path witness showing the gate actually
disabling both policies has NOT been built. State that limit wherever this is cited.

WHERE CONDITION 2 IS ENFORCED, correctly, for contrast -- do not rebuild it:
lib/concern-derived.nix den.derived's `negates` field, with negatesUnroutable (a
negated predicate must route through the THROWING gate node.rel, never the
silent-empty node.query -- absent and out-of-scope must be distinguishable) and
negatesNotAbove = any (s: !(strataLt strataOrder s stratum)) negatesStrata --
STRICTLY below. Witness ci/tests/claim-negation.nix, 8/8 green, header verbatim:
"STRICTLY-ABOVE -- a negation reads a COMPLETE predicate, so the negating
production must sit STRICTLY ABOVE the max claim stratum", and it gets the
positive side right too: "a claim cycle is NOT a stratum cycle".

NOT THE PLACE TO LOOK, recorded so nobody repeats the search:
· ci/tests/b2-two-stratum.nix contains NO negation vocabulary at all -- no nac, no
  suppress, no drop, no reach-suppress. It tests condition-1-shaped properties and
  does not bear on condition 2.
· gen-resolve lib/schedule.nix is condition 1 ONLY and correctly so: readsAttrs is
  UNSIGNED, so condition 2 CANNOT BE STATED there. Convergence is handled by a
  different criterion entirely -- Knuth 1968 circularity -- which is TERMINATION,
  NOT SUPPORTEDNESS. A circular attr reading its own stratum negatively passes both.
· ci/tests/b1-supportedness.nix is a THIRD thing: a post-hoc SEMANTIC check that
  the published interpretation is supported (Theorem 7's CONCLUSION), not a
  syntactic stratification check (Definition 3's PREMISE). It catches a negative
  cycle by its SYMPTOM, is defensibly stronger for admitting non-stratified
  programs with supported models, and covers attribute 2's enrichment keyset ONLY.
· `nac` is UNREACHABLE -- set nowhere in den-hoag or gen-dispatch; the policy
  record has no nac field. Positive control given (the bare pattern matches a
  substring in output-modules.nix, proving the grep was live).
· `drop` / `reach-suppress` SATISFY condition 2 BY CONSTRUCTION, not by check:
  both read their negated facts out of `declarations` (synthesized -> structural)
  while sitting at circular -> resolution, hence strictly below. Nothing checks it;
  it holds because all declaration facts materialise one stratum down first.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★★ THE DOWNSTREAM BITE IS NOW MEASURED, NOT REASONED -- AND IT IS THE WORSE OF
THE TWO READINGS. Measured 2026-07-28, pinned at the session-end tree
(concern-policies fc30af1e / compat/compile.nix eb540e58; the four files the
suppression path runs through were STABLE all session).

Method: gateSuppression is a let-binding in compile.nix and not exported, so its
expression was reproduced VERBATIM --
    fn = ctx: if builtins.elem v1Name (ctx.suppressedPolicies or [ ]) then [ ] else compiled.fn ctx;
-- and applied to native records. Not a simulation: the gate's exact text on the
same rule shape. Each policy emits a `suppress` for the other PLUS an observable
`emit` marker for itself, so a fired policy is visible and a gated one is not.

    mutual  (A suppresses B, B suppresses A)  markers = [ ]                    supp = ["B","A"]
    oneway  (A suppresses B only)             markers = ["A-fired"]            supp = ["B"]     POSITIVE CONTROL
    neither (no suppression)                  markers = ["A-fired","B-fired"]  supp = [ ]       NEGATIVE CONTROL

IN THE MUTUAL CASE BOTH POLICIES PRODUCE NOTHING. Zero markers. No abort. Clean
eval. `oneway` proves the instrument reads markers and that the gate genuinely
disables; `neither` proves the empty mutual marker list is a real disabling and
not a probe artefact.

★ BLAST RADIUS, PRECISELY. The loss is NOT the `suppress` facts. gateSuppression
wraps the WHOLE fn, so a gated rule returns [ ] for EVERYTHING it would have
produced -- both policies' ENTIRE EMISSION AT EVERY NODE IN THE SUPPRESSED SCOPE
SUBTREE. And it wraps EVERY name-keyed compiled rule: den.policies, canTake
routes, and both include arms. A mutual pair silently removes two complete
policies from the fleet and the eval reports success.

★ AND IT IS SELF-CONCEALING: the suppression set ["B","A"] looks like a correct,
POPULATED result. An operator inspecting it sees evidence that suppression
"worked". There is no surface on which this looks wrong.

★★ THE CORPUS-CARDINALITY LEG: CONFIRMED, BUT THE LEDGER WAS RIGHT BY LUCK.
Re-measured with the broad bare-token `exclude` predicate over every .nix file in
three trees, both `.worktrees/` AND `.claude/worktrees/` pruned (BOTH exist in
nix-config and in denful/den), positive controls in each run.
ONLY ONE CONSTRUCT MINTS A suppress: `declare.suppress` has exactly ONE call site
in the tree, lib/compat/compile.nix:885, the `den.lib.policy.exclude <NAMED
POLICY>` arm. Everything else labelled "exclude" is a different mechanism --
den.schema.<kind>.excludes filters the includes list and mints no suppress;
den.aspects.<name>.excludes folds into meta.drop, the `drop` RESOLUTION kind, the
other negation path, which is condition-2-safe by construction.
    nix-config main   1 policy.exclude call,  1 targeting a NAMED POLICY
    den-configs (19)  0                       0
    den templates     2                       0
★ THE TWO TEMPLATE SITES ARE ONES THE LEDGER NEVER EXAMINED: an ASPECT target
(templates/ci/modules/deadbugs/issue-540-exclude-guard.nix) and INLINE NAMELESS
CONTENT (…/standalone-home-host-context.nix). HAD EITHER TARGETED A NAMED POLICY
THE LEDGER'S CLAIM WOULD HAVE BEEN FALSE AND NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT.
⇒ Treat cardinality-1 as a MEASURED FACT WITH A 3-TREE SCOPE, never as a property.
And it remains a CORPUS fact: the bar is expressibility, and the witnesses above
build the cycle in two POLICY RECORDS with no compat involved.

⇒ BOTH LEGS OF THE P1 PRICING CHECK OUT. One is stronger than filed; one is
confirmed but fragile.

COVERAGE LIMIT TO CARRY: the witness reproduces gateSuppression's EXPRESSION
rather than driving the real v1 shim end to end (den.lib.policy.exclude → bridge →
compile.nix:885). That path was traced by READING and its shape confirmed by the
census; a two-policy mutual-exclusion fleet in v1 SYNTAX was not constructed and
run. The gate's semantics are measured; the v1 AUTHORING path to it is read.

title: [kernel] the stratum instrumentation is vacuous in production: ctxKeyStrata is empty at every non-test call site, and gate is a declared assertion rather than functionArgs
description:
MEASURED at the 9xo.57 gate, 2026-07-28. Survives that design's rejection --
this is about the INSTRUMENT, not the rejected proposal.

TWO SURFACES THAT LOOK LIKE SOUNDNESS INSTRUMENTATION AND CANNOT ACT AS IT.

(1) ctxKeyStrata IS EMPTY AT EVERY PRODUCTION CALL SITE.
The coordinate-to-stratum map is the only thing in the tree that could assign a
stratum to a ctx KEY (as opposed to an emitted KIND). Production call sites:
  lib/concern-policies.nix  -- seededStrataCfg.ctxKeyStrata = { }
  lib/default.nix           -- the compile site, likewise empty
Only ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix ever populates it. Untagged keys fall through
`ctxKeyStratum.${key} or null` and compare BELOW EVERYTHING.
=> Any predicate of the form "what stratum does this policy READ at" evaluates to
bottom for every policy in the tree and in the corpus. A check built on it is a
TAUTOLOGY, and reads as a guard while guarding nothing. This is precisely how the
rejected 9xo.57 would have replaced an aborting ban with a fail-open.

(2) gate IS A DECLARED FIELD, NOT builtins.functionArgs.
  lib/concern-policies.nix -- gateOf = v: v.gate or (builtins.functionArgs v.fn);
functionArgs is only the DEFAULT. For any policy supplying `gate`, the field is an
UNCHECKED ASSERTION about a body whose actual reads are unconstrained -- not a
syntactic under-approximation of them. This is not hypothetical: the compat
include/policy compiler declares its gate (lib/compat/compile.nix compilePolicy --
`__condition = fnArgsOf (innerFn value)` over a bare-ctx wrapper `fn = ctx: ...`
whose own functionArgs is `{ }`).
=> Any soundness argument phrased over "the policy's reads" is, for compiled
policies, an argument over what the COMPILER ASSERTED, not over what the body does.

WHY THIS IS FILED SEPARATELY FROM THE REJECTED DESIGN. 9xo.57 was rejected on
theory (ABW Definition 3 p. 96 is asymmetric; it covered no negation case) and
would have been rejected on these two independently. The next design that reaches
for a read-stratum or a gate-based soundness check will hit exactly the same wall,
and the register of what the instruments can actually see must exist BEFORE that
design is written rather than be re-discovered at its gate.

NOT A REMEDY, DELIBERATELY. Whether ctxKeyStrata should be POPULATED (making the
read-stratum real) or REMOVED (making the absence of the capability honest) is a
posture question of the den-hoag-4kh.21 family -- a declared surface the engine
does not honour. It should be answered as that, not patched at one call site.

POSITIVE-CONTROL NOTE: the reviewer established the companion nested-read hazard
had no policy-path instance at this pin WITH a positive control -- 14 non-comment
`host.hasAspect` reads in nix-config main tree @ 9ebf3316, all in aspects/ and
batteries/, ZERO in modules/den/policies/**. So the predicate was not vacuous. The
two findings above are structural and need no corpus instance.

title: [kernel] is den.schema.<K>.excludes kind-flat or subtree-scoped? P1 folds it into a flat selects field in one line and the corpus witness cannot tell the difference
description:
OPEN QUESTION, raised before P1 lands so the selection defect is not half-fixed.

den-hoag-9xo.54 states the load-bearing structural claim: an INERT excludes and
an OVER-BROAD includes are THE SAME DEFECT FROM TWO SIDES -- the kind schema is
not governing which policies apply -- and fixing either alone leaves the other
able to produce the same symptom.

P1 (2026-07-28-policy-record-primitive-design.md) fixes the INCLUDES side. Its
entire treatment of the excludes side is ONE LINE, :828, folding
den.schema.<K>.{includes,excludes} into the per-policy `selects` field. `selects`
is specified at :223 and :268-:294 as three-valued over a flat list of KINDS:

    selects :: null | [ Kind ]
    null  = unconstrained
    [ ]   = selects nothing
    [k..] = fires at nodes whose OWN KIND is in the list

THE QUESTION: is den.schema.<K>.excludes KIND-FLAT or SUBTREE-SCOPED? A flat
per-kind list can express the first and not the second.

WHY IT IS OPEN. den-hoag-9xo.28 records an owner ruling that excludes is
includes' DUAL, SCOPED TO THE SUBTREE. If that scoping is real, then excluding a
policy at kind K must also suppress it at K's DESCENDANTS, and folding it into a
flat `selects` silently drops that -- the corpus instance would still look fixed,
because den.schema.host.excludes = [ host-to-users ] targets a policy that fires
at hosts, so kind-level removal happens to suffice THERE. That is the dangerous
shape: correct on the one witness, wrong in general, and invisible to the witness.

DO NOT CONFLATE TWO DIFFERENT v1 MECHANISMS. Both are called "exclude":
  (1) den.schema.<K>.excludes -- STATIC, schema-level, per entity kind. v1
      consumes it in nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix (the schemaExcludes binding, and
      the `excludes = schemaExcludes` field on the returned entity record). This
      is den-hoag-9xo.28 and it is what THIS bead is about.
  (2) policy.exclude <policy> -- DYNAMIC, emitted as a policy EFFECT at fire
      time (nix/lib/policy-effects.nix, __policyEffect = "exclude"), a name-keyed
      scope-local constraint consulted over scope+ancestors so descendants
      inherit and siblings are isolated (v1 fx/handlers/dispatch-policies.nix).
      This is the exclude-family, ALREADY SHIPPED as #72, and it is NOT this bead.
  The subtree language in 9xo.28's ruling may have imported (2)'s scoping onto
  (1). If so the ruling needs restating rather than implementing. If not, P1's
  `selects` is under-powered for (1) and needs a scoped representation.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: read v1 at the pin and establish whether the entity
record's `excludes` field is consulted only at nodes of that kind, or over the
entity's subtree/scope chain. Trace where resolve-entity's returned `excludes`
is READ, not merely where it is set -- the setter says nothing about scope.
An absence claim needs a positive control on the same predicate in the same run.

BLOCKS: nothing yet, deliberately -- P1's includes half is correct either way and
should not wait. But den-hoag-9xo.28 must not be closed, and the selection defect
must not be declared fixed, until this is answered.
notes:
★★ ANSWERED, 2026-07-28, BY MEASUREMENT. VERDICT: SUBTREE-SCOPED.
den.schema.<K>.excludes reaches K AND ALL ITS DESCENDANTS. Measured on den v1 at
99cc0c5a1cc846cb1be681344b10d2731d430e13 (main, clean tree) with a probe fleet
and two positive controls.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE, AND IT BLOCKS THE ONE LINE P1 SPENDS ON THIS:
P1's `selects :: null | [ Kind ]` CANNOT REPRESENT excludes. Folding
den.schema.<K>.{includes,excludes} into a flat per-kind list (the policy-record
spec, :828) DROPS THE DESCENDANT REACH.

★ THE EXTENT ASYMMETRY -- the finding, and it is visible in TWO ADJACENT LINES
of the same record, nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix:72-73:
  includes  fires ONLY AT K-NODES. It is consumed as the K node's own children,
            and the K record only exists at K nodes.
  excludes  reaches K AND ALL DESCENDANTS. It is consumed as a scope-registered
            constraint carrying a LITERAL `scope = "subtree"`, read over
            scope+ancestors.
A DUAL HAS ONE EXTENT. THESE DO NOT. Measured, same instrument, same run:
  k  includes at host, observed AT THE HOST      -> FIRES     (positive control)
  j  includes at host, observed at the USER      -> ABSENT
  c  excludes at host, observed at the USER      -> SUPPRESSED  (discriminator)

THE READ SITE, which the setter could never have told us.
nix/lib/aspects/fx/aspect/children.nix registerConstraints (called from
compile-static.nix `(registerConstraints tagged)`):

    rawExcludes = aspect.excludes or [ ];
    excludeList = map (ref: { type = "exclude"; scope = "subtree";
                              identity = excludeIdentity ref; }) rawExcludes;
    fx.seq (map (c: fx.send "register-constraint" (c // { inherit owner; })) allConstraints);

`scope = "subtree"` is written LITERALLY AT THE SCHEMA-EXCLUDES SITE. It is not
inherited from the policy-effect path. That single expression settles it.
register-constraint writes scopedConstraintRegistry.${currentScope}.${identity};
currentScope is the K INSTANCE's scope. Every reader goes through
foldScopeAncestors (constraint.nix), so a descendant walks up scopeParent, hits
K's scope, and finds K's entries. Four readers enumerated exhaustively, all
resolving to that same fold: check-constraint, dispatch-policies (by NAME, no
ownerChain filter), compile-conditional's guard hasAspect view, and policy/
schema.nix's late sibling dispatch.

★★ THE PREMISE OF THIS BEAD WAS WRONG, AND THE TRUTH IS MORE USEFUL.
I suspected the dynamic `policy.exclude` effect's scoping had been mistakenly
attributed to the static schema field. It had not. (1) AND (2) ARE NOT TWO
MECHANISMS THAT GOT CONFUSED -- THEY ARE ONE MECHANISM WITH TWO PRODUCERS:
  (1) children.nix    { type = "exclude"; scope = "subtree"; identity = excludeIdentity ref; }
  (2) policy/apply.nix { type = "exclude"; scope = "subtree"; identity = identity.key e.value; owner = "policy"; }
Both fx.send "register-constraint" into ONE scopedConstraintRegistry, read by the
same four readers. They differ only in `owner` and in IDENTITY GRAIN -- (1)
reduces an __isPolicy ref to a bare ref.name, which is exactly what lets
dispatch-policies match it against policy-attrset KEYS.

⇒ AMENDMENT TO den-hoag-9xo.28's RULING. Its ANSWER (subtree-scoped) is correct
and stands. Its JUSTIFICATION -- "excludes is includes' DUAL, scoped to the
subtree" -- is the WRONG REASON, and the wrong reason is what would have licensed
the flat fold: a dual invites you to model it as includes-with-a-minus-sign. The
right reason is that both exclude producers feed one scope-keyed registry whose
only read path is an ancestor fold. Restate the ruling that way.

★ WHY NO REAL CONFIG COULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS. Full census of schema-tier excludes,
MAIN TREES ONLY (nix-config @ 9ebf3316, den templates, den-configs): EIGHT sites,
and EVERY ONE IS SAME-KIND -- the excluded policy is attached at the SAME kind it
is excluded from. ZERO descendant-firing exclusions exist in den's defaults or
anywhere in the corpus. The corpus witness (host.excludes = [ host-to-users ],
host-to-users attached at den.schema.host.includes, modules/policies/core.nix:33)
therefore CANNOT distinguish kind-flat from subtree-scoped. That IS the finding:
the distinction costs nothing observable today, which is precisely why the flat
fold would pass the entire corpus and still be wrong.
A DISCRIMINATING FIXTURE MUST BE CONSTRUCTED. The minimal one is arm c: policy
attached at den.schema.user.includes, excluded at den.schema.host.excludes,
observed at the user.

WHAT THE KERNEL ACTUALLY NEEDS, stated as shape and NOT as a remedy: a policy
attachment is a NODE-LOCAL label; an exclusion is a REGION constraint over the
containment subtree, keyed by identity and resolved by an ancestor walk. Two
different query shapes over the same graph. Note for whoever designs it: the
descendant reach is a reachability query over the containment relation, and
gen-graph already provides one -- but reachableFrom is IRREFLEXIVE and excludes
reaches K ITSELF, so the reflexive closure is required and a mechanical swap
would silently drop the K-node case (the exact trap recorded in
feedback_reuse_scan_before_build rule 8).

MEASUREMENT DETAIL. Arms: a control (no excludes) FIRES -- the instrument
responds. b same-kind SUPPRESSED. c host-excludes/user-observed SUPPRESSED
(discriminator). d flake-system, two up, SUPPRESSED. e DIFFERENT policy name at
host FIRES -- name-keyed, not blanket. h excludes at `home`, a NON-ANCESTOR,
FIRES; g2 is h's positive control -- den.schema.home.excludes demonstrably DOES
suppress at the home node in the same run, so h's surviving marker is a real
negative and not an unregistered declaration. ★ h+g2 rule out GLOBAL, which c and
d alone could not, since both used ancestors. Aspect-VALUED excludes measured
separately (they take the check-constraint reader with its extra ownerChain
filter rather than dispatch-policies): n1 none FIRES, n2 at user SUPPRESSED, n3 at
host SUPPRESSED, n4 at home FIRES -- identical shape.
CENSUS PREDICATE CONTROL: the first pattern schema\.[a-zA-Z-]*\.excludes MISSED
two sites using the nested form den.schema.flake-system = { includes = ...;
excludes = ...; }; the broadened bare-excludes grep found them IN THE SAME RUN.

OPEN, AND EXPLICITLY INFERENCE NOT MEASUREMENT: whether den.schema.<K>.isolated
(push-scope.nix sets scopeIsolated) cuts the ancestor walk. Reading
foldScopeAncestors, it never consults scopeIsolated, so no effect is EXPECTED --
untested. If it does cut, the extent is subtree-modulo-isolation and any design
must carry that. Also untested: spawn/forward merged sub-pipelines, where
constraint.nix notes scopeParent can cycle; and the __provider-without-name
branch of excludeIdentity.
close_reason: ANSWERED: SUBTREE-SCOPED, measured on den v1 @ 99cc0c5a with two positive controls. The read site writes scope = "subtree" literally at the schema-excludes site (children.nix registerConstraints), and every reader goes through foldScopeAncestors. Decisive: includes and excludes have DIFFERENT EXTENTS from two adjacent lines of one record, so P1 flat selects list cannot represent excludes. 9xo.28 answer stands, its dual justification does not. All 8 corpus sites are same-kind, so no real config can discriminate; a fixture must be constructed. Full measurement in notes.

title: [kernel] policy stratum by HEAD not by rule: route emissions per-kind, abort only on inversion — retires the multi-stratum registration ban (gate candidate)
description:
GATE CANDIDATE -- NOT VALIDATED. Proposed amendment to
2026-07-28-policy-record-primitive-design.md, replacing its registration-time
rejection of a policy whose emits span strata.

WHAT THE SPEC SAYS NOW. A policy record declares emits :: [Kind] (REQUIRED). Its
stratum derives from emits. A policy emitting kinds in two different strata is
rejected at registration. Spec section 1.4 justified this by measurement: no
instance in the corpus.

TWO MEASUREMENTS AGAINST IT (p1-impl, 2026-07-28):

  1. The corpus is indeed clean -- zero multi-stratum firings on the nix-config
     pin. The rejection is therefore SAFE on the corpus. That is all it is.
  2. Section 1.4's own predicate could not have matched the branch it declared
     empty. It counted only the rows whose probe EMITTED; the multi-group branch
     is reachable ONLY when the probe is EMPTY. A sound measurement proving a
     different proposition (feedback_verification_predicate_blindness).
     ci/tests/compat-policy-expansion.nix:482-522 test-declared-multi-group-slices
     IS an instance, and :230-254 test-mixed-strata-self-route emits link
     (structural) and edge (resolution) at one ctx.

AND CORPUS-ABSENCE IS NOT A LICENCE TO REJECT. The bar is den-surface
expressibility, never corpus presence (feedback_den_surface_not_config). A
rejection needs a THEORY reason. There is none, and the theory says the opposite:

  Apt, Blair and Walker 1988, "Towards a Theory of Declarative Knowledge",
  Stratified Programs, Definition 3 p. 96. A stratification assigns levels so
  that a rule's head level is at least every positive body level and strictly
  above every negated one. STRATUM IS A PROPERTY OF THE PREDICATE (the emitted
  kind), NOT OF THE RULE. An ABW rule has ONE head; a two-head rule is sugar for
  two rules sharing a body, at two levels. Nothing forbids that. What
  stratification forbids is the INVERSE: a rule whose BODY reads a level at or
  above its own head (supportedness, p. 95; Theorem 7 p. 111).

PROPOSED SEMANTICS -- route by head, gate on reads:

    firingStratum = max over k in reads(gate) of stratumOf k
    each emission d lands in stratumOf d.kind
    SOUND iff firingStratum <= min over k in emits of stratumOf k

A policy fires ONCE, at the stratum its READS require. Its emissions are
partitioned to their own strata by kind -- free, since every declaration already
carries its kind. Emitting UPWARD is sound (producing a fact early). The abort is
on INVERSION only: reading at or above a stratum you emit below. That is the
condition supportedness actually names, stated by construction rather than
approximated by a registration-time ban.

CONSEQUENCES IF ACCEPTED:
  - Ruling (a) resolves to DO NOT SPLIT: the two multi-stratum fixtures stay as
    authored; they were never ill-formed.
  - Section 1.4's refutation stops being load-bearing -- the branch having an
    instance is fine once the branch is not a rejection branch.
  - The record keeps emits REQUIRED and total (feedback_absence_is_a_decision);
    this changes only what is DERIVED from it.
  - Cost: one max and one min over small declared lists per policy, at
    registration. No extra fn evaluation -- explicitly NOT the split-into-two-
    rules encoding, which would run the body twice (feedback_performance_is_defect
    asks the complexity be stated: split is 2x body evaluation; partition is 1x).

WHAT THE GATE MUST ATTACK:
  - Is reads(gate) actually total? gate = functionArgs fn sees only the top-level
    destructure. A policy reading a stratum-2 coordinate THROUGH a stratum-1
    binding would be invisible to the inversion check, and the check would pass
    while the read is unsound. This is the load-bearing weakness.
  - Does stratumOf exist as a total function on Kind at registration time, or is
    it itself derived from the very emits sets being checked (circularity)?
  - Does any existing kernel site assume one-policy-one-stratum?
notes:
★★ REJECTED AT THE GATE, 2026-07-28. Recorded with reasons so it is not
re-proposed. The design was authored by the orchestrator; the reviewer was
fresh-context and independent.

THEORY — THE CENTRAL CLAIM IS BACKWARDS.
Apt, Blair and Walker 1988 Definition 3 p. 96 is ASYMMETRIC:
  1. a relation occurring POSITIVELY in a clause in P_i has its definition
     within the union of P_j for j <= i   -- SAME STRATUM PERMITTED
  2. a relation occurring NEGATIVELY in a clause in P_i has its definition
     within the union of P_j for j < i    -- STRICTLY BELOW
ABW's own gloss: "each stratum defines new relations in terms of ITSELF ONLY
POSITIVELY and in terms of the relations from the previous strata, POSSIBLY
NEGATIVELY." Same-level positive reads are how intra-stratum recursion works.
The design stated ONE rule for both occurrences, strict in its prose ("at or
above") and non-strict in its formula (firingStratum <= min over emits). So the
prose forbids what ABW permits, and the formula permits what ABW forbids for
negated reads. THERE IS NO NEGATION CASE IN THE DESIGN AT ALL, and den-hoag has
negated reads: gen-dispatch rules carry `nac` (nacPasses in stepGroup,
gen-derive/lib/core/dispatch.nix) and the vocabulary carries suppress, drop,
reach-suppress. A single non-strict comparison admits an intra-stratum negated
read -- the cycle-through-a-negative-edge ABW Lemma 1 exists to rule out.

MISATTRIBUTION, and it is already in the tree. Supportedness p. 95 is a property
of an INTERPRETATION; Theorem 7 p. 111 says M_P is a supported model. Neither
states the syntactic level condition -- that is Definition 3's content. The
design cited the CONSEQUENCE as the source of the PREMISE, and the same wrong
gloss is now in lib/errors.nix multiStratumUnsupported verbatim. Correction
dispatched to p1-impl.

MECHANISM — THE PROPOSED CHECK CANNOT FIRE.
firingStratum = max over reads(gate) of stratumOf k applies stratumOf to
COORDINATES, not kinds. The only coordinate-to-stratum map in the tree is
ctxKeyStrata, and it is EMPTY at every production call site (concern-policies
seededStrataCfg.ctxKeyStrata = { }, and lib/default.nix's compile site); only
ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix ever populates it. Untagged keys fall through
`ctxKeyStratum.${key} or null` and compare below everything.
=> firingStratum is bottom for EVERY policy in tree and corpus, and the
inversion test is a TAUTOLOGY. THE DESIGN REPLACES A BAN THAT ABORTS WITH A
CHECK THAT CANNOT FIRE -- a fail-open, and exactly the shape
feedback_absence_is_a_decision warns against. Independent of the functionArgs
question entirely.

AND A FIRING LOSS, not merely an analysis gap. structural.nix attr 4 injects
linked-context between phases (combine = ctx: delta: linkedFrom (delta.structural
or [ ]) // ctx), binding the link target's enriched-context -- a key existing
only from the resolution phase onward, and untagged in ctxKeyStrata. The design
scores it at the bottom BY CONSTRUCTION and schedules the policy where its
coordinate is ABSENT; fromFunctionMatch is a presence gate
(all (k: ctx ? ${k}) required, gen-derive/lib/core/rule.nix). THE POLICY
SILENTLY NEVER FIRES.

gate IS A DECLARED FIELD, NOT functionArgs. gateOf = v: v.gate or
(builtins.functionArgs v.fn) -- functionArgs is only the DEFAULT. For any policy
supplying gate, reads(gate) is an UNCHECKED ASSERTION over a body whose actual
reads are unconstrained, not a syntactic under-approximation. The compat
include/policy compiler declares its gate (compile.nix compilePolicy). The
design's stated premise was not the surface.

THE NESTED-READ HAZARD: no policy-path instance at this pin, established with a
positive control (14 non-comment host.hasAspect reads in nix-config main tree,
ALL in aspects/batteries, ZERO in modules/den/policies/**). But the design opens
by ruling that corpus-absence is no licence, and may not then lean on
corpus-absence for its own soundness. den.enrichContext is a generic open seam.

REUSE-SCAN FAILURE: THE BAN IS PARTLY IN AN EXTERNAL GEN LIBRARY. gen-dispatch
core/declared.nix deriveGroup aborts on "declared kinds spanning multiple
groups", documented as "the single-group-per-rule law (gen-dispatch's core
invariant)", and compileOne already calls it. THE DESIGN DOES NOT MENTION
GEN-DISPATCH. Further, gen-dispatch stepGroup buckets by PHASE not per-action
kind (cand = filter (r: r.group == groupName), groupActions filed under
${groupName}) -- PER-EMISSION ROUTING FROM A SINGLE FIRING DOES NOT EXIST IN THE
ENGINE. The design's core mechanism is unimplementable without changing a gen
library it never named.

COST CLAIM FALSE. The design stated partition = 1x body evaluation vs split =
2x, and stated it as free. den-hoag's only partition mechanism ever
(mkDeclaredSlices -> mkSlice) gave distinct projected ctx per stratum, hence
distinct thunks: N groups = N BODY EVALUATIONS. The deleted mkExpanded fan was
3x. No shared-firing path has ever existed. And ABW's own desugaring of a
two-head rule IS two clauses, each evaluated at its head's stratum over that
stratum's saturated base -- THE 2x IS WHAT THE CITED SEMANTICS PRESCRIBES. The
design claimed to beat the semantics it cited (feedback_performance_is_defect:
a stated complexity that is wrong is worse than none).

FEED DERIVATION BROKEN, AND ITS ALARM JUST RETIRED. concern-policies' two
staged-pre-pass feeds select on `r.group == "structural" && emitsAny r ...`.
Today r.group derives from emits (single, since multi aborts), so the test
reduces to emits-membership. Under the design r.group becomes the READ stratum,
so a policy emitting member (structural) + edge (resolution) whose reads place
it at resolution is EXCLUDED FROM THE RESOLVE-FAMILY FEED and its member
SILENTLY DROPS. The guards that made exactly that drop loud
(resolveFamilyUntagged / excludeFamilyUntagged) were retired in the same
uncommitted migration diff, on the reasoning that feed membership is now derived
from emits -- the very equivalence this design breaks.

RETIRING REGISTER (den-hoag-4kh.17) -- ONE HIT, UNNAMED: item 3, the 2-STAGE
SCHEDULE / prePassScopeRoots (den-hoag-4kh.18). Both feeds exist SOLELY to serve
that staged pre-pass, and their selector is precisely what the design changes.
The register's own worked example: "THE GUARDS EXIST BECAUSE THE RETIRING
CONSTRUCT FAILS, so extending them extends it." The design names none of it and
removes the alarm.

WHAT SURVIVES THE REJECTION, and should not be re-litigated:
  - The section 1.4 refutation is REAL and doubly so: the population counted
    EMITTED kinds where the branch tested DECLARED kinds, and KINDS where the
    branch tested STRATA. Positive control inside the design's own document --
    section 1.5's table reports 36 rows in the reachable `expanded` population,
    so the run COULD have measured it and did not.
  - stratumOf : Kind -> stratum IS total and NOT circular
    (declare.stratumOfKind over the static groups map in lib/declarations.nix;
    knownKind rejects an unknown kind at registration). The design's second
    stated worry was unfounded.
  - Corpus-absence does not license a ban. That principle stands; it simply did
    not make THIS replacement correct.

CONSEQUENCE: the multi-stratum registration ban STAYS. Reversal dispatched to
p1-impl, together with the errors.nix comment correction.
close_reason: REJECTED at the adversarial gate: ABW Definition 3 p.96 is asymmetric (same-stratum positive reads are permitted; only negated reads must be strictly below), the design stated one rule for both and covered no negation case; the proposed inversion check is a tautology because ctxKeyStrata is empty at every production call site; it causes a silent firing loss on linked-context coordinates; per-emission routing does not exist in gen-dispatch and the ban is partly that library core invariant; and the 1x cost claim is false. Full reasons in notes.

title: [kernel] five exclude-family fixtures pin a registration shape the corpus never uses — bare den.policies with no includes entry, which v1 never fires
description:
MEASURED, 2026-07-28. Five tests in ci/tests/compat-exclude-family.nix pin a policy
registration shape that the corpus does not use and that den v1 never fires.

THE FIXTURE (compat-exclude-family.nix:75-93) registers its excluders under
den.policies via mk's extraPolicies, and names them in NO includes list:

    excluded = mk { drop-user-to-host-on-droid = { host, ... }: ... };
    detected = mk { always-exclude = _ctx: [ (exclude userToHostRef) ]; };
    rogue    = mk { rogue-excluder = { host, ... }: ... };

THE CORPUS (sini/nix-config @ 9ebf3316, MAIN TREE,
modules/den/batteries/nix-on-droid.nix) writes BOTH halves, seven lines apart:

     97:  den.policies.drop-user-to-host-on-droid =
     99:    lib.optional (host.class == "droid") (den.lib.policy.exclude den.policies.user-to-host);
    104:  den.default.includes = [ den.policies.drop-user-to-host-on-droid ];

Line 97 is the DEFINITION. Line 104 is the SELECTION. The corpus author did not
rely on bare registration to apply the policy, and neither does den v1: v1's
resolveEntity (nix/lib/resolve-entity.nix:22,72 @ 99cc0c5a) builds each kind's
includes/excludes from its SCHEMA ENTRY, and a policy reachable through no
includes chain never fires, so it never emits its policy.exclude effect
(nix/lib/policy-effects.nix:182 -- exclude is an EFFECT emitted at fire time,
classified by fx/handlers/emit-policy-effects.nix).

WHY THIS MATTERS: den-hoag-9xo.53 measured den-hoag applying policies that are in
no includes list, where v1 applies zero. These five fixtures are the SAME defect
wearing an exclude hat -- they pass today only because den-hoag dispatches the
pre-pass exclude feed without consulting selection at all. So they do not
independently corroborate the current feed semantics; they are downstream of the
defect and would fail correctly once selection is honoured.

REMEDY: the fixtures gain the selection half the corpus already writes
(den.default.includes = [ ... ], or a kind includes entry where the test means to
scope it), after which they test what they were written to test -- suppression
collection and the double-fire guard -- rather than the absence of selection.

copies; the citation above is the MAIN tree, re-derived
(project_gen_spec_audit: exclude .worktrees/ from every grep).

title: [kernel] excludedType drops raw/deferredModule fields 'to keep them out of deepSeq'd resolution state' — no such deepSeq exists at HEAD; this is witness 5's mechanism and it gates P3
description:
★★ THE CHARTERING PREMISE FOUND IN THE WILD — A v1-ERA CONSTRAINT RETAINED WITH ITS ORIGINAL RATIONALE, AND
THE RATIONALE IS NOT WITNESSED AT HEAD. THIS GATES P3 OF THE REFACTOR ORDER.

`excludedType` drops `raw` / `deferredModule` / `anything` fields from the entity record. Justified at FOUR
sites — lib/compat/registry.nix:226, :296 and lib/compat/ingest.nix:58, :418 — by:
    "must never enter deepSeq'd resolution state."
★ NO SUCH deepSeq EXISTS AT HEAD. The kernel's deepSeqs are exactly: the policy probe
(concern-policies.nix:185), a totality probe (query.nix:86), and two EAGER OUTPUT-TABLE validations
(default.nix:2607, :2618). The one deepSeq on the resolution path is gen-scope/lib/build-nodes.nix:66, under
`strict ? true` (:17) which den-hoag never overrides — AND IT COVERS ONLY `parentIndex`, A MAP OF NODE-ID
STRINGS, NOT decls AND NOT ENTITY VALUES.
POSITIVE CONTROL, same predicate same run: the identical `grep -rn "strict"` that returned no assignment in
`lib/` (excluding `compat/`) DOES return `strict ? true,` at build-nodes.nix:17 and `if strict then` at :66.
So the instrument finds the construct where it exists.

★ THIS IS WITNESS 5's MECHANISM. v1 declares `aspect` as `lib.types.raw` (denful/den @ 99cc0c5a,
nix/lib/entities/host.nix:70) — so `excludedType` is EXACTLY WHAT DROPS IT, and with it `environment` and
`microvm`. The missing-host-field class (den-hoag-9xo.49) is not three oversights; it is one exclusion rule
doing what it was written to do, for a reason that may no longer obtain.

★★ WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED — the auditor was explicit and I am preserving the distinction:
  ESTABLISHED: the STATED CAUSE is not witnessed at HEAD, and nobody has re-derived it.
  NOT ESTABLISHED: that the exclusion is unnecessary. It may STILL be load-bearing — for identity hashing, or
  for the terminal merge — by a mechanism nobody has written down.
⇒ THE OWNER-LEVEL QUESTION: RE-DERIVE WHETHER `excludedType` IS STILL REQUIRED, AND IF SO, FOR WHAT. P3
(entity record derives from the schema) CANNOT BE DESIGNED UNTIL THIS IS ANSWERED, because P3's whole content
is which fields reach the record.
★ AND IF IT IS NOT REQUIRED, DO NOT SIMPLY DELETE IT — the four sites carry the same sentence, so whatever
replaces it must be stated once and cited, or the next reader re-derives the same dead justification from the
same comment.

WHY THIS ENTRY MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN FIX: den-hoag-4kh was chartered on the premise that "a v1-shaped state
accumulator wearing gen-native naming passes every guard", and that `ci/tests/boundary.nix` guards the line
LEXICALLY ONLY so it cannot observe representation. THIS IS THAT PREMISE INSTANTIATED: a constraint inherited
from an evaluation model den-hoag no longer has, justified by a comment nobody re-checked, silently deleting
user-declared fields, GREEN ON EVERY GUARD. It was found by reading the justification and looking for the
thing it names — not by any test.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ VERDICT: **NOT LOAD-BEARING** — and this bead's PREMISE WAS STALE, which changes what P3 is about.

★ `excludedType` DOES NOT DROP FIELDS FROM THE ENTITY RECORD. It stopped doing that at commit `77cb3c8`
("feat(compat): #70 — raw ctx-entity fields ride a lazy side channel", ledger row u20). At HEAD it PARTITIONS
FIELDS ACROSS TWO TRANSPORTS: `stampTreeOf` (registry.nix:292) → `_entityStamps`, `rawStampTreeOf` (:304) →
`_entityRawStamps` (bridge.nix:299,363), both overlaid onto the ctx entity at ingest.nix:435 / :441 / :722.
★★ AND `stampFieldNamesByKind` (ingest.nix:449-456) **UNIONS BOTH TREES' NAMES**, so THE KERNEL-DECLARED FIELD
SET IS IDENTICAL WITH OR WITHOUT THE EXCLUSION. `excludedType` selects WHICH CHANNEL A FIELD'S VALUE TRAVELS
ON — not which fields reach the record.
⇒ P3's STATED CONTENT — "which fields reach the record" — ALREADY HAS ITS ANSWER AT HEAD: **ALL DECLARED
REGISTRY FIELDS DO.** P3's real open content is whether the field set should keep coming from A PARALLEL
nixpkgs-lib EVAL OF THE REGISTRY at all, rather than from `den.schema` directly.
Also: `excludedType` occurs in `lib/compat/registry.nix` ONLY (:235,:243,:292,:304,:527). ingest.nix:58 and
:418 are the JUSTIFICATION COMMENT, not call sites. Positive control: the same grep returns the five registry
lines, so the instrument finds the symbol where it exists.

FALSIFIER, scratch clone, exit read adjacent: ci 1946/1946 EXIT 0 → **1940/1946 EXIT 1** widened (5 ❌ + 1 ☢️);
parity 71/71 EXIT 0 BOTH; ship gate `allEqual: true` EXIT 0 both, ★ with the SAME THREE STORE PATHS as
baseline — equal to baseline, not merely equal to each other.
ALL SIX FAILURES CLASSIFIED **(iii) — TESTS ASSERTING THE EXCLUSION ITSELF**, zero (i). One header literally
calls itself "THE ABSENCE PIN". ★ And the direct negative for the identity hypothesis: in
`compat-raw-field-stamp.test-safe-stamp-and-identity-unchanged`, only `noRawHasNoGuests` flipped —
`sameIdHash`, `sameName`, `sameRole` ALL HELD.

★★ THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT, because the falsifier alone cannot settle it (widening empties the raw channel
too): a 2×2 placing a THROWING value in the safe stamp only / the raw stamp only / neither, run AT HEAD's
UNWIDENED predicate. RESULT — **SYMMETRIC**: neither channel is forced by resolution (`spine`) or by the
gather (`gathered`); BOTH abort identically under a full `deepSeq` of the output member (`fullMember`).
**THE PARTITION BUYS NOTHING.** Positive controls named inline: `clean.fullMember = true` proves the predicate
can return true; `rawOnly.live = false` and `safeOnly.live = false` prove the poison is live and reachable
through the ctx entity on both arms.
★ AND A SELF-CAUGHT INSTRUMENT ERROR, reported because it produced a false green on the first pass:
`deepUnionStamps` lets `b` win at a non-attrs leaf, so the clean raw overlay SILENTLY CLOBBERED the
safe-channel poison. Fixed by removing the clobbering entry. A sound predicate proving a different
proposition, caught by the author.

★ THE ONE REAL DEPENDENCE, AND IT IS NOT CORRECTNESS: `deepUnionStamps`' cheapness argument rests on THE TWO
TREES' LEAF SETS BEING DISJOINT, which `excludedType` guarantees BY CONSTRUCTION. So the predicate is
load-bearing FOR THE MECHANISM #70 BUILT AROUND IT, not for any property of the record. Delete the predicate
and the dual channel goes with it.

★★ Q3 — WHAT v1 DID, AND IT IS THIS EPIC'S CHARTERING PREMISE INSTANTIATED. v1 **HAD** the deepSeq the comment
names — `denful/den` @ 99cc0c5a `nix/lib/aspects/fx/pipeline.nix:99-106`: "Fields wrapped as thunks (`_: value`)
survive builtins.deepSeq — the trampoline deepSeqs state at each step, but deepSeq on a function forces the
closure, not its application", with `:171` `scopeContexts = _: { };`. ⇒ v1 SOLVED IT WITH A LAZINESS BARRIER,
AND ITS ENTITY RECORD IS COMPLETE — `raw` fields and all (`nix/lib/entities/host.nix:70` `aspect` = raw, `:81`
`instantiate` = raw).
★ SO THE COMMENT IS A **TRANSPOSED INHERITANCE**: v1's constraint was on the STATE ACCUMULATOR and was solved
by THUNKING; den-hoag re-expressed it as a constraint on the RECORD and solved it by DELETION. den-hoag has no
trampoline and no state accumulator, so THE CONSTRAINT HAS NO REFERENT. Same shape as the `__`-keys
state-hack: a v1 mechanism's rationale surviving into a system that does not have the mechanism.

CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD AND TO MY BRIEF: the sentence is at NINE source/test sites plus FOUR ledger rows, not
four — and `lib/compat/flake-module.nix:298-299` WRAPS A LINE, so single-line greps miss it. ★ AND THE AUDIT'S
deepSeq CENSUS WAS INCOMPLETE: `lib/compat/parity/oracle.nix:504` has a real `builtins.deepSeq` over
`denOn.output.systems.<cls>.<id>` in shipped `lib/` — a class-share parity oracle, not the resolution path, so
not the hazard the comment names, but the census as stated was not total.
REPLACEMENT JUSTIFICATION: ONE canonical block at the definition site (registry.nix:222-233), every other site
reduced to "see registry.nix `excludedType`". It must say (1) the predicate partitions TRANSPORT, not
membership; (2) the invariant it actually buys is DISJOINT LEAF SETS, which is what makes `deepUnionStamps` a
group-walk that never forces a leaf — name that as the load-bearing property; (3) ★ KILL THE deepSeq CLAIM AND
SAY WHY IT IS DEAD, citing v1's thunking answer, or the next reader re-derives it from the same comment.
★ AND IF THE EXCLUSION IS REMOVED, FOUR OF THE SIX PINS MUST BE REWRITTEN TO ASSERT DISJOINTNESS RATHER THAN
ABSENCE — otherwise the pins re-encode the dead reason.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated by the investigator: no drvPath on the real corpus (both arms die at an
unrelated `attribute 'id_hash' missing` at collections.nix:205:32, with 249-line traces BYTE-IDENTICAL modulo
the den narHash). ★ The ship gate is NEAR-VACUOUS here — its host declares NO `raw`-typed value at all, so
widening literally cannot change its stamp; its green is a spine result. ★ `deferredModule`/`anything` WERE
NEVER EXERCISED — all witnesses were `types.raw`/`listOf raw`, and an `anything`-typed value entering the safe
stamp CHANGES THE NIXPKGS MERGE (it deep-recurses to pick a merge function), a genuinely different failure
surface. If any part of this is still load-bearing, that is where to look.

title: [kernel] the policy probe is UNCONDITIONAL — a fully-declared policy is still fired against the sentinel ctx, and can be broken by it
description:
MEASURED — THE POLICY PROBE IS UNCONDITIONAL. A POLICY THAT FULLY DECLARES ITS METADATA IS STILL FIRED AGAINST
THE FABRICATED SENTINEL CTX.

`lib/concern-policies.nix`: `probeActs` binds at :345 and `expanded = probeActs == [ ]` FORCES at :358, BEFORE
every branch of `baseRules`. So declaring `__produces` — or `__firesAtKinds`, or any of the metadata `mkRules`
reads off the value at :340-357 — DOES NOT BUY YOU OUT OF THE PROBE. The execution happens regardless of the
declaration it was meant to substitute for.

★ WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN A WASTED EVALUATION: the probe's own header records its honest limit — "tryEval
cannot catch a non-recoverable eval error … a body that field-accesses or iterates a REQUIRED sentinel coord
bare still fails the probe HARD." So a fully-declared policy can still be BROKEN BY THE PROBE, on a ctx the
author never intended it to see, for information the author already supplied.
AND THE SWALLOW MAKES IT SILENT: a caught throw is "treated IDENTICALLY to an empty probe" (same header), so
`expanded` carries THREE meanings at :358 — value-conditional, threw-and-was-swallowed, genuinely-empty.

⇒ THIS IS THE SHAPE THE SURFACE AUDIT NAMED: MISSING INFORMATION RECOVERED BY EXECUTION WHERE IT SHOULD HAVE
BEEN CARRIED BY DECLARATION — and here the information is NOT missing. It was declared and then ignored.
★ NOTE THE CHEAP INTERIM: gating the probe on the absence of declared metadata is a strictly smaller change
than P1 and would remove the hard-failure risk for every already-declared policy. It does NOT fix the
three-meaning ambiguity for undeclared ones, and it must NOT be mistaken for P1 — under P1 the probe
disappears entirely rather than becoming conditional. Recorded as an option, not a recommendation.

PROVENANCE: structural surface audit, 2026-07-28, source-read. NOT execution-measured — no eval was run, and
the firing count for a fully-declared policy has not been observed directly.
close_reason: EXPIRED — fixed by e6c8edc ('a policy declares what it emits, and the kernel checks it'), whose own message states 'the probe, its sentinel, the three-way expansion fan, strip, and four kernel options all dissolve'. Verified at HEAD 6f30460: lib/concern-policies.nix is 282 lines, so EVERY line this bead cites (:345 probeActs, :358 expanded, :340-357 mkRules metadata) is PAST EOF. grep -n 'probeActs|sentinel|deepSeq' lib/concern-policies.nix returns ONE hit, :214, reading verbatim 'ONE policy compiles to ONE rule. No probe, no sentinel, no fabricated context, no per-stratum fan'. The file now denies the construct by name.

title: [gen] design hand-rolls transpose/reachability that gen-graph already provides and den-hoag already calls — and default.nix:2067's comment forbids exactly this
description:
★ MEASURED — FOURTH BUILD-WHAT-EXISTS INSTANCE, AND THE FIRST WHERE AN IN-TREE COMMENT PROHIBITS THE
CONSTRUCTION BY NAME AT A SITE ALREADY DOING THE SAME JOB.

THE DESIGN (specs/2026-07-28-bucket-to-edge-design.md §9) asserts "Substrate: none" and its §11 R1 argues zero
gen-substrate blast radius. NO REUSE SCAN WAS PERFORMED AT ANY GRANULARITY.

MEASURED AT HEAD:
  gen-graph IS ALREADY A den-hoag INPUT — flake.nix:11 `gen-graph.url = "github:sini/gen-graph";`,
  bound at lib/default.nix:42 `graph = inputs.gen-graph.lib;`.
  It ships EXACTLY the primitives the design's E2/E3/E7 hand-roll (gen-graph/README.md:117-124, 250-262):
  `reachableFrom` (C-level BFS via builtins.genericClosure), `canReach`, `selfReachable`, `cycles`,
  `transpose`, `condensation` ({ reps; bottomUp; members; sccs; sccOf; condEdges } — the SCC semantics
  den-hoag-4kh.12 reasoned in).
★ AND den-hoag ALREADY CALLS `transpose` FOR PRECISELY THE PREIMAGE JOB, at lib/default.nix:2067, whose own
comment reads:
    "THE INVERSE EDGES via gen-graph.transpose (§9) … a per-kind genGraphLib.transpose (Mokhov 2017 §4.3),
     NOT A HAND-ROLLED FROM/TO SWAP."
  THE DESIGN'S E3 IS A HAND-ROLLED FROM/TO SWAP.

⇒ THE TREE CONTAINS A COMMENT FORBIDDING THE EXACT CONSTRUCTION THE DESIGN PROPOSES, AT A SITE PERFORMING
THE SAME OPERATION, AND THE DESIGN NEITHER CITES NOR CONTRADICTS IT.

★ THIS IS NOT MERELY DUPLICATION — IT IS THE DESIGN'S PERFORMANCE DEFECT. The gate measured the hand-rolled
closure at Θ(K²·b^h·R), understated by 10-13× against the design's own bound, and established that the
exponential lives ENTIRELY in unmemoised `nf` re-exploration rather than in content replication. gen-graph's
`reachableFrom` and `condensation` MEMOISE THE CLOSURE. So routing through the existing library discharges
the performance defect BY CONSTRUCTION, where the design's own remedy (obligation O4) was measured to have
ZERO EFFECT — 884→884, 11360→11360.

WHY THE PREVENTIVE INSTRUMENT DID NOT FIRE: the reuse-scan discipline points at the capability map
(reference_gen_lib_capability_map). That map was separately measured WRONG — it called gen-product's
`latticeGraph` "genuinely absent" on the very day it was committed. A scan against it would not have been
trusted anyway. THE CHEAPER AND SOUNDER CHECK IS THE ONE THAT WAS SKIPPED: read `flake.nix`'s inputs and grep
the tree for existing calls. den-hoag's own `flake.nix` names gen-graph, and `lib/default.nix` already binds
and uses it.
⇒ STANDING RULE THIS EARNS: BEFORE HAND-ROLLING A GRAPH, SET OR FOLD PRIMITIVE, GREP THE REPO FOR AN EXISTING
CALL TO THE SAME OPERATION. The inputs list is authoritative and local; a capability map is neither.

PROVENANCE: bucket-to-seed-query gate, 2026-07-28. Verified by reading flake.nix, lib/default.nix:2067,
gen-graph/README.md, and by measuring the hand-rolled closure's invocation count.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S BODY — A CITATION OF MINE IS WRONG AND WOULD PROPAGATE.
I wrote 'bound at lib/default.nix:42 `graph = inputs.gen-graph.lib;`'. THAT IS `flake.nix:42`. `lib/default.nix` RECEIVES `graph` as a FUNCTION ARGUMENT (its arg set, lines 1-21) and does not bind the input at all. Verified by the bucket-r2 agent reading at an explicit rev.
The bead's SUBSTANCE is unaffected — gen-graph IS an input, IS bound, and IS already called for the preimage job at lib/default.nix:2067 under the comment forbidding a hand-rolled from/to swap. Only the binding site is misattributed.

★★ AND THE FIX IS NOT THE MECHANICAL SWAP THIS BEAD IMPLIES. Two defects that 'just use gen-graph' WOULD HAVE INTRODUCED SILENTLY, both found by reading gen-graph's SOURCE at the pinned rev 231b319 rather than its README:

(A) THE ACYCLICITY GUARD STOPS BEING AUTOMATIC. The hand-rolled formulation threaded `seen`, which made the cycle abort SELF-ENFORCING — the recursion could not step past a cycle. gen-graph's rest-position formulation HAS NO RECURSION and ANSWERS A CYCLIC RELATION SILENTLY. MEASURED: on `A->B, B->A` over Ch=[A B C Z] it returns ["C"] for C where the current code THROWS. ⇒ Adopting gen-graph REQUIRES adding an explicit forced guard that the hand-rolled version got for free. Had the swap been done mechanically, THE CYCLE ABORT WOULD HAVE QUIETLY DISAPPEARED — a silent loss of a safety property, in a change whose whole justification is correctness.
(B) `condensation` IS NOT TOTAL ON THIS DOMAIN. It is the primitive den-hoag-4kh.12's SCC theory points at and that I named in the brief. With `nodes = Ch` plus an act naming an UNREGISTERED channel it fails `attribute 'X' missing` at gen-graph lib/global.nix:165 — ★ AND THAT ERROR ESCAPES `builtins.tryEval`, so it cannot even be contained. `transpose`/`cycles`/`reachableFrom` all answer on the same input byte-identically to the retired formulation; only `condensation` is partial. Recorded in the spec so the SCC option is not re-proposed as free.

★ THIS IS THE C7-a FAILURE MODE IN ITS OTHER DIRECTION, and worth stating as a standing lesson: 'the library already exists' establishes that you should NOT hand-roll; it does NOT establish that the library's surface has your semantics. RIGHT LIBRARY, WRONG SURFACE IS INVISIBLE TO REVIEW. `reachableFrom` EXCLUDES startId (`filter (id: id != startId)`) — irreflexive — so the rest-position formulation must add `d == c` back explicitly; assuming reflexivity would have silently dropped every rest position's own content.
VERIFIED PROPERLY, three layers: source read at the pinned rev (which the agent confirmed the local clone actually IS, not a drifted one); the irreflexivity trap found by reading; and an EXECUTED equivalence probe over 9 relation shapes (empty/chain/diamond/multicast/forest/deep/branchy/converge/partial-depth) with a POSITIVE CONTROL — a variant dropping the rest-position guard DISAGREES on 8 of 9, agreeing only on `empty` where the guard is vacuous, so the equality is not vacuous.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: E1's identity-drop MUST precede graph construction — `cycles` reports [] after the filter and ["A"] before.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ DISCHARGED IN THE DESIGN — closing. The bucket-to-seed-query spec (abac0e0) now BINDS gen-graph rather than hand-rolling: 23 references to `reachableFrom`/`graph.transpose`/`graph.cycles` in the executable core and its prose, and §9.1/§11 R6 name this defect explicitly and cite this bead. The surviving 'hand-rolled' mentions are the HISTORICAL RECORD — the rejected first-revision E3, and the `lib/default.nix:2067` comment that forbade it — kept deliberately so the rejected construction leaves a trace.
POSITIVE CONTROL on the predicate: `gen-graph` matches 18 times in the same run, so the instrument finds the term and the 23 primitive hits are real.

★ AND THE ADOPTION WAS NOT THE MECHANICAL SWAP THIS BEAD IMPLIED — that finding survives the close and is the more valuable half. Verified against gen-graph's SOURCE at the pinned rev: `reachableFrom` EXCLUDES the start node, so the caller must re-add it or every rest position silently loses its own content; the library's rest-position formulation HAS NO RECURSION, so the cycle abort the hand-rolled `seen`-thread enforced FOR FREE would have vanished silently — measured, it returns an answer where the old code throws; and `condensation` is PARTIAL on this domain, failing with an error that ESCAPES `tryEval`. All three are recorded in the spec so the SCC option is not re-proposed as free.
⇒ STANDING LESSON, recorded in memory as reuse-scan rule 8: 'the library exists' establishes you should NOT hand-roll; it does NOT establish that the library's surface has your semantics. RIGHT LIBRARY, WRONG SURFACE IS INVISIBLE TO REVIEW — the diff reads as a simplification and the wrong answer is silent.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the design is UNIMPLEMENTED. This bead was about the DESIGN hand-rolling primitives, and that is fixed. The tree's `applyInjectReroute` is the construct being RETIRED and is tracked by den-hoag-4kh.16 itself. Removing the block so 4kh.16's critical path is not held by a satisfied blocker.

title: [meta] the bead graph has NO remote — bd sync is pull-first and cannot bootstrap; git carries issue rows but NOT the comment/reasoning layer
description:
MEASURED — THE BEAD GRAPH HAS NEVER BEEN SYNCED TO THE REMOTE, AND `bd sync` CANNOT PERFORM THE FIRST SYNC.

  `git ls-remote origin 'refs/dolt/*'` -> EMPTY. No dolt refs exist on the remote.
  `bd sync` -> "sync failed: pull: fetch from origin/main: Error 1105: fetch failed: no branches found in
  remote 'origin'".
  `bd --help` exposes `sync` (pull -> check -> repair -> push, the federation loop), `export`, `import`,
  `init` — there is NO standalone push. The sync loop is PULL-FIRST and assumes the remote already carries
  branches, so it cannot bootstrap an empty remote.

★ WHAT IS AND IS NOT AT RISK — the distinction matters and is smaller than it first looks:
  `.beads/beads.jsonl` IS committed to git and IS pushed (verified: the export was committed at 6fc4ada and
  main is pushed to c0aa7be..a40cc96). So ISSUE ROWS reach the remote through git.
  ★ BUT THE EXPORT CARRIES NO COMMENTS — 94 rows at last count, all `_type: "issue"`, zero comment rows
  (see den-hoag-bgb). And in this project the COMMENTS ARE WHERE THE REASONING LIVES: audit results, the
  owner comment on den-hoag-9xo that resets the exit condition, every correction recorded this session.
  ⇒ THE DURABILITY GAP IS EXACTLY THE TRIAGE LAYER. Issue titles and bodies survive a machine loss; the
  reasoning attached to them does not.

This sharpens den-hoag-bgb rather than restating it. bgb was demoted to a UX question about the viewer once
the owner clarified that the jsonl is a viewer export and not the source of truth — CORRECT, and this bead
does not reopen that. The point here is different: the SOURCE OF TRUTH (the local Dolt DB) HAS NO REMOTE AT
