· `bridge.nix` -- "zero kind literals": THE LINE BENEATH CONTAINS TWO (E5)
· `compile.nix` -- claims R9 aborts an unresolvable ref: THE STRING ARM NEVER REACHES R9 (A4)
· `staged-resolution.nix` -- "the same `__`-key strip as attr 1": THE LISTS DIFFER (N6)
★ X3 -- MEASURED: COMMENT DENSITY IS ~3x THE ECOSYSTEM NORM. den-hoag kernel 40%, compat
42%; EVERY gen library 13-19%; the demos 7-17%. ⇒ 5,474 LINES OF PROSE IN THE KERNEL THAT
MUST STAY TRUE, AND X2 SHOWS IT IS ALREADY DRIFTING.
★★ NOT "WRITE FEWER COMMENTS" -- the audit is explicit that THE COMMENTS WERE REPEATEDLY THE
BEST EVIDENCE AVAILABLE, and SEVERAL FINDINGS CAME FROM A FILE CONTRADICTING ITSELF. But it
is A MAINTENANCE SURFACE AND SHOULD BE COUNTED AS ONE.
(X4 was a naming correction only: `edge.derive` is not an export name -- the module is
`derive.nix` and its export is `edgesFor`, which HAS a call site.)

title: [G29] turn the clean controls into a stated ecosystem standard — gen-graph is the library the others should look like, and gen-merge __pureModule is the __ key done right
description:
[G29] MEASURED. THE CLEAN CONTROLS, STATED AS FINDINGS -- ★ THESE ARE WHAT MAKE THE REST OF
THE GEN-SIDE FINDINGS CREDIBLE, and they name the target shape.
★ GEN-GRAPH IS CLEAN ON ALL FIVE SHAPES: zero invented `__` keys, formals `{ prelude }`
ONLY, uses `builtins.groupBy` RATHER THAN THE PRELUDE'S QUADRATIC SHADOW, no
prescribed-but-unimplemented convention. ⇒ ★★ IT IS THE LIBRARY THE OTHERS SHOULD LOOK LIKE.
★ gen-merge's `__pureModule` IS A REAL CONTRACT -- WRITTEN, READ by `classifyModule`, with
the classification DOCUMENTED. THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE TO G4: a `__` key with a writer, a
reader and a stated contract.
★ ZERO-`__` ROSTER: gen-class, gen-flake, gen-graph, gen-prelude (4 of 14).
⇒ ACTION: turn these into a STATED ECOSYSTEM STANDARD rather than an observation, so the
gen-side beads have a target to converge on instead of each proposing its own.
★ CAVEAT THE AUDIT STATES: gen-graph's and gen-merge's MODULE BODIES WERE NOT READ. The
gen-graph "clean" verdict rests on a `__`-key census, its formals, its `builtins.groupBy`
usage and a citation grep -- NOT on reading its ten modules. GEN-MERGE IS THE LARGER
UNSWEPT RISK OF THE TWO. Do not cite either as audited.

title: [G23+G26+G27] toposort cited to Kahn ships cubic, gen-edge kind carries a permanent byte-compat tail at three sites, and factor.nix bare path silently loses validation
description:
[G23+G26+G27] ARGUED. THREE gen-side items with stated resolutions.
★ G23: `toposort` IS CITED TO KAHN 1962 AND SHIPS CUBIC. `gen-edge/lib/toposort.nix` cites
Kahn's algorithm -- O(V+E) via a DECREMENTING INDEGREE ARRAY and a READY QUEUE. What ships
REBUILDS THE ENTIRE INDEGREE VECTOR AND RE-SORTS THE ENTIRE READY SET ON EVERY PICK:
`filter` O(n) + `sort` O(n log n) + `genList` over n each doing an O(n) `elem` scan, PER
STEP, OVER n STEPS = O(n^3). ★ The only complexity note in the file is about `predsOf`
construction, NOT THE LOOP. MITIGATING: on den-hoag this sits on the ORACLE path, not the
build path (see G12) -- ★ BUT THAT IS AN ACCIDENT, and n grows with fleet demand-edge count.
RESOLUTION: keep `predsOf`, add a `succsOf`, carry a ready set and decrement only the pick's
successors -> O(V+E+n log n), tie-break intact, OUTPUT BYTE-IDENTICAL. Minor, same file: the
`!(state.done ? ...)` guard is DEAD, since `remaining'` already removes the pick.
★ G26: AN ADDITIVE FIELD CARRYING A PERMANENT BYTE-COMPAT TAIL. gen-edge's `kind` was added
later and THREE SITES NOW CARRY A CONDITIONAL FOREVER so un-labeled edges render as though
the field never existed; one states the reason: "so existing goldens stay byte-identical".
★ THE PATCH-AFTER-BUILD SHAPE WITH AN INVARIANT THREE SITES MUST MAINTAIN IN STEP.
RESOLUTION: REGENERATING THE GOLDENS ONCE RETIRES ALL THREE CONDITIONALS.
★ G27: `factor.nix`'s BARE-GRAPH PATH IS A WEAKER DEFAULT WITH NOTHING STEERING. It
discriminates on FIELD PRESENCE (`spec ? graph`); the bare path sets `key = id: id;
entryOf = id: id;` and the header ADMITS "not-a-node detection is vacuous on this path".
⇒ A CALLER WHO FORGETS THE WRAPPER SILENTLY LOSES `notANode` VALIDATION. THE D3 SHAPE AGAIN.
RESOLUTION: REQUIRE THE SPEC FORM; the bare form becomes an EXPLICIT `bareFactor` OPT-OUT.

title: [G28+G18] six primitives duplicated across libraries including one twice in a single file — and the flagship gen-aspects demo models the wrong layering
description:
[G28+G18] MEASURED. CROSS-LIBRARY DUPLICATION OF PRIMITIVES THAT BELONG IN GEN-PRELUDE:
  firstDuplicate          3 copies -- gen-product/product.nix, chain.nix (★ TWICE IN ONE
                          LIBRARY), den-hoag/linearization.nix
  lexicographic int-list  2 -- gen-product/chain.nix, gen-demand/resolve.nix
  first-occurrence dedup  ★ 4 -- gen-edge/core.nix, gen-product/membership.nix,
                          gen-scope/resolve.nix (INLINED, and DEFENSIBLE there since `eq`
                          is a caller-supplied comparator so no attrset key is available),
                          vs the correct gen-prelude one
  indexOf                 gen-product/chain.nix RE-HAND-ROLLED, ★ WHILE GEN-PRELUDE'S OWN
                          COMMENT SAYS "so consumers adopt by `inherit (prelude) indexOf`"
                          AND GEN-PRODUCT TAKES `prelude`
  showSubset              2 IDENTICAL, gen-product/show.nix and chain.nix, SAME LIBRARY
  path writer/reader      gen-edge/core.nix + den-hoag/nest.nix (see G10+G11)
★ G18 -- AND THE FLAGSHIP DEMO MODELS THE WRONG LAYERING: gen-aspects'
`examples/demo/modules/composition.nix` HAND-ROLLS `flattenAttrs`/`unflattenAttrs`, which
ARE `record.flattenAttrs`/`record.unflattenAttrs` IN GEN-ALGEBRA, and `flattenSchema`, which
`gen-settings.mkSchema` OWNS. It calls gen-algebra directly BECAUSE IT DOES NOT DEPEND ON
GEN-SETTINGS. ⇒ Worth fixing SO THE FLAGSHIP DEMO MODELS THE INTENDED LAYERING -- it is what
a new consumer reads first.

title: [G13+G14+G19] the three libraries built for den-hoag have no second consumer, no REFERENCE.md, and one primitive motivated by a use case its only consumer solves another way
description:
[G13+G14+G19] ARGUED/MEASURED. THE THREE LIBRARIES BUILT FOR DEN-HOAG HAVE NO SECOND
CONSUMER, AND IT SHOWS.
★ G19, MEASURED: NEITHER GEN EXAMPLE USES gen-edge, gen-product OR gen-demand. den-hoag is
the SOLE CONSUMER of all three. All three carry a component spec dated 2026-07-05 derived
from ONE roadmap document naming den-hoag as the motivating consumer. ★ AND ALL THREE ARE
THE ONES WITH NO `REFERENCE.md` IN THE PAPERS ARCHIVE (`gen-specs/` has directories for
gen-scope, gen-schema, gen-merge, gen-resolve, gen-link -- AND NONE FOR THESE).
★ G13 IS WHAT THAT PRODUCES: gen-product's `quotient` has a STALE MOTIVATION AND ZERO
CONSUMERS. Its header claims class-share as "its motivating instantiation" AND CI SHIPS
THAT EXACT LINE -- but den-hoag implements class-share THROUGH GEN-CLASS and consumes the
MEMBER LIST, while `quotient` returns an ACCESSOR GRAPH whose value-add is COLLAPSED
ADJACENCY DEN-HOAG NEVER QUERIES. WRONG SHAPE. ⇒ A PRIMITIVE MOTIVATED BY A USE CASE ITS
ONLY CONSUMER SOLVES ANOTHER WAY.
★ G14: gen-product's `validateDimOrder` / `firstDuplicate` are UNEXPORTED, and
den-hoag's `lib/linearization.nix` RE-IMPLEMENTS `chain.nix` LINE-FOR-LINE -- WITH A
DOCUMENTED REASON (a den-named error at declaration time, before the list crosses into
gen-product). RESOLUTION: EXPORT `validateDimOrder` TAKING A CALLER-SUPPLIED ERROR
CONSTRUCTOR. ~20 of den-hoag's 44 code lines recoverable.
⇒ THREE ACTIONS: write the missing REFERENCE.md set; decide `quotient`'s fate (retire or
re-motivate); export `validateDimOrder`.

title: [G15+G25] gen-demand surface stops short and demand.adapters is permanently empty, failing with a bare attribute-missing and no library name
description:
[G15+G25] ARGUED/MEASURED. gen-demand's SURFACE STOPS SHORT, AND ITS ADAPTER FAILS SILENTLY.
★ G15: `wiringFor` / `spliceWiring` ARE UNREACHED, so a consumer reading
`config.<idHash>.wiring` gets RAW PER-KIND LISTS WITH NO GLOBAL SCHEDULE ORDER AND NO
SPLICE. And `demand.folds` (FIVE STOCK FOLDS) IS NOT RE-EXPORTED ON THE DEN SURFACE, so a
user writing `den.demandKinds.<k>.fold` HAND-WRITES WHAT GEN-DEMAND SHIPS.
★ BOTH ARE NON-USE, NOT HAND-ROLL -- the cascade discipline GENUINELY LIVES IN THE LIBRARY.
Do not file this as a duplication finding.
★★ G25, MEASURED: `demand.adapters` IS PERMANENTLY EMPTY AND FAILS SILENTLY.
`gen-demand/lib/default.nix` returns `{ }` when `select == null`, and `gen-demand/flake.nix`
declares ONLY gen-prelude and gen-graph -- ★ NO GEN-SELECT. The hub passes the flake lib
through unchanged, so `demand.adapters == { }` FOR EVERY CONSUMER, PERMANENTLY. Calling
`demand.adapters.select.filterDemands` yields a BARE `attribute 'select' missing` WITH NO
LIBRARY NAME.
★ COMPARE gen-edge GETTING THIS RIGHT FOR THE SAME SITUATION: a NAMED THROW identifying the
missing input.
RESOLUTION: `adapters.select` PRESENT-BUT-THROWING when uninjected -- the TOMBSTONE
DISCIPLINE `sel.entityKind` ALREADY USES. Same D3 shape: a weaker path with nothing
steering.

title: [G10+G11] den-hoag imports gen-edge unexported core to reach a non-public renderName, and gen-prelude has no path primitives so the reader twin was hand-rolled
description:
[G10+G11] ARGUED/MEASURED. TWO API-BOUNDARY DEFECTS AROUND gen-edge.
★ G10 -- DEN-HOAG BREACHES GEN-EDGE'S PUBLIC API: `flake.nix` imports
`gen-edge/lib/core.nix` DIRECTLY -- a module gen-edge's OWN DOCS SAY "stays unexported" --
to reach `renderName`, WHICH IS NOT PUBLIC (`edgeSortKey` is). Same import again for the
non-flake path. RESOLUTION: EXPORT `renderName` AND `toNameSpec`; delete the bypass.
(`toNameSpec` is also what A8 needs -- see that bead for why it is not a drop-in.)
★ G11 -- `setAttrByPath` IS IN THE WRONG LIBRARY, AND GEN-PRELUDE HAS NO PATH PRIMITIVES.
gen-edge DELIBERATELY EXPORTS IT ("exposed so consumers call it instead of mirroring a
local twin") -- but it is A PURE PATH PRIMITIVE WITH NO EDGE ALGEBRA IN IT. gen-prelude has
NEITHER A PATH WRITER NOR A READER (verified; positive control -- `groupBy`, `hasPrefix`,
`imap0` all present). ⇒ CONSEQUENCE: DEN-HOAG HAND-ROLLED THE MISSING READER TWIN at
`nest.nix`, WITH ITS OWN COMMENT SAYING WHY.
RESOLUTION: `setAttrByPath` + `getAttrByPath` AS A PAIR IN GEN-PRELUDE; gen-edge consumes
from there. One line of den-hoag disappears with it.

title: [G4+G24] unnamespaced __ keys crossing library boundaries by convention alone — and gen-product ships eight of them as a shadow public API
description:
[G4+G24] MEASURED. UNNAMESPACED `__` KEYS SHARED ACROSS LIBRARY BOUNDARIES BY CONVENTION
ALONE: `__identity` in gen-select AND gen-pipe; `__coords` in gen-select, gen-pipe AND
den-hoag; `__keyRef` in gen-aspects AND gen-link. ★ NONE IS A DECLARED CONTRACT.
★ POSITIVE CONTROL INSIDE THE ECOSYSTEM: gen-class and gen-flake carry ZERO INVENTED `__`
KEYS -- so it is A CHOICE, NOT A CONSTRAINT OF THE LANGUAGE. The NAMESPACED form
(`__genPipeChannel`, `__genSettingsRef`) is the better EXISTING pattern.
★★ G24 -- gen-product SHIPS EIGHT `__` KEYS ON ITS PUBLIC PRODUCT RECORD: `__def`,
`__base`, `__restriction`, `__cell`, `__cells`, `__freeDims`, `__showCoords`,
`__renderEntry`. THESE ARE NOT INTERNAL -- the library's OWN PUBLIC WRAPPERS READ THEM
ACROSS THE MODULE BOUNDARY. ⇒ A PRODUCT GRAPH IS AN ACCESSOR-RECORD WITH A SHADOW API
SMUGGLED UNDER `__`, and the README's claim that "a product IS an accessor-graph (every
gen-graph query works on it unchanged)" HOLDS ONLY BECAUSE GEN-GRAPH IGNORES KEYS IT DOES
NOT KNOW. FIVE OF THE EIGHT ARE ALREADY DUPLICATED on the declared `product` sibling field.
(gen-algebra ships two with 48 uses -- `__entries` and `__order` ARE the representation of
a record, which is a different and defensible case.)
★ THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE THAT DEFINES THE STANDARD: gen-merge's `__pureModule` is A REAL
CONTRACT -- written, READ by `classifyModule`, with the classification DOCUMENTED. A `__`
key with a writer, a reader and a stated contract.

title: [G8+G9] [gen-schema] two contradictory reservation policies, and neither reserved key set is published so consumers hardcode them three ways
description:
[G8+G9] ARGUED. gen-schema HOLDS TWO CONTRADICTORY RESERVATION POLICIES, AND PUBLISHES
NEITHER KEY SET.
★ `_`-prefixed KIND NAMES are excluded SILENTLY; COLLECTION KEYS throw LOUDLY. ONE LIBRARY,
TWO OPPOSITE ANSWERS to "what happens when a user names something reserved."
★ THE LOUD ONE IS DEFENSIBLE: a user writing `den.schema._internal = { ... }` gets NO KIND,
NO REGISTRY AND NO ERROR -- the declaration EVAPORATES. Same failure class as §4.
★★ BUT THE FILTER CANNOT SIMPLY BECOME A THROW -- it is DOING DOUBLE DUTY, legitimately
hiding gen-schema's OWN six introspection options from `_kindNames`. RESOLUTION: SEPARATE
THE TWO JOBS -- exclude the library's own reserved names by an EXPLICIT KNOWN-SET, and
THROW on any OTHER `_`-prefixed user kind.
★ G9 -- AND THE KNOWN-SET SHOULD BE PUBLISHED ANYWAY, because consumers hardcode it. TWO
SEPARATE UNEXPORTED SETS (the audit's own earlier framing CONFLATED them):
· THE SIX SCHEMA-LEVEL INTROSPECTION OPTIONS (`_kindNames`, `_topology`, `_refEdges`,
  `_edges`, `_roots`, `_leaves`) have NO EXPORTED LIST. den-hoag HARDCODES ALL SIX --
  correct today, SILENTLY WRONG THE DAY A SEVENTH IS ADDED -- ★ AND RE-DERIVES THE SAME
  FACT A SECOND WAY by prefix-filter at TWO more sites. THREE SPELLINGS OF ONE CONTRACT
  INSIDE ONE CONSUMER, because the library publishes neither.
· `collectionKeys` / `strippedDefs` are CLOSURE-LOCAL inside `mkSchemaEntryType`'s `merge`
  lambda WITH NO RETURN PATH -- ★ AN ACCIDENT OF BINDING SITE, NOT A BOUNDARY ANYONE DREW.
  That is why `bridge.nix` HARDCODES A NINE-ELEMENT LIST against an `allCollections` whose
  base is THREE plus whatever the caller declares.
RESOLUTION: publish BOTH -- a `_reservedIntrospectionKeys` list and `_collectionKeys` as a
further `_`-prefixed schema-level key, derived from data already in scope. ★ NOT
CORPUS-PIN CONSTRAINED (all three `mkSchemaOption` call sites run den-hoag's own gen-schema).
Closes S7's three spellings as a side effect.

title: [G2+G3+G5] gen-select bakes den-hoag private __entry into a library default and inverts who owns the convention — plus a live __coords collision and gen-scope prescribing twice
description:
[G2+G3+G5] ARGUED/MEASURED. gen-select's DEFAULT HARD-CODES DEN-HOAG'S PRIVATE KEY, and
the natural reading is INVERTED.
`gen-select/lib/adapters/scope.nix`: `entryFor ? (id: (node id).decls.__entry or null),`
with a comment naming den-hoag and asserting that gen-scope reserves the `__` namespace.
★ `__entry` IS MINTED BY DEN-HOAG (`build-roots.nix`, `fleet.nix`); GEN-SCOPE WRITES ONLY
`__edges`. ⇒ A LIBRARY DEFAULT ENCODES A CONSUMER'S CONVENTION, NAMES THAT CONSUMER IN A
COMMENT, AND ASSERTS A NAMESPACE RESERVATION THAT LIVES IN THE WRONG LIBRARY AND IS
ENFORCED IN NEITHER.
★★ `__entry` IS NOT A GEN CONTRACT DEN-HOAG MUST HONOUR; IT IS DEN-HOAG'S CONVENTION THAT
GEN-SELECT BAKED INTO A DEFAULT. (Recorded in the audit's corrections ledger as a claim it
made and inverted.)
RESOLUTION: `entryFor` has NO DEFAULT, or defaults to `id: node id` with the caller
projecting. If the convention is to exist, IT BELONGS IN GEN-SCOPE AS A WRITTEN KEY WITH A
READER -- the same EXTEND as N4.
★ G3 -- A LIVE `__coords` COLLISION: gen-select's product adapter WRITES `__coords` and
THROWS ON ITS ABSENCE; den-hoag INDEPENDENTLY writes `decls.__coords` on cells AND STRIPS
IT IN FOUR PLACES. SAME SPELLING, TWO PRODUCERS, ONE OF WHICH REMOVES IT. ★ WHETHER THEY
ARE THE SAME CONCEPT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED -- establish that before either is touched.
★ G5 -- gen-scope SPECIFIES CONVENTIONS IT DOES NOT IMPLEMENT, TWICE IN ONE LIBRARY: the
`@parent` multi-attachment convention (N4) and this `__` decls namespace. One shape, two
instances.

title: [G1] [gen-settings] hand-rolls a graph library including integer modulo, and does not depend on gen-graph — also a complexity defect
description:
★ ARGUED. gen-settings HAND-ROLLS A GRAPH LIBRARY.
`gen-settings/lib/graph.nix` implements a DFS cycle finder, cycle canonicalisation by
rotation, an adjacency index, and -- ★ INTEGER MODULO: `mod = a: b: a - ((a / b) * b);`.
Declared dependencies are `{ prelude, algebra, bind }` -- ★ NO GEN-GRAPH, which exports
`cycles`, `selfReachable`, `transitiveClosure`, `condensation`, `mkGraph`, `fromRegistry`.
POSITIVE CONTROLS FROM INSIDE THE ECOSYSTEM: gen-link's header states "delegates every
computation to a sibling"; gen-resolve TAKES `graph` AS A FORMAL; and den-hoag itself calls
`graph.cycles`.
★ ALSO A COMPLEXITY DEFECT, not tidiness: FULL DFS PER NODE with list-membership `elem` on
the path -- O(V*E*depth) -- against gen-graph's SINGLE SELF-REACHABILITY PASS.
RESOLUTION: gen-settings takes `graph` as a formal; `refGraph` returns a gen-graph accessor;
`assertAcyclic` calls `graph.cycles` and keeps ONLY the message rendering, which is
genuinely gen-settings'.

title: [G7] [gen-schema] hand-rolls parentMap/childrenMap/roots/leaves/edges — the same computation now exists three times, and the dependency would be legal
description:
★ ARGUED. gen-schema HAND-ROLLS WHAT GEN-GRAPH PROVIDES.
`entry-type.nix` builds `parentMap`, `childrenMap`, `roots`, `leaves`, `edges` BY HAND.
gen-schema DOES NOT DEPEND ON GEN-GRAPH, and ★ `gen-prelude -> gen-graph -> gen-schema` IS
ACYCLIC AND LEGAL (gen-graph needs only gen-prelude).
⇒ THE SAME COMPUTATION THEREFORE EXISTS THREE TIMES: gen-graph, gen-schema, den-hoag.
Pairs with S8 (den-hoag strips gen-schema's answer unread and recomputes a subset) and G1
(gen-settings hand-rolls the same library). ★ THREE LIBRARIES INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVING
GEN-GRAPH IS THE PATTERN, not three separate oversights -- worth one ecosystem ruling
rather than three fixes.

title: [T7] the test guarding strict cannot distinguish a strict throw from a conflicting-option-types throw — an instance of the coarse-assertion class
description:
[T7] ARGUED. THE TEST GUARDING STRICT CANNOT DISTINGUISH WHAT IT TESTS.
`ci/tests/flake-strict.nix` asserts `!(tryEval ...).success`. ★ A CONFLICTING-OPTION-TYPES
THROW SATISFIES THAT IDENTICALLY TO A STRICT-MODE THROW; THE MESSAGE IS NOT PINNED.
The arm that ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES is the DECLARED one, and the comment DOES NOT CREDIT
IT.
★★ THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF THE CLASS ALREADY TRACKED AT den-hoag-9xo.79 (assertions coarser
than their claim), and it should be fixed by that sweep's rule rather than ad hoc:
value-returning guard -> assert the message text; THROWING guard -> paired arms with a
negative control in the same run, because Nix CANNOT recover a throw's text.
The same document also flags the five exclude-family fixtures as a sibling case -- those
were fixed on 2026-07-28; this one was not.

title: [A9] ingest repeats the A1 parent collapse, safe only by evaluation order, with nothing marking it order-sensitive
description:
[A9] ARGUED. `ingest.nix` REPEATS THE A1 COLLAPSE AND IS SAFE ONLY BY EVALUATION ORDER.
`declared = builtins.mapAttrs (_: k: { parent = k.parent or null; }) v1Schema;`
-- harmless ONLY because `desugarLegacy` runs BEFORE it in `compileFull`.
★ NOTHING MARKS IT ORDER-SENSITIVE. A future reordering re-opens A1 at a second site with
no comment, no guard and no test.
⇒ Fix with A1 (same expression shape, same remedy: read the RAW DEFS, omit `parent` when
no def declares it) or, at minimum, state the ordering dependency where it can be seen.

title: [A5] den.attach keys are unvalidated strings — a typo-d row is stated intent landing in the branch written for absence, with the validator present twice in the same file
description:
[A5] ARGUED. `den.attach` KEYS ARE UNVALIDATED STRINGS. Typed `attrsOf (submodule ...)`;
THE ATTR NAME IS NEVER CHECKED AGAINST DECLARED KINDS. A typo yields `parentKind == null`
-> `[ ]` -> NOTHING, NO ERROR.
★ The declaration's OWN COMMENT says "ABSENCE OF A ROW MEANS THE KIND DOES NOT NATIVELY
ATTACH" -- so A TYPO'D ROW IS STATED INTENT LANDING IN THE BRANCH WRITTEN FOR ABSENCE.
That is the §4 class in one sentence.
POSITIVE CONTROL: kind-name validation EXISTS TWICE IN THE SAME FILE. The primitive is
present; this site does not call it.

title: [A6] a user den.productions."resolved-settings" is voided at merge — the only seeded merge in the file without the guard four sibling sites use
description:
[A6] ARGUED. A USER `den.productions."resolved-settings"` IS VOIDED AT MERGE.
`default.nix`: `(ent.config.den.productions or { }) // { "resolved-settings" =
settingsProduction; }`. The validator reserves the `__spawn` SUFFIX and NOT THIS NAME.
★ IT IS THE ONLY SEEDED MERGE IN THE FILE WITHOUT A GUARD -- four other sites establish
the opposite discipline, one stating "the guard is the sole protection (operand order is
not)."
⇒ The house rule exists, is written down, and this site is the exception. Cheap fix;
belongs with C1's derived reserved set if that lands, since it is the same question
(what names may a user occupy) at a different concern.

title: [A7] an undeclared per-instance key is silently dropped — and the mechanism doing it is an invariant E3 wants kept, so they are one design question
description:
[A7] ARGUED. AN UNDECLARED PER-INSTANCE KEY IS SILENTLY DROPPED.
`den.hosts.x86_64-linux.igloo.typo = "x"` produces NO ERROR from ANY of the four
entity-construction paths. The nixpkgs registry absorbs it via freeformType; THE STAMP
PROJECTION WALKS THE DECLARED OPTION SURFACE ONLY (`registry.nix`, leaf branch gated on
`isOption v`), so it NEVER ENTERS `entityFields` -> `instanceConfig` -> the kernel.
★ Per-instance keys sit OUTSIDE compile's surface-totality gate, which is top-level
`den.<key>` ONLY.
★★ SAME MECHANISM AS E3, WHICH IS AN INVARIANT WE WANT: the option-gating is what keeps
freeform-absorbed keys from crossing to the kernel. ⇒ FIXING A7 AND KEEPING E3 ARE THE
SAME DESIGN QUESTION -- the projection must distinguish "absorbed and deliberately not
crossed" from "absorbed because the user misspelled it". Do not fix one by deleting the
other.
Interacts with the always-on strict ruling (§6): under strict, an undeclared per-instance
key should arguably be REJECTED rather than absorbed -- which would close this by
construction. Establish whether strict reaches per-instance keys at all.

title: [S12] probe tree and build tree are different evals — a schema declaration conditional on an unset concern option sees absent in one and empty in the other
description:
[S12] ARGUED, LATENT. PROBE TREE AND BUILD TREE ARE DIFFERENT EVALS.
The probe declares only `options.schema` under a freeform `den`; the build tree adds ~35
CONCERN OPTIONS *WITH DEFAULTS*. ⇒ A user module whose schema declaration is CONDITIONAL
ON AN UNSET CONCERN OPTION sees ABSENT in one and `{ }` in the other.
Corpus-unreachable today. NO GUARD FOUND.
★★ THIS IS NOT A REFACTOR -- IT IS A SEMANTIC CHANGE, AND THE AUDIT IS EXPLICIT THAT IT
MUST NOT RIDE IN THE SAME SPEC AS S3. Consolidating the evals (S11) CHANGES WHICH TREE A
CONDITIONAL DECLARATION SEES. Decide the semantics deliberately: either the probe gains
the concern defaults, or conditional-on-concern schema declarations are refused by name.

title: [S11] discovery is four evaluations of the user module set — three byte-identical probes, one already copy-pasted into another file
description:
[S11] MEASURED. DISCOVERY IS FOUR EVALUATIONS OF THE USER MODULE SET.
`entity.nix` at three points plus `concern-collectors.nix` -- THREE BYTE-IDENTICAL PROBES
differing ONLY in the final `attrNames` read, plus the build tree.
★ THE TELL THAT IT IS NOT A PRIMITIVE: the pattern has ALREADY BEEN COPY-PASTED OUT OF
`entity.nix` INTO ANOTHER FILE.
RESOLUTION -- DEN-HOAG CONSOLIDATION, NO LIBRARY CHANGE. The probes differ only in whether
`options.schema` is mounted, AND MOUNTING IT IS STRICTLY ADDITIVE. ONE `evalModuleTree`,
`let`-bound once, serves all four lists.
★ gen-merge's `warmFrom` path is PUBLIC BUT KEYED ON THE WRONG AXIS (an appended module
tail, not a varying decl tree) -- so this is not a gen gap and should not be filed as one.
CONSTRAINT FROM S1: one call site CANNOT read `ent` (cycle through denAspects ->
aspectsDecl -> entity.build) and must read a probe. The consolidation must preserve that,
so "one eval" means one PROBE eval plus the build tree, not literally one.

title: [S9] the denMeta/_kindNames keyset agreement rests on one boolean gated in two places — a framework kind without a metaAugment entry silently gets no registry
description:
[S9] ARGUED. THE KEYSET AGREEMENT IS HELD BY TWO GATES ON ONE BOOLEAN IN TWO PLACES.
`attrNames ent.meta` differs from `_kindNames` by EXACTLY {collector}, when collectors are
declared -- maintained by `hasCollectors` consumed at two sites INDEPENDENTLY.
★ THE FAILURE MODE: a future FRAMEWORK KIND declared through a concern module WITHOUT a
matching `metaAugment` entry lands in the build tree's `_kindNames` and NOT in `denMeta`
-- and registries are minted PER `denMeta` KEY, so it SILENTLY GETS A SCHEMA ENTRY AND NO
REGISTRY.
⇒ Dissolves under S10 (framework kinds as ordinary declarations) -- that ruling deletes
`metaAugment`, the `collector` reserved-name branch and this keyset divergence TOGETHER.
Filed separately because if S10 is not taken, this needs its own guard.

title: [S7] kinds is defined by a hardcoded blacklist while the positive list sits eleven lines above — three spellings of one contract
description:
[S7] ARGUED. `kinds` is defined BY BLACKLIST while the POSITIVE LIST SITS ELEVEN LINES
ABOVE. `entity.nix` does `removeAttrs tree.config.den.schema [ "_kindNames" "_topology"
"_refEdges" "_edges" "_roots" "_leaves" ]` while `sch._kindNames` is used in the same file.
★ It RE-IMPLEMENTS THE `_`-PREFIX FILTER GEN-SCHEMA ALREADY RAN, as a HARDCODED SIX-NAME
LIST -- and `compat/schema-util.nix` re-implements it A THIRD TIME as a substring test.
⇒ Three spellings of one contract, two of them in den-hoag. Fix depends on G9 (gen-schema
publishes no list of its own introspection keys, so consumers hardcode them) -- once the
library publishes the set, all three sites collapse to reading it.

title: [S8] gen-schema computes the kind-level graph and den-hoag strips it unread, then recomputes a subset with the quadratic unique
description:
[S8] MEASURED. THE SUBSTRATE'S KIND-LEVEL GRAPH IS DELETED UNREAD.
gen-schema computes `edges = parentEdges ++ map (e: e // { type = "ref"; }) refEdges`,
described in its own source as "Unified edge view: parent (§ Neron 2015 P) + ref
(§ Neron 2015 I) edges". `_edges`, `_refEdges` and `_leaves` have ZERO READERS outside the
removal list.
★ Replaced by LIST ARITHMETIC OVER THE SIDECAR COPY, USING `prelude.unique` -- WHICH IS
QUADRATIC (see G20). So the substrate ships the answer, den-hoag deletes it, then
recomputes a subset of it by the slowest available primitive.
⇒ Sequence with S1/S3: the derived lists stop being derived once the substrate's own graph
is read instead of stripped.

title: [S3] three derived kind lists are proved identities — plus two traps a spec must carry as do-not-do lines (rootScopeKinds, dimKinds)
description:
[S3] ARGUED, WITH PROOFS. Three of ten derived lists are PROVED IDENTITIES:
· `parentKinds` = allKinds \ `_leaves`  -- proved from `childrenMap`'s construction
· `candidateKinds` = `_leaves` \ `_roots`
· `nonCandidateKinds` = `parentKinds` union `_roots`
`_roots` is ALREADY PLUMBED AND UNUSED at `entity.nix`; `_leaves` needs one line.
★★ S4 -- A TRAP WITH A DO-NOT-DO LINE THE SPEC MUST CARRY: `rootScopeKinds` is
`allKinds \ cellKinds` -- "everything that is not a cell", INCLUDING CHAIN-MIDDLE KINDS
WITH BOTH PARENT AND CHILDREN. `_roots` is only the PARENTLESS kinds. On the corpus
topology `_roots` is approximately {flake} while `rootScopeKinds` is EVERY KIND EXCEPT
`user`. ⇒ SUBSTITUTING `_roots` FOR `rootScopeKinds` DELETES MOST OF THE FLEET'S ROOT
SCOPE NODES. Write this as an explicit do-not-do in any spec.
★ S6 -- ANOTHER TRAP ON THE SAME CHAIN: `dimKinds` gaining an EMPTY-REGISTRY kind ZEROES
THE PRODUCT (silent empty fleet). `default.nix` states it in its own comment. Any change
touching that chain needs this as an EXPLICIT ASSERTION, not a comment.
⇒ THE CORRESPONDENCE PROOF MUST LAND STEP BY STEP, and S5's fixture must exist BEFORE
`candidateKinds` moves.

title: [N5] [gen-scope] EXTEND: no single-node constructor, so every NTA spawn body re-derives the node shape by convention
description:
[N5] ARGUED. NO SINGLE-NODE CONSTRUCTOR for NTA spawn bodies.
Cells are minted inside a `resolve.nta` spawn, and gen-scope exports NO WAY TO MAKE ONE
NODE -- `buildNodes` is whole-graph only. ⇒ EVERY NTA BODY IN EVERY CONSUMER re-derives
the four-field shape by convention. den-hoag's two constructors agree ONLY BECAUSE
SOMEONE KEEPS THEM IN SYNC (which is N3's three-shapes drift, from the other side).
RESOLUTION -- EXTEND gen-scope: export a single-node constructor, or admit `buildNodes`
on a one-vertex graph.

title: [N6] four hand-maintained strip-lists for __edges — three distinct sets, against a key den-hoag never writes and gen-scope never reads
description:
[N6] MEASURED. FOUR NON-IDENTICAL STRIP-LISTS for a key NO REACHABLE PATH WRITES.
`__edges` is stripped at staged-resolution, collections, resolved-settings and structural
-- THREE DISTINCT SETS, hand-maintained. It is written only by `gen-scope.buildNodes`,
WHICH DEN-HOAG NEVER CALLS (0 hits; positive control found seven other `scope.*` entry
points in use, so the predicate was live).
★ AND THE CONVENTION IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS (§11): gen-scope HAS NO READER FOR IT
EITHER -- control confirmed gen-scope never reads `decls.<anything>` internally. So this
is a convention with a WRITER, NO READER, AND FOUR CONSUMERS GUARDING AGAINST IT.
⇒ Dissolves when N1 lands (den-hoag starts calling `buildNodes`, so the key becomes real
and one strip-list becomes correct) OR the convention is retired in gen-scope. Decide
which; do not leave four hand-maintained lists against a key nobody writes.
Also listed at X2 as an in-tree comment measured false ("the same `__`-key strip as attr 1"
-- the lists differ).

title: [N3] three node shapes, not two — every difference absorbed by or-defaulting at each reader, so the invariant is carried by discipline
description:
[N3] MEASURED. THREE node shapes, and an in-tree comment claiming two.
root-as-minted, root-as-DECORATED, and cell. They differ in FIVE decls keys and one
count (a cell carries TWO kind-keyed entries, a root ONE).
★ EVERY DIFFERENCE IS ABSORBED BY `or`-DEFAULTING AT EACH CROSSING READER, so it NEVER
SURFACES AS AN ERROR -- the invariant is carried by DISCIPLINE.
`build-roots.nix` asserts "two -- and only two -- node constructors": TRUE of
CONSTRUCTORS, FALSE of SHAPES, because N2's decorator makes B != A.
⇒ Largely dissolves with N2 (which removes the decorated shape) plus N4/N5 (which give
gen-scope the constructors). Filed separately because the COMMENT is measured false and
must be corrected either way -- see X2, which lists it among five false comments.

title: [D7a] gen-select is 4 of 18 exports used and the unused half is exactly the scope-position vocabulary D1 needs — while den-hoag re-exports all 18 to users
description:
[D7a] MEASURED. gen-select is under-leveraged and THE UNUSED HALF IS EXACTLY THE MISSING
VOCABULARY. 4 OF 18 EXPORTS USED -- `matches`, `when`, `adapters`, `attrs`.
Unused: and, any, child, descendant, entity, entityKind, has, isIdentified, kind, not,
parentMatches, selectorEq, star, within.
★ THE UNUSED SET IS DOMINATED BY SCOPE-POSITION COMBINATORS -- child, descendant, within,
parentMatches, star -- which is PRECISELY the vocabulary D1 needs and `__firesAtKinds`
approximates.
★ And den-hoag RE-EXPORTS THE ENTIRE SURFACE TO USERS (`sel = select`) while internally
calling four. So users are handed a vocabulary the kernel does not use on itself.
NOTE: `sel.entityKind` is a THROWING TOMBSTONE, not live API -- do not count it as
available surface.

title: [D2] NARROWED: matchIdWith is NOT unwired — it is driven at lib/default.nix matchIdStructural and was at the audit's own baseline; the surviving claim is that it is unwired into the THREE POLICY-DISPATCH SITES
description:
[D2] MEASURED. den-hoag WROTE the scope adapter and never called it. `lib/scope-adapter.nix`
`matchIdWith` builds the gen-select scope context; its header says "A thin wrapper, no
algorithm of its own." ★ `matchId` HAS ZERO CALLERS -- one grep hit repo-wide, a comment.
It is the correct entry point for D1's resolution (see D3's navigational note: the
gen-side `mkMatch` forwards the wrong context object), so this is not dead code to
delete -- it is BUILT-AND-UNWIRED, and D1's fix is what wires it.
⇒ Scope with D1 rather than separately. Filed distinctly because "we already have the
adapter" changes D1's cost estimate materially.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS REFUTED AT THIS BEAD'S OWN BASELINE, NOT MERELY EXPIRED. Retitled to the surviving claim rather than closed, because the narrower version is real and closing would discard it.

CLAIMED, and labelled MEASURED: 'matchIdWith has zero callers' and 'matchId has one grep hit, a comment'.
MEASURED NOW: lib/default.nix:1975 IS CODE —
    matchIdStructural = scopeAdapter.matchIdWith structural { classOf = classNameOf; };
★ AND IT EXISTED AT c42df53, THE AUDIT'S OWN BASELINE, as lib/default.nix:2029, IDENTICAL EXPRESSION. matchId additionally has TWO live callers at ci/tests/entity-fleet.nix:165,169, also present at c42df53.
⇒ THIS IS NOT STALENESS. A single grep at the commit the audit itself named would have refuted it on the day it was written. That is a different and worse failure than a claim overtaken by later work: staleness is the record decaying, this is the record never having been right.

SURVIVING CLAIM, and it is worth keeping: matchIdWith is unwired INTO THE THREE POLICY-DISPATCH SITES. That is a real gap and it is what this bead should now be read as tracking. Anyone scoping from the old title would have gone looking for a dead binding and found live code, then either concluded the bead was fixed or re-implemented something that exists.

★ METHOD CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WHOLE INVENTORY (den-hoag-4kh.53): a 'MEASURED' label is a claim about a PROCEDURE, and the procedure can be wrong. Two of the thirteen deep-verified children were refuted at their own baseline. The other sixty children of that inventory received only an identifier-existence sweep, which CANNOT detect this failure mode — it confirms a symbol exists, not that the claim about it holds.

title: [D5] NARROWED: the ctxExt seam IS driven (lib/default.nix matchIdStructural passes { classOf = classNameOf; }) — the surviving claim is that cases (a) and (b) have no selector equivalent
description:
[D7] MEASURED. Three cases with NO selector equivalent today:
(a) PER-COORDINATE scoping needs the PRODUCT context, unreachable through the scope
    adapter -- the path is `matchIdWith`'s existing `ctxExt` seam, UNEXERCISED.
(b) A gate on an ENRICH-INJECTED ctx key: selectors see scope accessors, not enriched
    bindings. SAME SEAM.
(c) Multi-coordinate gates off the parent/child line need `sel.when`.
⇒ (a) and (b) are one seam that already exists and has never been driven. That is the
extension point D1's resolution needs for anything beyond kind-position selection.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THE KEY CLAIM IS REFUTED — 'the ctxExt seam is UNEXERCISED / has never been driven'. Retitled to the surviving claim rather than closed.

MEASURED: lib/scope-adapter.nix names the second formal LITERALLY ctxExt, and lib/default.nix:1975 DRIVES IT: scopeAdapter.matchIdWith structural { classOf = classNameOf; }. ★ AND THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT CITES THAT EXACT classOf CASE AS THE SEAM'S MOTIVATION — so the seam is not merely exercised, it is exercised by the use it was built for, and the code says so.
Anchor by expression: lib/scope-adapter.nix matchIdWith and lib/default.nix matchIdStructural.

NOT REFUTED, and this is what survives: that cases (a) and (b) have NO SELECTOR EQUIVALENT. That is the live gap.

Same family as den-hoag-4kh.53.4 — both refuted at the audit's own baseline c42df53 by a single grep, both labelled MEASURED. See that bead's method note.

title: [compat] compile.nix:436 stamps a SYNTACTIC positional key — safe only because the refs reaching it carry no content; an anonymous inline literal is content-bearing AND positional
description:
FILED SO AN INCIDENTAL SAFETY CANNOT SILENTLY BECOME UNSAFE. Measured 2026-07-28
at den-hoag c42df53 (audit closed at den-hoag-9xo.69).

lib/compat/compile.nix:436 stamps identity with `nm` = `fallbackName` for positional
or nameless refs. THE DANGEROUS PROPERTY IS ALREADY TRUE THERE:
★ `fallbackName` is built from the include-list POSITION -- a SYNTACTIC coordinate,
not a resolution one. Measured: a fleet run and a blade-only run produce THE SAME 69
stamps, i.e. ONE STAMP SET SHARED ACROSS ALL SEVEN HOSTS. Only three distinct keys
exist fleet-wide (__aspectInclude__bareFn__4__..., __aspectInclude__bareFn__6__...,
<emitted>@dev.slab.sini:content:0).

IT IS SAFE TODAY FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT A PROPERTY: the refs reaching this branch
carry NO CONTENT. They are genuinely empty attrsets or includes-only -- `hasRealContent`
is false, which is exactly WHY they fell through to it. So key-constant meets
content-constant, and there is nothing to collide.

★ WHAT BREAKS IT, and it is expressible on den's surface today: ANY ref reaching this
branch WITH PER-NODE CONTENT. An anonymous inline literal is the natural instance --
    h4.includes = [ { nixos = ...; } ];
-- content-bearing AND positional, so it lands here and takes a positional key. None
on the current corpus resolves to per-node content, which is why this is a hazard and
not a defect. By feedback_den_surface_not_config, corpus-absence does not discharge it.

WHY IT IS WORTH TRACKING RATHER THAN NOTING: a collision here would be SILENT.
`identity` at collections.nix:205 is the A12 producer key feeding sortByProducer and
the per-channel grouping; a collision does not throw, it merges or mis-orders
producers that should have been distinct, with a green eval.

RELATED AND NOT THE SAME: den-hoag-9xo.61's 31-way collision comes from the BARE-FN
WRAP NAMING (compile.nix:501-508), not from this site -- but it uses the SAME
`fallbackName` construction. ⇒ THE REAL SUBJECT IS THE CONSTRUCTION, NOT EITHER CALL
SITE: positional naming is unsound wherever per-node content follows it. A fix for
9xo.61 that repairs only the wrap leaves this site holding the same loaded shape.
Prefer a construction that cannot mint a node-invariant name for per-node content.

ALSO MEASURED: none of this site's three keys reach collections.nix:205 at all -- 0
rows each in the fleet-wide key->content map -- so today they never act as producer
identities there. ★ Consumers of id_hash OTHER than that one were NOT checked, so
"unused" is established for one consumer, not everywhere.

title: [parity] on a type-invalid host field den-hoag throws a named error while v1 SILENTLY DROPS THE WHOLE HOST from nixosConfigurations — a divergence with the opposite polarity to the rest of the arc
description:
★ UNSOUGHT DIVERGENCE, MEASURED IN PASSING 2026-07-28 while building a control for
den-hoag-9xo.68. Recorded because its POLARITY is the opposite of every other
divergence in this arc, and because nobody was looking for it.

THE PROBE: `environment = 42` (a type-invalid value) on
den.hosts.x86_64-linux.blade. Same probe, both arms, same run.
· den-hoag: LOUD NAMED TYPE ERROR --
    A definition for option `den.hosts.x86_64-linux.blade.environment' is not of
    type `string'
· den v1 (99cc0c5a): NO ERROR. It SILENTLY DROPS blade FROM nixosConfigurations
  ENTIRELY -- the host simply ceases to exist ("does not provide attribute
  'nixosConfigurations.blade...'").

⇒ ON A TYPE-INVALID VALUE, den-hoag IS STRICTER THAN v1. On an unknown KEY, both
are equally permissive (den-hoag-9xo.68). The two behaviours are independent and
pull in opposite directions.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN CELEBRATING:
· The parity target is BYTE EQUIVALENCE OF OUTPUT, and here the outputs differ in
  the strongest possible way -- one arm HAS a host and the other does not. Any
  parity harness comparing configurations would see a missing attribute and could
  attribute it to something else entirely.
· A den-hoag ABORT where v1 SILENTLY DROPS is arguably the better behaviour and is
  still a DIVERGENCE. It must be a DECIDED divergence, recorded as intended, rather
  than an accident nobody noticed -- otherwise a later "fix" restores v1's silent
  drop in the name of parity, which would be a regression wearing a parity
  justification.
· ★ AND v1's BEHAVIOUR HERE IS ITSELF ALARMING: a type error in one field makes an
  entire host VANISH from the fleet outputs with no diagnostic. That is a silent
  whole-host loss, and it is the shape this arc keeps finding (a failure that
  presents as an absence).

NOT DIAGNOSED. Neither side's mechanism was traced -- not why v1 drops rather than
throws, nor whether den-hoag's throw comes from its own typing or from a gen-schema
crossing. Only ONE field (`environment`) and ONE invalid value (an integer where a
string is wanted) were tested; whether this generalises to other fields or other
type mismatches is unknown.

SUGGESTED HANDLING, not a remedy: decide whether den-hoag's stricter behaviour is
INTENDED. If yes, record it as a deliberate divergence with its reason so no future
parity work reverses it. If the answer is that v1's silent drop must be reproduced,
that decision needs its own justification, because it means choosing a silent
whole-host loss over a named error.

title: [compat] an unrouted nixos.environment.etc line on a den host declaration is silently absorbed with zero drv change — accepted and dropped, neither honoured nor refused (observed, not investigated)
description:
OBSERVED IN PASSING 2026-07-28, as a DISCARDED control attempt rather than as a
targeted measurement. Reported because the shape is the fail-open class, not
because it was investigated. VERIFY BEFORE ACTING.

WHAT HAPPENED. While building a positive control for den-hoag-9xo.66, an attempt to
perturb a host's output added a `nixos.environment.etc."..."` line to the den HOST
DECLARATION in nix-config. It was SILENTLY ABSORBED: no error, no warning, and
system.build.toplevel.drvPath was UNCHANGED. The attempt was discarded as a failed
control rather than counted as evidence -- correctly -- and a different perturbation
(a linux-kernel optimization enum value) was used instead, which DID move the
drvPath, so the instrument was live.

WHY IT IS WORTH A BEAD. An unrouted field on a host declaration should either take
effect or be REFUSED BY NAME. Being accepted and dropped is the third option, and it
is the one that fails silently and everywhere -- a user writing that line has no
signal at all that it did nothing (feedback_absence_is_a_decision). It is also the
same shape as den-hoag-4kh.21's family: a declared surface the engine accepts and
does not honour, where the owner's standing ruling is NAMED-REJECT AT DEFINITION
TIME rather than silent acceptance.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is most of it:
· Whether this is v1 behaviour, den-hoag behaviour, or BOTH. The attempt was made on
  arm A (corpus own pin) -- so on the evidence it is a DEN V1 behaviour, and may be
  intended freeform absorption on the host submodule. If v1 intends it, this is not a
  parity defect and the question becomes whether den-hoag should reproduce it.
· Whether `nixos.` is a routed prefix at that position at all, or whether the correct
  spelling reaches the host differently -- an author error absorbed silently is still
  the same defect class, but a different fix.
· Whether any warning exists that was simply not surfaced by the command used.
· Whether other unrouted prefixes behave the same way, or this one specifically.

HOW TO SETTLE IT CHEAPLY: write a deliberately nonsense key at the same position and
see whether anything objects, on BOTH arms, with a positive control that a
correctly-spelled key at that position DOES move the drvPath. That distinguishes
"freeform absorption by design" from "silently dropped".

PROVENANCE NOTE: the agent that hit this flagged it as a discarded control and did
not offer it as a finding. That is the right handling -- it is filed here so the
observation is not lost, at the strength it actually has.
notes:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
★ ANSWERED 2026-07-28: BOTH ARMS SILENTLY ABSORB. INHERITED v1 BEHAVIOUR, NOT A
den-hoag REGRESSION. Three controls, including a rejection-VISIBILITY control at
the same depth.

Probe: `zzzNonsenseProbeKey = "deliberate-nonsense";` at the TOP LEVEL of
den.hosts.x86_64-linux.blade.
· ARM A (v1 99cc0c5a), observable = toplevel drvPath:
  pristine 73z2xmpx720rc6dkpw9pnrfjckazbjrd -> with nonsense key IDENTICAL, NO ERROR.
  POSITIVE CONTROL, correct key same position: networking.interfaces.wlp0s20f3.dhcp
  "yes" -> "ipv4" moves it to 4hgph1a5mg3y948dl7ywf3g81mf2aalr. Predicate live.
· ARM B (den-hoag + the rung-1 probe), observable = home-manager.users:
  pristine ["shuo","sini","will"] -> with nonsense key IDENTICAL, NO ERROR.
  CONTROL 1 (correct key, same position): system-access-groups += "server-access"
  -> ["dvicory","pol","shuo","sini","theutz","vic","will"]. Moves.
  ★ CONTROL 2 (REJECTION VISIBILITY at the same depth): `environment = 42` -> LOUD
  NAMED THROW. So this probe CAN see a rejection; the nonsense key's silence is a
  REAL NEGATIVE, not an unreachable predicate.
⇒ Unknown top-level keys on a den host declaration are silently absorbed by BOTH
arms. Not a parity defect. Whether v1 SHOULD absorb them is a separate question
about den's own surface and is not this bead's.

★ HOW THE MEASUREMENT NEARLY WENT WRONG, recorded because it is the arc's shape:
the first arm-B control used networking.hostName with an invalid dhcp = "no"; it
returned "blade" with no error, which LOOKED like arm B failing to type the option.
Re-running the SAME probe on ARM A also returned "blade" -- so it was PROBE DEPTH,
not the arm. The dhcp type rejection only surfaces at full toplevel depth, which
arm B cannot reach. Stopping at the first control would have reported AN ARM
DIFFERENCE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. The fix was a control that fires at hm-users depth.

DEMOTED to P3 and closed: the observation is real, the behaviour is inherited, and
nothing in the den-hoag arc turns on it.
UNTESTED: only ONE nonsense key at ONE position (top level of the host decl).
Other positions -- inside `settings`, inside `networking` -- untested. A bad VALUE
at settings.core.system.linux-kernel.optimization is known to reject loudly, but an
unknown KEY there was not tried.
close_reason: NOT A den-hoag DEFECT: both arms silently absorb an unknown top-level key on a den host declaration, measured with three controls including a rejection-visibility control at the same depth (environment = 42 throws loud, so the silence is a real negative). Inherited v1 behaviour. Whether den v1 SHOULD absorb unknown keys is a separate question about den own surface.

title: [kernel] negates and from are unchecked annotations while emits is a checked contract — and concern-derived uses strict < for POSITIVE reads where ABW condition 1 permits <=, opposite to gen-resolve
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-28 while auditing ABW condition 2. Two defects in the same guard
layer, both about the gap between what a field DECLARES and what the engine CHECKS.

★ (1) `negates` AND `from` ARE UNCHECKED ANNOTATIONS, WHILE `emits` IS NOW A
CHECKED CONTRACT. Same shape, opposite treatment, in the same tree.
· lib/concern-derived.nix -- `negates` defaults to [ ] and BOTH negation guards
  SKIP when it is empty. A derive body that reads a relation and branches on its
  emptiness WITHOUT listing it in `negates` is invisible to the gate.
· lib/concern-productions.nix says it verbatim of `from`: "it DRIVES the L2 gate +
  documents the contract, IT IS NOT EXECUTED."
· Meanwhile the policy record's `emits` became a CHECKED contract -- conformingProduce
  verifies every emission against the declaration and aborts emitsUndeclared.
⇒ The soundness of every negation guard rests on the author having DECLARED the
negation. This is exactly the hazard the emits contract was built to remove, left
standing one file over. And it is the permissive-default failure mode
(feedback_absence_is_a_decision): absent `negates` means "negates nothing", so the
guard fails OPEN and the omission lives in code that does not mention the field.
NOT A REMEDY, but note the asymmetry to weigh: `emits` could be checked because
emissions are observable at the funnel they pass through. A negated READ is not
obviously observable the same way -- establish whether it is before assuming the
emits treatment transfers.

★ (2) THE TWO LAYERS TAKE OPPOSITE POSITIONS ON ABW CONDITION 1, AND ONE OF THEM
IS OVER-RESTRICTIVE.
· lib/concern-derived.nix uses STRICT `<` for the POSITIVE `over` read:
  notLater = any (s: !(strataLt strataOrder s stratum)) overStrata
  ABW Definition 3 condition 1 permits `<=` for positive occurrences -- same
  stratum is legal, and that is how intra-stratum positive recursion works.
· gen-resolve lib/schedule.nix gets it right: the violation predicate is `pb > pa`
  ONLY, with its own comment "a rule may read predicates at strata <= its own
  (positive dep); reading a STRICTLY-LATER stratum is the violation."
· den-hoag's own circular attributes RELY on the permissive reading:
  `resolved-aspects` and `reach` are self-reading circular attrs.
This is SOUND (strictly-stratified is a subset of stratified) but the layer CANNOT
EXPRESS intra-stratum positive recursion, so a legitimate den.derived that needed
it would be refused with a stratum complaint rather than a real one.
★ AND THE BINDING IS NAMED FOR THE BEHAVIOUR IT DOES NOT HAVE: `notLater`
describes `<=`; the code does `<`. A reader checking this layer against the paper
would read the name and move on.

WHY BOTH ARE FILED TOGETHER: they are the same layer's two halves -- what the
guard is TOLD (1) and what the guard DOES with it (2). Fixing either alone leaves
a guard whose faithfulness to Definition 3 is still unestablished in the other
direction.

title: [kernel] enrich feed uses exact-list equality on produces, so a mixed enrich+member codomain silently bypasses the keyset-ascent fixpoint — admissible today, the multi-stratum ban does not catch it
description:
OBSERVED SHAPE at the 9xo.57 gate, 2026-07-28. Reported as observed, NOT as a
running witness -- no fixture was built to fire it. Verify before fixing.

lib/concern-policies.nix partitions the enrich feed by EXACT LIST EQUALITY:
    enrich = builtins.filter (r: r.produces == [ "enrich" ]) rules;
with the `policy` feed as its complement.

=> A policy whose codomain is `[ "enrich" "member" ]` fails the equality, lands in
the `policy` feed ONLY, and so its ENRICH declarations fire at structural.nix
attribute 4 and NEVER REACH attribute 2's keyset-ascent fixpoint.

WHY THIS IS LIVE AND NOT BLOCKED BY THE MULTI-STRATUM BAN: `enrich` and `member`
are BOTH structural. The ban (errors.multiStratumUnsupported) refuses a codomain
spanning STRATA; this codomain spans none. It is admissible today and passes every
guard.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH BEFORE ANY FIX:
  - Does a policy with a mixed enrich codomain exist in the tree, the corpus, or
    the templates? If none, the defect is den-surface-expressible but unwitnessed
    -- which under feedback_den_surface_not_config still counts, but changes the
    urgency and the shape of the fixture needed.
  - Does the enrich declaration actually get DROPPED, or does it fire late with
    different results? "Never reaches the fixpoint" is the reviewer's reading of
    the filter, not a measured outcome. Measure the outcome.
  - An absence claim here needs a positive control on the same predicate in the
    same run.

RELATED SHAPE, SAME FILE, ALREADY UNDERSTOOD: the two staged-pre-pass feeds
select on `r.group == "structural" && emitsAny r <kinds>`. That reduces to plain
emits-membership only because r.group derives from emits and a multi-stratum
codomain aborts. It is CORRECT AS LONG AS THE BAN STANDS, and the retirement of
resolveFamilyUntagged / excludeFamilyUntagged rests on exactly that equivalence.
Recording the dependency here so a future proposal to change r.group's derivation
knows it also silently removes two guards.

title: [ci] boundary.nix's seam guard scans only denHoag.* references — it does NOT police kernel config.den.* options, which is the crossing pattern designs are told to use
description:
MEASURED — `ci/tests/boundary.nix`'s SEAM-ENUMERATION GUARD DOES NOT POLICE THE SEAM IT IS NAMED FOR. Found by
running the check against a proposed design rather than by reading it.

The boundary suite has three guards: (1) a token scan over kernel files, (2) import direction, (3) seam
enumeration. ★ GUARD (3) SCANS ONLY `denHoag.<ident>` AND `inherit (denHoag)` REFERENCES. IT DOES NOT POLICE
`config.den.*` OPTIONS AT ALL — and its own comment LISTS them and says in the same breath that they are
"NOT scanned".
⇒ A DESIGN THAT CROSSES THE KERNEL⟂COMPAT LINE BY ADDING A KERNEL OPTION CROSSES UNGUARDED. The precedent is
already in the tree: `den.excludeFamilyNames` (lib/default.nix:968-974, written by lib/compat/flake-module.nix:552)
is exactly this shape and is NOT in the enumerated set and NOT caught.

★ WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A COVERAGE GAP: the option route is the ESTABLISHED, RECOMMENDED way to cross
the seam in this codebase — the kind-schema-excludes design cites `den.excludeFamilyNames` as its precedent,
and the policy-domain design proposes another. So the guard is blind to the crossing pattern designs are
actively told to use, while policing a pattern (`denHoag.<ident>`) that a design following house style would
not produce. THE GUARD IS STRONGEST WHERE THE RISK IS LOWEST.
AND THE CONSEQUENCE FOR REVIEW: "boundary.nix passes" has been quoted in this arc as evidence a design keeps
the seam clean. For an option-crossing design that sentence carries NO information. It should not be quoted
that way again until this is fixed.

ACCEPTANCE: guard (3) enumerates kernel `config.den.*` options as well as `denHoag.*` references, with the
existing crossings recorded as the baseline set — so a NEW option is what turns it red, not the existing ones.
★ AND THE BASELINE MUST BE CAPTURED AS A SET, NOT A COUNT: a count-based baseline passes when one crossing is
added and another removed, which is exactly the substitution a refactor makes.
NOTE the standing rule this serves: the kernel must be a pure graph representation, and `boundary.nix` guards
that line LEXICALLY ONLY — it cannot observe representation. This finding narrows what its lexical guarantee
actually covers.

PROVENANCE: policy-domain-selection investigation, 2026-07-28, while checking a proposed design against the
guard rather than assuming it would pass.

title: [ci] three fixture comments describe a corpus shape that does not exist, and one names a guard (errors.reservedClassInclude) that was never built
description:
MEASURED — THREE den-hoag CI TESTS DESCRIBE THE CORPUS WRONGLY, AND ONE NAMES AN ERROR THAT DOES NOT EXIST.
Found while establishing the includes ruling (den-hoag-9xo.48); each verified against the pinned corpus rev
b0b207693ce66fb57acf2bb09cf9549e1dbddec7 with a positive control.

 1. `ci/tests/compat-nested-class-named-aspect.nix:8` states "the corpus follows this by naming the shared-HM
    aspect `home-manager-shared`". ★ FALSE — `home-manager-shared` = ZERO occurrences repo-wide at that rev.
    The corpus has `den.aspects.core.users.home-manager`
    (modules/den/aspects/core/users/home-manager.nix:5), included at modules/den/aspects/roles/default.nix:16.
    POSITIVE CONTROL: the same grep for `home-manager` matches 20 files under modules/den/.
 2. ★ `ci/tests/compat-nested-class-named-aspect.nix:132` says the reservation-include "fires the loud
    reservation error (`errors.reservedClassInclude`)". THERE IS NO SUCH ERROR. `reservedClassInclude` appears

 3. `ci/tests/compat-settings-nav-hm-collision.nix:3` describes the corpus HM aspect as carrying "a `.settings`

★ WHY THIS IS WORTH A BEAD RATHER THAN A COMMENT SWEEP: these are not stale line numbers, they are FIXTURES

title: [ci] no fixture exercises a DIVERGENT declared slice firing through the staged pre-pass — green cannot distinguish 'never fires' from 'cannot fire'
description:
MEASURED COVERAGE GAP — NO TEST FORCES A `mkSlice`-BUILT DECLARED SLICE'S PRODUCE THROUGH THE STAGED PRE-PASS.
NOT EVEN INERTLY. The gap is TOTAL.

FOUR `ci/tests/` fixtures use any of the five `producesByName` key names (measured over all 205 files at
`a40cc96`, non-comment lines; positive control same run: `policies\.` → 59 files). EVERY ONE IS STOPPED SHORT
OF THE GUARD, EACH AT A DIFFERENT POINT:
  · `compat-entity-fields.nix:180` — genuinely declared (value-conditional `hubBody`, gated on
    `host.settings.core.network.syncthing.isHub or false`, so the probe is empty → `mkDeclaredSlices` →
    `mkSlice`). ★ But its family is `pipeOp` ⇒ COLLECTION, and the feed admits only `group == "structural"`
    (`lib/concern-policies.nix:420-421`), so IT NEVER ENTERS THE FEED. This is the only `ci/tests/` site where
    the kernel's `producesByName.${name}` lookup (`:357`) supplies a family.
  · `compat-hm-battery.nix:80` — NOT a declared slice. Its body emits unconditionally (`:80-90`), so
    `probeActs` is non-empty ⇒ `expanded = false` ⇒ the `!expanded` branch ⇒ `mkSingle`, and the table is
    NEVER READ. It is the design's own D11. It does still carry `produces = ["member"]` (PROBE-EXTRACTED, not
    declared), is tagged `__resolveFamily` off `rfOf`'s `!expanded` arm (`:377-382`), is structural, enters
    the feed and IS fired by `runPrePass` — ★ but as `mkSingle`, whose produce is `checkedProduce`
    (`:234`→`:160-162`), while the guard under design sits in `mkSlice` (`:250-270`).
  · `compat-resolve.nix:463` — `kiFeedIds` (`:223-225`) runs `denHoag.internal.compilePolicies` IN ISOLATION.
    No fleet, therefore NO `runPrePass` AT ALL — not merely an unforced produce.
  · `compat-feature-severed.nix:430` — wires `env-to-hosts` as a `rack.includes` kind-include
    (`kiResolveFixture` `:422-441`), value-conditional, family via the compat `__produces` stamp. Reads only
    `compileFull … .__resolveFamily` (`:442-445`), and `compileFull` is the compat compile stage
    (`lib/compat/default.nix:492-496`) — so IT NEVER BUILDS A RULE AT ALL. Stopped earliest of the four.
BOTH PRE-PASS FEEDS CHECKED, not just the first: `excludeRules = policiesRules.excludeFamily`
(`lib/default.nix:1111`, `staged-resolution.nix:204`) applies the same `group == "structural"` filter, and
none of the four sites emits `suppress`.

★ WHY IT MATTERS: with the design's core applied, a named abort becomes raisable FROM INSIDE the construct
tracked for retirement at `den-hoag-4kh.18`, and the 1914/1914 green suite is the ONLY evidence that path is
inert. GREEN CANNOT DISTINGUISH "the guard never fires here" FROM "the guard cannot fire here."

ACCEPTANCE: one fixture authoring a declared `structural` policy inside a `mkDen` fleet whose body emits a key
OUTSIDE its declaration, asserted to abort NAMED through the pre-pass path — red before the design's core,
green after, with a positive control on an aligned declaration that must NOT abort.
★ THE FIXTURE MUST BE VALUE-CONDITIONAL, AND THIS IS PROVEN, NOT ADVISORY: a probe-emitting body takes the
`!expanded` branch, compiles to `mkSingle`, never consults the table, and would silently exercise D11 —
PASSING WHILE MEASURING NOTHING. That is the same shape as the gap itself.
INSTRUMENT LIMIT: `mkCi`'s asserter has NO message-text channel (`ci/tests/_lib/den-compat-test.nix:27`) and
`builtins.tryEval` yields only a bool, so the NAMING must be pinned out-of-suite — the same constraint that
forced `den-hoag-4kh.13`'s naming witness out of the suite. Tracked as `den-hoag-9mo`.

★ THIS BODY WAS REWRITTEN 2026-07-28. Its first version asserted that `compat-hm-battery.nix:80` DOES fire a
declared slice and is "inert only because the body emits exactly the declared member" — BOTH SENTENCES FALSE.
That came from an agent's self-correction which was itself wrong and which the orchestrator propagated without
re-deriving. Corrected by execution; full case at `den-hoag-4kh.20`. Recorded here because the earlier version
understated the gap as partial when it is total, and because A CORRECTION BELONGS IN THE BODY, NOT ONLY IN A
COMMENT — a comment is a supplement for a reader who reaches it; the body is what a dispatch quotes.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORRECTION — THIS BEAD'S PREMISE WAS BUILT ON A REFUTED SELF-CORRECTION, AND THE FINDING IS NOW STRONGER, NOT WEAKER.

I recorded that ci/tests/compat-hm-battery.nix:80 DOES fire a declared structural slice through runPrePass, inert only because its body emits exactly the declared `member`. MEASURED FALSE by an independent confirmation pass: `env-users` there is NOT a declared slice at all. Its body emits at the VALUE-LESS PROBE, so `mkRules` takes the `!expanded` branch → `mkSingle`, and `producesByName` IS NEVER READ. It is the design's own D11 case. Established with a four-way branch discriminator whose same-run control proves the instrument can see the table being consulted (see den-hoag-4kh.20).

⇒ THE CORRECTED AND STRONGER BOUND, measured at a40cc96: only TWO ci/tests/ fixtures use any of the five table-key names — compat-entity-fields.nix:180 and compat-hm-battery.nix:80 (positive control same run: `policies\.` → 70 files). The FIRST declares `pipeOp` ⇒ collection, so it NEVER ENTERS THE FEED (concern-policies.nix:420-421 admits only `group == "structural"`). The SECOND is `mkSingle`. And compat-resolve.nix:463 puts a real declared structural rule in the feed but forces only `r.identity`.
★ SO NO TEST FORCES A `mkSlice`-BUILT DECLARED SLICE'S PRODUCE THROUGH `runPrePass` — NOT EVEN INERTLY. The gap this bead tracks is TOTAL, not partial. My original framing understated it by claiming an inert-but-exercised path exists; there is none.

THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS UNCHANGED AND NOW BETTER MOTIVATED: a fixture authoring a declared `structural` policy inside a mkDen fleet whose body emits outside its declaration, asserted to abort NAMED through the pre-pass path, red before the core and green after, with a positive control on an aligned declaration that must NOT abort.
★ AND ONE CONSTRAINT IS NOW PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the fixture MUST be value-conditional. A probe-emitting body takes the `!expanded` branch and never consults the table, so a fixture written the obvious way would silently test D11 instead of the declared path — passing while measuring nothing. That is the same shape as the coverage gap itself.

title: [gen-dispatch] declared-rule arm skips pure validation for no gain — the fix is a deletion, and it does NOT substitute for the consumer-side guard
description:
[gen-dispatch] MEASURED — THE DECLARED-RULE ARM SKIPS A PURE VALIDATION AND BUYS ALMOST NOTHING FOR IT. THE
FIX IS A DELETION.

`gen-derive/lib/core/dispatch.nix:104-107`: when `res.declared`, dispatch skips classify-validation.
MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: dispatch does NOT infer a declared rule's group — `deriveGroup` STAMPS IT AT DEFINITION
TIME — so that arm skips PURE VALIDATION and buys only `map classify res.actions`. Removing the arm restores
`:113-116` for ALL consumers.
⇒ This is a DELETION, not a feature: the branch exists to avoid a classification that is already performed
elsewhere, and its cost is a validation that consumers then have to re-implement downstream. den-hoag's
design 2 exists precisely to re-implement it.

★ IT DOES NOT, HOWEVER, SUBSTITUTE FOR THE CONSUMER-SIDE FIX, and this was measured rather than assumed —
TWO defects never reach dispatch at all:
  (i) the empty-declaration case builds ZERO rules (`map … []`), so nothing arrives for dispatch to check;
      `deriveGroup` would not catch it either — an empty `produces` gives `groups == []` and the rule is
      returned unchanged (`gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:49`).
  (ii) the multi-group declared case MUST keep den-hoag's pre-filter (otherwise emissions mis-place), and
      with the pre-filter in place dispatch's `:113` would ABORT A CORRECT multi-group policy — its predicate
      is per-rule single-group, whereas the needed one is UNION-COVERAGE OVER THE SLICE SET, a vocabulary gen
      does not currently have.
★ SO ADOPTING THIS INSTEAD OF THE CONSUMER FIX WOULD LEAVE THE GUARD LIVE ON NO CORPUS PATH — a guard that
cannot fire, which is the predicate-blindness failure this project keeps paying for. ADOPTING BOTH IS
COHERENT and is the recommendation: the gen change is right at its own layer, the consumer change is right at
its own.

RELATED FINDING, same investigation: gen-dispatch's trust comment cites gen-resolve `lib/schedule.nix:52-110`
as its analogy. That analogy FAILS — gen-resolve DOES discharge its declared `stratum` against the equation's
real readsAttrs cone. The trust is justified by pointing at code that does the opposite.

NOT MEASURED: read, not run. No clone built, no cost measured. Cost claims here are structural.
Filed in this tracker because it covers all gen-* repos.

PROVENANCE: produces-r2 redesign §5.0/§5(d), 2026-07-28.

title: [kernel] concern-policies.nix:11-12 asserts gen-dispatch validates declarations classify to their group — false for the declared path
description:
MEASURED — A KERNEL FILE HEADER ASSERTS AN INVARIANT THAT IS FALSE ON ONE OF ITS TWO PATHS.

`lib/concern-policies.nix:11-12` states that gen-dispatch "validates that its declarations all classify to
that group."
MEASURED: FALSE FOR THE DECLARED PATH. `gen-derive/lib/core/dispatch.nix:104-107` SKIPS classify-validation
when `res.declared` — that is the trust this whole arc's design 2 exists to discharge. The header describes
the fan path's behaviour and states it as the file's general contract.

★ WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A NIT: this file is KERNEL (`ci/tests/boundary.nix:37` names it), and the
header is what a reader consults to learn what the module guarantees. An invariant asserted in a kernel file
header, false on the path that carries the declaration mechanism, is the documented-but-unenforced pattern
the kernel-purity criteria name explicitly — in its worse form, since the text does not merely fail to
enforce the invariant, it asserts one that does not hold.
It also actively obstructs the fix: anyone auditing the declared path against this header concludes the
validation is already present.

RELATED, and the reason this surfaced: the design's own §9 cites gen-dispatch's trust comment, which points
at gen-resolve `lib/schedule.nix:52-110` as its analogy. That analogy ALSO fails — gen-resolve DOES discharge
its declared `stratum` against the equation's real readsAttrs cone. So the trust is justified in the comment
by an analogy to code that does the opposite, and re-asserted in den-hoag's kernel header as a fact.

ACCEPTANCE: the header states what is actually guaranteed on each path, or the declared path gains the
validation the header claims (which is design 2's core, at which point the header becomes true). Either way
the two must be made to agree, and whichever lands first should not leave the other stale.

PROVENANCE: produces-r2 redesign, 2026-07-28, found while writing the C7-a reuse scan. In no input.

title: [perf] producesByName guard costs the FAN path +3.8% for a provably-empty residue — 18 of 19 configs take that path
description:
MEASURED PERFORMANCE DEFECT — THE COMMON PATH PAYS FOR THE RARE PATH.

The producesByName trust guard (design at specs/2026-07-28-produces-declaration-trust-design.md) adds a
residue computation that the FAN PATH pays for and can never use.
MEASURED, and independently REPRODUCED by the re-gate reviewer: nrFunctionCalls 1,850,222 -> 1,920,222 on the
fan path = +3.8%, for a residue that is PROVABLY EMPTY on that path.

★ WHY THIS IS NOT A ROUNDING ERROR: the fan is the path taken by EVERY UNDECLARED VALUE-CONDITIONAL POLICY,
and 18 OF 19 den-configs DEFINE NONE OF THE FIVE KEYS the declared path needs. So essentially the entire
corpus runs the path that pays, to protect a path almost nothing takes. Under the standing rule that
PERFORMANCE IS A DEFECT AND NOT A TRADE-OFF, this is filed rather than absorbed into a disclosure bullet.

The spec DOES disclose it — one bullet — which is why this is a cost-allocation item and not a
correctness finding. C8 passed: no byte identity was purchased with complexity here.

GENUINELY OPEN, and the cheap answer may well be right:
  (a) price a variant that skips the residue when the declaration is absent (`produces = null`), so the fan
      pays nothing — note the fan ALREADY gets the equivalent check free by that same route, which is
      suggestive;
  (b) accept the 3.8% with the measurement recorded, if the branch costs more in complexity than it saves;
  (c) let it dissolve — if the gen-dispatch-layer construction (the C7-a gap) is taken instead, this cost
      may not arise at all, since the check would sit where the trust is rather than where the emission is.
Do NOT resolve this before the C7-a alternative is priced; (c) would make (a) wasted work.

PROVENANCE: re-gate of design 2, 2026-07-28. Reproduced by the reviewer, not inherited from the spec.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORRECTION — THIS BEAD'S OPTION (a) RESTS ON A CLAIM OF MINE THAT IS HALF WRONG. Measured and corrected by the produces-r2 agent, 2026-07-28.

I WROTE: 'the fan ALREADY gets the equivalent check free by that same route (`produces = null`), which is suggestive.'
MEASURED: the fan is CLASSIFIED for free (gen-derive/lib/core/dispatch.nix:111), but THE CHECK IS VACUOUS, NOT FREE. `mkSlice` PRE-FILTERS on EVERY path (concern-policies.nix:267), so `res.actions` is SINGLE-GROUP BY CONSTRUCTION and dispatch's :113/:115 CAN NEVER FIRE — for the fan OR for the declared path. Nothing is being obtained for free; the containment check is simply unreachable on both.
⇒ The fan's totality does NOT come from a check. It comes from `assertCovered` plus full coverage — A THEOREM, not an empirical property.

★ THIS MAKES OPTION (a) SAFE FOR A BETTER REASON THAN I GAVE. Skipping the residue when the declaration is absent is sound because the fan's coverage is PROVED, not because some other check happens to catch it. A justification resting on 'the other path checks it too' would have been false and would have failed the first time someone asked which check.

AND IT SHARPENS THE COST ITSELF: the fan's +3.8% is REDUNDANT work, not merely misallocated. Dispatch already classifies fan actions at dispatch.nix:111 (`classify = declarations.stratumOf`, structural.nix:297), so post-core the fan classifies the same emissions TWICE.

A FOURTH OPTION, ORTHOGONAL TO (a)/(b)/(c), recorded not applied: `prelude.partition` removes one traversal on BOTH paths. Not applied because the design's core is hash-frozen; it belongs to whoever implements.
RESOLUTION REMAINS DEFERRED behind the gen-layer question — options (a) and (c) are not independent, so prescribing (a) now is discarded work if the gen-layer route is taken.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ THE DEFERRAL REASON RECORDED ON THIS BEAD IS UNSOUND — corrected by the R2 focused gate, 2026-07-28.

I deferred resolution 'pending the gen-layer question', on the reasoning that options (a) and (c) are not independent and prescribing (a) now would be discarded work if the gen-layer route were taken.
MEASURED AGAINST THE SPEC'S OWN §5(d): that verdict is 'adopting (d) AS WELL AS §3 is coherent and is the recommendation for the gen side; on the den-hoag side §3 stands unchanged either way.' ★ UNDER THAT RECOMMENDED COMBINATION THE RESIDUE STILL RUNS ON THE FAN AND THE +3.8% DOES NOT DISSOLVE. Option (c) as I wrote it requires adopting (d) INSTEAD OF §3 — which §5(d) explicitly rejects, and which the gate separately established is impossible (D7's zero-rules case never reaches dispatch at all).
⇒ THE DEFERRAL RESTED ON AN OPTION THAT THE SAME ANALYSIS HAD ALREADY CLOSED. (c) is not live. This bead is therefore NOT blocked on the gen-layer question in the way recorded.

WHAT SURVIVES: option (a) — skip the residue when the declaration is absent — remains sound and is now sound for a STATED reason rather than an empirical one (the fan's totality is a theorem: assertCovered plus full coverage; see this bead's earlier correction). Option (b) accept-and-record remains available. The genuinely open question is narrower than I framed it: (a) versus (b), a complexity-versus-simplicity judgement on one branch, with no upstream dependency.
NEW, ORTHOGONAL TO BOTH: `prelude.partition` (gen-prelude/lib/default.nix:35,203) removes one traversal on BOTH paths. Recorded, not applied — the design's core is hash-frozen, so it belongs to whoever implements.
★ MEASURED FIGURES CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY by the gate: fan 1,850,222 → 1,920,222 = +3.784%; declared 630,224 → 660,224 = +4.760%, thunks +11.34%, env +5.53%. All arithmetic re-checked.

title: [release] den v2 public release + #43 branch migration to denful/den + #28 synthetic corpus — owner-gated and tracked NOWHERE
description:
MEASURED — THE den v2 PUBLIC RELEASE ARC IS ENTIRELY UNTRACKED. OWNER-GATED, WHICH IS WHY IT HAS NO BEAD, AND
EXACTLY WHY IT NEEDS ONE.

DESIGN DECISION (6), historical log :65: "SHIPS AS den v2 (public denful/den) — API carries community weight,

MEASURED: 0 beads; 0 hits in `STATUS/coverage-matrix.md`, `STATUS/compat-feature-register.md`,

ALSO UNTRACKED FROM THE SAME QUEUE: `#28` SYNTHETIC CORPUS — 0 beads, 0 trackers.

PROVENANCE: log-reconcile exhaustive pass, 2026-07-28, item C11.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ RULING B (den-hoag-9xo.48, owner 2026-07-28) CREATES A BREAKING MIGRATION REQUIREMENT THAT BELONGS TO THIS RELEASE ARC.

den-hoag now classifies aspect keys BY NAME EAGERLY AT NAVIGATION, where den v1 classified only at resolution of a specific aspect. CONSEQUENCE: an aspect whose key matches a declared class name is a RESERVED-NAME COLLISION under v2 and was silently fine under v1 — because v1's reservation trigger only fires when the PARENT aspect is resolved, and a sub-aspect that is never explicitly included is never resolved.
MEASURED IN THE REFERENCE CORPUS: `den.aspects.virtualization.microvm` collides with `den.classes.microvm`, both declared IN THE SAME FILE, and v1 DELIVERS the aspect's content (four witnesses — microvm.host.enable, the disk group, firewall port 67, the persistence directory). So this is not a latent bug the corpus got away with; IT IS WORKING v1 CONFIGURATION THAT v2 REJECTS.

⇒ THE MIGRATION OWES A RENAME RULE, NOT A NOTE: 'an aspect key that matches any declared class name must be renamed', with the reason (eager classification) and the remedy. TWO FURTHER CANDIDATE SITES ARE ALREADY VISIBLE across the 19 den-configs and were predicted-not-measured — adda-nixos-config `shells._.aliases` against `den.classes.aliases`, and netadr `profiles._.wsl` against the v1 built-in `wsl` class. Both reach the class-named key through `_`, which v1 aliases to `provides`; that key types freeform under den-hoag, so its children take class channels. ★ MEASURE THOSE TWO BEFORE PUBLISHING THE RULE — a rename rule that under-counts its own blast radius is worse than none, and 2-of-19 versus 2-of-19-plus-whatever-was-not-swept are different migrations.

★ AND THE HARD PREREQUISITE, WHICH IS PART OF THE RULING RATHER THAN A NICETY: THE DECLARATION-TIME NAMED ERROR MUST SHIP BEFORE OR WITH THE RENAME. Today the collision surfaces as a bare gen-aspects type throw at an INCLUDE POSITION with no aspect name, no class name and no file — so under B, every downstream den user meets an unattributable error that is in fact a rename requirement. den-hoag CAN attribute it cheaply: both names are in hand at declaration. Until that error exists, publishing the migration ships a requirement nobody can act on.
NOTE ALSO den-hoag-4kh.47: a shipped CI fixture ALREADY CLAIMS this error exists, calling it `errors.reservedClassInclude`. It does not. Building it makes that fixture honest and closes half of 4kh.47 at the same time.

title: [kernel] 'THE RED WINDOW' block at output-modules.nix:767-775 asserts corpus facts falsified by 6.2a/6.2b — and its self-quoting marker manufactures its own corroboration
description:
★ MEASURED — A STALE BLOCK IN THE KERNEL'S MOST-READ FILE ASSERTS A PRECONDITION THAT SHIPPED WEEKS AGO.

`lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:767-775`, "THE RED WINDOW", asserts:
  - "the corpus has NO reach-edge / reach-suppress / default-edge PRODUCERS until Phase 5"
  - the fleet golden suites are "MARKED PENDING (`# Phase 5: needs corpus edge producers`)"

MEASURED AT HEAD — BOTH FALSE:
  6.2a/6.2b SHIPPED. `lib/compat/compile.nix:987-998` emits `declare.reach-edge` PER NAMED CLASS. So corpus

title: [gen] checks.default is a homegrown asserter — nix-unit expectedError is unassertable, so no guard can be tested for its own failure
description:

  ci/flakeModule.nix:107  counts them
  `expectedError` -> 0 hits anywhere in the gen hub

⇒ `checks.default` is a HOMEGROWN ASSERTER, not nix-unit. nix-unit's `expectedError` is therefore
UNASSERTABLE through the default gate: a test that should verify a specific failure message has no way to
express it, and writing one crashes the gate rather than failing it.

The features memory parks this TWICE (lines 415-418 and 446) as an owner item. Bead scan for
"expectedError"/"assertTests" -> 0. Observed twice, tracked never — the same pattern as the (Task N) sweep.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ERGONOMICS: a gate that cannot assert an expected FAILURE can only test happy paths.
Every guard whose whole purpose is to abort for a named reason is untestable through the default gate — and
this project's standing rule is that a guard must be proven to fail FOR ITS OWN REASON before a pass is
trusted. So this defect directly weakens the discipline the arc relies on most.

ACCEPTANCE: `expectedError` assertable through checks.default (either by routing to nix-unit or by the
homegrown asserter growing the capability), with a witness that goes red when the expected message changes —
or an owner ruling that the dual gate is intentional, recorded WITH ITS REASON.
