comments.text:
★ NEW TRAP, ORCHESTRATOR-CAUSED — I DISPATCHED AN AGENT AGAINST A REPO I WAS CONCURRENTLY COMMITTING TO, AND SUPPLIED LINE NUMBERS FROM A DIRTY WORKING TREE THAT MATCHED NO COMMITTED STATE. 2026-07-28.

WHAT HAPPENED: I briefed a redesign agent with 'Repo at HEAD a40cc96' and a citation 'fired at structural.nix:309-382'. While it worked, I committed ec6ba23 to that same tree. The agent measured and reported:
  - HEAD had ADVANCED to ec6ba23 mid-revision;
  - at DISPATCH the tree was DIRTY (lib/errors.nix and lib/attributes/structural.nix modified, ci/tests/b1-supportedness.nix untracked);
  - ★ my ':309-382' RANGE BELONGED TO NEITHER STATE — at a40cc96 the block is :302-334 firing at :316/:325, and :382 is the NEW HEAD's number. I HAD READ THE DIRTY WORKING TREE AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO A COMMIT.
The agent recovered correctly by anchoring every read to `git show a40cc96:` so its citations matched the spec's declared measured tree, and recorded the drift in the spec header.

⇒ TWO DISTINCT RULES, and the second is the one I did not know:
1. A BRIEF'S REPO ANCHOR IS A MEASUREMENT AND IT EXPIRES — especially when the orchestrator is ALSO the one committing. Re-measure HEAD at the moment of dispatch, and say whether the tree is clean.
2. ★ NEVER TAKE A LINE NUMBER FROM A DIRTY WORKING TREE FOR A BRIEF THAT NAMES A COMMIT. Reading the tree gives you the WORKING state; naming a rev promises the COMMITTED one. The two silently differ exactly when you are mid-change, which is exactly when briefs get written. If the brief names a rev, read with `git show <rev>:<path>` — not with the editor.
★ THE FAILURE IS INVISIBLE FROM EITHER SIDE ALONE: the line number was real (I had just read it) and the rev was real (it existed), so nothing about the brief looks wrong. Only someone holding both discovers they do not correspond. This is the stale-anchor family — four incidents now, all orchestrator-caused — but the previous three were about a FROZEN ARTEFACT drifting; this one is about a CITATION belonging to no state that ever existed on disk under that name.

SELF-CAUGHT? NO — caught by the agent, because the brief told it to treat my facts as refutable. That instruction has now caught orchestrator errors in five consecutive dispatches and should be considered mandatory rather than good practice.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NEW CASE — A SELF-REFUTATION IS STILL A CLAIM, AND THIS ONE WAS FALSE. THE ORIGINAL SENTENCE WAS RIGHT. 2026-07-28.

SEQUENCE:
 1. An author drafted a coverage bound: 'no test fires a declared slice through runPrePass'.
 2. It then CAUGHT ITSELF and reported that as FALSE — ci/tests/compat-hm-battery.nix:80's `env-users` is in both compat tables, so (it reasoned) it must be a declared slice in the feed. I recorded this as the most valuable item of the round and PROPAGATED IT INTO TWO BEADS.
 3. An independent confirmation pass REPRODUCED IT AND REFUTED THE REFUTATION. `env-users` is NOT a declared slice: its body emits at the VALUE-LESS PROBE, so `mkRules` takes `!expanded` → `mkSingle`, and `producesByName` IS NEVER READ. That is the spec's own D11 case (concern-policies.nix:358-374).
 ⇒ THE ORIGINAL DRAFT SENTENCE WAS CORRECT. The 'correction' inverted it, and I amplified the inversion.

HOW IT WAS SETTLED — a branch discriminator with a same-run positive control, run through the real compat desugar with the fixture body verbatim:
  A = fixture body + REAL table  → 1 rule, produces=["member"], structural, in feed
  B = fixture body + EMPTY table → IDENTICAL ⇒ THE TABLE IS NOT CONSULTED
  C = value-conditional twin + REAL table  → 1 rule, produces=["member"]
  D = value-conditional twin + EMPTY table → 3 fan rules, produces all NULL
C ≠ D proves the instrument CAN see the table being consulted; A ≡ B proves it is not. Plus a live abort on the mkDen path reachable ONLY on the !expanded branch, and a counterfactual control where the value-conditional twin silently drops instead.

★★ AND THE DEEPER FAULT — THE SUB-ARGUMENT THAT JUSTIFIED THE 'CORRECTION' USED A PREDICATE THAT COULD NOT DISCRIMINATE. The author argued: 'if the key did not match, `resolveFamilyUntagged` would abort this fixture, and the suite is green.' MEASURED FALSE: on the `!expanded` branch `rfOf = explicitRF || any isResolveFamily probeActs` (concern-policies.nix:377-382), so THE PROBE'S OWN `member` TAGS IT REGARDLESS OF NAME. Renaming to `zz-not-in-either-table` still runs green — measured.
⇒ THIS IS THE PREDICATE-BLINDNESS FAILURE ONE LEVEL DOWN FROM THE ONE IT CAUGHT. The author correctly refused a tempting absence claim, then justified the refusal with an instrument that would have been silent either way. Catching a trap does not immunise the correction against the same trap.

STANDING RULES THIS EARNS:
 (1) ★ A SELF-REPORTED CATCH IS STILL A CLAIM AND MUST BE RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY. It arrives with maximum credibility — the agent looks rigorous precisely because it corrected itself — which is exactly why it should be checked. Put 'verify the self-caught items independently; a self-reported catch is still a claim' in every confirmation brief. Here that instruction was present and is the only reason this was caught.
 (2) A CORRECTION NEEDS THE SAME EVIDENCE BAR AS THE CLAIM IT CORRECTS, INCLUDING A DISCRIMINATING CONTROL. 'X would have aborted and the suite is green' is only evidence if X CAN abort for that reason — prove the predicate discriminates before resting a retraction on it.
 (3) ORCHESTRATOR FAULT, MINE: I amplified a self-refutation into two bead comments within minutes of receiving it, WITHOUT re-deriving it, because it was framed as the agent's own honest catch. Honesty about method is not evidence about facts.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ TWO NEW TRAPS FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW, PLUS A CONFIRMATION THAT AN EXISTING ONE IS STRONGER THAN RECORDED. 2026-07-28.

★ (1) AN UNTRACKED FILE IS INVISIBLE TO A GIT FLAKE, AND THE RESULT IS A FALSE PASS THAT LOOKS LIKE A FULL RUN.
The reviewer's first probe added a test file, ran the suite, and got 1922/1922 — the SAME COUNT as the unmodified tree. The file was untracked, so the flake never saw it: ZERO tests were added and the run reported complete success. `git add` fixed it.
⇒ THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND FLATTERING: no error, no warning, and the total is a number you were expecting anyway. Any claim of the form 'I added a witness and the suite is green' is UNFALSIFIED until the COUNT MOVES. This composes with nix-unit's `test` name-prefix detection, where a bare-leaf target silently reports 0/0 — two independent ways to run zero tests and be told everything passed.
STANDING FORM: after adding a fixture, assert the TOTAL CHANGED, not that the suite is green.

★ (2) `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` IS EMPTY UNDER ZSH — THE SHELL THIS SESSION USES. zsh spells it `$pipestatus` (lowercase array). So the standing 'runner | tail masks failure' warning is STRONGER than recorded: in zsh the usual bash workaround does not merely mislead, IT RETURNS NOTHING AT ALL, and a careless reader treats empty as success. I hit this myself earlier tonight and so did the reviewer independently.
STANDING FORM: redirect to a file and read `$?` IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT to the command. Do not use PIPESTATUS in this environment.

(3) CONFIRMATION, and it is the reason the review's verdict can be trusted: the four red witnesses all failed with `got false, expected true` — i.e. NO ABORT OCCURRED. ★ THE DIRECTION OF FAILURE IS ITSELF THE PROOF THAT THEY FAIL FOR THE INTENDED GUARD'S REASON: had an EARLIER guard aborted first, the assertion would have been satisfied and the test would have PASSED — a false green. So a red here cannot be another guard's red. That is a stronger discharge than the usual 'point it at a case only this guard can catch', and it is available whenever the assertion is 'this aborts'.

(4) COST NON-REPRODUCTION, recorded as method rather than as a defect: the commit's +0.48% came from a corpus workload; a fixture-free-by-construction workload (a SEPARATE FLAKE that cannot import the fixtures) showed −0.09%. Both negligible, neither refuted. ★ The lesson is that 'fixture-free' is best obtained BY CONSTRUCTION — choosing a workload that structurally cannot contain the guard's own fixtures — rather than by excluding them from a workload that could.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NEW TRAP — **TOTALITY IS NOT AGREEMENT**, and the distinction is invisible because both are checked with the word 'total'. 2026-07-28.

A design adopted `gen-graph.transpose` and wrote that the node-domain choice 'is not free: it is TOTAL for transpose/cycles/reachableFrom'. TRUE — none of the three aborts on an unregistered channel. AND IT DID NOT MEAN WHAT IT WAS USED TO MEAN: `transpose` materialises via `genAttrs nodes`, so an edge whose SOURCE lies outside the declared node set IS NEVER MATERIALISED. With `[A→X, X→B]` and `X ∉ Ch`, both oracles (today's fold AND the retired path enumeration) land the content at B; the query SILENTLY DROPS IT.
⇒ A PRIMITIVE CAN BE TOTAL ON YOUR DOMAIN — answers every input, never throws — AND STILL BE UNFAITHFUL, returning a DIFFERENT ANSWER than the construct it replaces. 'Does it abort?' and 'does it agree?' are DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, and only the second needs an oracle. The design asked the first and recorded the answer using a word that reads as if it had asked both.

★ AND THE ARM THAT HID IT IS THE GENERAL LESSON. Unregistered TARGET and unregistered SOURCE were BOTH measured and BOTH byte-identical — so the domain looked cleared, by two measurements, correctly taken. The divergence needs an unregistered channel IN THE MIDDLE, which is a two-hop shape, and no one-hop probe can reach it. §6 had the right instrument aimed at the right domain AND STOPPED ONE HOP SHORT.
⇒ WHEN ENUMERATING ARMS OVER A RELATION, THE ENDPOINTS ARE NOT THE ENUMERATION. Include the arms with something in the middle: an intermediate, a chain, a shape where the property must SURVIVE A HOP rather than merely hold locally. This is the same family as 'a fixture that only tests a single-route policy cannot distinguish three readings' — a case analysis that covers the easy positions and misses the one where composition happens.

RELATED AND ALREADY RECORDED: the FIRST thing this same adoption lost was ACYCLICITY, which a `seen`-threaded recursion enforced for free and a `genericClosure` does not — that one the design DID catch. So one library swap silently dropped TWO structural guarantees, one found and one missed, and the found one did not prompt a search for the other. ★ FINDING ONE LOST INVARIANT SHOULD TRIGGER A SWEEP FOR MORE, not satisfaction that the swap was audited.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NEW CASE — I INHERITED A LINE NUMBER FROM A  COPY AND PROPAGATED IT THROUGH THREE BRIEFS. This is the trap I put in every dispatch, and I am the one who fell into it. 2026-07-28.

I briefed `fireFeedAt` as `lib/staged-resolution.nix:185-204` — in the C9 finding on den-hoag-9xo.54, in the P1 spec brief, and in the selection-implementation brief. MEASURED AT HEAD: it is **:145-152**, with its two feed bindings at **:153-155**.
★ THE RANGE I QUOTED IS A WORKTREE COPY'S NUMBERING. den-hoag has four worktrees, two pinned at an older rev; the copies of these files differ by ROUGHLY 40 LINES, and **AN UNEXCLUDED grep RETURNS BOTH SETS INTERLEAVED** — so a plausible-looking line number is available for the same symbol at two different offsets, and nothing in the output says which tree it came from.

⇒ THE STANDING RULE 'EXCLUDE .worktrees/' IS NOT ONLY ABOUT STALE CONTENT CONFIRMING A STALE CLAIM. IT IS ALSO ABOUT LINE NUMBERS: an unexcluded search over a repo with worktrees produces citations that are internally consistent, individually plausible, and attributable to no tree the reader has. That is worse than a wrong number, because it survives a spot-check against the wrong file.
★ AND IT COMPOSES WITH THE EARLIER TRAP IN THIS LOG: 'never take a line number from a dirty working tree for a brief that names a commit'. Both produce a citation belonging to no state anyone can reproduce. The general form is now: **A LINE NUMBER IS ONLY MEANINGFUL WITH ITS TREE. Cite `git show <rev>:<path>`, or cite the expression rather than the line.**
NOTE ALSO the register (den-hoag-4kh.17) has ALREADY had three different line ranges asserted for one strip list, none of which held — the same disease at the same site. The fix recorded there was to cite by EXPRESSION rather than by line, and this case is the second independent argument for it.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT: the P1 spec author re-derived every cited site at c42df53 instead of inheriting them, and noticed the interleave. That instruction — treat the brief's facts as refutable — has now caught an orchestrator error in FOURTEEN consecutive dispatches, and this is the second where the error was a citation I had passed on from an earlier agent's report without re-deriving it.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ SMALL INSTRUMENT TRAP, MINE, 2026-07-28 — BACKTICKS IN A DOUBLE-QUOTED SHELL STRING ARE COMMAND-SUBSTITUTED.
I posted a bead comment using an inline double-quoted string containing markdown backticks around identifiers
(`den.systems`, `fleet-demo`). The shell executed them: "command not found: den.systems". The bd call still
SUCCEEDED and reported success, so the failure was visible only as two stray lines above a green result — and
the comment landed with its text silently altered.
⇒ RULE: ANY bd comment or commit message containing backticks MUST go through a QUOTED heredoc
(`<<'EOF'`) or --body-file, never an inline double-quoted string. I use heredocs for long content by habit and
inline strings for short ones; the length is irrelevant — the BACKTICK is the trigger, and technical prose in
this project is full of them.
★ AND THE DANGEROUS PART IS THE PARTIAL SUCCESS: the tool reports success because the tool succeeded. Only the
CONTENT was corrupted, and nothing downstream re-reads it. Same family as the other entries here — a signal
that cannot distinguish two states, read as though it can.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NEW INSTRUMENT TRAP, MEASURED 2026-07-29, AND IT IS THE FLATTERING KIND (same family as entry 7): THE codebase-memory COMPLEXITY METRICS ARE STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE OF FIRING ON NIX, AND THEY REPORT THE KERNEL CLEAN.

QUERY RUN: query_graph over project den-hoag —
  MATCH (f:Function) WHERE (f.linear_scan_in_loop >= 1 OR f.transitive_loop_depth >= 3 OR f.recursion_in_loop >= 1 OR f.unguarded_recursion = true) AND NOT f.file_path CONTAINS '.worktrees' RETURN ... ORDER BY f.linear_scan_in_loop DESC, f.transitive_loop_depth DESC
RESULT: 6 rows. linear_scan_in_loop = 0 for EVERY den-hoag Nix function. loop_depth = 0, alloc_in_loop = 0, transitive_loop_depth = 0 for every one.

THE SAME SESSION HAD ALREADY MEASURED, BY READING, AT LEAST THREE QUADRATIC LINEAR-SCAN-IN-LOOP SITES:
  gen-prelude unique = foldl' (acc: x: if elem x acc then acc else acc ++ [ x ]) [ ] — elem is a linear scan INSIDE the fold, and acc ++ [x] copies the accumulator every element. SIXTEEN den-hoag kernel call sites.
  gen-algebra foldLayersTraced's semilattice-set strategy — foldl' (acc: e: foldl' (a2: x: if builtins.elem x a2 then a2 else a2 ++ [ x ]) acc e.layer.${name}) ..., O(m^2).
  den-hoag's own whole-pool filter-per-kind sites (inverseRelationEdges, reverseByKind, projectedByKind, edgesBelowStratum) plus contentIdsOf's |classes| x |allNodeIds| scan.
NONE APPEARED. The metric did not under-report them; it reported ZERO.

★ POSITIVE CONTROL, UNASKED-FOR AND IN THE SAME RESULT SET — which is what makes this diagnosable rather than merely disappointing: the ONLY row carrying non-zero loop metrics is a PYTHON file. parity/tools/order-equivalence-check.py main: loop_depth 1, transitive_loop_depth 3, alloc_in_loop 1, complexity 5. The instrument WORKS. It works on Python.

MECHANISM: the detectors key on LOOP SYNTAX (for/while). NIX HAS NONE. Every loop in this codebase is a higher-order call — foldl', filter, concatMap, genAttrs, mapAttrs — so a scan nested inside a fold is, to this extractor, two ordinary function applications. The five properties loop_depth, transitive_loop_depth, linear_scan_in_loop, alloc_in_loop and recursion_in_loop are therefore ALL vacuous on Nix.
(The unguarded_recursion flag DID fire — 5 rows, one in lib/compat/namespace.nix stampNode and four in ci fixtures — so that ONE property is live and is the reason the query returned rows at all. Do not generalise from it to the others.)

⇒ CONSEQUENCE, and it is the whole reason this belongs in the trap log: A COMPLEXITY AUDIT ROUTED THROUGH THIS QUERY RETURNS A CLEAN BILL FOR THE EXACT FILES THAT CONTAIN THE QUADRATICS. It is fast, it is authoritative-looking, it is ORDER BY'd so it looks ranked, and it is wrong in the direction nobody re-checks. Per entry 7: a trap that flatters is worse than one that fails, because a pleasant result is not re-measured.
⇒ RULE: NEVER SOURCE A NIX COMPLEXITY OR HOT-PATH CLAIM FROM codebase-memory's loop metrics. Read the source, or grep for the shape (elem/hasAttr/filter INSIDE foldl'/concatMap/genAttrs). This joins the two already-recorded codebase-memory gaps — the languages field omitting Nix, and CALLS missing attrset-mediated calls — and the three together mean the index is usable for WHAT EXISTS and for CLUSTERING, and for nothing that decides correctness or cost.

★ WHAT THE INDEX *DID* ANSWER WELL IN THE SAME RUN, recorded so this is not read as a blanket rejection: get_architecture(aspects=[clusters,boundaries,layers], path=lib) returned 12 Leiden clusters over 1,181 scoped nodes / 3,414 edges with cohesion 0.83-1.00, and the de-facto seams it found match the census's hand-read module structure — cluster 13 (mkDen;runPrePass;mintedRootId;buildRoots;ancNodeId) is the fleet-construction stage, cluster 16 (classSliceOf;remapOver;routeRemapFor;projectClass) the class projection, cluster 130 (mkGather;exposeEdgesFor;gatherMarkWith;denQuery;allNodeIds) the query/gather surface. It also placed default and output as 'core, high fan-in, 0 out' and staged-resolution/outputs/concern-relations as 'entry, only outbound' — a structural picture consistent with the read. STRUCTURE: TRUSTWORTHY. COST AND REACHABILITY: NOT.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ NEW INSTRUMENT TRAP, MEASURED 2026-07-29, AND IT SILENTLY DEFEATS EVERY CITATION AUDIT OF THE BEAD GRAPH: **bd show's TEXT output HARD-WRAPS AT ~78 COLUMNS AND SPLITS path:NNN TOKENS ACROSS LINES.**

OBSERVED: an agent auditing 74 bead descriptions for file:line citations grepped the TEXT output of bd show and got ONE HIT ACROSS ALL 74 BEADS. The beads demonstrably contain dozens. The wrap breaks 'lib/compat/ingest.nix:243' mid-token, so no regex for a path-colon-number pattern can match, and the result is a CLEAN ZERO rather than an error.
FIX: 'bd show <id> --json --include-comments' is UNWRAPPED. Audit from JSON, never from the rendered text.
★ CLASSIFICATION: this is the FLATTERING kind (entry 7's family). 'Zero citations found across the inventory' reads as 'this inventory has no file:line anchors to check' — a tidy, plausible, actionable-looking finding — when the truth is the instrument could not see them. Nobody re-measures a clean result.
★ AND IT COMPOSES WITH A KNOWN LIMIT ALREADY IN THIS LOG: the multi-line-conjunction trap. Both are cases of a TEXT RENDERER changing the token stream the predicate runs against. GENERAL FORM WORTH STATING ONCE: NEVER RUN A STRUCTURED-DATA PREDICATE OVER A HUMAN-FORMATTED RENDERING. Ask the tool for its machine format, or read the range.

★★ A SECOND, INDEPENDENT LESSON FROM THE SAME RUN, AND IT IS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ERROR: I DISPATCHED THAT AUDIT ON A PREMISE THAT WAS FALSE, AND THE PREMISE WAS MINE TO CHECK. I stated that den-hoag-4kh.53's inventory 'audited c42df53, three commits behind HEAD, two of which are 222af84 and e6c8edc'. MEASURED, and re-derived by me after the agent refuted it:
    git merge-base --is-ancestor 222af84 c42df53 -> TRUE   (also ec6ba23, 6f472d3 -> TRUE)
    git merge-base --is-ancestor e6c8edc c42df53 -> FALSE
    git log --oneline c42df53..HEAD -- ':!.beads' -> e6c8edc  (ONE line)
c42df53 IS ITSELF A chore(beads) EXPORT, and it sits AFTER 222af84. The audit baseline ALREADY CONTAINED the class-content query, the ABW supportedness fix and the closure-equality repair. ONE code commit is post-baseline, not three.
⇒ I inherited that framing from a prior agent's report and passed it into a dispatch WITHOUT RUNNING merge-base, which is one command. It sent an agent hunting expiry in territory the baseline already covered. ★ THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN THIS ARC AN ORCHESTRATOR HAS AMPLIFIED AN AUTHOR'S FRAMING WITHOUT TESTING ITS PREMISE, and the second time TODAY. The standing rule 'state every brief's fact as REFUTABLE' worked exactly as designed — the agent refuted it in its first paragraph — but the rule is a BACKSTOP, not a substitute for checking a one-command claim before spending an agent on it.
GENERAL FORM: A COMMIT ORDERING IS NOT A FACT ABOUT A COMMIT MESSAGE. 'Three commits behind' and 'behind which three' are different claims, and a chore/export commit interleaved in the log makes the second one unguessable from the first.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ TWO ENTRIES FROM ONE RUN, 2026-07-29 — and the first is an agent catching its OWN false result before reporting it, which is the outcome this log exists to make normal.

ENTRY A — A SOUND PREDICATE PROVING A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION, CAUGHT IN FLIGHT.
An agent establishing the error TYPE of den-hoag's compose-commitment failures first probed via
builtins.getFlake "path:.../den-hoag/ci" under --impure. The ci flake's own den-hoag.url = "path:.." input
DOES NOT RESOLVE THAT WAY, so the probe actually threw 'flake.nix' is too short to be a valid store path.
nix-unit dutifully reported that error's type as `Error`.
★ THE WRITE-UP IT ALMOST PRODUCED: "the module system downgrades ThrownError to Error." Plausible,
mechanistic, and completely false — it would have measured the PROBE HARNESS and reported it as a fact about
the kernel. The predicate was sound (nix-unit really did catch an error and really did report its type); it
proved a different proposition than the sentence being written.
IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BECAUSE the agent had supplied a DELIBERATELY WRONG msg, which made nix-unit PRINT THE
TEXT IT ACTUALLY CAUGHT — and the text was the flake-path error, not the kernel's. The re-probe against
errors.opsInBody directly and through lib.evalModules gave ThrownError both ways.

★ ENTRY B — THE TECHNIQUE, WHICH IS THE GENERALISABLE PART: WHEN ASSERTING WHAT AN INSTRUMENT CAUGHT,
DELIBERATELY SUPPLY A NON-MATCHING EXPECTATION SO THE INSTRUMENT PRINTS WHAT IT ACTUALLY SAW.
A matching assertion returns only PASS, which is compatible with having measured the wrong thing entirely.
A deliberately-wrong one returns the OBSERVED VALUE, which is the evidence. This is the same shape as the
positive-control rule, applied to identity rather than to existence: a control proves the instrument CAN
fire; a wrong-expectation read-out proves WHAT it fired ON.
Concrete payoff in the same run: the compose-commitment message is a TEMPLATE with an interpolated policy
name. Transcribing it from lib/errors.nix source would have produced the template; reading it out of the
instrument produced the ELEVEN DISTINCT INTERPOLATIONS that actually reach nix-unit — which is the
difference between "no msg regex can distinguish these twelve" (what the orchestrator asserted) and "a msg
regex distinguishes eleven of twelve" (what is true).
⇒ ADOPT AS STANDARD for any claim of the form "X raises error E with message M".

ENTRY C — A SMALLER ONE, SAME RUN, WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT INVALIDATES CACHED KNOWLEDGE:
THE LOCAL gen CLONE IS AHEAD OF THE PINNED REV AND IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE. ci/flake.lock pins gen at 793f83f
(store path z2zkagz7ny8j4r75f9pwx9fr3ir5x9x6-source); the local working clone sits at cb10282.
MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: testSingletons EXISTS at the local clone and DOES NOT EXIST at the locked rev, so
#testSingletons.<suite>.<test> single-test targeting is UNAVAILABLE until the ci lock is bumped, and
#tests.<suite> is the finest granularity that runs.
★ GENERAL FORM: READING A DEPENDENCY FROM ITS LOCAL CLONE MEASURES A DIFFERENT ARTEFACT THAN THE ONE THE
BUILD USES. Every gen-library claim in this project must name which it read — clone or locked rev — and a
capability found in the clone is not a capability available to the build.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ MEASURED 2026-07-29 — `grep` IN THIS SHELL IS NOT `grep`, AND ITS COUNTS DIFFER FROM THE REAL BINARY'S
BY UP TO 10x. Every count-based claim in this project is affected unless it names its binary.

WHAT IT IS: `type grep` → "grep is a shell function from ~/.claude/shell-snapshots/snapshot-zsh-*.sh".
It wraps ugrep with ignore-file handling. The real GNU binary is `/run/current-system/sw/bin/grep`.

MEASURED, den-hoag at HEAD, each figure from a command, both runs reproducible:

  RECURSING FROM `.` — THE WRAPPER HONOURS .gitignore AND THE REAL BINARY DOES NOT:
    grep   -rn 'tryEval' .   | grep -c worktrees  ->   14      (twice, identical)
    REAL   -rn 'tryEval' .   | grep -c worktrees  ->  436
    grep   -rn 'removeAttrs' . | grep -c worktrees ->    9
    REAL   -rn 'removeAttrs' . | grep -c worktrees ->   92
    TOTAL LINES, same pattern from `.`:  wrapper 340  vs  real 762
  `.worktrees/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:4`), which is the bulk of the gap here.

  NAMING THE IGNORED PATH EXPLICITLY — THEY AGREE EXACTLY:
    files under .worktrees/ :  wrapper 174  real 174
    lines under .worktrees/ :  wrapper 422  real 422
    single file, ci/tests/edge-substrate.nix : -n 27/27, -c 27/27
  So the wrapper searches an explicitly-named ignored path and skips it during `.` recursion. Standard
  ugrep --ignore-files behaviour, and INVISIBLE unless you compare against the real binary.

★ THE OPERATIONAL RULE, and it is narrower and more useful than "grep is broken":
  1. AN ABSENCE CLAIM CARRYING A POSITIVE CONTROL IS STILL SOUND. If the control fired in the same run, the
     instrument fired. The wrapper does not fail to match; it searches a SMALLER TREE.
  2. ★ A COUNT IS ONLY COMPARABLE TO ANOTHER COUNT TAKEN WITH THE SAME BINARY, THE SAME FLAGS AND THE SAME
     PATH ARGUMENT. Two figures in one report, one from `.` and one from an explicit path, ARE NOT
     COMPARABLE — and that is exactly how a "wrapper under-reports" story gets constructed or refuted.
  3. FOR ANY COUNT REPORTED AS EVIDENCE, INVOKE `/run/current-system/sw/bin/grep` EXPLICITLY, or state the
     wrapper and the path form. Naming the tree you searched is now part of naming the predicate.
  4. WHAT THE WRAPPER SILENTLY EXCLUDES IS ALSO WHAT WE USUALLY WANT EXCLUDED (`.worktrees/`, build output).
     So it has been FLATTERING us: the exclusion discipline this project enforces by hand was partly being
     applied for free, which means some `.worktrees/`-exclusion positive controls were confirming something
     already true rather than a filter doing work.

★★ AND A CLAIM ABOUT THIS HAZARD WAS ITSELF PARTLY WRONG — recorded because it is the same lesson twice.
An agent reported: "`command grep` and `/usr/bin/grep` BOTH fail on NixOS — and every count printed 0 from
command-not-found, indistinguishable from an absence."
MEASURED: `command grep -c ... ` → 10, EXIT 0. IT WORKS. `/usr/bin/grep` → "no such file or directory",
EXIT 127, WITH a message on stderr — NOT a silent zero.
THE SILENT ZERO IS REAL BUT REQUIRES A SECOND MISTAKE: `/usr/bin/grep -c X f 2>/dev/null | wc -l` → 0.
Suppressing stderr, or piping a failed command into `wc -l`, is what converts a loud 127 into a quiet 0.
⇒ THE HAZARD IS NOT "the binary is missing", IT IS "2>/dev/null CONVERTS A MISSING INSTRUMENT INTO AN
ABSENCE FINDING". That generalises far beyond grep and belongs in the standing rules: NEVER DISCARD STDERR
ON A MEASUREMENT COMMAND. The error text is part of the measurement.

★ ORCHESTRATOR NOTE ON MY OWN FIRST PASS: my initial verification produced 48 worktree lines where the
re-run produced 14, and an `-rl` comparison that showed NO difference where `-rn` showed a large one. I
nearly recorded "the wrapper caps matches per file" from it. RE-DERIVING BEFORE WRITING is what stopped a
third wrong version of this entry from entering the log — after the agent's version and my own. A hazard
report is a claim like any other, and this one took three attempts to state correctly.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ FOUR FLATTERING RESULTS HIT LIVE IN ONE CALIBRATION SESSION, 2026-07-29 — each would have been written
up as a den-hoag finding, and each was caught only because the author was building an instrument and
therefore distrusting his own arms. This is the largest single harvest this log has taken.

(a) A SOUND FORCE OF A NONEXISTENT OBSERVABLE. `den.systems` is `[ ]` on a native fleet. Forcing it measured
    4,034 calls FLAT at H in {2,4,8,16,32}, BYTE-IDENTICAL with and without a policy declared. Perfect
    flatness, perfectly reproducible, and about nothing at all.

(b) A HOT SITE MEASURED AS FREE BECAUSE THE FIXTURE NEVER DECLARED THE FEATURE. `relAt` on a fleet declaring
    NO relations: nrOpUpdateValuesCopied FLAT at 976, and ★ THE ARM CAME OUT CHEAPER THAN THE PLAIN NODE
    ARM. den-hoag-ag3's hot site, measured as free. A fixture that does not exercise the feature reports the
    feature as costless — and reports it CONFIDENTLY.

(c) ★ THE HARNESS WAS THE WORKLOAD. Probe v1's result string interpolated `builtins.length ids`, so the arm
    named force="none" — THE FLOOR — enumerated every node: 1,205,900 calls for an arm whose entire purpose
    was to force nothing. Every per-field decomposition built on that floor (relAt targets / closure / paths)
    was three views of one shared cost. Caught by making the reporter a CONSTANT, after which the floor
    dropped to ONE call. ⇒ THE REPORTER IS PART OF THE WORKLOAD. Any harness that formats its own result
    must be measured with the formatting removed.

(d) ★★★ TWO SPELLINGS OF "THE NODE SET", ONE LINEAR AND ONE CUBIC, SAME FIXTURE AND SAME CLEAN HARNESS:
        attrNames den.scopeRoots               -> 6081 6181 6381 6781 7581 9181  = EXACTLY 2x PER DOUBLING
        attrNames den.structural.eval.allNodes -> CUBIC
    `scopeRoots` EXCLUDES CELLS, and the entire cost lives in the cell path. Both are defensible readings of
    "enumerate the nodes"; one is textbook linear and one is the worst scaling defect in the project.
    ⇒ ★ AN ARM NAMED FOR A CONCEPT RATHER THAN MEASURED AGAINST A DECLARED SHAPE PICKS THE FLATTERING
    SPELLING ABOUT HALF THE TIME. This is the deepest version of the predicate-blindness law: the predicate
    was sound, the binding existed, the numbers were real — and it answered a different question than the
    one whose name it carried. Remedy adopted in the spec: `expectedShape` is REQUIRED per arm and must be
    ANALYTIC (it may not read `den`), so an arm must state what it believes it is enumerating and be checked
    against it.

★ AND THE FIFTH, WHICH IS THE INVERSE AND VALIDATES THE RULE: the policy-dispatch arm ABORTED at every rung
(`narrow accessor (A10): aspect 'app' is not present at scope 'env:prod'`) — a defect in the FIXTURE. Under
a tryEval-lowered harness those five rungs would have produced FLAT, CHEAP, PLAUSIBLE ROWS: a clean linear
result from an arm that measured nothing. ⇒ AN ARM THAT DOES NOT EXIT 0 IS A FAILURE, NEVER A DATAPOINT.
This is the same family as the tryEval-discards-the-message defects already logged, arriving through a
performance harness instead of a test.

★ ONE COUNTER-FACT WORTH KEEPING, because it bounds what any counter-based instrument can ever see: WORK
INSIDE A PRIMOP IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY COUNTER. `elem`-in-a-fold over n distinct elements is O(n^2) yet
nrPrimOpCalls grows LINEARLY (15 -> 325). ⇒ gen-prelude `unique`'s quadratic COMPARISONS (den-hoag-4kh.53.47)
ARE UNOBSERVABLE by this instrument; only its allocation half is. By contrast G22's toJSON IS visible (100
calls -> 103 primops, 200 -> 203), so its call COUNT is gateable and its payload growth is not.
⇒ A COUNTER-BASED SCALING GATE CANNOT SEE INSIDE A PRIMOP. State that hole wherever the witness is cited,
or someone will read a green scaling gate as evidence that `unique` is fine.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ THE MOST DANGEROUS INSTRUMENT RESULT YET RECORDED HERE: A COUNTER-BASED SCALING GATE DOES NOT GO BLIND
ON PRIMOP-INTERNAL COST — IT ISSUES A CONVERGED FALSE GREEN CERTIFICATE. Measured 2026-07-29 by an
adversarial reviewer of the scaling-witness spec, on its own closed counter set.

THE WORKLOAD: a Theta(n^2)-COMPARISON workload with O(1) ALLOCATION —
    foldl' (acc: x: acc + (if elem x xs then 1 else 0)) 0 xs
run beside a LINEAR REFERENCE OF THE SAME SHAPE, against EVERY counter the spec declares:
    counter                    quadratic        linear reference
    nrFunctionCalls            31 -> 961        31 -> 961   ★ IDENTICAL
    list.elements              13 -> 323        13 -> 323   ★ IDENTICAL
    nrPrimOpCalls              15 -> 325        5 flat
    sets.elements              136 flat         136 flat
    nrThunks                   7 flat           7 flat
    nrOpUpdateValuesCopied     0                0
EVERY COUNTER <= 2x PER DOUBLING. Under the spec's own decision rule: CONVERGED, p_top <= maxExponent, both
controls recovered ⇒ **PASS**.
⇒ THE SPEC SAID SUCH COST IS "UNOBSERVABLE". IT IS WORSE THAN UNOBSERVABLE: IT IS OBSERVABLE AS LINEAR, WITH
A CONVERGED CERTIFICATE. Silence would prompt someone to look. A green certificate stops them.

★★ AND IT LANDS ON A DEFECT THIS PROJECT HAS ALREADY BEEN BITTEN BY. `builtins.match ".*zzz.*"` over a string
growing 32x -> nrPrimOpCalls FLAT AT 6, every other counter flat or tracking the fixture. den-hoag and the
gen libraries had CI stack overflows caused by nixpkgs `lib.hasInfix` regex, fixed ecosystem-wide via
genPrelude.hasInfix. ⇒ **THE WITNESS WOULD CERTIFY A hasInfix-SHAPED BLOWUP AS LINEAR.** A regression of the
exact class already suffered would pass the gate built to catch scaling defects.

★ AND THE SAME ALGORITHM IS VISIBLE OR INVISIBLE DEPENDING ON SPELLING:
    builtins.sort builtins.lessThan   -> comparisons INVISIBLE (nrFunctionCalls 11 -> 321, just the genList)
    builtins.sort (a: b: a < b)       -> comparisons VISIBLE   (-> 961)
Identical algorithm, identical complexity, opposite observability — decided by whether the comparator is a
primop or a Nix lambda. This is the two-spellings-of-the-node-set disease in the COUNTER dimension, and it
means an author can make a quadratic invisible without intending to, simply by reaching for the builtin.
MINOR BUT REAL: `nrFunctionCalls` for the lambda-sort is NON-MONOTONIC (101 at n=10, 61 at n=20, reproduced
2/2), so log2(m2/m1) goes NEGATIVE. Any successive-ratio estimator assumes monotonicity and nothing enforces
it.

★★ THE GENERAL LAW, and it is stronger than the existing entries because it is about a class of instrument
rather than a single predicate: **A COUNTER MEASURES WHAT THE EVALUATOR DID, NOT WHAT THE ALGORITHM COST.**
Work performed INSIDE a primop is real work that no counter attributes to anyone. So:
  · A GREEN COUNTER-BASED SCALING RESULT IS EVIDENCE ONLY ABOUT NIX-LEVEL WORK. It says nothing about
    comparisons, regex backtracking, string scanning, sorting via a builtin comparator, or anything else
    that happens below the evaluator.
  · gen-prelude's `unique` is the live example: its O(n^2) COMPARISONS are unobservable while its O(n^2)
    ALLOCATION is visible. Half the defect is gateable and half is not, and the gateable half is the half
    that is cheaper to fix.
⇒ ANY CITATION OF A SCALING WITNESS MUST CARRY THIS HOLE EXPLICITLY. A green gate read as "the fleet is
linear" is a category error; it means "no Nix-level superlinearity was detected in the arms declared".
EOF

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ A VERIFICATION PREDICATE THAT CANNOT DETECT AN OVER-APPLICATION OF ITS OWN SUBSTITUTION. Measured
2026-07-29, and the defect was MINE.

WHAT HAPPENED. Eight comments were being corrected from "Mokhov 2017 §4.3" to "§5". I then upgraded them to
the precise "§5.2" with:
    sed -i 's/Mokhov 2017 §5\b/Mokhov 2017 §5.2/g'
★ `\b` IS A WORD BOUNDARY, AND ONE SITS BETWEEN `5` AND `.`. So on a file an agent had ALREADY corrected to
`§5.2`, the pattern matched the `§5` INSIDE IT and produced **`§5.2.2`**. It hit single-replace files too, so
this was not a replace_all error — the pattern was simply not anchored against its own output.

★★ AND THE VERIFICATION PASSED ON THE CORRUPTED CONTENT:
    grep -rn --include='*.nix' 'Mokhov 2017 §5\.2'   ->  8   ✅ "correct"
BECAUSE **`§5.2` IS A PREFIX OF `§5.2.2`**. The predicate that confirms the substitution is a SUBSTRING of
the string the over-application produces, so it reports success on exactly the failure it exists to catch.
⇒ **A COUNT-BASED CHECK OF A SUBSTITUTION IS BLIND TO OVER-APPLICATION OF THAT SUBSTITUTION, BY
CONSTRUCTION.** Not bad luck; a structural property of using the replacement text as the predicate.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT: the agent **PRINTED THE MATCHED LINES AND READ THEM** instead of trusting the count. That
is the whole lesson. My own follow-up compounded it — I ran `grep -c` across a tree and piped to `wc -l`,
which counts FILES SCANNED (grep -c emits `file:0` for non-matching files) rather than MATCHES, and read
"305" as a match count. Two bad counting predicates in one verification.

THE ANCHORED FORMS THAT ACTUALLY WORK:
    grep -rnoP 'Mokhov 2017 §5\.2(?!\.)'   -> 8   (negative lookahead: the correct string, not a prefix of a longer one)
    grep -rnoP '§5\.2\.2'                  -> 0   (assert the corrupted form is ABSENT)
    grep -rno ...                          -> counts MATCHES; grep -rnc | wc -l counts FILES
Final state confirmed by reading all eight lines: 8 anchored §5.2, 0 §5.2.2, 0 §4.3 on a Mokhov line, total
Mokhov lines 8 (unchanged), positive control Arntzenius 4 (unchanged), tree == HEAD.

★ RULES THIS ADDS, both general:
1. **NEVER VERIFY A SUBSTITUTION WITH THE SUBSTITUTED TEXT AS AN UNANCHORED PATTERN.** Assert the OLD form is
   ABSENT and the NEW form is present ANCHORED — and assert the over-applied form is absent by name. Three
   predicates, not one.
2. **A SUBSTITUTION PATTERN MUST BE ANCHORED AGAINST ITS OWN OUTPUT**, or re-running it is not idempotent. Ask
   before every sed: what does this do if it runs twice? Here it ran once against another agent's already-
   correct text, which is the same thing.
★ AND THE STANDING ONE THIS RE-PROVES: **PRINT AND READ, DO NOT COUNT.** A count is a projection; the whole
failure lived in the part the projection discards.

★ ONE THING THAT WENT RIGHT AND IS WORTH IMITATING: the agent added a positive control ON THE LAYOUT CLAIM
ITSELF, not just on the answer. To confirm that the paper's section numbers sit on their own line it ran
`grep -n '^5\.[0-9]$'` -> 859, 923, 961, 1066, 1119, 1176, 1223 = §5.1 through §5.7. So the bare-number-on-
its-own-line layout holds ACROSS THE WHOLE SECTION rather than at the one line the answer needed. That turns
my multi-line-predicate diagnosis from an assumption into a measurement.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ TRAP — READING A BACKGROUND TASK'S OUTPUT FILE INSTEAD OF ITS REDIRECT TARGET SILENTLY MEASURES THE
WRAPPER, NOT THE WORKLOAD. Caught 2026-07-29 by the ops gate reviewer, on the suite baseline.

MECHANISM. A long run is launched in the background with its real output redirected to a scratchpad file, and
the launching command itself does something small and chatty around it (an echo, a tail). The harness ALSO
captures that launching command's own stdout to a task-output file. Both files exist, both are non-empty,
both look like a test-run log, and NEITHER PATH ERRORS. Grepping the task file for the pass-count returns a
number — just a number from the echo/tail fragment rather than from the suite.

WHAT CAUGHT IT: a positive control on the expected magnitude. 17 checkmarks where 1919 were expected. The
count was not zero and not an error — it was PLAUSIBLE-SHAPED AND OFF BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE. A predicate
that only asked "did I get a count" passes; one that asks "is the count the right SIZE" fails.

⇒ THE LAW. WHEN A MEASUREMENT IS REDIRECTED TO A FILE, ASSERT ON THE ARTEFACT YOU REDIRECTED TO, BY PATH, AND
CHECK ITS MAGNITUDE AGAINST A KNOWN EXPECTATION BEFORE USING IT. Two files that both parse is the failure
shape; only the magnitude distinguishes them.

★ THE FAMILY THIS BELONGS TO, WHICH IS THE POINT: it is the same shape as `2>/dev/null` converting a missing
instrument into an absence finding, and as `grep -rc | wc -l` counting files scanned rather than matches. In
all three A SECOND, WRONGER SOURCE OF THE SAME DATA TYPE IS SITTING NEXT TO THE RIGHT ONE and the tool
happily reads it. The defence is never "check for an error"; it is ALWAYS a same-run expectation about the
VALUE — sign, magnitude, or a known-positive that must appear.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THREE NEW INSTRUMENT TRAPS, ALL HIT IN LIVE WORK 2026-07-29, ALL PRODUCING A FALSE CLEAN RESULT.

1. ★★ **`diff` ON PATH IS A WRAPPER THAT DOES NOT EMIT `<`/`>` LINES.** Hit by the corpus-frontier scout.
   `diff A B | grep -c '^[<>]'` returned **0 for a file that HAD changed**. Real binary:
   /run/current-system/sw/bin/diff.
   ⇒ WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE grep CASE: a "no delta" result is precisely what gets used to CERTIFY THAT A
   PROBE TREE IS FAITHFUL TO ITS SOURCE. The trap fires exactly where the answer is load-bearing, and it
   fires in the flattering direction. Same class as grep-is-ugrep — a familiar tool name resolving to
   something whose OUTPUT FORMAT differs, so the predicate reading that output measures nothing.

2. ★ **`--include=*.nix` UNQUOTED UNDER zsh** globs in the shell, fails with "no matches found", and a piped
   `wc -l` then reports **0**. A clean false absence. Quoted re-run on the same predicate: **469**.

3. ★★ **A FILTER THAT MATCHES NOTHING IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A COMMAND THAT DID NOTHING** — and both look
   like a quiet success. Hit by the ORCHESTRATOR, twice in one turn.
   (a) Four `bd create` calls were run after a `cd` into the scratchpad. `bd` RESOLVES ITS WORKSPACE FROM THE
       CWD, so every one failed with "no beads database found" — but the calls were piped through
       `grep 'Created'`, which printed nothing, and **the empty output read as success**. All four beads were
       silently not created. Caught only by a follow-up count that expected 4 and got 0.
   (b) The same turn, six `bd dep add` calls were filtered through a `grep -o` pattern that did not match the
       actual output format. They printed nothing. The dependencies HAD been added — so this time the silence
       meant the opposite. ★ THE SAME EMPTY OUTPUT MEANT "TOTAL FAILURE" IN (a) AND "COMPLETE SUCCESS" IN (b),
       ONE COMMAND APART.
   ⇒ **NEVER FILTER THE OUTPUT OF A COMMAND WHOSE FAILURE YOU HAVE NOT ALREADY RULED OUT.** Check `$?` or read
   the output first; filter only for display, never for verification. And when a filtered command yields
   nothing, that is not a result — it is an ABSENT MEASUREMENT.

★ THE UNIFYING SHAPE ACROSS ALL THREE, AND WITH `2>/dev/null` AND `grep -rc | wc -l` BEFORE THEM: **A
TRANSFORMATION APPLIED TO OUTPUT FOR CONVENIENCE SILENTLY CONVERTED "I DID NOT MEASURE" INTO "I MEASURED
ZERO".** The defence is never "check for an error" — errors were absent or discarded in every case. It is a
SAME-RUN EXPECTATION ABOUT THE VALUE: a magnitude, a sign, or a known-positive that MUST appear.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ TWO MORE TRAPS, BOTH MEASURED 2026-07-29, BOTH ABOUT AN INSTRUMENT SILENTLY NOT COVERING WHAT IT APPEARS TO.

1. ★★ **`builtins.tryEval` DOES NOT CATCH `attribute … missing` IN THIS NIX.** Same-run positive control:
   `tryEval (throw "x")` → `false`, EXIT 0 (caught). `tryEval ({}.missing)` → **error, EXIT 1** (NOT caught).
   ⇒ CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED: **a `(tryEval c.ok).success` HARNESS CANNOT CONTAIN
   THAT ERROR CLASS.** A spec core built on that harness reports N/N green for every check it CAN evaluate
   while a missing-attribute anywhere in the same run takes down the WHOLE RUN — so the failure does not
   appear as a red check, it appears as no result at all. Found when a bare `pipe.as` fixture aborted a core
   with `error: attribute 'srcCh' missing` instead of reporting a named failed check.
   Sits directly beside the standing entry that a `lib.fix` BLACK HOLE is not tryEval-catchable. Same family:
   **the set of things tryEval catches is smaller than "errors", and the gap is exactly where accessors and
   recursion live.**

2. ★★★ **A SOUND POSITIVE CONTROL CAN PROVE A DIFFERENT PROPOSITION — ORCHESTRATOR CASE, CAUGHT BY A
   REVIEWER.** To verify that a v1 citation read at rev A was still valid at the corpus pin B, I ran
   `git diff --stat B..A -- lib/assemble-pipes.nix lib/compile.nix`, got EMPTY, and reported the coordinate
   verified — WITH a positive control showing 17 files / 1004 insertions changed across the same rev range.
   ★ **`lib/assemble-pipes.nix` EXISTS IN NEITHER REV** (`git cat-file -e` EXIT 128 at both). The real path is
   `nix/lib/aspects/fx/assemble-pipes.nix`, and on it: **92 lines changed, 53 insertions / 39 deletions.**
   ⇒ THE CONTROL WAS SOUND AND ANSWERED "DOES THE REPO CHANGE OVER THIS RANGE". THE CONCLUSION NEEDED "DOES
   THIS PATH CHANGE". **An empty `git diff -- <path>` is IDENTICAL for "unchanged" and "not present".**
   ⇒ ★ **LAW: WHEN VERIFYING A CITATION, CONFIRM THE PATH EXISTS AT THAT REV FIRST** (`git cat-file -e
   <rev>:<path>`), and make the positive control run on THE SAME PATH — not on the repo, the directory, or
   the range. A control at a coarser granularity than the claim cannot discriminate the claim.
   ⇒ The conclusion survived only because the REVIEWER re-derived it on the correct path (the `as` and
   `broadcast` hunks ARE byte-identical, line-shifted by 14). **Survival by luck, not by method.**
   This is the third time this arc that a predicate was SOUND and proved something other than what was
   claimed — and the first where the failure was the ORCHESTRATOR'S, in a message telling an agent the
   coordinate was already checked.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ THE INVERSE TRAP — A RELAYED WARNING THAT DID NOT APPLY, AND WOULD HAVE "CORRECTED" A SOUND RESULT.
Measured 2026-07-29. First instance in this arc of a CORRECTION that would have INTRODUCED the error.

WHAT HAPPENED. The orchestrator measured that `diff` on PATH is a wrapper emitting no `<`/`>` lines, filed it
here, and RELAYED it into a running reviewer's brief as an instrument warning.
★ **IN THAT SESSION `type diff` RESOLVED TO /run/current-system/sw/bin/diff — THE REAL BINARY.** The reviewer
checked instead of adopting, with a positive control on the trap's OWN predicate: two genuinely-differing
files gave 2 `<`/`>` lines through PATH diff AND 2 through the absolute path; `diff -q` exited 1. It then
re-verified its six mutants on an INDEPENDENT instrument anyway (md5, all six distinct from the original and
from each other), and its earlier result stood.
Had it accepted the warning, it would have discarded a sound sanity check and re-done work to fix nothing —
or worse, distrusted a correct set of mutants.

⇒ ★★★ **A TRAP LOG IS A SET OF CONDITIONAL HAZARDS. SHIPPING THEM AS UNCONDITIONAL CREATES A NEW FAILURE
MODE POINTING THE OTHER WAY.** Everything in this log was true where and when it was measured. Whether it is
true in ANOTHER session, another shell, another PATH, another repo state is a SEPARATE QUESTION with its own
one-command answer.

⇒ THE RULE, AND IT BINDS THE ORCHESTRATOR HARDEST BECAUSE RELAYS CARRY AUTHORITY:
1. **State the ENVIRONMENT PREDICATE with the warning, not just the remedy.** Not "use the absolute diff" but
   "`type diff` may resolve to a wrapper — CHECK, and use the absolute path IF it does."
2. **A relayed warning is a HYPOTHESIS TO TEST, exactly like a relayed fact.** The dispatch-discipline rule
   already says a brief is a likely error source and its facts must be verified not inherited. ★ THAT APPLIES
   TO THE INSTRUMENT WARNINGS IN THE BRIEF TOO — which is precisely what nobody thought to check, because a
   warning FEELS like the safe direction.
3. **Asymmetry is the trap.** A missed hazard produces a false green, which this log exists to catch. An
   over-applied hazard produces a false red — work redone, sound results retracted, and NOTHING in the
   process is looking for it.
4. Corroboration: the same session's `.worktrees/` exclusion is the same shape from the other end — a control
   that was doing real work when measured and now correctly reads zero because the world moved.

★ COMPANION FINDING, SAME EXCHANGE: the reviewer SELF-REPORTED that its own closure walk was scoped to
`lib/attributes/` while the instance args it needed to observe are bound in `lib/default.nix` (11 further
quirkDag references outside its scope). Its conclusion survived by independent re-derivation. **Sound
predicate, different proposition — reported rather than quietly fixed**, which is the behaviour to keep.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ A SECOND UNCATCHABLE ERROR CLASS, AND THE RESTRUCTURING THAT REMOVES THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN ACCOMMODATING
IT. Measured 2026-07-29 on the ops-representation core.

**`builtins.tryEval` DOES NOT CATCH A COERCION ERROR EITHER.** Deleting a guard produced
`cannot coerce null to a string` — an UNNAMED kill that took down the whole run, exactly like the
already-recorded `attribute … missing` case. Together with the `lib.fix` black hole that is now THREE classes
a `(tryEval c.ok).success` harness cannot contain.
⇒ **STOP ENUMERATING WHAT tryEval CATCHES. THE SET IS SMALLER THAN "ERRORS" AND ITS BOUNDARY IS NOT
DOCUMENTED ANYWHERE.** Any harness that reports "N/N green" while a sibling check can abort the process is
reporting on a strictly smaller population than it appears to.

★★★ THE FIX IS THE GENERALISABLE PART, AND IT IS CONSTRUCTION OVER REPAIR APPLIED TO AN INSTRUMENT:
· BEFORE: `siteOf` aborted on a nameless record. Deleting the abort produced an unnamed coercion kill — so the
  mutation could not be OBSERVED, only survived-or-crashed.
· AFTER: **`siteKeyOf` is deliberately TOTAL** — a nameless record yields a well-formed but UNSTABLE key,
  **which is what the defect actually looks like in production** — and the abort is a SEPARATE GUARD layered
  over it. Now deleting the guard yields a WRONG VALUE that a named check observes.
· And every possibly-missing lookup goes through a `mustGet` helper turning `attribute … missing` into a
  named `throw` the harness CAN catch.
⇒ ★ **MAKE THE UNDERLYING FUNCTION TOTAL AND PUT THE ABORT BESIDE IT, RATHER THAN MAKING THE FUNCTION ABORT.**
A partial function's mutation is an uncatchable crash; a total function's mutation is a comparable value. This
converts "the harness cannot see this failure" into "the harness sees a wrong answer", which is the whole game.
★ MEASURED EFFECT ON THE SAME ARTEFACT ACROSS ONE REVISION: **r2 had 3 unnamed kills, r3 has 0.**

★ COROLLARY FOR REVIEWERS: an artefact whose mutations produce unnamed kills is not merely inconvenient to
test — **its green runs are evidence about fewer checks than it lists**, because any check ordered after the
crash never ran. Count unnamed kills as a coverage defect, not a harness annoyance.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ A SWEEP THAT DROPS ITS LAST TARGET REPORTS ALL-GREEN-ALL-RED AND LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE SUCCESS.
Caught mid-run 2026-07-29 by the containment-as-edges r5 author, and REPORTED rather than quietly fixed.

MECHANISM. A mutation sweep read its target list from a file. **`targets.txt` had NO TRAILING NEWLINE, so
`while read` SILENTLY DROPPED THE LAST LINE.** The sweep reported **swept = 33** against a real 34, and every
one of the 33 behaved perfectly: 33 mutated, 33 exit 1, 33 with their own named row.
★ **NOTHING IN THE OUTPUT DISTINGUISHES 33/33 FROM 34/34 EXCEPT THE COUNT.** The dropped check (`T4`) was
never mutated, never reported, and its absence produced no error, no warning and no anomalous row — the run
looked like a clean, complete, discriminating sweep.

⇒ THE LAW. **A COVERAGE INSTRUMENT MUST ASSERT ITS OWN CARDINALITY AGAINST AN INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED COUNT.**
"Everything I ran passed/failed correctly" is not coverage; it is a statement about a set whose SIZE the
instrument also chose. The r5 artefact does this correctly and it is the pattern to copy: the file-derived
name set (`grep -c '^      name = "'`) is diffed against the tool-derived set, and a deliberately added extra
check is confirmed auto-counted, auto-listed and auto-swept.

★ THE FAMILY. This is the same shape as `grep -rc | wc -l` counting FILES not matches, as `2>/dev/null`
turning a missing instrument into an absence, and as reading a background task's own output file instead of
its redirect target: **a mechanical detail silently shrinks the population, and every downstream statistic is
then correct ABOUT THE WRONG POPULATION.** The defence is never "check for an error" — there was none. It is a
same-run assertion on the SIZE.
★ Corollary specific to shell: `while read` needs `|| [ -n "$line" ]`, or generate the list in-process and
never round-trip it through a file at all.

title: [kernel] the 2-stage schedule at default.nix:1074 is a live effect-runtime holdover — and was recorded as tracked by a bead that is neither
description:
EFFECT-RUNTIME HOLDOVER, LIVE AND VERIFIED AT HEAD (a40cc96). Criterion 5's live known-positive, and until now
UNTRACKED — it was believed tracked and was not.

THE SITE, verbatim at lib/default.nix:1074-1098:
  :1074  "# THE STAGING THAT BREAKS THE CYCLE (design note §3b). Naive 'cellKinds <- tuples <- pre-pass <-
          roots <- ...'"
  :1076  "(`prePassScopeRoots`, over the STRUCTURAL non-candidates), derives the membership tuples, and the"
  :1083  prePassScopeRoots = buildRoots { ... }
  :1095  "# values. The pre-pass reads `prePassScopeRoots` (structural, un-injected) + `policiesRules` —
          neither"
  :1098  scopeRoots = prePassScopeRoots;
A STAGED PRE-PASS WHOSE ORDERING EXISTS TO BREAK A DEPENDENCY CYCLE IS THE SHAPE THE HOAG MODEL REPLACES WITH
DEMAND-DRIVEN ATTRIBUTES — and the kernel already owns that idiom (`resolve.attr` / `self.get` throughout
lib/attributes/). The file names the staging itself; this is acknowledged, in-tree, and not disputed.

★ WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS: THE TRACKING CLAIM WAS FALSE. W2's kernel-purity audit (den-hoag-4kh.2) recorded this
as criterion 5's replacement known-positive after the A1 accumulator was measured genuinely dissolved, and
stated "Already tracked as den-hoag-9xo.10. NOTE ITS CITED LINE RANGE HAS DRIFTED — 9xo.10 says 961-968; at
HEAD it is 1074-1086."
den-hoag-9xo.10 IS NOT THIS. It is "TOPOLOGY: parent-chain kinds are membership-INDEPENDENT flat roots", and
it is CLOSED — "RESOLVED by the node-multiplication arc, 84fc117..fc29920". So the holdover was recorded as
tracked, the tracker named was a different bug, and that bug then closed. NOBODY VERIFIED THE CITATION.
An orchestrator then carried the same false claim into the retiring-constructs register (den-hoag-4kh.17,
entry 3) without checking it. Corrected there.

⇒ THE PATTERN, which is the reusable part: "already tracked as X" IS A CLAIM, NOT A CITATION. It must be
checked like any other — read the bead, confirm it is the same construct, confirm it is open. A closed bead
named as a tracker silently converts live work into finished work.

RELATIONSHIP TO A1: den-hoag-4kh.2 verified the A1 `runPrePass` STATE ACCUMULATOR is genuinely gone at HEAD —
in the pre-image (6bef742^) the per-element step READ the accumulator (`st.relationBindings.${id}`); at HEAD
no fold in the file does, and every surviving `foldl'` is a monoid merge over independently-computed
elements. THIS IS A DIFFERENT, ADJACENT HOLDOVER AT THE CALL SITE. Do not re-file it as an A1 regression;
A1 is dissolved.

ACCEPTANCE: either the staging is replaced by demand-driven attributes (the kernel's own idiom), or the
reason it must remain is recorded with the dependency cycle it breaks NAMED and a statement of why laziness
at the attribute cannot break it. "It works" is not a reason under the standing bar.

NOT MEASURED: whether removing the staging is behaviour-preserving, and what the cycle actually is. The
design note §3b it cites should be read first — it may already answer why the naive order fails.
notes:
★★ NEW BINDING REQUIREMENT ON THIS RETIREMENT, measured 2026-07-28. Recorded here
because it is invisible from every site the retirement would touch.

THE STAGED PRE-PASS IS LOAD-BEARING FOR ABW DEFINITION 3 CONDITION 2, AND NOTHING
IN THE TREE SAYS SO.

The suppression gate (lib/compat/compile.nix gateSuppression) performs a NEGATED
READ -- it fires iff the policy's name is ABSENT from ctx.suppressedPolicies.
Condition 2 requires a negated literal's definition to sit STRICTLY BELOW the
stratum of the rule reading it. That requirement is met today NOT by any check,
but by the STAGING ITSELF: the pre-pass's ctx (baseCtxOf / deliverCtxOf) is built
from prePassScopeRoots, FIXED BEFORE ANY SUPPRESSION EXISTS, so during the
pre-pass the negative literal is evaluated against an EMPTY extension of the very
relation being computed. The suppressions then arrive as inherited EDB.

⇒ REMOVE THE STAGING AND THE READ BECOMES AN UNGUARDED SAME-STRATUM NEGATED READ.
No guard replaces it: den.derived's `negates` and den.productions' `from` range
over RELATIONS, and `suppress` quantifies over POLICY NAMES -- they have no
vocabulary for it (den-hoag-4kh.51 has the full argument and the live witness).

⇒ THIS RETIREMENT NOW OWES A CONDITION-2 STORY, stated before any replacement is
designed: what, after the pre-pass is gone, prevents a suppression from being
derived from the absence of another suppression? A cycle through a negative edge
is ALREADY ADMITTED SILENTLY on this path today (measured: mutual A/B and self-
negating A both produce a suppressed set with NO abort, with positive and negative
controls in the same run) -- so the retirement is not introducing the hazard, it is
removing the accident that bounds it.

★ NOTE THIS IS INDEPENDENT OF den-hoag-9xo.57, which was REJECTED. That design
also touched this pre-pass, and it would be easy to read this requirement as
falling with it. It does not. This one comes from the negation semantics and holds
whatever replaces the schedule.

★ AND NOTE THE PATTERN, because it is the third instance in this arc: the
construct scheduled for retirement is silently discharging an obligation nobody
wrote down. The register's own worked example says the guards exist BECAUSE the
retiring construct fails; this is the converse and it is more dangerous -- the
retiring construct SUCCEEDS at something unrecorded, so its removal looks free.
Before retiring it, enumerate what currently holds only because of the staging.

title: [kernel] RESIDUE of the bucket retirement: classBucketsOf, plus the reach-element MISSING SCOPE COORDINATE — E10(b) is DISSOLVED, neither reading is live and no owner ruling is owed
description:
RETIRE THE PER-CLASS CONTENT BUCKET. Class content becomes DIRECT GEN-EDGE GRAPH QUERIES, not accumulated
state. Owner-directed since 2026-07-24; scope doc written; NEVER TRACKED IN THE GRAPH UNTIL NOW — which is
precisely why a design was written, reviewed three times and VALIDATED entirely in bucket vocabulary without
anyone noticing.

THE POSITION (owner, 2026-07-24, restated 2026-07-28): den v1's per-class buckets — collecting each aspect's
class content into `{ <class> = [ <deferredModule> ] }` per node — were required ONLY by v1's NIX-EFFECTS
STATE ACCUMULATOR. In pure gen, class content reduces to DIRECT GEN-EDGE GRAPH QUERIES. den-hoag STRIPPED
THE EFFECT RUNTIME BUT KEPT THE ACCUMULATOR'S SHAPE (eager per-class bucket collection).
Owner 2026-07-28: "we worked really hard to revert that part of the design to avoid recreation of the
nix-effects shape. we even built 3 new gen libraries for formalizing materialization as an alternative to
bucketing — those should be satisfied instead by graph queries, not accumulated state."

★ THE BUCKET IS THE ROOT OF A COLLISION CLASS, not a local inefficiency. The per-class declared
`deferredModule` option is what shadows a same-named nested aspect ⇒ THE ASPECT-NAME ⟂ CLASS-NAME COLLISION
(microvm = den.classes.microvm AND aspect den.aspects.virtualization.microvm; home-manager likewise).
Because a node is EAGERLY COMMITTED to "this key is class content" AT TYPING, the value-shape predicates
`looksLikeClassContent` / `isNestedKey` (lib/compat/compile.nix:245,263, ported from v1 key-classification)
exist ONLY to recover the aspect interpretation after the fact. Under an edge model the eager commitment
vanishes and the collision, both predicates, and the over-collapsed buckets may DISSOLVE TOGETHER.

EVIDENCE, verified at the time of scoping:
· lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:133 — "gen-edge is class-coordinate-generic (README: 'den's NixOS class
  buckets … are ONE instantiation')" ⇒ gen-edge is the GENERAL model; buckets are a v1-shaped instantiation.
· lib/attributes/class-modules.nix pre-collects buckets, marked "NO EFFECT RUNTIME" — EFFECT STRIPPED, SHAPE
  KEPT.
· gen-aspects lib/types.nix:257-264 `classOptions = genAttrs (keyOf "class") deferredModule` = the per-class
  DECLARED bucket-landing option.

SCOPE DOC: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-24-bucket-to-edge-refactor-scope.md (21 KB).
★ ITS CORE OPEN QUESTION, unanswered and unread by the arc that touched this code: DOES THE
ASPECT/CLASS DISAMBIGUATION DISSOLVE under an edge model (distinct class-content-edge vs aspect-nesting
constructions ⇒ the value-shape predicates become DELETABLE), OR DOES IT MOVE TO QUERY TIME?

WHAT IS PARKED PENDING THIS: the whole aspect/class collision class, the value-shape predicates, and
host.settings rung 5+ (the nix-config compile-frame grind).

★ WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS NOW: den-hoag-4kh.12's confluence design uses "bucket" 52 times, cites this scope
ZERO times, and never asks whether the bucket should exist. Three adversarial gate reviews passed over it.
The rubric had no predicate for "does this design ENTRENCH a construct already scoped for retirement" —
criterion 1 asks whether a design USES state accumulation, not whether it BUILDS ON one already marked for
deletion. That gap is now gate check C9 (den-hoag-4kh.6). AN UNTRACKED RETIREMENT IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY
PROCESS THAT READS THE GRAPH; that is the reason this is a bead and not a note.

ACCEPTANCE: the scope doc's open question ANSWERED with evidence, and a decision recorded — either the
retirement proceeds (and dependent designs are re-expressed against the edge model BEFORE implementation),
or the bucket survives with a STATED REASON and a stated position on which side of the kernel/compat line it
lands. "The corpus does it" is not a reason under the standing bar.

DO NOT treat this as a refactor ticket. It is a REPRESENTATION question with a collision class and two
value-shape anti-patterns hanging off its answer.

comments.text:
★★★ CORRECTION — THIS BEAD REGISTERED SHIPPED WORK. Filed 2026-07-28 from a 2026-07-24 memory WITHOUT
VERIFYING IT AGAINST THE TREE. Owner caught it within the hour. Two of its three load-bearing claims are
FALSE at HEAD.

════ WHAT SHIPPED, and the bead claimed was open ════
★ THE CLASS / CHANNEL / FACET / ASPECT DISAMBIGUATION IS SOLVED AND SHIPPED — by DECLARATION, via
gen-schema key-semantics + gen-aspects generic dispatch. This is the "Shape B" arc (owner-ruled 2026-07-15),
not the bucket retirement.
  lib/key-semantics.nix, verbatim: "The ONE keySemantics vocabulary builder (gen-aspects `cnf.keySemantics`).
  gen-aspects builds every declared aspect key's option GENERICALLY from this map: `class → deferredModule`,
  `channel → raw passthrough`, `facet → the entry's own option/module`. den-hoag declares its whole aspect
  vocabulary through here, so an aspect key's semantics live in ONE place … from which `classifyKey` also
  reads a key's category." And: "so a quirk-channel key never falls to freeform"; a `.settings` block is
  "never freeform-absorbed as a nested aspect".
  lib/concern-aspects.nix:103-113 — `classifyKey = _aspectName: key: let cat = aspectSchema.keyCategory key;
  in if cat == "class" then "class" else if cat == "channel" then "channel" else "facet"`.
  ⇒ DISPATCH IS ON THE DECLARED CATEGORY. No value shape. The eager-commitment-at-typing problem the bead
  described is gone, and it was solved WITHOUT retiring the bucket.

  lib/module-shape.nix:6 — a comment referencing the retired guard
  Neither exists as a live predicate. Only comments naming them remain.

predicates were NOT parked on bucket retirement — they were resolved by the key-semantics route. Whether

THE BUCKET AS A DATA STRUCTURE. key-semantics declares `class → deferredModule`, i.e. THE PER-CLASS BUCKET
STILL EXISTS — it is now DECLARED rather than INFERRED. Declaration fixed the disambiguation; it did not
change the representation. So the open question is the narrower one:
    SHOULD CLASS CONTENT BE A DIRECT GEN-EDGE GRAPH QUERY RATHER THAN A PER-CLASS ACCUMULATED BUCKET?
That is a REPRESENTATION question, and it stands on its own evidence — output-modules.nix:133 ("gen-edge is
class-coordinate-generic … den's NixOS class buckets are ONE instantiation") and class-modules.nix's
bucket map marked "NO EFFECT RUNTIME" (effect stripped, shape kept). It is NO LONGER load-bearing for a

THE SCOPE DOC (specs/2026-07-24-bucket-to-edge-refactor-scope.md) PREDATES THE KEY-SEMANTICS LANDING and its
core open question — "does the disambiguation DISSOLVE or MOVE to query time" — HAS BEEN ANSWERED BY A THIRD
ROUTE: it dissolved, via declaration, without the edge model. ANYONE READING THAT DOC MUST BE TOLD SO.

════ CONSEQUENCE FOR den-hoag-4kh.12 ════
The blocking edge 4kh.12 → 4kh.16 was justified on "the mechanism does not survive the retirement". THAT
REASONING IS UNCHANGED — keyedBucketsOf / classSliceKeyedBaseAt / applyInjectReroute are still the
accumulator's shape and would still be deleted rather than amended under an edge model. But the URGENCY
behind it was inflated by the stale collision framing. The edge stays; its priority claim does not.

════ THE PROCESS FAILURE, recorded because it is the same one the owner is auditing elsewhere ════
This bead was created from MEMORY (project_class_bucket_holdover, 2026-07-24) and a SCOPE DOC of the same
date, and NEITHER WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE TREE before filing. The verification took four commands once
someone asked. A memory is a point-in-time observation; a scope doc is a snapshot of intent. NEITHER IS
EVIDENCE ABOUT HEAD.
★ RULE, now in the register (den-hoag-4kh.17): NO RETIREMENT ENTRY MAY BE FILED OR TRUSTED WITHOUT
VERIFYING ITS SITES AT HEAD IN THE SAME SESSION. An entry that names a file:line must have had that line

comments.text:
DESIGN WRITTEN — specs/2026-07-28-bucket-to-edge-design.md, 617 lines, md5 b26937103d8252b6b7804a1395fe9ba1. NOT YET GATED.

DECISION: class content becomes a DEMAND-DRIVEN QUERY per (node, channel), evaluated from Λ(n)+Acts(n) alone. ONE attribute `class-seeds` replaces `class-modules` + `class-modules-keyed`. Successor named in gen-edge's OWN vocabulary — CHANNEL-COORDINATE SEED QUERY (channel / seed / preimage), not the retiring construct's terms.

★ THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN THIS BEAD ASSUMED — HALF ALREADY SHIPPED. class-modules.nix:168-171 states the base is ALREADY a direct per-(node,class) query. THE RESIDUE IS TWO WRAPPERS: `applyInjectReroute` (whole-map) and `forceContentKeysAt` (eager O(A·k̄) force on any demand). THOSE TWO ARE THE ACCUMULATOR; THE ATTRSET IS NOT. 'Retire the bucket' as a slogan overstates what remains.

★ THE GATE HOOK IS A CHECKABLE CRITERION, NOT A SLOGAN (E12, §5): TODAY `class-modules-keyed.<C>` CANNOT BE STATED WITHOUT STATING THE WHOLE MAP, because `acc.${t} ++ acc.${f}` READS OTHER KEYS' VALUES. AFTER: `classSeedsAt n c` is closed-form in Λ(n)/Acts(n)/Ch and mentions no other channel's value. The map becomes the MEMO OF A QUERY rather than the DEFINITION. Decidable by inspection.

APPLYINJECTREROUTE IS DELETED, AND ALL THREE den-hoag-4kh.12 FAILURE MODES BECOME INEXPRESSIBLE RATHER THAN CORRECTED: diamond loss — nothing is ever written so nothing is emptied, `pre` reads the RELATION; four-answers/permutation — E1-E4 are set/filter ops and act order does not appear; self-reroute abort — E1 drops from==to before any attrset exists, and the core has ZERO dynamic-key literals.

COMPLEXITY, STATED AND ONE COST REPORTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: at Ρ(n)=∅ (every corpus node) per-channel and all-channels cost are identical and the EAGER WORK IS STRICTLY BETTER — forceContentKeysAt's O(A·k̄) leaves the class path entirely (E11 moves the totality driver to `resolved-aspects`, one driver instead of two). At Ρ(n)≠∅, Σ|pre(c)| = Σ|nf(d)|, which under multicast is EXPONENTIAL IN THE DECLARED RELOCATION FOREST'S DEPTH. NOT absorbed: §7 reports it and O4 makes `nf` dedup an OBLIGATION with a fixture, bounding it to O(K²·A).
★ THE MEMO IS LOAD-BEARING: replacing `resolve.attr` with a bare function takes `classSubtreeAt` from O(Σ_subtree A) to O(H·Σ_subtree A). Called out so an implementer does not 'simplify' it away.

C9/C9-a SELF-CHECK: register entry 1 IS this retirement — THEORY survives (class-as-coordinate is gen-edge's own, output-modules.nix:133), MECHANISM does not (whole-map fold + eager driver + bare/keyed pair all deleted). Entry 4 hit NAMED rather than swept: `forwardSourceClassesOf` reads `content.meta.__forward` (class-modules.nix:66), carried UNCHANGED with no new reader — its retirement belongs to entry 4's arc. `__action` is a gen-dispatch KIND TAG, not a state carrier. Entries 2/3 untouched. C9-a: §4, the executable core, contains ZERO occurrences of the retiring construct's word, verified by awk-range grep exiting 1.

MIGRATION COST STATED: 15 call sites / 10 CI files read the public `class-modules` attribute. ★ SEVERAL READ IT ONLY TO FORCE CLASSIFICATION (compat-materialized-class-ground.nix:28, declared-classes.nix:54) — under E11 those must force `resolved-aspects` instead, so THAT SUBSET IS NOT A MECHANICAL RENAME and each needs its intent re-read. §9.
Obligations O1-O7 in §10, each with what falsifies it. O6 sharpens the existing projection anchor, which currently RELIES on Ρ=Ι=∅ without ASSERTING it.

★ ONE OWNER RULING REQUIRED (§13 Q1) — see the P0 terminal-divergence bead. Unifying both consumers closes that defect BY CONSTRUCTION, but it CHANGES WHAT A PUBLIC EXPORT DOES (`declare`, lib/default.nix:2730). It makes the export behave as documented; it is still an observable change. Fallback if 'no': keep two disagreeing sources — explicitly not recommended.

★ MY BRIEF WAS WRONG ON ONE POINT THAT MATTERED, and the correction SHRINKS the blast radius: I asserted that retiring the per-node map 'touches a gen-aspects DECLARATION' at gen-aspects lib/types.nix:257-264. THAT RANGE HAS DRIFTED — it is now `gatedFreeformElem`, unrelated. `classOptions` is at :385-392, spread at :484. Reading it settles the substance: it declares that an ASPECT may carry content at a channel-named key — a PER-ASPECT AUTHORING SURFACE, the INPUT to classSliceOf, not a per-node index. Retiring the per-node map neither reads nor changes it. ⇒ BLAST RADIUS IS den-hoag-LOCAL, ZERO GEN-SUBSTRATE. The scope doc had this right at :24-28/:89-91; my brief re-conflated it.

Proof: 24 act-permutations produced EXACTLY ONE answer — an accumulator gives four. The bead's founding failure did not recur.
★★ BUT THE GATE MEANT TO PROTECT THAT IS BROKEN — C2-a FAIL, and this is the sharpest finding. E12/O1's 'checkable criterion' is a NAME CHECK: 'no occurrence of `classSeedsAt n c'` in the definition of `classSeedsAt n c`'. COUNTEREXAMPLE AT HEAD, verbatim class-modules.nix:219-221: `classSliceKeyedAt = self: id: class: (keyedBucketsOf self id).${class} or [ ];` — no occurrence of itself at another channel. THE RETIRED ACCUMULATOR PASSES O1'S LITERAL CHECK. The real criterion is O1's FALSIFIER ('any cross-channel value read'), a whole-program dataflow property, not 'decidable by inspection'. Check and falsifier are different predicates and the gate can pass while the falsifier holds.

★ C7-a FAIL — BUILD-WHAT-EXISTS, FOURTH INSTANCE, AND THIS TIME AN IN-TREE COMMENT FORBIDS IT BY NAME. §9 asserts 'Substrate: none' with NO SCAN PERFORMED. gen-graph IS ALREADY A den-hoag INPUT (flake.nix:11, bound lib/default.nix:42 `graph = inputs.gen-graph.lib`) and ships exactly the primitives E2/E3/E7 hand-roll: `reachableFrom` (C-level BFS via builtins.genericClosure), `canReach`, `selfReachable`, `cycles`, `transpose`, `condensation` (reps/bottomUp/members/sccs/sccOf/condEdges — the SCC semantics den-hoag-4kh.12 reasoned in).
AND den-hoag ALREADY CALLS `transpose` FOR PRECISELY THE PREIMAGE JOB at lib/default.nix:2067, whose own comment reads: 'THE INVERSE EDGES via gen-graph.transpose (§9) … a per-kind genGraphLib.transpose (Mokhov 2017 §4.3), NOT A HAND-ROLLED FROM/TO SWAP.' ★ E3 IS A HAND-ROLLED FROM/TO SWAP. The tree contains a comment prohibiting the exact construction the design proposes, at a site doing the same job.

★ C3 + C7-b FAIL — THE COMPLEXITY STATEMENT IS REFUTED ON FOUR COUNTS, ALL MEASURED BY INSTRUMENTING E2 AND COUNTING INVOCATIONS ACROSS 7 (h,b) POINTS:
(a) EXACT COST LAW: nf invocations = 2·K·Σ_d |subtree(d)|, verified at every point (2·3·5=30, 2·4·7=56, 2·7·17=238, 2·40·142=11360). Each invocation recomputes `rho n` = O(R) ⇒ Θ(K²·b^h·R).
(b) THE DESIGN'S BOUND IS UNDERSTATED 10-13×: §7 claims K·b^h; at h=3,b=3 that is 1080 vs 11360 MEASURED; at h=4,b=3, 9801 vs 132374. §7's closure term O(K·R)=14520 elementary ops vs actual ~1.59e7 — ~1094×.
(c) ★ THE EXPONENTIAL IS AN IMPLEMENTATION ARTIFACT, NOT THE SEMANTICS, AND §7 SAYS THE OPPOSITE TO LICENSE ABSORBING IT. `pre n c = builtins.filter … Ch` ⇒ |pre(c)| ≤ K ALWAYS ⇒ Σ_c|pre(c)| ≤ K² — the content-replication term CAN NEVER BE EXPONENTIAL. The exponential lives entirely in the unmemoised `nf` re-exploration. §7 locates it in the one term where it cannot be. Under 'performance is a defect, never acceptable cost', this is the FAIL.
(d) ★ O4 IS VACUOUS — MEASURED ZERO EFFECT: 884→884 and 11360→11360. Dedup of the RESULT does not bound the RECURSION. And O4's falsifier tests the ANSWER, which `pre`'s `builtins.elem` already makes path-insensitive, so O4'S FIXTURE PASSES WITHOUT O4 and cannot detect the cost it names. An obligation with no working falsifier.
(e) FREE 2× LEFT ON THE TABLE: E4 evaluates `pre n c` TWICE, unshared; Nix does no CSE. Let-binding halved invocations (11360→5680, 132374→66187) with byte-identical answers.
⇒ (c)+(d) together: the correct fix is MEMOISING THE CLOSURE, which is what gen-graph's `reachableFrom`/`condensation` already do. BY CONSTRUCTION, not by obligation.

C1-a + C5 FAIL — E10(b) IS A TYPE ERROR AND THE TERMINAL HALF HAS NO EXECUTABLE FORM. The two consumers have DIFFERENT ARITIES: the seed path is NODE-indexed; `projectClass` is ASPECT-indexed over `reach`, and `reach` (resolved-aspects.nix:313, emit :126-133) yields `{ key; content; sharedFoldKey; }` with NO SCOPE COORDINATE. E10(b) does `concatMap (n: … classSeedsAt n class) reach` where `classSeedsAt` needs a NODE ID. Internally inconsistent within four lines: the same `let` calls `forwardSourceClassesOf reach` (treating elements as aspect records) then feeds those same elements to `classSeedsAt` (needing ids).
C5.2 — ★ A SECOND, UNSTATED BEHAVIOUR DELTA: the `exempt` set silently changes scope. Today `projectClass` (output-modules.nix:741-745) computes `exempt = forwardSourceClassesOf reach` — REACH-sourced DELIBERATELY (class-modules.nix:56: 'an unregistered fromClass a meta.__forward spec on a REACHED node names'). E6 computes it own-node only, and in E10(b) the reach-sourced exempt is used ONLY by routeRemapFor/forwardModulesFor — the content leg loses it. A `meta.__forward` spec on a reached-but-not-own aspect stops exempting ⇒ classifyKey typo-abort where content materializes today. Unstated anywhere.
C4 FAIL, ERRS UNSAFE: §7 row 2 claims eager work becomes 'O(1) beyond the demanded channel', but E11 puts the totality force on `resolved-aspects` and E6 READS `Λ(n) = self.get n "resolved-aspects"` — so demanding any channel still pays O(A·k̄). Worse and unreported: today `forceContentKeysAt` fires only on the class path; under E11 EVERY reader of resolved-aspects pays it, including `reach`, has-aspect-verbs.nix:41, resolve-verbs.nix:85. A BROADENING of eager classification presented as a reduction.
C6 FAIL: E11 and E7 sit INSIDE 'THE EXECUTABLE CORE' as PROSE COMMENTS WITH NO EQUATION. E11 is load-bearing — E10(b) drops `builtins.seq (assertKeysRegistered exempt n)` (live at output-modules.nix:750) and E11 is the only thing standing in for it. A load-bearing claim living solely in prose is itself a defect, and this one is inside the block the stamp would attest.

CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION, the design's strongest section — CLAIM 2, ALL THREE INEXPRESSIBILITY CLAIMS, no counterexample found: diamond (24 permutations → nDistinct=1, cA present at D); permutation (act order cannot appear — `pre` tests membership with `builtins.elem` and filters over Ch, so srcOrder is Ch-ordered regardless of Acts order); self-reroute ([A→A] is a no-op, A keeps its content, no dynamic-key abort). The E7 cycle throw IS `tryEval`-containable, confirming O2(c).
CLAIM 4 CONFIRMED EXACTLY: 15 occurrences across exactly the 10 named files; zero readers in lib/ (one hit = the definition, class-modules.nix:236 — predicate matches where the string exists, so the absence is real); and the not-mechanical subset confirmed VERBATIM at compat-materialized-class-ground.nix:28 and declared-classes.nix:54, both reading it for CLASSIFICATION not content.
§8 FIXTURE CLAIM CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION: all three class-bucket-query rows replayed through E1-E6 reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the fixture's expected values at :88-115.
MINOR ERRATUM: §3.2 says classSliceKeyedAt 'is exported for the class-bucket-query fixture (attributes/default.nix:249-253)'. The fixture takes `internal.classModulesBuilder` and calls `cm.class-modules.compute` — IT NEVER CALLS classSliceKeyedAt, WHICH HAS NO LIVE CALLER AT ALL. Harmless (it is on the delete list) but the stated justification is wrong.
