★★ DESIGN FORK POSED — §13 Q2, THE REACH-COORDINATE QUESTION. OWNER RULING OWED. Spec now 1024 lines, md5 7e42a7d7dbd4a51bde91aee527129347 (was 617 / b2693710…). gen-graph adopted.

THE SITUATION: `classSeedsAt` is NODE-indexed (reads Λ(n), Acts(n)). `projectClass` folds over `reach`, whose elements are `{ key; content; sharedFoldKey; }` — NO SCOPE COORDINATE. The shape is fixed at the preorder emit (resolved-aspects.nix:126-133) and preserved through the edge closure's project (:403-411). So 'apply the node's relocations to a reached aspect' HAS NO REFERENT until someone says WHICH node, and the two candidates differ exactly when an aspect reaches a node that did not declare it — the only case where terminal relocation is interesting at all.

READING A — THE PROJECTING SCOPE'S ACTS GOVERN. One relocation relation per projection; Ρ(id) read once at the projecting node and applied uniformly to every aspect in reach id.
  MAKES TRUE: relocation is a property of the ASSEMBLING scope. A host says 'everything reaching me that lands on homeManager should land on nixos instead', holding over content from its cells, its edges and itself alike. Composes with `reach` without changing it.
  COSTS: an aspect's own node's relocations become invisible at the terminal while remaining visible at the edge seed — ★ THE SEED PATH AND THE TERMINAL PATH DISAGREE AGAIN, ON A DIFFERENT AXIS, which is the defect §3.3 (den-hoag-4kh.41) exists to close. And class-seeds (node-indexed) and the terminal (projection-indexed) become two different functions that COINCIDE ONLY WHEN Ρ IS EMPTY — which is every corpus node, so THE DIVERGENCE WOULD BE CORPUS-INVISIBLE, exactly like the one being fixed.

READING B — THE OWNING SCOPE'S ACTS GOVERN. Each reached aspect carries its own node's relocations; the terminal reads class-seeds at each contributing node and concatenates.
  MAKES TRUE: relocation is a property of the DECLARING scope, so an aspect means the same thing wherever it is assembled. The terminal becomes a pure gather over the same per-node query the edge seed reads — THE TWO CONSUMERS ARE THE SAME FUNCTION BY CONSTRUCTION, which is this design's whole premise.
  COSTS: ★ IT REQUIRES `reach` TO CARRY A SCOPE COORDINATE, WHICH IT DOES NOT. That is a change to a shipped, load-bearing attribute whose dedup discipline (sharedFoldKey, per-provider multiplicity, the cross-scope collapse at resolved-aspects.nix:390-399) is delicate and fixture-pinned. Adding an owning-node field to elements DELIBERATELY DEDUPED ACROSS SCOPES needs its own analysis of what 'the owning node' means for a node that survived a cross-scope collapse. Not a casual one-field addition.

★ WHAT DISTINGUISHES THEM — AND WHY PARITY CANNOT SETTLE IT: a cell declares an aspect with homeManager content and `reroute { from = "homeManager"; to = "nixos"; }`; the host reaches that cell structurally and declares no relocation. Under A the host's Ρ = ∅ so content stays on homeManager at the terminal — while the edge seed, reading the cell's own class-seeds, has ALREADY MOVED IT. Under B both move it. The mirror case separates them the other way.
NO CORPUS OR COMPAT SHAPE DISTINGUISHES THEM TODAY: den-hoag-4kh.12 records zero reroute call sites fleet-wide and §3.3 finds no inject producer, so Ρ(n) = Ι(n) = ∅ everywhere and A and B are EXTENSIONALLY EQUAL on everything currently built. ⇒ THE CHOICE IS PURE THEORY AND CANNOT BE SETTLED BY PARITY — precisely the case the north-star ruling anticipates, where corpus-green is a symptom and not the bar.

RECOMMENDATION FROM THE DESIGN AGENT — READING B. EXPLICITLY NOT ADOPTED; THE OWNER RULES.
Its reasoning, and I find it strong: this design's entire claim is 'one query, two consumers', and THAT CLAIM IS ONLY TRUE UNDER B. Under A the two consumers are different functions again — ★ AND THE FACT THAT THEY AGREE ON THE CORPUS IS PRECISELY THE PROPERTY THAT LET THE CURRENT DIVERGENCE SURVIVE THREE GATE REVIEWS. A also puts a scope's declaration in charge of content it did not declare, the direction den-hoag has consistently moved away from — offered SECOND because it is an argument from this codebase's habits, not from theory. The theory argument is first: A DECLARATION'S MEANING SHOULD NOT DEPEND ON WHO ASSEMBLES IT.
★ AND IT ARGUES AGAINST ITSELF HONESTLY: 'the cost of B is real and is a genuine reason to rule the other way; it is a change to `reach`, and it should be scoped as its own piece of work rather than smuggled into this one.'
IF THE RULING IS A, the design still lands: E10(b) becomes `concatMap (n: map (e: e.module) (raw n exempt)) reach` folded over `srcOrder (frameAt id) class`, and §4.3's by-construction claim MUST be downgraded to 'one relation, two indexings' — honestly, in the document.

Q3 IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DELTA, not covered by the 2026-07-28 ruling and introduced silently: today projectClass computes `exempt = forwardSourceClassesOf reach` (output-modules.nix:746), REACH-sourced deliberately per class-modules.nix:56, and threads it to the totality assertion, content extraction, routeRemapFor and forwardModulesFor alike. E6 computes it OWN-NODE only, and in the rewritten E10(b) the reach-sourced set survived only on the routeRemapFor/forwardModulesFor legs — THE CONTENT LEG LOST IT. Consequence: a `meta.__forward` spec on an aspect REACHED BUT NOT OWNED stops exempting, so classifyKey aborts where content materializes today.

★ Q3 RECOMMENDATION IS READING A — `exempt` STAYS REACH-SOURCED — WHICH IS A DIFFERENT ANSWER FROM Q2's B, LEGITIMATELY. The reach-sourcing is not incidental: class-modules.nix:56 documents it as a deliberate collect-coupling ('silencing the abort alone delivers nothing'), and the exemption exists so a ROUTE can move content THE PROJECTING SCOPE CAN SEE — projection-scoped by construction, so it should stay projection-scoped even if Q2 rules CONTENT owner-scoped. The resulting asymmetry is FLAGGED not papered over: E6's own-node exempt is correct for the seed path and INSUFFICIENT for the terminal, and the implementation must carry that explicitly. And papers HEAD was f88e6a4, not 06c2f9e (which is the commit that ADDED the spec).

title: [gen-graph] order.nix cites Mokhov 2017 for topological enumeration; the paper contains neither the word nor the claim
description:
CITATION OVERSTATEMENT, verified independently TWICE with positive controls in the same run.

SITE: gen-graph/lib/order.nix:5-6 - THEORY: home-manager dag idiom (generalized strings-with-deps) over Mokhov 2017 section 4 quotient-graph topological enumeration.

OVERSTATES ON TWO COUNTS:

1. THE WORD. topological occurs ZERO times in Mokhov 2017. Source of record: papers/den-architecture/used/markdown/mokhov-2017-algebraic-graphs.md. Positive controls, same file same run: graph = 421 hits, condensation = 2 hits at lines 750 and 755, preorder = 4 hits, stem topolog = 0. So the grep works and the absence is real, not a dead predicate.

2. THE SCOPE, which is the substantive half. Section 4.6 Preorders and Equivalence Relations DERIVES the quotient - it is a construction, not an assumption - but says nothing about enumerating an ORDER over it. Verified exactly: the only occurrences of strongly-connected and scc in the entire paper are THREE LINES of section 4.6 - strongly-connected at 747 and 748, scc at 749. Mokhov explicitly DELEGATES the SCC computation to the containers library, so his contribution is the algebraic representation of the quotient - set-valued vertices, well-typed as Graph g, Vertex g ~ Set Int => g - not an algorithm and not an ordering procedure.

WHAT IS CORRECTLY CITED, for contrast - gen-graph/lib/global.nix:136 cites Tarjan 1972 / Kosaraju for SCCs; Mokhov 2017 section 4 for the quotient-graph idiom. THAT SPLIT IS CORRECTLY APPORTIONED: algorithm to Tarjan/Kosaraju, IDIOM to Mokhov. order.nix collapses the same split into one over-attributed phrase.

ADJACENT, worth reading together - global.nix:131-133 directly above that correct citation DISCLAIMS the algorithm: closure-based O(n squared) ... NOT Tarjan's linear O(V+E) single-DFS - its mutable stack/lowlink is out-of-substrate for pure Nix. So gen-graph is honest at global.nix and loose at order.nix.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NIT: the gen theory-conformance audit treats provenance as a real gate, and its C5 COORDINATES check - does the cited section actually contain the cited content - has already found two defects in this corpus (Vogt, Mokhov). This is a third, in the same class. The gate's own posture is that prose is load-bearing because implementers act on it.

FIX: restate order.nix:5-6 to cite Mokhov only for what he supplies - the algebraic quotient representation - and attribute the phase-ordering / topological enumeration to whatever actually warrants it, mirroring the correct split already present at global.nix:136. If nothing warrants it, say so rather than borrowing.

PROVENANCE OF THIS FINDING: surfaced during the den-hoag kernel-purity arc while verifying a design that leans on condensation. Confirmed by the orchestrator and again by an independent adversarial reviewer, each with positive controls. The citation the DESIGN leans on - global.nix:136 - holds; this one does not.

comments.text:
INSTRUMENT VERIFIED AND CALIBRATED (2026-07-27, session resumed with Nix-aware codebase-memory). Read this
BEFORE any agent uses the graph, and treat the two limitations as load-bearing.

VERIFICATION: den-hoag indexed at 3094 nodes / 9279 edges, 2213 Function nodes, edge types incl. CALLS 1461,
USAGE 4182, DEFINES 2730. Positive control PASSED: search_graph "runPrePass" resolves to
lib/staged-resolution.nix:131-446 as a Function. Nix symbols ARE extracted.

★ TRAP 1 — get_architecture's `languages` FIELD DOES NOT LIST NIX. It reports only YAML (3 files) and
Python (1). An agent following the standing instruction "confirm coverage via get_architecture before
trusting a query" would read that field, conclude Nix is uncovered, and fall back to grep — discarding the
whole capability. COVERAGE MUST BE CONFIRMED BY A KNOWN-POSITIVE SYMBOL QUERY, not by the languages list.

★★ TRAP 2 — CALLS EDGES MISS ATTRSET-MEDIATED CALLS, WHICH IS NIX'S DOMINANT IDIOM. Measured:
  trace_path runPrePass inbound  -> ZERO callers
  grep runPrePass                -> lib/default.nix:1097  `prePass = stagedResolution.runPrePass { ... }`
The call is real; the graph does not see it, because the callee is reached through an imported attrset
(module imported as a value, member called off it) rather than by a bare identifier.
POSITIVE CONTROL PROVING THE DIRECTION WORKS AT ALL: trace_path fail inbound -> 23 callers. So caller-tracing
is functional; it is specifically the attrset-mediated cross-module call that is invisible.
⇒ "ZERO CALLERS" FROM THIS GRAPH IS NOT EVIDENCE OF DEAD CODE. Every zero-caller result must be cross-checked
with grep before any conclusion, and especially before any deletion. Within-file CALLS appear reliable;
cross-module CALLS through an attrset are incomplete.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RELAUNCH: the graph is a genuine upgrade for STRUCTURE questions (what exists, what a
function calls, clustering, fan-in ranking) and must NOT be trusted alone for REACHABILITY or
liveness/deadness. The text-search prior from the previous session is not superseded — the two instruments
are complementary, and a disagreement between them is a finding to investigate, not a tie to break by
preferring the newer tool.

SUBSTANTIVE LEAD FOR THE A1 QUESTION, established while calibrating (NOT a verdict):

title: SPIKE (user-guided): does the alternate graph API belong in den-hoag or gen?
description:
NEEDS A USER-GUIDED DESIGN DECISION, and it is a design spike, not a lookup.

THE VISION (owner): an alternate den API that makes graph expressions explicit — a companion to, and alternative to, den's current surface.

THE QUESTION: is that a den-hoag surface, or a den BINDING of a gen-level surface? gen-graph already owns accessor-based query combinators (reachableFrom, canReach, dependentsOf, cycles, condensation, phaseOrder) and gen-select owns a selector algebra over graph positions with 12 constructors and adapters for both gen-scope and gen-graph. A new den API that re-expresses those would be the built-what-exists pattern this project has hit three times.

WHY IT IS GATED: specifying this before the kernel purity audit (W2) reports would design against the CURRENT representation, which is the very thing under question. If W2 finds the kernel carries value-shaped machinery, an API designed on top of it inherits the shape.

INPUT WHEN IT RUNS: the reuse-scan on den-hoag-8rf already inventoried all 20 gen libraries for query surface and found that gen-product supplies coordinate-tuple addressing (cells, coordsOf, fiber, slice, restrict) and that uniformity over a lifted graph is a THEOREM of the existing layering rather than new code. That scan is directly reusable here.

title: W3: drift and lost-context sweep over the 2026-07 corpus
description:
Sweep 66 specs/2026-07-*.md + 151 plans/2026-07-*.md for design drift, architecture errors and lost context.

LOOK FOR, in order of demonstrated yield:
  - SUPERSEDED DECISIONS STILL STATED AS LIVE. Known instance: REFERENCE.md Chosen #3 says the three resolution layers run sequentially while L214 says they alternate in a joint fixpoint and EXPLICITLY supersedes the sequential rule — the tree matches L214, and Chosen #3 was left standing.
  - THE INVERSE CASE, where the CODE is the stale artifact. Known instance: lib/production-guard.nix:11 states there is NO den.productions user surface yet, while lib/default.nix:656 declares it. Do not assume the document is always the wrong side.
  - DESIGNS WHOSE RATIONALE WAS LOST — a decision recorded with its conclusion but not its reason, which is what makes it get re-litigated.
  - CLAIMS INVERTED. Known instance: the semilattice-set discipline is documented as reserved-but-REJECTED-at-registration; it is shipped and witnessed in two ci tests.

DEPENDS ON den-hoag-9w8 for cheapness, not for correctness: the corpus reorganization manifest already classifies all 359 documents by subject, so a subject-scoped sweep is far cheaper than a flat one. It can proceed without it at higher cost.

OVERLAPS den-hoag-deb (orphaned pre-beads work). Coordinate: deb finds work that was SCOPED and never tracked; W3 finds statements that are WRONG. A document can be both.

OUTPUT: findings classified as (a) document wrong, (b) design intentionally changed, (c) genuinely unimplemented — with the (a)-vs-(b) ambiguities named rather than guessed, since that distinction needs intent no measurement recovers.

title: __provider identity reconstruction is still live on the bridge path
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger part 2 (row 20.8), 2026-07-27.

REFERENCE.md "Chosen #8" states the __provider shadow-identity layer "is DELETED" and that the only
remaining __provider is "the single v1-reserved literal in key-classification.nix (the reserved-key
exclusion, NOT a reconstruction)".

HALF OF THAT HOLDS: annotate.nix and stamp-provider.nix are gone, and compile does ground identity on
gen-aspects' native .key. But two parts are false as written:

(i) It is NOT the single v1-reserved literal there. builtinStructuralKeys carries __contentValues,
    __providesForwarded, __ctxId, __entityKind, __parametricResolvedArgs, __scopeHandlers, __fn and __args
    alongside it.

(ii) A LIVE IDENTITY RECONSTRUCTION SURVIVES. lib/compat/den-brackets.nix:41-47 tagProvider WRITES
     result // { __provider = path; }. Its own comment says it exists "so the pipeline can compute stable
     identity ... without this, they get anonymous identities and dedup fails". It is wired in as __findFile
     at lib/compat/bridge.nix:171.

So the doc claims a layer is dissolved while a writer for it is still on the bridge path. Whether that
stamp is REMOVABLE is a code question, not a docs question — which is why this is a bead and not a ledger
row correction. The docs fix is downstream of the answer.

Relevant: the north star is dissolving effect-runtime holdovers, and a surviving identity-reconstruction
stamp is exactly that shape. See [[project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface]] and the effects audit.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ ADDENDUM — THE ARCHIVED LOG ASSERTS THIS WAS COMPLETED. It was not, and the assertion is the reason a session would stop looking.

Historical log :315 (archived at den-hoag-4kh.27) claims `__provider` was DELETED.
MEASURED at HEAD 2026-07-28: it is STILL MINTED on the compat path.
  lib/compat/den-brackets.nix:43-44 — `if builtins.isAttrs result && !(result ? __provider) && !(result ? __fn) then result // { __provider = path; }`
  18 `__provider` occurrences across lib/*.nix
  lib/compat/compile.nix:1585 still names "a bridge-side `__provider`-style annotation" as THE UPGRADE PATH
  lib/compat/compile.nix:1605-1606 still names board #58 as OPEN
Corroborated independently the same day by a second agent: `__provider` = 25 hits, all comments PLUS the one v1-reserved carve-out at lib/compat/key-classification.nix:50.

This bead already records the writer as live, so the mechanism is not news. THE NEWS IS THE FALSE COMPLETION CLAIM: a session trusting the log will not go looking, and the claim sits in the same document that is otherwise a reliable historical record. A record that is right about 900 lines and wrong about this one is more dangerous than a record that is wrong throughout.

title: claim-accessor ships an undocumented queryEdges variant outside the L4 silent/throwing contract
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger part 2 (row 15.9), 2026-07-27.

The claim-accessor ships a THIRD variant, queryEdges, that REFERENCE.md L121 does not mention. The
documented contract is a two-variant capability boundary:
  .query <kind>   SILENT  — a missing or out-of-scope claim kind yields [ ] (the exploratory-query mode)
  .rel.<kind>     THROWING — an out-of-scope kind is REPLACED with a NAMED throw

That silent-vs-throwing split is load-bearing for L4 stratified negation: a negation MUST be read through
the throwing gate, because a negation over a silently-empty predicate cannot distinguish "absent" from
"out-of-scope".

An undocumented third variant is therefore not a doc-completeness nit. If queryEdges is silent and a
consumer writes a stratified negation against it, that is precisely the error the L4 contract exists to
prevent — and the contract cannot warn about a variant it does not name.

NEEDED: establish queryEdges' silent-vs-throwing behaviour, decide whether it belongs in the documented
contract or should be internal, and if it is silent, whether the L4 guidance needs to name it explicitly.
Docs follow the answer.

title: Sweep specs/plans for orphaned pre-beads work
description:
Sweep specs/ + plans/ for DESIGNED OR SCOPED WORK that predates beads adoption and was never tracked —
work that exists as a design document and as nothing else.

CORPUS: 154 specs + 208 plans (+93 .md.tasks.json sidecars from the pre-beads task format) against 73 beads
(42 open / 30 closed / 1 in progress). Most of the corpus predates the tracker.

CLASSIFY each work-scoping document as:
  SHIPPED     — the work exists in the tree (cite the evidence)
  TRACKED     — a bead covers it (cite the id)
  SUPERSEDED  — a later document replaced it (cite which)
  ORPHANED    — designed/scoped, not shipped, not tracked, not superseded  <- THE DELIVERABLE
  HISTORICAL  — a record, review, or decision log that scopes no work

BLOCKED ON den-hoag-9w8 (corpus reorganization). Deliberate: sweeping a flat 362-document corpus costs far
more than sweeping a subject-organized one, and 9w8's manifest — filename, date, first heading, Status line,
subject — is most of the input this sweep needs. Running this first would mean building that manifest twice.

METHOD NOTES, learned this session:
- An ABSENCE claim needs a positive control on the same predicate. The h5d ledger had a predicate false-clean
  on shipped `pipe.<verb>` names because they are defined inside a `pipe = { ... }` block and used only in
  ci/. Confirm each predicate finds a known-positive before reporting nothing.
- "Not implemented" and "cut from scope" are INDISTINGUISHABLE from the tree — the h5d ledger hit this on
  fleet features. Where they cannot be separated, say so; do not pick one.
- Report coverage depth honestly. A partial sweep reported as partial is useful; reported as complete it is
  worse than nothing.

OUT OF SCOPE: gen-rebuild, hola (owner ruling). Also used/, reference-catalog/ (academic PDFs), demos/.
DO NOT create beads from findings — the orphan list comes back for review first, then gets filed.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
SIDECARS ARE THIS BEAD'S PRIMARY EVIDENCE — measured 2026-07-27, and it makes this sweep cheaper.

The 93 plans/*.md.tasks.json sidecars are the PRE-BEADS TASK FORMAT, superseded to the day (last sidecar
2026-07-25, earliest bead 2026-07-26). Their aggregate status:

  360 completed · 38 done · 1 done_except_push · 220 PENDING

220 pending tasks across 93 plans, each already carrying `subject`, `description`, `blockedBy`, and
metadata `files` / `verifyCommand` / `acceptanceCriteria`. That is a structured record of scoped work that
never completed and never migrated to the tracker — exactly what this bead is looking for, without having
to infer it from prose.

METHOD CONSEQUENCE: first pass is a JOIN, not a read. Extract the 220 pending tasks, then classify each as
SHIPPED (the work exists in the tree anyway) / TRACKED (a bead covers it) / SUPERSEDED / ORPHANED. Only the
residue needs document reading. This also means the bead is partly INDEPENDENT of den-hoag-9w8 — the
sidecar join does not need the corpus reorganized first, though the prose-reading residue still benefits.

CAUTION: `pending` in a sidecar means "not marked done in a file nobody updated after 2026-07-25". It is
evidence of an unfinished RECORD, not proof of unfinished WORK — a task may well have shipped with the
sidecar left stale. Every pending item needs a tree check before it is called orphaned, and the count 220
should never be reported as an orphan count.

title: Papers corpus reorganization: subject subfolders + cheap-tier classification
description:
SPEC (pre-review, no files moved): papers/den-architecture/plans/2026-07-27-papers-corpus-reorganization-plan.md

WHY: specs/ (154 files) and plans/ (208 .md + 93 .md.tasks.json sidecars) are flat date-ordered dumps mixing
every subject. gen-specs/ already has 23 subject subfolders and 120 files — the pattern existed and was lost.
A flat corpus makes both the design-vs-tree audit (den-hoag-h5d) and the orphaned-work sweep expensive.

MEASURED: filenames are YYYY-MM-DD-<subject-slug>.md, so the slug carries the subject — that is what makes a
cheap classification tier viable. But slug keywords cover only a MINORITY: hoag 63 / den-hoag 55 (a subset) /
gen-schema 17 / parity 8 / gen-aspects 7 / nix-config 5 / rest <= 4. A large remainder names a TOPIC rather
than a subject (hero-canvas-animation, generic-sidecars, library-decomposition). The residue is what the
cheap tier exists for.

THE HAZARD, and it shapes the design: 185 papers files carry 416 references to 179 DISTINCT specs//plans/
paths; 108 memory files reference them; 14 beads; 2 den-hoag tracked files. A move without a rewrite breaks
all of it. Mitigation is the cheapest tier of all and uses NO model: the move manifest IS the rewrite map,
applied as pure textual substitution, plus a MOVES.md redirect index generated from the same manifest.
ACCEPTANCE TEST: zero references match a specs//plans/ path that no longer exists.

PIPELINE, cheapest first:
  T0  deterministic, no model — build manifest (filename, date, first heading, Status line, sidecar pairing),
      apply an explicit keyword->subject map, emit subject|UNRESOLVED + confidence. A .md.tasks.json sidecar
      ALWAYS moves with its parent and is never classified independently.
  T1  CHEAP AGENT (haiku), manifest METADATA ONLY — never reads file bodies, which is what keeps it cheap and
      makes a small model appropriate. Returns subject + confidence, instructed to answer UNSURE rather than
      guess. Batched.
  T2  orchestrator — adjudicates only UNSURE and disagreements. Input should be tens of files, not hundreds.
  T0' deterministic apply — moves, reference rewrite, MOVES.md. No model.

TAXONOMY: subject names MIRROR the existing 23 gen-specs/ folders so one vocabulary serves both trees, plus
non-library subjects derived from the corpus (den-v1, den-hoag, nix-config, diagram, theory, infra,
unrelated). Recommended layout is subject subfolders INSIDE the artifact-type dirs (specs/<subject>/,
plans/<subject>/), leaving gen-specs/<subject>/ unchanged as living CONTRACTS — folding 63 dated hoag design
docs into gen-specs/den-hoag/ would bury its 6 contract files under their own history.

OUT OF SCOPE: gen-rebuild and hola (owner ruling) — recorded in the manifest as deliberately skipped, not as
unresolved. Also untouched: used/, reference-catalog/ (academic PDFs), demos/, parity/, STATUS/. Content is
never rewritten, nothing is deleted, and SHIPPED-vs-ORPHANED is explicitly NOT decided here — that is the
audit this unblocks, and conflating them would put a judgment call inside a mechanical pass.

OPEN FOR REVIEW (spec §8): (1) subject-inside-artifact-type vs subject-first — expensive to reverse once 416
references are rewritten; (2) does archive/ stay a location or become per-subject, i.e. how do the lifecycle
and subject axes compose; (3) do the 93 .md.tasks.json sidecars survive at all, or are they superseded by
beads — answer BEFORE the move or the work is wasted; (4) is theory a subject or a cross-cutting tag.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER DECISIONS (2026-07-27).

LAYOUT (spec §8.1) — SUBJECT INSIDE ARTIFACT-TYPE. specs/<subject>/ and plans/<subject>/;
gen-specs/<subject>/ stays untouched as living contracts. Smallest move, preserves the artifact-type
distinction that already exists, adds only the missing subject axis.

SIDECARS (spec §8.3) — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, and my framing in the spec was WRONG.
The 93 .md.tasks.json files are SUPERSEDED BY BEADS, confirmed to the day: last sidecar 2026-07-25,
earliest bead 2026-07-26. Schemas map 1:1 — id / subject / status / description / blockedBy /
metadata{files, verifyCommand, acceptanceCriteria} onto bd's issue, dependency and acceptance fields.

But they are NOT dead weight, which is what the spec speculated. Status distribution across all 93:
  360 completed · 38 done · 1 done_except_push · 220 PENDING
220 pending tasks that predate the tracker, already structured, carrying `files` and `acceptanceCriteria`.
That is den-hoag-deb's PRIMARY EVIDENCE, not clutter.
=> ARCHIVE IN PLACE (do not distribute into subject folders, do not delete), and mine them as deb's
   first-pass input. deb is consequently cheaper than specced and partly independent of this reorg.

CORPUS SUBJECT — NO. Only 10 documents mention den-configs, and they are den-hoag work ABOUT the external
corpus rather than work ON it. A tag, not a folder. denconfigs-revalidated resolves to den-hoag.

CLASSIFICATION COMPLETE, 359/359, persisted at plans/2026-07-27-papers-corpus-manifest.tsv (with .bak):
  T0 deterministic 166 · T0b heading-aware +44 · T1 haiku (metadata only) +149 · T2 orchestrator +12
  corrected, 4 held for owner.
  den-hoag 189 · gen-schema 32 · gen-aspects 30 · unrelated 24 · gen 22 · gen-other 12 · parity 7 ·
  nix-config 6 · UNSURE 4 · rest <= 4.
BOTH VALIDATION GATES FOUND REAL DEFECTS: my deterministic tier ran ~14% wrong until sampling caught it
(slug tokens beat headings); haiku ~6-12% with one clear miss (fleet-pipe-visualization -> diagram).
Neither surfaced without sampling a bucket that looked fine in aggregate.

4 STILL HELD FOR OWNER (T2:HOLD-owner): denconfigs-revalidated (now resolved to den-hoag per above),
f1-inputs-self-nodes-design (gen-scope vs den-hoag — the inputs'/self' battery straddles both),
den-server-m1-projection-plan (den-server/gen-lsp vs den-hoag), bitstream-f1-gap-diagnosis (reads like
neither den nor gen).

STILL GATED: T0' (the moves + the 416-reference rewrite) has no remaining blocker except execution.

title: [codebase-memory-mcp] Nix bindings mint no Variable nodes — nix_var_types has no name resolver
description: nix_var_types = {"binding"} is declared in lang_specs.c, but extract_defs.c has a Nix name resolver only for function_expression (line 827, via the parent binding's attrpath). A plain 'x = value;' binding therefore resolves no name and mints nothing. Measured: den-hoag Variable count is 10 on v0.8.1, 10 on HEAD, and 10 on HEAD+the function-header fix — unchanged across all three, and those 10 are not Nix. Fix shape mirrors the existing function resolver: for a 'binding' node take child_by_field_name(attrpath) then its 'attr'. Separate from den-hoag-cah; do not bundle.
acceptance_criteria: A let/attrset binding of a non-function value mints a Variable node with the correct name

description: nix-config pins pkgs.codebase-memory-mcp from nixpkgs at v0.8.1 (2026-06-12), which predates Nix def/call extraction (landed 0849f28c 2026-06-27, shipped v0.9.0). title: Docs conformance pass: measure den-hoag design docs against the tree
description:
SPEC (pre-review, no edits): papers/den-architecture/plans/2026-07-27-docs-conformance-pass-plan.md

GAP: DEVIATIONS.md and CHANGES.md are both spec-vs-spec (which spec superseded which). NOTHING tracks spec-vs-IMPLEMENTATION, so doc drift has no detector. Same failure shape as den-hoag-9xo.27 at the code level: the only check that exists cannot observe the thing that drifted. The tell is two independent docs carrying the SAME phantom vocabulary (den.collections, spawn/emit) — they were updated from each other, not from the tree.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 vs den-hoag c0aa7be:
- REFERENCE.md 'Shipped vs Spec-Only Status' is INVERTED — lists HOAG eval model / 12 attributes / buildRoots / parseParent / neededBy / bind.wrapAll as NOT IMPLEMENTED; all ship. Only den.collections is absent (0 files) and that is a rename that never happened (den.quirks, 9 files).
- Library inventory: doc says '8 gen libraries'; den-hoag flake has 19. Missing incl. gen-resolve — which the doc's own Phase-5 sections lean on as the one conductor.
- Purity claim reversed: gen-schema/gen-aspects are no longer nixpkgs-lib-tethered (re-hosted on gen-merge).
- 12-attribute table drifted structurally: guard-set no longer exists (folded into resolved-aspects self-circular, default.nix:897); 9 attributes have no row.
- Headline compression claim '~1,010-1,510 lines replacing ~7,000, 4-5x' vs measured lib/ = 24,655 (kernel 13,337 + compat 11,318). Kernel-only is ~10x the estimate. Needs an EXPLANATION, not a silent restatement.
- specs/2026-05-24-unified-vocabulary.md is a redirect to ~/Documents/repos/gen-docs/ — path does not exist. Live: ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen/TERMINOLOGY.md.
- TERMINOLOGY.md is well-maintained on the LIBRARY axis (18 libs, 2026-07-06) but its den-side vocabulary is stale identically to REFERENCE.md. gen-class and gen-link have no entry. gen-link's ABSENCE from den-hoag's lock is CORRECT (verified: no node, no import; origin identity routes through gen-aspects aspectId).

SCOPE: two repos, five files — papers (REFERENCE, new CONFORMANCE.md, CHANGES, the redirect stub) + the gen repo (TERMINOLOGY.md, docs-only commit). NO code changes.

METHOD: every corrected claim sourced to a COMMAND recorded beside it in CONFORMANCE.md. Each drift classified (a) doc wrong (b) intentional evolution -> CHANGES.md (c) genuinely unimplemented, with evidence. Deliverable is a re-runnable ledger, not prose — that is what makes the NEXT drift detectable.

NEXT STEP IS REVIEW OF THE SPEC. See §9 open questions (CONFORMANCE.md separate vs inline; whether the gen-repo commit is its own change; where the line-budget finding lands; whether to drop per-library test counts as a drift class).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
RESOLVED (owner, 2026-07-27) — spec §9.4: per-library TEST COUNTS are DROPPED as a class, not re-verified.

title: [gen-schema] Composite registries: grouped indexing + uniform meta-query
description:
den's grammar den.hosts.<system>.<hostname> is a COMPOSITE registry — per-system sub-registries composing one host kind. gen-schema cannot represent it, so den-hoag FLATTENS it (lib/compat/registry.nix preprocessHosts + flattenRegistry) to fit a single attrsOf, and meta-query over the composite then has nowhere to live.

Root gap (measured 2026-07-27): gen-schema has NO registry-level surface at all. Introspection is entirely schema-level (_kindNames/_topology/_edges/_roots/_leaves on the schema option); mkInstanceRegistry returns a bare merge.mkOption. Kinds are first-class, instances are first-class, registries are not.

Depends on the registry DESCRIPTOR landing first (den-hoag-m0a): the descriptor carries index.shape, so grouped registries slot into the same field without a breaking change.

BEFORE DESIGNING: reuse-scan the gen ecosystem — gen-graph query combinators, gen-select selector algebra, gen-resolve. 'Uniform query over a grouped collection' may already exist one layer up. Prior art on building-what-exists is recorded in [[feedback_reuse_scan_before_build]].

Owner framing: pure gen libs must have real usage outside den; prefer a general library solution over den-hoag special-casing.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
REUSE-SCAN COMPLETE (2026-07-27, all 20 gen libs, read-only). Verdict per capability:

CAP 1 — grouped indexing (path/tuple addressing, group coordinate on each entry)
  declaration layer: DOES NOT EXIST.
  graph/query layer: EXISTS FULLY — gen-product. Cells are coordinate tuples; view.nix:161,219-227
  nodeData = coordsOf cellId puts the coordinate on every cell; fiber (default.nix:37-39) addresses one
  group; slice composes fixings (view.nix:249-267); restrict enumerates sparsely without materializing
  the dense product (membership.nix:37-63,132-144). factor.nix:26-40 already accepts a non-id_hash
  key/entryOf pair, so plain system strings are legal coordinates.

CAP 2 — uniform meta-query over the composite: PARTIALLY EXISTS.
  The uniformity MECHANISM ships and does not branch on shape — a product IS an accessor graph, so every
  gen-graph query and gen-select adapter runs unchanged. Missing piece is only the LIFT: gen-graph
  registry.fromRegistry is flat-only BY CONSTRUCTION (gen-graph/lib/registry.nix:11,
  nodes = builtins.attrNames registry).

NESTED-REGISTRY QUESTION — ANSWERED NO, tested both directions. This was the most likely
"it already exists" result and it fails:
  FORWARD: mkInstanceRegistry returns an mkOption, NOT a type (gen-schema/lib/instance.nix:478), so it
  cannot be a freeformType; a nested registry must hang off a NAMED option, yielding
  den.hosts.<sys>.hosts.<name> — not den's grammar. It also requires <system> to be a declared KIND with
  instances; den's keys are lib.systems.flakeExposed strings, and a non-kind can never enter _topology
  (kind-to-kind off a parent collection, entry-type.nix:328-357).
  BACKWARD (cost if forced): drops the ENTIRE apply pipeline — ref-binding validation, deferred coerce,
  refinements, validators, derive. The pipeline is flat-keyed throughout, and validators infer option
  names via attrNames (head (attrValues instances)) (instance.nix:344-348) — on two-level input that
  reads HOST NAMES AS OPTION NAMES. options.name defaults to the immediate submodule key (:54-57), so
  under attrsOf (attrsOf ...) the group coordinate is structurally INVISIBLE to the entry, which is
  exactly why den-hoag hand-injects it (den-hoag/lib/compat/registry.nix:114-121).

THE GAP — two pieces, two libraries, do not build a third thing:
  gen-schema: mkInstanceRegistry needs an INDEX SHAPE parameter — type nests to declared depth,
  applyPipeline walks at that depth instead of assuming one level, group coordinate materializes on
  entries. This is EXACTLY the index.shape field den-hoag-y53's __registry descriptor reserves.
  gen-graph: extend registry.fromRegistry to lift a grouped registry into the accessor-graph convention.
  That is the WHOLE of cap 2 — uniformity is then a theorem of the existing layering, not new code.

NEW SUB-GAP, not previously on this bead: den admits a UNION of two index shapes on ONE option
(den.hosts.slab carrying a system field, OR den.hosts.x86_64-linux.slab). NO gen library models a
declaration accepting two shapes. There is also no general shape-coercion-at-registration mechanism:
mkInstanceRegistry's apply runs POST-merge, too late to reshape input before type-checking. den-hoag's
two-phase workaround (permissive deepMergeAttrs collector, then apply re-merges through the strict inner
type, registry.nix:446-522) is built on the CONSUMER's nixpkgs lib.types — not on the gen substrate at all.

FALSE FRIEND, recorded so it is not mistaken for prior art: gen-flake selectHosts (compose.nix:169-171)
says "nested registry" meaning a registry at a nested option PATH — still a flat attrset, not grouping.

Adjacent, non-transferring: gen-aspects flatten (path-keyed string identity, homogeneous unbounded
recursion); gen-class mkClasses (real partition-by-key, no lookup surface, no member coordinate);
gen-link disjointUnion (composes per-group subgraphs by ID QUALIFICATION, the same move as den-hoag's
node-multiplication ruling, not tuple indexing).

CONSEQUENCE FOR den-hoag-y53: its spec 9.3 asked whether index earns its place before this arc is
designed. Independent evidence says YES — the composite gap lands exactly on that field.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (2026-07-27) — the two index shapes: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE IS FINE.

The reuse-scan flagged a sub-gap: den admits a UNION of two index shapes on ONE option, and no gen library
models a declaration accepting two shapes. That sub-gap is now OUT OF SCOPE — a registry declares ONE index
shape. The composite arc therefore needs grouped `<system>.<host>` ONLY.

Owner adds: `host.system` (the FLAT form — `den.hosts.slab` carrying a `system` field) is largely
UNDOCUMENTED in den; most external users are still on `system.host` (the two-level
`den.hosts.<system>.<hostname>` grammar).

CONSEQUENCES:
- The shape-coercion-at-registration gap the scan reported (mkInstanceRegistry's `apply` runs post-merge,
  too late to reshape input) does NOT need a general mechanism. den-hoag's `preprocessHosts`
  (lib/compat/registry.nix:468) stays a COMPAT-BOUNDARY coercion for the undocumented flat form, and is a
  deprecation candidate rather than something to lift into gen.
- The arc's declaration surface is single-shape, which is materially smaller than the scan assumed.

DOC CONFLICT TO RESOLVE (feeds den-hoag-h5d): gen-specs/den-hoag/REFERENCE.md calls the TWO-LEVEL form the
"legacy" one and presents the flat form as the enabling feature — the owner's reading is the inverse (the
two-level form is what external users use; the flat form is undocumented). One of those is wrong and the
docs currently assert the one the owner contradicts.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (2026-07-27) — DOGFOODING: internally den-hoag uses gen modules EXCLUSIVELY; nixpkgs lib only
when TRANSLATING or TESTING.

This bears directly on the arc. The reuse-scan measured that den-hoag's own host-registry machinery —
`mkHostsOption`'s two-phase trick (permissive `deepMergeAttrs` collector, then `apply` re-merging through the
strict inner type, lib/compat/registry.nix:440-522) — is built on the CONSUMER's nixpkgs `lib.types`, not on
the gen substrate at all. Under this ruling that is a violation, not a detail: it is den-hoag's own registry
construction, not a translation.

So moving `den.hosts` onto the gen substrate is now a REASON for this arc, independent of query uniformity.
The scan's finding that `den.hosts.<system>.<hostname>` is built by `mkHostsOption` and NOT by
`mkInstanceRegistry` is the same fact seen from the other side: the one composite registry den has was built
outside gen because gen could not express it.

Boundary question the arc must answer explicitly rather than assume: the bridge's `options.den` declaration
uses nixpkgs `lib.types.submodule` (lib/compat/bridge.nix:447). That one is plausibly legitimate TRANSLATION
— it is where den-hoag meets the consumer's flake-parts/nixpkgs module system. `mkHostsOption` is not.
Draw the line where the ruling puts it, and state which side each site falls on.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
PARKED BY OWNER RULING 2026-07-27 (full text on den-hoag-4kh.7, which is closed as resolved).

★ THE NEW BLOCKING EDGE ON den-hoag-4kh ENCODES CORRECTNESS, NOT COST. Do not strip it as a cheapness
dependency. This project has previously had two blocking edges removed for encoding cost against the beads'
own text — this is not one of them, and here is the reason in full so a future sweep can check rather than
guess.

THEORY: compat is a THIN VAN WYK MAP ONTO THE KERNEL'S REPRESENTATION. This work hardens a compat seam
(y53: the bridge arm feeding _registryKinds at lib/compat/ingest.nix:528; 8rf: registry shape). A map onto
an unsettled denotation is built against a moving target — constructing a morphism WHOSE CODOMAIN IS STILL
CHANGING. The kernel-purity arc is precisely the work of fixing that codomain. So the dependency is not
"cheaper to do later", it is "the thing this maps onto is not yet defined".

UNPARK CONDITION — AN EVENT, NOT A DATE: when the kernel-purity arc has ruled on the registry/identity
representation these seams map onto.

WHAT DID NOT PARK, and why the distinction matters:
 · den-hoag-m0a STAYS OPEN as the defect record. A declared registry resolving to NO kind, reaching the
   fleet EMPTY with nothing reddening, is MEASURED FACT and belongs in the graph on its own — regardless of
   which remedy is chosen or whether the chosen remedy changes shape. SEPARATE THE DEFECT FROM THE REMEDY.
   Beads hold VALIDATED work: a measured defect qualifies, a proposed fix does not. Same treatment as
   den-hoag-4kh.12.
 · den-hoag-00g PROCEEDS. gen-merge silently right-biasing a redeclared option WHERE NIXPKGS ABORTS is a
   soundness violation in the algebra itself, independent of den-hoag's representation, so no kernel-shape
   risk attaches to fixing it. y53 was blocked on it regardless, so this ordering costs nothing even on the
   parked branch.

title: [v1 defect] policy relation has 70 nodes and 0 edges; and the graph is a forest, not a rooted DAG
description:
V1 DEFECT. A relation exists as a NODE ROLE with NO CORRESPONDING EDGE, in every
config measured. This is "every relation an edge" violated inside v1 itself.

policyEdges (graph.nix:515-530) emits style="policy" ONLY when entry.to != null.
MEASURED on nix-config: `to` is null on ALL 843 nodes, while `from` is non-null
on exactly the 70 isPolicyDispatch nodes. So ZERO policy edges exist in ANY
measured IR, in ANY of the 12 configs.

AND IT WOULD DANGLE IF FIXED NAIVELY: the intended target id (ctx_<kind>) refers
to graph.entityKinds, which fleet-ir.nix never copies into `nodes`. So even with
`to` populated, the edge would point at a node that is not in the graph.

⇒ 70 policy-dispatch nodes, 0 policy edges, and the target vocabulary is not in
the node set.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md (papers 9eb5439).

RELATED, from the same map: the graph is a FOREST, NOT A ROOTED DAG. With the
flake root filtered out (correctly -- see den-hoag-9xo.31), every config has >=1
parentless scope and 3 have more: nix-config has 3 roots (fleet:fleet,
flake-system:aarch64-darwin, flake-system:x86_64-linux), example and fleet-demo
have 2, and nvf-standalone has NINE ROOTS, ZERO EDGES AND ZERO ASPECT NODES --
a valid den template whose entire topology is nine isolated points.

WHY BOTH MATTER: the owner's target is "correct and pure topology -- every
entity a node, every relation an edge". These are the two places v1's own graph
does not meet it. Under the standing instruction, where den-hoag uncovers a real
v1 defect we correct it rather than reproduce it -- so these bound what "parity
with v1" can mean.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: Most external den configs cannot evaluate against their own pin or den HEAD — the templates are the usable witness set
description:
MOST EXTERNAL den CONFIGS CANNOT BE EVALUATED against either their own den pin
or den HEAD. This bounds what "parity with v1" can be measured against.

MEASURED (papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md, papers
9eb5439): of 9 external configs attempted, 3 produced full IRs.

  against their OWN den pin:
    dotfiles, denix, oceangreendev, nixos.den, slashfiles
    -> error: attribute 'capture' missing
    These configs pin den revisions PREDATING den.lib.capture.

  against LOCAL den HEAD (API drift):
    slashfiles      -> option '...users.theutz.id_hash' is read-only, set multiple times
    gwenodai-nixos  -> function 'anonymous lambda' called without required argument 'class'
    oceangreendev   -> option 'perSystem.x86_64-linux.__provider' does not exist
    adda-nixos-config -> attribute 'each' missing

  not den failures:
    nixfos -> private input (ssh://git@github.com/xfo-0/moor), fetch failure
    several -> HTTP 403 from api.github.com after lock deletion (harness artifact)

Templates fared better: 8 of 13 produced IRs. The 5 failures were mostly BY
DESIGN (bogus is deliberately broken; noflake has no flake.nix; ci is a test
harness) plus 2 harness artifacts.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXIT CONDITION. "Parity with v1" has a moving target: the
external corpus largely cannot run against current den, so it cannot serve as a
parity oracle without first resolving which den revision parity is against.
DEN'S OWN TEMPLATES ARE THE USABLE WITNESS SET -- they track den, they are
authored by den, and 8 of 13 evaluate.

⇒ AND IT REFRAMES THE STANDING RULE. "Gate on den-surface expressibility, not
corpus-presence" is right, but the practical corpus is the TEMPLATES plus
nix-config, not the 19 external configs. Claiming a surface is unused should
cite the templates.

Related: reference memory `reference_den_corpus_set`.
NOT SCHEDULED -- this is a constraint to plan around, not a task.

title: [v1 defect] scope tree and aspect graph key on different identities; three of the owner's host scopes are orphans
description:
V1 DEFECT, and it affects the owner's own fleet TODAY.

The scope tree and the aspect graph key on DIFFERENT IDENTITIES, and the aspect
graph silently drops the difference. Scopes are keyed by FULL CTX; aspect nodes
are keyed by host NAME (hostGraphs.<name>, prefixId hostName). Where an entity
has two scopes, lib.findFirst collapses them -- in THREE places:

  fleet-ir.nix:341     picks one host scope per host name for the root edge
  context.nix:67-69    picks one scope per (kind,name) for the projection itself
  fleet-ir.nix:360-364 does it again for pipe-flow endpoints

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE on nix-config: 11 host scopes, only 8 hostRootEdges.
axon-01, axon-02 and axon-03's CLUSTER-PATH SCOPES ARE ORPHANS -- zero children,
no aspect graph, no root edge. They exist as nodes with a containment edge in
and nothing else.

It is the ONLY config in the 12 measured that exhibits it, and it exhibits it
because it is the only one with a `cluster` kind creating a SECOND ROUTE to a
host. So it is a defect that only appears once an entity is reachable by two
paths -- exactly the multi-attachment shape den-hoag's node multiplication was
built for.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md (papers 9eb5439).

WHY IT MATTERS FOR den-hoag: this is v1 silently losing a scope. Under the
owner's exit condition (parity with v1) the question is NOT "does den-hoag do
the same" -- the owner's standing instruction is that where den-hoag uncovers a
REAL DEFECT in v1, we CORRECT it. This is one, with a measurement.

NOT SCHEDULED. Adjacent to den-hoag-9xo.9 (cluster-path routes) and to the
node-multiplication arc.

title: edges.nix to-vocabulary is documented and unvalidated; a typo silently degrades to the default arm
description:
edges.nix:97 documents the `to` vocabulary for relation edge targets. THE
VOCABULARY IS NOT VALIDATED -- a typo'd member is accepted silently.

MEASURED (a15-spike, 2026-07-27; papers plans/2026-07-27-a15-spike.md section 3,
papers 5f825a9).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: den-hoag-9xo.30's candidate S adds a FOURTH member to that
vocabulary --

  structural = false (default) -> to = "query"      (query surface only)
  structural = true            -> to = "structure"  (off-trace AND
                                                     reachability-bearing)

A typo'd "structure" under S would silently fall back to the default arm, so a
relation the author declared as reachability-bearing would be treated as
query-only. THE ROOT WOULD NOT EXIST AND NOTHING WOULD SAY SO -- which is the
exact silent-loss class den-hoag-9xo.8, .26 and m0a are all instances of.

⇒ D2 IS A PREREQUISITE OF S, not an adjacent nit. S amplifies an unchecked
vocabulary from three members to four, and the new member is the one that
decides whether a node materialises.

Note candidate C (relation rows feed containmentAttachments directly) does NOT
touch the vocabulary and so does not amplify this -- one of the reasons C is
cheaper. See the cost table in section 6.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): validate `to` against the declared vocabulary
and ABORT NAMED on an unknown member. Arm both ways -- a valid member that must
pass, and a near-miss typo that must abort FOR ITS OWN REASON rather than by
failing something downstream.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: [gen-schema] mkSchemaOption silently drops unknown kind keys — a typo is indistinguishable from an unsupported field
description:
gen-schema's mkSchemaOption keeps a FIXED KEY SET and SILENTLY DROPS unknown
keys from a kind declaration. No abort, no warning -- the field is simply
absent from the processed kind value.

MEASURED (denhoag-writer, 2026-07-27, while implementing den-hoag-9xo.13's
route 2):

  declared:  den.schema.host = { parent = "env"; parentRef = "environment";
                                 attachIf = "intoAttr"; }

  processed keys: [__functor keySemantics kind methods mixins options parent
                   refinements refs strict validators]

Both new keys absent. An implementation reading them off the processed kind
value gets null for every kind, attaches nothing, AND LOOKS LIKE THE CODE IS
WRONG rather than like the declaration was discarded.

WHY THIS IS THE ARC'S RECURRING SHAPE: a DECLARED FACT the framework accepts
and does not read. Same family as den-hoag-9xo.8 (registry kinds never
resolved), .9 (intoAttr ignored), .26 (instances dropped), and the inert
den.schema.<kind>.excludes bead -- in every case the user wrote something
true, the framework took it without complaint, and nothing consumed it.

ROUTE 2 DID NOT NEED THE FIX: den.attach lives on den's OWN surface, needs no
gen-schema change, and is arguably where attachment resolution belongs anyway.
So this is filed as a defect in its own right, not as a blocker.

DECISION THIS BEAD NEEDS: should mkSchemaOption ABORT on an unknown key rather
than dropping it? A typo in a kind declaration is currently indistinguishable
from a field the framework does not support, and both are silent. Note the
tension: den-hoag's own compat boundary deliberately accepts and ignores some
v1 surface, so a blanket abort may be wrong -- the decision is where the line
sits, and whether an unknown key on a KIND (as opposed to on an instance) is
ever legitimate.

Cross-reference: gen-aspects' Model C already settled the analogous question
for aspect keys -- scalar-undeclared aborts as a typo, attrset-undeclared is
admitted lazily as a nested aspect. That precedent is the obvious starting
point and may already decide this.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: compat-identity-boundary lint misses bare-id sites it exists to catch; the design's table has grown every review round
description:
ci/tests/compat-identity-boundary.nix is meant to catch bare "${kind}:${name}"
id construction. It does not catch them all, and it is DEMONSTRABLY BLIND to at
least one site the .13 default-attachment design itself lists.

FOUND BY: design-reviewer, rev 6 review (papers bc7981c), while checking whether
the design's hand-maintained site table was trustworthy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TABLE. The .13 design has carried a list of
bare-id sites through four review rounds and EACH ROUND ADDED ONE:
  round 1  the original seven -- four of them turned out to be COMMENTS, and
           four real sites were missing (two of which .13 had listed and the
           design silently dropped)
  round 2  structural.nix:225-233 vs :365-367 -- the two consumers ALREADY
           DISAGREE, one aborts on N>1 while the other fans out
  round 3  ancNodeId (staged-resolution.nix:76-87) -- inside the seam the
           design depends on; multiplication was built CHILD-side only, the
           parent side of containment is bare throughout
  round 4  fleet.nix:125 -- __containment from bare coordinate-root ids,
           feeding resolved-aspects.nix:185/:197, so a multi-attached host
           leaves every user cell naming a node that was never built

A list that needs extending every round is not a list, it is a symptom. The
lint is the durable fix and it is the thing that is broken.

THE ARC'S OWN RULE APPLIES TO THE LINT ITSELF: a check that cannot match the
at-risk path is not a check. This one passes while sites it exists to catch go
unlisted -- the same shape as .8 surviving a green suite, one level up.

DECISION THIS BEAD NEEDS: widen the lint's predicate so it finds the sites the
design enumerates, THEN delete the design's table and let the lint be the
authority. Arm it both ways -- a bare construction it must catch, and a
legitimately-single-attachment site it must NOT flag -- otherwise a widened
predicate that flags everything is as useless as one that flags nothing.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so the next round does not add a fifth table entry.

title: [gen-merge] deprecationMessage never read; getSubModules/substSubModules divergent on 4 of 5 containers
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-merge. Two protocol findings surfaced by wj0's work, neither in
wj0's original four, neither actioned.

--- 1. deprecationMessage is stored but NEVER READ ---

gen-merge stores deprecationMessage faithfully on a type record, so a
field-presence check passes. Nothing ever reads it, so the warning is never
emitted.

MEASURED (genmerge-writer, 2026-07-27), direct (non-nested) use of a deprecated
type:
    nixpkgs    warned = 1
    gen-merge  warned = 0

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and why the method matters: this came out of the POSITIVE
CONTROL for a different question. The audit had listed "nestedTypes deprecation
walk parity" as UNVERIFIED. That premise is FALSE -- nixpkgs does not walk
nestedTypes for deprecation at all (lib/modules.nix:1139 reads only
opt.type.deprecationMessage, the outer type's own field; the only nestedTypes
read at :1521 is unrelated). A nested deprecated type warns on NEITHER engine.

Without the direct-use control in the same run, that would have been reported
as "nested deprecation: parity, both silent" -- true, and it would have hidden
that gen-merge cannot emit the warning AT ALL.

Same shape as the original wj0 catalogue: field PRESENT, behaviour ABSENT.
test-protocol-complete asserts presence only.

--- 2. getSubModules / substSubModules, protocol rows 10 and 11 ---

nixpkgs propagates the element's; gen-merge returns null / `_m: null` on
attrsOf, lazyAttrsOf, listOf, nullOr, deferredModule. 4 of 5 divergent.

Outside the getSubOptions scope wj0 covered. gen-merge has shipped the
implemented-getSubOptions / null-getSubModules combination on the containers
since 8daa25d without incident, so this is not urgent -- but it is the same
family and the same presence-vs-behaviour gap.

--- NOT IN SCOPE (owner ruling 2026-07-27, do not re-litigate) ---

specialArgs propagation is NOT a divergence: a parent specialArg read inside a
submodule body fails on BOTH engines for the same reason. gen-merge's submodule
is equivalent to nixpkgs' submodule. The propagating shape is
submoduleWith { specialArgs = ...; }, which gen-merge deliberately does not
ship. Settled, nothing owed.

title: [gen-schema] strict mode names the INSTANCE as the undeclared key when a kind declares zero options
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-schema. Work happens in ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen-schema.
Tracked here because this is where we dispatch from.

A kind declaring ZERO options reports the INSTANCE NAME as the undeclared key,
so the strict-mode error names the wrong thing and its suggested fix is
nonsense.

Observed (denhoag-writer, 2026-07-27, converting ci/tests/_lib/den-compat-test
onto a real mkInstanceRegistry):

  STRICT MODE: "prod" is not declared on environment.
  Fix: schema.environment.options.prod = mkOption { ... };

"prod" is the INSTANCE name, not a key the author wrote. The suggested fix
would declare an option named after one instance. Correct diagnostic would name
the kind as having no declared options at all, or name the actual undeclared
key.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE, not a fix: the scaffold's environment kind was given a
`domain` option so it has a non-empty option set. den-hoag-9xo.23 does not chase
this.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond cosmetics: strict mode is a guard, and a guard whose
message names the wrong entity sends the reader to the wrong file. This arc has
repeatedly found that a diagnostic naming the wrong thing costs more than no
diagnostic -- see the bare `_type` collision key that named nothing until a path
prefix was threaded through it (DL-HS-70 method note a).

Reproduce: declare a kind with an empty options set, build a registry through
mkInstanceRegistry, instantiate one member, force it.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so it is not re-discovered.
close_reason:
Fixed upstream in gen-schema af3dbe9 (pushed): one hoisted primitiveTypeNames/isPrimitiveOption at lib/identity.nix:33, both local copies deleted. Two copies is HOW they stop agreeing, so the twin's own header claim ('can drift from neither') is now structural rather than aspirational.

den-hoag bumped past it at b2e5373 (three targeted --update-input, node-by-node diff after each, exactly the named node moved). parity's corpus/gen-schema node deliberately NOT moved -- e789c334 is the FROZEN CORPUS's own pin and moving it would invalidate every comparison the parity gate makes.

THE INVARIANT WAS ALREADY UNDER TEST AND THE TEST COULD NOT FAIL. gen-schema's test-forKind-matches-module asserts twin == stamp, but its fixture declares the identity field genMerge.types.int -- and int is the ONE name both type systems share. It stayed green through the entire divergence. Third independent arrival at the same rule in one day, from a new angle: A FIXTURE SAMPLED FROM THE AGREEING CASE CANNOT WITNESS DISAGREEMENT.

New test test-forKind-matches-module-nixpkgs-str, both halves armed:
  fixed                          equality PASS  contents PASS   green
  one shared list, str removed   equality PASS  contents FAIL   red
  twin given a private list back equality FAIL  contents PASS   red
Row 2 is why the contents pin exists: both sides degenerate together, equality
agrees perfectly, and only the contents pin catches it. Neither assertion is
redundant -- demonstrated, not assumed.

The den-hoag drift guard shipped too (compat-registry-engine::test-identity-reflection-agrees-with-the-stamp). It fired for real on the bump: equality held true across the move while only the contents pin shifted, so the two reflections agreed BEFORE and AFTER but now agree on the RIGHT key set instead of a too-small one. Checking WHICH HALF failed before touching either is the discipline; re-baselining both would have destroyed the signal.

title: Identity reflection keys on type.name string membership, so both engines' spellings must be enumerated
description:
Identity reflection decides which kind options are identity keys by testing
opt.type.name against a HARDCODED LIST of primitive type-name strings
(primitiveTypeNames, consumed by gen-schema mkIdentityModule and its
option-level twin identityHashForKind).

That is fragile by construction: the two engines spell the same type
differently.

  nixpkgs lib.types.str  -> type.name == "str"
  gen-types str          -> type.name == "string"    <-- ONLY divergent name
  int / bool             -> identical on both engines

MEASURED (denhoag-writer, real mkInstanceRegistry, 2026-07-27):
  corpus gen-schema  e789c334  primitives ["str","int","bool"]
  den-hoag gen-schema 017062cd primitives ["string","int","bool"]
  (16 commits apart; changed by 39d3d5d0 "re-host gen-schema registry onto
  gen-merge + gen-types")

So a kind option authored lib.types.str is an identity key under one pin and
not the other, and NOTHING RAISES -- the carried id_hash is simply computed
over a different key set, and the consumer's lookup misses.

den-hoag-9xo.23 routes registryKindOf through gen-schema's own
identityHashForKind so den-hoag cannot diverge from whichever list gen-schema
carries. THAT FIX DOES NOT REMOVE THIS FRAGILITY -- it only makes den-hoag
consistent with the list. Any two components that must agree on "is this a
primitive" still agree only by both enumerating the same spellings.

The question this bead exists to settle: should identity reflection key on
type.name at all, or on something that cannot drift between engines (a
structural predicate, a type-level tag, or a single shared source for the
list)? Note gen-types' "string" vs nixpkgs' "str" may itself be worth
reconciling -- but that is a separate decision with its own consumers, and
renaming a type is not obviously the right fix.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so the fragility is not re-discovered as a bug later.
Do not chase without a decision.

Origin: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-27-suite-type-coverage-scoping.md
plus den-hoag-9xo.23's conversion of compat-registry-kind-marker.

title: Mixed attrs/fn collision silently drops the attrset arm (den.default.nixos, measured live)
description: See notes. The measured mixed case .20's guard deliberately leaves alone.
notes:
LIVE, MEASURED, and deliberately left alone by the .20 fix. Found by .20's complete census (exclusion-loop enumeration over the bridge path, 2 hits then clean).

THE INSTANCE: ci/tests/den-behavioral/static-include-dup-package.nix:132 declares `den.default.nixos` as a FUNCTION; it collides with an ATTRSET `den.default.nixos` from the scaffold. Measured `shapeAcc=attrs, shapeNew=fn` at v1DeepMerge's `else bv` (bridge.nix:76) => **the ATTRSET arm is silently discarded today.** The test passes because it only asserts the fn arm's content (services.locate.package), so nothing announces the loss.

WHY .20 DOES NOT FIX IT — and this is a scope decision, not an oversight. The .20 fix's collision branch normalizes both sides through `unwrapDeferredModule`, which is LOSSY on an attrset carrying content beside `imports`. Routing a mixed attrs/fn collision through that carrier would keep the fn and GUT the attrset — strictly worse than today's `else bv`, which at least returns one side intact. So .20's guard is deliberately `isFunction && isFunction`, narrower than its census predicate, and mixed collisions stay as they are.

=> This is the pre-existing defect .20's R7 tracked as "unmeasured". It is now MEASURED and NAMED: one live instance, on the `options.default` surface.

WHAT A FIX WOULD NEED (not designed): the attrs/fn case has no obvious correct merge. v1's answer is `aspectContentType` collecting BOTH into `__contentValues` regardless of shape (nix/lib/aspects/types.nix:404+) — so the principled fix is the same one .20 takes for fn/fn, but it cannot use the deferredModule carrier because of the sibling-content loss above. Either the carrier grows an arm for content-bearing attrsets (see den-hoag-9xo.21 — WIDER than it looks, it changes isEmptyDeferredModule's verdict for every caller), or the mixed case gets a different collection shape entirely. Scope before treating as adjacent to .20.

SURFACE NOTE: this is on `options.default` (bridge.nix:684), not `options.aspects` (:765). Both are folded by the SAME `v1DeepMerge`, and `options.default`'s own description calls it "den.default aspect — cross-module folded at the bridge boundary (v1 aspectType parity)" — so it is a class key on an aspect exactly as `den.aspects.<name>.<class>` is. Same defect, same helper, two surfaces.

NOT a regression: present before this arc, surfaced by measuring rather than by failing.

★ FRAMING CORRECTION (rung-writer, measured — supersedes the sharper reading in my filing note).

I wrote that routing this mixed collision through .20's carrier 'would keep the fn and GUT the attrset'. That is the hazard IN GENERAL, but NOT for this instance: the attrs side here has **no `imports` key**, so unwrapDeferredModule returns `[ m ]` — the module is passed through whole, nothing is gutted.

The gutting hazard is specific to CONTENT-BEARING MODULES (an attrset carrying content BESIDE `imports`), and .20's complete census found **none anywhere** — which is also what settled den-hoag-9xo.21's stop-condition as not-triggered.

=> **.22 is a PRESERVED-ARM question, not a data-loss-under-fix question.** The defect is that the attrset arm is silently discarded TODAY (measured: shapeAcc=attrs, shapeNew=fn at bridge.nix:76's `else bv`). Whoever picks it up should not inherit the belief that a carrier-based fix would actively corrupt this instance — for THIS shape it would not. The reason .20's guard stays `isFunction && isFunction` is the general hazard plus scope discipline, not a demonstrated corruption here.

The entanglement with .21 stands but is weaker than I implied: .21's helper limitation is why a carrier-based mixed fix is unsafe IN GENERAL, not why it is unsafe here.

title: unwrapDeferredModule silently drops content sitting beside imports (isEmptyDeferredModule reads it at compile.nix:348)
description: See notes.
notes:
LATENT, pre-existing, surfaced while reviewing the .20 fix design. Not introduced by that work — but the design leans harder on the same helper, which is why it is filed now.

`unwrapDeferredModule` (lib/module-shape.nix:12-17) is LOSSY on an attrset that carries content BESIDE `imports`:

    unwrapDeferredModule = m:
      if builtins.isAttrs m && m ? imports
      then builtins.concatMap unwrapDeferredModule m.imports
      else [ m ];

There is no arm for content sitting next to `imports`, so an ordinary NixOS module —
    { imports = [ ./x.nix ]; services.foo.enable = true; }
— unwraps to `[ ./x.nix ]` and **silently discards `services.foo.enable`**.

THE CONSUMER THAT MAKES IT REACHABLE: `isEmptyDeferredModule` (same file) is
    m: builtins.all (leaf: isAttrs leaf && all (k: hasPrefix "_" k) (attrNames leaf)) (unwrapDeferredModule m)
and it runs TODAY on class-key values at lib/compat/compile.nix:348. So `{ imports = [ { } ]; services.y = 1; }` unwraps to `[ { } ]`, is judged EMPTY, and the class slice is dropped as a declared no-op — losing real content, silently.

REACHABILITY — UNSETTLED, and deliberately not asserted either way. Likely unreachable post-typing, because the typed body is a pure `{ _file; imports }` wrap with no sibling content. BUT compile.nix:348 runs PRE-gen-aspects, on values that may be user-authored. That is the gap.

SETTLING TEST, already scheduled at no extra cost: the .20 design's T0.2 records per-collision ARM SHAPES. **If any class key turns out to be a content-bearing module (an attrset with `imports` AND other keys), this is LIVE** and wants its own fix. If none is, it stays latent and this bead records the shape that would make it live.

RELATION TO .20: the .20 fix's collision branch normalizes through this same helper, which is why its guard must be `isFunction && isFunction` and NOT the `||` its census predicate uses — a mixed fn/content-module collision routed through the carrier would keep the fn and GUT the module, strictly worse than today's `else bv` (which returns the whole module intact and loses the fn). That guard asymmetry is recorded in the .20 design; this bead is the underlying helper limitation it works around.

SCOPING WARNING from the .20 design work — the fix here is NOT symmetrical with .20's, and is wider than it looks.

.20's answer is to keep content-bearing modules OFF the carrier path (the fix's guard is isFunction && isFunction, deliberately narrower than its census predicate). That works because .20 only needs to avoid routing such a module through unwrapDeferredModule.

.21's answer cannot be that. The helper ITSELF has to grow an arm for sibling content — and that changes isEmptyDeferredModule's verdict for EVERY caller, not just the one that surfaced it. module-shape.nix:4-6 lists them: classSliceOf's no-op drop, compile's guard, and the annotate-battery read. A module currently judged EMPTY (because its sibling content is invisible to the unwrap) would start being judged NON-empty, which flips a no-op drop into a live slice at every one of those sites.

So: scope before treating it as a one-liner. The blast radius is the caller set, not the helper.

MEASURED, not inferred (rung-writer, by evaluation rather than inspection):
    unwrapDeferredModule { imports = [ { a = 1; } ]; services.foo.enable = true; }  =>  [ { a = 1; } ]
siblingSurvives = false. The sibling is silently gone.

FREE EVIDENCE INCOMING: .20's T0.2 census now records whether any class-key arm is a content-bearing module (an attrset with imports AND sibling content). If one exists, .21 is LIVE via compile.nix:348's pre-typing path and wants its own arc. If none does, it stays latent and the census is the record of that.

title: Correct den-hoag's recorded FALSE 'deferred gen-resolve change' (concern-productions.nix:270-271)
description:
den-hoag lib/concern-productions.nix:270-271 records VERBATIM: "The full static fix = `resolve.nta` accepting stratum + readsAttrs (a DEFERRED gen-resolve change); until then the demand-order is the honest residual."

The PREMISE is true but the CONCLUSION is FALSE — no gen-resolve change is needed. VERIFIED by orchestrator directly:
- gen-resolve/lib/equation.nix:66-73 — `nta` does hardcode readsAttrs = [] and omits stratum (so stratumOf yields "structural"). Premise correct.
- equation.nix:47-63 — `attr` takes { name; kind; compute; readsAttrs; stratum ? null; } EXPLICITLY.
- equation.nix:8-17 — `stratumOf kind explicit` returns `explicit` FIRST, for ANY kind, before any kind-based default.
- grep for .kind across gen-resolve/lib/ outside equation.nix returns EXACTLY ONE hit: schedule.nix:9 isCircular. `kind` has no other schedule or runtime effect.

=> `attr { name = "children"; kind = "nta"; readsAttrs = [ ... ]; stratum = "..."; compute = spawn; }` is a stratum-declared, read-declared, SCHEDULE-VISIBLE NTA today. `resolve.nta` is sugar for the zero-read case, not a ceiling.

This is a FIFTH instance of the 0-for-4 "needs a new/extended gen primitive" pattern (prior four all expressible via expandPreorder / wrapGatedFn / inheritSet). Fix the comment so it stops advertising a gen gap that does not exist. Per feedback_no_temporal_comments: cite the mechanism (attr/stratumOf), not a task key.
close_reason: Comment corrected @22c78c6. The false 'DEFERRED gen-resolve change' claim removed; premise (resolve.nta hardcodes readsAttrs=[] + omits stratum) retained as true. Gate SEEN: CI_EXIT=0, PARITY_EXIT=0, allEqual=true. Comment-only change (verified: zero non-comment diff lines); nix fmt clean (0 changed).

title: [meta] 'bd export' with no -o writes to stdout and exits 0 without touching the file — the committed viewer JSONL silently goes stale
description:
MEASURED 2026-07-29 at HEAD 6f30460, by accident, while preparing a routine export commit.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. After a session that created EIGHT beads and closed THREE, .beads/beads.jsonl showed a diff of 3 insertions / 2 deletions. Checked by id:
  present: den-hoag-2rh (the FIRST bead created in the session)
  ABSENT:  den-hoag-yl3, den-hoag-5ae, den-hoag-5bp, den-hoag-ag3, den-hoag-9uv, den-hoag-6jo, den-hoag-1xl
  and den-hoag-4kh.13 — closed with a reason earlier the same session — still read "status":"open" IN THE EXPORT.
POSITIVE CONTROL, same predicate same run: den-hoag-4kh.17 -> 1 hit, den-hoag-2rh -> 1 hit. The grep fires. The absence is about the file.

CAUSE, and it is a trap of the flattering kind: **bd export WITH NO -o WRITES TO STDOUT.** 'bd export' appears to succeed — it emits well-formed JSONL, scrolls past, and returns 0 — while the FILE IS NEVER TOUCHED. The correct form is 'bd export -o .beads/beads.jsonl', which reports 'Exported 269 issues to .beads/beads.jsonl'. After running it, all eight new ids are present and all three closes read "status":"closed"; the diff becomes 17 insertions / 9 deletions.
★ WHAT MADE IT SURVIVE: the file WAS modified (3+/2-), so 'git status' showed the expected churn and the commit would have looked correct. A partially-stale export is indistinguishable from a fresh one by every signal a committer normally reads — the file is dirty, the command exited 0, and the commit message says what it always says.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN IN A NORMAL REPO. den-hoag-pm3 records that THE LOCAL DOLT DB HAS NO REMOTE. So .beads/beads.jsonl is THE ONLY REPRESENTATION OF THE ISSUE GRAPH THAT TRAVELS VIA GIT. A stale export is not cosmetic: it is the difference between the graph existing off this machine and not. And the git log already carries several 'chore(beads): export the issue graph' commits, so the practice exists — what is unverified is whether those exports were complete.
★ AND IT COMPOUNDS A KNOWN LIMITATION: the JSONL CARRIES NO COMMENTS ('bd show' is the only complete read). So even a CURRENT export loses the reasoning layer — every correction, every rejection-with-its-reason, every measured refutation recorded as a comment. A reconstruction from the JSONL alone gets titles, descriptions and dependencies, and none of the arguments.

WHAT TO ESTABLISH (not done here, and NOT to be assumed either way):
  1. Whether earlier 'chore(beads)' commits were themselves partial. Checkable: for a few beads whose creation date precedes a given export commit, grep that commit's blob for their ids.
  2. Whether an automatic export hook exists and is dropping writes, or whether the 3+/2- churn came from something else entirely. The one bead that DID land was the first created in the session, which is suggestive of a hook that fired once, but that is a HYPOTHESIS and the mechanism was not read.
  3. Whether the right fix is a pre-commit hook that runs 'bd export -o' and fails the commit if the working tree changes as a result — the by-construction form, where a stale export cannot be committed — rather than remembering the flag.
DO NOT PATCH BY HABIT. The failure is that a command which does nothing to the file exits 0 and looks identical to one that does.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★★ ORCHESTRATOR ERROR — THIS BEAD'S SEVERITY ARGUMENT WAS FALSE AND IS WITHDRAWN. Owner correction 2026-07-29: 'you're using local dolt on a branch for beads; the jsonl file is my beads-viewer compat interface to see what the tasks look like.' Downgraded P1 -> P3 and retitled.

WHAT I ASSERTED: 'the Dolt DB has no remote, so the JSONL is the only thing that travels via git', and therefore a stale export is 'the difference between the graph existing off this machine and not'. BOTH CLAUSES ARE WRONG.
MEASURED AFTER THE CORRECTION: git ls-remote origin 'refs/dolt/*' -> cfd3fd0ed5d1e8e878e7afc7eb87dae80848ef01 refs/dolt/data. THE REAL RECORD TRAVELS VIA GIT ON ITS OWN REF. The JSONL is a VIEWER COMPAT INTERFACE, not the transport.

★ HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism matters more than the fact. CLAUDE.md states the architecture IN ONE LINE AT THE TOP OF THE FILE: 'issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses refs/dolt/data on your git remote; .beads/issues.jsonl is a passive export.' I READ THAT AT SESSION START AND THEN WROTE ITS INVERSE. The inversion came from bead den-hoag-pm3, whose title I carried forward as 'the bead graph has NO remote' — ★ AND pm3's ACTUAL SENTENCE IS NARROWER: bd sync is pull-first and CANNOT BOOTSTRAP, and git carries issue ROWS but not the COMMENT layer. 'Cannot bootstrap' became 'has no remote' in my paraphrase, and the paraphrase then out-ranked the primary source sitting in my own context.
⇒ ★ THE LESSON, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS RE-LEARNING FROM THE OTHER SIDE: I have spent this session telling agents that a bead title is a CLAIM and must be opened and checked. I then let a bead TITLE override a PRIMARY SOURCE I had already read. A summary is a lossy compression of a claim, and the loss is invisible precisely because the summary reads as settled fact.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING AT P3: the mechanism is real and is a flattering trap. 'bd export' WITH NO -o WRITES TO STDOUT, emits well-formed JSONL, and RETURNS 0 WITHOUT TOUCHING THE FILE. The correct form is 'bd export -o .beads/beads.jsonl', which reports 'Exported N issues to ...'. Measured: before, the file held ONE of eight new beads and showed three closed beads as 'status':'open'; after, all eight present and all three closed. POSITIVE CONTROL same predicate same run: den-hoag-4kh.17 and den-hoag-2rh both -> 1 hit, so the grep fires and the absence was about the file.
★ WHAT MAKES IT A TRAP RATHER THAN A TYPO: the file WAS dirty from other churn (3 insertions / 2 deletions), so git status showed the expected signal and the commit looked correct. A partially-stale export is indistinguishable from a fresh one by every signal a committer normally reads.
CONSEQUENCE AT ITS TRUE SEVERITY: THE OWNER'S VIEWER SHOWS A STALE TASK LIST. Not data loss. Still misleading, and misleading in the direction of 'work that is done still looks open' — which is the same class of confusion this session spent hours unwinding in the bead graph itself.

REMAINING OPEN QUESTION, NARROWED: local 'git for-each-ref refs/dolt/*' returns EMPTY while origin carries refs/dolt/data. Whether this machine's bd is actually syncing to that ref, or only writing locally, is UNESTABLISHED — and I am explicitly NOT asserting either answer, having just over-claimed once on exactly this topic. Instrument: 'bd sync' and compare the ref before and after.
SUGGESTED FIX UNCHANGED AND STILL BY-CONSTRUCTION: a pre-commit hook that runs 'bd export -o' and fails if the working tree changes as a result, so a stale viewer export cannot be committed. Better than remembering a flag.

title: [E4] A/B field asymmetry reads as drift — the kernel injects outputs and edges per kind, buildRegistries has no equivalent, and nothing forces it
description:
[E4] ARGUED. A/B FIELD ASYMMETRY READS AS DRIFT.
The kernel injects `outputs` and `edges` PER KIND (`entity.nix`); `buildRegistries` has NO
EQUIVALENT. ★ NOTHING IN THE PIN SPLIT FORCES IT.
Identity is UNAFFECTED (both `raw` -- see E2), but THE RECORDS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE,
which undercuts the "byte-identical call text" reading of E1(A)/(B).
⇒ Either state why the two views legitimately differ, or align them. Cheap; do it while
E1's consolidation is being scoped rather than after.

title: [T6] flakeModules.strict registers two phantom kinds — inert, but a den-hoag-shipped demonstration of the pattern A1 punishes
description:
